shelves.title: Cancer cachexia Deposit #11 · Oct 23, 2026
shelves.question: What is cancer cachexia, how much does it shorten life, and can anything be done about it?
shelves.balance: The definition is settled (Fearon 2011: weight loss >5%, or >2% with BMI <20 or sarcopenia — three stages) and the prognosis is precisely grim: median survival falls stepwise from 20.9 months (grade 0) to 4.3 months (grade 4) in 8,160 patients, CT muscle measures predict survival far better than BMI alone (concordance 0.92 vs 0.73), and sarcopenic obesity carries a fourfold mortality hazard. The mechanisms are real biology — lipolysis switched on, tumor PTHrP browning fat, MIC-1 switching appetite off, tumor vesicles driving muscle wasting through TLR4, glucose recycling running fivefold through the Cori cycle while glycogen stores empty, and autophagy switched on in muscle with its cleanup stalled — but treatment remains the honest gap: anamorelin adds lean mass in two phase III trials yet did not improve grip strength, a multimodal program preserved weight only in a small feasibility trial, and nothing on the shelf reverses the syndrome.

cards.headline: The consensus definition of cancer cachexia
cards.summary: International expert consensus — ongoing muscle loss not fully reversed by nutrition; diagnosis: weight loss over 5% , or over 2% with BMI under 20 or sarcopenia; stages: precachexia, cachexia, refractory.
cards.type: International expert consensus using focus groups and two Delphi rounds, Lancet Oncol 2011
cards.people: International panel of 21 listed experts
cards.result: Ongoing skeletal-muscle loss not fully reversible with conventional nutritional support, causing progressive functional impairment; diagnosis: weight loss over 5% , or over 2% with BMI under 20 or sarcopenia; stages: precachexia, cachexia, refractory cachexia
cards.watchOut: A consensus framework, not a prospective diagnostic-accuracy or treatment study
cards.source: Fearon et al., Lancet Oncol 2011; PMID 21296615
cards.search: consensus definition cancer cachexia fearon lancet oncology 2011 international expert delphi precachexia refractory sarcopenia weight loss diagnosis stages pmid 21296615

cards.headline: Weight-loss grade and survival — 8,160 patients
cards.summary: Prospective cohort — median survival fell stepwise: 20.9 months (grade 0), 14.6 , 10.8 , 7.6 , to 4.3 months (grade 4).
cards.type: International prospective cohort analysis and prognostic-model development, J Clin Oncol 2015
cards.people: 8,160 Canadian and European patients with cancer
cards.result: Median survival fell stepwise: 20.9 months (grade 0), 14.6 (grade 1), 10.8 (grade 2), 7.6 (grade 3), to 4.3 months (grade 4) (P <0.001)
cards.watchOut: The grading is prognostic; it does not establish that preventing weight loss will improve survival
cards.source: Martin et al., J Clin Oncol 2015; PMID 25422490
cards.search: weight loss grade survival 8160 patients martin journal clinical oncology 2015 bmi-adjusted grading median survival prospective cohort pmid 25422490

cards.headline: CT muscle measures beat BMI for prognosis
cards.summary: Cohort, 1,473 lung/GI cancer patients — survival model with muscle index and attenuation reached concordance 0.92 vs 0.73 for the conventional model.
cards.type: Consecutive-patient observational cohort with multivariable survival modeling, J Clin Oncol 2013
cards.people: 1,473 patients with lung or gastrointestinal cancer
cards.result: Conventional model (diagnosis, stage, age, performance status) concordance 0.73 ; model with BMI, weight loss, skeletal-muscle index and muscle attenuation concordance 0.92 (P <0.001)
cards.watchOut: Single-center observational analysis; prognostic cut points require validation across populations and CT protocols
cards.source: Martin et al., J Clin Oncol 2013; PMID 23530101
cards.search: ct muscle measures prognosis bmi concordance martin journal clinical oncology 2013 skeletal muscle index attenuation lung gastrointestinal cancer cohort pmid 23530101

cards.headline: Sarcopenic obesity — the high-risk phenotype
cards.summary: Population cohort — 38 of 250 obese patients ( 15% ) had sarcopenic obesity; mortality HR 4.2 (2.4–7.2) .
cards.type: Population-based observational cohort with CT body-composition analysis, Lancet Oncol 2008
cards.people: 2,115 patients identified; 325 obese, 250 with evaluable CT images; 38 of 250 (15%) met sarcopenia cut points
cards.result: Sarcopenic obesity independently predicted mortality: HR 4.2 (2.4–7.2) (P <0.0001); poorer functional status than obesity without sarcopenia (P =0.009)
cards.watchOut: Only obese patients with suitable CT imaging entered the main analysis; sarcopenia thresholds were derived within the cohort
cards.source: Prado et al., Lancet Oncol 2008; PMID 18539529
cards.search: sarcopenic obesity high-risk phenotype prado lancet oncology 2008 population cohort ct body composition mortality hazard ratio pmid 18539529

cards.headline: Lean mass and 5-FU toxicity
cards.summary: Prospective cohort, 62 colon cancer patients — a dose above 20 mg of 5-FU per kg lean body mass marked the toxicity threshold; in women, OR 16.73 for dose-limiting toxicity.
cards.type: Prospective cohort study, Clin Cancer Res 2007
cards.people: 62 patients with stage II or III colon cancer receiving 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin
cards.result: A dose above 20 mg 5-FU per kg lean body mass marked the toxicity threshold (P =0.005); in women, exposure above the threshold carried OR 16.73 for dose-limiting toxicity (P =0.021)
cards.watchOut: Small cohort; the strong association was demonstrated in women, with no confidence interval reported in the abstract
cards.source: Prado et al., Clin Cancer Res 2007; PMID 17545532
cards.search: lean mass 5-fu fluorouracil toxicity prado clinical cancer research 2007 prospective cohort colon cancer lean body mass dose limiting pmid 17545532

cards.headline: BCAA-enriched TPN and protein kinetics (1986)
cards.summary: Randomized crossover metabolic trial, 10 patients — protein synthesis rose from 2.2 to 3.9 g/kg/day and leucine balance improved; the nitrogen-balance change was not significant ( P=0.15 ).
cards.type: Prospective randomized crossover metabolic trial, Cancer 1986
cards.people: 10 malnourished patients with intra-abdominal metastatic adenocarcinoma; each received conventional TPN (19% BCAA) and isonitrogenous TPN (50% BCAA)
cards.result: BCAA-enriched TPN increased whole-body leucine flux from 68 ± 5 to 145 ± 11 μmol/kg/hour (P <0.001), whole-body protein synthesis from 2.2 ± 0.2 to 3.9 ± 0.3 g protein/kg/day (P <0.005), leucine balance from 2.5 ± 0.4 to 6.5 ± 0.6 g/day (P <0.001), and labeled leucine incorporation into albumin from 2.37 ± 0.23 to 4.21 ± 0.33 μmol/g/hour (P <0.001). The fractional albumin synthetic rate rose from 9.3 ± 0.9% per day to 16.6 ± 1.3% per day (P <0.001); 9 of 10 patients showed marked improvement. The 24-hour urinary nitrogen-balance improvement was not significant: 6.6 ± 3.9 versus 11.4 ± 2.9 g protein/day (P =0.15).
cards.watchOut: Very small, short metabolic study; did not test function, treatment tolerance, or survival
cards.source: Tayek et al., Cancer 1986; PMID 3085914
cards.search: bcaa branched chain amino acid tpn parenteral nutrition protein kinetics tayek cancer 1986 randomized crossover metabolic trial leucine synthesis pmid 3085914

cards.headline: Lipolysis switched on in cachexia
cards.summary: Human case-control, 26 patients — body fat 40% lower and lipolytic activity 2-fold higher in cachexia; hormone-sensitive lipase expression up 50–100% .
cards.type: Human translational case-control study using subcutaneous adipocytes, Cancer Res 2007
cards.people: 26 patients with cancer, with and without cachexia
cards.result: Body fat 40% lower and in-vivo lipolytic activity 2-fold higher in cachexia (P =0.001); stimulated lipolysis 2- to 3-fold higher; HSL mRNA up 50% and protein up 100%
cards.watchOut: Cross-sectional design; cannot determine whether increased HSL activity initiates cachexia or develops as a consequence of it
cards.source: Agustsson et al., Cancer Res 2007; PMID 17545636
cards.search: lipolysis adipose cachexia agustsson cancer research 2007 hormone-sensitive lipase case-control body fat adipocytes pmid 17545636

cards.headline: Tumor PTHrP browns fat and drives wasting
cards.summary: Mouse model + 47 -patient cohort — blocking PTHrP stopped browning and wasting in mice; 17 of 47 patients had detectable PTHrP, with lower lean mass and higher energy expenditure.
cards.type: Translational study — Lewis lung carcinoma mouse model plus human cohort, Nature 2014
cards.people: Mouse experiments plus 47 patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung or colorectal cancer
cards.result: Neutralizing PTHrP in mice blocked adipose browning and substantially reduced loss of fat, muscle mass and strength; 17 of 47 patients had detectable PTHrP, with lower lean body mass and higher resting energy expenditure per kg lean body mass
cards.watchOut: The human component was small and associative; the causal intervention was performed in mice
cards.source: Kir et al., Nature 2014; PMID 25043053
cards.search: pthrp parathyroid hormone related protein adipose browning wasting kir nature 2014 mouse model lewis lung carcinoma cohort lean mass energy expenditure pmid 25043053

cards.headline: Multimodal intervention — feasible, weight-preserving
cards.summary: Randomized phase II feasibility trial, 46 patients — at 6 weeks weight changed +0.91 kg (intervention) vs −2.12 kg (control); compliance 48–76% across components.
cards.type: Randomized open-label phase II feasibility trial, J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2017
cards.people: 46 patients with incurable lung or pancreatic cancer; 25 multimodal treatment, 21 standard care
cards.result: At 6 weeks, mean weight changed +0.91 kg (intervention) vs −2.12 kg (control); compliance 76% celecoxib, 60% exercise, 48% nutritional supplements; attrition 11%
cards.watchOut: Small, unblinded, powered for feasibility rather than efficacy; celecoxib-related fluid retention could affect weight
cards.source: Solheim et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2017; PMID 28614627
cards.search: multimodal intervention feasibility weight solheim journal cachexia sarcopenia muscle 2017 randomized phase ii nutrition exercise celecoxib chemotherapy pmid 28614627

cards.headline: Anamorelin — more lean mass, no more strength
cards.summary: Two phase III RCTs (ROMANA 1 & 2), 979 patients total — lean body mass +0.99 vs −0.47 kg and +0.65 vs −0.98 kg (both P<0.0001 ); handgrip strength did not improve in either trial.
cards.type: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trials (ROMANA 1 & 2), Lancet Oncol 2016
cards.people: 979 patients total — ROMANA 1: 484 (323 anamorelin, 161 placebo); ROMANA 2: 495 (330 anamorelin, 165 placebo)
cards.result: At 12 weeks, lean body mass +0.99 kg vs −0.47 kg (ROMANA 1) and +0.65 kg vs −0.98 kg (ROMANA 2), both P <0.0001 ; handgrip strength did not improve in either trial
cards.watchOut: Increased lean mass but no improvement in the co-primary functional endpoint; sponsor-funded trials
cards.source: Temel et al., Lancet Oncol 2016; PMID 26906526
cards.search: anamorelin lean body mass handgrip strength temel lancet oncology 2016 romana phase iii randomized trials nsclc cachexia ghrelin pmid 26906526

cards.headline: Cori cycle activity in metastatic carcinoma (Holroyde 1975)
cards.summary: Cori cycle activity 90 mg/kg/hr (range 22–193) in the weight-losing patients vs 18 mg/kg/hr (range 13–24) in controls (p <0.02).
cards.people: 14 patients with metastatic carcinoma — 8 with progressive weight loss vs 6 without
cards.result: Cori cycle activity 90 mg/kg/hr (range 22–193) in the weight-losing patients vs 18 mg/kg/hr (range 13–24) in controls (p <0.02). Total glucose turnover 196 vs 110 mg/kg/hr; glucose oxidation 62 vs 48 mg/kg/hr; total caloric expenditure 36 vs 33 kcal/sq m/hr. The means were skewed by four patients with markedly high recycling rates, equivalent to the total endogenous glucose turnover of a normal subject.
cards.watchOut: n=14 and heterogeneous — the energy-loss explanation applies to a subgroup, not every weight-losing patient.
cards.source: Holroyde CP, Gabuzda TG, Putnam RC, Paul P, Reichard GA. Cancer Research. 1975;35:3710–3714. PMID: 1192429
cards.search: cori cycle activity metastatic carcinoma holroyde 1975 metabolic tracer glucose recycling weight loss cancer research pmid 1192429

cards.headline: Glucose metabolism in cachectic colorectal cancer (Holroyde 1984)
cards.summary: Glucose production 136.4 ± 9.0 vs 101.0 ± 4.6 mg/kg/hr (p <0.01); Cori-cycle recycling 43.0 ± 7.2 vs 15.4 mg/kg/hr (p <0.01).
cards.type: Metabolic tracer study with oral glucose tolerance and glucagon challenge
cards.people: 12 weight-losing patients with metastatic colorectal cancer vs age-matched controls without cancer; [1-14C]glucose infusion 50–100 µCi
cards.result: Glucose production 136.4 ± 9.0 vs 101.0 ± 4.6 mg/kg/hr (p <0.01); Cori-cycle recycling 43.0 ± 7.2 vs 15.4 mg/kg/hr (p <0.01). After an oral glucose load of 40 g/sq m (10 of 12 patients), glucose clearance was delayed (p <0.01) and the insulin secretory response blunted (p <0.025). Glucagon infusion (15 ng/kg/min over 40 min, 7 subjects) gave a blunted glycemic response: Δ25.0 ± 6.9 vs 57.8 ± 8.5 mg/dl (p <0.025), reflecting depleted glycogen stores. Increased production and recycling were seen only with carbohydrate intolerance.
cards.watchOut: n=12; values ranged from normal to markedly elevated — the abnormality tracks with carbohydrate intolerance, not with weight loss alone.
cards.source: Holroyde CP, et al. Cancer Research. 1984;44(12 Pt 1):5910–5914.
cards.search: glucose metabolism cachectic colorectal cancer holroyde 1984 metabolic tracer cori recycling glycogen glucagon cancer research

cards.headline: MIC-1/GDF15 mediates tumor anorexia and weight loss (Johnen 2007)
cards.summary: MIC-1 abundance in sera was directly related to weight loss in advanced prostate cancer. Xenografted tumors caused marked weight, fat, and lean loss via decreased food intake, reversed by anti-MIC-1 antibody.
cards.type: Mouse xenograft and transgenic overexpression study with a small human correlation
cards.people: Sera from patients with advanced prostate cancer; xenografted prostate tumors in nude mice (40 mice); transgenic MIC-1 overexpression
cards.result: MIC-1 abundance in sera was directly related to weight loss in advanced prostate cancer. Xenografted tumors caused marked weight, fat, and lean loss via decreased food intake, reversed by anti-MIC-1 antibody. Systemic MIC-1 and transgenic overexpression caused hypophagia and reduced body weight, acting centrally via hypothalamic TGF-betaRII, ERK1/2, STAT3, NPY, and POMC. Arcuate GHRH mRNA fell to 71±9% of control from 100±8% (P=0.0343); human weight change vs serum MIC-1 r=0.419 (P=0.0087), vs IL-6 r=0.02 (P=0.9292).
cards.watchOut: Mostly mouse work; the human arm is a small correlation; the GHRH and correlation numbers are from the paper’s figures as reproduced.
cards.source: Johnen H, et al. Nature Medicine. 2007;13:1333–1340. DOI: 10.1038/nm1677.
cards.search: mic-1 gdf15 tumor anorexia weight loss johnen 2007 mouse xenograft transgenic nature medicine prostate cancer antibody

cards.headline: Tumor Hsp70/Hsp90 vesicles drive muscle wasting via TLR4 (Zhang 2017)
cards.summary: Cachexia-inducing tumor cells released Hsp70/Hsp90 about 10-fold higher than non-cachexia cells; serum Hsp70/Hsp90α was about 3–4-fold higher in LLC tumor-bearing mice (day 21) and cachectic ApcMin/+ mice (20 weeks), but not in EL4 tumor mice or pre-cachectic ApcMin/+ mice (12 weeks).
cards.people: Cachexia-inducing tumor cells vs non-tumorigenic/non-cachexia cells; LLC tumor-bearing mice, ApcMin/+ mice, EL4 tumor mice
cards.result: Cachexia-inducing tumor cells released Hsp70/Hsp90 about 10-fold higher than non-cachexia cells; serum Hsp70/Hsp90α was about 3–4-fold higher in LLC tumor-bearing mice (day 21) and cachectic ApcMin/+ mice (20 weeks), but not in EL4 tumor mice or pre-cachectic ApcMin/+ mice (12 weeks). Hsp70/90-expressing vesicles were necessary and sufficient for wasting; Rab27a/b knockdown blocked vesicle release and spared muscle wasting without changing tumor burden; the mechanism runs via TLR4 (not TLR2), and TLR4-knockout mice were spared.
cards.watchOut: Mouse and cell work only — no human data; a mechanism, not a treatment.
cards.source: Zhang G, et al. Nature Communications. 2017;8:589. PMID: 28928431. PMCID: PMC5605540.
cards.search: tumor hsp70 hsp90 vesicles muscle wasting tlr4 zhang 2017 nature communications extracellular vesicles llc apcmin pmid 28928431

cards.headline: Autophagy in the muscle of cachectic cancer patients (Aversa 2016)
cards.summary: Beclin-1 protein up, LC3B-II protein significantly up, LC3B-I unchanged, p62 up in cachectic AND non-cachectic cancer patients (impaired autophagosome clearance), Parkin significantly up, PINK1 unchanged; LC3B mRNA up, PINK1 mRNA down.
cards.type: Human muscle-biopsy study (autophagy and mitophagy markers, protein and mRNA)
cards.people: 29 cancer patients (17 men, 12 women; mean age 68 ± 2 years) undergoing abdominal surgery — cachexia in 12, pre-cachexia in 3, non-cachectic in 14; 11 controls (6 men, 5 women; 63 ± 4 years) undergoing surgery for non-neoplastic disease; rectus abdominis biopsies
cards.result: Beclin-1 protein up, LC3B-II protein significantly up, LC3B-I unchanged, p62 up in cachectic AND non-cachectic cancer patients (impaired autophagosome clearance), Parkin significantly up, PINK1 unchanged; LC3B mRNA up, PINK1 mRNA down. Mean body weight loss 6.7 ± 1.5% over 6 months (range 0–33%); 38% had anorexia-related symptoms.
cards.watchOut: Directional findings only in the abstract — no fold-changes or p-values printed there (fold-changes are in the full text); most patients were over 65, so age-related sarcopenia may contribute to the clearance impairment.
cards.source: Aversa Z, et al. Scientific Reports. 2016;6:30340. DOI: 10.1038/srep30340.
cards.search: autophagy muscle cachectic cancer patients aversa 2016 scientific reports biopsy beclin lc3b p62 parkin pink1

shelves.title: Blood thinners for cancer-associated clots: pills vs daily injections
shelves.question: In cancer-associated venous thromboembolism, can an oral factor Xa inhibitor replace six months of daily dalteparin injections?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Anticoagulants · Dalteparin · Factor Xa Inhibitors · Female · Fibrinolytic Agents · Follow-Up Studies · Hemorrhage · Heparin, Low-Molecular-Weight · Humans · Incidence · Injections, Subcutaneous · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasms · Pilot Projects · Proportional Hazards Models · Pulmonary Embolism · Pyrazoles · Pyridines · Pyridones · Recurrence · Rivaroxaban · Secondary Prevention · Single-Blind Method · Survival Rate · Thiazoles · Treatment Outcome · Venous Thromboembolism · Venous Thrombosis
shelves.balance: Three trials, one pattern with a drug-specific catch. The pills prevent recurrence at least as well as the injections — and patients prefer them. But the bleeding price depends on the drug: apixaban showed no excess major bleeding at all, while edoxaban and rivaroxaban bled more, especially from the gut. "A pill instead of injections" is earned; "any pill" is not.

cards.headline: Caravaggio 2020: apixaban matched dalteparin on recurrence (5.6% vs 7.9%) with no extra major bleeding (3.8% vs 4.0%).
cards.summary: Recurrent VTE 5.6% (32/576) on apixaban vs 7.9% (46/579) on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.63 , 95% CI 0.37–1.07; P<0.001 for non-inferiority). Major bleeding 3.8% (22 patients) vs 4.0% (23) (hazard ratio 0.82 , 0.40–1.69).
cards.people: 1,155 patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (576 apixaban, 579 dalteparin)
cards.result: Recurrent VTE 5.6% (32/576) on apixaban vs 7.9% (46/579) on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.63 , 95% CI 0.37–1.07; P<0.001 for non-inferiority). Major bleeding 3.8% (22 patients) vs 4.0% (23) (hazard ratio 0.82 , 0.40–1.69).
cards.watchOut: Non-inferiority, not proven superiority, on recurrence — and open-label, though outcomes were adjudicated blinded.
cards.source: Agnelli G et al., N Engl J Med 2020 (PMID 32223112 · NCT03045406)

cards.headline: Hokusai 2018: edoxaban equal on the composite (12.8% vs 13.5%) — fewer recurrences, more major bleeds.
cards.summary: Composite of recurrent VTE or major bleeding 12.8% (67/522) on edoxaban vs 13.5% (71/524) on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.97 , 95% CI 0.70–1.36; non-inferior). Recurrent VTE 7.9% vs 11.3% (risk difference −3.4 points); major bleeding 6.9% vs 4.0% (risk difference +2.9 points, 95% CI 0.1–5.6).
cards.people: 1,046 patients with cancer-associated VTE in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (522 edoxaban, 524 dalteparin)
cards.result: Composite of recurrent VTE or major bleeding 12.8% (67/522) on edoxaban vs 13.5% (71/524) on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.97 , 95% CI 0.70–1.36; non-inferior). Recurrent VTE 7.9% vs 11.3% (risk difference −3.4 points); major bleeding 6.9% vs 4.0% (risk difference +2.9 points, 95% CI 0.1–5.6).
cards.watchOut: The composite hides a trade — the bleeding excess was concentrated in gastrointestinal cancers. Same drug class as Card 1, different bleeding bill.
cards.source: Raskob GE et al., N Engl J Med 2018 (PMID 29231094 · NCT02073682)

cards.headline: SELECT-D 2018: rivaroxaban cut recurrence (4% vs 11%) but tripled clinically relevant non-major bleeding (13% vs 4%).
cards.summary: Six-month VTE recurrence 4% on rivaroxaban vs 11% on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.43 , 95% CI 0.19–0.99). Major bleeding 6% vs 4% (hazard ratio 1.83 , 0.68–4.96); clinically relevant non-major bleeding 13% vs 4% (hazard ratio 3.76 , 1.63–8.69).
cards.people: 406 patients with active cancer and VTE (203 per arm); 58% had metastatic disease
cards.result: Six-month VTE recurrence 4% on rivaroxaban vs 11% on dalteparin (hazard ratio 0.43 , 95% CI 0.19–0.99). Major bleeding 6% vs 4% (hazard ratio 1.83 , 0.68–4.96); clinically relevant non-major bleeding 13% vs 4% (hazard ratio 3.76 , 1.63–8.69).
cards.watchOut: A pilot — sized for estimates, not proof — and it excluded patients at high bleeding risk partway through. Its signal (recurrence down, nuisance bleeding up) is what the two big trials then refined.
cards.source: Young AM et al., J Clin Oncol 2018 (PMID 29746227 · ISRCTN86712308)

shelves.title: Colorectal cancer screening: what the randomized trials actually showed
shelves.question: Does endoscopic screening prevent colorectal cancer deaths — and why did the biggest colonoscopy trial look weaker than the smaller sigmoidoscopy trials?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Colonic Polyps · Colonoscopy · Colorectal Neoplasms · Early Detection of Cancer · Equipment Contamination · Europe · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Incidence · Male · Mass Screening · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Staging · Odds Ratio · Risk · Sigmoidoscopes · Sigmoidoscopy
shelves.balance: The sigmoidoscopy trials — one look, or two — cut both incidence and mortality by a fifth to a third. The colonoscopy trial cut incidence by 18% but showed no significant mortality benefit at 10 years, in a trial where only 42% of the invited actually got scoped. Read together: screening works roughly in proportion to how much of it actually happens; intention-to-screen arithmetic punishes low uptake, and the per-protocol numbers in the older trials show the biological effect is real.

cards.headline: Once-only sigmoidoscopy: colorectal cancer incidence down 23%, mortality down 31% over 11 years.
cards.summary: Over a median 11.2 years, colorectal cancer incidence fell 23% (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.70–0.84) and colorectal cancer mortality fell 31% (hazard ratio 0.69, 0.59–0.82) in intention-to-treat analysis. Among those actually screened, incidence fell 33% and mortality 43%. Distal colorectal cancer incidence was halved.
cards.people: 170,432 adults aged 55–64 (57,237 assigned to one flexible sigmoidoscopy; 71% attended)
cards.result: Over a median 11.2 years, colorectal cancer incidence fell 23% (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.70–0.84) and colorectal cancer mortality fell 31% (hazard ratio 0.69, 0.59–0.82) in intention-to-treat analysis. Among those actually screened, incidence fell 33% and mortality 43%. Distal colorectal cancer incidence was halved.
cards.watchOut: One examination of the distal colon only — it cannot see the proximal colon, yet still moved mortality; the effect is prevention (polyp removal), concentrated where the scope reaches.
cards.source: Atkin WS et al., Lancet 2010 (PMID 20430429 · ISRCTN28352761)

cards.headline: PLCO: screening sigmoidoscopy cut incidence 21% and mortality 26% — including a proximal benefit.
cards.summary: After a median 11.9 years, colorectal cancer incidence was 11.9 vs 15.2 cases per 10,000 person-years (relative risk 0.79, 95% CI 0.72–0.85) and mortality 2.9 vs 3.9 per 10,000 person-years — a 26% reduction.
cards.people: 154,900 adults (77,445 assigned to flexible sigmoidoscopy at baseline and again at 3–5 years; 83.5% screened at baseline)
cards.result: After a median 11.9 years, colorectal cancer incidence was 11.9 vs 15.2 cases per 10,000 person-years (relative risk 0.79, 95% CI 0.72–0.85) and mortality 2.9 vs 3.9 per 10,000 person-years — a 26% reduction.
cards.watchOut: A screening trial inside a screening-saturated country — usual-care contamination dilutes the contrast, so the true effect of the examination is likely larger than the trial contrast.

shelves.title: Lung cancer screening with low-dose CT: two trials, two continents, same answer
shelves.question: Does screening heavy smokers with low-dose CT actually prevent lung-cancer deaths — or just find more cancers?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Belgium · Bias · Cone-Beam Computed Tomography · Early Detection of Cancer · False Positive Reactions · Female · Humans · Incidence · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Medical Overuse · Middle Aged · Netherlands · Patient Compliance · Radiography, Thoracic · Registries · Sex Factors · Smoking · Tomography, X-Ray Computed
shelves.balance: Both mega-trials answer the mortality question the same way: about a fifth to a quarter fewer lung-cancer deaths over a decade. The price is printed on the same cards: in NLST, 96% of positive screens were false alarms — and NELSON shows protocol design can shrink that burden. This is a benefit with a known, countable cost — the rare screening shelf where both numbers come from randomized trials.

cards.headline: NLST 2011: low-dose CT screening cut lung-cancer mortality 20% vs chest X-ray — with a 96% false-positive rate among positives.
cards.summary: Lung-cancer deaths were 247 per 100,000 person-years with CT vs 309 with radiography — a relative reduction of 20.0% (95% CI 6.8–26.7; P=0.004). Death from any cause fell 6.7%. But 24.2% of CT screens were positive across the three rounds, and 96.4% of those positives were false positives.
cards.people: 53,454 people at high risk for lung cancer; three annual screens, low-dose CT (26,722) vs chest radiography (26,732)
cards.result: Lung-cancer deaths were 247 per 100,000 person-years with CT vs 309 with radiography — a relative reduction of 20.0% (95% CI 6.8–26.7; P=0.004). Death from any cause fell 6.7%. But 24.2% of CT screens were positive across the three rounds, and 96.4% of those positives were false positives.
cards.watchOut: The comparator was chest X-ray, not no screening — so this trial alone left open whether CT beat nothing. NELSON (Reference 2) closed that gap. The false-positive burden is the intervention's real cost: most positive screens meant more scans and worry, not cancer.
cards.source: Aberle DR et al. (National Lung Screening Trial), N Engl J Med 2011 (PMID 21714641 · NCT00047385)

cards.headline: NELSON 2020: volume CT screening cut lung-cancer death 24% in men at 10 years (rate ratio 0.76) — against no screening at all.
cards.summary: At 10 years, lung-cancer mortality in men was 2.50 deaths per 1,000 person-years screened vs 3.30 unscreened (rate ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.61–0.94; P=0.01). shelves.title: PSA screening for prostate cancer: a small mortality benefit at a large overdiagnosis cost
shelves.question: Does PSA screening reduce deaths from prostate cancer?
shelves.mesh: Prostatic Neoplasms · Prostate-Specific Antigen · Mass Screening · Digital Rectal Examination · Biopsy · Humans · Male
shelves.balance: The European trial found a 20% lower prostate-cancer death rate with screening at 9 years, bought with heavy overdiagnosis — 1,410 men screened and 48 extra cases treated for each death prevented. The US trial found no benefit, but its control group was screened anyway at high rates (PSA use rose from 40% to 52% over the trial), which dilutes any difference. The two trials are not as contradictory as they look; the honest reading is a small benefit at a large overdiagnosis cost. Developer’s verdict: MAYBE (weak evidence) — the one positive mortality ratio (0.80) sits inside the house gray zone, and the second trial is null.

cards.headline: ERSPC (Schröder 2009): a 20% lower prostate-cancer death rate — 1,410 men screened for each death prevented
cards.summary: Prostate-cancer mortality rate ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.98); 1,410 men screened and 48 additional cases treated per death prevented — 182,000 men, median follow-up 9 years.
cards.people: 182,000 men aged 50–74 in seven European countries; PSA screening (mostly every 4 years, biopsy at PSA ≥3.0) vs no organized screening; pre-specified core group aged 55–69
cards.result: Median follow-up 9 years: prostate cancer incidence 8.2% vs 4.8%; prostate-cancer deaths 214 vs 326 in the core group; mortality rate ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.98); absolute difference 0.71 deaths per 1,000 men; 1,410 men screened and 48 additional cases treated per death prevented. An 11-year update found the same pattern (rate ratio 0.79).
cards.watchOut: The benefit was bought with heavy overdiagnosis — incidence 8.2% vs 4.8% against one death prevented per 1,410 men screened.
cards.source: Schröder et al. N Engl J Med. 2009;360:1320–1328. PMID 19297566 · ISRCTN49127736.

shelves.title: Mammography screening for breast cancer: the two longest trials disagree
shelves.question: Does mammography screening reduce deaths from breast cancer?
shelves.mesh: Breast Neoplasms · Mammography · Mass Screening · Early Detection of Cancer · Physical Examination · Humans · Female
shelves.balance: The two longest trials point in opposite directions. The Swedish trial found about 30% fewer breast-cancer deaths over 29 years of follow-up. The Canadian trial found no mortality difference over 25 years and measured the overdiagnosis directly: about 22% of screen-detected invasive cancers — one excess diagnosis for every 424 women screened — would never have surfaced on their own. Both trials predate modern imaging and modern drug therapy, which shrinks the margin screening can add. Developer’s verdict: MAYBE (weak evidence) — the two best trials disagree; older technology in both.

cards.watchOut: The trial began in 1980 and predates modern imaging and modern drug therapy, which shrinks the margin screening can add.

shelves.title: Ovarian cancer screening with CA-125 and ultrasound: no lives saved
shelves.question: Does screening average-risk women with CA-125 and ultrasound reduce deaths from ovarian cancer?
shelves.mesh: Ovarian Neoplasms · CA-125 Antigen · Early Detection of Cancer · Mass Screening · Ultrasonography · False Positive Reactions · Humans · Female
shelves.balance: Two very large trials give one answer: screening average-risk women does not reduce ovarian cancer deaths. The UK trial's early, non-significant suggestion of benefit (15% at the primary analysis) disappeared with longer follow-up (HR 0.94). The US trial found no benefit and quantified the harm: of women with false-positive results who went to surgery, 15% suffered a serious complication. Developer’s verdict: LIKELY — no mortality benefit; a negative shelf resting on two huge, concordant trials.

shelves.title: HPV testing vs cytology for cervical cancer screening: less cancer at the second round
shelves.question: Does HPV-based cervical screening prevent more invasive cervical cancer than cytology alone?
shelves.mesh: Uterine Cervical Neoplasms · Uterine Cervical Dysplasia · Papillomavirus Infections · Mass Screening · Vaginal Smears · Early Detection of Cancer · Humans · Female
shelves.balance: HPV-based screening catches more precancer at the first round and leaves less disease to find at the next. In the Italian trial, invasive cancers across two rounds numbered 7 with HPV testing vs 18 with cytology, and none appeared in the HPV arm in round 2; the Dutch trial showed the same pattern for high-grade lesions and for cancer (4 vs 14 cases). The trade-off is more positive tests and, in younger women, treatment of lesions that would have regressed on their own. Developer’s verdict: LIKELY for earlier detection of high-grade lesions · POSSIBLE for fewer invasive cancers — concordant, but the event counts are small.

shelves.title: HPV vaccination: near-complete protection against vaccine-type precancer when given before infection
shelves.question: Does HPV vaccination prevent high-grade cervical lesions?
shelves.mesh: Papillomavirus Vaccines · Papillomavirus Infections · Uterine Cervical Neoplasms · Uterine Cervical Dysplasia · Human papillomavirus 16 · Human papillomavirus 18 · Humans · Female
shelves.balance: In young women not previously infected, both vaccines prevented nearly all high-grade cervical lesions caused by the vaccine HPV types (98% for the quadrivalent vaccine per-protocol; 93% for the bivalent vaccine). The protection is preventive, not treatment: counted across all randomized women regardless of prior infection, efficacy against vaccine-type lesions was 44%, and against high-grade lesions from all HPV types combined only 17–30%. Both trials measured precancer (CIN 2/3), not cancer itself — the cancer claim rests on the surrogate. Developer’s verdict: LIKELY — prevention of vaccine-type high-grade lesions in HPV-naive young women (surrogate endpoint; no cancer endpoint in either trial).

shelves.title: Tamoxifen and raloxifene to prevent breast cancer: fewer cancers, real harms, no mortality benefit
shelves.question: In women at increased risk, do tamoxifen or raloxifene prevent breast cancer, and at what cost?
shelves.mesh: Breast Neoplasms · Tamoxifen · Raloxifene Hydrochloride · Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators · Estrogen Antagonists · Humans · Female
shelves.balance: Tamoxifen cut invasive breast cancer by about half in high-risk women (cumulative incidence 43.4 vs 22.0 per 1,000 over about 6 years), entirely among estrogen-receptor-positive tumors, at the cost of more endometrial cancer (RR 2.53) and blood clots, partly offset by fewer fractures. In the head-to-head trial, raloxifene matched tamoxifen against invasive cancer with fewer clots and cataracts and a trend toward fewer uterine cancers, but was weaker against noninvasive cancer. Neither trial showed any mortality benefit — this shelf is about incidence and harm trade-offs, and says so. Developer’s verdict: LIKELY for incidence reduction (tamoxifen vs placebo) and for raloxifene's equivalence on invasive cancer — no mortality claim.

cards.headline: NSABP P-1 (Fisher 1998): tamoxifen cut invasive breast cancer 49% — endometrial cancer risk rose (RR 2.53)
cards.summary: Invasive breast cancer reduced 49% (cumulative incidence through 69 months 43.4 vs 22.0 per 1,000); endometrial cancer rate increased (RR 2.53, 95% CI 1.35–4.97) — 13,388 high-risk women.
cards.people: 13,388 women at increased risk (age ≥60, or 35–59 with 5-year predicted risk ≥1.66%, or prior lobular carcinoma in situ); tamoxifen 20 mg/day vs placebo for 5 years
cards.result: Invasive breast cancer reduced 49% (cumulative incidence through 69 months 43.4 vs 22.0 per 1,000); noninvasive cancer reduced 50%; estrogen-receptor-positive tumors reduced 69% with no difference in ER-negative tumors. Endometrial cancer rate increased (RR 2.53, 95% CI 1.35–4.97), mainly in women aged 50+. Hip, radius, and spine fractures were fewer; ischemic heart disease rates were unchanged.
cards.watchOut: No mortality benefit was shown — the gain is fewer diagnoses, bought with more endometrial cancer and blood clots.
cards.source: Fisher et al. J Natl Cancer Inst. 1998;90:1371–1388. PMID 9747868 · no registry ID (pre-registration era).

shelves.title: Finasteride and dutasteride to prevent prostate cancer: fewer diagnoses, mostly low-grade
shelves.question: Do 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors prevent prostate cancer?
shelves.mesh: Prostatic Neoplasms · 5-alpha Reductase Inhibitors · Finasteride · Dutasteride · Prostate-Specific Antigen · Humans · Male
shelves.balance: Both drugs cut the chance of a prostate-cancer diagnosis by about a quarter, and the reduction is concentrated in low-grade tumors — the kind most often overdiagnosed and overtreated. Both trials also produced a high-grade warning signal (more Gleason 7–10 tumors among cancers found in PCPT; a 12-vs-1 excess of Gleason 8–10 tumors late in REDUCE), partly explained by the drugs shrinking the prostate so biopsy samples it better. Long-term PCPT follow-up found no survival difference either way. Neither drug is approved for prevention; the shelf presents the trade-off, not a recommendation. Developer’s verdict: LIKELY for fewer diagnoses, mostly low-grade · MAYBE (weak evidence) for any effect on the cancers that matter.

cards.headline: PCPT (Thompson 2003): finasteride cut prostate-cancer diagnoses by a quarter — with a high-grade warning signal
cards.summary: Prostate cancer prevalence 18.4% vs 24.4% — a 24.8% reduction (95% CI 18.6–30.6); Gleason 7–10 tumors were more common with finasteride (37.0% vs 22.2% of tumors found) — 18,882 men.

Sexual side effects were more common on finasteride; urinary symptoms were fewer.
cards.watchOut: Follow-up to 18 years found no difference in overall survival or in survival after a prostate-cancer diagnosis; the reduction is concentrated in low-grade tumors.

shelves.title: Eradicating H. pylori to prevent gastric cancer: incidence halved in high-risk populations
shelves.question: Does eradicating Helicobacter pylori prevent gastric cancer?
shelves.mesh: Stomach Neoplasms · Helicobacter pylori · Helicobacter Infections · Precancerous Conditions · Proton Pump Inhibitors · Humans
shelves.balance: In a high-risk Chinese county, two weeks of antibiotics for H. pylori roughly halved gastric cancer incidence over 22 years (OR 0.48 — the one ratio on this slate that clears the house floor) and reduced gastric-cancer deaths (HR 0.62). In Korean patients who had already had an early gastric cancer removed endoscopically, eradication halved new cancers appearing elsewhere in the stomach (HR 0.50). Both trials come from high-incidence East Asian populations; benefit in low-incidence populations is unproven. The Shandong trial's vitamin arm also reduced incidence and mortality — reported on Card 1; the trial's one home is this shelf. Developer’s verdict: POSSIBLE — two randomized trials, concordant, large and long; one population type.

cards.headline: Shandong Intervention Trial, Linqu County (Li 2019): two weeks of antibiotics halved gastric cancer incidence over 22 years (OR 0.48)
cards.summary: H. pylori treatment: incidence OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.32–0.71); gastric-cancer mortality HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.39–0.99) over 22.3 years — 3,365 residents of a high-risk Chinese county.
cards.people: 3,365 residents of a high-risk county in Shandong, China; the 2,258 participants seropositive for H. pylori were assigned to 2 weeks of amoxicillin plus omeprazole or placebo, with vitamin (C, E, selenium) and garlic supplementation arms running in parallel for 7.3 years
cards.result: Over 22.3 years, 151 gastric cancers and 94 gastric-cancer deaths occurred. H. pylori treatment: incidence OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.32–0.71); gastric-cancer mortality HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.39–0.99). Vitamin supplementation also reduced incidence (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.46–0.91) and mortality (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.31–0.75); garlic supplementation reduced mortality only (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.43–1.00).
cards.watchOut: A high-incidence East Asian population; benefit in low-incidence populations is unproven. The vitamin and garlic arms ran inside the same trial — this shelf is the trial's one home.

shelves.title: Aspirin in Lynch syndrome: one trial, a delayed and durable benefit
shelves.question: Does daily aspirin prevent colorectal cancer in carriers of Lynch syndrome?
shelves.mesh: Colorectal Neoplasms, Hereditary Nonpolyposis · Aspirin · Anti-Inflammatory Agents, Non-Steroidal · Chemoprevention · Adenoma · Humans
shelves.balance: One trial, reported twice. At about 5 years the intention-to-treat analysis was not significant (HR 0.63) though the per-protocol analysis was (HR 0.41); at the planned 10-year follow-up both were significant (ITT HR 0.65; per-protocol HR 0.56), with protection appearing roughly 5 years after starting and persisting in registry follow-up to 20 years. The dose was high — 600 mg daily for about 2 years — and the follow-on trial testing lower doses (CaPP3) has not reported. Cancers outside the colon in Lynch syndrome were not reduced (36 vs 36 cases). Developer’s verdict: POSSIBLE — single randomized trial; delayed effect consistent across two reports and both analyses.

Adverse events during the intervention did not differ between groups.
cards.watchOut: One trial, reported twice on this shelf; the dose was high — 600 mg daily for about 2 years.

shelves.title: Daily sunscreen: fewer squamous-cell tumors; the melanoma signal is fragile
shelves.question: Does daily sunscreen use prevent skin cancer?
shelves.mesh: Skin Neoplasms · Sunscreening Agents · Basal Cell Carcinoma · Carcinoma, Squamous Cell · Melanoma · beta Carotene · Humans
shelves.balance: One community trial in subtropical Australia. Daily sunscreen did not significantly reduce the rate of first basal-cell or squamous-cell cancers per person, but it did reduce the total number of squamous-cell tumors (rate ratio 0.61); beta-carotene had no effect on either cancer. Ten years after the trial ended, the daily-use group had half as many melanomas (11 vs 22) and fewer invasive melanomas (3 vs 11) — a result resting on only 33 melanomas, presented as fragile. Developer’s verdict: POSSIBLE for squamous-cell tumor burden · MAYBE (weak evidence) for melanoma (one trial, 33 events) · no effect on basal-cell carcinoma.

cards.headline: Nambour Trial (Green 1999): daily sunscreen cut the total squamous-cell tumor rate (0.61) — first-cancer rates did not differ
cards.summary: First new cancer per person: basal-cell RR 1.03 (95% CI 0.73–1.46), squamous-cell RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.50–1.56) — not significant; total squamous-cell tumor rate ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.46–0.81) — 1,621 Queensland residents.
cards.people: 1,621 residents of Nambour, Queensland, in a 2×2 factorial design: daily SPF 15+ sunscreen to the head, neck, arms, and hands vs discretionary use, crossed with beta-carotene 30 mg/day vs placebo; 4.5 years
cards.result: Rates of first new cancer per person did not differ significantly (basal-cell RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.73–1.46; squamous-cell RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.50–1.56), but the total squamous-cell tumor rate was lower with daily sunscreen (rate ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.46–0.81); about 45 people using sunscreen for 4.5 years prevented one squamous-cell tumor. Beta-carotene showed no benefit or harm for either cancer.
cards.watchOut: One community trial in subtropical Australia; the win is in total tumor burden, not in first cancers per person.

shelves.title: Three versus six months of adjuvant chemotherapy in colon cancer (IDEA): noninferiority NOT confirmed overall — the answer splits by regimen and by risk
shelves.question: In stage III colon cancer, can adjuvant chemotherapy stop at 3 months instead of 6 — and for whom?
shelves.mesh: Colonic Neoplasms · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Capecitabine · Fluorouracil · Oxaliplatin · Disease-Free Survival
shelves.balance: Stated first, because it is the headline the collaboration itself reported: in 12,834 patients, noninferiority of 3 months was NOT confirmed overall (HR 1.07 against a prespecified 1.12 margin). Inside that null, the split that governs practice: CAPOX 3 months was noninferior (HR 0.95), FOLFOX was not (HR 1.16); low-risk (T1–3N1) disease was noninferior (HR 1.01), high-risk was not (HR 1.12, 6 months superior). The reason the question was worth asking is toxicity: significant neuropathy roughly halves with the shorter course (SCOT: grade ≥2 in 25% vs 58%). With a decade of follow-up, SCOT's final analysis (J Clin Oncol 2026, Card 4) proved noninferiority for overall survival itself — 82.4% in both arms — with the same CAPOX/FOLFOX split. Developer-approved Nov 7, 2026.

cards.headline: IDEA pooled analysis (Grothey 2018): noninferiority of 3 months was NOT confirmed overall — HR 1.07 against a 1.12 margin, stated first
cards.summary: 12,834 patients with stage III colon cancer in six pooled phase 3 trials, 3 vs 6 months of FOLFOX or CAPOX: 3-year disease-free survival 74.6% vs 75.5%; HR 1.07 [1.00–1.15] — the upper limit crossed the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.12 in the wrong direction for a claim: noninferiority NOT confirmed in the overall population . The split inside: CAPOX HR 0.95 [0.85–1.06] — noninferior; FOLFOX HR 1.16 [1.06–1.26] — not . By risk: low-risk (T1–3, N1) HR 1.01 [0.90–1.12] — noninferior (3-year DFS 83.1% vs 83.3%); high-risk (T4 and/or N2) HR 1.12 [1.03–1.23] — 6 months superior (64.4% vs 62.7%).
cards.type: Prospective, preplanned pooled analysis of six randomized phase 3 trials (IDEA collaboration), N Engl J Med 2018. The record carries no registry databank entry — the six component trials carry their own registrations.
cards.people: 12,834 patients with stage III colon cancer in 12 countries, treated at their physician's discretion with FOLFOX or CAPOX; median follow-up 39 months at this analysis; 3,263 events of recurrence or death reported. The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: After 3,263 events, the noninferiority of 3 months vs 6 months was not confirmed in the overall population (HR 1.07 [1.00–1.15]; the noninferiority margin was an upper confidence limit of 1.12). Noninferiority of the shorter regimen was seen for CAPOX (HR 0.95 [0.85–1.06]) but not for FOLFOX (HR 1.16 [1.06–1.26]). In an exploratory combined-regimen analysis, 3 months was noninferior among patients with T1, T2, or T3 and N1 cancers (3-year DFS 83.1% vs 83.3%; HR 1.01 [0.90–1.12]), while among patients with T4, N2, or both, 6 months was superior (64.4% vs 62.7%; HR 1.12 [1.03–1.23]; P=0.01 for superiority).
cards.watchOut: This is a noninferiority question, and 'not significantly different' would not have answered it — the trial declared its margin (1.12) in advance and the overall result missed it (see the Noninferiority trial definition). Practice settled where the split points: 3 months of CAPOX for most, 6 months of FOLFOX (or high-risk disease) where the longer course earned it. The regimen split was not itself randomized — doctors chose FOLFOX or CAPOX — so the CAPOX/FOLFOX contrast carries a selection caution the duration contrast does not.
cards.source: Grothey A et al.; IDEA Collaboration. Duration of adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III colon cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;378:1177–1188. PMID 29590544. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1713709

cards.headline: IDEA final results (André 2020): at 5 years, overall survival 82.4% vs 82.8% (HR 1.02) — noninferiority still not formally shown, absolute gap 0.4 points
cards.summary: With median follow-up of 72.3 months and 2,584 deaths among 12,835 patients, 5-year overall survival was 82.4% with 3 months vs 82.8% with 6 months — HR 1.02 [0.95–1.11] ; noninferiority for overall survival was not formally shown (adjusted P=0.058 against the margin). The authors' own framing, stated with the numbers: the absolute 0.4-percentage-point difference should be placed in clinical context, and the survival results support 3 months of CAPOX for most patients with stage III colon cancer.
cards.type: Final results of the prospective pooled analysis of six randomized phase 3 trials (IDEA collaboration), Lancet Oncol 2020
cards.people: 12,835 patients with stage III colon cancer aged at least 18, performance status 0–1, recruited 2007–2015 across 12 countries in the CALGB/SWOG 80702, IDEA France, SCOT, ACHIEVE, TOSCA, and HORG trials. The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: With a median follow-up of 72.3 months, 2,584 deaths were observed among 12,835 patients. Five-year overall survival was 82.4% [81.4–83.3] with 3 months of therapy and 82.8% [81.8–83.8] with 6 months (HR 1.02 [0.95–1.11]; noninferiority FDR-adjusted P=0.058). The authors conclude that noninferiority of 3 vs 6 months was not confirmed in terms of overall survival, but that the absolute 0.4% difference in 5-year overall survival should be placed in clinical context, and that the results support 3 months of adjuvant CAPOX for most patients.
cards.watchOut: Formally 'not proven noninferior' and practically 'a 0.4-point survival difference' are both true, and the shelf states both — the first is a statement about a margin declared in advance, the second is the number a patient is actually choosing around, against roughly half the cumulative oxaliplatin neurotoxicity (Reference 3).

cards.headline: SCOT (Iveson 2018): within IDEA's largest trial, 3 months WAS noninferior for disease-free survival — and grade ≥2 neuropathy was 25% vs 58%
cards.summary: 6,088 patients with high-risk stage II or stage III colorectal cancer: 3-year disease-free survival 76.7% vs 77.1% — HR 1.01 [0.91–1.11] , significantly below SCOT's own noninferiority margin of 1.13 (P=0.012 for noninferiority). The toxicity ledger that drives the whole question: peripheral neuropathy of grade 2 or worse in 25% (103 of 420 assessed) on 3 months vs 58% (237 of 409) on 6 months — long-lasting, and associated with worse quality of life. Serious adverse events 492 vs 606 reports; treatment-related deaths 16 in each group.
cards.type: Randomized phase 3 noninferiority trial (SCOT), Lancet Oncol 2018. Registry verified against the record's own databank: ISRCTN59757862.
cards.people: 6,088 patients randomized at 244 centers (3,044 per group); intended treatment FOLFOX in 1,981 and CAPOX in 4,107. The record does not state a mean age or sex split. The neuropathy figures come from the subset with safety data (420 and 409 patients assessed).
cards.result: Three-year disease-free survival was 76.7% [75.1–78.2] in the 3-month group and 77.1% [75.6–78.6] in the 6-month group (HR 1.006 [0.909–1.114]; test for noninferiority P=0.012, against a margin HR of 1.13). Peripheral neuropathy of grade 2 or worse was more common in the 6-month group (237 [58%] of 409 patients in the safety subset) than in the 3-month group (103 [25%] of 420), was long-lasting, and was associated with worse quality of life. There were 1,098 serious adverse events (492 reports in the 3-month group, 606 in the 6-month group) and 32 treatment-related deaths (16 in each group).
cards.watchOut: SCOT and the pooled IDEA analysis (Reference 1) are not contradicting each other: SCOT tested against a wider margin (1.13) in its own population and passed; the pooled analysis tested against 1.12 across six trials and missed overall, passing for CAPOX. The IDEA brief's neurotoxicity summary — roughly 14% vs 35% grade ≥2 on CAPOX across the pooled trials — is the same ledger as SCOT's 25% vs 58% (SCOT assessed a safety subset with scheduled neuropathy follow-up, hence higher rates in both arms): whichever cut is used, halving treatment roughly halves significant neuropathy.
cards.source: Iveson TJ et al. 3 versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine combination therapy for colorectal cancer (SCOT): an international, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial. Lancet Oncol. 2018;19:562–578. PMID 29611518 · ISRCTN59757862 (verified against the record's own databank). DOI 10.1016/S1470-2045(18)30093-7

cards.headline: SCOT final analysis (Iveson, J Clin Oncol 2026 — DATED 2026): 5-year overall survival 82.4% in BOTH arms, HR 0.96 — noninferiority for survival proven
cards.summary: With 38 further months of follow-up (median 113 months; 1,255 deaths), SCOT's final analysis reports 5-year overall survival of 82.4% with 3 months and 82.4% with 6 months — HR 0.96 [0.86–1.07] (confidence interval as stated in the record), and states that noninferiority of 3 months was proven for overall survival , including in 1,087 patients with rectal cancer. The regimen dependence persisted: noninferiority shown for CAPOX, not for FOLFOX. This card is dated 2026, as the shelf requires — it is the newest evidence in this batch.
cards.type: Final analysis of a randomized phase 3 noninferiority trial (SCOT), J Clin Oncol 2026
cards.people: 6,088 patients with high-risk stage II and stage III colorectal cancer, assigned 1:1 to 3 or 6 months of CAPOX or FOLFOX (regimen chosen before randomization). The record — published January 2026 — carries no MeSH terms yet and no databank entry; the trial's registration, ISRCTN59757862, is named in the record's abstract and verified on the 2018 SCOT record (Reference 3). The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: With a median of 113 months of follow-up and 1,255 overall-survival events, 5-year overall survival for 3 vs 6 months of treatment was 82.4% in both groups (hazard ratio 0.96), proving noninferiority of 3 months of treatment. Noninferiority for overall survival was also shown in 1,087 patients with rectal cancer. The duration effect was regimen-dependent, with noninferiority shown for CAPOX but not for FOLFOX. The authors conclude that 3 months of adjuvant treatment should be recommended for most patients.
cards.watchOut: SCOT's final verdict is stronger than the pooled IDEA verdict (References 1–2) because SCOT alone reached its survival margin with a decade of follow-up — but note the recurring boundary in every cut of these data: the answer is regimen-split. 'Three months is enough' is a CAPOX sentence; for FOLFOX, no analysis on this shelf has proven it.
cards.source: Iveson T et al. Three versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy for colorectal cancer: final results of SCOT — an international, randomized, phase III, noninferiority trial. J Clin Oncol. 2026;44:534–539. PMID 41512219. DOI 10.1200/JCO-25-00621. The record carries no MeSH terms (none assigned yet at verification).

shelves.title: First-line immunotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer: survival proven — with the benefit concentrated where PD-L1 is high
shelves.question: In advanced NSCLC without targetable mutations, does first-line immunotherapy prolong survival — and in whom?
shelves.mesh: Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Lung Neoplasms · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Programmed Cell Death 1 Receptor · B7-H1 Antigen · Immunotherapy
shelves.balance: Three independent drug families won the same argument: adding a checkpoint inhibitor to first-line chemotherapy (or, at high PD-L1, giving it alone) prolongs survival in metastatic NSCLC — KEYNOTE-189 5-year survival 19.4% vs 11.3% (HR 0.60), KEYNOTE-407 in squamous disease (HR 0.64 at its primary report), KEYNOTE-024 monotherapy at PD-L1 ≥50% (5-year survival 31.9% vs 16.3%), CheckMate 9LA (HR 0.69), IMpower150 (HR 0.78). The survival gaps persisted despite 57–66% crossover from the control arms. The shelf's fence is Card 4: pembrolizumab monotherapy at PD-L1 1–49% produced HR 0.92 and no significant benefit — the class's benefits concentrate at high PD-L1, and below it the chemotherapy combinations carry the evidence. Every hazard ratio on this shelf is a relative measure, stated with its absolute rates. Developer-approved Nov 7, 2026.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-189: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy in nonsquamous NSCLC — 5-year survival 19.4% vs 11.3%, HR 0.60, achieved despite 57.3% effective crossover
cards.summary: 616 patients with untreated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations, pembrolizumab + pemetrexed-platinum vs placebo + pemetrexed-platinum. At the primary report, 12-month survival was 69.2% vs 49.4% (HR 0.49, relative). At 5 years (median follow-up 64.6 months): overall survival 19.4% vs 11.3% — HR 0.60 [0.50–0.72], relative , and progression-free survival HR 0.50. The control arm's survival was itself lifted by crossover: the effective crossover rate to immunotherapy was 57.3% — the HR 0.60 was earned against a control group most of whom eventually got the drug class.
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial (KEYNOTE-189), N Engl J Med 2018; 5-year outcomes, J Clin Oncol 2023. Registry verified against the records' own databank: NCT02578680.
cards.people: 616 patients randomly assigned 2:1 (410 pembrolizumab-combination, 206 placebo-combination). The records do not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: Primary report (median follow-up 10.5 months): estimated 12-month overall survival 69.2% [64.1–73.8] with the pembrolizumab combination vs 49.4% [42.1–56.2] with placebo (HR for death 0.49 [0.38–0.64]; P<0.001); median progression-free survival 8.8 vs 4.9 months (HR 0.52). Five-year update: HR for overall survival 0.60 [0.50–0.72] and for progression-free survival 0.50 [0.42–0.60]; 5-year overall-survival rates 19.4% vs 11.3%. Benefit was seen across PD-L1 categories. Grade ≥3 adverse events at the primary report: 67.2% vs 65.8%.
cards.watchOut: Two disciplines: survival in the placebo arm is not 'chemotherapy alone' survival — with 57.3% effective crossover it is substantially 'chemotherapy, then immunotherapy' survival, which makes the persistent HR 0.60 more, not less, persuasive. And in the pooled PD-L1–negative (TPS <1%) population across the pembrolizumab trials, the survival HR was 0.64 — a pooled, cross-trial cut, labeled as such; the individual trials were not powered for that stratum.
cards.source: Gandhi L et al. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;378:2078–2092. PMID 29658856 · NCT02578680 (verified against the record's own databank). DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1801005. Five-year outcomes: Garassino MC et al. J Clin Oncol. 2023;41:1992–1998. PMID 36809080.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-407: pembrolizumab + chemotherapy in SQUAMOUS NSCLC — median survival 15.9 vs 11.3 months, HR 0.64 at the primary report
cards.summary: 559 patients with untreated metastatic squamous NSCLC, pembrolizumab + carboplatin-taxane vs placebo + carboplatin-taxane: median overall survival 15.9 vs 11.3 months — HR 0.64 [0.49–0.85], relative; P<0.001 ; median progression-free survival 6.4 vs 4.8 months (HR 0.56). The survival benefit was consistent regardless of PD-L1 expression level. Discontinuation for adverse events was more frequent with pembrolizumab (13.3% vs 6.4%); grade ≥3 adverse events were similar (69.8% vs 68.2%).
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial (KEYNOTE-407), N Engl J Med 2018. Registry verified against the record's own databank: NCT02775435.
cards.people: 559 patients with untreated metastatic squamous NSCLC, randomized 1:1; all received carboplatin plus paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel for 4 cycles, with pembrolizumab or placebo for up to 35 cycles. The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: After a median follow-up of 7.8 months, median overall survival was 15.9 months [13.2 to not reached] in the pembrolizumab-combination group and 11.3 months [9.5–14.8] in the placebo-combination group (HR for death 0.64 [0.49–0.85]; P<0.001). Median progression-free survival was 6.4 vs 4.8 months (HR 0.56 [0.45–0.70]). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 69.8% vs 68.2%; discontinuation because of adverse events was more frequent in the pembrolizumab group (13.3% vs 6.4%).
cards.watchOut: This card states the trial's primary report, its record-verified numbers. Later updated analyses of KEYNOTE-407 report a survival HR of about 0.71 with longer follow-up — the attenuation expected as crossover accumulates; the shelf's claim does not depend on which cut is quoted, and the primary record is the one carded.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-024: pembrolizumab alone when PD-L1 is ≥50% — 5-year survival 31.9% vs 16.3%
cards.summary: 305 patients with untreated metastatic NSCLC, PD-L1 tumor proportion score ≥50%, no EGFR/ALK alterations: pembrolizumab monotherapy vs platinum chemotherapy. At 5 years: overall survival 31.9% vs 16.3% — median 26.3 vs 13.4 months; HR 0.62 [0.48–0.81], relative . Among chemotherapy patients, 99 received subsequent anti-PD-(L)1 therapy — an effective crossover rate of 66.0% — so, as in KEYNOTE-189, the long-term gap survived the control arm getting the drug later. Of 39 patients who completed 2 years of pembrolizumab, 82.1% were still alive at about 5 years.
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (KEYNOTE-024), N Engl J Med 2016; five-year outcomes, J Clin Oncol 2021. Registry verified against the records' own databank: NCT02142738.
cards.people: 305 patients randomly assigned (154 pembrolizumab, 151 chemotherapy) with PD-L1 tumor proportion score ≥50% and no sensitizing EGFR or ALK alterations. The records do not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: Five-year report: median overall survival 26.3 months [18.3–40.4] with pembrolizumab vs 13.4 months [9.4–18.3] with chemotherapy (HR 0.62 [0.48–0.81]); Kaplan–Meier 5-year overall-survival rates 31.9% vs 16.3%. Among patients initially assigned to chemotherapy, 99 received subsequent anti-PD-1 or PD-L1 therapy (66.0% effective crossover). Thirty-nine patients received 35 cycles (about 2 years) of pembrolizumab, 82.1% of whom were alive at data cutoff. Toxicity did not increase with longer treatment exposure.
cards.watchOut: This is the high-PD-L1 pole of the shelf's gradient — the stratum where monotherapy (no chemotherapy at all) doubles 5-year survival. Compare Card 4 before generalizing it downward: the same drug, the same design, at PD-L1 1–49% produced no significant survival benefit.

cards.headline: The fence — KEYNOTE-042: at PD-L1 1–49%, pembrolizumab monotherapy's survival HR was 0.92 and NOT significant; the benefit concentrates at high PD-L1
cards.summary: 1,274 patients with PD-L1 tumor proportion score ≥1%: pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy improved survival in the prespecified ≥50% stratum (HR 0.69), ≥20% (HR 0.77), and ≥1% (HR 0.81) populations — a gradient driven by the high expressors. In the exploratory PD-L1 1–49% population, the survival HR was 0.92 — not significant . Stated as this shelf's fence: pembrolizumab monotherapy's proven home is PD-L1 ≥50% (Reference 3); below that, the chemotherapy combinations (References 1–2) carry the evidence, not monotherapy.
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (KEYNOTE-042), Lancet 2019. Registry verified against the record's own databank: NCT02220894.
cards.people: 1,274 patients (902 men, 372 women; median age 63 years [IQR 57–69]) with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, PD-L1 TPS ≥1%, no sensitizing EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, at 213 centers in 32 countries; 599 (47%) had TPS ≥50% and 818 (64%) TPS ≥20%.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer with pembrolizumab in all three prespecified TPS populations (≥50%: HR 0.69 [0.56–0.85], P=0.0003; ≥20%: HR 0.77 [0.64–0.92], P=0.0020; ≥1%: HR 0.81 [0.71–0.93], P=0.0018), with median survival 20.0 vs 12.2, 17.7 vs 13.0, and 16.7 vs 12.1 months respectively. In the exploratory analysis of patients with TPS 1–49%, the overall-survival hazard ratio was 0.92 and not significant. Treatment-related grade ≥3 adverse events: 18% with pembrolizumab vs 41% with chemotherapy; treatment-related deaths 13 (2%) vs 14 (2%).
cards.watchOut: The three 'positive' populations are nested — ≥1% contains ≥20% contains ≥50% — so the ≥1% significance is inherited from the high expressors inside it, which is precisely why the disjoint 1–49% cut is the honest one to state. A nested-population win is not a low-PD-L1 win (see the Subgroup analysis definition).

cards.headline: CheckMate 9LA: nivolumab + ipilimumab with just two cycles of chemotherapy — survival HR 0.69
cards.summary: 719 patients with treatment-naive stage IV or recurrent NSCLC: nivolumab + ipilimumab plus two cycles of platinum-doublet chemotherapy vs four cycles of chemotherapy alone. Median overall survival 14.1 vs 10.7 months — HR 0.69 [0.55–0.87], relative; P=0.00065 at the prespecified interim analysis; with longer follow-up, 15.6 vs 10.9 months (HR 0.66). Serious treatment-related adverse events 30% vs 18%; treatment-related deaths 2% in each group (7 vs 6 patients). A class card: the dual-checkpoint-plus-brief-chemotherapy route reaches the same destination as the pembrolizumab combinations.
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (CheckMate 9LA), Lancet Oncol 2021. Registry verified against the record's own databank: NCT03215706.
cards.people: 719 patients randomly assigned (361 combination, 358 chemotherapy alone) of 1,150 enrolled, at 103 hospitals in 19 countries; adults with treatment-naive stage IV or recurrent NSCLC and performance status 0–1. The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: At the preplanned interim analysis (median follow-up 9.7 months), overall survival was significantly longer in the experimental group (median 14.1 months [13.2–16.2] vs 10.7 months [9.5–12.4]; HR 0.69 [96.71% CI 0.55–0.87]; P=0.00065). With 3.5 months' longer follow-up, median overall survival was 15.6 vs 10.9 months (HR 0.66 [0.55–0.80]). Serious treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30% vs 18%; seven (2%) treatment-related deaths in the experimental group and six (2%) in the control group.
cards.watchOut: The design idea is chemotherapy as a bridge, not a backbone — two cycles to cover the weeks before immunotherapy acts, then dual checkpoint blockade alone. It is carded as a class card beside the pembrolizumab trials: separate sponsor, separate drugs, same survival shape, which is what makes the class claim sturdier than any single trial.

cards.headline: IMpower150: atezolizumab + bevacizumab + chemotherapy in nonsquamous NSCLC — median survival 19.2 vs 14.7 months, HR 0.78
cards.summary: In the wild-type population (EGFR/ALK alterations excluded), 692 patients: atezolizumab + bevacizumab + carboplatin-paclitaxel (ABCP) vs bevacizumab + chemotherapy (BCP): median overall survival 19.2 vs 14.7 months — HR 0.78 [0.64–0.96], relative; P=0.02 ; median progression-free survival 8.3 vs 6.8 months (HR 0.62). Progression-free-survival benefit also appeared in the low-or-negative PD-L1 and liver-metastases subgroups — stated as subgroup findings of a positive trial, not separate proofs.
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (IMpower150), N Engl J Med 2018. Registry verified against the record's own databank: NCT02366143.
cards.people: Patients with metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC and no previous chemotherapy; the survival comparison covers the wild-type population — 356 assigned to ABCP and 336 to BCP. The record does not state a mean age or sex split.
cards.result: In the wild-type population, median progression-free survival was 8.3 vs 6.8 months (HR for progression or death 0.62 [0.52–0.74]; P<0.001), and median overall survival was 19.2 vs 14.7 months (HR for death 0.78 [0.64–0.96]; P=0.02). Progression-free survival was also longer with ABCP in the entire intention-to-treat population and among patients with low or negative PD-L1 expression, low effector T-cell gene-signature expression, and liver metastases. The safety profile was consistent with the known risks of the individual medicines.
cards.watchOut: The four-drug regimen is the most complex on this shelf, and its HR (0.78) is the most modest — bevacizumab in both arms means this trial isolates atezolizumab's addition to an already-active backbone. It earns its card as the third independent first-line immunotherapy family with a survival win, and as the shelf's reminder that effect sizes shrink as the control arm gets stronger.

shelves.title: PARP inhibitor maintenance in ovarian cancer: the benefit follows the biomarker — BRCA, then HRD, then a survival null
shelves.question: In newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer, does PARP-inhibitor maintenance after platinum chemotherapy help — and in whom?
shelves.mesh: Ovarian Neoplasms · Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerase Inhibitors · Maintenance Chemotherapy · Genes, BRCA1 · Genes, BRCA2 · Bevacizumab
shelves.balance: The gradient is this shelf's point, and every card is placed on it. Top: BRCA-mutated disease, where olaparib produced the class's largest effects — PFS HR 0.30 and, at 7 years, 67.0% vs 46.5% alive (SOLO-1). Middle: HRD-positive disease, where niraparib's PFS HR was 0.43 and olaparib-plus-bevacizumab's survival HR 0.62 (PRIMA; PAOLA-1). Bottom: HRD-negative disease, where the PFS effect shrinks (HR 0.68) and no survival benefit has been shown — graded POSSIBLE/disfavored inside this shelf. Stated where it belongs, on Card 2: PRIMA's final overall survival was HR 1.01 — null , and the FDA restricted niraparib's first-line indication to HRD-positive tumors. PAOLA-1's overall survival was likewise null overall (HR 0.92, NS) — the survival claims on this shelf live inside the biomarker strata, labeled as such. Developer-approved Nov 7, 2026.

cards.headline: SOLO-1: olaparib maintenance in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer — PFS HR 0.30; at 7 years, 67.0% vs 46.5% alive (OS HR 0.55, descriptive)
cards.summary: 391 women with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer and a BRCA1/2 mutation, in response after platinum chemotherapy: olaparib vs placebo for up to 2 years. Progression-free survival: HR 0.30 [0.23–0.41], relative — freedom from progression or death at 3 years 60% vs 27%. At 7 years (a prespecified descriptive analysis): 67.0% vs 46.5% alive — OS HR 0.55 [0.40–0.76] ; alive without a first subsequent treatment 45.3% vs 20.6%. The OS P value (0.0004) did not cross the prespecified significance threshold (P<0.0001) — stated, because 'clinically meaningful, not formally significant by the trial's own rule' is the accurate label.
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial (SOLO-1/GOG 3004), N Engl J Med 2018; 7-year overall-survival follow-up, J Clin Oncol 2023. Registry verified against the records' own databank: NCT01844986.
cards.people: 391 patients randomized 2:1 (260 olaparib, 131 placebo) with FIGO stage III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid cancer and a germline (388) or somatic (2) BRCA1/2 mutation, in complete or partial response after platinum chemotherapy. The records do not state a mean age.
cards.result: Primary analysis (median follow-up 41 months): the risk of disease progression or death was 70% lower in relative terms with olaparib (HR 0.30 [0.23–0.41]; P<0.001); the 3-year rate of freedom from progression and death was 60% vs 27%. Seven-year follow-up: HR for overall survival 0.55 [0.40–0.76]; P=0.0004, against a prespecified threshold of P<0.0001 to declare statistical significance; 67.0% of olaparib patients vs 46.5% of placebo patients were alive, and 45.3% vs 20.6% were alive without having received a first subsequent treatment. Myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia remained uncommon and new primary malignancies balanced.
cards.watchOut: The BRCA-mutated stratum is the top of this shelf's biomarker gradient — the largest PARP effect in the library. The threshold discipline on the OS analysis matters for how agents should quote it: HR 0.55 with a 20-point absolute survival gap at 7 years can be described as a large, clinically meaningful difference; calling it 'statistically proven' would contradict the trial's own prespecified rule.
cards.source: Moore K et al. Maintenance olaparib in patients with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;379:2495–2505. PMID 30345884 · NCT01844986 (verified against the record's own databank). DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1810858. Seven-year overall survival: DiSilvestro P et al. J Clin Oncol. 2023;41:609–617. PMID 36082969. DOI 10.1200/JCO.22.01549

cards.headline: PRIMA: niraparib's PFS gradient — HR 0.43 (HRD-positive) / 0.62 (overall) / 0.68 (HRD-negative) — and final overall survival HR 1.01, stated
cards.summary: 733 women with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer in response after platinum chemotherapy, niraparib vs placebo. Progression-free survival: HRD-positive HR 0.43 [0.31–0.59] (median 21.9 vs 10.4 months); overall HR 0.62 [0.50–0.76] (13.8 vs 8.2 months); HRD-negative (homologous-recombination-proficient) HR 0.68 — all relative. The final overall-survival analysis (median follow-up 73.9 months) is stated on the same card: OS HR 1.01 [0.84–1.23], P=0.88 — no survival difference (HRD-positive 0.95; HR-proficient 0.93). The FDA subsequently restricted niraparib's first-line maintenance indication to HRD-positive disease.
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial (PRIMA/ENGOT-OV26/GOG-3012), N Engl J Med 2019; final overall-survival analysis, Ann Oncol 2024. Registry verified against the primary record's own databank: NCT02655016.
cards.people: 733 patients randomized 2:1 (487 niraparib, 246 placebo) with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer at high risk of recurrence, in response to first-line platinum chemotherapy; 373 (50.9%) had homologous-recombination-deficient tumors. The records do not state a mean age.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer with niraparib in the HRD population (median 21.9 vs 10.4 months; HR 0.43 [0.31–0.59]; P<0.001) and in the overall population (13.8 vs 8.2 months; HR 0.62 [0.50–0.76]; P<0.001). Grade ≥3 adverse events at the primary report: anemia 31.0%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%; no treatment-related deaths. Final overall survival: HR 1.01 [0.84–1.23] in the overall population (P=0.8834), 0.95 [0.70–1.29] in the HRD population, and 0.93 [0.69–1.26] in the HR-proficient population; 5-year progression-free rates still favored niraparib (overall 22% vs 12%; HRD 35% vs 16%). Subsequent PARP therapy was received by 37.8% of placebo patients overall and 48.4% in the HRD population. MDS/AML incidence: 2.3% vs 1.6%.
cards.watchOut: PRIMA is the gradient's middle made honest: a real progression-free benefit that shrinks as the biomarker fades, and a final survival analysis at 1.01 — the null stated, not buried. Crossover (nearly half the HRD placebo group later got a PARP inhibitor) blurs survival in every trial on this shelf; it does not manufacture a 1.01 out of a real survival effect of SOLO-1's size. The regulatory consequence followed the gradient: the US first-line indication was restricted to HRD-positive tumors.
cards.source: González-Martín A et al. Niraparib in patients with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer. N Engl J Med. 2019;381:2391–2402. PMID 31562799 · NCT02655016 (verified against the record's own databank). DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1910962. Final overall survival: Monk BJ et al. Ann Oncol. 2024;35:981–992. PMID 39284381. DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2024.08.2241

cards.headline: PAOLA-1: olaparib + bevacizumab — overall survival HR 0.92 NS overall; HRD-positive HR 0.62 (5-year survival 65.5% vs 48.4%)
cards.summary: 806 women with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer in response after platinum chemotherapy plus bevacizumab: olaparib + bevacizumab vs placebo + bevacizumab. Final overall survival: overall HR 0.92 [0.76–1.12], P=0.41 — not significant (median 56.5 vs 51.6 months), stated first. In the prespecified exploratory HRD-positive population: OS HR 0.62 [0.45–0.85], relative; 5-year survival 65.5% vs 48.4% ; updated 5-year progression-free rates 46.1% vs 19.2% (HR 0.41). Nearly half the placebo arm (45.7%) later received a PARP inhibitor. The gradient again: where the biomarker is absent, this shelf has no proven maintenance benefit to offer.
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial (PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25), N Engl J Med 2019; final overall-survival analysis, Ann Oncol 2023. Registry verified against the primary record's own databank: NCT02477644.
cards.people: 806 patients randomized 2:1 to olaparib plus bevacizumab or placebo plus bevacizumab, in clinical response after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus bevacizumab. The records do not state a mean age.
cards.result: After median follow-up of about 62 months, median overall survival was 56.5 vs 51.6 months in the intention-to-treat population (HR 0.92 [0.76–1.12]; P=0.4118). In the HRD-positive population, overall survival was longer with olaparib plus bevacizumab (HR 0.62 [0.45–0.85]; 5-year overall-survival rate 65.5% vs 48.4%), and updated progression-free survival also favored the combination (HR 0.41 [0.32–0.54]; 5-year PFS 46.1% vs 19.2%). Subsequent PARP therapy was received by 19.6% of the olaparib arm vs 45.7% of the placebo arm. MDS, AML, aplastic anemia, and new primary malignancies remained uncommon and balanced.
cards.watchOut: The HRD-positive survival analysis is labeled prespecified-but-exploratory in the paper itself, and the shelf keeps that label — it is strong, coherent with SOLO-1 and PRIMA's PFS gradient, and still a stratum analysis inside an overall-null trial. The HRD-negative stratum of this shelf is graded POSSIBLE/disfavored in the shelf stamp: no trial here shows a survival benefit without the biomarker, and PRIMA's HRD-negative PFS effect (HR 0.68) never converted to survival.
