cards.headline: Donovan 2016 (NEJM), ProtecT patient-reported outcomes: surgery worst for continence and sexual function throughout; radiotherapy worst early for bowel — no differences in anxiety, depression or general quality of life
cards.summary: Patient-reported outcomes in the 1,643 ProtecT participants, questionnaires before diagnosis, at 6 and 12 months, then annually (completion >85% for most measures; complete 6-year data analysed). Prostatectomy had the greatest negative effect on sexual function and urinary continence, with partial recovery but persistently worse scores than the other groups throughout. Radiotherapy's sexual-function effect peaked at 6 months then partly recovered; it had little effect on continence; bowel function was worse at 6 months then recovered except for increasing bloody stools. Function declined gradually on monitoring. No significant differences in anxiety, depression, or general or cancer-related quality of life.
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcomes analysis of a randomised trial (ProtecT), N Engl J Med 2016. Registries verified against the record's own databank/abstract: ISRCTN20141297 · NCT02044172.
cards.people: 1,643 randomised men completing validated urinary, bowel and sexual function and quality-of-life instruments over 6 years. The record's abstract does not print a mean age.
cards.result: Qualitative pattern as printed in the record: prostatectomy — greatest and persistent harm to sexual function and urinary continence; radiotherapy — early bowel harm and rising bloody stools, transient voiding/nocturia effects mostly recovered by 12 months; monitoring — gradual decline in sexual and urinary function. No significant between-group differences in anxiety, depression, general health-related or cancer-related quality of life. The record's abstract prints no numerical scores, and none are printed here.
cards.watchOut: These are the harms that must travel with Card 1's metastasis numbers in any honest summary: radical treatment trades a halving of metastasis/progression for the functional costs described here, against a background of ~3% cancer mortality in every arm. Numerical scores exist in the full text but are not in the record's abstract; the card does not import them.

cards.headline: Sushentsev 2025 (JAMA Oncol), ProtecT secondary analysis: cribriform-positive disease tripled metastasis risk (HR 3.61) — cribriform-negative men did well on every strategy
cards.summary: Retrospective central pathology review of diagnostic biopsies from 712 ProtecT participants (mean age 62.0 years); 93 (13.1%) were cribriform-positive and 42 (5.9%) developed metastasis over 15 years. Cribriform-positive disease independently raised metastasis risk (HR 3.61 [95% CI 1.60–8.11], P=0.003). Among cribriform-positive men, 15-year cumulative metastasis incidence was 8% with radiotherapy plus neoadjuvant ADT (HR 0.35 [0.16–0.78] versus monitoring), 26% with surgery (HR 0.52 [0.25–1.08], not significant) and 25% with monitoring. Among cribriform-negative men, metastasis incidence was low and did not differ by treatment.
cards.type: Retrospective secondary analysis of a randomised trial (ProtecT), JAMA Oncol 2025 (found in the freshness sweep). Registry verified against the record's own databank: NCT02044172.
cards.people: 712 of the 1,643 ProtecT participants whose diagnostic biopsy slides were available for central review; mean age 62.0 years (SD 5.0); 93 (13.1%) cribriform-positive.
cards.result: Metastasis at 15 years: cribriform status HR 3.61 (95% CI 1.60 to 8.11; P=0.003). Cribriform-positive cumulative incidence: radiotherapy 8%, surgery 26%, monitoring 25%. Cribriform-negative: low incidence, no treatment difference. Surgery versus monitoring in cribriform-positive disease: HR 0.52 (0.25 to 1.08; P=0.09) — not significant.
cards.watchOut: Secondary, retrospective, and based on the 712 of 1,643 men whose slides survived — a selected subset with only 42 metastasis events. It refines who might need treatment; it does not change the randomised headline, and its radiotherapy arm included neoadjuvant ADT, which ProtecT's main comparison also used but which must be named when quoting the 8%.

cards.headline: Synthesis (TIER C): at 15 years the choice is between a ~5-point metastasis excess on monitoring and the functional harms of radical treatment — survival does not decide it
cards.summary: Synthesis of Cards 1–4. Prostate-cancer mortality ~3% and all-cause mortality ~22% at 15 years did not differ between monitoring, surgery and radiotherapy. Radical treatment roughly halved metastases (9.4% to 4.7–5.0%) and progression (25.9% to 10.5–11.0%) and reduced later ADT use; a quarter of monitored men never needed treatment. Functional harms are treatment-specific and durable (Reference 3); cribriform morphology may identify the minority in whom monitoring is riskiest (Card 4, secondary analysis). This shelf is Tier C: it makes mortality claims, and its stamp is proposed for the developer's personal ruling, not bulk approval.
cards.type: Synthesis card — no new study; reads Cards 1–4 together. Tier C.
cards.people: 1,643 randomised men (References 1–3); 712 with reviewed biopsies (Reference 4).
cards.result: 15-year prostate-cancer death: 3.1% / 2.2% / 2.9% (P=0.53). Metastases: 9.4% / 4.7% / 5.0%. Progression: 25.9% / 10.5% / 11.0%. Untreated and alive at 15 years on monitoring: 24.4%.
cards.watchOut: Never present the metastasis advantage without the mortality equivalence and the functional harms in the same breath; and never present the mortality equivalence without the metastasis cost. Each half alone misleads in opposite directions.

shelves.title: Adjuvant bisphosphonates in early breast cancer
shelves.question: Do adjuvant bisphosphonates reduce recurrence and breast-cancer death, and in whom?
shelves.mesh: Bone Density Conservation Agents/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Diphosphonates/therapeutic use · Drug Administration Schedule
shelves.balance: LIKELY — PROPOSED, pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, slow lane — breast-cancer mortality claim): The EBCTCG individual-patient-data meta-analysis found definite benefit only in women who were postmenopausal when treatment began: among 11,767 postmenopausal women, adjuvant bisphosphonates reduced recurrence (rate ratio 0.86), distant recurrence (0.82), bone recurrence (0.72) and breast-cancer mortality (rate ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.73 to 0.93 — a relative reduction), with 10-year breast-cancer mortality of 14.7% on bisphosphonate versus 18.0% on control (a 3.3-percentage-point absolute reduction) and 10-year bone recurrence of 6.6% versus 8.8%. In premenopausal women there was no apparent effect on any outcome, and the overall results across all women were only of borderline significance. This stamp is proposed only and does not take effect without the developer's personal Tier C verdict. Tier C — built Nov 8, 2026 and held for the developer’s personal verdict; no approval stamp is claimed for this shelf.

cards.headline: EBCTCG: adjuvant bisphosphonates cut breast-cancer death only in postmenopausal women — rate ratio 0.82 (relative); 10-year mortality 14.7% vs 18.0%
cards.summary: EBCTCG: across all women the reductions were borderline (recurrence rate ratio 0.94; mortality 0.91); in postmenopausal women, breast-cancer mortality rate ratio 0.82 (relative), 10-year rates 14.7% vs 18.0% — the absolute rates are cross-checked beyond the abstract, and the card discloses exactly that.
cards.people: Individual patient data on 18,766 women with early breast cancer from unconfounded trials randomising between bisphosphonate and control (18,206 [97%] in trials of 2–5 years of bisphosphonate), with median follow-up of 5.6 woman-years, 3,453 first recurrences and 2,106 subsequent deaths; 11,767 women were postmenopausal (natural and artificial menopause combined); the abstract does not state mean age.
cards.result: Across all women, reductions were of only borderline significance: recurrence rate ratio 0.94 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.01), distant recurrence 0.92 (0.85 to 0.99) and breast-cancer mortality 0.91 (0.83 to 0.99), with bone recurrence more definite at 0.83 (0.73 to 0.94). Among premenopausal women, treatment had no apparent effect on any outcome. Among the 11,767 postmenopausal women, reductions were highly significant: recurrence rate ratio 0.86 (0.78 to 0.94), distant recurrence 0.82 (0.74 to 0.92), bone recurrence 0.72 (0.60 to 0.86) and breast-cancer mortality 0.82 (0.73 to 0.93; 2p=0.002) — all relative figures. At 10 years in postmenopausal women, breast-cancer mortality was 14.7% with bisphosphonate versus 18.0% without (absolute reduction 3.3 percentage points) and bone recurrence was 6.6% versus 8.8%. No differences were seen in non-breast-cancer mortality, and bone fractures were reduced overall (rate ratio 0.85, 0.75 to 0.97).
cards.watchOut: Tier C: this card carries a breast-cancer mortality claim and the shelf's stamp is proposed pending the developer's personal verdict. The benefit is a postmenopausal-subgroup finding — menopausal status is the primary subgroup of the analysis, heterogeneity of the bone-recurrence benefit by menopausal status was only barely significant (2p=0.06 for trend), and the all-women results were borderline. The 10-year absolute rates are the published analysis's own 10-year rates, reproduced identically in the Lancet commentary on the paper and the US National Cancer Institute's summary of the same analysis; they do not appear in the PubMed abstract, which reports rate ratios only — see the build summary's gate note.
cards.source: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group (EBCTCG). Adjuvant bisphosphonate treatment in early breast cancer: meta-analyses of individual patient data from randomised trials. Lancet. 2015 Oct 3;386(10001):1353-1361. PMID: 26211824. Registry ID: none in the record's databank fields — this is a collaborative meta-analysis of trials, not a single trial.

cards.headline: Synthesis: a real postmenopausal benefit, proposed as LIKELY — and fenced to Tier C until the developer rules
cards.summary: A real postmenopausal benefit, fenced to postmenopausal women in the same sentence, always — Tier C, proposed LIKELY.
cards.people: Synthesis of the card above: one individual-patient-data pooling of 18,766 women (11,767 postmenopausal) across the adjuvant bisphosphonate trials.
cards.result: The claim this shelf may carry, if the developer approves it, is narrow: in women postmenopausal at the start of treatment, 2–5 years of adjuvant bisphosphonate lowered breast-cancer mortality (rate ratio 0.82, relative; 10-year rates 14.7% vs 18.0%) and bone recurrence (rate ratio 0.72, relative; 10-year rates 6.6% vs 8.8%). In premenopausal women there was no apparent effect, and pooling everyone dilutes the result to borderline. The stamp is therefore proposed as LIKELY for the postmenopausal claim only, pending the developer's personal Tier C verdict. One-home note: bisphosphonates for postmenopausal osteoporosis live on Shelf #91 and bisphosphonate drug holidays on Shelf #351 — none of those osteoporosis trials is carded here, and this shelf's cancer question does not change them.

shelves.title: Neuroendocrine tumours: lutetium-177 DOTATATE and everolimus
shelves.question: In progressive midgut neuroendocrine tumours, does peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy beat high-dose octreotide (NETTER-1) — and does everolimus help across GI/lung NET (RADIANT-4)?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Agents/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Delayed-Action Preparations · Disease-Free Survival · Drug Administration Schedule · Gastrointestinal Neoplasms/drug therapy,mortality · Infusions, Intravenous · Kaplan-Meier Estimate
shelves.balance: LIKELY (for progression-free survival; no overall-survival claim is made): NETTER-1 (229 patients) estimated 20-month progression-free survival at 65.2% on 177Lu-Dotatate versus 10.8% on high-dose octreotide LAR, with an 18% versus 3% response rate; RADIANT-4 (302 patients) found median progression-free survival of 11.0 versus 3.9 months on everolimus versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.67 — a relative measure just outside the 0.5–2.0 caution band, printed with its absolute medians). NETTER-1's overall-survival analysis at this report was a prespecified INTERIM look (14 vs 26 deaths, P=0.004) and is reported as interim only — it is not converted into a survival claim on this shelf, which keeps the shelf out of Tier C as drafted.

cards.headline: NETTER-1 2017: 177Lu-Dotatate gave an estimated 65.2% progression-free survival at month 20 versus 10.8% on high-dose octreotide
cards.summary: NETTER-1 2017: 177Lu-Dotatate gave an estimated 65.2% progression-free survival at month 20 vs 10.8% on high-dose octreotide (overall survival reported as interim only — not carded as a claim).
cards.type: Randomised, controlled trial (open-label; radionuclide therapy vs high-dose somatostatin analogue)
cards.people: 229 patients with well-differentiated, metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumours progressing on first-line somatostatin analogue therapy, randomised to 177Lu-Dotatate (116; 7.4 GBq every 8 weeks, four infusions, plus octreotide LAR 30 mg) or octreotide LAR alone at 60 mg every 4 weeks (113). The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: At the primary-analysis data cutoff, the estimated rate of progression-free survival at month 20 was 65.2% (95% confidence interval 50.0 to 76.8) in the 177Lu-Dotatate group and 10.8% (3.5 to 23.0) in the control group. The response rate was 18% versus 3% (P<0.001). In the planned interim analysis of overall survival, 14 deaths had occurred in the 177Lu-Dotatate group and 26 in the control group (P=0.004) — reported by the trialists as preliminary evidence requiring confirmation in the planned final analysis, and carded here as interim only. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia occurred in 1%, 2% and 9% of the 177Lu-Dotatate group versus no patients in the control group, with no evidence of renal toxic effects during the observed period.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the survival numbers are an interim look with few deaths (14 vs 26): the shelf's claim rests on progression-free survival and response, exactly as the trial's primary endpoint framed it.
cards.source: Strosberg J et al. Phase 3 Trial of 177Lu-Dotatate for Midgut Neuroendocrine Tumors. N Engl J Med. 2017;376(2):125-135. PMID: 28076709. Registry IDs: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01578239 and EudraCT 2011-005049-11, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: RADIANT-4 2016: everolimus prolonged median progression-free survival to 11.0 vs 3.9 months across GI and lung NET — relative hazard 0.48
cards.summary: RADIANT-4 2016: everolimus prolonged median progression-free survival to 11.0 vs 3.9 months across GI and lung NET — relative hazard 0.48.
cards.people: 302 adults with advanced, progressive, well-differentiated, non-functional neuroendocrine tumours of lung or gastrointestinal origin, enrolled at 97 centres in 25 countries, randomised 2:1 to everolimus 10 mg daily (205) or placebo (97), both with supportive care. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by central review was 11.0 months (95% confidence interval 9.2 to 13.3) on everolimus versus 3.9 months (3.6 to 7.4) on placebo — described by the authors as a 52% relative reduction in the estimated risk of progression or death (hazard ratio 0.48, 0.35 to 0.67; p<0.00001 — a relative measure, printed with its absolute medians). The first pre-planned interim overall-survival analysis was not statistically significant by its boundary (hazard ratio 0.64, 0.40 to 1.05; one-sided p=0.037 against a significance boundary of 0.0002), and no survival claim is made from it here. Grade 3 or 4 drug-related adverse events included stomatitis (9% vs 0), diarrhoea (7% vs 2%), infections (7% vs 0), anaemia (4% vs 1%), fatigue (3% vs 1%) and hyperglycaemia (3% vs 0).
cards.watchOut: Non-functional tumours of lung or GI origin only — functioning tumours and pancreatic NET are outside this trial's population; and the survival interim did not cross its boundary, so everolimus's claim here is progression delay.

Everolimus for the treatment of advanced, non-functional neuroendocrine tumours of the lung or gastrointestinal tract (RADIANT-4): a randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study. shelves.title: Alpha blockade before pheochromocytoma surgery
shelves.question: Is phenoxybenzamine better than doxazosin for preoperative alpha blockade in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma — the PRESCRIPT head-to-head?
shelves.mesh: Adrenal Gland Neoplasms/surgery · Adrenergic alpha-Antagonists/administration & dosage,therapeutic use · Blood Pressure/drug effects · Doxazosin/administration & dosage,therapeutic use · Phenoxybenzamine/administration & dosage,therapeutic use · Pheochromocytoma/surgery
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE: A single randomised head-to-head trial (PRESCRIPT, 134 patients) found no difference between phenoxybenzamine and doxazosin on its primary endpoint — median cumulative intraoperative time outside blood-pressure targets was 11.1% versus 12.2% (P=0.75) — while a secondary hemodynamic instability score favoured phenoxybenzamine (38.0 vs 50.0; P=0.02), with the trialists themselves stating it could not be established whether that was associated with a better clinical outcome; 30-day cardiovascular complication rates were 8.8% versus 6.9% (P=0.68) and there was no mortality at 30 days in either group. One open-label trial with a null primary and a positive secondary lands at POSSIBLE, and the shelf does not convert the secondary score into a superiority claim.

cards.headline: PRESCRIPT 2020: no difference on the primary endpoint — time outside blood-pressure targets 11.1% vs 12.2% — with a secondary instability score favouring phenoxybenzamine
cards.summary: PRESCRIPT 2020: no difference on the primary endpoint — time outside blood-pressure targets 11.1% vs 12.2% — with a secondary instability score favouring one agent, kept in its place.
cards.people: 134 patients with nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma or sympathetic paraganglioma at nine centres in the Netherlands, pretreated for 2 to 3 weeks before surgery with phenoxybenzamine or doxazosin on a blood-pressure-targeted titration schedule, with standardised intraoperative hemodynamic management. The abstract does not state mean age, sex mix, or the per-group numbers.
cards.result: The primary endpoint — median cumulative intraoperative time outside the blood-pressure target range (systolic above 160 mmHg or mean arterial pressure below 60 mmHg), as a percentage of total procedure time — was 11.1% (interquartile range 4.3 to 20.6) on phenoxybenzamine versus 12.2% (5.3 to 20.2) on doxazosin (P=0.75, r=0.03). The secondary hemodynamic instability score was 38.0 (28.8 to 58.0) on phenoxybenzamine versus 50.0 (35.3 to 63.8) on doxazosin (P=0.02, r=0.20). The 30-day cardiovascular complication rate was 8.8% versus 6.9% (P=0.68), and there was no mortality after 30 days in either group. The authors conclude the duration of blood pressure outside target did not differ, that phenoxybenzamine was more effective at preventing intraoperative hemodynamic instability on the score, and that whether this meant a better clinical outcome could not be established.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, single trial, and the positive finding is a secondary composite score while the primary endpoint and the clinical complication rate are both null — exactly the pattern that must not be upgraded into 'phenoxybenzamine is better'.

shelves.title: How long trastuzumab for early HER2-positive breast cancer: 12 months, 6 months, or shorter?
shelves.question: Is six months of adjuvant trastuzumab non-inferior to twelve (PERSEPHONE) — and what did six months versus twelve show in the French PHARE trial?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy,metabolism · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Drug Administration Schedule · Infusions, Intravenous · Injections, Subcutaneous
shelves.balance: Split: The two non-inferiority trials disagree because they set different margins and enrolled somewhat different patients. PERSEPHONE (4,089 patients; 3% absolute margin for 4-year disease-free survival) showed 6 months non-inferior: 4-year disease-free survival 89.4% vs 89.8% (hazard ratio 1.07; 90% CI 0.93 to 1.24; non-inferiority p=0.011), with fewer severe adverse events (19% vs 24%) and far fewer early stops for cardiotoxicity (3% vs 8%). PHARE (3,380 patients; hazard-ratio margin 1.15) failed to show non-inferiority: 2-year disease-free survival 91.1% vs 93.8% (hazard ratio 1.28; 95% CI 1.05 to 1.56), with fewer cardiac events on 6 months (1.9% vs 5.7%). A shorter course is a defensible, margin-dependent option for lower-risk patients — not a proven equal for everyone. Disease-free-survival claims only; no mortality claim is made. Tier C: no, after evaluating the topic file's candidacy against the brief's mortality/MI/stroke/CV-benefit rule.

cards.headline: PERSEPHONE 2019: 6 months of trastuzumab was non-inferior to 12 — 4-year disease-free survival 89.4% vs 89.8%
cards.summary: PERSEPHONE 2019: 6 months of trastuzumab was non-inferior to 12 — 4-year disease-free survival 89.4% vs 89.8% (by its 3% margin).
cards.type: Open-label, randomised phase 3 non-inferiority trial (152 UK centres)
cards.people: 4,089 patients aged 18 years or older with HER2-positive early breast cancer and a clear indication for chemotherapy, randomised to 6 months (2,044) or 12 months (2,045) of trastuzumab every 3 weeks, given with chemotherapy concurrently or sequentially; median follow-up 5.4 years. The abstract does not state mean age.
cards.result: A disease-free survival event occurred in 265 of 2,043 patients (13%) in the 6-month group and 247 of 2,045 (12%) in the 12-month group. Four-year disease-free survival was 89.4% (95% CI 87.9 to 90.7) with 6 months and 89.8% (88.3 to 91.1) with 12 months (hazard ratio 1.07 [90% CI 0.93 to 1.24], non-inferiority p=0.011, against a 3% absolute margin). Fewer patients on 6 months reported severe adverse events (373 [19%] of 1,939 vs 459 [24%] of 1,894; p=0.0002) or stopped early because of cardiotoxicity (61 [3%] vs 146 [8%]; p<0.0001).
cards.watchOut: Non-inferiority is only as strong as its margin: a 3% absolute margin at 4 years accepts a real, small loss as 'non-inferior', and the hazard ratio's interval reaches 1.24. The authors themselves frame reduced duration as for women at similar (lower) risk of recurrence to those in the trial.
cards.source: Earl HM et al. 6 versus 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab for HER2-positive early breast cancer (PERSEPHONE): 4-year disease-free survival results of a randomised phase 3 non-inferiority trial. cards.headline: PHARE 2013: 6 months failed to show non-inferiority to 12 — 2-year disease-free survival 91.1% vs 93.8%, hazard ratio 1.28
cards.summary: PHARE 2013: 6 months failed to show non-inferiority to 12 — 2-year disease-free survival 91.1% vs 93.8%, hazard ratio 1.28, relative.
cards.type: Open-label, randomised phase 3 non-inferiority trial (156 French centres)
cards.people: 3,384 patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who had received at least four cycles of chemotherapy, breast-axillary surgery, and up to 6 months of trastuzumab before randomisation, assigned to stop at 6 months (1,693) or continue to 12 months (1,691); 1,690 per group were analysed; median follow-up 42.5 months. The abstract does not state mean age.
cards.result: Disease-free survival events numbered 219 in the 6-month group and 175 in the 12-month group. Two-year disease-free survival was 91.1% (95% CI 89.7 to 92.4) with 6 months and 93.8% (92.6 to 94.9) with 12 months (hazard ratio 1.28, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.56; p=0.29 for the non-inferiority test) — non-inferiority against the prespecified hazard-ratio margin of 1.15 was not shown. Cardiac events were more frequent with 12 months (96 [5.7%] of 1,690 vs 32 [1.9%] of 1,690; p<0.0001); 93% of the 128 cardiac events occurred while patients were receiving trastuzumab. The authors concluded 12 months should remain the standard of care.
cards.watchOut: PHARE's hazard-ratio margin (1.15) was much stricter than PERSEPHONE's absolute margin, and patients were randomised only after completing up to 6 months of treatment — the two trials' different verdicts are largely a margin-and-design story, not one trial 'refuting' the other.

cards.headline: Synthesis: a margin-dependent split — shorter trastuzumab is an option for lower-risk patients, not a proven equal
cards.summary: A margin-dependent split — shorter trastuzumab is an option for lower-risk patients, not a proven equal.
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: PERSEPHONE 2019 (4,089 patients) and PHARE 2013 (3,380 analysed).
cards.result: Both trials agree on the trade: 6 months costs, at most, a small disease-free-survival difference and buys substantially less cardiotoxicity and fewer severe adverse events. They disagree only on whether that cost clears their chosen non-inferiority bar (PERSEPHONE's 3% absolute margin: yes; PHARE's 1.15 hazard margin: no). The split stamp records both verdicts in their own terms. Trastuzumab DURATION is this shelf's only question; endocrine and chemotherapy choices for HER2-positive disease live on Shelves #368 and #603 and are not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: Do not quote PERSEPHONE's 'non-inferior' without its 3% margin, or PHARE's failure without its stricter 1.15 margin.

shelves.title: Adjuvant immunotherapy after resected melanoma: pembrolizumab and nivolumab
shelves.question: Does a year of adjuvant anti-PD-1 after resected stage III melanoma improve recurrence-free survival versus placebo (KEYNOTE-054) or versus ipilimumab (CheckMate 238)?
shelves.mesh: Adjuvants, Immunologic/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects,therapeutic use · B7-H1 Antigen/analysis,antagonists & inhibitors · Disease-Free Survival · Infusions, Intravenous · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate
shelves.balance: LIKELY: Two large double-blind phase 3 trials agree that a year of adjuvant anti-PD-1 prolongs recurrence-free survival after resected high-risk melanoma — KEYNOTE-054 vs placebo: 1-year recurrence-free survival 75.4% vs 61.0% (hazard ratio for recurrence or death 0.57; 98.4% CI 0.43 to 0.74); CheckMate 238 vs high-dose ipilimumab: 12-month recurrence-free survival 70.5% vs 60.8% (hazard ratio 0.65; 97.56% CI 0.51 to 0.83), with far fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events than ipilimumab (14.4% vs 45.9%). The claim stamped is recurrence-free survival: overall-survival data were immature at these anchor reports, so no survival claim is made and the shelf is not Tier C, after evaluating the candidacy flagged in the topic file.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-054 2018: adjuvant pembrolizumab lengthened recurrence-free survival vs placebo — 1-year rate 75.4% vs 61.0%
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-054 2018: adjuvant pembrolizumab lengthened recurrence-free survival vs placebo — 1-year rate 75.4% vs 61.0% .
cards.people: 1,019 patients with completely resected stage III melanoma, randomised to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 18 doses (about 1 year; 514) or placebo (505); median follow-up 15 months at this report; 853 patients had PD-L1-positive tumours. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Recurrence-free survival at 1 year was 75.4% (95% CI 71.3 to 78.9) with pembrolizumab vs 61.0% (56.5 to 65.1) with placebo (hazard ratio for recurrence or death 0.57; 98.4% CI 0.43 to 0.74; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates. In the PD-L1-positive subgroup the 1-year rates were 77.1% vs 62.6% (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% CI 0.42 to 0.69; P<0.001). Grade 3–5 adverse events related to the regimen occurred in 14.7% with pembrolizumab vs 3.4% with placebo; there was one treatment-related death (myositis) in the pembrolizumab group.
cards.watchOut: An early report (median follow-up 15 months) of a recurrence endpoint: overall survival was not yet reported, and immune toxicity, while mostly manageable, included a treatment-related death.

cards.summary: CheckMate 238 2017: adjuvant nivolumab beat ipilimumab on recurrence-free survival — 70.5% vs 60.8% at 12 months — with far less high-grade toxicity.

shelves.title: Durvalumab after chemoradiation in stage III lung cancer (PACIFIC)
shelves.question: Does consolidation durvalumab after definitive chemoradiotherapy improve survival in unresectable stage III NSCLC?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects,therapeutic use · B7-H1 Antigen/antagonists & inhibitors · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung/mortality,secondary,therapy · Chemoradiotherapy · Disease-Free Survival · Intention to Treat Analysis
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, an overall-survival claim from a single pivotal trial): In PACIFIC, consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiotherapy prolonged progression-free survival (median 16.8 vs 5.6 months; stratified hazard ratio 0.52) and overall survival (24-month survival 66.3% vs 55.6%; stratified hazard ratio for death 0.68; 99.73% CI 0.47 to 0.997). cards.result: Median progression-free survival (blinded independent central review) was 16.8 months (95% CI 13.0 to 18.1) with durvalumab vs 5.6 months (4.6 to 7.8) with placebo (stratified hazard ratio for disease progression or death 0.52; 95% CI 0.42 to 0.65; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians; 12-month PFS rates were 55.9% vs 35.3% and 18-month rates 44.2% vs 27.0%. The response rate was 28.4% vs 16.0% (P<0.001), and median time to death or distant metastasis was 23.2 vs 14.6 months (P<0.001). Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 29.9% vs 26.1%; the most common was pneumonia (4.4% and 3.8%); discontinuation for adverse events was 15.4% vs 9.8%.

cards.headline: PACIFIC 2018 (overall survival): 24-month survival 66.3% with durvalumab vs 55.6% with placebo; hazard ratio for death 0.68
cards.summary: PACIFIC 2018 (overall survival): 24-month survival 66.3% with durvalumab vs 55.6% with placebo; hazard ratio for death 0.68, relative.
cards.type: Second primary-endpoint report of the same phase 3 randomised trial
cards.people: The same PACIFIC population: 713 randomised, 709 treated (473 durvalumab, 236 placebo); median follow-up 25.2 months at this report. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: The 24-month overall survival rate was 66.3% (95% CI 61.7 to 70.4) in the durvalumab group vs 55.6% (48.9 to 61.8) in the placebo group (two-sided P=0.005); durvalumab significantly prolonged overall survival (stratified hazard ratio for death 0.68; 99.73% CI 0.47 to 0.997; P=0.0025) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates. shelves.title: Adjuvant osimertinib in resected EGFR-mutated lung cancer (ADAURA)
shelves.question: Does three years of adjuvant osimertinib after resection of EGFR-mutated NSCLC improve disease-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Acrylamides/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Aniline Compounds/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung/drug therapy,genetics,mortality,surgery · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · ErbB Receptors/genetics
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, an overall-survival claim from a single pivotal trial): In ADAURA, adjuvant osimertinib produced an unusually large disease-free-survival effect (stage II–IIIA at 24 months: 90% alive and disease-free vs 44%; hazard ratio 0.17) and, in the final survival analysis, higher 5-year overall survival (stage II–IIIA: 85% vs 73%; overall population: 88% vs 78%; hazard ratio for death 0.49 in both). One trial, however dramatic, caps at POSSIBLE — and a survival claim is Tier C.

cards.headline: ADAURA 2020 (disease-free survival): 24-month DFS 90% vs 44% in stage II–IIIA disease; hazard ratio 0.17
cards.summary: ADAURA 2020 (disease-free survival): 24-month DFS 90% vs 44% in stage II–IIIA disease; hazard ratio 0.17, relative. (Tier C — survival claim on the shelf; PROPOSED.)
cards.people: 682 patients with completely resected EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC (stage IB to IIIA), randomised to osimertinib 80 mg once daily (339) or placebo (343) for 3 years. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Among patients with stage II to IIIA disease, 90% (95% CI 84 to 93) in the osimertinib group and 44% (37 to 51) in the placebo group were alive and disease-free at 24 months (overall hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death 0.17; 99.06% CI 0.11 to 0.26; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates, and below the 0.5 threshold the library treats as solid for a single relative measure. In the overall population (stage IB to IIIA), the 24-month rates were 89% vs 52% (hazard ratio 0.20; 99.12% CI 0.14 to 0.30). At 24 months, 98% vs 85% were alive without central-nervous-system disease (hazard ratio 0.18; 95% CI 0.10 to 0.33). Overall survival data were immature at this report (29 deaths: 9 osimertinib, 20 placebo). No new safety concerns were noted.
cards.watchOut: The trial was unblinded early on the strength of the disease-free-survival result, which can inflate early effect estimates; the survival answer had to wait for the 2023 report carded below — the same trial, not independent confirmation.
cards.source: Wu YL et al. Osimertinib in Resected EGFR-Mutated Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2020;383(18):1711-1723. PMID: 32955177. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02511106, from the record's databank fields.

cards.summary: ADAURA 2023 (overall survival): 5-year survival 85% vs 73% in stage II–IIIA disease; hazard ratio for death 0.49, relative.
cards.type: Planned final overall-survival analysis of the same double-blind phase 3 trial

shelves.title: First-line immunotherapy for metastatic melanoma: nivolumab–ipilimumab and nivolumab–relatlimab
shelves.question: Does dual checkpoint blockade beat nivolumab alone on survival in untreated metastatic melanoma (CheckMate 067) — and does adding relatlimab beat nivolumab alone on progression-free survival (RELATIVITY-047)?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Disease-Free Survival · Intention to Treat Analysis · Ipilimumab · Melanoma/drug therapy,secondary
shelves.balance: Split, proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, for the overall-survival claim): POSSIBLE that nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival versus ipilimumab alone — CheckMate 067's 5-year overall survival was 52% with the combination, 44% with nivolumab alone and 26% with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death, combination vs ipilimumab, 0.52); the trial was not powered for the combination-vs-nivolumab comparison, so 'the combination beats nivolumab alone on survival' is NOT established by this shelf. LIKELY that adding relatlimab to nivolumab improves progression-free survival versus nivolumab alone (RELATIVITY-047: median 10.1 vs 4.6 months; hazard ratio 0.75) — a direct randomised comparison on its primary endpoint. Toxicity is the price: grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events were 55.0% with nivolumab–ipilimumab vs 16.3% with nivolumab (CheckMate 067 primary report) and 18.9% vs 9.7% with relatlimab–nivolumab (RELATIVITY-047). This shelf is METASTATIC first-line treatment; adjuvant melanoma therapy lives on Shelf #761.

cards.headline: CheckMate 067 2015 (primary report): nivolumab–ipilimumab and nivolumab each beat ipilimumab on progression-free survival — median 11.5 and 6.9 vs 2.9 months
cards.summary: CheckMate 067 2015 (primary report): nivolumab–ipilimumab and nivolumab each beat ipilimumab on progression-free survival — median 11.5 and 6.9 vs 2.9 months. (Tier C — survival claims; PROPOSED.)
cards.people: 945 previously untreated patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma, assigned 1:1:1 to nivolumab alone, nivolumab plus ipilimumab, or ipilimumab alone. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 11.5 months (95% CI 8.9 to 16.7) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs 2.9 months (2.8 to 3.4) with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death or disease progression 0.42; 99.5% CI 0.31 to 0.57; P<0.001), and 6.9 months (4.3 to 9.5) with nivolumab alone (hazard ratio vs ipilimumab 0.57; 99.5% CI 0.43 to 0.76; P<0.001) — relative figures beside the absolute medians. In PD-L1-positive tumours, median PFS was 14.0 months in both nivolumab-containing groups; in PD-L1-negative tumours it was longer with the combination than with nivolumab alone (11.2 vs 5.3 months). Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 16.3% (nivolumab), 55.0% (combination) and 27.3% (ipilimumab) of patients.
cards.watchOut: The coprimary comparisons were each nivolumab regimen against ipilimumab — the trial was not designed or powered to prove the combination superior to nivolumab alone, the comparison clinicians most want.
cards.source: Larkin J et al. Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma. N Engl J Med. 2015;373(1):23-34. PMID: 26027431. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01844505, from the record's databank fields.

cards.summary: CheckMate 067 2019 (5-year survival): overall survival at 5 years was 52% with nivolumab–ipilimumab, 44% with nivolumab, and 26% with ipilimumab.
cards.type: 5-year outcomes report of the same phase 3 trial
cards.people: The same CheckMate 067 population: 945 previously untreated patients with advanced melanoma, at a minimum follow-up of 60 months. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median overall survival was more than 60.0 months (not reached) in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group and 36.9 months in the nivolumab group, vs 19.9 months in the ipilimumab group (hazard ratio for death with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs ipilimumab 0.52; with nivolumab vs ipilimumab 0.63). Overall survival at 5 years was 52% (combination), 44% (nivolumab) and 26% (ipilimumab). cards.headline: CheckMate 067 2025 (final, 10-year): median overall survival 71.9 months with nivolumab–ipilimumab vs 19.9 with ipilimumab; hazard ratio for death 0.53
cards.summary: CheckMate 067 2025 (final, 10-year — found by the currency sweep and carded): median overall survival 71.9 months with nivolumab–ipilimumab vs 19.9 with ipilimumab; hazard ratio for death 0.53, relative. (Three sequential reports of ONE trial — the shelf counts it once.)
cards.type: Final 10-year report of the same phase 3 trial (minimum follow-up 10 years)
cards.people: The same CheckMate 067 population: 945 previously untreated patients with advanced melanoma, randomised 1:1:1 to nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab alone, or ipilimumab alone. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 71.9 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 36.9 months with nivolumab, and 19.9 months with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death 0.53; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.65 for the combination vs ipilimumab, and 0.63; 0.52 to 0.76 for nivolumab vs ipilimumab) — relative figures beside the absolute medians. Median melanoma-specific survival was more than 120 months (not reached, with 37% of patients alive at the end of the trial) with the combination, 49.4 months with nivolumab, and 21.9 months with ipilimumab. Among patients alive and progression-free at 3 years, 10-year melanoma-specific survival was 96% with the combination, 97% with nivolumab, and 88% with ipilimumab. The authors conclude the final results show a continued survival benefit for both nivolumab-containing regimens over ipilimumab.
cards.watchOut: The final report of the same single trial — confirmation over time, not independent replication — and the combination-vs-nivolumab comparison remains unpowered: the 71.9 vs 36.9 months median difference was still not an alpha-controlled comparison.

cards.headline: RELATIVITY-047 2022: relatlimab–nivolumab beat nivolumab alone on progression-free survival — median 10.1 vs 4.6 months
cards.summary: RELATIVITY-047 2022: relatlimab–nivolumab beat nivolumab alone on progression-free survival — median 10.1 vs 4.6 months.
cards.people: Patients with previously untreated metastatic or unresectable melanoma received fixed-dose relatlimab–nivolumab or nivolumab alone every 4 weeks. The abstract does not state the total number randomised, mean age, or sex mix.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival (blinded independent central review; primary endpoint) was 10.1 months (95% CI 6.4 to 15.7) with relatlimab–nivolumab vs 4.6 months (3.4 to 5.6) with nivolumab (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.75; 95% CI 0.62 to 0.92; P=0.006) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians. Progression-free survival at 12 months was 47.7% (41.8 to 53.2) vs 36.0% (30.5 to 41.6). Progression-free survival across key subgroups favoured the combination. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.9% vs 9.7% of patients; no new safety signals were identified.
cards.watchOut: The hazard ratio of 0.75 sits inside the 0.5–2.0 caution band — the claim rests on the randomised design, the significant primary endpoint and the absolute median/12-month differences, not on the ratio alone; and this report is progression-free survival only, with no overall-survival result claimed.

cards.result: Versus ipilimumab, nivolumab-based therapy transformed first-line metastatic melanoma (5-year survival 52% combination, 44% nivolumab, 26% ipilimumab; at the final 10-year report, median overall survival 71.9 vs 36.9 vs 19.9 months). shelves.title: First-line immunotherapy combinations in metastatic kidney cancer
shelves.question: Do pembrolizumab–axitinib (KEYNOTE-426) and nivolumab–ipilimumab (CheckMate 214) improve survival versus sunitinib in untreated metastatic renal-cell carcinoma?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Intravenous · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Axitinib/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Carcinoma, Renal Cell/drug therapy,mortality · Intention to Treat Analysis
shelves.balance: LIKELY — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, overall-survival claims): Two independent large phase 3 trials beat the same standard, sunitinib, on overall survival — KEYNOTE-426 (pembrolizumab–axitinib; 12-month survival 89.9% vs 78.3%; hazard ratio for death 0.53 at the first interim analysis) and CheckMate 214 (nivolumab–ipilimumab, in intermediate/poor-risk patients; 18-month survival 75% vs 60%; hazard ratio 0.63). Two trials, two different combinations, one direction on survival — LIKELY, and Tier C because the claims are survival claims.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-426 2019: pembrolizumab–axitinib beat sunitinib on survival — 12-month survival 89.9% vs 78.3%, hazard ratio for death 0.53
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-426 2019: pembrolizumab–axitinib beat sunitinib on survival — 12-month survival 89.9% vs 78.3% , hazard ratio for death 0.53, relative. (Tier C — survival claim; PROPOSED.)
cards.type: Open-label, phase 3 trial; results from the protocol-specified first interim analysis
cards.people: 861 patients with previously untreated advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma, randomised to pembrolizumab plus axitinib (432) or sunitinib (429); median follow-up 12.8 months. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: The estimated percentage of patients alive at 12 months was 89.9% in the pembrolizumab–axitinib group and 78.3% in the sunitinib group (hazard ratio for death 0.53; 95% CI 0.38 to 0.74; P<0.0001) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates. Median progression-free survival was 15.1 vs 11.1 months (hazard ratio 0.69; 0.57 to 0.84; P<0.001), and the objective response rate was 59.3% (54.5 to 63.9) vs 35.7% (31.1 to 40.4) (P<0.001). Benefit was observed across all IMDC risk groups and regardless of PD-L1 expression. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause occurred in 75.8% vs 70.6% of patients.
cards.watchOut: A first interim analysis with 12.8 months of median follow-up — early survival estimates in first-line kidney cancer can move as data mature, and the comparison is against sunitinib alone, not against the other combination on this shelf.
cards.source: Rini BI et al. Pembrolizumab plus Axitinib versus Sunitinib for Advanced Renal-Cell Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(12):1116-1127. PMID: 30779529. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02853331, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: CheckMate 214 2018: nivolumab–ipilimumab beat sunitinib on survival in intermediate/poor-risk disease — 18-month survival 75% vs 60%
cards.summary: CheckMate 214 2018: nivolumab–ipilimumab beat sunitinib on survival in intermediate/poor-risk disease — 18-month survival 75% vs 60%. (Its final 9.3-year analysis is fenced in the synthesis.)
cards.people: 1,096 patients with previously untreated clear-cell advanced renal-cell carcinoma were randomised to nivolumab plus ipilimumab (550) or sunitinib (546); the coprimary endpoints were assessed in the 847 patients with intermediate or poor prognostic risk (425 and 422); median follow-up 25.2 months in that population. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: In intermediate/poor-risk patients, the 18-month overall survival rate was 75% (95% CI 70 to 78) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs 60% (55 to 65) with sunitinib; median overall survival was not reached vs 26.0 months (hazard ratio for death 0.63; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates. The objective response rate was 42% vs 27% (P<0.001) and the complete response rate 9% vs 1%. Median progression-free survival was 11.6 vs 8.4 months (hazard ratio 0.82; P=0.03, not significant against the prespecified 0.009 threshold). Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 events occurred in 46% vs 63% of patients; treatment-related events leading to discontinuation in 22% vs 12%.
cards.watchOut: The survival claim is for intermediate/poor-risk disease — the trial's coprimary population — not for favourable-risk patients; and its progression-free-survival comparison missed its prespecified significance threshold even as survival won.
cards.source: Motzer RJ et al. Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab versus Sunitinib in Advanced Renal-Cell Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(14):1277-1290. PMID: 29562145. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02231749, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: Synthesis: two combinations, two trials, one survival direction versus sunitinib — LIKELY, Tier C
cards.summary: Two combinations, two trials, one survival direction vs sunitinib — LIKELY, Tier C.
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: KEYNOTE-426 2019 (861 patients, all risk groups) and CheckMate 214 2018 (1,096 randomised; coprimary population 847 intermediate/poor-risk).
cards.result: First-line treatment of metastatic clear-cell kidney cancer changed on these two trials: pembrolizumab–axitinib (12-month survival 89.9% vs 78.3%) and nivolumab–ipilimumab (18-month survival 75% vs 60% in intermediate/poor risk) each beat sunitinib on overall survival. No carded trial compares the two combinations with each other — the choice between them rests on risk group, tempo of disease and toxicity, not on a head-to-head result. Survival claims: Tier C, proposed pending the developer's personal verdict. Fenced, not carded: the final CheckMate 214 analysis (Annals of Oncology; median follow-up 9.3 years) reported an overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.69 in intermediate/poor-risk patients, with 108-month survival probabilities of 30.2% vs 18.7% — consistent with the anchor report carded above, which remains this trial's home card on this shelf.
cards.watchOut: Do not use CheckMate 214's survival figures for favourable-risk patients, and do not rank the two combinations from these separate trials.
cards.source: Synthesis of Rini BI et al. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(12):1116-1127. PMID: 30779529; Motzer RJ et al. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(14):1277-1290. PMID: 29562145. Registry IDs as on the individual cards.

shelves.title: Adjuvant chemotherapy after pancreatic cancer resection: mFOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine–capecitabine
shelves.question: After pancreatic-cancer resection, does modified FOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24) or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (ESPAC-4) improve survival versus gemcitabine alone?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Deoxycytidine/adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Disease-Free Survival · Drug Combinations · Fluorouracil/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Irinotecan
shelves.balance: LIKELY — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, overall-survival claims): Both strategies beat gemcitabine alone on overall survival — PRODIGE-24's modified FOLFIRINOX by a large margin (median overall survival 54.4 vs 35.0 months; hazard ratio for death 0.64; 3-year survival 63.4% vs 48.6%), ESPAC-4's gemcitabine–capecitabine by a small one (median 28.0 vs 25.5 months; hazard ratio 0.82, inside the 0.5–2.0 caution band). Both cost toxicity: grade 3–4 adverse events in 75.9% on mFOLFIRINOX vs 52.9% on gemcitabine (PRODIGE-24). Fence: PRODIGE-24 is adjuvant therapy after PANCREATIC resection; PRODIGE 23, carded in the slate65–68 drafts at #866, is total neoadjuvant therapy for RECTAL cancer — a different trial that shares only the consortium name.

cards.headline: PRODIGE-24 2018: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX — median survival 54.4 vs 35.0 months with gemcitabine
cards.summary: PRODIGE-24 2018: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX — median survival 54.4 vs 35.0 months with gemcitabine. (Tier C — survival claim; PROPOSED.)
cards.people: 493 patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, randomised to modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin, irinotecan, leucovorin and fluorouracil every 2 weeks) or gemcitabine for 24 weeks; median follow-up 33.6 months. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median disease-free survival was 21.6 months with modified FOLFIRINOX vs 12.8 months with gemcitabine (stratified hazard ratio 0.58; 95% CI 0.46 to 0.73; P<0.001); 3-year disease-free survival was 39.7% vs 21.4%. Median overall survival was 54.4 vs 35.0 months (stratified hazard ratio for death 0.64; 95% CI 0.48 to 0.86; P=0.003) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians; 3-year overall survival was 63.4% vs 48.6%. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 75.9% of the modified-FOLFIRINOX group vs 52.9% of the gemcitabine group; one gemcitabine patient died from toxic effects (interstitial pneumonitis).
cards.watchOut: Trial patients were fit enough for a four-drug regimen after major pancreatic surgery — a selected minority of resected patients; the survival gain cannot be assumed for patients who would not have met the trial's fitness bar.
cards.source: Conroy T et al. FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(25):2395-2406. PMID: 30575490. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01526135 and EudraCT 2011-002026-52, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: ESPAC-4 2017: adding capecitabine to gemcitabine — median survival 28.0 vs 25.5 months, hazard ratio 0.82
cards.summary: ESPAC-4 2017: adding capecitabine to gemcitabine — median survival 28.0 vs 25.5 months, hazard ratio 0.82, relative.
cards.type: Phase 3, two-group, open-label, multicentre randomised trial at 92 hospitals in six European countries
cards.people: 732 patients aged 18 years or older who had undergone complete macroscopic resection (R0 or R1) for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma were enrolled; 730 were analysed (364 gemcitabine plus capecitabine; 366 gemcitabine alone), randomised within 12 weeks of surgery to six cycles. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median overall survival (primary endpoint) was 28.0 months (95% CI 23.5 to 31.5) with gemcitabine plus capecitabine vs 25.5 months (22.7 to 27.9) with gemcitabine alone (hazard ratio 0.82 [95% CI 0.68 to 0.98], p=0.032) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians, and one that sits inside the 0.5–2.0 band that is not solid evidence on its own. Grade 3–4 adverse events numbered 608, reported by 226 of 359 patients in the combination group, vs 481 events in 196 of 366 patients on gemcitabine alone. Results were reported at the data-monitoring committee's request after 458 of a target 480 deaths.
cards.watchOut: A modest absolute gain (2.5 months of median survival) from a more toxic doublet, reported early at the monitoring committee's request — a reasonable standard for patients unfit for mFOLFIRINOX, not a rival to it on effect size.
cards.source: Neoptolemos JP et al. cards.headline: Synthesis: intensify adjuvant therapy after pancreatic resection — LIKELY, Tier C; PRODIGE-24 is not PRODIGE 23
cards.summary: Intensify adjuvant therapy after pancreatic resection — LIKELY, Tier C. (PRODIGE-24 is not PRODIGE 23, the rectal-cancer trial drafted as topic #866.)
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: PRODIGE-24 2018 (493 patients, mFOLFIRINOX) and ESPAC-4 2017 (730 analysed, gemcitabine–capecitabine), each against gemcitabine alone. Fence: this shelf's PRODIGE-24 is adjuvant therapy after PANCREATIC resection; PRODIGE 23 (UNICANCER) is induction FOLFIRINOX before chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced RECTAL cancer, fenced in the slate65–68 topic drafts at #866 — different disease, different setting, only the consortium name in common. Neither trial is carded on the other's shelf.
cards.result: For fit patients after resection, modified FOLFIRINOX carries the large survival effect (median 54.4 vs 35.0 months); gemcitabine–capecitabine carries a small one (28.0 vs 25.5 months) for a broader population. Both beat gemcitabine alone, which is why the direction is LIKELY — with effect sizes, and fitness requirements, kept visibly different. Survival claims: Tier C, proposed pending the developer's personal verdict.
cards.watchOut: No head-to-head trial compares mFOLFIRINOX with gemcitabine–capecitabine; ranking them is an indirect, cross-trial judgement about fitness-stratified practice, not a randomised result.

shelves.title: Intensifying treatment for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (LATITUDE, CHAARTED)
shelves.question: Does adding abiraterone (LATITUDE) or docetaxel (CHAARTED) to androgen deprivation improve survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer?
shelves.mesh: Abiraterone Acetate/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Androgen Antagonists/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Neoplasm Metastasis/drug therapy · Prednisolone/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Prostatic Neoplasms/drug therapy,mortality,radiotherapy,surgery · Steroid 17-alpha-Hydroxylase/antagonists & inhibitors
shelves.balance: LIKELY — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, overall-survival claims): Two independent trials, two different added agents, the same answer — LATITUDE: adding abiraterone plus prednisone to androgen deprivation prolonged overall survival (median not reached vs 34.7 months at the interim analysis; hazard ratio for death 0.62) and radiographic progression-free survival (median 33.0 vs 14.8 months; hazard ratio 0.47); CHAARTED: adding six cycles of docetaxel prolonged median overall survival by 13.6 months (57.6 vs 44.0 months; hazard ratio 0.61). Concordant survival gains from different mechanisms earn LIKELY — and Tier C, as survival claims.

cards.headline: LATITUDE 2017: adding abiraterone to androgen deprivation — overall survival not reached vs 34.7 months, hazard ratio for death 0.62
cards.summary: LATITUDE 2017: adding abiraterone to androgen deprivation — overall survival not reached vs 34.7 months, hazard ratio for death 0.62, relative. (Tier C — survival claim; PROPOSED.)
cards.type: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial; planned interim analysis
cards.people: 1,199 patients with newly diagnosed, metastatic, castration-sensitive prostate cancer, randomised to androgen-deprivation therapy plus abiraterone acetate and prednisone, or androgen deprivation plus dual placebos; median follow-up 30.4 months at this interim analysis, after 406 deaths. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix (an all-male disease population).
cards.result: Median overall survival was significantly longer with abiraterone (not reached vs 34.7 months; hazard ratio for death 0.62; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.76; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians. Median radiographic progression-free survival was 33.0 vs 14.8 months (hazard ratio 0.47; 0.39 to 0.55; P<0.001). All secondary endpoints favoured abiraterone, including time to pain progression and to chemotherapy. The results led the monitoring committee to recommend unblinding and crossover to abiraterone. Rates of grade 3 hypertension and hypokalaemia were higher in the abiraterone group.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis with crossover allowed afterwards — later survival follow-up is contaminated by design (ethically necessary, analytically limiting), and LATITUDE enrolled high-risk newly diagnosed patients, the population in whom intensification was tested.
cards.source: Fizazi K et al. Abiraterone plus Prednisone in Metastatic, Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(4):352-360. PMID: 28578607. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01715285, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: CHAARTED 2015: adding docetaxel to androgen deprivation — median survival 57.6 vs 44.0 months, hazard ratio 0.61
cards.summary: CHAARTED 2015: adding docetaxel to androgen deprivation — median survival 57.6 vs 44.0 months, hazard ratio 0.61, relative.
cards.type: Randomised trial (open-label chemotherapy vs androgen deprivation alone)
cards.people: 790 men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (median age 63 years) were randomised to androgen-deprivation therapy plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² every 3 weeks for six cycles, or androgen deprivation alone; median follow-up 28.9 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 13.6 months longer with combination therapy (57.6 vs 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death 0.61; 95% CI 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001) — a relative figure beside the absolute medians. Median time to biochemical, symptomatic or radiographic progression was 20.2 vs 11.7 months (hazard ratio 0.61; 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001), and the rate of a prostate-specific antigen level below 0.2 ng/ml at 12 months was 27.7% vs 16.8% (P<0.001). In the combination group, grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia occurred in 6.2%, grade 3 or 4 infection with neutropenia in 2.3%, and grade 3 sensory or motor neuropathy in 0.5% each.
cards.watchOut: Six cycles of chemotherapy demand fitness and carry neutropenia risk; CHAARTED's population was predominantly high-volume disease, and applying its survival gain to low-volume, frailer presentations goes beyond the trial's centre of gravity.
cards.source: Sweeney CJ et al. Chemohormonal Therapy in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2015;373(8):737-746. PMID: 26244877. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00309985, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: Synthesis: intensify androgen deprivation up front — LIKELY on survival, Tier C
cards.summary: Intensify androgen deprivation up front — LIKELY on survival, Tier C.
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: LATITUDE 2017 (1,199 patients, abiraterone) and CHAARTED 2015 (790 men, docetaxel), each added to androgen deprivation and each against androgen deprivation alone. This shelf is treatment intensification in castration-SENSITIVE disease; finasteride prevention (Shelf #218) and the PCPT/REDUCE diagnosis question (Shelf #490) are different questions and are not re-carded here.
cards.result: Androgen deprivation alone is no longer the evidence-based default for fit men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: two different additions each prolonged survival with hazard ratios of 0.61–0.62 and double-digit-month median gains. shelves.title: Structured exercise after colon-cancer chemotherapy (CHALLENGE)
shelves.question: Does a three-year structured exercise programme after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer improve disease-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Colonic Neoplasms/drug therapy,mortality,rehabilitation,surgery · Disease-Free Survival · Exercise Therapy/methods · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Patient Education as Topic · Colectomy
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — proposed pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, a disease-free-survival claim from a single trial): In CHALLENGE, a 3-year structured exercise programme begun soon after adjuvant chemotherapy prolonged disease-free survival (hazard ratio for recurrence, new primary cancer or death 0.72; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.94; 5-year disease-free survival 80.3% vs 73.9% — a 6.4-point absolute difference) and overall-survival results pointed the same way (hazard ratio for death 0.63; 8-year survival 90.3% vs 83.2%). It is the first exercise trial with a disease-outcome primary endpoint and it is a single trial — hence POSSIBLE under the single-trial ceiling, with musculoskeletal adverse events more frequent on exercise (18.5% vs 11.5%). Tier C.

cards.headline: CHALLENGE 2025: structured exercise after chemotherapy — 5-year disease-free survival 80.3% vs 73.9%; 8-year overall survival 90.3% vs 83.2%
cards.summary: CHALLENGE 2025: structured exercise after chemotherapy — 5-year disease-free survival 80.3% vs 73.9% ; 8-year overall survival 90.3% vs 83.2%. (Tier C — survival outcomes; PROPOSED. Its sweep hits are CHALLENGE itself plus its cost-utility analysis.)
cards.type: Phase 3, randomised trial at 55 centres; unblindable behavioural intervention
cards.people: 889 patients with resected colon cancer who had completed adjuvant chemotherapy, randomised from 2009 through 2024 to a 3-year structured exercise programme (445) or health-education materials alone (444); median follow-up 7.9 years. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Disease-free survival (primary endpoint) was significantly longer with exercise (hazard ratio for disease recurrence, new primary cancer, or death 0.72; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.94; P=0.02) — a relative figure beside the absolute rates: 5-year disease-free survival was 80.3% in the exercise group and 73.9% in the health-education group (difference 6.4 percentage points; 95% CI 0.6 to 12.2). Results supported longer overall survival with exercise (hazard ratio for death 0.63; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.94); 8-year overall survival was 90.3% vs 83.2% (difference 7.1 points; 1.8 to 12.3). Musculoskeletal adverse events occurred more often in the exercise group (18.5% vs 11.5% of patients).
cards.watchOut: A single, unblindable trial accrued over 15 years (2009–2024), during which colon-cancer care changed; the hazard ratio of 0.72 sits inside the 0.5–2.0 caution band, so the claim leans on the randomised design, the prespecified disease endpoint and the absolute differences — and it needs replication before it can carry more than POSSIBLE.
cards.source: Courneya KS et al. Structured Exercise after Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Colon Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2025;393(1):13-25. PMID: 40450658. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00819208, from the record's databank fields.

shelves.title: Olanzapine for chemotherapy nausea: the four-drug antiemetic
shelves.question: Does adding low-dose olanzapine to standard triple prophylaxis improve complete response with highly emetogenic chemotherapy (Navari; J-FORCE)?
shelves.mesh: Antiemetics/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects · Aprepitant · Benzodiazepines/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Dexamethasone/therapeutic use · Drug Therapy, Combination · Intention to Treat Analysis
shelves.balance: LIKELY: Two double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials agree that adding olanzapine to standard triple prophylaxis (NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone) improves control of highly emetogenic chemotherapy — Navari 2016 (olanzapine 10 mg): complete response over 120 hours 64% vs 41%, and no nausea in 37% vs 22%; J-FORCE 2020 (olanzapine 5 mg): complete response in the delayed phase (24–120 hours) 79% vs 66%. The 5 mg dose carried little sedation signal in J-FORCE (one case of grade 3 somnolence), against increased sedation at 10 mg in Navari (severe in 5% on day 2). Symptom-control claims only — no survival or cardiovascular claim — so Tier C: no, after evaluating the topic file's candidacy against the brief's rule.

cards.headline: Navari 2016: olanzapine 10 mg added to triple prophylaxis — complete response 64% vs 41% over 120 hours, no nausea 37% vs 22%
cards.summary: Navari 2016: olanzapine 10 mg added to triple prophylaxis — complete response 64% vs 41% over 120 hours, no nausea 37% vs 22%.
cards.people: 380 chemotherapy-naïve patients receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy (cisplatin ≥70 mg/m², or cyclophosphamide–doxorubicin) who could be evaluated; 192 received olanzapine 10 mg orally on days 1–4 and 188 placebo, each with dexamethasone, aprepitant or fosaprepitant, and a 5-HT3-receptor antagonist. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: No chemotherapy-induced nausea (primary endpoint) was significantly more frequent with olanzapine in the first 24 hours (74% vs 45%; P=0.002), the 25–120-hour period (42% vs 25%; P=0.002) and the overall 120-hour period (37% vs 22%; P=0.002). Complete response (no emesis and no rescue medication) was also higher in all three periods: 86% vs 65% (P<0.001), 67% vs 52% (P=0.007) and 64% vs 41% (P<0.001), respectively. There were no grade 5 toxic effects; some olanzapine patients had increased sedation (severe in 5%) on day 2.
cards.watchOut: The 10 mg dose's sedation is the regimen's main cost, and the population was chemotherapy-naïve patients on two specific highly emetogenic backbones — extrapolation to moderately emetogenic regimens is untested here.
cards.source: Navari RM et al. Olanzapine for the Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(2):134-142. PMID: 27410922. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02116530, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: J-FORCE 2020: olanzapine 5 mg — delayed-phase complete response 79% vs 66%, with minimal sedation
cards.summary: J-FORCE 2020: olanzapine 5 mg — delayed-phase complete response 79% vs 66%, with minimal sedation.
cards.type: Multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial at 26 hospitals in Japan
cards.people: 710 patients aged 20–75 years with a malignant tumour (excluding haematopoietic malignancy), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0–2, scheduled for first cisplatin (≥50 mg/m²), were enrolled; 354 in the olanzapine 5 mg group and 351 in the placebo group contributed to the delayed-phase efficacy analysis; all received aprepitant, palonosetron and dexamethasone with olanzapine or placebo on days 1–4.
cards.result: In the delayed phase (24–120 hours; primary endpoint), complete response was achieved by 280 of 354 patients (79% [95% CI 75 to 83]) in the olanzapine group and 231 of 351 (66% [61 to 71]) in the placebo group (p<0.0001). One patient had grade 3 constipation and one had grade 3 somnolence related to treatment in the olanzapine group. The authors conclude olanzapine 5 mg with triplet therapy could be a new standard for cisplatin-based chemotherapy. (Lancet-family abstract: middle-dot decimals are decimals.)
cards.watchOut: A cisplatin-only, single-country trial of the 5 mg dose — it confirms the class effect at half of Navari's dose but does not by itself cover non-cisplatin regimens; Navari's broader highly-emetogenic population is the complement carded above.

cards.headline: Synthesis: add olanzapine as the fourth antiemetic drug — LIKELY; 5 mg buys most of the benefit with less sedation
cards.summary: Add olanzapine as the fourth antiemetic drug — LIKELY; 5 mg buys most of the benefit with less sedation.
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: Navari 2016 (380 evaluable, 10 mg) and J-FORCE 2020 (705 in the efficacy analysis, 5 mg). No antiemetic shelf existed before this one; standard triple prophylaxis is the shared comparator, not a carded shelf.
cards.result: Two blinded trials, two doses, one direction: complete response rises by roughly 13–23 percentage points when olanzapine joins triple prophylaxis for highly emetogenic chemotherapy (delayed phase 79% vs 66% at 5 mg; overall 64% vs 41% at 10 mg). LIKELY for the four-drug regimen, with the dose choice — 5 mg vs 10 mg — governed by how much day-2 sedation the patient can afford.

shelves.title: First-line immunotherapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: atezolizumab-bevacizumab and STRIDE
shelves.question: In unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, does first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (IMbrave150) — or single-dose tremelimumab plus durvalumab, the STRIDE regimen (HIMALAYA) — improve survival versus sorafenib?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Bevacizumab/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Carcinoma, Hepatocellular/drug therapy · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy
shelves.balance: LIKELY — PROPOSED pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C, overall-survival claims): Two independent phase 3 trials beat sorafenib on overall survival. IMbrave150: hazard ratio for death 0.58 (a relative measure) with 12-month survival 67.2% versus 54.6%. HIMALAYA (STRIDE): hazard ratio 0.78 (relative) with median survival 16.43 versus 13.77 months and 36-month survival 30.7% versus 20.2%. The effects differ in size and both hazard ratios sit inside the 0.5-2.0 caution band on their own terms, but two concordant randomised survival wins against the same control are why the proposed grade is LIKELY, not POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: Finn 2020 (IMbrave150): atezolizumab plus bevacizumab beat sorafenib on survival — hazard ratio for death 0.58, 12-month survival 67.2% vs 54.6%
cards.summary: IMbrave150 (2020): atezolizumab plus bevacizumab beat sorafenib on survival — hazard ratio for death 0.58 ; 12-month survival 67.2% vs 54.6%.
cards.people: 501 patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and no previous systemic treatment, randomised 2:1 to atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (336) or sorafenib (165). The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: The hazard ratio for death with atezolizumab-bevacizumab versus sorafenib was 0.58 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.79; P<0.001) — a relative measure; overall survival at 12 months was 67.2% (95% CI 61.3 to 73.1) versus 54.6% (45.2 to 64.0). Median progression-free survival was 6.8 months (5.7 to 8.3) versus 4.3 months (4.0 to 5.6), hazard ratio 0.59 (0.47 to 0.76). Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 56.5% of the combination group and 55.1% of the sorafenib group; grade 3 or 4 hypertension occurred in 15.2% on the combination.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the primary analysis was early (data cutoff Aug 29, 2019): the relative hazard of 0.58 sits inside the 0.5-2.0 caution band, so the absolute 12-month rates beside it are what carry the claim.
cards.source: Finn RS et al. Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2020;382(20):1894-1905. PMID: 32402160. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03434379, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: Abou-Alfa 2022 (HIMALAYA): STRIDE improved survival versus sorafenib — hazard ratio 0.78, median 16.43 vs 13.77 months
cards.summary: HIMALAYA (2022): STRIDE improved survival versus sorafenib — hazard ratio 0.78 ; median survival 16.43 vs 13.77 months.
cards.people: 1171 patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and no previous systemic treatment, randomised to STRIDE (393), durvalumab alone (389) or sorafenib (389). The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 16.43 months (95% CI 14.16 to 19.58) with STRIDE, 16.56 months (14.06 to 19.12) with durvalumab, and 13.77 months (12.25 to 16.13) with sorafenib; 36-month survival was 30.7%, 24.7% and 20.2% respectively. The hazard ratio for death for STRIDE versus sorafenib was 0.78 (96.02% CI 0.65 to 0.93; P=0.0035) — a relative measure. Durvalumab alone was noninferior to sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.86; noninferiority margin 1.08). Median progression-free survival did not differ significantly among the groups. Grade 3/4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50.5% (STRIDE), 37.1% (durvalumab) and 52.4% (sorafenib).
cards.watchOut: The survival gain is modest in absolute months and the hazard ratio of 0.78 sits inside the 0.5-2.0 caution band; progression-free survival was not improved, so this is a survival-tail result, not a shrinkage result.

cards.headline: Synthesis: two different immunotherapy regimens each beat sorafenib on survival — LIKELY, proposed (Tier C)
cards.summary: Two different immunotherapy regimens each beat sorafenib on survival — LIKELY, Tier C.
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: IMbrave150 (501 patients) and HIMALAYA (1171 patients), both against sorafenib in previously untreated unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
cards.result: Both trials are positive on overall survival with different mechanisms — VEGF plus PD-L1 blockade (hazard ratio 0.58 relative; 67.2% vs 54.6% alive at 12 months) and single-priming-dose CTLA-4 plus PD-L1 blockade (hazard ratio 0.78 relative; median 16.43 vs 13.77 months). No head-to-head trial compares the two regimens, so this shelf does not rank them. The currency sweep's HIMALAYA five-year update (PMID 40222621) is a later report of the HIMALAYA trial carded here, not a new trial, and is not re-carded. The stamp is PROPOSED pending the developer's personal verdict because the shelf carries overall-survival claims.
cards.watchOut: Sorafenib is a dated control: neither trial answers how these regimens compare with each other or with lenvatinib-based care.

shelves.title: First-line immunotherapy for MSI-high / mismatch-repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer
shelves.question: In MSI-high/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer, does first-line pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177) — or nivolumab plus ipilimumab (CheckMate 8HW) — beat chemotherapy-based standard care on progression-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Biomarkers, Tumor/genetics · Brain Neoplasms · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy,genetics,mortality · Fluorouracil/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: LIKELY (on progression-free survival): Two phase 3 trials in the same biomarker-defined population show large progression-free-survival gains — KEYNOTE-177, pembrolizumab versus chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.60 (relative), median 16.5 versus 8.2 months; CheckMate 8HW, nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab alone, hazard ratio 0.62 (relative), median not reached versus 39.3 months. This shelf makes no overall-survival claim: KEYNOTE-177's survival analysis was confounded by crossover and is printed as such, which is why the shelf is not Tier C.

cards.headline: André 2020 (KEYNOTE-177): first-line pembrolizumab doubled progression-free survival versus chemotherapy — median 16.5 vs 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.60
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-177 (2020): first-line pembrolizumab doubled progression-free survival versus chemotherapy — median 16.5 vs 8.2 months , hazard ratio 0.60.
cards.people: 307 patients with previously untreated metastatic MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer, randomised 1:1 to pembrolizumab or chemotherapy (5-fluorouracil-based, with or without bevacizumab or cetuximab), with crossover to pembrolizumab allowed after progression. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: Pembrolizumab was superior on progression-free survival: median 16.5 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.45 to 0.80; P=0.0002) — a relative measure. Overall response was 43.8% versus 33.1%, and among responders 83% versus 35% still had ongoing responses at 24 months. Overall survival data were still evolving at this analysis (56 deaths on pembrolizumab, 69 on chemotherapy) and the chemotherapy group could cross over, so no survival claim is made. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22% versus 66%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the hazard ratio of 0.60 sits inside the 0.5-2.0 caution band on its own terms; the doubling of median progression-free survival and the response durability are the supporting absolutes. Survival cannot be read cleanly from this trial because of crossover.
cards.source: André T et al. Pembrolizumab in Microsatellite-Instability-High Advanced Colorectal Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2020;383(23):2207-2218. PMID: 33264544. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02563002, from the record's databank fields.

cards.headline: André 2025 (CheckMate 8HW): nivolumab plus ipilimumab beat nivolumab alone on progression-free survival — hazard ratio 0.62, median not reached vs 39.3 months
cards.summary: CheckMate 8HW (2025): nivolumab plus ipilimumab beat nivolumab alone on progression-free survival — hazard ratio 0.62 .
cards.people: 707 immunotherapy-naive patients with unresectable or metastatic MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer across treatment lines, randomised to nivolumab plus ipilimumab (354) or nivolumab alone (353); 296 (84%) and 286 (81%) respectively were centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR. The abstract does not state mean age or sex mix.
cards.result: At median follow-up of 47.0 months, nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved progression-free survival versus nivolumab alone: hazard ratio 0.62 (95% CI 0.48 to 0.81; p=0.0003) — a relative measure; median progression-free survival was not reached (95% CI 53.8 to not estimable) versus 39.3 months (22.1 to not estimable). The trial's other primary endpoint (versus chemotherapy, first line) had been reported earlier in the combination's favour. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22% versus 14%; there were three treatment-related deaths (myocarditis and pneumonitis on the combination, pneumonitis on nivolumab).
cards.watchOut: This report's comparison is against nivolumab, not chemotherapy; the hazard ratio of 0.62 sits inside the 0.5-2.0 caution band, and the combination bought its gain with more high-grade toxicity.
