shelves.title: Sotorasib versus docetaxel in previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC (CodeBreaK 200)
shelves.question: In KRAS G12C-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-(L)1 inhibitor, does sotorasib improve progression-free survival versus docetaxel?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Adolescent · Adult · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung/drug therapy · Docetaxel/therapeutic use · Proto-Oncogene Proteins p21(ras)/genetics/therapeutic use · Lung Neoplasms/drug therapy · Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Mutation · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Disease-Free Survival · Piperazines · Pyridines · Pyrimidines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — the single phase 3 trial met its primary endpoint: progression-free survival 5.6 versus 4.5 months (hazard ratio 0.66; p=0.0017) by blinded central review, with fewer grade 3 or worse and serious treatment-related adverse events than docetaxel. The absolute gain at the median is 1.1 months, and this record prints no overall-survival results — a correction to the topic file, which described survival as showing 'no difference': whatever later or fuller reports show, the carded record contains no survival figures, and none are claimed. The trial was open-label. PROPOSED as a two-trial-gate exception candidate: a single trial with a surrogate endpoint; the shelf should be withdrawn or re-scoped if the developer rejects the exception.

cards.headline: CodeBreaK 200: progression-free survival 5.6 versus 4.5 months (HR 0.66; p=0.0017); fewer severe treatment-related events than docetaxel
cards.summary: CodeBreaK 200: progression-free survival 5.6 versus 4.5 months (HR 0.66; p=0.0017); fewer severe treatment-related events than docetaxel
cards.type: Phase 3, randomised, open-label trial (148 centres in 22 countries; sotorasib 960 mg daily versus docetaxel 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks; primary endpoint progression-free survival by blinded independent central review)
cards.people: 345 patients with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced NSCLC who had progressed after platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor were randomised (171 sotorasib, 174 docetaxel). Median follow-up was 17.7 months. The abstract does not print mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months (95% CI 4.3 to 7.8) on sotorasib versus 4.5 months (3.0 to 5.7) on docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.86; p=0.0017 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 33% versus 40%, and serious treatment-related adverse events in 11% versus 23%. The commonest severe events on sotorasib were diarrhoea (12%), ALT increase (8%) and AST increase (5%); on docetaxel, neutropenia (9%), fatigue (6%) and febrile neutropenia (5%). This record reports no overall-survival results.
cards.watchOut: Open-label treatment (endpoints centrally blinded). Sotorasib's advantage is a modest delay in progression with better tolerability — not, on this record, longer life. Any survival or crossover discussion belongs to fuller reports not carded here.
cards.source: de Langen AJ et al. Sotorasib versus docetaxel for previously treated non-small-cell lung cancer with KRASG12C mutation: a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. shelves.title: First-line selpercatinib in RET fusion-positive advanced NSCLC (LIBRETTO-431)
shelves.question: In untreated RET fusion-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, does selpercatinib improve progression-free survival versus platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy with or without pembrolizumab?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/administration & dosage/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung/drug therapy/genetics · Lung Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics · Proto-Oncogene Proteins c-ret/antagonists & inhibitors · Pyrazoles · Pyridines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — a single randomised phase 3 trial with a large progression-free survival effect: median 24.8 versus 11.2 months (hazard ratio 0.46) in the primary analysis population, with higher response rates (84% versus 65%) and strong protection against CNS progression (cause-specific hazard ratio 0.28). The endpoint is progression-free survival at a preplanned interim analysis; crossover to selpercatinib was allowed, which will blur any survival comparison; and the record's abstract reports adverse events only qualitatively, so no comparative safety figures are carded. PROPOSED as a two-trial-gate exception candidate: a single trial with a surrogate endpoint; the shelf should be withdrawn or re-scoped if the developer rejects the exception.

cards.headline: LIBRETTO-431: progression-free survival 24.8 versus 11.2 months (HR 0.46; P<0.001); responses 84% versus 65%
cards.summary: LIBRETTO-431: progression-free survival 24.8 versus 11.2 months (HR 0.46; P<0.001); responses 84% versus 65%
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial (selpercatinib versus platinum-based chemotherapy with or without pembrolizumab at the investigator's discretion; primary endpoint progression-free survival by blinded independent central review; crossover to selpercatinib permitted at progression; preplanned interim efficacy analysis)
cards.people: The primary analysis population (intention-to-treat-pembrolizumab: patients whose physicians had planned pembrolizumab if assigned to control) comprised 212 randomised patients; the overall intention-to-treat population was 261, with similar results. The abstract does not print mean age or the sex split, nor the arm sizes within the primary population.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 24.8 months (95% CI 16.9 to not estimable) on selpercatinib versus 11.2 months (8.8 to 16.8) on control treatment (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.46, 95% CI 0.31 to 0.70; P<0.001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). Objective responses occurred in 84% (95% CI 76 to 90) versus 65% (54 to 75). The cause-specific hazard ratio for CNS progression was 0.28 (95% CI 0.12 to 0.68). The abstract states that adverse events were consistent with those previously reported for both treatments, but prints no comparative rates.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis with a surrogate endpoint; permitted crossover means overall survival, when reported, will compare strategies (immediate versus delayed selpercatinib) rather than drug versus none. The dual analysis populations (with and without planned pembrolizumab) are a design wrinkle the reader should notice: the headline numbers come from the pembrolizumab-planned population, with the overall population described as similar but not numerically carded in this record.

cards.headline: Synthesis: selpercatinib doubles first-line progression-free survival in RET fusion-positive NSCLC — POSSIBLE
cards.summary: Synthesis: selpercatinib doubles first-line progression-free survival in RET fusion-positive NSCLC — POSSIBLE
cards.people: Synthesis of the card above: LIBRETTO-431 (Zhou 2023), 261 randomised patients (212 in the primary analysis population).
cards.result: A selective RET inhibitor more than doubled median progression-free survival against modern chemotherapy (with or without pembrolizumab), with higher response rates and marked CNS protection — a decisive targeted-therapy result in a small molecularly defined population, on progression endpoints at interim analysis.

shelves.title: Postoperative radiotherapy after complete resection of stage IIIA-N2 non-small-cell lung cancer (Lung ART; PORT-C)
shelves.question: In completely resected stage IIIA N2 NSCLC after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, does modern postoperative radiotherapy improve disease-free or overall survival versus no PORT?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung/mortality/pathology/radiotherapy · Combined Modality Therapy · Female · Humans · Lung Neoplasms/mortality/pathology/radiotherapy · Male · Mediastinum/pathology · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Staging · Radiotherapy, Intensity-Modulated
shelves.balance: Two large phase 3 trials asked whether modern mediastinal postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) helps after complete resection of stage IIIA-N2 non-small-cell lung cancer, and both missed their primary endpoint. In Lung ART (n=501), 3-year disease-free survival was 47% with PORT versus 44% without (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.68–1.08, p=0.18). In PORT-C (n=364 eligible), 3-year disease-free survival was 40.5% versus 32.7% (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.65–1.09, P=.20 unadjusted), and 3-year overall survival was 78.3% with PORT versus 82.8% without (HR 1.02) — no survival gain in either direction of the comparison. PORT did improve locoregional control in PORT-C (locoregional recurrence-free survival HR 0.71), but at a toxicity price: in Lung ART, late grade 3–4 cardiopulmonary toxicity was 11% with PORT versus 5% without, and all three treatment-related deaths (two from pneumonitis, one from chemotherapy sepsis) occurred in the PORT arm. The exploratory and per-protocol analyses suggesting a DFS signal in PORT-C were pre-planned as exploratory or post-randomisation subsets and do not overturn the intention-to-treat nulls. Balance: routine mediastinal PORT after complete resection of IIIA-N2 disease does not improve disease-free or overall survival and adds cardiopulmonary harm; it is not standard care. PROPOSED LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: Lung ART: mediastinal PORT did not improve 3-year disease-free survival after complete resection of stage IIIA-N2 NSCLC — 47% versus 44%, HR 0.86, p=0.18, with more late cardiopulmonary toxicity
cards.summary: Lung ART: mediastinal PORT did not improve 3-year disease-free survival after complete resection of stage IIIA-N2 NSCLC — 47% versus 44%, HR 0.86, p=0.18, with more late cardiopulmonary toxicity
cards.people: 501 patients with completely resected NSCLC and cytologically or histologically proven N2 involvement, most staged with FDG-PET (91%) and most having received neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy; 252 assigned to PORT and 249 to no PORT. The abstract does not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: 3-year disease-free survival was 47% (95% CI 40–54) with PORT versus 44% (37–51) without; median disease-free survival 30.5 versus 22.8 months (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.68–1.08; p=0.18) — the primary endpoint was not met. The most common grade 3–4 adverse events in the PORT arm were pneumonitis (5% vs <1%), lymphopenia (4% vs 0) and fatigue (3% vs <1%). Late grade 3–4 cardiopulmonary toxicity was reported in 11% of the PORT group versus 5% of controls. Two patients died from pneumonitis and one from chemotherapy-toxicity sepsis, all in the PORT group.
cards.watchOut: Open-label superiority trial; the abstract prints no overall-survival rates, so no survival claim either way can be carded from this record. The authors' conclusion — that conformal PORT cannot be recommended as standard care in this population — matches the primary result.

cards.summary: PORT-C: postoperative radiotherapy after resection and adjuvant chemotherapy in pIIIA-N2 NSCLC did not significantly improve disease-free survival (HR 0.84, P=.20) and overall survival was numerically worse (HR 1.02)
cards.people: 394 patients enrolled with pIIIA-N2 NSCLC after complete resection and 4 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy; 364 were eligible for the primary analysis (184 PORT, 180 observation). Median age 55 years (range 25–70); 55.5% were men.
cards.result: 3-year disease-free survival was 40.5% with PORT versus 32.7% with observation (median 22.1 vs 18.6 months; HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.65–1.09; P=.20) — not significant in the primary unadjusted analysis. shelves.title: ctDNA-guided adjuvant therapy in stage II colon cancer (DYNAMIC)
shelves.question: In resected stage II colon cancer, does a ctDNA-guided strategy (chemotherapy only if ctDNA-positive) safely reduce chemotherapy use without compromising recurrence-free survival versus standard clinicopathological management?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Australia · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant/methods · Circulating Tumor DNA/analysis/blood · Colonic Neoplasms/blood/mortality/pathology/therapy · Disease-Free Survival · Fluorouracil/therapeutic use · Humans · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/prevention & control · Neoplasm Staging · Oxaliplatin/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: One strategy trial answers this question. In DYNAMIC (n=455), management guided by circulating tumour DNA results roughly halved adjuvant chemotherapy use (15% vs 28%) while 2-year recurrence-free survival was noninferior to standard clinicopathological management (93.5% vs 92.4%; absolute difference +1.1 percentage points, 95% CI −4.1 to 6.2, against a noninferiority margin of −8.5 points). At 3 years, recurrence-free survival was 86.4% in ctDNA-positive patients who received chemotherapy and 92.5% in ctDNA-negative patients who did not. Two cautions keep the stamp moderate: this is a single trial with a wide noninferiority margin, and the record does not show that chemotherapy actually improves outcomes for ctDNA-positive patients — DYNAMIC tested the strategy, not the treatment; the confirmatory trials (COBRA, CIRCULATE and others) were still in flight when this record was published. No survival (mortality) claim is made or supported by this record. PROPOSED POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: DYNAMIC: ctDNA-guided management halved adjuvant chemotherapy use (15% vs 28%) and was noninferior for 2-year recurrence-free survival in stage II colon cancer
cards.summary: DYNAMIC: ctDNA-guided management halved adjuvant chemotherapy use (15% vs 28%) and was noninferior for 2-year recurrence-free survival in stage II colon cancer
cards.people: 455 patients with resected stage II colon cancer randomised 2:1 — 302 to ctDNA-guided management and 153 to standard clinicopathological management; median follow-up 37 months. The abstract does not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: Adjuvant chemotherapy was given to 15% of the ctDNA-guided group versus 28% of the standard group (relative risk of receiving chemotherapy with standard management 1.82; 95% CI 1.25–2.65, as printed). 2-year recurrence-free survival was 93.5% with ctDNA guidance versus 92.4% with standard management — an absolute difference of +1.1 percentage points (95% CI −4.1 to 6.2), which met the pre-set noninferiority margin of −8.5 percentage points. 3-year recurrence-free survival was 86.4% among ctDNA-positive patients who received adjuvant chemotherapy and 92.5% among ctDNA-negative patients who did not.
cards.watchOut: A strategy trial with a generous noninferiority margin (−8.5 points) on a 2-year endpoint; it does not establish that chemotherapy benefits ctDNA-positive patients, only that withholding it from ctDNA-negative patients was not worse within the margin. Confirmatory strategy trials were still in flight at publication.

shelves.title: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (RECOURSE; TERRA)
shelves.question: In metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and biologics, does trifluridine/tipiracil improve overall survival versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma/drug therapy/mortality/secondary · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Double-Blind Method · Drug Combinations · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis/drug therapy · Proportional Hazards Models · Pyrrolidines · Survival Analysis · Thymine · Trifluridine/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Uracil/adverse effects/analogs & derivatives/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: Two double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in chemotherapy-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer agree. In the global RECOURSE trial (n=800), trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) improved median overall survival from 5.3 to 7.1 months (HR for death 0.68, 95% CI 0.58–0.81, P<0.001) and delayed worsening of performance status. In the Asian TERRA trial (n=406), the survival benefit replicated: median overall survival 7.8 versus 7.1 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62–0.99, P=.035). The absolute gains are modest — roughly one to two months of median survival in a population with no remaining standard options — and the price is myelosuppression: neutropenia in 38% and febrile neutropenia in 4% in RECOURSE, with one treatment-related death; TERRA reported no treatment-related deaths and serious adverse-event rates similar to placebo (23.2% vs 23.7%). Balance: a real, replicated survival benefit of modest absolute size in refractory disease. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: RECOURSE: TAS-102 improved median overall survival from 5.3 to 7.1 months in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (HR 0.68, P<0.001)

cards.people: 800 patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer randomised 2:1 to TAS-102 or placebo (the abstract does not print the arm counts, mean age, or sex split).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 7.1 months with TAS-102 versus 5.3 months with placebo (HR for death 0.68; 95% CI 0.58–0.81; P<0.001). Median time to worsening of ECOG performance status (from 0–1 to ≥2) was 5.7 versus 4.0 months (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.56–0.78; P<0.001). Clinically significant adverse events with TAS-102 were neutropenia (38%) and leukopenia (21%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 4% and one death related to TAS-102 was reported.
cards.watchOut: The absolute survival gain is about 2 months of median survival; the benefit is consistent but modest, and myelosuppression is the dominant harm.

shelves.title: Regorafenib in treatment-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (CORRECT; CONCUR)
shelves.question: In metastatic colorectal cancer after all standard therapies, does regorafenib improve overall survival versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis/drug therapy · Phenylurea Compounds/therapeutic use · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/therapeutic use · Pyridines/therapeutic use · Survival Rate
shelves.balance: Regorafenib was the first agent to prolong survival in treatment-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer — flagged OUTSTANDING-SINGLE for CORRECT in the topic plan — and the benefit was then confirmed by a second double-blind trial, so the shelf stands on two trials. In CORRECT (n=760, global), median overall survival was 6.4 months on regorafenib versus 5.0 on placebo (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64–0.94); in CONCUR (n=204, Asian patients), median overall survival was 8.8 versus 6.3 months (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.40–0.77). Both trials report one-sided P values (CORRECT one-sided p=0.0052, endpoint met at a pre-planned interim analysis; CONCUR one-sided p=0.00016), which are flagged as one-sided on the cards. The absolute gain is modest — about 1.4 months of median survival in CORRECT — and toxicity is substantial: treatment-related adverse events in 93% on regorafenib in CORRECT, with grade ≥3 hand-foot skin reaction in 17%, fatigue 10%, diarrhoea 7% and hypertension 7%. Balance: a real, replicated survival benefit of small absolute size, bought with considerable skin and constitutional toxicity in patients without other options. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: CORRECT: regorafenib was the first agent to improve overall survival in metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to all standard therapy — 6.4 versus 5.0 months, HR 0.77 (one-sided p=0.0052)
cards.summary: CORRECT: regorafenib was the first agent to improve overall survival in metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to all standard therapy — 6.4 versus 5.0 months, HR 0.77 (one-sided p=0.0052)
cards.people: 760 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer progressing during or within 3 months of their last standard therapy, randomised 2:1 at 114 centres in 16 countries — 505 to regorafenib plus best supportive care and 255 to placebo plus best supportive care. The abstract does not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: The primary endpoint of overall survival was met at a pre-planned interim analysis: median overall survival 6.4 months with regorafenib versus 5.0 months with placebo (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.64–0.94; one-sided p=0.0052 — a one-sided P value, as printed). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 93% of regorafenib patients versus 61% on placebo; the most common grade ≥3 events related to regorafenib were hand-foot skin reaction (17%), fatigue (10%), diarrhoea (7%), hypertension (7%) and rash or desquamation (6%).
cards.watchOut: The headline P value is one-sided, and the survival result comes from a pre-planned interim analysis. The absolute median gain is 1.4 months; nearly all patients had treatment-related adverse events.

cards.summary: CONCUR: regorafenib confirmed the survival benefit in Asian patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer — 8.8 versus 6.3 months, HR 0.55 (one-sided p=0.00016)

shelves.title: Triplet FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab versus doublet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in metastatic colorectal cancer (TRIBE; TRIBE2)
shelves.question: In untreated metastatic colorectal cancer fit for intensive therapy, does triplet FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab improve outcomes versus a doublet plus bevacizumab?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Bevacizumab · Camptothecin/adverse effects/analogs & derivatives/therapeutic use · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Fluorouracil/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Leucovorin/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy/secondary · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis/drug therapy · Organoplatinum Compounds/adverse effects/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: Upfront triplet chemotherapy improves progression outcomes but has not, on the carded primary records, been shown to extend life. In TRIBE (n=508), FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab beat FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab on the primary endpoint of progression-free survival (12.1 vs 9.7 months; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62–0.90, P=0.003) and response rate (65% vs 53%), but overall survival — 31.0 versus 25.8 months, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.63–1.00), P=0.054 — did NOT reach significance in the primary report; the drafting topic file's implication of an overall-survival benefit is not supported by the record and is corrected here. In TRIBE2 (n=679), an upfront-triplet strategy with reintroduction beat a pre-planned doublet sequence on its primary endpoint, progression-free survival 2 (19.2 vs 16.4 months; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63–0.88, p=0.0005); the TRIBE2 record prints no overall-survival figures, so none are carded. The cost is real toxicity: in TRIBE2's first-line phase, grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 50% versus 21% and diarrhoea in 17% versus 5%, with eight treatment-related deaths in the triplet-strategy arm versus four in the control arm. Balance: for fit patients the triplet buys response and progression control, not proven survival. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: TRIBE: FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab improved progression-free survival (12.1 vs 9.7 months, HR 0.75) and response (65% vs 53%) — but overall survival was NOT significant in the primary report (HR 0.79, P=0.054)
cards.summary: TRIBE: FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab improved progression-free survival (12.1 vs 9.7 months, HR 0.75) and response (65% vs 53%) — but overall survival was NOT significant in the primary report (HR 0.79, P=0.054)
cards.people: 508 patients with untreated metastatic colorectal cancer assigned to FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab or FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab (the abstract does not print the arm counts, mean age, or sex split).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 12.1 months in the FOLFOXIRI group versus 9.7 months in the FOLFIRI group (HR for progression 0.75; 95% CI 0.62–0.90; P=0.003), and the objective response rate was 65% versus 53% (P=0.006). Overall survival was longer numerically but not significantly: 31.0 versus 25.8 months (HR for death 0.79; 95% CI 0.63–1.00; P=0.054). The incidences of grade 3 or 4 neurotoxicity, stomatitis, diarrhoea and neutropenia were significantly higher in the experimental group (the abstract does not print the percentages).
cards.watchOut: The survival claim sometimes attached to this trial is not in its primary report: the overall-survival confidence interval reaches 1.00 and P=0.054. A later long-term update exists but is not the record carded here; the primary analysis leads.

shelves.title: Adding bevacizumab to first-line chemotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer (AVF2107g; NO16966)
shelves.question: In untreated metastatic colorectal cancer, does adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improve overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Bevacizumab · Camptothecin/administration & dosage/analogs & derivatives · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/pathology · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Fluorouracil/administration & dosage · Humans · Irinotecan · Leucovorin/administration & dosage · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis/drug therapy · Quality of Life · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: The answer depends on the chemotherapy backbone. With the irinotecan–bolus-fluorouracil regimen (IFL) used in the 2004 pivotal trial AVF2107g (n=813), adding bevacizumab produced a clear survival benefit: median overall survival 20.3 versus 15.6 months (HR for death 0.66, P<0.001), with progression-free survival 10.6 versus 6.2 months (HR 0.54) and response 44.8% versus 34.8%. With the oxaliplatin doublets that later became standard, the much larger NO16966 trial (n=1,401) found a significant progression-free-survival gain (9.4 vs 8.0 months; HR 0.83, P=.0023) but overall survival of 21.3 versus 19.9 months (HR 0.89; 97.5% CI 0.76–1.03; P=.077) — not significant — and no response-rate improvement; the trial's own analysis noted that few patients were actually treated until progression (29% of the bevacizumab group), which may have diluted the survival effect. The consistent harm is hypertension (grade 3 hypertension 11.0% vs 2.3% in AVF2107g). Balance: bevacizumab prolongs progression-free survival across backbones; a survival benefit is proven with IFL and attenuated, not excluded, with modern oxaliplatin doublets. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.people: 813 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer; 402 assigned to IFL (irinotecan, bolus fluorouracil, leucovorin) plus bevacizumab and 411 to IFL plus placebo. The abstract does not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 20.3 months with IFL plus bevacizumab versus 15.6 months with IFL plus placebo (HR for death 0.66; P<0.001). Median progression-free survival was 10.6 versus 6.2 months (HR 0.54; P<0.001), response rates were 44.8% versus 34.8% (P=0.004), and median response duration was 10.4 versus 7.1 months. Grade 3 hypertension was more common with bevacizumab (11.0% vs 2.3%) but was described as easily managed.
cards.watchOut: The chemotherapy backbone (bolus IFL) is obsolete, so the size of this survival benefit should not be assumed for modern infusional doublets. The record predates trial registration and carries no registry ID in its databank fields; none is printed on this card.

shelves.title: Total neoadjuvant therapy with watch-and-wait organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer (OPRA)
shelves.question: In locally advanced rectal cancer, does total neoadjuvant therapy with a watch-and-wait option for clinical complete responders achieve organ preservation without compromising disease-free survival versus chemoradiotherapy, total mesorectal excision and adjuvant chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma/drug therapy · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects · Capecitabine · Chemoradiotherapy · Disease-Free Survival · Fluorouracil · Humans · Neoadjuvant Therapy/adverse effects · Neoplasm Staging · Organ Preservation · Oxaliplatin · Prospective Studies · Rectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/pathology
shelves.balance: One randomised phase 2 trial supports the strategy, with an important design caveat. In OPRA (n=324 with stage II–III rectal adenocarcinoma), total neoadjuvant therapy — induction chemotherapy then chemoradiotherapy, or chemoradiotherapy then consolidation chemotherapy — followed by total mesorectal excision or watch-and-wait according to response achieved 3-year disease-free survival of 76% in both sequence groups, matching the 75% rate of the historical controls the trial was designed against. Organ preservation differed by sequence: 3-year TME-free survival was 53% with chemoradiotherapy-then-consolidation and 41% with induction-then-chemoradiotherapy (the drafting topic file's figure of 47% does not appear in the record and is corrected here — no overall-survival claim is made or supported). No differences were found between the groups in local recurrence-free, distant metastasis-free, or overall survival, and patients salvaged with TME after tumour regrowth had similar disease-free survival to those taken straight to TME. The caveat: OPRA was designed as two stand-alone studies benchmarked against historical data, not as a randomised comparison against the standard chemoradiotherapy–TME–adjuvant-chemotherapy pathway, so 'without detriment' rests partly on that historical benchmark. PROPOSED POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: OPRA: total neoadjuvant therapy with response-guided watch-and-wait preserved the rectum in about half of patients (3-year TME-free survival 53% with consolidation sequencing) with 3-year disease-free survival of 76%, matching historical controls
cards.summary: OPRA: total neoadjuvant therapy with response-guided watch-and-wait preserved the rectum in about half of patients (3-year TME-free survival 53% with consolidation sequencing) with 3-year disease-free survival of 76%, matching historical controls
cards.people: 324 patients with stage II or III rectal adenocarcinoma treated with induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy (INCT-CRT) or chemoradiotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy (CRT-CNCT), then total mesorectal excision (TME) or watch-and-wait according to tumour response; median follow-up 3 years. The abstract does not print the arm counts, mean age, or sex split.
cards.result: Three-year disease-free survival was 76% (95% CI 69–84) in the INCT-CRT group and 76% (69–83) in the CRT-CNCT group, in line with the 75% 3-year rate observed historically. Three-year TME-free survival was 41% (95% CI 33–50) in the INCT-CRT group and 53% (45–62) in the CRT-CNCT group. No differences were found between groups in local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, or overall survival. Patients who underwent TME after restaging and those who underwent TME after regrowth had similar disease-free survival rates.
cards.watchOut: The trial was designed as two stand-alone studies with disease-free survival compared against a historical null (75%), not as a head-to-head randomised comparison with the standard pathway — the 'no detriment' conclusion leans on that benchmark. The drafting topic file quoted a 47% organ-preservation figure; the record prints 41% and 53%, and the record governs.
cards.source: Garcia-Aguilar J et al. Organ Preservation in Patients With Rectal Adenocarcinoma Treated With Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (OPRA). Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2022. PMID: 35483010. Registry ID: NCT02008656, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Oxaliplatin HIPEC added to cytoreductive surgery for colorectal peritoneal metastases (PRODIGE 7)
shelves.question: In colorectal peritoneal metastases undergoing complete cytoreductive surgery, does adding oxaliplatin HIPEC improve overall survival versus cytoreductive surgery alone?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/administration & dosage · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/pathology/surgery · Combined Modality Therapy/adverse effects · Cytoreduction Surgical Procedures · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Fluorouracil/administration & dosage · France · Humans · Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy/adverse effects · Male · Middle Aged · Oxaliplatin/administration & dosage · Peritoneal Neoplasms/drug therapy/pathology/secondary/surgery · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: A single phase 3 trial overturned an entrenched practice. In PRODIGE 7 (n=265 patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases in whom complete or near-complete cytoreduction was achieved), adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to cytoreductive surgery produced median overall survival of 41.7 months versus 41.2 months with surgery alone — a hazard ratio of 1.00 (95.37% CI 0.63–1.58; p=0.99), as flat a null as a trial prints. Treatment-related deaths at 30 days were 2% in each group, but by 60 days grade 3 or worse adverse events were more frequent with HIPEC (26% vs 15%; p=0.035). The confidence interval is wide — the trial cannot exclude a moderate benefit or harm — which is why the stamp is POSSIBLE rather than LIKELY: the point estimate is exactly null and the practice-changing weight of the trial is high, but it is one trial of 265 patients. Balance: oxaliplatin HIPEC as delivered in PRODIGE 7 adds late morbidity and no survival; cytoreductive surgery alone is the cornerstone. PROPOSED POSSIBLE (the treatment made no difference) pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: PRODIGE 7: adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to complete cytoreductive surgery did not improve overall survival in colorectal peritoneal metastases — median 41.7 versus 41.2 months, HR 1.00, p=0.99 — and increased late grade ≥3 complications
cards.summary: PRODIGE 7: adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to complete cytoreductive surgery did not improve overall survival in colorectal peritoneal metastases — median 41.7 versus 41.2 months, HR 1.00, p=0.99 — and increased late grade ≥3 complications
cards.people: 265 patients aged 18–70 at 17 French centres with colorectal peritoneal metastases (Peritoneal Cancer Index ≤25) in whom complete macroscopic resection or resection with <1 mm residual tumour was completed; 133 assigned to cytoreductive surgery plus oxaliplatin HIPEC and 132 to cytoreductive surgery alone, all also receiving systemic chemotherapy. The abstract does not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: After a median follow-up of 63.8 months, median overall survival was 41.7 months (95% CI 36.2–53.8) with HIPEC versus 41.2 months (35.1–49.7) without (HR 1.00; 95.37% CI 0.63–1.58; stratified log-rank p=0.99). At 30 days, two treatment-related deaths (2%) had occurred in each group, and grade 3 or worse adverse events were 42% versus 32% (p=0.083); at 60 days, grade 3 or worse adverse events were more common in the HIPEC group (26% vs 15%; p=0.035).
cards.watchOut: The 95.37% confidence interval (0.63–1.58) is wide: the trial rules out a large benefit, not a moderate one. The verdict applies to oxaliplatin HIPEC given for 30 minutes as in this protocol; other agents and durations were not tested.
cards.source: Quénet F et al. Cytoreductive Surgery Plus Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy Versus Cytoreductive Surgery Alone for Colorectal Peritoneal Metastases (PRODIGE 7). The Lancet Oncology. 2021. PMID: 33476595. Registry ID: NCT00769405, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Perioperative FOLFOX for resectable colorectal liver metastases (EORTC 40983): a progression-free-survival gain that did not become a survival gain
shelves.question: In resectable colorectal liver metastases, does perioperative FOLFOX improve progression-free survival versus surgery alone, and does the benefit persist as overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Colorectal Neoplasms/pathology · Combined Modality Therapy · Female · Fluorouracil/administration & dosage · Humans · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy/secondary/surgery · Male · Middle Aged · Organoplatinum Compounds/administration & dosage · Oxaliplatin · Perioperative Care/methods
shelves.balance: One trial answers both halves of the question, and the two halves diverge. In EORTC 40983 (n=364 with up to four resectable liver metastases), perioperative FOLFOX4 (six cycles before and six after surgery) raised 3-year progression-free survival from 28.1% to 35.4% in the intention-to-treat analysis — an absolute gain of 7.3 points that narrowly missed significance (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62–1.02, p=0.058) and was significant in the eligible (HR 0.77, p=0.041) and resected (HR 0.73, p=0.025) populations. With 8.5 years of median follow-up, however, overall survival showed no difference: median 61.3 versus 54.3 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.68–1.14, p=0.34), 5-year survival 51.2% versus 47.8%, deaths 59% versus 63%. Postoperative complications were more frequent after chemotherapy (25% vs 16%; p=0.04). No mortality claim is made or supported by this shelf: overall survival was not the trial's primary endpoint, the comparison was underpowered for it, and the honest summary is a progression-free-survival benefit that did not persist as a survival benefit. PROPOSED POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: EORTC 40983: perioperative FOLFOX4 improved 3-year progression-free survival around liver-metastasis resection (35.4% vs 28.1% intention-to-treat) but long-term overall survival was not different (HR 0.88, p=0.34)
cards.summary: EORTC 40983: perioperative FOLFOX4 improved 3-year progression-free survival around liver-metastasis resection (35.4% vs 28.1% intention-to-treat) but long-term overall survival was not different (HR 0.88, p=0.34)
cards.type: Randomized trial (phase 3; primary progression-free-survival report and its long-term overall-survival report, one trial)
cards.people: 364 patients with histologically proven colorectal cancer and up to four resectable liver metastases, randomised 182 to perioperative FOLFOX4 plus surgery and 182 to surgery alone (171 eligible per group; 151–152 resected per group). The abstracts do not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: Primary report: the absolute increase in 3-year progression-free survival was 7.3 points (28.1% to 35.4%; HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.62–1.02; p=0.058) in randomised patients, 8.1 points (HR 0.77; p=0.041) in eligible patients, and 9.2 points (HR 0.73; p=0.025) in resected patients. Reversible postoperative complications occurred more often after chemotherapy (25% vs 16%; p=0.04); 139 patients had died at that report (64 vs 75). Long-term report (median follow-up 8.5 years): 107 (59%) patients in the chemotherapy group and 114 (63%) in the surgery group had died (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.68–1.14; p=0.34); median overall survival was 61.3 versus 54.3 months and 5-year overall survival 51.2% versus 47.8%.
cards.watchOut: The two reports are one trial counted once: the 2008 report is the primary progression-free-survival analysis, the 2013 report its pre-planned long-term survival follow-up. The intention-to-treat progression-free-survival result narrowly missed significance (p=0.058); the significant figures come from the eligible and resected subsets, flagged as such. The trial authors concluded perioperative FOLFOX4 should remain the reference treatment on the strength of the progression benefit despite the null survival result — that judgment goes beyond the carded numbers and is noted, not endorsed, here.

shelves.title: First-line cetuximab versus bevacizumab with chemotherapy in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (FIRE-3; CALGB/SWOG 80405)
shelves.question: In KRAS/RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, is FOLFIRI plus cetuximab superior to FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab as first-line therapy?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Austria · Bevacizumab · Camptothecin/analogs & derivatives/therapeutic use · Cetuximab · Colorectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Disease-Free Survival · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Fluorouracil/therapeutic use · Germany · Humans · Infusions, Intravenous · Leucovorin/therapeutic use · Male · Maximum Tolerated Dose · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Invasiveness/pathology · Neoplasm Staging · Patient Selection · Prognosis · Survival Rate · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult
shelves.balance: The two head-to-head trials disagree, and the disagreement is the answer. FIRE-3 (n=592, Germany/Austria, FOLFIRI backbone) MISSED its primary endpoint — objective response 62.0% on cetuximab versus 58.0% on bevacizumab (OR 1.18, p=0.18) — with no progression-free-survival difference (10.0 vs 10.3 months; HR 1.06), yet reported longer overall survival with cetuximab (28.7 vs 25.0 months; HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.62–0.96, p=0.017), an advantage that grew in the post-hoc extended-RAS wild-type subgroup (33.1 vs 25.0 months; HR 0.70) — a subgroup analysis, labelled as such on the card, not the randomised primary population. CALGB/SWOG 80405 (n=1,137, North America, physician-choice FOLFOX or FOLFIRI backbone, overall survival as the PRIMARY endpoint) found no significant difference: median overall survival 30.0 versus 29.0 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77–1.01, P=.08), progression-free survival HR 0.95, response 59.6% versus 55.2% (P=.13). The trials differ in backbone, geography and era, and neither carded record provides the tumour-sidedness analysis that later came to dominate this choice, so no sidedness figures are carded here. Balance: cetuximab-first is not proven superior; FIRE-3's survival signal is real but rests on a secondary endpoint and a post-hoc subgroup against a larger trial whose primary survival analysis was null. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: FIRE-3: FOLFIRI plus cetuximab missed its primary response endpoint versus FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab (62.0% vs 58.0%, p=0.18) but showed longer overall survival (28.7 vs 25.0 months, HR 0.77), larger in a post-hoc extended-RAS analysis
cards.summary: FIRE-3: FOLFIRI plus cetuximab missed its primary response endpoint versus FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab (62.0% vs 58.0%, p=0.18) but showed longer overall survival (28.7 vs 25.0 months, HR 0.77), larger in a post-hoc extended-RAS analysis
cards.type: Randomized trial (open-label, phase 3; primary report and its post-hoc final-RAS-subgroup report, one trial)
cards.people: 592 patients aged 18–75 with KRAS exon 2 wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer in Germany and Austria; 297 assigned to FOLFIRI plus cetuximab and 295 to FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. The post-hoc analysis covers the final RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2–4) wild-type subgroup of 400 patients. The abstracts do not print a mean age or the sex split.
cards.result: Primary report: objective response was 62.0% in the cetuximab group versus 58.0% in the bevacizumab group (OR 1.18; 95% CI 0.85–1.64; p=0.18) — the primary endpoint was not met. Median progression-free survival was 10.0 versus 10.3 months (HR 1.06; 95% CI 0.88–1.26; p=0.55). Median overall survival was 28.7 versus 25.0 months (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.62–0.96; p=0.017). The most common grade ≥3 adverse events were haematotoxicity (25% vs 21%), skin reactions (26% vs 2%) and diarrhoea (11% vs 14%). Post-hoc report (final RAS wild-type subgroup, n=400): median overall survival 33.1 versus 25.0 months (HR 0.70; 0.54–0.90; p=0.0059), with centrally reviewed response (72.0% vs 56.1%), early tumour shrinkage (68.2% vs 49.1%) and depth of response (−48.9% vs −32.3%) all favouring cetuximab while investigator-assessed response and progression-free survival remained comparable.
cards.watchOut: The survival advantage appears on a secondary endpoint after the primary response endpoint failed, and the larger effect comes from a post-hoc redefinition of the biomarker population — both flagged here; the authors' interpretation that cetuximab 'could be the preferred' regimen goes beyond what a missed-primary trial establishes alone.
cards.source: Heinemann V et al. FOLFIRI Plus Cetuximab Versus FOLFIRI Plus Bevacizumab as First-Line Treatment for Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer (FIRE-3). The Lancet Oncology. 2014. The Lancet Oncology. 2016. PMID: 27575024. Registry ID: NCT00433927, from both records' databank fields. cards.headline: CALGB/SWOG 80405: with overall survival as the primary endpoint, cetuximab was NOT significantly better than bevacizumab added to first-line chemotherapy (30.0 vs 29.0 months, HR 0.88, P=.08)
cards.summary: CALGB/SWOG 80405: with overall survival as the primary endpoint, cetuximab was NOT significantly better than bevacizumab added to first-line chemotherapy (30.0 vs 29.0 months, HR 0.88, P=.08)
cards.people: 1,137 patients with untreated KRAS wild-type advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer in the United States and Canada, randomised to cetuximab (n=578) or bevacizumab (n=559) added to a physician-choice backbone of mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI; median age 59 years, 39% women.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 30.0 months in the cetuximab group and 29.0 months in the bevacizumab group (stratified HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.77–1.01; P=.08) — not significant on the trial's primary endpoint. Median progression-free survival was 10.5 versus 10.6 months (HR 0.95; 95% CI 0.84–1.08; P=.45), and response rates were 59.6% versus 55.2% (P=.13). Median follow-up of surviving patients was 47.4 months, and 82% of patients had progressed.
cards.watchOut: CALGB 80405 enrolled a KRAS exon-2 wild-type population with a mixed chemotherapy backbone (physician choice), unlike FIRE-3's all-FOLFIRI design — design differences, not just chance, may explain the discordance. Extended-RAS and sidedness analyses of this trial are not in this record and are not carded.

shelves.title: Adjuvant low-dose aspirin in PI3K-altered localised colorectal cancer (ALASCCA) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
shelves.question: In resected stage I–III colorectal cancer with PI3K-pathway alterations (PIK3CA / PIK3R1 / PTEN), does low-dose aspirin reduce recurrence versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Aspirin/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Class I Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinases/genetics · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Mutation · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/epidemiology/genetics/prevention & control · Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinases/genetics · PTEN Phosphohydrolase/genetics · Colonic Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/pathology · Rectal Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/pathology · Neoplasm Staging · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Incidence · Biomarkers, Tumor/genetics · Class Ia Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase/genetics · Aged, 80 and over
shelves.balance: OUTSTANDING-SINGLE: one double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a recurrence risk roughly halved in a biomarker-defined population, flagged under the developer's standing rule for outstanding single trials. In ALASCCA (626 patients randomised from 2,980 genotyped; PI3K-pathway alterations found in 37.0%), aspirin 160 mg daily for 3 years cut the estimated 3-year recurrence incidence from 14.1% to 7.7% in the pre-specified primary group with PIK3CA exon 9/20 hotspot mutations (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24–0.98, P=0.04) and from 16.8% to 7.7% in the broader group with other PIK3CA/PIK3R1/PTEN alterations (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21–0.83). Disease-free survival favoured aspirin in both groups (HR 0.61 in group A, not significant; HR 0.51 in group B), and severe adverse events were more frequent on aspirin (16.8% vs 11.6%). The cautious points: the confidence intervals are wide, the group A result rests on P=0.04, and this is a recurrence endpoint — the record makes NO mortality claim, and none is carded. Until a second trial or a survival analysis appears, this stays a single-trial shelf the developer may card as OUTSTANDING-SINGLE. PROPOSED POSSIBLE.

cards.summary: ALASCCA: aspirin 160 mg daily for 3 years halved 3-year recurrence in resected PI3K-altered colorectal cancer — 7.7% versus 14.1% in the primary PIK3CA hotspot group (HR 0.49) and 7.7% versus 16.8% in the broader alteration group (HR 0.42)

cards.result: The estimated 3-year cumulative incidence of recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo in group A (HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.24–0.98; P=0.04 — the primary endpoint) and 7.7% versus 16.8% in group B (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.21–0.83). Estimated 3-year disease-free survival was 88.5% versus 81.4% in group A (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.34–1.08) and 89.1% versus 78.7% in group B (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.29–0.88). Severe adverse events occurred in 16.8% of aspirin recipients and 11.6% of placebo recipients.

shelves.title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (DESTINY-Breast04) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
shelves.question: In previously treated HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH−) metastatic breast cancer, does trastuzumab deruxtecan improve progression-free and overall survival versus physician's-choice chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/metabolism/secondary · Camptothecin/analogs & derivatives · Disease Progression · Female · Humans · Immunoconjugates/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Immunohistochemistry · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases/analysis/biosynthesis/genetics · Trastuzumab/adverse effects/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: OUTSTANDING-SINGLE: one open-label trial that created a new treatment category and showed a survival benefit in it. In DESTINY-Breast04 (n=557 with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after one or two lines of chemotherapy), trastuzumab deruxtecan beat physician's-choice chemotherapy on every pre-specified endpoint: in the hormone-receptor-positive cohort (494 patients), median progression-free survival was 10.1 versus 5.4 months (HR 0.51) and overall survival 23.9 versus 17.5 months (HR 0.64, P=0.003); among all patients, overall survival was 23.4 versus 16.8 months (HR 0.64, P=0.001). Grade ≥3 adverse events were actually less frequent on the conjugate (52.6% vs 67.4%), but its signature harm is interstitial lung disease: adjudicated drug-related ILD or pneumonitis in 12.1%, with grade 5 events in 0.8%. The stamp is POSSIBLE, not LIKELY, because the result stands on a single — albeit large and internally consistent — open-label trial; distinct from the HER2-positive comparison on Shelf #856 (trastuzumab deruxtecan versus T-DM1), this shelf's question is the HER2-low population. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

The abstract does not print a mean age.
cards.result: In the hormone-receptor-positive cohort, median progression-free survival was 10.1 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan versus 5.4 months with physician's-choice chemotherapy (HR for progression or death 0.51; P<0.001), and overall survival was 23.9 versus 17.5 months (HR for death 0.64; P=0.003). Among all patients, median progression-free survival was 9.9 versus 5.1 months (HR 0.50; P<0.001) and overall survival 23.4 versus 16.8 months (HR 0.64; P=0.001). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 52.6% of the trastuzumab-deruxtecan group versus 67.4% of the chemotherapy group. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 12.1% of trastuzumab-deruxtecan patients, with grade 5 events in 0.8%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label against a heterogeneous physician's-choice comparator; the survival result is strong but single-trial. The interstitial-lung-disease risk (12.1%, occasionally fatal) is intrinsic to the drug and part of the balance. shelves.title: PD-(L)1 blockade plus chemotherapy in advanced triple-negative breast cancer (KEYNOTE-355; IMpassion130)
shelves.question: In untreated PD-L1-positive (CPS ≥10) advanced triple-negative breast cancer, does pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improve overall survival versus chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · B7-H1 Antigen/biosynthesis/genetics · Humans · Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/metabolism
shelves.balance: For the question as posed — pembrolizumab in CPS ≥10 disease — a double-blind trial answers yes. In KEYNOTE-355 (n=847), pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved median overall survival in the CPS ≥10 subgroup from 16.1 to 23.0 months (HR for death 0.73, 95% CI 0.55–0.95; two-sided P=0.0185, the pre-set significance criterion met), while the broader CPS ≥1 subgroup was not significant (HR 0.86; P=0.1125) and the intention-to-treat analysis (HR 0.89) was not formally tested — the benefit is bounded by the CPS ≥10 biomarker gate, and grade 3–5 regimen-related adverse events were similar (68.1% vs 66.9%). The class contrast is sobering: IMpassion130 (n=902), testing atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel, improved progression-free survival (ITT HR 0.80) but its intention-to-treat overall survival was not significant (21.3 vs 17.6 months; HR 0.84; P=0.08), which stopped the hierarchical testing — so its striking PD-L1-positive survival figures (25.0 vs 15.5 months; HR 0.62) are descriptive only, never formally tested, and its PD-L1-positive definition differs from KEYNOTE-355's combined positive score. Balance: pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy prolongs survival in CPS ≥10 triple-negative disease; the atezolizumab experience shows the class effect cannot be assumed across agents and assays. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

In the CPS ≥1 subgroup, median overall survival was 17.6 versus 16.0 months (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.72–1.04; two-sided P=0.1125 — not significant). In the intention-to-treat population, median overall survival was 17.2 versus 15.5 months (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.76–1.05; significance not tested). shelves.title: Sacituzumab govitecan in heavily pretreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (ASCENT) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
shelves.question: In metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after ≥2 prior lines, does sacituzumab govitecan improve progression-free and overall survival versus single-agent chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antigens, Neoplasm · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Camptothecin/adverse effects/analogs & derivatives · Cell Adhesion Molecules/antagonists & inhibitors · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm · Female · Humans · Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors/therapeutic use · Immunoconjugates/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/drug therapy · Progression-Free Survival · Survival Analysis · Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality · Tumor Burden
shelves.balance: OUTSTANDING-SINGLE: one open-label trial with an unusually large effect in refractory disease. In ASCENT's primary population (468 patients without brain metastases, all previously treated with taxanes), sacituzumab govitecan tripled median progression-free survival (5.6 vs 1.7 months; HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.32–0.52) and nearly doubled median overall survival (12.1 vs 6.7 months; HR for death 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.59), with response in 35% versus 5%. The harms are myelosuppression and gastrointestinal toxicity: grade ≥3 neutropenia 51% versus 33%, diarrhoea 10% versus <1%, febrile neutropenia 6% versus 2%; three adverse-event deaths occurred in each group, none attributed to sacituzumab. The stamp is POSSIBLE, not LIKELY, because this remains a single trial — but its effect size (a death hazard ratio of 0.48 in a population with a 6.7-month median survival on standard chemotherapy) is exactly the outstanding hard-endpoint result the developer's standing rule wants surfaced on one trial. cards.headline: ASCENT: sacituzumab govitecan nearly doubled overall survival in relapsed/refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (12.1 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.48) and tripled progression-free survival (HR 0.41)
cards.summary: ASCENT: sacituzumab govitecan nearly doubled overall survival in relapsed/refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (12.1 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.48) and tripled progression-free survival (HR 0.41)
cards.people: 468 patients without brain metastases with relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer — 235 assigned to sacituzumab govitecan and 233 to single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine); median age 54 years, and all patients had previously received taxanes. (Patients with brain metastases were enrolled separately and are not in this primary population.)
cards.result: Median progression-free survival (blinded independent central review) was 5.6 months (95% CI 4.3–6.3) with sacituzumab govitecan versus 1.7 months (1.5–2.6) with chemotherapy (HR for progression or death 0.41; 95% CI 0.32–0.52; P<0.001). Median overall survival was 12.1 months (10.7–14.0) versus 6.7 months (5.8–7.7) (HR for death 0.48; 95% CI 0.38–0.59; P<0.001). Objective response occurred in 35% versus 5%. Key grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were neutropenia (51% vs 33%), leukopenia (10% vs 5%), diarrhoea (10% vs <1%), anaemia (8% vs 5%) and febrile neutropenia (6% vs 2%). Three deaths owing to adverse events occurred in each group; none was considered related to sacituzumab govitecan.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the primary population excludes patients with brain metastases — the carded figures do not cover that subgroup. The comparator was single-agent chemotherapy with a median survival under 7 months, which frames the size of the relative benefit.

shelves.title: Ribociclib plus endocrine therapy and overall survival in HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (MONALEESA-2; MONALEESA-3)
shelves.question: In postmenopausal HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, does adding ribociclib to letrozole improve overall survival versus letrozole alone?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Aminopyridines/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Female · Humans · Intention to Treat Analysis · Letrozole/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Grading · Neutropenia/chemically induced · Purines/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Receptors, Estrogen · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: Two double-blind trials of ribociclib plus endocrine therapy show significant overall-survival benefits. In MONALEESA-2 (n=668, first-line letrozole in postmenopausal patients), the protocol-specified final survival analysis after a median 6.6 years of follow-up showed median overall survival of 63.9 months with ribociclib versus 51.4 months with placebo — more than a year longer (HR for death 0.76, 95% CI 0.63–0.93, P=0.008; deaths 54.2% vs 65.6%). In MONALEESA-3 (n=726, ribociclib plus fulvestrant as first- or second-line therapy), the protocol-specified survival analysis likewise favoured ribociclib (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.57–0.92, P=0.00455; estimated 42-month survival 57.8% vs 45.9%). Neither record reports new safety signals in these analyses. Two boundaries: the shelf answers the ribociclib question — whether the other CDK4/6 inhibitors share the survival benefit is a separate question whose trials are not carded here — and the adjuvant/early-breast-cancer CDK4/6 question is homed on Shelf #365, not here. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.summary: MONALEESA-3: ribociclib plus fulvestrant also improved overall survival (HR 0.72, P=0.00455; 42-month survival 57.8% vs 45.9%)
cards.type: Randomized trial (double-blind, phase 3; protocol-specified overall-survival analysis)
cards.people: 726 postmenopausal patients with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer receiving ribociclib or placebo plus fulvestrant as first-line or second-line treatment, randomised 2:1 — 484 to ribociclib and 242 to placebo. The abstract does not print a mean age.
cards.result: At this protocol-specified second interim survival analysis, based on 275 deaths — 167 among 484 patients (34.5%) receiving ribociclib and 108 among 242 (44.6%) receiving placebo — ribociclib plus fulvestrant showed a significant overall-survival benefit: estimated overall survival at 42 months was 57.8% (95% CI 52.0–63.2) versus 45.9% (36.9–54.5) (HR for death 0.72; 95% CI 0.57–0.92; P=0.00455), consistent across most subgroups. The record does not print median overall survival, so none is carded.

shelves.title: Adjuvant olaparib in germline BRCA1/2-mutated high-risk early breast cancer (OlympiA) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
shelves.question: In germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative early breast cancer at high recurrence risk after chemotherapy, does one year of adjuvant olaparib improve invasive disease-free and overall survival versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/surgery · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Genes, BRCA1 · Genes, BRCA2 · Germ-Line Mutation · Humans · Mastectomy · Middle Aged · Phthalazines/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Piperazines/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerase Inhibitors/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases
shelves.balance: OUTSTANDING-SINGLE: one double-blind trial, and the first to show a survival benefit from adjuvant PARP inhibition. In OlympiA (n=1,836 patients with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants and high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer after local treatment and (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy), one year of olaparib improved 3-year invasive disease-free survival from 77.1% to 85.9% (HR 0.58; 99.5% CI 0.41–0.82) at the first interim analysis; deaths were fewer on olaparib (59 vs 86; HR 0.68) but that difference did NOT cross the strict interim significance boundary (P<0.01 required; P=0.02 observed) — a boundary detail earlier summaries often drop, kept on the card here. At the pre-specified second interim analysis (median follow-up 3.5 years), overall survival did cross its boundary: HR 0.68 (98.5% CI 0.47–0.97; P=0.009 against a required P<0.015), with 4-year overall survival 89.8% versus 86.4% and 4-year invasive disease-free survival 82.7% versus 75.4%; no new safety signals and no new cases of acute myeloid leukaemia or myelodysplastic syndrome. The ovarian-cancer PARP-inhibitor questions are a different diagnosis and are homed on Shelf #364, not here. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.summary: OlympiA: one year of adjuvant olaparib improved invasive disease-free survival (3-year 85.9% vs 77.1%, HR 0.58) and, at the second interim analysis, overall survival (HR 0.68, boundary crossed) in germline BRCA1/2-mutated high-risk early breast cancer
cards.type: Randomized trial (double-blind, phase 3; primary report and pre-specified second-interim overall-survival report, one trial) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
cards.people: 1,836 patients with HER2-negative early breast cancer, germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, and high-risk clinicopathological factors, after local treatment and neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy; randomised 1:1 to one year of oral olaparib or placebo. The abstracts do not print a mean age.
cards.result: Primary report (median follow-up 2.5 years): 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% with olaparib versus 77.1% with placebo (difference 8.8 percentage points; HR for invasive disease or death 0.58; 99.5% CI 0.41–0.82; P<0.001), and 3-year distant disease-free survival was 87.5% versus 80.4% (HR 0.57; P<0.001). Deaths were fewer with olaparib (59 vs 86; HR 0.68; 99% CI 0.44–1.05; P=0.02), but this did not meet the interim-analysis boundary of P<0.01. Second-interim report (median follow-up 3.5 years): overall survival improved significantly (HR 0.68; 98.5% CI 0.47–0.97; P=0.009, against a required P<0.015); 4-year overall survival was 89.8% versus 86.4% (difference 3.4 percentage points), 4-year invasive disease-free survival 82.7% versus 75.4%, and 4-year distant disease-free survival 86.5% versus 79.1%. No new safety signals were identified, including no new cases of acute myeloid leukaemia or myelodysplastic syndrome.
cards.watchOut: One trial, counted once across its two reports; the survival benefit is real but young (4-year absolute difference 3.4 points) and the population is narrowly defined — germline BRCA1/2 carriers with high-risk features after chemotherapy. This record's second report carries a corrupted MeSH list in the database (it includes the unrelated heading 'Gold Alloys'); the MeSH printed on this card is from the trial's primary report, as disclosed here.

shelves.title: Omitting adjuvant chemotherapy guided by the 21-gene recurrence score in HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer (TAILORx; RxPONDER)
shelves.question: In HR-positive/HER2-negative node-negative (and 1–3-node) early breast cancer with intermediate genomic risk, can adjuvant chemotherapy be omitted without compromising invasive disease-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Age Factors · Aged · Antineoplastic Agents, Hormonal/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/surgery · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Gene Expression Profiling · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Invasiveness · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/genetics/prevention & control · Prospective Studies · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Receptors, Estrogen · Receptors, Progesterone · Young Adult
shelves.balance: Two large prospective randomised trials answer this with an age/menopause boundary, not a blanket yes. In TAILORx (6,711 randomised patients with node-negative disease and recurrence scores of 11–25), endocrine therapy alone was noninferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease-free survival (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.94–1.24), with 9-year invasive disease-free survival of 83.3% versus 84.3% and overall survival of 93.9% versus 93.8% — but the treatment effect varied with age and score (interaction P=0.004), with some chemotherapy benefit in women aged 50 or younger with scores of 16–25. In RxPONDER (5,083 patients with 1–3 positive nodes and scores of 25 or lower), postmenopausal women gained nothing from chemotherapy (5-year invasive disease-free survival 91.9% endocrine-only vs 91.3% chemoendocrine; HR 1.02, P=0.89), while premenopausal women clearly benefited (89.0% vs 93.9%; HR 0.60, P=0.002; interaction P=0.008). No mortality claim is made or supported by this shelf — the carded endpoints are invasive disease-free survival, and the survival rates printed (TAILORx 9-year overall survival ~94% in both arms) show no difference. Balance: chemotherapy can be omitted in postmenopausal patients within these score ranges, node-negative or 1–3-node; younger and premenopausal patients are the exception, not the rule. PROPOSED LIKELY.

cards.result: Endocrine therapy was noninferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease-free survival (HR for invasive disease recurrence, second primary cancer, or death 1.08; 95% CI 0.94–1.24; P=0.26). At 9 years, invasive disease-free survival was 83.3% with endocrine therapy and 84.3% with chemoendocrine therapy; freedom from distant recurrence was 94.5% versus 95.0%, and overall survival was 93.9% versus 93.8%. The chemotherapy benefit varied with the combination of recurrence score and age (P=0.004 for the interaction), with some benefit of chemotherapy found in women 50 years of age or younger with a recurrence score of 16–25.
cards.watchOut: Noninferiority applies to the randomised score band (11–25) in node-negative disease; scores above 25 were not randomised (those patients were assigned chemotherapy), and the younger-women subgroup signal is an interaction finding, flagged as such.

cards.summary: RxPONDER: in 1–3-node disease with recurrence scores ≤25, postmenopausal women gained nothing from chemotherapy (HR 1.02) while premenopausal women benefited substantially (HR 0.60)
cards.people: 5,083 women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, one to three positive axillary lymph nodes, and a recurrence score of 25 or lower, randomised to endocrine therapy only or chemoendocrine therapy (5,018 participated); 33.2% were premenopausal and 66.8% postmenopausal.
cards.result: The chemotherapy benefit differed by menopausal status (P=0.008 for the interaction), so pre-specified separate analyses were conducted. Among postmenopausal women, 5-year invasive disease-free survival was 91.9% in the endocrine-only group and 91.3% in the chemoendocrine group (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.82–1.26; P=0.89) — no chemotherapy benefit. Among premenopausal women, 5-year invasive disease-free survival was 89.0% with endocrine-only therapy and 93.9% with chemoendocrine therapy (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.43–0.83; P=0.002), with a similar gain in distant relapse-free survival (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.39–0.87; P=0.009). The relative chemotherapy benefit did not increase as the recurrence score increased.
cards.watchOut: Whether the premenopausal 'chemotherapy benefit' is partly an endocrine effect of chemotherapy-induced ovarian suppression cannot be separated within this record — a recognised interpretive caveat; the card reports the randomised comparison as printed.
cards.source: Kalinsky K et al. 21-Gene Assay to Inform Chemotherapy Benefit in Node-Positive Breast Cancer (RxPONDER). The New England Journal of Medicine. 2021. PMID: 34914339. shelves.title: Adjuvant T-DM1 for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer (KATHERINE) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
shelves.question: In HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy, does adjuvant T-DM1 improve invasive disease-free and overall survival versus trastuzumab?
shelves.mesh: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy/metabolism/mortality/therapy · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Lymphatic Metastasis · Maytansine/adverse effects/analogs & derivatives · Middle Aged · Neoadjuvant Therapy · Neoplasm Metastasis · Neoplasm Staging · Neoplasm, Residual · Peripheral Nervous System Diseases/chemically induced · Radiotherapy · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases/metabolism · Trastuzumab/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult
shelves.balance: OUTSTANDING-SINGLE: one open-label trial in the highest-risk early-disease setting, with benefits that grew at final analysis. In KATHERINE (n=1,486 patients with residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after neoadjuvant taxane-plus-trastuzumab therapy), switching adjuvant treatment to T-DM1 halved invasive disease events at the primary analysis (events in 12.2% vs 22.2%; 3-year invasive disease-free survival 88.3% vs 77.0%; HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.39–0.64). At the pre-specified final analysis (median follow-up 8.4 years), the invasive disease-free-survival advantage was sustained (HR 0.54; 7-year rates 80.8% vs 67.1%) and overall survival was significantly better with T-DM1 (HR for death 0.66, 95% CI 0.51–0.87, P=0.003; 7-year overall survival 89.1% vs 84.4%). Grade ≥3 adverse events were more frequent on T-DM1 (26.1% vs 15.7%). The stamp is POSSIBLE because a single trial carries the shelf; its size, consistency and hard-endpoint final analysis are why it is flagged OUTSTANDING-SINGLE rather than treated as a reluctant exception. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: KATHERINE: adjuvant T-DM1 halved invasive disease events versus trastuzumab in residual HER2-positive disease (HR 0.50), and at final analysis improved overall survival (HR 0.66; 7-year 89.1% vs 84.4%)
cards.summary: KATHERINE: adjuvant T-DM1 halved invasive disease events versus trastuzumab in residual HER2-positive disease (HR 0.50), and at final analysis improved overall survival (HR 0.66; 7-year 89.1% vs 84.4%)
cards.type: Randomized trial (open-label, phase 3; primary report and pre-specified final report, one trial) — OUTSTANDING-SINGLE
cards.people: 1,486 patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer and residual invasive disease in the breast or axilla at surgery after neoadjuvant therapy containing a taxane (with or without anthracycline) and trastuzumab; 743 assigned to adjuvant T-DM1 and 743 to trastuzumab, each for 14 cycles. The abstracts do not print a mean age.
cards.result: Primary analysis: invasive disease or death had occurred in 91 patients in the T-DM1 group (12.2%) and 165 in the trastuzumab group (22.2%); estimated 3-year freedom from invasive disease was 88.3% versus 77.0% (HR for invasive disease or death 0.50; 95% CI 0.39–0.64; P<0.001). Distant recurrence as the first event occurred in 10.5% versus 15.9%. Final analysis (median follow-up 8.4 years): the invasive disease-free-survival benefit was sustained (unstratified HR 0.54; 95% CI 0.44–0.66), with 7-year invasive disease-free survival of 80.8% versus 67.1% (difference 13.7 percentage points), and overall survival was significantly better with T-DM1 (unstratified HR for death 0.66; 95% CI 0.51–0.87; P=0.003), with 7-year overall survival of 89.1% versus 84.4% (difference 4.7 percentage points). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 26.1% of the T-DM1 group and 15.7% of the trastuzumab group.
cards.watchOut: One trial counted once across its two reports; open-label (endpoints are objective recurrence/death events, centrally defined). The population is exclusively patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy — the result does not speak to patients achieving pathological complete response.
cards.source: von Minckwitz G et al. Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer (KATHERINE). The New England Journal of Medicine. 2019. PMID: 30516102; and Geyer CE et al. Trastuzumab Emtansine for Residual Invasive HER2-Positive Breast Cancer — Final Analysis. The New England Journal of Medicine. 2025. PMID: 39813643. Registry ID: NCT01772472, from the primary record's databank fields (the final report's record carries no databank fields).
