shelves.title: Adjuvant nivolumab after resection of high-risk urothelial carcinoma (CheckMate 274; AMBASSADOR)
shelves.question: In high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery, does one year of adjuvant PD-1 blockade improve disease-free survival versus no adjuvant therapy?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological · B7-H1 Antigen · Carcinoma, Transitional Cell · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Humans · Intention to Treat Analysis · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Invasiveness · Neoplasm Staging · Nivolumab · Placebos · Quality of Life · Urinary Bladder Neoplasms
shelves.balance: Two phase 3 trials of one year of adjuvant PD-1 blockade after radical surgery for high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma agree closely. CheckMate 274 (709 patients, double-blind, nivolumab vs placebo) doubled median disease-free survival (20.8 vs 10.8 months; HR 0.70), with a larger effect in PD-L1-positive tumours (HR 0.55). AMBASSADOR (702 patients, open-label, pembrolizumab vs observation) found the same class effect with a different antibody and a no-treatment comparator (median disease-free survival 29.6 vs 14.2 months; HR 0.73). Neither carded record establishes an overall-survival benefit — CheckMate 274's primary report is a disease-free-survival analysis and AMBASSADOR's abstract reports its disease-free-survival co-primary end point as met without a survival claim — so this shelf claims delayed recurrence, not longer life. Toxicity is real: grade 3 or higher treatment-related events in 17.9% on nivolumab (including two pneumonitis deaths) and grade 3 or higher events of any attribution in 50.6% on pembrolizumab. PROPOSED LIKELY.

cards.headline: CheckMate 274: adjuvant nivolumab doubled median disease-free survival after radical surgery (20.8 vs 10.8 months; HR 0.70), PD-L1-positive HR 0.55
cards.summary: CheckMate 274: adjuvant nivolumab doubled median disease-free survival after radical surgery (20.8 vs 10.8 months; HR 0.70), PD-L1-positive HR 0.55
cards.people: 709 patients with high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery (neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy before entry was allowed), randomised to nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks or placebo for up to 1 year (353 vs 356). The primary end points were disease-free survival in all patients and in patients whose tumours expressed PD-L1 at 1% or more.
cards.result: Median disease-free survival was 20.8 months (95% CI 16.5 to 27.6) with nivolumab and 10.8 months (95% CI 8.3 to 13.9) with placebo; 74.9% vs 60.3% were alive and disease-free at 6 months (HR for recurrence or death 0.70; 98.22% CI 0.55 to 0.90; P<0.001). In the PD-L1-positive population the 6-month figures were 74.5% vs 55.7% (HR 0.55; 98.72% CI 0.35 to 0.85). Survival free from recurrence outside the urothelial tract also favoured nivolumab (median 22.9 vs 13.7 months; HR 0.72). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 17.9% vs 7.2%, and two treatment-related deaths from pneumonitis occurred in the nivolumab group.
cards.watchOut: The carded record is the primary disease-free-survival report; it makes no overall-survival claim, and none should be read into this shelf. The comparator was placebo in a double-blind design — the cleaner of the two trials on this shelf for both efficacy and adverse-event attribution.
cards.source: Bajorin DF et al. Adjuvant Nivolumab versus Placebo in Muscle-Invasive Urothelial Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2021. PMID: 34077643. Registry ID: NCT02632409, from the record's databank fields. cards.summary: AMBASSADOR: adjuvant pembrolizumab versus observation improved disease-free survival (median 29.6 vs 14.2 months; HR 0.73) — class replication with a second PD-1 antibody
cards.people: 702 patients with high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma after radical surgery, randomised to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 1 year (354) or observation (348), stratified by pathological stage, centrally tested PD-L1 status and previous neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The co-primary end points were disease-free survival and overall survival; median follow-up for disease-free survival was 44.8 months.
cards.result: Median disease-free survival was 29.6 months (95% CI 20.0 to 40.7) with pembrolizumab and 14.2 months (95% CI 11.0 to 20.2) with observation (HR for disease progression or death 0.73; 95% CI 0.59 to 0.90; P=0.003). Grade 3 or higher adverse events regardless of attribution occurred in 50.6% of the pembrolizumab group and 31.6% of the observation group. The abstract reports the disease-free-survival end point as met; it makes no overall-survival claim.
cards.watchOut: Open-label with an observation comparator, so adverse-event rates are all-cause and not comparable with CheckMate 274's treatment-related, placebo-controlled figures — the 50.6% grade ≥3 rate should not be read as pembrolizumab being three times as toxic as nivolumab. The slate-era summary of this trial quoted a disease-free-survival HR of 0.69; the record itself reports 0.73, and 0.73 is what this card uses.

shelves.title: Avelumab maintenance after first-line chemotherapy in advanced urothelial cancer (JAVELIN Bladder 100)
shelves.question: In advanced urothelial cancer without progression after first-line platinum chemotherapy, does switch-maintenance avelumab plus best supportive care improve overall survival versus best supportive care alone?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · B7-H1 Antigen · Carboplatin · Cisplatin · Deoxycytidine · Female · Humans · Maintenance Chemotherapy · Male · Middle Aged · Progression-Free Survival · Survival Analysis · Urologic Neoplasms · Urothelium · Gemcitabine
shelves.balance: A single large randomised trial created this standard, and it is an outstanding single. In JAVELIN Bladder 100, 700 patients whose advanced urothelial cancer had not progressed on four to six cycles of gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin were randomised to maintenance avelumab plus best supportive care or best supportive care alone; overall survival improved (median 21.4 vs 14.3 months; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56–0.86), with 1-year survival of 71.3% vs 58.4% and a larger effect in PD-L1-positive tumours (HR 0.56). The trial was open-label — survival is a hard end point, but adverse-event comparisons (grade 3 or higher: 47.4% vs 25.2%) carry that caveat. No second trial asks the switch-maintenance question. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: JAVELIN Bladder 100: maintenance avelumab after non-progression on first-line chemotherapy prolonged overall survival (median 21.4 vs 14.3 months; HR 0.69)
cards.summary: JAVELIN Bladder 100: maintenance avelumab after non-progression on first-line chemotherapy prolonged overall survival (median 21.4 vs 14.3 months; HR 0.69)
cards.type: Randomized phase 3 trial (open-label; single outstanding trial)
cards.people: 700 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer whose disease had not progressed with first-line chemotherapy (four to six cycles of gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin), randomised to best supportive care with or without maintenance avelumab. The primary end point was overall survival in all randomised patients and in patients with PD-L1-positive tumours.
cards.result: Overall survival at 1 year was 71.3% in the avelumab group and 58.4% in the control group (median overall survival 21.4 vs 14.3 months; HR for death 0.69; 95% CI 0.56 to 0.86; P=0.001) — a 31% relative reduction in the risk of death. In the PD-L1-positive population, 1-year survival was 79.1% vs 60.4% (HR 0.56; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.79). Median progression-free survival was 3.7 vs 2.0 months in the overall population (HR 0.62). Adverse events of any cause occurred in 98.0% vs 77.7%, and grade 3 or higher events in 47.4% vs 25.2%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label and single: the survival end point is objective, but the trial has no replication and its population is selected — only patients who did not progress on platinum chemotherapy were randomised, so the survival times are measured from post-chemotherapy randomisation in chemotherapy-sensitive disease, not from the start of first-line treatment. The claim does not extend to patients whose disease progresses on first-line chemotherapy.
cards.source: Powles T et al. Avelumab Maintenance Therapy for Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2020. PMID: 32945632. Registry ID: NCT02603432, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Chemoradiotherapy for bladder preservation in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (BC2001; BCON)
shelves.question: In muscle-invasive bladder cancer managed with radical radiotherapy, does adding a concurrent radiosensitiser improve locoregional control versus radiotherapy alone?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Combined Modality Therapy · Disease-Free Survival · Dose Fractionation, Radiation · Female · Fluorouracil · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Mitomycin · Neoplasm Invasiveness · Radiotherapy · Survival Rate · Urinary Bladder Neoplasms
shelves.balance: Two randomised trials of two different radiosensitising strategies on a radical-radiotherapy backbone both favour adding treatment. BC2001 (360 patients) added synchronous fluorouracil/mitomycin to radiotherapy and improved 2-year locoregional disease-free survival from 54% to 67% (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48–0.96), with no significant increase in late toxicity; its overall-survival difference was not significant (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.63–1.09) — the treatment made no established difference to survival in that trial. BCON (333 patients) added carbogen breathing and nicotinamide to radiotherapy: its primary end point, cystoscopic control at 6 months, was not significantly improved (81% vs 76%), but 3-year overall survival was 59% vs 46% (P=.04). Read together: concurrent sensitisation improves control of the bladder primary (LIKELY), while the survival picture rests on one trial's secondary end point and is stated here as reported, not claimed. PROPOSED LIKELY.

cards.headline: BC2001: adding synchronous 5-FU/mitomycin to radiotherapy improved locoregional control (2-year 67% vs 54%; HR 0.68); the survival difference was not significant
cards.summary: BC2001: adding synchronous 5-FU/mitomycin to radiotherapy improved locoregional control (2-year 67% vs 54%; HR 0.68); the survival difference was not significant
cards.people: 360 patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer randomised to radiotherapy with or without synchronous chemotherapy — fluorouracil (500 mg/m²/day during fractions 1–5 and 16–20) and mitomycin C (12 mg/m² on day 1). A second randomisation compared whole-bladder with reduced-volume radiotherapy (reported separately). The primary end point was survival free of locoregional disease; median follow-up was 69.9 months.
cards.result: At 2 years, locoregional disease-free survival was 67% (95% CI 59 to 74) with chemoradiotherapy and 54% (95% CI 46 to 62) with radiotherapy alone (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.48 to 0.96; P=0.03). Five-year overall survival was 48% vs 35% (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.63 to 1.09; P=0.16) — the treatment made no established difference to overall survival. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events were slightly more common with chemoradiotherapy during treatment (36.0% vs 27.5%, P=0.07) but not during follow-up (8.3% vs 15.7%, P=0.07).
cards.watchOut: The verified claim is locoregional control, not survival: the overall-survival hazard ratio's confidence interval crosses 1 and the trial's own conclusion is about control. The trial also does not compare chemoradiotherapy with cystectomy — it answers the radiosensitiser question for patients on a bladder-preservation path.

cards.headline: BCON: adding carbogen and nicotinamide to radical radiotherapy — cystoscopic control not significantly improved, but 3-year overall survival 59% vs 46%
cards.summary: BCON: adding carbogen and nicotinamide to radical radiotherapy — cystoscopic control not significantly improved, but 3-year overall survival 59% vs 46%
cards.people: 333 patients with locally advanced bladder carcinoma randomised to radiotherapy alone or radiotherapy with concurrent carbogen breathing and nicotinamide (CON), using schedules of 55 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks or 64 Gy in 32 fractions over 6.5 weeks. The primary end point was cystoscopic control at 6 months; secondary end points included overall survival, local relapse-free survival and morbidity.
cards.result: Cystoscopic control at 6 months was 81% with RT + CON and 76% with RT alone (P=.3) — no significant difference, and only just over half of patients underwent the 6-month cystoscopy. Three-year overall survival estimates were 59% vs 46% (P=.04) and 3-year local relapse-free survival 54% vs 43% (P=.06); the risk of death was 14% lower in relative terms with CON (P=.04), and on multivariate comparison CON significantly reduced the risks of relapse (P=.05) and death (P=.03). Late urinary and gastrointestinal morbidity did not differ significantly.
cards.watchOut: The survival signal comes from secondary end points in a trial whose primary end point was not met, with incomplete cystoscopic follow-up — the right reading is supportive, not definitive, which is why the shelf's claimed benefit is locoregional control across the two trials rather than survival. No registry ID appears in the record's databank fields.

shelves.title: Adjuvant pembrolizumab after nephrectomy in high-risk clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (KEYNOTE-564)
shelves.question: In clear-cell renal cell carcinoma at high recurrence risk after nephrectomy (± metastasectomy), does one year of adjuvant pembrolizumab improve disease-free and overall survival versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological · Carcinoma, Renal Cell · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Humans · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kidney Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Nephrectomy · Recurrence · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: One double-blind placebo-controlled trial carries this shelf, and it is an outstanding single. In KEYNOTE-564, 994 patients with clear-cell renal cell carcinoma at high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy (with or without metastasectomy) received pembrolizumab or placebo for about a year: disease-free survival at 24 months was 77.3% vs 68.1% (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53–0.87), and the interim overall-survival estimate also favoured pembrolizumab (96.6% vs 93.5% alive at 24 months; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30–0.96) — the first adjuvant therapy in this disease to show such a signal, though survival data were immature at this prespecified interim analysis and the confidence interval is wide. The class context cuts the other way and is fenced on the card: other adjuvant checkpoint-inhibitor trials in renal cancer did not meet their end points, so this is a pembrolizumab result, not a class effect. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 32.4% vs 17.7%, with no treatment-related deaths. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-564: adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival after nephrectomy (24-month DFS 77.3% vs 68.1%; HR 0.68), with an immature interim survival signal (HR 0.54)
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-564: adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival after nephrectomy (24-month DFS 77.3% vs 68.1%; HR 0.68), with an immature interim survival signal (HR 0.54)
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (single outstanding trial)
cards.people: 994 patients with clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma at high risk for recurrence after nephrectomy, with or without metastasectomy, randomised to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo intravenously every 3 weeks for up to 17 cycles (approximately 1 year): 496 vs 498. The primary end point was investigator-assessed disease-free survival; overall survival was a key secondary end point. This card reports the prespecified interim analysis, at which the median time from randomisation to data cutoff was 24.1 months.
cards.result: Disease-free survival at 24 months was 77.3% with pembrolizumab and 68.1% with placebo (HR for recurrence or death 0.68; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.87; P=0.002). The estimated percentage alive at 24 months was 96.6% vs 93.5% (HR for death 0.54; 95% CI 0.30 to 0.96). Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause occurred in 32.4% of the pembrolizumab group and 17.7% of the placebo group; no deaths were related to pembrolizumab therapy.
cards.watchOut: Overall survival was immature at this interim analysis — few deaths had occurred, the HR 0.54 rests on small numbers, and this card claims the disease-free-survival result firmly and the survival result only as an early signal. Fenced class context (named, not carded): the adjuvant checkpoint trials CheckMate 914 (nivolumab ± ipilimumab) and IMmotion010 (atezolizumab) did not meet their primary end points, so adjuvant immunotherapy in renal cancer is not a class effect on current evidence.
cards.source: Choueiri TK et al. Adjuvant Pembrolizumab after Nephrectomy in Renal-Cell Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2021. PMID: 34407342. Registry ID: NCT03142334, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Adjuvant VEGF-targeted therapy after nephrectomy in high-risk renal cell carcinoma (S-TRAC versus ASSURE and PROTECT)
shelves.question: In high-risk localized renal cell carcinoma after nephrectomy, does adjuvant VEGF-targeted therapy improve disease-free survival, and at what toxicity cost?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Renal Cell · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Double-Blind Method · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Humans · Indoles · Kidney Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Nephrectomy · Pyrroles · Sunitinib · Survival Analysis · Young Adult
shelves.balance: This is a discordance shelf: four randomised reads of adjuvant VEGF inhibition after nephrectomy, one positive and three negative. S-TRAC (615 patients, double-blind) found one year of sunitinib lengthened median disease-free survival on blinded central review (6.8 vs 5.6 years; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59–0.98). But ASSURE (1,943 patients) found no disease-free-survival difference for sunitinib (HR 1.02) or sorafenib (HR 0.97) against placebo — median disease-free survival was numerically longest on placebo — and PROTECT's primary analysis of pazopanib 600 mg was likewise negative (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.70–1.06), with only its 800-mg secondary cohort positive. No trial shows an overall-survival benefit. The toxicity, by contrast, is consistent everywhere: roughly a third to nearly half of patients needed dose reductions or stopped treatment (ASSURE recorded five deaths related to treatment or within 30 days of it). Balance: a sunitinib disease-free-survival effect may exist (POSSIBLE, one trial), but as a class strategy adjuvant VEGF therapy made no established difference, at substantial cost in tolerability. PROPOSED SPLIT.

cards.headline: S-TRAC: adjuvant sunitinib lengthened median disease-free survival on blinded review (6.8 vs 5.6 years; HR 0.76) — the class's one positive trial, at heavy toxicity
cards.summary: S-TRAC: adjuvant sunitinib lengthened median disease-free survival on blinded review (6.8 vs 5.6 years; HR 0.76) — the class's one positive trial, at heavy toxicity
cards.people: 615 patients with locoregional, high-risk clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma after nephrectomy, randomised to sunitinib 50 mg daily (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) or placebo for 1 year. The primary end point was disease-free survival by blinded independent central review; overall survival data were not mature at the analysis.
cards.result: Median disease-free survival was 6.8 years (95% CI 5.8 to not reached) with sunitinib and 5.6 years (95% CI 3.8 to 6.6) with placebo (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.59 to 0.98; P=0.03). Toxicity was substantial: dose reductions in 34.3% vs 2%, dose interruptions 46.4% vs 13.2%, discontinuations 28.1% vs 5.6%; grade 3 adverse events in 48.4% and grade 4 in 12.1% (vs 15.8% and 3.6% on placebo). Serious adverse events were similar (21.9% vs 17.1%) and no deaths were attributed to toxic effects.
cards.watchOut: The positive result is endpoint- and review-dependent: it is the blinded central review of disease-free survival in one trial, with overall survival immature, and it stands against three negative reads of the same strategy (next cards). A median-DFS gain of about a year bought with a 60% grade 3–4 adverse-event burden is the honest trade this trial offers.
cards.source: Ravaud A et al. Adjuvant Sunitinib in High-Risk Renal-Cell Carcinoma after Nephrectomy. N Engl J Med. 2016. PMID: 27718781. Registry ID: NCT00375674, from the record's databank fields. cards.headline: ASSURE: adjuvant sunitinib and sorafenib both failed against placebo in 1,943 patients (DFS HR 1.02 and 0.97) — the treatment made no difference
cards.summary: ASSURE: adjuvant sunitinib and sorafenib both failed against placebo in 1,943 patients (DFS HR 1.02 and 0.97) — the treatment made no difference
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (three arms)
cards.people: 1,943 patients with completely resected non-metastatic renal-cell carcinoma at high risk of recurrence (high-grade T1b or greater), randomised 1:1:1 to 54 weeks of sunitinib (647), sorafenib (649) or placebo (647). Toxicity-related discontinuation ran so high (44% on sunitinib, 45% on sorafenib among the first 1,323 enrolled) that starting doses were reduced mid-trial and titrated.
cards.result: There were no significant differences in disease-free survival: median 5.8 years for sunitinib (HR 1.02; 97.5% CI 0.85 to 1.23), 6.1 years for sorafenib (HR 0.97; 97.5% CI 0.80 to 1.17) and 6.6 years for placebo — the treatment made no difference, and follow-up was stopped early for low conditional power. The commonest grade 3 or worse events were hypertension (17% sunitinib, 16% sorafenib), hand-foot syndrome (15% and 33%) and fatigue (18% on sunitinib). Five deaths were related to treatment or occurred within 30 days of its end — four in patients receiving sunitinib and one receiving sorafenib. The investigators concluded the results argue against adjuvant use of these drugs.
cards.watchOut: ASSURE enrolled a broader risk spectrum and all histologies (not clear-cell only), and its mid-trial dose reductions complicate a head-to-head reading against S-TRAC — the discordance may be partly population and dosing, not pure chance. Even so, the burden of proof sits with the positive trial when the largest trial of the same drug is null.

cards.headline: PROTECT: adjuvant pazopanib's primary analysis was negative (DFS HR 0.86 for the 600-mg cohort); only the abandoned 800-mg dose cohort was positive
cards.summary: PROTECT: adjuvant pazopanib's primary analysis was negative (DFS HR 0.86 for the 600-mg cohort); only the abandoned 800-mg dose cohort was positive
cards.people: 1,538 patients with resected pT2 (high-grade) or ≥pT3 clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma randomised to pazopanib or placebo for 1 year. shelves.title: Carboplatin versus radiotherapy in stage I seminoma (MRC TE19 / EORTC 30982)
shelves.question: In stage I seminoma after orchidectomy, is one cycle of carboplatin noninferior to adjuvant para-aortic radiotherapy for relapse-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Agents · Carboplatin · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Europe · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Neoplasm Staging · Orchiectomy · Proportional Hazards Models · Prospective Studies · Radiation Dosage · Radiotherapy, Adjuvant · Risk Assessment · Risk Factors · Seminoma · Testicular Neoplasms · Time Factors · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: One large randomised trial answers this, with mature follow-up. TE19 randomised 1,447 men with stage I seminoma after orchidectomy to a single infusion of carboplatin (AUC 7) or para-aortic radiotherapy: 5-year relapse-free rates were 94.7% vs 96.0%, meeting the trial's noninferiority design, and carboplatin clearly reduced contralateral germ-cell tumours (2 vs 15; HR 0.22). Relapse in this disease is highly salvageable — only one seminoma death occurred, in the radiotherapy arm — so the real choice the trial informs is between two effective adjuvant strategies with different late-effect profiles, not between treatment and danger. The modern third option, active surveillance, was not an arm of this trial and is fenced. PROPOSED POSSIBLE: a single trial, however large and mature, on a relapse end point.

cards.headline: TE19: one dose of carboplatin was noninferior to radiotherapy for relapse-free survival in stage I seminoma (5-year 94.7% vs 96.0%) and reduced contralateral tumours (HR 0.22)
cards.summary: TE19: one dose of carboplatin was noninferior to radiotherapy for relapse-free survival in stage I seminoma (5-year 94.7% vs 96.0%) and reduced contralateral tumours (HR 0.22)
cards.type: Randomized noninferiority trial (mature report, median follow-up 6.5 years)
cards.people: 1,447 patients with stage I seminoma after orchidectomy, randomised between a single infusion of carboplatin dosed at AUC 7 (573 patients) and adjuvant radiotherapy (904 patients). The trial was powered to exclude a doubling of the relapse rate (hazard ratio approximately 2.0) against an expected 96–97% 2-year relapse-free rate after radiotherapy. This is the mature report, at a median follow-up of 6.5 years.
cards.result: Relapse-free rates at 5 years were 94.7% for carboplatin and 96.0% for radiotherapy (difference −1.3 percentage points; 90% CI for the difference 0.7% to 3.5% in radiotherapy's favour; HR 1.25; 90% CI 0.83 to 1.89), confirming noninferiority on the trial's terms. There was a clear reduction in contralateral germ-cell tumours with carboplatin (2 vs 15 events; HR 0.22; 95% CI 0.05 to 0.95; P=.03). One death from seminoma occurred, in the radiotherapy arm. Patients who received at least 99% of the intended AUC-7 dose had a 5-year relapse-free rate of 96.1%, versus 92.6% in those who received lower doses (HR 0.51; P=.08).
cards.watchOut: Noninferiority here means 'not unacceptably worse' against a generous margin (the design excluded a doubling of relapses), and the point estimate slightly favours radiotherapy — the choice turns on late effects and patient preference, not on carboplatin being better. Dose adequacy mattered numerically, so the result belongs to full AUC-7 dosing. Active surveillance — now the commonest management of stage I seminoma — was not randomised in this trial and is fenced, not answered.

shelves.title: Second-line therapy after antiangiogenic treatment in advanced renal cell carcinoma: nivolumab and cabozantinib versus everolimus (CheckMate 025; METEOR)
shelves.question: In advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma after antiangiogenic therapy, does nivolumab improve overall survival versus everolimus — and what does the shared-comparator cabozantinib trial show?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Renal Cell · Everolimus · Female · Humans · Kidney Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Nivolumab · Quality of Life · Sirolimus · Survival Analysis · Young Adult
shelves.balance: Everolimus is the shared comparator of the two pivotal second-line trials, and both beat it on survival. CheckMate 025 (821 patients after one or two antiangiogenic regimens) found nivolumab prolonged overall survival versus everolimus (median 25.0 vs 19.6 months; HR 0.73, 98.5% CI 0.57–0.93) with fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related events (19% vs 37%) — despite no progression-free-survival difference (HR 0.88), a dissociation worth teaching. METEOR (658 patients after VEGFR-TKI therapy) found cabozantinib likewise superior to everolimus on survival (median 21.4 vs 16.5 months; HR 0.66), with progression-free survival (HR 0.51) and response (17% vs 3%) also in its favour, at the price of more hypertension and diarrhoea. The third member of the era's family, axitinib (AXIS), showed a progression-free but not survival benefit and is fenced as framing. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: CheckMate 025: nivolumab prolonged overall survival versus everolimus after antiangiogenic therapy (median 25.0 vs 19.6 months; HR 0.73) with fewer severe adverse events
cards.summary: CheckMate 025: nivolumab prolonged overall survival versus everolimus after antiangiogenic therapy (median 25.0 vs 19.6 months; HR 0.73) with fewer severe adverse events
cards.people: 821 patients with advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma previously treated with one or two regimens of antiangiogenic therapy, randomised to nivolumab 3 mg/kg intravenously every 2 weeks or everolimus 10 mg orally daily. The primary end point was overall survival.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 25.0 months (95% CI 21.8 to not estimable) with nivolumab and 19.6 months (95% CI 17.6 to 23.1) with everolimus (HR for death 0.73; 98.5% CI 0.57 to 0.93; P=0.002, meeting the prespecified superiority criterion) — a 27% relative reduction in the risk of death. The objective response rate was 25% vs 5%, but median progression-free survival did not differ significantly (4.6 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.75 to 1.03). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 19% of the nivolumab group and 37% of the everolimus group (commonest: fatigue 2% and anaemia 8%, respectively).
cards.watchOut: Open-label. The survival-without-progression-free-survival pattern is the trial's signature and is reported as found: this shelf does not convert the response or survival result into a progression claim. Everolimus was the era's standard comparator and is a low bar by current sequencing standards — the trial answers nivolumab versus everolimus, not nivolumab versus later-generation options.
cards.source: Motzer RJ et al. Nivolumab versus Everolimus in Advanced Renal-Cell Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2015. PMID: 26406148. Registry ID: NCT01668784, from the record's databank fields. cards.headline: METEOR: cabozantinib beat the same comparator on survival (median 21.4 vs 16.5 months; HR 0.66), progression-free survival (HR 0.51) and response (17% vs 3%)
cards.summary: METEOR: cabozantinib beat the same comparator on survival (median 21.4 vs 16.5 months; HR 0.66), progression-free survival (HR 0.51) and response (17% vs 3%)
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (final overall-survival report)
cards.people: 658 patients with advanced or metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma who had progressed after one or more VEGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, randomised to cabozantinib 60 mg daily (330) or everolimus 10 mg daily (328). This record is the final overall-survival analysis; median follow-up was about 18.7 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 21.4 months (95% CI 18.7 to not estimable) with cabozantinib and 16.5 months (95% CI 14.7 to 18.8) with everolimus (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83; p=0.00026). Progression-free survival (HR 0.51) and objective response (17% vs 3%) also favoured cabozantinib. The commonest grade 3–4 adverse events with cabozantinib were hypertension (15% vs 4%), diarrhoea (13% vs 2%), fatigue (11% vs 7%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia (8% vs 1%); anaemia was commoner on everolimus (17% vs 6%). One treatment-related death occurred on cabozantinib and two on everolimus.
cards.watchOut: METEOR is carded as the shared-comparator companion: it corroborates that everolimus was beatable on survival in this line, but it is a different drug answering its own question, and its survival analysis was an unplanned second interim analysis per the record. It does not compare cabozantinib with nivolumab — no randomised trial here does.
cards.source: Choueiri TK et al. Cabozantinib versus everolimus in advanced renal cell carcinoma (METEOR): final results from a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. Lancet Oncol. 2016. PMID: 27279544. Registry ID: NCT01865747, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Pembrolizumab in platinum-refractory advanced urothelial cancer (KEYNOTE-045; the IMvigor211 contrast)
shelves.question: In advanced urothelial cancer progressing after platinum chemotherapy, does pembrolizumab improve overall survival versus investigator-choice chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents · Docetaxel · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Paclitaxel · Platinum Compounds · Programmed Cell Death 1 Receptor · Survival Analysis · Taxoids · Urologic Neoplasms · Urothelium · Vinblastine
shelves.balance: One positive trial and one instructive failure define this shelf. KEYNOTE-045 (542 patients) found pembrolizumab prolonged overall survival versus investigator-choice chemotherapy after platinum failure (median 10.3 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.59–0.91), with far fewer severe treatment-related events (15.0% vs 49.4%) — despite no progression-free-survival difference (HR 0.98). The discordant sibling matters: IMvigor211 (931 patients) tested the PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in the same setting and missed its primary end point — in the PD-L1-high (IC2/3) population survival was 11.1 vs 10.6 months (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.63–1.21), and the hierarchical design precluded formal testing beyond that. So checkpoint blockade after platinum is not an automatic class effect: the survival claim belongs to pembrolizumab on KEYNOTE-045's evidence. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-045: pembrolizumab prolonged overall survival versus chemotherapy after platinum failure (median 10.3 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.73) with a third of the severe toxicity
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-045: pembrolizumab prolonged overall survival versus chemotherapy after platinum failure (median 10.3 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.73) with a third of the severe toxicity
cards.people: 542 patients with advanced urothelial cancer that recurred or progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy, randomised to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks or the investigator's choice of paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine. The co-primary end points were overall survival and progression-free survival in all patients and in patients with a PD-L1 combined positive score of 10% or more.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 10.3 months (95% CI 8.0 to 11.8) with pembrolizumab versus 7.4 months (95% CI 6.1 to 8.3) with chemotherapy (HR for death 0.73; 95% CI 0.59 to 0.91; P=0.002); in the PD-L1 combined-positive-score ≥10% population, median survival was 8.0 vs 5.2 months (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.37 to 0.88). Progression-free survival did not differ (HR 0.98 in the total population). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3, 4 or 5 occurred in 15.0% of the pembrolizumab group versus 49.4% of the chemotherapy group, and events of any grade in 60.9% vs 90.2%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, with a three-drug investigator-choice comparator. As with CheckMate 025 on Shelf #1877, the survival benefit arrives without a progression-free-survival benefit — the shelf reports both rather than smoothing them over.
cards.source: Bellmunt J et al. Pembrolizumab as Second-Line Therapy for Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma. N Engl J Med. 2017. PMID: 28212060. cards.headline: IMvigor211 (the discordant sibling): atezolizumab missed its primary survival end point in PD-L1-high disease (11.1 vs 10.6 months; HR 0.87, not significant)
cards.summary: IMvigor211 (the discordant sibling): atezolizumab missed its primary survival end point in PD-L1-high disease (11.1 vs 10.6 months; HR 0.87, not significant)
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial — carded as the contrast that disciplines the class claim
cards.people: 931 patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy, randomised to atezolizumab 1200 mg or physician's-choice chemotherapy (vinflunine, paclitaxel or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. The primary end point of overall survival was tested hierarchically: first in the PD-L1 IC2/3 population (expression on ≥5% of tumour-infiltrating immune cells; n=234), then IC1/2/3, then the intention-to-treat population.
cards.result: In the IC2/3 population, overall survival did not differ significantly between atezolizumab and chemotherapy (median 11.1 vs 10.6 months; stratified HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.63 to 1.21; p=0.41) — the treatment made no established difference where the design required the win, and the hierarchy precluded further formal statistical analysis. Objective response rates in IC2/3 were similar (23% vs 22%), though responses on atezolizumab were numerically more durable (median 15.9 vs 8.3 months). In the intention-to-treat population, grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events were fewer with atezolizumab (20% vs 43%), as were discontinuations (7% vs 18%).
cards.watchOut: A negative primary end point under hierarchical testing is not proof of no effect in wider populations — but it is proof the trial did not demonstrate one, and the exploratory intention-to-treat signals cannot be promoted past the failed gate. Differences in the PD-L1 assays and populations between this trial and KEYNOTE-045 mean the two records cannot be merged into a single class estimate.

shelves.title: Erdafitinib in FGFR-altered advanced urothelial cancer (THOR, cohort 1)
shelves.question: In advanced urothelial cancer with susceptible FGFR3/2 alterations after platinum chemotherapy and PD-(L)1 therapy, does erdafitinib improve overall survival versus chemotherapy?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Humans · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carcinoma, Transitional Cell · Docetaxel · Urinary Bladder Neoplasms · Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors · Receptors, Fibroblast Growth Factor · Antineoplastic Agents · Pyrazoles · Quinoxalines · Vinblastine
shelves.balance: One randomised trial answers this, in a biomarker-selected population, and it is an outstanding single. In THOR cohort 1, 266 patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma bearing susceptible FGFR3/2 alterations, all previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and an anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent, were randomised to erdafitinib or investigator-choice chemotherapy: overall survival improved (median 12.1 vs 7.8 months; HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47–0.88), as did progression-free survival (5.6 vs 2.7 months; HR 0.58). Severe toxicity was comparable (grade 3–4 treatment-related events 45.9% vs 46.4%), with fewer treatment-related deaths on erdafitinib (0.7% vs 5.4%). The trial was open-label and the eligible population is the FGFR-altered minority; no second randomised trial of the question exists (the earlier BLC2001 study was single-arm). PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: THOR (cohort 1): erdafitinib prolonged overall survival versus chemotherapy in FGFR-altered urothelial cancer after PD-(L)1 therapy (median 12.1 vs 7.8 months; HR 0.64)
cards.summary: THOR (cohort 1): erdafitinib prolonged overall survival versus chemotherapy in FGFR-altered urothelial cancer after PD-(L)1 therapy (median 12.1 vs 7.8 months; HR 0.64)
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (single outstanding trial; biomarker-selected)
cards.people: 266 patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma and susceptible FGFR3/2 alterations who had progression after one or two previous treatments including an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 agent (and, per the drug's established setting, platinum-containing chemotherapy), randomised to erdafitinib (136) or the investigator's choice of chemotherapy — docetaxel or vinflunine (130). The primary end point was overall survival; median follow-up was 15.9 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 12.1 months with erdafitinib and 7.8 months with chemotherapy (HR for death 0.64; 95% CI 0.47 to 0.88; P=0.005) — a 36% relative reduction in the risk of death. Median progression-free survival was 5.6 vs 2.7 months (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.78). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were similar (45.9% vs 46.4%), and treatment-related deaths were less common with erdafitinib (0.7% vs 5.4%).
cards.watchOut: Open-label and single-trial, in a molecularly selected subgroup: the claim extends only to tumours with susceptible FGFR3/2 alterations tested as the trial tested them, after prior checkpoint therapy. The comparator did not include the antibody–drug conjugates that now populate this line, so the trial ranks erdafitinib against chemotherapy, not against every modern option.

shelves.title: Perioperative FLOT in resectable gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (FLOT4; the MAGIC lineage)
shelves.question: In locally advanced resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, does perioperative FLOT improve overall survival versus perioperative epirubicin-based chemotherapy (ECF/ECX)?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Administration, Oral · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Capecitabine · Cisplatin · Digestive System Surgical Procedures · Disease-Free Survival · Docetaxel · Esophagogastric Junction · Female · Fluorouracil · Humans · Leucovorin · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Staging · Oxaliplatin · Stomach Neoplasms · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: FLOT4 is the trial that matters here, with MAGIC as its historical pillar. FLOT4 (716 patients with locally advanced resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma) randomised perioperative FLOT against the epirubicin-based standard ECF/ECX and improved overall survival (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.63–0.94; median 50 vs 35 months), with similar rates of serious adverse events (27% in both arms) and toxic deaths (2 in each). MAGIC (503 patients) is the trial that created the comparator: perioperative ECF beat surgery alone (HR 0.75; 5-year survival 36% vs 23%), establishing that perioperative chemotherapy helps at all. The two-trial lineage reads: chemotherapy around surgery works (MAGIC), and FLOT is the better chemotherapy (FLOT4). PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: FLOT4: perioperative FLOT improved overall survival versus ECF/ECX (HR 0.77; median 50 vs 35 months)
cards.summary: FLOT4: perioperative FLOT improved overall survival versus ECF/ECX (HR 0.77; median 50 vs 35 months)
cards.people: 716 patients with locally advanced, resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (clinical stage cT2 or higher, and/or node-positive, no distant metastases) at 38 German centres, randomised to perioperative ECF/ECX (360) — three preoperative and three postoperative cycles of epirubicin and cisplatin plus fluorouracil or capecitabine — or perioperative FLOT (356): four preoperative and four postoperative 2-weekly cycles of docetaxel, oxaliplatin, leucovorin and fluorouracil. The primary outcome was overall survival, analysed by intention to treat.
cards.result: Overall survival was increased in the FLOT group (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.63 to 0.94; median overall survival 50 vs 35 months) — a 23% relative reduction in the risk of death. Related serious adverse events were similar (27% in both groups), as were toxic deaths (two in each group) and hospitalisation for toxicity (25% with FLOT vs 26% with ECF/ECX).
cards.watchOut: Open-label, single-country (German) trial, and the comparison is regimen against regimen: FLOT4 cannot say whether perioperative chemotherapy beats surgery alone (that was MAGIC's question), nor how FLOT compares with the chemoradiotherapy approach in junctional tumours (that head-to-head is Shelf #1882's question in oesophageal adenocarcinoma).

cards.summary: MAGIC: perioperative ECF versus surgery alone — the trial that established perioperative chemotherapy (OS HR 0.75; 5-year survival 36% vs 23%)
cards.type: Randomized phase 3 trial (the historical pillar FLOT displaced)
cards.people: 503 patients with resectable adenocarcinoma of the stomach, oesophagogastric junction or lower oesophagus, randomised to perioperative chemotherapy and surgery (250) — three preoperative and three postoperative cycles of epirubicin, cisplatin and infused fluorouracil (ECF) — or surgery alone (253). The primary end point was overall survival; median follow-up was four years.
cards.result: Perioperative ECF improved overall survival (HR for death 0.75; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.93; P=0.009; five-year survival 36% vs 23%) and progression-free survival (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.81). Resected tumours were smaller and less advanced in the chemotherapy group; postoperative complication rates (46% vs 45%) and 30-day deaths were similar.
cards.watchOut: Carded as lineage, not as the shelf's answer: MAGIC's regimen is the one FLOT4 beat, and its surgery-alone comparator belongs to an era before modern staging and D2 surgery were uniform. Its role here is to show the perioperative principle predates FLOT and was itself survival-proven.

shelves.title: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in oesophageal and junctional cancer (CROSS; NEOCRTEC5010)
shelves.question: In resectable oesophageal or oesophagogastric-junction cancer, does neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus surgery improve overall survival versus surgery alone?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carboplatin · Chemoradiotherapy, Adjuvant · Esophageal Neoplasms · Esophagogastric Junction · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoadjuvant Therapy · Paclitaxel · Preoperative Care
shelves.balance: Two randomised trials, in different populations with different chemotherapy backbones, give the same answer. CROSS (366 patients, 75% adenocarcinoma) added weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel with 41.4 Gy before surgery and improved overall survival (median 49.4 vs 24.0 months; HR 0.657, 95% CI 0.495–0.871), with R0 resection in 92% vs 69% and no increase in in-hospital mortality (4% in both arms). NEOCRTEC5010 (451 patients, all squamous-cell carcinoma, China) used cisplatin/vinorelbine with 40 Gy and likewise improved survival (median 100.1 vs 66.5 months; HR 0.71), with a pathological complete response rate of 43.2% and R0 resection in 98.4% vs 91.2%. The principle — chemoradiotherapy before surgery — replicates across histology and regimen; the absolute numbers differ with the populations and should not be averaged. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: CROSS: preoperative chemoradiotherapy improved overall survival versus surgery alone (median 49.4 vs 24.0 months; HR 0.657) and doubled clean-margin resections
cards.summary: CROSS: preoperative chemoradiotherapy improved overall survival versus surgery alone (median 49.4 vs 24.0 months; HR 0.657) and doubled clean-margin resections
cards.people: 368 patients with resectable oesophageal or oesophagogastric-junction cancer enrolled (366 analysed): 275 (75%) adenocarcinoma, 84 (23%) squamous-cell carcinoma, 7 (2%) large-cell undifferentiated carcinoma. Patients were randomised to surgery alone (188) or weekly carboplatin (AUC 2) and paclitaxel (50 mg/m²) for 5 weeks with concurrent radiotherapy (41.4 Gy in 23 fractions) followed by surgery (178).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 49.4 months in the chemoradiotherapy-surgery group versus 24.0 months in the surgery group (HR 0.657; 95% CI 0.495 to 0.871; P=0.003). Complete (R0) resection was achieved in 92% vs 69% (P<0.001), and a pathological complete response in 47 of 161 resected patients (29%) after chemoradiotherapy. Postoperative complications were similar and in-hospital mortality was 4% in both groups; the commonest major toxic effects of chemoradiotherapy were leukopenia (6%) and neutropenia (2%).
cards.watchOut: A mixed-histology, Dutch trial from the pre-immunotherapy era: its surgery-alone comparator makes it the proof of the chemoradiotherapy principle, not a ranking against perioperative chemotherapy — that head-to-head (ESOPEC, in adenocarcinoma) is Shelf #1882. The survival benefit persisted in the trial's long-term follow-up, which is not the carded record here.

cards.headline: NEOCRTEC5010: neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved survival in squamous-cell oesophageal cancer (median 100.1 vs 66.5 months; HR 0.71; pCR 43.2%) — independent replication in SCC
cards.summary: NEOCRTEC5010: neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved survival in squamous-cell oesophageal cancer (median 100.1 vs 66.5 months; HR 0.71; pCR 43.2%) — independent replication in SCC
cards.people: 451 patients with potentially resectable locally advanced thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma (clinically T1-4N1M0 or T4N0M0) in China, randomised to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus surgery (224) — vinorelbine and cisplatin for two cycles with 40.0 Gy in 20 fractions — or surgery alone (227), with McKeown or Ivor Lewis oesophagectomy in both groups. The primary end point was overall survival.
cards.result: The chemoradiotherapy group had a higher R0 resection rate (98.4% vs 91.2%; P=.002), a pathological complete response rate of 43.2%, better median overall survival (100.1 vs 66.5 months; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.96; P=.025) and longer disease-free survival (median 100.1 vs 41.7 months; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.78). Grade 3–4 leukopenia (48.9%) and neutropenia (45.7%) were the commonest severe chemoradiotherapy toxicities; postoperative complications were similar except arrhythmia (13% vs 4.0%), and peritreatment mortality was 2.2% vs 0.4% (P=.212).
cards.watchOut: Squamous-cell carcinoma only, with a cisplatin/vinorelbine backbone and 40 Gy — a different regimen from CROSS; the replication is of the strategy, not the prescription. The surgery-alone arm's median survival (66.5 months) is far longer than CROSS's (24.0 months), reflecting a different population and stage mix; cross-trial absolute comparisons are not licensed.

shelves.title: Perioperative FLOT versus CROSS chemoradiotherapy in oesophageal adenocarcinoma (ESOPEC)
shelves.question: In resectable locally advanced oesophageal adenocarcinoma, is perioperative FLOT chemotherapy superior to CROSS-regimen neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Adenocarcinoma · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carboplatin · Chemoradiotherapy · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Docetaxel · Esophageal Neoplasms · Esophagectomy · Fluorouracil · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Leucovorin · Neoadjuvant Therapy · Oxaliplatin · Paclitaxel · Perioperative Care · Radiotherapy Dosage · Neoplasm Staging · Follow-Up Studies · Aged, 80 and over · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: The first direct head-to-head of the two curative-intent standards favours chemotherapy — on one trial. ESOPEC randomised 438 patients with resectable oesophageal adenocarcinoma to perioperative FLOT plus surgery or CROSS-regimen chemoradiotherapy (41.4 Gy with carboplatin/paclitaxel) plus surgery: at a median follow-up of 55 months, 3-year overall survival was 57.4% vs 50.7% (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53–0.92) and 3-year progression-free survival 51.6% vs 35.0% (HR 0.66). FLOT carried somewhat more grade 3 or higher toxicity (58.0% vs 50.0% of patients starting treatment) but lower 90-day postoperative mortality (3.1% vs 5.6%). There is no second head-to-head trial, and the comparison applies to adenocarcinoma only — squamous disease was not studied here. A single-trial survival claim is capped at POSSIBLE. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: ESOPEC: perioperative FLOT beat CROSS chemoradiotherapy on overall survival in oesophageal adenocarcinoma (3-year 57.4% vs 50.7%; HR 0.70) — the first head-to-head of the two standards
cards.summary: ESOPEC: perioperative FLOT beat CROSS chemoradiotherapy on overall survival in oesophageal adenocarcinoma (3-year 57.4% vs 50.7%; HR 0.70) — the first head-to-head of the two standards
cards.type: Randomized phase 3 trial (open-label; single head-to-head trial)
cards.people: 438 patients with resectable oesophageal adenocarcinoma (clinical stage cT1 node-positive, cT2–4a node-positive, or cT2–4a node-negative; no metastases), randomised 1:1 to perioperative chemotherapy with FLOT plus surgery (221) or preoperative chemoradiotherapy (41.4 Gy with carboplatin and paclitaxel) plus surgery (217). The primary end point was overall survival; median follow-up was 55 months.
cards.result: Overall survival at 3 years was 57.4% (95% CI 50.1 to 64.0) in the FLOT group and 50.7% (95% CI 43.5 to 57.5) in the chemoradiotherapy group (HR for death 0.70; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.92; P=0.01). Progression-free survival at 3 years was 51.6% vs 35.0% (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.85). Among patients who started the assigned treatment, grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 58.0% (FLOT) vs 50.0% (chemoradiotherapy), serious adverse events in 47.3% vs 41.8%, and mortality at 90 days after surgery was 3.1% vs 5.6%.
cards.watchOut: One trial, adenocarcinoma only, and the record reports 3-year survival rates and hazard ratios rather than median survivals — this card uses the record's figures (an earlier slate summary quoted median survivals of 66 vs 37 months, which do not appear in the record and are not used). The chemoradiotherapy arm predates routine adjuvant nivolumab for residual disease (Shelf #1888), which may narrow the gap in current practice; ESOPEC cannot speak to that sequence.

shelves.title: FOLFIRINOX in metastatic pancreatic cancer (PRODIGE 4 / ACCORD 11)
shelves.question: In metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with good performance status, does FOLFIRINOX improve overall survival versus gemcitabine?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Adult · Aged · Antimetabolites, Antineoplastic · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Camptothecin · Deoxycytidine · Female · Fluorouracil · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Irinotecan · Leucovorin · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis · Organoplatinum Compounds · Oxaliplatin · Pancreatic Neoplasms · Proportional Hazards Models · Quality of Life · Severity of Illness Index · Survival Analysis · Gemcitabine
shelves.balance: One trial redefined first-line treatment for fit patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer, and it is an outstanding single. PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 randomised 342 patients with ECOG performance status 0–1 to FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine: overall survival improved by the largest relative margin of the gemcitabine era (median 11.1 vs 6.8 months; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.45–0.73), with progression-free survival (6.4 vs 3.3 months; HR 0.47) and response rate (31.6% vs 9.4%) also strongly in FOLFIRINOX's favour — and, notably, slower quality-of-life deterioration despite more toxicity (febrile neutropenia in 5.4%). The price is real and the population was selected for fitness; the trial says nothing about patients with performance status 2 or worse. No second trial of the same regimen exists; the later NALIRIFOX regimen is a different question and is fenced. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11: FOLFIRINOX improved overall survival versus gemcitabine in metastatic pancreatic cancer (median 11.1 vs 6.8 months; HR 0.57) in fit patients
cards.summary: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11: FOLFIRINOX improved overall survival versus gemcitabine in metastatic pancreatic cancer (median 11.1 vs 6.8 months; HR 0.57) in fit patients
cards.type: Randomized phase 3 trial (open-label; single outstanding trial)
cards.people: 342 patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer and an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1, randomised to FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², and fluorouracil bolus plus 46-hour infusion, every 2 weeks) or gemcitabine (1000 mg/m² on the standard weekly schedule). Six months of chemotherapy were recommended in responding patients in both groups. The primary end point was overall survival.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 11.1 months with FOLFIRINOX versus 6.8 months with gemcitabine (HR for death 0.57; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.73; P<0.001) — a 43% relative reduction in the risk of death. Median progression-free survival was 6.4 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.37 to 0.59) and the objective response rate 31.6% vs 9.4% (P<0.001). More adverse events occurred with FOLFIRINOX, including febrile neutropenia in 5.4% of patients; nevertheless, at 6 months only 31% of the FOLFIRINOX group had a definitive degradation of quality of life, versus 66% with gemcitabine (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.30 to 0.70).
cards.watchOut: A fit-patient trial: eligibility required ECOG 0–1, and the regimen's toxicity is substantial — the result must not be generalised to unselected metastatic pancreatic cancer. Open-label and unreplicated for this exact regimen; the modern NALIRIFOX combination (NAPOLI-3) is a distinct regimen and is fenced, not carded, so this shelf does not rank today's triplet options against each other.
cards.source: Conroy T et al. FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine for metastatic pancreatic cancer. N Engl J Med. 2011. PMID: 21561347. Registry ID: NCT00112658, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Maintenance olaparib in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer (POLO)
shelves.question: In germline BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer without progression on platinum chemotherapy, does maintenance olaparib improve progression-free survival versus placebo — and does it extend survival?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents · Double-Blind Method · Female · Genes, BRCA1 · Genes, BRCA2 · Germ-Line Mutation · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Maintenance Chemotherapy · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis · Pancreatic Neoplasms · Phthalazines · Piperazines · Progression-Free Survival
shelves.balance: POLO is the library's cleanest lesson in surrogate dissociation. Of 3,315 patients screened, 154 with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer that had not progressed on first-line platinum chemotherapy were randomised to maintenance olaparib or placebo in a double-blind trial. Progression-free survival (blinded central review) was clearly longer on olaparib (median 7.4 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.35–0.82). But overall survival showed no difference at the carded interim analysis (median 18.9 vs 18.1 months; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56–1.46, at 46% data maturity), and health-related quality of life did not differ either. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 40% vs 23%. So: maintenance olaparib delays scans turning positive in this small molecular subgroup (POSSIBLE), without demonstrated survival or quality-of-life benefit (POSSIBLE that the treatment made no difference to survival, on interim data). The split is the shelf. PROPOSED SPLIT.

cards.headline: POLO: maintenance olaparib doubled progression-free survival (7.4 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.53) but showed no overall-survival difference at interim analysis (HR 0.91)
cards.summary: POLO: maintenance olaparib doubled progression-free survival (7.4 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.53) but showed no overall-survival difference at interim analysis (HR 0.91)
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (single trial; biomarker-selected)
cards.people: 3,315 patients underwent screening; 154 with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer whose disease had not progressed during first-line platinum-based chemotherapy were randomised 3:2 to maintenance olaparib tablets 300 mg twice daily (92) or placebo (62). The primary end point was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 7.4 months with olaparib versus 3.8 months with placebo (HR for disease progression or death 0.53; 95% CI 0.35 to 0.82; P=0.004). An interim analysis of overall survival, at 46% data maturity, showed no difference (median 18.9 vs 18.1 months; HR for death 0.91; 95% CI 0.56 to 1.46; P=0.68) — on the carded data, the treatment made no difference to survival. There was no significant between-group difference in health-related quality of life. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 40% (olaparib) vs 23% (placebo), with discontinuation for adverse events in 5% vs 2%.
cards.watchOut: Two disciplines on one card. First, the survival analysis carded here is interim (46% maturity); a later final analysis exists in the literature but was not verified for this shelf, so the survival half of the split is stamped POSSIBLE, not LIKELY. Second, the screened-to-randomised ratio (3,315 to 154) is the population statement: this is a small, platinum-sensitive, germline-BRCA subgroup, and nothing here transfers to unselected pancreatic cancer.
cards.source: Golan T et al. Maintenance Olaparib for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2019. PMID: 31157963. Registry ID: NCT02184195, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Second-line FOLFOX in advanced biliary tract cancer (ABC-06)
shelves.question: In advanced biliary tract cancer progressing after gemcitabine–cisplatin, does second-line FOLFOX plus active symptom control improve overall survival versus active symptom control alone?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Biliary Tract Neoplasms · Female · Fluorouracil · Humans · Leucovorin · Male · Middle Aged · Organoplatinum Compounds · Prospective Studies
shelves.balance: One modest-sized trial is the entire randomised evidence for second-line chemotherapy in this disease. ABC-06 randomised 162 patients with advanced biliary tract cancer progressing after cisplatin–gemcitabine (ECOG 0–1) to active symptom control with or without FOLFOX (up to 12 cycles): overall survival improved (median 6.2 vs 5.3 months; adjusted HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.97). The median gain of 0.9 months understates the tail: 6-month survival was 50.6% vs 35.5% and 12-month survival 25.9% vs 11.4%. The cost was grade 3–5 adverse events in 69% vs 52%, including three chemotherapy-related deaths. An honest small win in a disease with few options — and a single open-label trial, so the survival claim is stamped POSSIBLE. PROPOSED POSSIBLE pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: ABC-06: second-line FOLFOX improved overall survival versus active symptom control alone (median 6.2 vs 5.3 months; HR 0.69), doubling 12-month survival (25.9% vs 11.4%)
cards.summary: ABC-06: second-line FOLFOX improved overall survival versus active symptom control alone (median 6.2 vs 5.3 months; HR 0.69), doubling 12-month survival (25.9% vs 11.4%)
cards.people: 162 adults with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder or ampullary carcinoma) and documented progression on first-line cisplatin–gemcitabine, with ECOG performance status 0–1, at 20 UK centres, randomised to active symptom control (ASC) plus FOLFOX (81) — oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil every 2 weeks for a maximum of 12 cycles — or ASC alone (81). The primary end point was overall survival; median follow-up was 21.7 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 6.2 months (95% CI 5.4 to 7.6) with ASC plus FOLFOX versus 5.3 months (95% CI 4.1 to 5.8) with ASC alone (adjusted HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50 to 0.97; p=0.031). Survival at 6 months was 50.6% vs 35.5% and at 12 months 25.9% vs 11.4%. Grade 3–5 adverse events were reported in 69% of the FOLFOX group and 52% of the ASC-alone group, including three chemotherapy-related deaths (infection, acute kidney injury, febrile neutropenia); the commonest severe FOLFOX-related events were neutropenia (12%), fatigue or lethargy (11%) and infection (10%).
cards.watchOut: A single, small, open-label trial with a modest absolute median gain — the honest summary is the doubling of 6- and 12-month survival rates against real toxicity, in patients fit enough (ECOG 0–1) to receive second-line chemotherapy at all. The trial's ASC-alone arm is the right comparator for the question it asked; it does not rank FOLFOX against targeted options for the molecular subgroups (FGFR2, IDH1) carved out since.
cards.source: Lamarca A et al. Second-line FOLFOX chemotherapy versus active symptom control for advanced biliary tract cancer (ABC-06): a phase 3, open-label, randomised, controlled trial. Lancet Oncol. 2021. PMID: 33798493. Registry IDs: NCT01926236 and EudraCT 2013-001812-30, from the record's databank fields. shelves.title: Ramucirumab in previously treated gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (RAINBOW; REGARD)
shelves.question: In advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma progressing on first-line chemotherapy, does ramucirumab — with paclitaxel, or alone — improve overall survival versus control?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Adult · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Confidence Intervals · Disease-Free Survival · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Double-Blind Method · Drug Administration Schedule · Esophageal Neoplasms · Esophagogastric Junction · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Maximum Tolerated Dose · Middle Aged · Paclitaxel · Prognosis · Proportional Hazards Models · Remission Induction · Stomach Neoplasms · Survival Analysis · Treatment Outcome · Ramucirumab
shelves.balance: Two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of the same VEGFR-2 antibody make this a clean two-trial shelf. RAINBOW (665 patients) added ramucirumab to paclitaxel in the second line and improved overall survival (median 9.6 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.807, 95% CI 0.678–0.962), at the cost of more neutropenia (grade ≥3: 41% vs 19%), hypertension (14% vs 2%) and fatigue (12% vs 5%). REGARD (355 patients) tested ramucirumab alone against placebo plus best supportive care and also improved survival (median 5.2 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.776, 95% CI 0.603–0.998), with hypertension the main excess (16% vs 8%). The effects are moderate, the design quality is the best on this slate (both randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled), and the two questions — combination and monotherapy — are kept distinct on their cards. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: RAINBOW: ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved overall survival versus paclitaxel alone in previously treated gastric/GEJ cancer (median 9.6 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.807)
cards.summary: RAINBOW: ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved overall survival versus paclitaxel alone in previously treated gastric/GEJ cancer (median 9.6 vs 7.4 months; HR 0.807)
cards.people: 665 patients with advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma progressing on or within 4 months after first-line chemotherapy (platinum plus fluoropyrimidine, with or without an anthracycline) at 170 centres in 27 countries, randomised to ramucirumab 8 mg/kg (330) or placebo (335) on days 1 and 15, both with paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. The primary end point was overall survival, analysed by intention to treat.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer with ramucirumab plus paclitaxel (median 9.6 months; 95% CI 8.5 to 10.8) than with placebo plus paclitaxel (median 7.4 months; 95% CI 6.3 to 8.4) (HR 0.807; 95% CI 0.678 to 0.962; p=0.017). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurring more often with ramucirumab included neutropenia (41% vs 19%), leucopenia (17% vs 7%), hypertension (14% vs 2%), fatigue (12% vs 5%) and abdominal pain (6% vs 3%); grade 3 or higher febrile neutropenia was low in both groups (3% vs 2%).
cards.watchOut: The comparison isolates ramucirumab's contribution on a paclitaxel backbone; it does not compare the combination against ramucirumab alone (that is REGARD's separate question, in a population treated without concurrent chemotherapy). The absolute survival gain is about 2 months at the median — real, and worth stating without inflation.
cards.source: Wilke H et al. Lancet Oncol. 2014. PMID: 25240821. Registry ID: NCT01170663, from the record's databank fields. cards.headline: REGARD: ramucirumab monotherapy improved overall survival versus placebo in previously treated gastric/GEJ cancer (median 5.2 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.776) — the first single-agent biological survival benefit in this setting
cards.summary: REGARD: ramucirumab monotherapy improved overall survival versus placebo in previously treated gastric/GEJ cancer (median 5.2 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.776) — the first single-agent biological survival benefit in this setting
cards.people: 355 patients aged 24–87 with advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma progressing after first-line platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing chemotherapy, at 119 centres in 29 countries, randomised 2:1 to best supportive care plus ramucirumab 8 mg/kg (238) or placebo (117) every 2 weeks. The primary end point was overall survival, analysed by intention to treat.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 5.2 months in the ramucirumab group and 3.8 months in the placebo group (HR 0.776; 95% CI 0.603 to 0.998; p=0.047), unchanged after multivariable adjustment (HR 0.774). Hypertension was more frequent with ramucirumab (16% vs 8%); other adverse-event rates were mostly similar (94% vs 88% any grade), and deaths considered related to study drug were 2% in both groups.
cards.watchOut: The p-value (0.047) and the confidence interval's upper bound (0.998) sit close to the line — REGARD alone would be a fragile claim; it is carded as the second, concordant trial behind RAINBOW, in a sicker, chemotherapy-free comparison. Cross-trial median comparisons with RAINBOW are not licensed (different backbones, different populations).

shelves.title: Trastuzumab in HER2-positive advanced gastric cancer (ToGA)
shelves.question: In HER2-positive advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, does adding trastuzumab to cisplatin–fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy improve overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Capecitabine · Cisplatin · Deoxycytidine · Drug Therapy, Combination · Esophagogastric Junction · Female · Fluorouracil · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Stomach Neoplasms · Survival Analysis · Trastuzumab · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: One trial established HER2 as the first actionable target in gastric cancer, and it is an outstanding single. ToGA randomised 594 patients with HER2-positive advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma (overexpression by immunohistochemistry or amplification by FISH) to cisplatin plus a fluoropyrimidine with or without trastuzumab: overall survival improved (median 13.8 vs 11.1 months; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.60–0.91), with no excess in overall grade 3–4 adverse events (68% in both groups) or cardiac adverse events (6% in both). The trial was open-label and has no randomised replication for this exact question; its population is defined by the HER2 testing of its era. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: ToGA: adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy improved overall survival in HER2-positive advanced gastric cancer (median 13.8 vs 11.1 months; HR 0.74) without added severe or cardiac toxicity
cards.summary: ToGA: adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy improved overall survival in HER2-positive advanced gastric cancer (median 13.8 vs 11.1 months; HR 0.74) without added severe or cardiac toxicity
cards.type: Randomized, open-label phase 3 trial (single outstanding trial)
cards.people: 594 patients with HER2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma — HER2 overexpression by immunohistochemistry or gene amplification by fluorescence in-situ hybridisation — at 122 centres in 24 countries, randomised to chemotherapy (capecitabine or fluorouracil, plus cisplatin, every 3 weeks for six cycles) alone (296) or with intravenous trastuzumab (298); 584 patients were included in the primary analysis. The primary end point was overall survival; median follow-up was 18.6 vs 17.1 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 13.8 months (95% CI 12 to 16) with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy versus 11.1 months (95% CI 10 to 13) with chemotherapy alone (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.91; p=0.0046) — a 26% relative reduction in the risk of death. The commonest adverse events were nausea, vomiting and neutropenia in both groups; rates of overall grade 3 or 4 adverse events (68% vs 68%) and cardiac adverse events (6% vs 6%) did not differ between groups.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, single trial, and HER2-defined by 2010-era testing: subsequent practice concentrated the benefit in the highest expressors and tightened assay criteria, a refinement that sits in later guidance rather than in this carded record — the shelf's claim is for HER2-positive disease as ToGA enrolled it. Trastuzumab duration in early breast cancer is a different question, homed on Shelf #760.

shelves.title: Adjuvant nivolumab after chemoradiotherapy and resection in oesophageal cancer (CheckMate 577)
shelves.question: In resected oesophageal/GEJ cancer with residual pathological disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, does adjuvant nivolumab improve disease-free and overall survival versus placebo?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · B7-H1 Antigen · Carcinoma, Squamous Cell · Chemoradiotherapy, Adjuvant · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Esophageal Neoplasms · Esophagogastric Junction · Female · Humans · Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoadjuvant Therapy · Nivolumab · Stomach Neoplasms
shelves.balance: One double-blind placebo-controlled trial created the adjuvant standard for this high-risk residue, and it is an outstanding single. CheckMate 577 randomised 794 patients with R0-resected stage II–III oesophageal or GEJ cancer who had residual pathological disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy to up to a year of nivolumab or placebo: disease-free survival doubled at the median (22.4 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.69, 96.4% CI 0.56–0.86), with grade 3–4 treatment-related events in 13% vs 6% and discontinuation for related events in 9% vs 3%. The carded primary record reports disease-free survival; no overall-survival claim is taken from it, and the Tier C flag reflects the shelf's survival question and the developer's designation. The population is precisely fenced: complete responders to chemoradiotherapy were not eligible — this is a treatment for proven residual disease. PROPOSED LIKELY pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).

cards.headline: CheckMate 577: adjuvant nivolumab doubled median disease-free survival after chemoradiotherapy and resection with residual disease (22.4 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.69)
cards.summary: CheckMate 577: adjuvant nivolumab doubled median disease-free survival after chemoradiotherapy and resection with residual disease (22.4 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.69)
cards.type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (single outstanding trial)
cards.people: 794 adults with resected (R0) stage II or III oesophageal or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer who had received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and had residual pathological disease in the resection specimen, randomised 2:1 to nivolumab (532; 240 mg every 2 weeks for 16 weeks, then 480 mg every 4 weeks) or matching placebo (262), for a maximum treatment period of 1 year. The primary end point was disease-free survival; median follow-up was 24.4 months.
cards.result: Median disease-free survival was 22.4 months (95% CI 16.6 to 34.0) with nivolumab versus 11.0 months (95% CI 8.3 to 14.3) with placebo (HR for disease recurrence or death 0.69; 96.4% CI 0.56 to 0.86; P<0.001), with benefit across multiple prespecified subgroups. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events considered related to the trial regimen occurred in 13% of the nivolumab group and 6% of the placebo group, and the regimen was discontinued for related adverse events in 9% vs 3%.
cards.watchOut: The carded record is the primary disease-free-survival report and contains no overall-survival result; this shelf claims delayed recurrence and does not upgrade it to longer life. Eligibility required residual pathological disease after chemoradiotherapy — patients with a pathological complete response, whose prognosis is better, were not studied, and the result must not be extended to them.
