cards.headline: Synthesis: two trials, two verdicts — HABITS (progestogen-heavy) found harm and stopped; Stockholm (progestogen-minimised) found no overall excess but more contralateral cancers
cards.summary: Synthesis: two trials, two verdicts — HABITS (progestogen-heavy) found harm and stopped; Stockholm (progestogen-minimised) found no overall excess but more contralateral cancers
cards.people: The carded evidence is two Scandinavian randomised trials, each reported twice: HABITS (447 assigned; reports PMID 14962527 and 18364505) and Stockholm (378 randomised; reports PMID 15812079 and 22892060). Gate note: every candidate PMID for this pack was checked against the carded-PMID gate list twice this session (search listing and full-record fetch); none is gate-listed or homed elsewhere.
cards.result: HABITS: hazard ratio 2.4 (95% CI 1.3–4.2) for a new breast-cancer event, 5-year incidence 22.2% versus 8.0%. Stockholm: relative hazard 0.82 at 4.1 years and hazard ratio 1.3 (0.9–1.9) at 10.8 years overall, with contralateral cancers at hazard ratio 3.6 (1.2–10.9). Between-trial heterogeneity P=.02. No mortality difference in either trial. PROPOSED SPLIT: the answer depends on the regimen tested — the honest summary is 'harm shown for the HABITS regimen, not shown overall for the Stockholm regimen, safety proven for neither'.
cards.watchOut: Both trials stopped early and neither reached its planned size; observational literature suggesting lower recurrence on hormones is confounded by selection (healthier survivors are offered hormones) and is not carded here. This shelf does not cover tibolone (tested separately in LIBERATE) or local vaginal estrogen, which is homed elsewhere in the library.

shelves.title: Lutetium-177 edotreotide versus everolimus in GEP neuroendocrine tumours (COMPETE): progression-free survival 23.9 vs 14.1 months in the first head-to-head phase 3 — with a single-arm phase 2 and a heterogeneous meta-analysis behind it
shelves.question: In adults with grade 1–2 gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours progressing on somatostatin analogues, does lutetium-177 edotreotide, compared with everolimus, prolong progression-free survival?
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — the randomised evidence is one trial. In COMPETE (309 patients with advanced, somatostatin-receptor-positive grade 1–2 GEP NETs), lutetium-177 edotreotide (the DOTATOC peptide, from ITM — named here under the clarification exception as the specific tested radiopharmaceutical) prolonged median progression-free survival versus everolimus: 23.9 vs 14.1 months, stratified hazard ratio 0.67 (95% CI 0.48–0.95; p=0.022) — a relative measure; overall survival was immature in the record. Treatment-related grade 3–4 adverse events were less frequent with edotreotide (18% vs 40%). Behind the trial sit only uncontrolled data: a 56-patient retrospective phase 2 series of lutetium-177 DOTATOC (median PFS 17.4 months, objective response 33.9%) and a 2026 systematic review/meta-analysis of eight uncontrolled studies (GEP-NET objective response 34%, median PFS 24.9 months, with heterogeneity I² >70% throughout) — consistent with COMPETE but unable to confirm it. The slate noted an FDA complete response letter in August 2026 on non-clinical grounds; that is a regulatory fact, not an efficacy signal, and is not verified in the fetched records, so it is flagged rather than asserted. One positive head-to-head trial with supportive uncontrolled data: POSSIBLE, not LIKELY.

cards.headline: COMPETE (phase 3): median PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 months for edotreotide vs everolimus — hazard ratio 0.67 (a relative measure); grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events 18% vs 40%
cards.summary: COMPETE (phase 3): median PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 months for edotreotide vs everolimus — hazard ratio 0.67 (a relative measure); grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events 18% vs 40%
cards.people: 309 adults (207 edotreotide, 102 everolimus; 54% male) with treatment-naive or previously treated unresectable or metastatic grade 1–2, somatostatin-receptor-positive GEP NETs, enrolled at 49 specialist centres in 14 countries; edotreotide 7.5 ± 0.7 GBq intravenously every 3 months for up to four cycles vs everolimus 10 mg/day for up to 30 months; median follow-up 27.5 vs 21.2 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival (blinded central review) was 23.9 months (95% CI 18.7–30.0) with edotreotide vs 14.1 months (9.2–20.9) with everolimus; stratified hazard ratio 0.67 (95% CI 0.48–0.95; p=0.022) — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 82% vs 97%; at least one grade 3–4 treatment-related event in 18% vs 40%. The most common treatment-related events with edotreotide were diarrhoea and nausea (36% each) and asthenia (33%).
cards.watchOut: Open-label design (mitigated by blinded central review of the primary endpoint) and a 2:1 randomisation; overall survival was not mature in this report, so the claim is a progression-free-survival claim only.
cards.source: COMPETE — Walter T et al. [177Lu]Lu-edotreotide versus everolimus for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (COMPETE): a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, superiority trial. Lancet. 2026. PMID: 42392118. Registry ID: NCT03049189 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.headline: Phase 2 lutetium-177 DOTATOC series (56 patients, uncontrolled): median PFS 17.4 months, objective response 33.9%, no serious adverse events reported
cards.summary: Phase 2 lutetium-177 DOTATOC series (56 patients, uncontrolled): median PFS 17.4 months, objective response 33.9%, no serious adverse events reported
cards.people: 56 consecutive patients with metastasised, progressive neuroendocrine tumours (50% gastroenteral, 26.8% pancreatic, 23.2% other primary sites) treated with lutetium-177 DOTATOC (mean 2.1 cycles; median 7.0 GBq doses at three-monthly intervals), analysed retrospectively.
cards.result: In the total population, median progression-free survival was 17.4 months and median overall survival 34.2 months; objective response rate was 33.9% and disease control rate 66.1%. In patients receiving more than one cycle, median PFS was 32.0 months. There were no serious adverse events; one case of self-limiting grade 3 myelotoxicity was reported, and no exacerbated or de novo renal toxicity was seen despite 20% having mild renal insufficiency at baseline.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm and retrospective: response and survival figures have no comparator and cannot separate drug effect from patient selection; carded as programme support for COMPETE, not as independent proof.

cards.headline: Systematic review and meta-analysis of lutetium-177 edotreotide (8 uncontrolled studies): GEP-NET objective response 34%, median PFS 24.9 months — heterogeneity I² >70% on every outcome
cards.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of lutetium-177 edotreotide (8 uncontrolled studies): GEP-NET objective response 34%, median PFS 24.9 months — heterogeneity I² >70% on every outcome
cards.type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of uncontrolled studies
cards.people: Eight eligible studies in advanced neuroendocrine tumours, mostly grade 1/2; objective response and disease control were reported in six studies (GEP-NETs n=222; all NETs n=423), median PFS in five (GEP-NETs n=294) and median overall survival in six (GEP-NETs n=256); updated data were obtained from investigators for four studies.
cards.result: In GEP-NETs the pooled objective response rate was 34%, disease control rate 78%, median PFS 24.9 months and median overall survival 44.8 months (all-NET figures were lower: 19%, 57%, 18.6 and 39.1 months). Heterogeneity was consistently high (I² >70%) across outcomes and populations. Grade 3/4 toxicities were rarely noted, but safety reporting was inconsistent across studies.
cards.watchOut: Every pooled study was uncontrolled and heterogeneity exceeded 70% throughout, so the pooled numbers describe what treated cohorts experienced, not a treatment effect; the randomised comparison lives only in Card 1.
cards.source: Baum RP et al. Systematic review and meta-analysis of the efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-edotreotide ([177Lu]Lu-DOTATOC) for the treatment of neuroendocrine tumors. J Neuroendocrinol. 2026. PMID: 41204752. Registry ID: none listed in the record. shelves.title: Surufatinib in advanced neuroendocrine tumours (SANET-p and SANET-ep): progression-free survival roughly tripled versus placebo in two Chinese phase 3 trials — final overall survival not significantly different, with 69% crossover
shelves.question: In adults with advanced pancreatic or extrapancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, does surufatinib, compared with placebo, prolong progression-free survival?
mesh: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions/classification,pathology
shelves.balance: LIKELY for delaying progression; not shown to extend life. Two double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials conducted in China were both stopped early for efficacy at interim analysis: SANET-p (pancreatic NETs, n=172) median PFS 10.9 vs 3.7 months, hazard ratio 0.49; SANET-ep (extrapancreatic NETs, n=198) median PFS 9.2 vs 3.8 months, hazard ratio 0.33 — hazard ratios are relative measures, printed beside the absolute medians. The pooled final overall-survival analysis (398 patients) found median OS 50.1 vs 46.8 months, hazard ratio 0.935 (95% CI 0.684–1.278; p=0.67) — not significant — after 69% of the placebo group crossed over to surufatinib; crossover-corrected estimates ranged from 0.558 to 0.825 and are model-dependent. Quality of life was preserved overall except diarrhoea, which worsened. The main grade 3+ harms were hypertension (36–38%) and proteinuria (~10%). Surufatinib (marketed as Sulanda by HUTCHMED — named under the clarification exception) is a single-country evidence base: both trials enrolled only in China, and the slate records an FDA complete response letter in 2022 requiring a multi-regional trial. LIKELY on progression, with the null survival result and the single-region base printed on the face.

cards.headline: SANET-p (phase 3, pancreatic NETs): median PFS 10.9 vs 3.7 months — hazard ratio 0.49 (a relative measure); grade 3+ hypertension 38% vs 7%
cards.summary: SANET-p (phase 3, pancreatic NETs): median PFS 10.9 vs 3.7 months — hazard ratio 0.49 (a relative measure); grade 3+ hypertension 38% vs 7%
cards.people: 172 adults in 21 hospitals across China with progressive, advanced, well-differentiated pancreatic NETs, ECOG 0–1, progression on up to two previous systemic regimens; randomised 2:1 to surufatinib 300 mg daily (n=113) or placebo (n=59); median follow-up 19.3 vs 11.1 months; crossover to surufatinib was permitted at progression.
cards.result: Median investigator-assessed progression-free survival was 10.9 months (95% CI 7.5–13.8) with surufatinib vs 3.7 months (2.8–5.6) with placebo; hazard ratio 0.49 (95% CI 0.32–0.76; p=0.0011) — a relative measure. The trial met early-stopping criteria at interim analysis and was terminated on the data monitoring committee's recommendation. The most common grade 3 or worse treatment-related events were hypertension (38% vs 7%), proteinuria (10% vs 2%) and hypertriglyceridaemia (7% vs 0%); treatment-related serious adverse events 22% vs 7%; three on-treatment deaths occurred in the surufatinib group (one possibly treatment-related gastrointestinal haemorrhage, one cerebral haemorrhage judged unlikely related, one disease progression).
cards.watchOut: Stopped early at a preplanned interim analysis, which tends to flatter effect sizes; single-country (China) enrolment limits generalisability.
cards.source: SANET-p — Xu J et al. Surufatinib in advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (SANET-p): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study. Lancet Oncol. 2020. PMID: 32966810. Registry ID: NCT02589821 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.headline: SANET-ep (phase 3, extrapancreatic NETs): median PFS 9.2 vs 3.8 months — hazard ratio 0.33 (a relative measure)
cards.summary: SANET-ep (phase 3, extrapancreatic NETs): median PFS 9.2 vs 3.8 months — hazard ratio 0.33 (a relative measure)
cards.people: 198 adults at 24 hospitals across China with unresectable or metastatic, well-differentiated extrapancreatic NETs, ECOG 0–1, progression on no more than two previous systemic regimens; randomised 2:1 to surufatinib 300 mg daily (n=129) or placebo (n=69); median follow-up 13.8 vs 16.6 months; crossover allowed at progression.
cards.result: Investigator-assessed median progression-free survival was 9.2 months (95% CI 7.4–11.1) with surufatinib vs 3.8 months (3.7–5.7) with placebo; hazard ratio 0.33 (95% CI 0.22–0.50; p<0.0001) — a relative measure. The trial met predefined early-discontinuation criteria at interim analysis and was terminated early on the independent data monitoring committee's recommendation. The most common grade 3 or worse treatment-related event was hypertension (36% of the surufatinib group).
cards.watchOut: Also stopped early for efficacy; investigator-assessed (not centrally reviewed) progression is the primary endpoint in both SANET trials.

cards.headline: Final overall survival, pooled SANET-p + SANET-ep: 50.1 vs 46.8 months, hazard ratio 0.935 (p=0.67) — not significant, after 69% of placebo patients crossed over to surufatinib
cards.summary: Final overall survival, pooled SANET-p + SANET-ep: 50.1 vs 46.8 months, hazard ratio 0.935 (p=0.67) — not significant, after 69% of placebo patients crossed over to surufatinib
cards.type: Pooled final overall-survival analysis of two phase 3 trials
cards.people: Pooled intention-to-treat population of both phase 3 trials: 398 patients with unresectable/metastatic well-differentiated grade 1/2 NETs (surufatinib n=265, placebo n=133); after progression or unblinding, placebo patients crossed over or switched to open-label surufatinib (69% did so).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 50.1 months for patients initially on surufatinib vs 46.8 months for those initially on placebo; stratified hazard ratio 0.935 (95% CI 0.684–1.278; p=0.6727) — the treatment made no significant difference to overall survival in the primary analysis. Exploratory crossover-corrected models gave hazard ratios from 0.558 to 0.825. Common grade 3/4 treatment-related events (≥10%) were hypertension and proteinuria; no new safety signals were observed.
cards.watchOut: With 69% crossover, the intention-to-treat survival comparison is heavily diluted; the corrected estimates depend on modelling assumptions and are exploratory — neither the null nor the corrected figures should be quoted alone.
cards.source: Xu J et al. Surufatinib in advanced neuroendocrine tumours: final overall survival from two randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 studies (SANET-ep and SANET-p). Eur J Cancer. 2025. PMID: 40306120. Registry ID: NCT02589821 and NCT02588170 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.headline: Quality of life across SANET-p and SANET-ep: preserved overall, except diarrhoea — time to definitive deterioration for diarrhoea was shorter on surufatinib (hazard ratio 2.91, a relative measure)
cards.summary: Quality of life across SANET-p and SANET-ep: preserved overall, except diarrhoea — time to definitive deterioration for diarrhoea was shorter on surufatinib (hazard ratio 2.91, a relative measure)
cards.type: Prespecified quality-of-life analysis of two phase 3 trials
cards.people: 370 randomised patients (surufatinib n=242, placebo n=128) completing EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-G.I.NET21 questionnaires; the prespecified outcome was mean change from baseline to the last available visit, plus time until definitive deterioration (≥10-point deterioration, progression, or death).
cards.result: No significant between-group differences in mean score change were seen for any domain except diarrhoea, which worsened by 11.7 points on surufatinib and improved by 1.2 points on placebo (between-group difference 12.9 points). Time until definitive deterioration was significantly longer on surufatinib for dyspnoea (hazard ratio 0.58; 95% CI 0.39–0.86; p=0.0058) and significantly shorter for diarrhoea (hazard ratio 2.91; 95% CI 1.66–5.10; p<0.0001) — both relative measures; all other domains did not differ significantly.
cards.watchOut: Questionnaire completion falls as patients progress, so late time-points over-represent patients doing well in both arms.
cards.source: Li J et al. Health-related quality of life in patients with advanced well-differentiated pancreatic and extrapancreatic neuroendocrine tumors treated with surufatinib versus placebo: results from two randomized, double-blind, phase III trials (SANET-p and SANET-ep). Eur J Cancer. 2022. PMID: 35489301. Registry ID: NCT02589821 and NCT02588170 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.summary: Synthesis: progression delayed in two concordant trials; survival not shown to differ — LIKELY (progression endpoint), single-country base
cards.people: Adults with advanced well-differentiated pancreatic or extrapancreatic NETs after up to two prior systemic regimens.
cards.result: Two independent double-blind phase 3 trials agree on a large progression-free-survival benefit (hazard ratios 0.49 and 0.33, relative measures, with absolute median gains of 7.2 and 5.4 months), quality of life is broadly preserved, and the pooled survival analysis is null in the presence of 69% crossover. The stamp is LIKELY for the progression question asked; it is not a survival claim, and the whole randomised base is from China.
cards.watchOut: Early stopping in both trials and the single-region base are the two reasons not to read the hazard ratios as settled worldwide magnitudes.

shelves.title: Capecitabine plus temozolomide (CAPTEM) versus temozolomide alone in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (E2211): progression-free survival 22.7 vs 14.4 months in a randomised phase 2 — overall survival not significantly different
shelves.question: In adults with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, does capecitabine plus temozolomide (CAPTEM), compared with temozolomide alone, prolong progression-free survival?
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE. The only randomised comparison is ECOG-ACRIN E2211 (144 patients with advanced low- or intermediate-grade pancreatic NETs progressing within the previous 12 months): median progression-free survival 22.7 months on capecitabine plus temozolomide vs 14.4 months on temozolomide alone (hazard ratio 0.58, a relative measure; stratified log-rank p=0.022), while median overall survival was 58.7 vs 53.8 months (hazard ratio 0.82; p=0.42) — not significantly different. MGMT deficiency was associated with response. The supporting evidence is retrospective: the original 30-patient first-line series (objective response 70%, median PFS 18 months, grade 3–4 events in 12%) and a 462-patient single-centre cohort (response 46%, median PFS 18 months, median OS 51 months; grade 4 thrombocytopenia 7% and neutropenia 3%, both significantly more frequent in women; the only myelodysplastic-syndrome cases had prior peptide receptor radionuclide therapy). Retrospective response rates of 46–70% come from selected, uncontrolled cohorts and should not be read as randomised effects. Generic agents; no product-naming issue. One randomised phase 2, null on survival: POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: E2211 (randomised phase 2): median PFS 22.7 vs 14.4 months for CAPTEM vs temozolomide alone (hazard ratio 0.58, a relative measure); overall survival 58.7 vs 53.8 months, hazard ratio 0.82, p=0.42 — not significant
cards.summary: E2211 (randomised phase 2): median PFS 22.7 vs 14.4 months for CAPTEM vs temozolomide alone (hazard ratio 0.58, a relative measure); overall survival 58.7 vs 53.8 months, hazard ratio 0.82, p=0.42 — not significant
cards.people: 144 patients enrolled (72 per arm) with advanced low-grade or intermediate-grade pancreatic NETs and progression within the preceding 12 months, no prior temozolomide, dacarbazine-class, capecitabine or fluorouracil exposure; the primary analysis population was 133 eligible patients; MGMT status was assessed by immunohistochemistry and promoter methylation.
cards.result: At the January 2018 interim analysis, median progression-free survival was 14.4 months for temozolomide vs 22.7 months for capecitabine/temozolomide (hazard ratio 0.58 — a relative measure; stratified log-rank p=0.022), meeting the primary endpoint. In the final analysis (May 2021), median overall survival was 53.8 vs 58.7 months (hazard ratio 0.82; p=0.42) — the treatment made no statistically significant difference to overall survival. MGMT deficiency was associated with response; the authors note routine MGMT testing is not recommended but can be considered for select patients needing an objective response.
cards.watchOut: Phase 2, not phase 3, and sized for progression-free survival: the survival comparison is underpowered, so 'not significant' is not proof of no survival effect — but no survival benefit has been shown either.
cards.source: ECOG-ACRIN E2211 — Kunz PL et al. Randomized study of temozolomide or temozolomide and capecitabine in patients with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (ECOG-ACRIN E2211). J Clin Oncol. 2023. PMID: 36260828. Registry ID: NCT01824875 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.headline: Original CAPTEM series (30 patients, retrospective, first-line): objective response 70%, median PFS 18 months, 2-year survival 92%, grade 3–4 events in 12%
cards.summary: Original CAPTEM series (30 patients, retrospective, first-line): objective response 70%, median PFS 18 months, 2-year survival 92%, grade 3–4 events in 12%
cards.people: 30 patients with metastatic, well- or moderately differentiated pancreatic endocrine carcinomas and no prior systemic chemotherapy, treated with capecitabine 750 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 plus temozolomide 200 mg/m² daily on days 10–14 of each 28-day cycle, evaluated retrospectively.
cards.result: 21 of 30 patients (70%) achieved an objective radiographic response; median progression-free survival was 18 months and the 2-year survival rate was 92%. Only 4 patients (12%) experienced grade 3 or 4 adverse events.
cards.watchOut: A small, selected, uncontrolled first-line cohort from the regimen's originating centre: the 70% response rate is the programme's ceiling, not an estimate of effect versus any comparator.

cards.headline: Largest CAPTEM cohort (462 patients, retrospective): response 46%, median PFS 18 months, median overall survival 51 months; grade 4 thrombocytopenia 7% and neutropenia 3%, both significantly more frequent in women
cards.summary: Largest CAPTEM cohort (462 patients, retrospective): response 46%, median PFS 18 months, median overall survival 51 months; grade 4 thrombocytopenia 7% and neutropenia 3%, both significantly more frequent in women
cards.people: 462 patients with advanced neuroendocrine neoplasms (pancreatic and non-pancreatic) treated with CAPTEM at a single cancer centre between January 2008 and June 2019; well-differentiated NETs and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas were both included.
cards.result: The objective response rate was 46% and disease control rate 81%; median progression-free survival was 18 months (95% CI 14.0–21.9) and median overall survival 51 months (95% CI 42.8–59.2) — 62 months in well-differentiated NETs vs 14 months in poorly differentiated carcinomas (p<0.0001). Patients with pancreatic primaries had the highest response rates and longest median PFS. Grade 4 thrombocytopenia occurred in 7% and grade 4 neutropenia in 3%, both substantially more frequent in women (p=0.02 and p=0.004). Only one suspected Pneumocystis pneumonia case (0.2%, in a patient on corticosteroids) was seen; three patients developed myelodysplastic disease, all after prior peptide receptor radionuclide therapy; there were no acute treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Mixes pancreatic with non-pancreatic tumours and well-differentiated NETs with poorly differentiated carcinomas, whose outcomes differ fourfold; the pancreatic-NET randomised answer rests on Card 1 alone.
cards.source: Al-Toubah T et al. Efficacy and toxicity analysis of capecitabine and temozolomide in neuroendocrine neoplasms. J Natl Compr Canc Netw. 2021. PMID: 34433130. Registry ID: none listed in the record. shelves.title: Sunitinib in metastatic phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma (FIRSTMAPPP): the first randomised trial in this disease — 12-month progression-free survival 36% vs 19% on placebo, in 78 patients recruited over seven years
shelves.question: In adults with metastatic phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma, does sunitinib, compared with placebo, prolong progression-free survival?
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE, on a very small base — the stamp carries the N. FIRSTMAPPP is the first randomised trial ever done in metastatic phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma: 78 patients recruited across 14 centres in four European countries between 2011 and 2019 (a decade-scale recruitment effort for a rare disease). Its primary endpoint was met: 12-month progression-free survival was 36% (14/39) on sunitinib 37.5 mg daily vs 19% (7/39) on placebo, against a design hypothesis of 40% vs 20%. Grade 3–4 asthenia (18% vs 3%) and hypertension (13% vs 10%) were the most frequent severe events; three deaths occurred on sunitinib, one (rectal bleeding) judged drug-related. The single-arm SUTNET phase 2 (50 patients, sunitinib 50 mg 4-weeks-on/2-weeks-off) found a 1-year PFS rate of 53.4%, median PFS 14.1 months and objective response 15.6%, with grade ≥3 treatment-related events in 34%. A 2026 meta-analysis of the sunitinib arms of three prospective trials (114 patients) pooled an objective response rate of 21.2% and 12-month PFS of 48.2%, rating its own evidence low to very low certainty. No overall-survival benefit has been shown in a randomised comparison. The neighbouring systemic-therapy questions are different interventions; no sunitinib card from any other shelf is duplicated here.

cards.headline: FIRSTMAPPP (randomised phase 2): 12-month progression-free survival 36% (14/39) on sunitinib vs 19% (7/39) on placebo — the primary endpoint was met
cards.summary: FIRSTMAPPP (randomised phase 2): 12-month progression-free survival 36% (14/39) on sunitinib vs 19% (7/39) on placebo — the primary endpoint was met
cards.people: 78 adults with sporadic or inherited progressive metastatic phaeochromocytomas or paragangliomas (39 per group) at 14 academic centres in four European countries, enrolled December 2011 to January 2019; 32% had germline SDHx variants and 69% had received previous therapies; sunitinib 37.5 mg daily vs placebo, stratified by SDHB status and prior systemic therapy; crossover from placebo was allowed.
cards.result: The 12-month progression-free survival rate (central review, RECIST 1.1) was 36% (90% CI 23–50) in the sunitinib group vs 19% (90% CI 11–31) in the placebo group, meeting the trial's two-step Simon design target (an improvement from 20% to 40%). The most frequent grade 3 or 4 adverse events were asthenia (18% vs 3%), hypertension (13% vs 10%) and back/bone pain. Three deaths occurred in the sunitinib group (respiratory insufficiency, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, rectal bleeding — only the last considered drug-related) and two in the placebo group (aspiration pneumonia, septic shock).
cards.watchOut: The endpoint is a 12-month PFS rate in 78 patients, not a median-survival comparison; the confidence intervals (23–50% vs 11–31%) overlap substantially, and crossover was allowed.
cards.source: FIRSTMAPPP — Baudin E et al. Sunitinib for metastatic progressive phaeochromocytomas and paragangliomas: results from FIRSTMAPPP, an academic, multicentre, international, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 2 trial. Lancet. 2024. PMID: 38402886. Registry ID: NCT01371201 (ClinicalTrials.gov, as listed in the record). cards.headline: SUTNET (single-arm phase 2, 50 patients): 1-year PFS rate 53.4%, median PFS 14.1 months, objective response 15.6%; grade ≥3 treatment-related events in 34%
cards.summary: SUTNET (single-arm phase 2, 50 patients): 1-year PFS rate 53.4%, median PFS 14.1 months, objective response 15.6%; grade ≥3 treatment-related events in 34%
cards.people: 50 patients with metastatic or unresectable phaeochromocytomas or paragangliomas receiving sunitinib 50 mg daily for 4 weeks followed by a 2-week rest, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal; median follow-up 71.7 months; primary endpoint was the 12-month progression-free survival rate.
cards.result: The 1-year progression-free survival rate was 53.4% (95% CI 41.1–69.3) and median PFS 14.1 months (95% CI 8.9–25.7); the objective response rate was 15.6% and median overall survival 49.4 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were reported in 34% of patients. No significant correlation was found between specific genetic alterations or genomic clusters and sunitinib efficacy.
cards.watchOut: No comparator and a different dose schedule (50 mg, 4 weeks on / 2 off) from FIRSTMAPPP's continuous 37.5 mg: its higher 1-year PFS rate cannot be compared across trials.
cards.source: SUTNET — Nasca V et al. Sunitinib for the treatment of patients with advanced pheochromocytomas or paragangliomas: the phase 2 non-randomized SUTNET clinical trial. Eur J Cancer. 2024. PMID: 39128186. Registry ID: EudraCT 2011-002632-99, as listed in the record (no ClinicalTrials.gov number in the record). cards.headline: Meta-analysis of sunitinib arms from three prospective trials (114 patients): objective response 21.2%, 12-month PFS 48.2% — the authors rate the evidence low to very low certainty
cards.summary: Meta-analysis of sunitinib arms from three prospective trials (114 patients): objective response 21.2%, 12-month PFS 48.2% — the authors rate the evidence low to very low certainty
cards.type: Meta-analysis of prospective trial treatment arms
cards.people: 114 patients given sunitinib across three prospective clinical trials in advanced or metastatic phaeochromocytomas/paragangliomas; because only one included study had a comparator, the synthesis was performed at the level of the sunitinib-treated arms.
cards.result: The pooled objective response rate was 21.2% (95% CI 11.7–35.3), all partial responses; stable disease 51.8% and progressive disease 27.1%. The 12-month PFS rate was 48.2% (95% CI 38.1–58.5) and median PFS 11.9 months (95% CI 6.9–16.9). Treatment discontinuation for adverse events was 13.2%; grade ≥3 adverse events were 57.8% with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 86%). The authors describe the evidence as low to very low certainty but prospective, suggesting clinically relevant disease control in a subset of patients.
cards.watchOut: An arm-level synthesis of mostly single-arm data — it summarises what treated patients experienced and inherits the FIRSTMAPPP and SUTNET patients rather than adding an independent population.
cards.source: Román-González A et al. Efficacy and safety of sunitinib in treatment of advanced or metastatic pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas: a meta-analysis of sunitinib-treated arms from prospective clinical trials. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2026. PMID: 42960482. Registry ID: none listed in the record.

cards.summary: Synthesis: the only randomised evidence in this disease favours sunitinib on progression, on a very small base — POSSIBLE, N printed
cards.people: Adults with progressive metastatic phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma.
cards.result: One 78-patient randomised trial met its 12-month PFS endpoint (36% vs 19%); a 50-patient single-arm trial and a 114-patient arm-level meta-analysis are directionally consistent, at low to very low certainty. shelves.title: Y-90 radioembolisation (SIRT) versus sorafenib in unresectable HCC: no survival difference in SARAH or SIRveNIB (8.0 vs 9.9 and 8.8 vs 10.0 months); fewer severe adverse events with SIRT
shelves.question: In adults with locally advanced/unresectable HCC, does selective internal radiation therapy with yttrium-90 resin microspheres versus sorafenib improve overall survival and tolerability?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Agents/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Brachytherapy/methods · Carcinoma, Hepatocellular/drug therapy/mortality/pathology/radiotherapy · Disease-Free Survival · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology/radiotherapy · Male · Microspheres · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Invasiveness/pathology · Neoplasm Staging · Niacinamide/administration & dosage/adverse effects/analogs & derivatives · Phenylurea Compounds/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Radiotherapy Dosage · Sorafenib · Survival Analysis · Treatment Outcome · Yttrium Radioisotopes/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: No survival benefit in either head-to-head trial. In SARAH (PMID: 29107679), median overall survival was 8.0 months on SIRT with yttrium-90 resin microspheres (SIR-Spheres, Sirtex — the tested device, named under the clarification exception) versus 9.9 months on sorafenib (HR 1.15, p=0.18); in SIRveNIB (PMID: 29498924) it was 8.8 versus 10.0 months (HR 1.1, p=0.36) — in both, (the treatment made no difference) to survival. Tolerability favoured SIRT in both trials (grade 3 or worse adverse events 27.7% versus 50.6% in SIRveNIB). SORAMIC (PMID: 31421157) is carded with its premise stated plainly: it tested SIRT ADDED TO sorafenib, not SIRT instead of it, and was also null (12.1 versus 11.4 months, HR 1.01). The honest answer: choose on tolerability and liver-directed considerations, not on survival.

cards.headline: Vilgrain 2017 (SARAH): median survival 8.0 months on SIRT versus 9.9 months on sorafenib (HR 1.15, p=0.18) — (the treatment made no difference) to survival; fewer severe treatment-related events with SIRT
cards.summary: Vilgrain 2017 (SARAH): median survival 8.0 months on SIRT versus 9.9 months on sorafenib (HR 1.15, p=0.18) — (the treatment made no difference) to survival; fewer severe treatment-related events with SIRT
cards.people: 459 patients analysed (467 randomised) with locally advanced or inoperable hepatocellular carcinoma at 25 centres in France, assigned to yttrium-90 resin microspheres (SIR-Spheres, Sirtex — the tested product, named under the clarification exception for a named device) or continuous oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; 22% assigned to SIRT never received it.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 8.0 months (95% CI 6.7 to 9.9) with SIRT versus 9.9 months (8.7 to 11.4) with sorafenib (hazard ratio 1.15, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.41; p=0.18) — no significant difference. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 77% versus 82%. Grade 3 or worse treatment-related fatigue (9% versus 19%), diarrhoea (1% versus 14%) and hand-foot skin reaction (<1% versus 6%) were less frequent with SIRT; 19 versus 12 deaths were deemed treatment-related.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and nearly a quarter of the SIRT arm never received SIRT (half of those crossed to sorafenib), which dilutes any intention-to-treat difference in either direction.
cards.source: Vilgrain V et al. Efficacy and safety of selective internal radiotherapy with yttrium-90 resin microspheres compared with sorafenib in locally advanced and inoperable hepatocellular carcinoma (SARAH): an open-label randomised controlled phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2017. PMID: 29107679. Registry ID: NCT01482442. cards.headline: Chow 2018 (SIRveNIB): median survival 8.8 months on radioembolisation versus 10.0 months on sorafenib (HR 1.1, p=0.36) — no difference; grade 3 or worse events 27.7% versus 50.6%
cards.summary: Chow 2018 (SIRveNIB): median survival 8.8 months on radioembolisation versus 10.0 months on sorafenib (HR 1.1, p=0.36) — no difference; grade 3 or worse events 27.7% versus 50.6%
cards.people: 360 patients with locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma in 11 Asia-Pacific countries, randomised to yttrium-90 resin microspheres radioembolisation (182) or sorafenib 800 mg/day (178); 28.6% of the radioembolisation group and 9.0% of the sorafenib group never received the assigned therapy.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 8.8 months with radioembolisation versus 10.0 months with sorafenib (hazard ratio 1.1, 95% CI 0.9 to 1.4; p=0.36) — no significant difference. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 27.7% versus 50.6% (p<0.001) and serious adverse events in 20.8% versus 35.2%, favouring radioembolisation on tolerability.
cards.watchOut: Open-label Asia-Pacific trial with high non-receipt of assigned radioembolisation (28.6%); the tolerability advantage is consistent with SARAH, the survival null is too.
cards.source: Chow PKH et al. SIRveNIB: Selective Internal Radiation Therapy Versus Sorafenib in Asia-Pacific Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2018. PMID: 29498924. Registry ID: NCT01135056. cards.headline: Ricke 2019 (SORAMIC, palliative cohort): adding SIRT to sorafenib gave median survival 12.1 versus 11.4 months (HR 1.01, p=0.95) — no benefit from the combination either
cards.summary: Ricke 2019 (SORAMIC, palliative cohort): adding SIRT to sorafenib gave median survival 12.1 versus 11.4 months (HR 1.01, p=0.95) — no benefit from the combination either
cards.people: 424 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma not eligible for transarterial chemoembolisation, randomised 11:10 to SIRT with yttrium-90 resin microspheres plus sorafenib (216) or sorafenib alone (208) in the palliative cohort of SORAMIC. PREMISE NOTE: SORAMIC tested SIRT ADDED TO sorafenib, not SIRT instead of sorafenib — it is carded as the combination limb of this question, not as a third head-to-head trial.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 12.1 months with SIRT plus sorafenib versus 11.4 months with sorafenib alone (hazard ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.25; p=0.9529) — (the treatment made no difference). Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 64.8% versus 53.8% (p=0.04). Per-protocol subgroup signals (no cirrhosis, non-alcoholic aetiology, age 65 or under) were hypothesis-generating only.
cards.watchOut: A different comparison (add-on, not head-to-head) and only 114 of 216 combination patients were in the per-protocol population; subgroup findings must not be read as proven benefit in those groups.
cards.source: Ricke J et al. Impact of combined selective internal radiation therapy and sorafenib on survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. Journal of hepatology. 2019. PMID: 31421157. cards.headline: Synthesis: two head-to-head phase 3 trials and one add-on trial, all null on survival — SIRT's case rests on tolerability, not longer life
cards.summary: Synthesis: two head-to-head phase 3 trials and one add-on trial, all null on survival — SIRT's case rests on tolerability, not longer life
cards.people: SARAH (459 patients, France), SIRveNIB (360 patients, Asia-Pacific) and the SORAMIC palliative cohort (424 patients, SIRT added to sorafenib) — all randomised, all using yttrium-90 resin microspheres (SIR-Spheres, Sirtex).
cards.result: Overall survival: 8.0 versus 9.9 months (HR 1.15), 8.8 versus 10.0 months (HR 1.1), and 12.1 versus 11.4 months for the combination (HR 1.01) — in each trial (the treatment made no difference) to survival. Tolerability consistently favoured SIRT (grade 3 or worse events 27.7% versus 50.6% in SIRveNIB). PROPOSED verdict: no survival benefit; a tolerability/quality-of-life choice in selected patients.
cards.watchOut: Sorafenib is no longer the default first-line systemic standard in many regions, so these trials answer the question as asked in their era. High non-receipt rates in the SIRT arms (22-29%) temper all three trials.
cards.source: Synthesis of the three cards above (PMIDs: 29107679, 29498924, 31421157).

shelves.title: SIRT added to first-line FOLFOX in colorectal liver metastases: liver progression delayed (20.5 vs 12.6 months) but overall survival unchanged (22.6 vs 23.3 months, HR 1.04)
shelves.question: In adults with liver-dominant metastatic colorectal cancer, does adding Y-90 radioembolisation to first-line FOLFOX chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone improve liver progression-free survival or overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Colorectal Neoplasms/pathology · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy/radiotherapy/secondary · Male · Middle Aged · Radiotherapy, Adjuvant · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: SPLIT by endpoint. Adding SIRT (yttrium-90 resin microspheres, SIR-Spheres, Sirtex — tested device) to first-line FOLFOX delayed progression in the liver in SIRFLOX (PMID: 26903575): median liver progression-free survival 20.5 versus 12.6 months (HR 0.69). But overall progression-free survival did not improve (HR 0.93), and the prespecified combined analysis of FOXFIRE, SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global (1,103 patients, PMID: 28781171) found overall survival of 22.6 versus 23.3 months (HR 1.04, p=0.61) — (the treatment made no difference) to survival. A secondary analysis (PMID: 30033117) found a survival signal confined to right-sided primaries (HR 0.641, n=179), unconfirmed. Keep the liver result and the survival result separate: this is a liver-control intervention, not a life-prolonging one, on current evidence.

cards.headline: van Hazel 2016 (SIRFLOX): liver progression-free survival 20.5 versus 12.6 months (HR 0.69, p=0.002) with SIRT added, but overall PFS 10.7 versus 10.2 months (HR 0.93, NS)
cards.summary: van Hazel 2016 (SIRFLOX): liver progression-free survival 20.5 versus 12.6 months (HR 0.69, p=0.002) with SIRT added, but overall PFS 10.7 versus 10.2 months (HR 0.93, NS)
cards.people: 530 chemotherapy-naive patients with liver metastases (with or without limited extrahepatic metastases) from metastatic colorectal cancer, randomised to mFOLFOX6 (control, 263) or mFOLFOX6 plus SIRT with yttrium-90 resin microspheres (SIR-Spheres, Sirtex — tested device, clarification exception), with or without bevacizumab in either arm.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival at any site was 10.7 versus 10.2 months (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.12; p=0.43) — not significant. Median liver progression-free survival was 20.5 versus 12.6 months (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.90; p=0.002), a 31% relative reduction in the hazard of liver progression. Liver response rate was 78.7% versus 68.8% (p=0.042). Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 85.4% versus 73.4%.
cards.watchOut: The benefit was confined to the liver — the organ the radiation treats — with no gain in overall progression-free survival and more severe adverse events; a liver-PFS result must not be read as a survival result.
cards.source: van Hazel GA et al. cards.summary: Wasan 2017 (FOXFIRE, SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global combined, n=1,103): overall survival 22.6 versus 23.3 months (HR 1.04, p=0.61) — (the treatment made no difference) to survival
cards.type: Combined analysis of three randomised phase 3 trials (Wasan 2017)
cards.people: 1,103 chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and liver metastases not suitable for curative resection or ablation, pooled from FOXFIRE, SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global: FOLFOX alone (549) versus FOLFOX plus single-treatment SIRT (554), with 43.3 months median follow-up.
cards.result: There was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.19; p=0.61): median survival 22.6 months with FOLFOX plus SIRT versus 23.3 months with FOLFOX alone, with 433 (78%) versus 411 (75%) deaths. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was more common with SIRT (37% versus 24%), as were serious adverse events of any grade (54% versus 43%).
cards.watchOut: A prespecified combined analysis designed for the survival endpoint — the most reliable survival answer for this programme, and it is null despite the liver-specific gains in SIRFLOX.

cards.headline: Gibbs 2018 (tumour-side analysis of SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global, n=739): survival gain with SIRT only in right-sided primaries (22.0 versus 17.1 months, HR 0.641); none in left-sided (HR 1.120); interaction p=0.002
cards.summary: Gibbs 2018 (tumour-side analysis of SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global, n=739): survival gain with SIRT only in right-sided primaries (22.0 versus 17.1 months, HR 0.641); none in left-sided (HR 1.120); interaction p=0.002
cards.type: Secondary combined analysis of two randomised trials (Gibbs 2018)
cards.people: 739 patients from SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global with prospectively collected primary tumour side: 179 (24.2%) right-sided primaries and 540 left-sided primaries, comparing chemotherapy plus SIRT versus chemotherapy alone.
cards.result: Overall, SIRT had no effect on survival (median 24.3 versus 24.6 months; hazard ratio 1.021; p=0.810). In right-sided primaries, survival was longer with SIRT (22.0 versus 17.1 months; hazard ratio 0.641; p=0.008); in left-sided primaries it was not (24.6 versus 26.6 months; hazard ratio 1.120; p=0.264). The treatment-by-side interaction was significant (p=0.002).
cards.watchOut: A subgroup analysis, however prespecified the side data collection: the right-sided subgroup is only 179 patients, and the finding sits against a null overall result — hypothesis-generating for patient selection, not proof.

cards.headline: Synthesis: liver progression delayed (20.5 versus 12.6 months) but overall survival unchanged (22.6 versus 23.3 months) — the endpoints must stay separate
cards.summary: Synthesis: liver progression delayed (20.5 versus 12.6 months) but overall survival unchanged (22.6 versus 23.3 months) — the endpoints must stay separate
cards.people: SIRFLOX (530 patients), the prespecified combined FOXFIRE/SIRFLOX/FOXFIRE-Global analysis (1,103 patients), and a tumour-side secondary analysis (739 patients) of first-line FOLFOX with or without yttrium-90 resin-microsphere SIRT in liver-dominant metastatic colorectal cancer.
cards.result: Adding SIRT delayed progression in the liver (median liver PFS 20.5 versus 12.6 months, HR 0.69) but did not improve overall progression-free survival (HR 0.93) or overall survival (22.6 versus 23.3 months, HR 1.04) — on survival, (the treatment made no difference). A right-sided-primary subgroup signal (HR 0.641) is unconfirmed. PROPOSED SPLIT: liver-control benefit without survival benefit, at the cost of more grade 3-4 neutropenia.
cards.watchOut: All trials used SIR-Spheres resin microspheres (Sirtex); results do not automatically transfer to glass-microsphere products. First-line chemotherapy backbones have also moved on since 2006-2014 enrolment.
cards.source: Synthesis of the three cards above (PMIDs: 26903575, 28781171, 30033117).

shelves.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy in advanced HCC: FOLFOX-HAIC strongly positive in two Chinese trials (HR 0.41 and 0.35); cisplatin-based HAIC null in SILIUS (HR 1.009)
shelves.question: In adults with advanced HCC (including portal-vein invasion), does hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (FOLFOX-HAIC, alone or added to sorafenib) versus sorafenib alone improve overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Biomarkers, Tumor/genetics · Carcinoma, Hepatocellular/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/pathology · China · Female · Fluorouracil/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Hepatic Artery · Humans · Infusions, Intra-Arterial · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/pathology · Male · Middle Aged · Mutation · Oxaliplatin/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Progression-Free Survival · Sorafenib/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Time Factors
shelves.balance: SPLIT — by regimen and region. Two Chinese randomised trials of oxaliplatin-based (FOLFOX) hepatic arterial infusion were strongly positive against sorafenib: FOHAIC-1 (PMID: 34905388), HAIC instead of sorafenib, median survival 13.9 versus 8.2 months (HR 0.41); and He 2019 (PMID: 31070690), HAIC added to sorafenib in portal-vein invasion, 13.37 versus 7.13 months (HR 0.35). The Japanese SILIUS trial (PMID: 29631810) of a different, low-dose cisplatin/fluorouracil infusion was null: 11.8 versus 11.5 months (HR 1.009) — (the treatment made no difference). All evidence is single-region (China/Japan, predominantly hepatitis B) against a sorafenib comparator that is no longer first-line standard in many regions; the regimens must not be pooled.

cards.headline: Lyu 2022 (FOHAIC-1): FOLFOX hepatic arterial infusion versus sorafenib — median survival 13.9 versus 8.2 months (HR 0.41, p<0.001)
cards.summary: Lyu 2022 (FOHAIC-1): FOLFOX hepatic arterial infusion versus sorafenib — median survival 13.9 versus 8.2 months (HR 0.41, p<0.001)
cards.people: 262 patients in China with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma and no prior systemic therapy, randomised to hepatic arterial infusion of oxaliplatin, fluorouracil and leucovorin (HAIC-FO) or sorafenib; median tumour size 11.2 cm, macrovascular invasion in 65.6%, and 49.2% had over 50% liver involvement and/or Vp-4 portal vein thrombosis.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 13.9 months with HAIC-FO versus 8.2 months with sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.408, 95% CI 0.301 to 0.552; p<0.001), a 59% relative reduction in the hazard of death. In the high-risk subgroup, survival was 10.8 versus 5.7 months (HR 0.343). Tumour downstaging occurred in 12.3% of the HAIC-FO group, 15 of whom received curative surgery or ablation.
cards.watchOut: Single-country (China) trial with a predominantly hepatitis B population and very bulky liver disease; sorafenib is no longer the first-line comparator in many regions, so the size of the advantage over modern immunotherapy-based standards is unknown.

cards.headline: He 2019: sorafenib plus FOLFOX hepatic arterial infusion versus sorafenib alone in portal-vein invasion — median survival 13.37 versus 7.13 months (HR 0.35); response 40.8% versus 2.5%
cards.summary: He 2019: sorafenib plus FOLFOX hepatic arterial infusion versus sorafenib alone in portal-vein invasion — median survival 13.37 versus 7.13 months (HR 0.35); response 40.8% versus 2.5%
cards.people: 247 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and portal vein invasion at 5 hospitals in China, randomised to sorafenib 400 mg twice daily plus FOLFOX hepatic arterial infusion every 3 weeks, or sorafenib alone; median age 49 years, 223 men and 24 women.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 13.37 months (95% CI 10.27 to 16.46) with sorafenib plus HAIC versus 7.13 months (6.28 to 7.98) with sorafenib alone (hazard ratio 0.35, 95% CI 0.26 to 0.48; p<0.001), a 65% relative reduction in the hazard of death. Response rate was 40.8% versus 2.5% and median progression-free survival 7.03 versus 2.6 months. Grade 3/4 neutropenia (9.7% versus 2.5%), thrombocytopenia (12.9% versus 5.0%) and vomiting (6.5% versus 0.8%) were more frequent with HAIC.
cards.watchOut: Single-country trial in a young, predominantly male, hepatitis B population with portal-vein invasion only; the effect size is very large for an add-on therapy and has not been replicated outside China.

cards.people: 206 patients at 31 sites in Japan with advanced unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, randomised to sorafenib 400 mg twice daily alone or plus hepatic arterial infusion of low-dose cisplatin (20 mg/m2 days 1 and 8) and fluorouracil (330 mg/m2 days 1-5 and 8-12 of each 28-day cycle) via an implanted catheter.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 11.8 months (95% CI 9.1 to 14.5) with sorafenib plus HAIC versus 11.5 months (8.2 to 14.8) with sorafenib alone (hazard ratio 1.009, 95% CI 0.743 to 1.371; p=0.955) — (the treatment made no difference). Grade 3-4 anaemia (17% versus 6%) and neutropenia (17% versus 1%) were more frequent with HAIC.
cards.watchOut: A different, lower-dose cisplatin-based regimen than the FOLFOX-HAIC trials — the split in this shelf is between regimens as much as between studies, and the regimens must not be pooled into one HAIC claim.

cards.people: FOHAIC-1 (262 patients, HAIC instead of sorafenib), He 2019 (247 patients, HAIC added to sorafenib, portal-vein invasion) and SILIUS (206 patients, low-dose cisplatin/fluorouracil HAIC added to sorafenib) — 715 randomised patients, all in China or Japan, all against sorafenib-era controls.
cards.result: FOLFOX-HAIC: median survival 13.9 versus 8.2 months (HR 0.41) and 13.37 versus 7.13 months (HR 0.35). Cisplatin-HAIC: 11.8 versus 11.5 months (HR 1.009, NS). PROPOSED SPLIT: the answer depends on the regimen — large survival gains for oxaliplatin-based HAIC in Chinese hepatitis B-predominant populations, none for the Japanese cisplatin regimen; neither has been tested against current immunotherapy-based first-line standards.
cards.watchOut: Regional and aetiology limits are on the face of each card (FOHAIC-1 was conducted in China with bulky, mostly HBV-related disease). HAIC requires interventional expertise and catheter programmes that many centres do not run.
cards.source: Synthesis of the three cards above (PMIDs: 34905388, 31070690, 29631810).

shelves.title: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib first-line in unresectable HCC (CARES-310): final median survival 23.8 versus 15.2 months on sorafenib (HR 0.64) — one trial, three reports
shelves.question: In adults with unresectable HCC and no prior systemic therapy, does camrelizumab plus rivoceranib (apatinib) versus sorafenib improve overall and progression-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Carcinoma, Hepatocellular/drug therapy · Sorafenib/therapeutic use · Liver Neoplasms/drug therapy · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Pyridines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — a single large trial, reported three times, and the shelf says so. CARES-310 randomised 543 patients with untreated unresectable HCC to camrelizumab plus rivoceranib or sorafenib. The primary analysis (PMID: 37499670) showed progression-free survival of 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.52) and interim survival of 22.1 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.62). The final analysis (PMID: 41308676) confirmed median overall survival of 23.8 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.64) — an 8.6-month absolute median gain — with grade 3-4 hypertension in 38% versus 15%. A post-hoc patient-reported-outcomes analysis by age (PMID: 41972014) is the third cardable report and favoured the combination in both age groups. No second trial exists; enrolment was 83% Asian, and the combination is not FDA-approved in the US.

cards.headline: Qin 2023 (CARES-310, primary analysis): progression-free survival 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.52); interim overall survival 22.1 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.62)
cards.summary: Qin 2023 (CARES-310, primary analysis): progression-free survival 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.52); interim overall survival 22.1 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.62)
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial — primary analysis (Qin 2023, CARES-310)
cards.people: 543 patients with unresectable or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma and no prior systemic therapy at 95 sites in 13 countries, randomised to camrelizumab 200 mg intravenously every 2 weeks plus rivoceranib 250 mg daily (272) or sorafenib 400 mg twice daily (271).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months (95% CI 5.5 to 6.3) versus 3.7 months (2.8 to 3.7) (hazard ratio 0.52, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.65; p<0.0001), a 48% relative reduction in the hazard of progression or death. At the interim survival analysis, median overall survival was 22.1 months (19.1 to 27.2) versus 15.2 months (13.0 to 18.5) (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.80; p<0.0001).
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial; survival was still interim at this report. Enrolment was predominantly Asian — the final analysis reports 83% Asian participants — which limits direct transfer to other populations.
cards.source: Qin S et al. Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib versus sorafenib as first-line therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (CARES-310): a randomised, open-label, international phase 3 study. Lancet (London, England). 2023. PMID: 37499670. Registry ID: NCT03764293. cards.headline: Qin 2025 (CARES-310, final analysis): median overall survival 23.8 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.64); grade 3-4 hypertension 38% versus 15%
cards.summary: Qin 2025 (CARES-310, final analysis): median overall survival 23.8 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.64); grade 3-4 hypertension 38% versus 15%
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial — final analysis (Qin 2025, CARES-310)
cards.people: The same 543 CARES-310 patients (84% male, 83% Asian), with median follow-up of 22.1 months in the camrelizumab-rivoceranib group and 14.9 months in the sorafenib group at the final analysis (June 14, 2023).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 23.8 months (95% CI 20.6 to 27.2) with camrelizumab plus rivoceranib versus 15.2 months (13.2 to 18.5) with sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.79; p<0.0001), a 36% relative reduction in the hazard of death and an 8.6-month absolute median gain. Updated median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.54). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related event was hypertension (38% versus 15%).
cards.watchOut: The final analysis of the same single trial, not independent confirmation — the shelf's structure is one trial reported twice, plus the post-hoc report below. Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib is not FDA-approved in the US.

cards.headline: Chan 2026 (CARES-310 post-hoc patient-reported outcomes by age): quality-of-life, functioning, pain and fatigue favoured camrelizumab-rivoceranib in both under-65 and 65-and-over groups, despite more treatment-related adverse events
cards.summary: Chan 2026 (CARES-310 post-hoc patient-reported outcomes by age): quality-of-life, functioning, pain and fatigue favoured camrelizumab-rivoceranib in both under-65 and 65-and-over groups, despite more treatment-related adverse events
cards.type: Post-hoc analysis of the phase 3 trial (Chan 2026, CARES-310)
cards.people: CARES-310 participants split at age 65, assessed for patient-reported outcomes (time to a 10-point or greater deterioration in quality of life, physical and role functioning, and symptoms), survival and safety. This is the third cardable CARES-310 report confirmed this session — a post-hoc analysis of the same trial, carded and labelled as such.
cards.result: Patient-reported outcomes showed clinically meaningful benefits with camrelizumab-rivoceranib versus sorafenib for quality of life, functioning, pain and fatigue in both age groups, and both age groups kept the survival advantage, even though treatment-related adverse-event rates were higher with the combination; the commonest grade 3 or worse events in the combination arm were hypertension and raised AST, versus hand-foot syndrome with sorafenib.
cards.watchOut: Post-hoc and age-subgroup: supportive texture for the main result, not a separate trial. No MeSH terms were captured from this record this session.

STRUCTURE STATED HONESTLY: three reports, one trial — there is no second randomised trial of this combination.

shelves.title: Retifanlimab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel in advanced anal cancer (POD1UM-303): progression-free survival 9.3 versus 7.4 months (HR 0.63); final overall survival 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75)
shelves.question: In adults with inoperable locally recurrent or metastatic squamous-cell anal carcinoma, does retifanlimab added to carboplatin/paclitaxel versus chemotherapy alone improve progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Carboplatin/administration & dosage/therapeutic use/adverse effects · Paclitaxel/administration & dosage/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Male · Female · Middle Aged · Anus Neoplasms/drug therapy/pathology/mortality · Double-Blind Method · Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use/adverse effects/administration & dosage · Carcinoma, Squamous Cell/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/drug therapy · Adult · Progression-Free Survival
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one randomised programme. In POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2 (308 patients, no prior systemic therapy), adding retifanlimab to carboplatin-paclitaxel lengthened median progression-free survival from 7.4 to 9.3 months (HR 0.63, PMID: 40517007), and the final survival analysis (PMID: 42097353) found median overall survival of 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75) despite 77 placebo patients crossing over to retifanlimab. Grade 3 or worse adverse events were more frequent with retifanlimab (83.1% versus 75.0%). The single-arm POD1UM-202 study (PMID: 35816951) is carded as supporting evidence only: response 13.8% after platinum failure, showing drug activity but no comparative estimate. Single programme, so the stamp caps at POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: Rao 2025 (POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2): progression-free survival 9.3 versus 7.4 months with retifanlimab added to carboplatin-paclitaxel (HR 0.63, p=0.0006); grade 3 or worse events 83.1% versus 75.0%
cards.summary: Rao 2025 (POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2): progression-free survival 9.3 versus 7.4 months with retifanlimab added to carboplatin-paclitaxel (HR 0.63, p=0.0006); grade 3 or worse events 83.1% versus 75.0%
cards.people: 308 patients with inoperable locally recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal and no previous systemic therapy, at 70 centres in 12 countries, randomised to retifanlimab 500 mg every 4 weeks or placebo, each with carboplatin-paclitaxel for up to 1 year; placebo patients could cross over to retifanlimab at progression. 72% were female.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 9.3 months (95% CI 7.5 to 11.3) with retifanlimab versus 7.4 months (7.1 to 7.7) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.84; one-sided p=0.0006), a 37% relative reduction in the hazard of progression or death. Serious adverse events occurred in 47.4% versus 38.8% and grade 3 or worse events in 83.1% versus 75.0%; the commonest grade 3 or worse events were neutropenia (35.1% versus 29.6%) and anaemia (19.5% versus 20.4%).
cards.watchOut: Primary endpoint was progression-free survival; overall survival was immature in this report (see the final survival card). Crossover at progression dilutes the survival comparison toward no difference.

cards.headline: Rao 2026 (POD1UM-303 final survival): median overall survival 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75); response 56.5% versus 44.8%, despite crossover of 77 placebo patients to retifanlimab
cards.summary: Rao 2026 (POD1UM-303 final survival): median overall survival 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75); response 56.5% versus 44.8%, despite crossover of 77 placebo patients to retifanlimab
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial — final overall-survival analysis (Rao 2026, POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2)
cards.people: The same 308 POD1UM-303 patients (154 per arm); 77 patients in the placebo group crossed over to retifanlimab monotherapy after progression.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 32.8 months with retifanlimab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel versus 22.2 months with placebo plus chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.01; p=0.0305), a 25% relative reduction in the hazard of death and a 10.6-month absolute median gain. Progression-free survival benefit persisted (HR 0.62). Overall response was 56.5% versus 44.8% and disease control 87.7% versus 80.5%. Crossover-adjusted analyses were consistent. No new safety signals were reported.
cards.watchOut: The survival confidence interval reaches 1.01 and half the placebo arm crossed over to retifanlimab, so the survival estimate is the least precise part of the programme — directionally supportive, not definitive on its own.

cards.people: 94 patients with locally advanced or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal who had progressed after, or were ineligible for, platinum-based therapy; retifanlimab 500 mg every 4 weeks, open-label, no comparator.
cards.result: Overall response rate was 13.8% (95% CI 7.6% to 22.5%), with 1 complete and 12 partial responses; stable disease in 35.1% gave a disease control rate of 48.9%. cards.watchOut: Single-arm with no comparator: response and durability show the drug has activity in this disease, but nothing here estimates how much it adds — that estimate comes only from POD1UM-303.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one randomised trial shows longer progression-free and overall survival when retifanlimab is added first-line; a single-arm study shows modest later-line activity
cards.summary: Synthesis: one randomised trial shows longer progression-free and overall survival when retifanlimab is added first-line; a single-arm study shows modest later-line activity
cards.people: POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2 (308 patients, retifanlimab or placebo added to carboplatin-paclitaxel, reported for progression-free survival in 2025 and final overall survival in 2026) plus POD1UM-202 (94 patients, single-arm retifanlimab after platinum failure).
cards.result: First-line: progression-free survival 9.3 versus 7.4 months (HR 0.63) and overall survival 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75), with more serious and grade 3 or worse adverse events on the retifanlimab arm (47.4% versus 38.8%; 83.1% versus 75.0%). cards.watchOut: Anal cancer is uncommon and this is the only randomised programme; the survival interval estimate is wide (HR 95% CI 0.55 to 1.01) and crossover complicates it. FDA approved retifanlimab for this indication in May 2025 (per the slate record).
cards.source: Synthesis of the three cards above (PMIDs: 40517007, 42097353, 35816951).

shelves.title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-positive gastric/GEJ cancer: second-line survival 14.7 versus 11.4 months versus ramucirumab plus paclitaxel (HR 0.70, DESTINY-Gastric04); interstitial lung disease in 13.9%
shelves.question: In adults with HER2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal-junction cancer, does trastuzumab deruxtecan versus standard therapy improve survival, in second-line and later settings?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Adenocarcinoma/drug therapy/mortality/secondary · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects/administration & dosage · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Esophageal Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Esophagogastric Junction/pathology · Immunoconjugates/adverse effects/administration & dosage · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Paclitaxel/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Progression-Free Survival · Ramucirumab/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases/analysis · Stomach Neoplasms/drug therapy/mortality/pathology · Trastuzumab/adverse effects/administration & dosage · Biopsy · Pathologic Complete Response · Lung Diseases, Interstitial/chemically induced/epidemiology · Pneumonia/chemically induced/epidemiology · Young Adult · Camptothecin/analogs & derivatives
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit). The randomised anchor is DESTINY-Gastric04 (PMID: 40454632): in second line, after progression on trastuzumab-based therapy with HER2 re-confirmed on biopsy, trastuzumab deruxtecan gave median overall survival of 14.7 versus 11.4 months against ramucirumab plus paclitaxel (HR 0.70) and response of 44.3% versus 29.1%. Single-arm support is consistent: DESTINY-Gastric02 in the USA/Europe (PMID: 37329891) response 42%, and the phase 1 gastric cohort (PMID: 31047804) response 43.2%. The harm to keep on the face is interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis: 13.9% adjudicated drug-related cases in the randomised trial and two treatment-associated deaths in Gastric02. PREMISE NOTE: the DESTINY-Gastric01 primary report is already carded elsewhere in the library, so under the one-home rule it is cross-pointed here, not re-carded; this shelf leads with the second-line randomised question.

cards.headline: Shitara 2025 (DESTINY-Gastric04, second-line): trastuzumab deruxtecan versus ramucirumab plus paclitaxel — median survival 14.7 versus 11.4 months (HR 0.70, p=0.004); response 44.3% versus 29.1%; drug-related interstitial lung disease 13.9%
cards.summary: Shitara 2025 (DESTINY-Gastric04, second-line): trastuzumab deruxtecan versus ramucirumab plus paclitaxel — median survival 14.7 versus 11.4 months (HR 0.70, p=0.004); response 44.3% versus 29.1%; drug-related interstitial lung disease 13.9%
cards.people: 494 patients with HER2-positive metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, HER2 status confirmed on biopsy after progression on trastuzumab-based therapy, randomised to second-line trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg or ramucirumab plus paclitaxel.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer with trastuzumab deruxtecan (median 14.7 versus 11.4 months; hazard ratio for death 0.70, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.90; p=0.004), a 30% relative reduction in the hazard of death and a 3.3-month absolute median gain. Progression-free survival also favoured it (HR 0.74) and confirmed objective response was 44.3% versus 29.1%. Drug-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 50.0% versus 54.1%. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 13.9% on trastuzumab deruxtecan (mostly grade 1-2, one grade 3) versus 1.3% on the comparator.
cards.watchOut: Interstitial lung disease is the signature harm and must stay on the face: about 1 in 7 patients on the drug in this trial. HER2 status was re-confirmed on a post-progression biopsy, so results apply to patients who remain HER2-positive.
cards.source: Shitara K et al. Trastuzumab Deruxtecan or Ramucirumab plus Paclitaxel in Gastric Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2025. PMID: 40454632. Registry ID: NCT04704934. cards.headline: Van Cutsem 2023 (DESTINY-Gastric02, single-arm): response 42% at updated analysis (79 patients, USA/Europe); two treatment-associated deaths from interstitial lung disease
cards.summary: Van Cutsem 2023 (DESTINY-Gastric02, single-arm): response 42% at updated analysis (79 patients, USA/Europe); two treatment-associated deaths from interstitial lung disease
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 trial (Van Cutsem 2023, DESTINY-Gastric02) — supporting evidence, labelled single-arm
cards.people: 79 patients in the USA and Europe with HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer progressing on or after a trastuzumab-containing regimen, given trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks; no comparator. Median age 60.7 years, 72% male.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response was 38% (30 of 79) at the primary analysis and 42% (33 of 79, including 5% complete responses) at the updated analysis (median follow-up 10.2 months). The commonest grade 3 or worse events were anaemia (14%), nausea (8%) and low neutrophil count (8%). Drug-related serious events occurred in 13%, and two patients (3%) died of treatment-associated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: the response rate shows activity in Western patients (the earlier randomised evidence was East Asian) but cannot estimate a survival effect — the randomised survival estimate on this shelf comes from DESTINY-Gastric04.
cards.source: Van Cutsem E et al. cards.headline: Shitara 2019 (phase 1 dose-expansion, gastric cohort): response 43.2% (19 of 44) in heavily pretreated HER2-positive gastric cancer; grade 3 or worse anaemia 30%; four pneumonitis cases, no drug-related deaths
cards.summary: Shitara 2019 (phase 1 dose-expansion, gastric cohort): response 43.2% (19 of 44) in heavily pretreated HER2-positive gastric cancer; grade 3 or worse anaemia 30%; four pneumonitis cases, no drug-related deaths
cards.type: Phase 1 dose-expansion cohort (Shitara 2019) — early supporting evidence, labelled phase 1
cards.people: 44 patients with HER2-positive gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer, all previously treated with trastuzumab, at hospitals in the USA and Japan, given trastuzumab deruxtecan at the recommended expansion doses (5.4 or 6.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks); open-label, no comparator.
cards.result: 19 of 44 patients (43.2%, 95% CI 28.3 to 59.0) had a confirmed objective response. All patients had at least one treatment-emergent adverse event; the most frequent grade 3 or worse were anaemia (30%), low neutrophils (20%), low platelets (18%) and low white cell count (16%). Serious events occurred in 25%; there were four pneumonitis cases (three grade 2, one grade 3) and no drug-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Small, early, uncontrolled cohort in heavily pretreated patients — carded to complete the development record honestly, not as effectiveness evidence. NOTE: the randomised DESTINY-Gastric01 primary report (third-line, Japan/South Korea) is already carded elsewhere in the library and is therefore not re-carded here (one-home rule); this shelf leads with the second-line randomised trial instead.

cards.people: DESTINY-Gastric04 (494 patients, randomised, second-line), DESTINY-Gastric02 (79 patients, single-arm, USA/Europe) and the phase 1 gastric dose-expansion cohort (44 patients) — 617 patients in total on this shelf. The earlier randomised DESTINY-Gastric01 report is homed elsewhere in the library and is cross-pointed, not duplicated.
cards.result: Trastuzumab deruxtecan improved second-line overall survival versus ramucirumab plus paclitaxel (median 14.7 versus 11.4 months, HR 0.70) with response rates of 44.3% versus 29.1% in the randomised trial and 42-43% in the single-arm studies. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 13.9% of randomised-trial patients on the drug, including fatal cases in the single-arm study (2 of 79). PROPOSED POSSIBLE (benefit): one randomised trial plus consistent uncontrolled support, capped at POSSIBLE.
cards.watchOut: Applies only to HER2-positive disease (about 15-20% of advanced gastric/GEJ cancers), with HER2 re-confirmation after trastuzumab progression in the randomised trial. Lung toxicity monitoring is part of the treatment, not an afterthought.

shelves.question: In adults with previously untreated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer, does encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 versus standard chemotherapy improve progression-free and overall survival?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — one first-line trial programme. BREAKWATER randomised patients with untreated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer to encorafenib plus cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 or standard care. Response was 60.9% versus 40.0% (PMID: 39863775), progression-free survival 12.8 versus 7.1 months (HR 0.53) and interim overall survival 30.3 versus 15.1 months (HR 0.49) (PMID: 40444708); Cohort 3, using a FOLFIRI backbone, was concordant (PMID: 42219860). The previously treated question — BEACON, encorafenib plus cetuximab after prior therapy — is homed at pack #5165, which was read in full before building; no BEACON PMID is carded here. cards.headline: Kopetz 2025 (BREAKWATER, response report): objective response 60.9% with encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 versus 40.0% with standard care (odds ratio 2.44); median duration of response 13.9 versus 11.1 months
cards.summary: Kopetz 2025 (BREAKWATER, response report): objective response 60.9% with encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 versus 40.0% with standard care (odds ratio 2.44); median duration of response 13.9 versus 11.1 months
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial — objective-response report (Kopetz 2025, BREAKWATER)
cards.people: Patients with previously untreated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer randomised to encorafenib plus cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 or standard of care (chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab) in the phase 3 BREAKWATER study; progression-free survival data were not yet mature at this data cutoff.
cards.result: BREAKWATER met its objective-response dual primary endpoint: response was 60.9% with encorafenib-cetuximab-mFOLFOX6 versus 40.0% with standard care (odds ratio 2.443, 95% CI 1.403 to 4.253; one-sided p=0.0008) — an odds ratio is a relative measure; the absolute difference was 20.9 percentage points. Median duration of response was 13.9 versus 11.1 months. At this first interim survival look the hazard ratio was 0.47 (95% CI 0.318 to 0.691). Serious adverse events occurred in 37.7% versus 34.6%.
cards.watchOut: An early report with immature survival and progression data — superseded on those endpoints by the 2025 NEJM report carded next; carded because response was itself a dual primary endpoint and drove the accelerated approval.
cards.source: Kopetz S et al. Encorafenib, cetuximab and chemotherapy in BRAF-mutant colorectal cancer: a randomized phase 3 trial. Nature medicine. 2025. PMID: 39863775. Registry ID: NCT04607421. cards.headline: Elez 2025 (BREAKWATER, progression-free and overall survival): PFS 12.8 versus 7.1 months (HR 0.53); interim overall survival 30.3 versus 15.1 months (HR 0.49); serious adverse events 46.1% versus 38.9%
cards.summary: Elez 2025 (BREAKWATER, progression-free and overall survival): PFS 12.8 versus 7.1 months (HR 0.53); interim overall survival 30.3 versus 15.1 months (HR 0.49); serious adverse events 46.1% versus 38.9%
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial — PFS/OS report (Elez 2025, BREAKWATER)
cards.people: Patients with untreated BRAF V600E-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer randomised to encorafenib plus cetuximab (EC), EC plus mFOLFOX6, or standard care (chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab); the comparisons reported here are EC plus mFOLFOX6 versus standard care.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer with EC plus mFOLFOX6 (median 12.8 versus 7.1 months; hazard ratio for progression or death 0.53, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.68; p<0.001), a 47% relative reduction in the hazard. In an interim analysis, overall survival was also significantly longer (median 30.3 versus 15.1 months; hazard ratio for death 0.49, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.63; p<0.001) — a 15.2-month absolute median difference. Serious adverse events during treatment occurred in 46.1% versus 38.9%.
cards.watchOut: Overall survival is an interim analysis, however striking; the trial is open-label. This is FIRST-LINE treatment — the previously treated question (BEACON) is homed at pack #5165 and is not duplicated here.
