cards.headline: SERENA-6 extended analysis (Turner 2026): progression-free survival 16.8 vs 9.2 months (hazard ratio 0.45, relative) and second progression-free survival 25.7 vs 19.1 months (hazard ratio 0.63, relative)
cards.summary: SERENA-6 extended analysis (Turner 2026): progression-free survival 16.8 vs 9.2 months (hazard ratio 0.45, relative) and second progression-free survival 25.7 vs 19.1 months (hazard ratio 0.63, relative)
cards.type: Extended analysis of the SERENA-6 phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary report above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 315 randomised SERENA-6 patients (157 camizestrant + CDK4/6 inhibitor, 158 aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor), now at median follow-up 23.5 months (data cutoff January 2, 2026). Of 3,325 screened patients, 3,256 had at least one ESR1 test and 548 had a positive test by screening closure.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 16.8 months (95% CI 14.7 to 19.4) versus 9.2 months (7.2 to 9.7); hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.59; nominal P<0.0001) — a relative measure with absolute medians beside it. Median second progression-free survival was 25.7 months (95% CI 20.4 to 30.3) versus 19.1 months (16.8 to 21.0); hazard ratio 0.63 (0.46 to 0.86; P=0.0037), also relative. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (27% vs 17%) and neutrophil count decreased (23% vs 19%) — largely CDK4/6-inhibitor effects; serious adverse events occurred in 15% versus 19%. Three deaths were considered possibly treatment-related (one sudden death in the camizestrant group, possibly related to camizestrant; sepsis and ileus in the control group).
cards.watchOut: Updated progression-free survival at this cutoff was descriptive, and overall survival is not reported in this record: the benefit shown is progression-free and second-progression-free survival, not a demonstrated survival gain.
cards.source: Turner NC et al. Switching to camizestrant at ESR1 mutation emergence before disease progression during first-line treatment of hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer (SERENA-6): extended analysis of a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2026. PMID: 42442380. Registry ID: NCT04964934. cards.headline: SERENA-2 phase 2 (Oliveira 2024): camizestrant after endocrine progression — median progression-free survival 7.2 months (75 mg) and 7.7 months (150 mg) vs 3.7 months on fulvestrant
cards.summary: SERENA-2 phase 2 (Oliveira 2024): camizestrant after endocrine progression — median progression-free survival 7.2 months (75 mg) and 7.7 months (150 mg) vs 3.7 months on fulvestrant
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised open-label multi-dose trial (SERENA-2), camizestrant vs fulvestrant after endocrine progression
cards.people: 240 post-menopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer recurring or progressing on at least one line of endocrine therapy (no more than one prior endocrine line in the advanced setting), randomised to camizestrant 75 mg (n=74), 150 mg (n=73) or 300 mg (n=20, arm closed early) once daily, or fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly (n=73). Median follow-up about 16 months in the main arms.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 7.2 months (90% CI 3.7 to 10.9) with camizestrant 75 mg, 7.7 months (5.5 to 12.9) with 150 mg, and 3.7 months (2.0 to 6.0) with fulvestrant. Hazard ratios versus fulvestrant were 0.59 (90% CI 0.42 to 0.82; P=0.017) for 75 mg and 0.64 (0.46 to 0.89; P=0.0090) for 150 mg — relative measures with the absolute medians beside them. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 53% (75 mg), 67% (150 mg) and 70% (300 mg) versus 18% on fulvestrant; no single grade 3-or-worse treatment-emergent event occurred in more than 3% of any group, and no treatment-related deaths occurred.
cards.watchOut: A phase 2 dose-finding comparison in a different slice (post-progression) from SERENA-6's pre-progression switch: the two slices are labelled on this shelf and their results are not pooled. No formal comparison was planned for the closed 300 mg arm.
cards.source: Oliveira M et al. cards.headline: SERENA-1 phase 1 monotherapy (Hamilton 2024): camizestrant 25-450 mg in heavily pretreated disease — visual effects in 56% and sinus bradycardia in 44% were the characteristic harms; efficacy seen at all doses
cards.summary: SERENA-1 phase 1 monotherapy (Hamilton 2024): camizestrant 25-450 mg in heavily pretreated disease — visual effects in 56% and sinus bradycardia in 44% were the characteristic harms; efficacy seen at all doses
cards.type: Phase 1 single-arm dose-escalation/expansion study (SERENA-1), camizestrant monotherapy
cards.people: 108 women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, refractory or intolerant to therapy, received camizestrant monotherapy at 25-450 mg once daily (dose escalation) or 75, 150 or 300 mg once daily (expansion), by the March 9, 2021 cutoff.
cards.result: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 93 patients (86.1%), 82.4% of them grade 1 or 2. The most common were visual effects (56%), (sinus) bradycardia (44%), fatigue (26%) and nausea (15%). There were no grade 3-or-worse treatment-related events and no treatment-related serious adverse events at doses of 150 mg or below. Antitumour efficacy was observed at all doses, including after CDK4/6 inhibitors and/or fulvestrant, with and without baseline ESR1 mutations, and in visceral disease including liver metastases. This study established the 75, 150 and 300 mg doses taken into phase 2. Registry note: the abstract of this record names the study as SERENA-1 (NCT03616587), while the record's DataBank field lists NCT04214288 and NCT04588298 (the SERENA-2/SERENA-3 trials) — the source line below reproduces the DataBank field as required, and the discrepancy is flagged here and in the build summary.
cards.watchOut: Phase 1, single-arm, dose-ranging: it establishes dose, pharmacokinetics and the visual/bradycardia harm profile — the photopsia/visual effects flagged for this SERD — but carries no comparative efficacy weight.
cards.source: Hamilton E et al. cards.headline: Synthesis: two randomised slices point the same way — a ctDNA-guided switch before progression (SERENA-6) and treatment after progression (SERENA-2) both prolong progression-free survival
cards.summary: Synthesis: two randomised slices point the same way — a ctDNA-guided switch before progression (SERENA-6) and treatment after progression (SERENA-2) both prolong progression-free survival
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: SERENA-6 (315 randomised from 3,256 under ctDNA surveillance) shows the switch strategy prolonging progression-free survival (16.8 vs 9.2 months at extended analysis; hazard ratio 0.45, a relative measure) and second progression-free survival (25.7 vs 19.1 months; hazard ratio 0.63, relative), with overall survival not yet reported in these records. SERENA-2 (240 randomised) shows camizestrant beating fulvestrant after endocrine progression (median progression-free survival 7.2-7.7 vs 3.7 months). SERENA-1 (phase 1, n=108) supplies the dose and the characteristic harms — visual effects (56%) and sinus bradycardia (44%), mostly low grade. The two slices (molecular-emergence switch vs post-progression therapy) are distinct and are not pooled. Imlunestrant is a different oral SERD, homed on its own shelf (pack #7228) — the two agents are not merged and have never been compared head-to-head in this record.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Imlunestrant in advanced breast cancer (EMBER-3): benefit only in ESR1-mutated disease as monotherapy; adding abemaciclib helps all comers at more toxicity
shelves.question: In patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer recurring or progressing on aromatase-inhibitor therapy (with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor), does imlunestrant, versus standard endocrine monotherapy, prolong progression-free survival in ESR1-mutated and in all patients — and does adding abemaciclib beat imlunestrant alone?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Middle Aged · Aminopyridines · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Benzimidazoles · Breast Neoplasms · Estrogen Receptor alpha · Mutation · Progression-Free Survival · Benzopyrans · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Fulvestrant · Breast Neoplasms, Male · Male · Treatment Outcome · Androstadienes
shelves.balance: SPLIT, on a single programme (one trial, four reports). EMBER-3's monotherapy comparison is positive only where the biology predicts: ESR1-mutated disease (median progression-free survival 5.5 vs 3.8 months) and not in all patients (5.6 vs 5.5 months; hazard ratio 0.87, a relative measure; P=0.12). The combination comparison is positive in all comers (updated median progression-free survival 10.9 vs 5.5 months; hazard ratio 0.59, relative) but grade 3-or-higher events were 48.6% versus 17.1% for monotherapy. Interim overall survival in ESR1-mutated disease (34.5 vs 23.1 months; hazard ratio 0.60, relative) did not reach its significance boundary and is not claimed as a survival benefit. Product: imlunestrant (Inluriyo, Eli Lilly).

cards.headline: EMBER-3 primary report (Jhaveri 2025): imlunestrant beat standard therapy ONLY in ESR1-mutated disease (median progression-free survival 5.5 vs 3.8 months); in all patients it did not (hazard ratio 0.87, P=0.12) — while adding abemaciclib beat imlunestrant alone (9.4 vs 5.5 months, hazard ratio 0.57)
cards.summary: EMBER-3 primary report (Jhaveri 2025): imlunestrant beat standard therapy ONLY in ESR1-mutated disease (median progression-free survival 5.5 vs 3.8 months); in all patients it did not (hazard ratio 0.87, P=0.12) — while adding abemaciclib beat imlunestrant alone (9.4 vs 5.5 months, hazard ratio 0.57)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label three-arm trial (EMBER-3), imlunestrant vs standard endocrine therapy vs imlunestrant + abemaciclib
cards.people: 874 patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer recurring or progressing during or after aromatase-inhibitor therapy (alone or with a CDK4/6 inhibitor), randomised 1:1:1 to imlunestrant (n=331), standard endocrine monotherapy (n=330), or imlunestrant + abemaciclib (n=213); 256 patients had ESR1 mutations.
cards.result: Among ESR1-mutated patients, median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with imlunestrant versus 3.8 months with standard therapy; restricted mean survival time at 19.4 months was 7.9 versus 5.4 months (difference 2.6 months; P<0.001). In the overall population, median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 5.5 months (hazard ratio 0.87, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.72 to 1.04; P=0.12) — not significant. Among the 426 concurrently randomised patients in the combination comparison, median progression-free survival was 9.4 months with imlunestrant + abemaciclib versus 5.5 months with imlunestrant alone (hazard ratio 0.57, relative; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.73; P<0.001). Grade 3-or-higher adverse events: 17.1% (imlunestrant), 20.7% (standard therapy), 48.6% (combination). Product naming (clarification exception, per the commissioning row): imlunestrant (Inluriyo, Eli Lilly).
cards.watchOut: The trial's own hierarchy is the honesty point: monotherapy benefit is confined to the ESR1-mutated population, the all-patient monotherapy comparison was not significant, and the combination's gain comes with nearly triple the grade 3-or-higher event rate of monotherapy.
cards.source: Jhaveri KL et al. Imlunestrant with or without Abemaciclib in Advanced Breast Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2025. PMID: 39660834. Registry ID: NCT04975308. cards.headline: EMBER-3 updated efficacy / interim overall survival (Jhaveri 2026): in ESR1-mutated disease median overall survival 34.5 vs 23.1 months (hazard ratio 0.60) but the significance boundary was NOT reached; combination progression-free survival 10.9 vs 5.5 months
cards.summary: EMBER-3 updated efficacy / interim overall survival (Jhaveri 2026): in ESR1-mutated disease median overall survival 34.5 vs 23.1 months (hazard ratio 0.60) but the significance boundary was NOT reached; combination progression-free survival 10.9 vs 5.5 months
cards.type: Updated efficacy and prespecified interim overall-survival analysis of EMBER-3 (same trial as the primary report above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 874 randomised patients (imlunestrant n=331, standard therapy n=330, combination n=213), at median follow-up 28.5 months (data cutoff August 18, 2025); 10.1% remained on treatment.
cards.result: In ESR1-mutated patients, median overall survival was 34.5 months with imlunestrant versus 23.1 months with standard therapy (hazard ratio 0.60, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.86; P=0.0043) — but the boundary for significance was not reached, because only two of the three progression-free-survival endpoints had been met and only a limited significance level passed to the survival comparisons, so this is not a demonstrated survival benefit. For the combination versus imlunestrant in all patients, median overall survival was not reached versus 34.4 months (hazard ratio 0.82; P=0.2622). Updated median progression-free survival for the combination versus imlunestrant was 10.9 versus 5.5 months (hazard ratio 0.59, relative; nominal P<0.0001). All prespecified exploratory endpoints favoured imlunestrant-based regimens, and safety was consistent with prior reports.
cards.watchOut: Interim survival analysis with an unreached significance boundary: the ESR1-mutated survival numbers are encouraging but must not be presented as a proven overall-survival benefit.
cards.source: Jhaveri KL et al. Imlunestrant with or without abemaciclib in advanced breast cancer: updated efficacy results from the phase III EMBER-3 trial. cards.headline: EMBER-3 safety analyses (O'Shaughnessy 2026): discontinuation in 5% on imlunestrant and 6% on the combination; combination events managed with dose adjustments in 61%
cards.summary: EMBER-3 safety analyses (O'Shaughnessy 2026): discontinuation in 5% on imlunestrant and 6% on the combination; combination events managed with dose adjustments in 61%
cards.type: Safety analysis of the EMBER-3 trial (same trial as the cards above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: Patients in the imlunestrant-containing arms of EMBER-3, including prespecified age subgroups (under 65 versus 65 or older). This record carries no MeSH terms and no registry ID in PubMed, so the source line records that plainly.
cards.result: In both imlunestrant-containing arms the most common treatment-emergent adverse events were reversible, low grade, single occurrences, arose early, and led to few discontinuations (imlunestrant 5%; imlunestrant + abemaciclib 6%). Events in the combination arm were managed with dose adjustments (61%) and supportive medication. Imlunestrant monotherapy's safety profile was similar in patients under 65 and 65 or older, and the combination's profile resembled other abemaciclib + endocrine-therapy combinations in both age groups.
cards.watchOut: A safety-characterisation report without quantified event rates in its abstract record: the graded event rates on this shelf come from the primary report (grade 3-or-higher 17.1% / 20.7% / 48.6%).

cards.result: Global health status/quality of life and function were generally maintained over time in all treatment arms, with treatment differences favouring imlunestrant over standard therapy in the ESR1-mutated population and fewer deterioration events in the imlunestrant arm. cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial (EMBER-3), three reports deep — monotherapy works in ESR1-mutated disease, not in all comers; the combination works more broadly at higher toxicity
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial (EMBER-3), three reports deep — monotherapy works in ESR1-mutated disease, not in all comers; the combination works more broadly at higher toxicity
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: EMBER-3 is a single programme: one three-arm trial (n=874) reported as primary, updated-efficacy/interim-survival, safety and patient-reported-outcome papers. Its two comparisons must stay separate: (1) imlunestrant versus standard endocrine therapy — progression-free-survival benefit in ESR1-mutated disease (median 5.5 vs 3.8 months; restricted-mean difference 2.6 months) but not in all patients (hazard ratio 0.87; P=0.12), with interim overall survival of 34.5 versus 23.1 months in ESR1-mutated disease that did not reach its significance boundary; (2) imlunestrant + abemaciclib versus imlunestrant — progression-free survival 10.9 versus 5.5 months at update (hazard ratio 0.59, relative), regardless of ESR1 status, at the cost of grade 3-or-higher events in 48.6% versus 17.1%. Quality of life was generally maintained in all arms. Camizestrant is a different oral SERD, homed on its own shelf (pack #7227) — not merged, never head-to-head in this record.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Niraparib + abiraterone in mCRPC (MAGNITUDE, prostate): progression delayed in BRCA/HRR-positive disease — final overall survival not different, futility without HRR alterations
shelves.question: In men with treatment-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and homologous-recombination-repair gene alterations (notably BRCA1/2), does niraparib plus abiraterone acetate + prednisone, versus placebo plus abiraterone + prednisone, prolong radiographic progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Male · Humans · Abiraterone Acetate · Prostatic Neoplasms, Castration-Resistant · BRCA1 Protein · BRCA2 Protein · Prednisone · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Indazoles · Piperidines
shelves.balance: SPLIT, on a single programme (one trial, five reports). MAGNITUDE (prostate, NCT03748641 — not the nex-z ATTR trial of the same name) delayed radiographic progression in HRR-positive disease (16.5 vs 13.7 months; hazard ratio 0.73, a relative measure) and most in BRCA1/2 disease (16.6 vs 10.9 months; hazard ratio 0.53, relative), and delayed symptomatic progression and cytotoxic chemotherapy. But final overall survival did not differ (hazard ratio 0.931 in HRR-positive; 0.788 in BRCA1/2, nominal P=0.183), the HRR-negative cohort (n=247) was stopped for futility, and the FDA limited approval to BRCA-mutated disease, finding the broader HRR benefit was driven by that subgroup. Anaemia (including transfusion in 27%) and hypertension are the added harms. Benefit must not be generalised to unselected mCRPC.

cards.headline: MAGNITUDE primary report (Chi 2023): niraparib + abiraterone prolonged radiographic progression-free survival in BRCA1/2 disease (16.6 vs 10.9 months; hazard ratio 0.53, relative) and in all HRR-positive disease (16.5 vs 13.7; hazard ratio 0.73) — and the HRR-negative cohort was stopped for futility
cards.summary: MAGNITUDE primary report (Chi 2023): niraparib + abiraterone prolonged radiographic progression-free survival in BRCA1/2 disease (16.6 vs 10.9 months; hazard ratio 0.53, relative) and in all HRR-positive disease (16.5 vs 13.7; hazard ratio 0.73) — and the HRR-negative cohort was stopped for futility
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (MAGNITUDE, prostate), niraparib + abiraterone + prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone + prednisone, first-line mCRPC
cards.people: MAGNITUDE randomised patients with treatment-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer 1:1 to niraparib + abiraterone acetate + prednisone or placebo + abiraterone + prednisone, in two prospectively tested cohorts: HRR-positive (n=423) and HRR-negative (n=247). The primary endpoint, radiographic progression-free survival by central review, was tested first in the BRCA1/2 subgroup, then in the full HRR-positive cohort. This is the prostate MAGNITUDE trial (NCT03748641) — not the nex-z transthyretin-amyloidosis trial of the same programme name.
cards.result: In the BRCA1/2 subgroup, median radiographic progression-free survival was 16.6 versus 10.9 months (hazard ratio 0.53, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.36 to 0.79; P=.001). In the overall HRR-positive cohort it was 16.5 versus 13.7 months (hazard ratio 0.73, relative; 95% CI 0.56 to 0.96; P=.022). Secondary endpoints of time to symptomatic progression and time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy also improved. In the HRR-negative cohort, futility was declared per the prespecified criteria — the negative cohort is part of the answer. Anaemia and hypertension were the most reported grade 3-or-worse adverse events.
cards.watchOut: Benefit is biomarker-bounded: the hierarchical result is strongest in BRCA1/2, weaker in all HRR-positive disease, and absent (futility) without HRR alterations — it must not be generalised to unselected mCRPC.
cards.source: Chi KN et al. Niraparib and Abiraterone Acetate for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2023. PMID: 36952634. Registry ID: NCT03748641. cards.headline: MAGNITUDE second interim analysis (Chi 2023): BRCA1/2 radiographic progression-free survival 19.5 vs 10.9 months (hazard ratio 0.55, relative); overall survival hazard ratio 0.88, not significant, in BRCA1/2 disease
cards.summary: MAGNITUDE second interim analysis (Chi 2023): BRCA1/2 radiographic progression-free survival 19.5 vs 10.9 months (hazard ratio 0.55, relative); overall survival hazard ratio 0.88, not significant, in BRCA1/2 disease
cards.type: Second prespecified interim analysis of the MAGNITUDE phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary report above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The HRR-positive cohort at longer follow-up: 212 patients received niraparib + abiraterone + prednisone (BRCA1/2 subgroup n=113 in this arm); median follow-up 24.8 months in the BRCA1/2 subgroup and 26.8 months in the total HRR-positive population.
cards.result: In the BRCA1/2 subgroup, median radiographic progression-free survival was 19.5 versus 10.9 months (hazard ratio 0.55, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.39 to 0.78; nominal P=0.0007). In the total HRR-positive population the hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI 0.60 to 0.97; nominal P=0.0280), also relative. Time to symptomatic progression and time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy improved. Overall survival in the BRCA1/2 subgroup gave a hazard ratio of 0.88 (95% CI 0.58 to 1.34; nominal P=0.5505) — not significant; a prespecified weighting analysis adjusting for subsequent PARP-inhibitor and other life-prolonging therapy use gave 0.54 (95% CI 0.33 to 0.90; nominal P=0.0181). No new safety signals were observed. This record carries no registry ID in its DataBank field, so the source line records that plainly.
cards.watchOut: Interim, nominal P values: the adjusted survival analysis is a sensitivity analysis that accounts for treatment switching; the unadjusted survival comparison at this point was null, and the final analysis below is the definitive survival read.

cards.headline: MAGNITUDE final overall-survival analysis (Chi 2025): NO difference in overall survival — hazard ratio 0.931 in HRR-positive disease and 0.788 (nominal P=0.183) in BRCA1/2 disease — despite the progression-free benefit and delayed symptomatic progression
cards.summary: MAGNITUDE final overall-survival analysis (Chi 2025): NO difference in overall survival — hazard ratio 0.931 in HRR-positive disease and 0.788 (nominal P=0.183) in BRCA1/2 disease — despite the progression-free benefit and delayed symptomatic progression
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the MAGNITUDE phase 3 trial (same trial as the cards above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The HRR-positive cohort (niraparib + abiraterone + prednisone n=212, placebo + abiraterone + prednisone n=211) at the prespecified event-driven final analysis, median follow-up 37.3 months. This record carries no registry ID in its DataBank field, so the source line records that plainly.
cards.result: Overall survival did not differ between arms in the HRR-positive population (hazard ratio 0.931, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.720 to 1.203; P=0.585) or in the BRCA1/2 subgroup (hazard ratio 0.788; 95% CI 0.554 to 1.120; nominal P=0.183). Prespecified multivariable analyses adjusted for baseline prognostic factors showed a trend in HRR-positive disease (hazard ratio 0.785; nominal P=0.066) and a nominally significant adjusted result in BRCA1/2 disease (hazard ratio 0.663; nominal P=0.024). Time to symptomatic progression improved significantly in both the HRR-positive population (hazard ratio 0.547; P=0.006) and the BRCA1/2 subgroup (hazard ratio 0.562; nominal P=0.006), as did time to cytotoxic chemotherapy (hazard ratios 0.688 and 0.598). The safety profile was unchanged, with adverse events primarily haematologic and manageable.
cards.watchOut: The definitive survival analysis is null on its primary (unadjusted) comparison: adjusted analyses are supportive only. The shelf's claim is delayed radiographic and symptomatic progression, not longer life.

European urology oncology. 2025. PMID: 40328571. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: MAGNITUDE patient-reported outcomes in BRCA1/2 disease (Rathkopf 2025): quality of life maintained, no significant difference in time to pain deterioration, and most patients reported little or no side-effect bother
cards.summary: MAGNITUDE patient-reported outcomes in BRCA1/2 disease (Rathkopf 2025): quality of life maintained, no significant difference in time to pain deterioration, and most patients reported little or no side-effect bother
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcome analysis of the MAGNITUDE trial, BRCA1/2 subgroup (same trial as the cards above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: All patients with BRCA1/2-altered metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in MAGNITUDE (n=225), with on-treatment patient-reported-outcome compliance above 80% for on-site completion, assessed with the Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form, FACT-P and EQ-5D-5L.
cards.result: Time to deterioration in pain by Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form and FACT-P scores did not significantly differ between niraparib + abiraterone + prednisone and placebo + abiraterone + prednisone. EQ-5D-5L showed no clinically meaningful differences in overall health-related quality of life between arms in the BRCA-positive subgroup. Tolerability was similar between arms; side-effect bother rated 'not at all' or 'a little bit' ranged from 79.8% to 95.9% during treatment. The authors note the analysis may not have been powered to detect a difference in patient-reported outcomes.
cards.watchOut: Patient-reported outcomes show maintained quality of life, not improvement: they support tolerability of the combination, not an efficacy claim.

Patient-reported Outcomes for Patients with Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer and BRCA1/2 Gene Alterations: Final Analysis from the Randomized Phase 3 MAGNITUDE Trial. cards.headline: FDA approval summary (Maguire 2025): approval limited to BRCA-mutated disease — FDA exploratory analyses found the HRR-positive progression benefit was primarily driven by the BRCA subgroup; anaemia requiring transfusion in 27%
cards.summary: FDA approval summary (Maguire 2025): approval limited to BRCA-mutated disease — FDA exploratory analyses found the HRR-positive progression benefit was primarily driven by the BRCA subgroup; anaemia requiring transfusion in 27%
cards.type: FDA approval summary of the MAGNITUDE trial (regulatory review of the same programme — not an independent trial)
cards.people: Cohort 1 of MAGNITUDE as reviewed by the FDA: 423 randomised patients with HRR-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with BRCA-mutation status as a stratification factor. This record carries no registry ID in its DataBank field, so the source line records that plainly.
cards.result: Median radiographic progression-free survival in the BRCA-mutated subpopulation was 16.6 months (95% CI 13.9 to not estimable) with niraparib + abiraterone + prednisone versus 10.9 months (95% CI 8.3 to 13.8) with placebo + abiraterone + prednisone (hazard ratio 0.53, a relative measure; 95% CI 0.36 to 0.79; P=0.0014). Although radiographic progression-free survival also improved in the all-HRR-mutated intention-to-treat population, FDA exploratory analyses indicated the improvement was primarily attributable to the BRCA-mutated subgroup, supporting limiting the indication to that population. Adding niraparib increased toxicity, including anaemia requiring transfusion in 27% of patients. The FDA approved the fixed-dose combination, with prednisone, on August 11, 2023 for deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
cards.watchOut: The licensed slice is BRCA-mutated disease only: carding the broader HRR-positive result without the FDA's subgroup finding would overstate who the approved treatment is for.
cards.source: Maguire WF et al. FDA Approval Summary: Niraparib plus Abiraterone Acetate Fixed-Dose Combination for BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer. cards.headline: Synthesis: one programme (prostate MAGNITUDE) — radiographic progression delayed in HRR-positive and especially BRCA disease, final overall survival not different, and futility without HRR alterations
cards.summary: Synthesis: one programme (prostate MAGNITUDE) — radiographic progression delayed in HRR-positive and especially BRCA disease, final overall survival not different, and futility without HRR alterations
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: MAGNITUDE (NCT03748641 — the prostate trial, unrelated to the nex-z transthyretin-amyloidosis programme of the same name) is a single programme reported five times. Radiographic progression-free survival improved in BRCA1/2 disease (16.6 vs 10.9 months at the primary report; 19.5 vs 10.9 at the second interim analysis) and in all HRR-positive disease (16.5 vs 13.7 months), and time to symptomatic progression and to cytotoxic chemotherapy improved. But the final overall-survival analysis showed no difference (hazard ratio 0.931 in HRR-positive disease; 0.788, nominal P=0.183, in BRCA1/2 disease), the HRR-negative cohort (n=247) was stopped for futility, quality of life was maintained rather than improved, and the FDA limited approval to BRCA-mutated disease after finding the HRR-positive benefit was driven by that subgroup — with anaemia requiring transfusion in 27%. The parallel talazoparib + enzalutamide PARP question (TALAPRO-2) has a different biomarker structure and is a cross-point only, not merged here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: TALAPRO-2: talazoparib + enzalutamide prolongs survival in first-line mCRPC — benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient disease (OS 45.1 vs 31.1 months), priced in anaemia
shelves.question: In men with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic first-line metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, does talazoparib plus enzalutamide, versus placebo plus enzalutamide, prolong radiographic progression-free and overall survival — in all comers and in HRR-deficient disease — and at what cost in anaemia and treatment burden?
shelves.mesh: Male · Humans · Adolescent · Prostatic Neoplasms, Castration-Resistant · Receptors, Androgen · Androgen Antagonists · Anemia · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Double-Blind Method · Benzamides · Nitriles · Phenylthiohydantoin · Phthalazines
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, TALAPRO-2, reported for two overlapping populations. In all comers (805 randomised), talazoparib + enzalutamide improved radiographic PFS (median not reached vs 21.9 months at primary analysis; hazard ratio 0.63, relative) and, at the final analysis, overall survival (median 45.8 vs 37.0 months; hazard ratio 0.80, relative). In HRR-deficient disease (399 randomised) the effects were larger: radiographic PFS hazard ratio 0.45 and final overall survival 45.1 vs 31.1 months (hazard ratio 0.62, relative), with BRCA1/2-altered patients showing 4-year survival of 53% vs 23%. In HRR-non-deficient/unknown disease the survival hazard ratio was 0.88 and not significant, and the US FDA limited approval to HRR gene-mutated disease — keep the all-comer and HRR-deficient claims separate. The price is anaemia: grade 3–4 in about 41–49% on the combination, transfusion in about 36–39%, dose reduction in about half. The MAGNITUDE question (niraparib + abiraterone) is the parallel PARP shelf — cross-point, do not merge.

cards.headline: TALAPRO-2 primary report, all-comer cohort (Agarwal 2023): talazoparib + enzalutamide improved radiographic PFS versus enzalutamide alone — median not reached vs 21.9 months, hazard ratio 0.63 (a relative measure)
cards.summary: TALAPRO-2 primary report, all-comer cohort (Agarwal 2023): talazoparib + enzalutamide improved radiographic PFS versus enzalutamide alone — median not reached vs 21.9 months, hazard ratio 0.63 (a relative measure)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (TALAPRO-2 cohort 1, all comers), talazoparib + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide
cards.people: 805 men with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic first-line metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer on ongoing androgen deprivation, prospectively tested for tumour HRR gene alterations (169 HRR-deficient) and randomised 1:1 (402 talazoparib 0.5 mg daily + enzalutamide 160 mg daily; 403 placebo + enzalutamide) at 223 centres in 26 countries.
cards.result: At median follow-up of about 25 months, median radiographic progression-free survival was not reached (95% CI 27.5 months–not reached) with talazoparib + enzalutamide versus 21.9 months (16.6–25.1) with enzalutamide alone; hazard ratio 0.63 (95% CI 0.51–0.78; P<0.0001) — a relative measure, with the absolute medians printed here. The most common grade 3–4 event on the combination was anaemia, in 185 of 398 patients (46%), which improved after dose reduction; only 33 (8%) discontinued talazoparib because of anaemia. No treatment-related deaths occurred on the combination versus two (<1%) on placebo + enzalutamide. Overall survival was immature at this report (see the final overall-survival cards below).
cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence: every card on this shelf is a report of the one TALAPRO-2 trial, not independent trials. This all-comer cohort mixes HRR-deficient and HRR-non-deficient disease — keep its claim separate from the HRR-deficient cohort card below.
cards.source: Agarwal N et al. Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in men with first-line metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet (London, England). 2023. PMID: 37285865. Registry ID: NCT03395197. cards.headline: TALAPRO-2 HRR-deficient cohort primary report (Fizazi 2024): radiographic PFS median not reached vs 13.8 months, hazard ratio 0.45 (relative); overall survival immature, hazard ratio 0.69
cards.summary: TALAPRO-2 HRR-deficient cohort primary report (Fizazi 2024): radiographic PFS median not reached vs 13.8 months, hazard ratio 0.45 (relative); overall survival immature, hazard ratio 0.69
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial report (TALAPRO-2 combined HRR-deficient population, cohorts 1 + 2), talazoparib + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide
cards.people: 399 men with HRR-deficient metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer — 169 from the all-comer cohort plus 230 enrolled into a subsequent HRR-deficient-only cohort — randomised 1:1 to talazoparib + enzalutamide or placebo + enzalutamide, all prospectively assessed for tumour HRR gene alterations.
cards.result: Median radiographic progression-free survival was not reached with talazoparib + enzalutamide versus 13.8 months with enzalutamide alone; hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.33–0.61; P<0.0001) — a relative measure. Overall survival was immature but favoured the combination (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.46–1.03; P=0.07); the final overall-survival analysis is carded separately below. Common adverse events on the combination were anaemia, fatigue and neutropenia.
cards.watchOut: The HRR-deficient population overlaps the all-comer cohort above (169 of its patients are counted in both) — the two cards are two populations of one trial, not two trials.

cards.headline: TALAPRO-2 final overall survival, all-comer cohort (Agarwal 2025): median overall survival 45.8 vs 37.0 months, hazard ratio 0.80 (relative) — benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient disease
cards.summary: TALAPRO-2 final overall survival, all-comer cohort (Agarwal 2025): median overall survival 45.8 vs 37.0 months, hazard ratio 0.80 (relative) — benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient disease
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial final overall-survival report (TALAPRO-2 cohort 1, all comers) — same trial as the primary-report card above, not a separate trial
cards.people: The same 805 randomised men of the all-comer cohort (402 combination, 403 control), followed for overall survival to a median of 52.5 months.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly improved with talazoparib + enzalutamide: hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.96; P=0.016) — a relative measure — with median overall survival 45.8 months (39.4–50.8) versus 37.0 months (34.1–40.4), an absolute median gain of 8.8 months. By HRR status the relative effect was larger in HRR-deficient patients (n=169; hazard ratio 0.55, 0.36–0.83) and smaller and non-significant in HRR-non-deficient or unknown patients (n=636; hazard ratio 0.88, 0.71–1.08; P=0.22). Updated radiographic PFS: median 33.1 vs 19.5 months (hazard ratio 0.67). Grade 3-or-higher anaemia occurred in 195 patients (49%) on the combination versus 18 (4%) on control; neutropenia in 77 (19%) versus 6 (1%).
cards.watchOut: The all-comer survival claim rests substantially on the HRR-deficient minority (169 of 805); in the HRR-non-deficient/unknown majority the survival hazard ratio was 0.88 and not significant — do not read the all-comer result as proof of benefit in HRR-non-deficient disease.

cards.headline: TALAPRO-2 final overall survival, HRR-deficient cohort (Fizazi 2025): median overall survival 45.1 vs 31.1 months, hazard ratio 0.62 (relative); BRCA1/2 subgroup 4-year survival 53% vs 23%
cards.summary: TALAPRO-2 final overall survival, HRR-deficient cohort (Fizazi 2025): median overall survival 45.1 vs 31.1 months, hazard ratio 0.62 (relative); BRCA1/2 subgroup 4-year survival 53% vs 23%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial final overall-survival report (TALAPRO-2 combined HRR-deficient population) — same trial as the cards above, not a separate trial
cards.people: The same 399 randomised men with HRR-deficient disease (200 combination, 199 control), followed to a median of 44.2 months; 155 (39%) had BRCA1/2 alterations and 244 (61%) did not.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly improved: hazard ratio 0.62 (95% CI 0.48–0.81; P=0.0005) — a relative measure — with median overall survival 45.1 months versus 31.1 months, an absolute median gain of 14.0 months. In the BRCA1/2 subgroup, median overall survival was not reached on the combination versus 28.5 months on control (hazard ratio 0.50, 0.32–0.78), and 4-year overall survival rates were 53% versus 23% — an absolute difference of 30 percentage points. In patients without BRCA1/2 alterations, median overall survival was 42.4 versus 32.6 months (hazard ratio 0.73, 0.52–1.02; P=0.066, not significant). Updated radiographic PFS: median 30.7 vs 12.3 months (hazard ratio 0.47). Commonest grade 3-or-higher events on the combination were anaemia (86 patients, 43%) and neutropenia (39, 20%).
cards.watchOut: The BRCA1/2 and non-BRCA splits are subgroups of one cohort: the survival benefit is clearest with BRCA1/2 alteration, and the non-BRCA HRR subgroup's hazard ratio (0.73) did not reach significance on its own.

cards.headline: FDA approval summary (Heiss 2024): the US approval is LIMITED to HRR gene-mutated disease — the all-comer radiographic-PFS gain was not judged clinically meaningful enough for a broad indication (a regulatory report OF TALAPRO-2, not a separate trial)

cards.type: Regulatory approval summary (FDA) of the TALAPRO-2 programme — companion card, not independent comparative evidence
cards.people: The TALAPRO-2 programme as assessed by the US Food and Drug Administration: 1,035 patients randomised across the all-comer cohort and the HRR-mutated-only cohort.
cards.result: The FDA approved talazoparib with enzalutamide for first-line treatment of HRR gene-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer only. Radiographic PFS hazard ratios (relative measures) were 0.63 in all comers and 0.45 in the combined HRR-mutated population; in an exploratory analysis of 155 patients with BRCA-mutated disease the radiographic-PFS hazard ratio was 0.20, and in the non-HRR-mutated/unknown stratum (n=636) it was 0.70. The FDA stated that despite the statistically significant all-comer result it did not consider the magnitude of benefit clinically meaningful for a broad indication given the combination treatment and its safety profile, and limited approval to HRR-mutated disease, where the benefit was larger and overall-survival results were favourable. Regulatory slices differ by jurisdiction; this card states the US position as verified at build.
cards.watchOut: A regulatory summary of the same single trial: it adds the licensing position, not new efficacy data. Other jurisdictions' labels may differ and are not stated here.

cards.headline: Patient-reported outcomes in HRR-deficient disease (Fay 2025): time to definitive deterioration of global health status/quality of life was longer on the combination — 27.1 vs 19.3 months (a report OF TALAPRO-2, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: Patient-reported outcomes in HRR-deficient disease (Fay 2025): time to definitive deterioration of global health status/quality of life was longer on the combination — 27.1 vs 19.3 months (a report OF TALAPRO-2, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcomes report of the TALAPRO-2 HRR-deficient population — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: 394 of the 399 HRR-deficient randomised patients (197 per arm) with a baseline and at least one post-baseline patient-reported outcome assessment; median follow-up 22.2 months (combination) and 20.2 months (control).
cards.result: Median time to definitive deterioration in global health status/quality of life was 27.1 months on talazoparib + enzalutamide versus 19.3 months on placebo + enzalutamide (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.49–0.97; P=0.032 — a relative measure). Time to definitive deterioration in urinary symptoms was also longer (hazard ratio 0.56, 0.34–0.93); time to deterioration in pain symptoms did not differ significantly (hazard ratio 0.58, 0.33–1.01; P=0.051). Between-group differences in mean change scores did not reach the 10-point clinically meaningful threshold, although they favoured the combination.
cards.watchOut: PROs cover only the HRR-deficient population and only the deterioration-time endpoints favoured the combination significantly; mean score differences were below the clinically meaningful threshold.

cards.headline: Safety analysis (Azad 2024): grade 3/4 anaemia in about 47% of all-comer and 41% of HRR-deficient patients on the combination; packed red-cell transfusion in 39% and 36% (a report OF TALAPRO-2, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: Safety analysis (Azad 2024): grade 3/4 anaemia in about 47% of all-comer and 41% of HRR-deficient patients on the combination; packed red-cell transfusion in 39% and 36% (a report OF TALAPRO-2, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Safety-analysis report of TALAPRO-2 — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: Safety populations on talazoparib + enzalutamide: 398 patients from the all-comer cohort and 198 from the combined HRR-deficient population, all receiving talazoparib 0.5 mg (0.35 mg with moderate renal impairment) plus enzalutamide 160 mg daily.
cards.result: All-cause grade 3/4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 71.9% (all comers) and 66.2% (HRR-deficient). The commonest grade 3/4 haematological events were anaemia (46.7% and 40.9%), neutropenia (18.3% and 18.7%) and thrombocytopenia (7.3% and 7.1%); median time to grade 3/4 anaemia was 3.3 months in both populations. Management burden was substantial: dose interruption in 62.1% and 57.6%, dose reduction in 52.8% and 52.0%, packed red-blood-cell transfusion in 39.2% and 35.9%, and discontinuation of talazoparib in 18.8% and 10.1%. Anaemia is the combination's defining added harm.
cards.watchOut: Safety percentages are for the combination arm only, pooled across two overlapping populations of one trial; they describe management burden, not a randomised harm comparison.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (TALAPRO-2) — talazoparib + enzalutamide prolongs radiographic PFS and, at final analysis, overall survival versus enzalutamide alone, with the survival benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient (above all BRCA1/2) disease and priced in anaemia
cards.summary: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (TALAPRO-2) — talazoparib + enzalutamide prolongs radiographic PFS and, at final analysis, overall survival versus enzalutamide alone, with the survival benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient (above all BRCA1/2) disease and priced in anaemia
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single TALAPRO-2 trial (805 all-comer and 399 combined HRR-deficient randomised patients, overlapping populations).
cards.result: Final overall survival: median 45.8 vs 37.0 months in all comers (hazard ratio 0.80, relative) and 45.1 vs 31.1 months in HRR-deficient disease (hazard ratio 0.62, relative); in BRCA1/2-altered disease 4-year survival was 53% vs 23%. In HRR-non-deficient/unknown disease the survival hazard ratio was 0.88 and not significant, and the US FDA limited its approval to HRR gene-mutated disease. The defining added harm is anaemia: grade 3–4 in roughly 41–49% on the combination across reports, with packed red-cell transfusion in about 36–39% and dose reduction in about half. Patient-reported deterioration was delayed in HRR-deficient disease. The parallel PARP question with a different biomarker structure — niraparib + abiraterone in HRR-altered disease (MAGNITUDE) — is a separate shelf; cross-point only, not merged here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. All hazard ratios are relative measures and are printed with their absolute medians or rates on the cards above.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: CROWN: first-line lorlatinib vs crizotinib — median PFS still not reached at 7 years (5-year PFS 60% vs 8%) with near-complete intracranial protection
shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, does lorlatinib, versus crizotinib, prolong progression-free survival and prevent intracranial progression, and at what cost in chronic toxicity?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aminopyridines · Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Crizotinib · Female · Humans · Hyperlipidemias · Intention to Treat Analysis · Lactams · Lactams, Macrocyclic · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Mutation · Pyrazoles · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, CROWN (296 randomised). Lorlatinib versus crizotinib gave 12-month progression-free survival of 78% vs 39%, and the advantage proved exceptionally durable: median PFS was still not reached at 7 years versus 9.1 months on crizotinib (hazard ratio 0.19, a relative measure), with 5-year PFS 60% vs 8% and 7-year PFS 55% vs 3%. Intracranial progression was nearly abolished (time-to-intracranial-progression hazard ratio 0.06, relative; 12-month CNS progression 7% vs 72% in patients with baseline brain metastases). No completed overall-survival comparison exists in the fetched records. Two caveats price the claim: the comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation agent no longer the benchmark where alectinib or brigatinib are available (no head-to-head trial among later-generation agents exists), and lorlatinib's harms are chronic — hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain, peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects (mood/cognition/speech), with grade 3–4 events in about three quarters of patients over 5 years but permanent discontinuation in only 11%. Cross-point: alectinib first-line is live #1833; brigatinib first-line is the ALTA-1L shelf.

cards.headline: CROWN primary report (Shaw 2020): lorlatinib versus crizotinib — 12-month progression-free survival 78% vs 39%, hazard ratio 0.28 (relative); intracranial response 82% vs 23% in measurable brain metastases
cards.summary: CROWN primary report (Shaw 2020): lorlatinib versus crizotinib — 12-month progression-free survival 78% vs 39%, hazard ratio 0.28 (relative); intracranial response 82% vs 23% in measurable brain metastases
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (CROWN) primary interim report, lorlatinib vs crizotinib
cards.people: 296 patients with advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer and no previous systemic treatment for metastatic disease, randomised to lorlatinib 100 mg daily (n=149) or crizotinib 250 mg twice daily (n=147) in a global phase 3 trial.
cards.result: At the planned interim analysis, the proportion alive without progression at 12 months was 78% (95% CI 70–84) on lorlatinib versus 39% (30–48) on crizotinib — an absolute difference of 39 percentage points — with hazard ratio 0.28 (0.19–0.41; P<0.001), a relative measure. Objective response: 76% versus 58%. Among patients with measurable brain metastases, intracranial response was 82% versus 23%, and 71% of lorlatinib patients with brain metastases had an intracranial complete response. The commonest lorlatinib adverse events were hyperlipidaemia, oedema, increased weight, peripheral neuropathy and cognitive effects; grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 72% versus 56% (mainly altered lipid levels), and discontinuation for adverse events in 7% versus 9%.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation ALK inhibitor that is no longer the relevant benchmark where alectinib or brigatinib are available — this shelf answers 'lorlatinib vs crizotinib', not 'lorlatinib vs best alternative'. Single-programme evidence: all cards are reports of the one CROWN trial.
cards.source: Shaw AT et al. First-Line Lorlatinib or Crizotinib in Advanced ALK-Positive Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2020. PMID: 33207094. Registry ID: NCT03052608. cards.headline: CROWN 3-year updated analysis (Solomon 2023): median PFS not reached vs 9.3 months; 3-year PFS 64% vs 19%; intracranial progression in patients without baseline brain metastases 1% vs 23% (a report OF CROWN, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: CROWN 3-year updated analysis (Solomon 2023): median PFS not reached vs 9.3 months; 3-year PFS 64% vs 19%; intracranial progression in patients without baseline brain metastases 1% vs 23% (a report OF CROWN, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Phase 3 trial updated analysis (CROWN, 3-year, unplanned/descriptive) — same trial as the primary-report card above
cards.people: The same 296 randomised patients (149 lorlatinib, 147 crizotinib), in an unplanned descriptive analysis after 3 years (median PFS follow-up 36.7 months lorlatinib, 29.3 months crizotinib).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review was not reached on lorlatinib versus 9.3 months on crizotinib (hazard ratio 0.27, 95% CI 0.18–0.39 — relative); 3-year progression-free survival was 64% versus 19%, an absolute difference of 45 percentage points. For time to intracranial progression, the hazard ratio was 0.10 (0.04–0.27) in patients with baseline brain metastases (37 lorlatinib, 39 crizotinib) and 0.02 (0.002–0.14) in those without; among patients without baseline brain metastases, intracranial progression occurred in 1 of 112 (1%) on lorlatinib versus 25 of 108 (23%) on crizotinib. Grade 3–4 adverse events: 113 of 149 (76%) versus 81 of 142 (57%), mostly altered lipids; discontinuation for adverse events 7% versus 10%. No new safety signals.
cards.watchOut: An unplanned, descriptive update — no further formal PFS testing was planned after the primary endpoint was met, so these figures characterise durability rather than add a second confirmatory test.

cards.summary: CROWN intracranial post hoc analysis (Solomon 2022): 12-month cumulative CNS progression 7% vs 72% with baseline brain metastases and 1% vs 18% without; CNS adverse events in 35% on lorlatinib, mostly grade 1 (a report OF CROWN, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Post hoc intracranial efficacy and CNS-safety analysis of CROWN — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: Patients randomised in CROWN, analysed post hoc by presence or absence of brain metastases at baseline, with CNS imaging at screening and every 8 weeks; CNS adverse events were assessed in the lorlatinib group.
cards.result: Progression-free survival by blinded review favoured lorlatinib in both strata (12-month PFS 78% vs 22% with baseline brain metastases; 78% vs 45% without). The 12-month cumulative incidence of CNS progression was 7% versus 72% in patients with baseline brain metastases and 1% versus 18% in those without — absolute differences of 65 and 17 percentage points. CNS adverse events occurred in 35% of lorlatinib patients, most of grade 1 severity; their occurrence did not produce a clinically meaningful difference in patient-reported quality of life, 56% had resolved at analysis (33% without intervention, 17% with dose modification), and dose modification did not notably influence PFS.
cards.watchOut: Post hoc subgroup analysis of one trial; the CNS adverse-event figures are lorlatinib-arm descriptions without a randomised comparator for those specific events.

cards.headline: CROWN 5-year adverse-event kinetics (Liu 2025): hyperlipidaemia onset at a median 0.5 months, 71% of events managed with lipid-lowering agents; dose interruption 62%, reduction 23%, permanent discontinuation 11% (a report OF CROWN, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: CROWN 5-year adverse-event kinetics (Liu 2025): hyperlipidaemia onset at a median 0.5 months, 71% of events managed with lipid-lowering agents; dose interruption 62%, reduction 23%, permanent discontinuation 11% (a report OF CROWN, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Post hoc adverse-event kinetics/management analysis of CROWN (lorlatinib arm) — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: The 149 patients assigned to lorlatinib in CROWN, in a post hoc safety analysis after 5 years of follow-up, covering hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain, CNS adverse events and peripheral neuropathy.
cards.result: All-cause adverse events of any grade occurred in 100% and grade 3/4 events in 77% of lorlatinib patients; adverse events led to dose reduction in 23%, dose interruption in 62% and permanent discontinuation in 11%. Median time to onset of hyperlipidaemia was 0.5 months, and 71% of hyperlipidaemia events were managed with lipid-lowering agents; median onset of oedema, weight gain, CNS events and peripheral neuropathy was 2–4 months. Most weight-gain events (95%) were mitigated with lifestyle modifications, the incidence and prevalence of CNS adverse events did not increase over time, and 58% of CNS events required no medical intervention. No new safety signals emerged over 5 years. Hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain and CNS effects (mood, cognition, speech) are lorlatinib's defining harms.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm safety description of the lorlatinib group only; management success rates are observational within that arm.
cards.source: Liu G et al. Kinetics and management of adverse events associated with lorlatinib after 5 years of follow-up in the CROWN study. The oncologist. 2025. PMID: 41124598. cards.headline: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (CROWN) — lorlatinib produces exceptionally durable progression-free and intracranial control versus crizotinib (5-year PFS 60% vs 8%), with hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain and CNS effects as the standing price, and no completed overall-survival comparison yet
cards.summary: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (CROWN) — lorlatinib produces exceptionally durable progression-free and intracranial control versus crizotinib (5-year PFS 60% vs 8%), with hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain and CNS effects as the standing price, and no completed overall-survival comparison yet
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single CROWN trial (296 randomised patients).
cards.result: CROWN's primary, 3-year, 5-year and 7-year reports agree: median PFS on lorlatinib was still not reached at 7 years versus 9.1 months on crizotinib, with absolute progression-free survival differences of about 52 percentage points at both 5 years (60% vs 8%) and 7 years (55% vs 3%), and near-complete prevention of intracranial progression (hazard ratio 0.06, relative, for time to intracranial progression). Overall survival has not been reported as a completed analysis in any fetched record — at 7 years its protocol-specified event count had not been met. The comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation agent no longer the relevant benchmark where alectinib (live shelf #1833) or brigatinib (the ALTA-1L shelf) are available, and there is no head-to-head trial among the later-generation agents. Harms are chronic and manageable rather than usually treatment-ending: hyperlipidaemia (early onset, usually treated with lipid-lowering agents), oedema, weight gain, peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects, with permanent discontinuation for adverse events in 11% at 5 years.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. All hazard ratios are relative measures and are printed with absolute rates on the cards above.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: ALTA-1L: first-line brigatinib vs crizotinib — PFS 24.0 vs 11.1 months and delayed quality-of-life worsening; no overall-survival advantage shown
shelves.question: In patients with advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer who have not received an ALK inhibitor, does brigatinib, versus crizotinib, prolong progression-free survival and improve intracranial response, and at what harm?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase · Antineoplastic Agents · Brain Neoplasms · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Crizotinib · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Organophosphorus Compounds · Progression-Free Survival · Pyrimidines
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, ALTA-1L (275 randomised). Brigatinib 180 mg daily (after a 7-day 90 mg lead-in) versus crizotinib roughly doubled progression-free survival: final median 24.0 vs 11.1 months (hazard ratio 0.48, a relative measure), 3-year PFS 43% vs 19%, with higher intracranial response (78% vs 29% in measurable lesions) and delayed worsening of global quality of life (median 26.7 vs 8.3 months to worsening). Overall survival was not significantly different (hazard ratio 0.81; medians not reached). The defining harm is early-onset pulmonary events — the dose lead-in exists because of them and is part of the tested intervention; the fetched abstract records do not quantify those events, so no rate is printed. Same caveat as CROWN: the comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation agent no longer the benchmark where alectinib or lorlatinib are available, and there is no head-to-head trial among the later-generation agents. Cross-points: lorlatinib first-line is the CROWN shelf; alectinib first-line is live #1833.

cards.headline: ALTA-1L primary report (Camidge 2018): brigatinib (90 mg 7-day lead-in, then 180 mg) versus crizotinib — 12-month PFS 67% vs 43%, hazard ratio 0.49 (relative); intracranial response 78% vs 29% in measurable lesions
cards.summary: ALTA-1L primary report (Camidge 2018): brigatinib (90 mg 7-day lead-in, then 180 mg) versus crizotinib — 12-month PFS 67% vs 43%, hazard ratio 0.49 (relative); intracranial response 78% vs 29% in measurable lesions
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (ALTA-1L) first interim report, brigatinib vs crizotinib
cards.people: 275 patients with advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer who had not previously received an ALK inhibitor, randomised 1:1 to brigatinib 180 mg once daily with a 7-day lead-in at 90 mg (n=137) or crizotinib 250 mg twice daily (n=138), in an open-label phase 3 trial.
cards.result: At the first interim analysis (99 events; median follow-up 11.0 months brigatinib, 9.3 months crizotinib), estimated 12-month progression-free survival was 67% (95% CI 56–75) with brigatinib versus 43% (32–53) with crizotinib — an absolute difference of 24 percentage points — with hazard ratio 0.49 (0.33–0.74; P<0.001), a relative measure. Confirmed objective response: 71% versus 60%. Confirmed intracranial response among patients with measurable lesions: 78% versus 29%. No new safety concerns were noted in this report; the 90 mg lead-in week is part of the tested intervention (see the watch-out).
cards.watchOut: Early-onset pulmonary events are brigatinib's defining harm and are the reason the tested regimen begins with a 7-day 90 mg lead-in before 180 mg; the fetched abstract records do not quantify those events, so no rate is printed here — the lead-in itself is part of the intervention being evaluated, not an optional extra. The comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation agent (see the synthesis).

cards.headline: ALTA-1L second interim analysis (Camidge 2020): median PFS 24.0 vs 11.0 months by blinded review, hazard ratio 0.49 (relative); time to worsening of global health status/quality of life delayed (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: ALTA-1L second interim analysis (Camidge 2020): median PFS 24.0 vs 11.0 months by blinded review, hazard ratio 0.49 (relative); time to worsening of global health status/quality of life delayed (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Phase 3 trial second prespecified interim analysis (ALTA-1L) — same trial as the primary-report card above
cards.people: The same 275 randomised patients (137 brigatinib, 138 crizotinib), at the second prespecified interim analysis (150 progression events; median brigatinib follow-up 24.9 months).
cards.result: Blinded-review progression-free survival again favoured brigatinib: hazard ratio 0.49 (95% CI 0.35–0.68; P<0.0001 — relative), median 24.0 versus 11.0 months, an absolute median difference of 13.0 months. Investigator-assessed PFS hazard ratio was 0.43 (median 29.4 vs 9.2 months). Brigatinib delayed median time to worsening of global health status/quality-of-life scores versus crizotinib (hazard ratio 0.70, 0.49–1.00; P=0.049). No new safety concerns emerged.
cards.watchOut: A second interim look at the same trial and the same primary endpoint — confirmatory of durability, not independent evidence.

cards.headline: ALTA-1L final results (Camidge 2021): 3-year PFS 43% vs 19% (median 24.0 vs 11.1 months); overall survival not significantly different (hazard ratio 0.81, relative), medians not reached in either group (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: ALTA-1L final results (Camidge 2021): 3-year PFS 43% vs 19% (median 24.0 vs 11.1 months); overall survival not significantly different (hazard ratio 0.81, relative), medians not reached in either group (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Phase 3 trial final results report (ALTA-1L) — same trial as the cards above
cards.people: The same 275 randomised patients, at study end (median brigatinib follow-up 40.4 months).
cards.result: Three-year progression-free survival by blinded review was 43% on brigatinib versus 19% on crizotinib — an absolute difference of 24 percentage points — with median PFS 24.0 versus 11.1 months (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.35–0.66, relative). Median overall survival was not reached in either group and the overall-survival hazard ratio was 0.81 (0.53–1.22), not significant; a post hoc analysis suggested a survival benefit in patients with baseline brain metastases (hazard ratio 0.43, 0.21–0.89), which the authors state warrants future study. Detectable baseline EML4-ALK variant 3 and TP53 mutation in plasma were associated with poorer PFS, but brigatinib's superiority held regardless of variant and TP53 status. No new safety signals were observed.
cards.watchOut: The brain-metastases survival signal is post hoc and hypothesis-generating; the trial's overall-survival comparison overall was not significant, in a trial where post-progression treatment can dilute survival differences.
cards.source: Camidge DR et al. Brigatinib Versus Crizotinib in ALK Inhibitor-Naive Advanced ALK-Positive NSCLC: Final Results of Phase 3 ALTA-1L Trial. cards.headline: ALTA-1L health-related quality of life (Garcia Campelo 2021): time to worsening of global health status delayed — median 26.7 vs 8.3 months; longer duration of improvement on brigatinib (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: ALTA-1L health-related quality of life (Garcia Campelo 2021): time to worsening of global health status delayed — median 26.7 vs 8.3 months; longer duration of improvement on brigatinib (a report OF ALTA-1L, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Health-related quality-of-life report of ALTA-1L — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: 262 patients (131 per arm) with quality-of-life assessments in ALTA-1L (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13; compliance above 90% in both groups).
cards.result: Brigatinib significantly delayed time to worsening in global health status/quality of life versus crizotinib (median 26.74 vs 8.31 months; hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.49–1.00; P=0.0485 — relative), and likewise in emotional and social functioning, fatigue, nausea and vomiting, appetite loss and constipation (each P<0.05); delays for physical, role and cognitive functioning were not significant. Among patients whose global health status improved, duration of improvement was longer on brigatinib (median not reached vs 11.99 months). Median time to worsening of dyspnoea (QLQ-LC13) was 23.98 versus 8.25 months (hazard ratio 0.64, 0.39–1.05, not significant).
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial: patients knew which drug they were taking, which can influence self-reported quality of life; several functioning scales did not reach significance.
cards.source: Garcia Campelo MR et al. Health-related quality of life in the randomized phase III trial of brigatinib vs crizotinib in advanced ALK inhibitor-naive ALK + non-small cell lung cancer (ALTA-1L). cards.headline: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (ALTA-1L) — brigatinib (with its 90 mg lead-in week) roughly doubles progression-free survival versus crizotinib and delays quality-of-life worsening, without a demonstrated overall-survival advantage
cards.summary: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (ALTA-1L) — brigatinib (with its 90 mg lead-in week) roughly doubles progression-free survival versus crizotinib and delays quality-of-life worsening, without a demonstrated overall-survival advantage
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single ALTA-1L trial (275 randomised patients).
cards.result: Across the primary, second-interim and final reports, brigatinib's progression-free-survival advantage over crizotinib was consistent (hazard ratios 0.48–0.49, relative; final median 24.0 vs 11.1 months; 3-year PFS 43% vs 19%), intracranial response in measurable lesions was higher (78% vs 29% at the primary report), and quality-of-life worsening was delayed. Overall survival was not significantly different (hazard ratio 0.81; medians not reached). The defining harm is early-onset pulmonary events, managed in the trial design by the 7-day 90 mg lead-in before the 180 mg dose — the fetched abstract records do not quantify those events, so this shelf prints no rate for them. The comparator is crizotinib, a first-generation agent no longer the relevant benchmark where alectinib (live #1833) or lorlatinib (the CROWN shelf) are available; there is no head-to-head trial among the second/third-generation agents and none should be implied.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. All hazard ratios are relative measures and are printed with absolute medians or rates on the cards above.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: MET exon 14 NSCLC: capmatinib and tepotinib each respond in roughly half of patients — two single-arm programmes, no randomised evidence
shelves.question: In patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, do the selective MET inhibitors capmatinib or tepotinib, versus no concurrent control, produce objective responses, in treatment-naïve and previously treated disease?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents · Benzamides · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Edema · Exons · Female · Gene Dosage · Humans · Imidazoles · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Mutation · Nausea · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Proto-Oncogene Proteins c-met · Triazines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on an entirely uncontrolled base, stated plainly: this shelf rests on two single-arm phase 2 programmes with no concurrent comparator for either drug. Capmatinib (GEOMETRY mono-1) produced responses in 68% of treatment-naïve and 41–44% of previously treated patients with MET exon 14-skipping NSCLC (160 such patients at final analysis). Tepotinib (VISION) produced responses in 46% at its primary report and 51.4% overall at long-term follow-up in 313 patients (57.3% treatment-naïve, 45.0% previously treated), with median response durations up to 18.0 months. Response in a biomarker-selected, uncontrolled population supports possible benefit but cannot establish a survival effect or rank the two drugs against each other. Peripheral oedema is the class-defining harm (47–67% across the programmes; grade 3-or-worse in 11.2% on tepotinib at long-term follow-up). The MET-amplified cohorts of GEOMETRY mono-1 are a different biomarker question — cross-point only, not carded here.

cards.headline: GEOMETRY mono-1 primary report (Wolf 2020) — CAPMATINIB, single-arm: response in 68% of 28 treatment-naïve and 41% of 69 previously treated patients with MET exon 14-skipping NSCLC (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: GEOMETRY mono-1 primary report (Wolf 2020) — CAPMATINIB, single-arm: response in 68% of 28 treatment-naïve and 41% of 69 previously treated patients with MET exon 14-skipping NSCLC (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Single-arm multiple-cohort phase 2 trial (GEOMETRY mono-1), capmatinib — MET exon 14 cohorts only; NO concurrent control
cards.people: Patients with MET-dysregulated advanced NSCLC assigned to cohorts by prior therapy and MET status in a multiple-cohort phase 2 study; this card covers only the MET exon 14-skipping cohorts — 69 patients who had received one or two prior lines and 28 treatment-naïve patients. (The same study's MET-amplified cohorts ask a different biomarker question and are NOT carded on this shelf — cross-point only.) All received capmatinib 400 mg twice daily.
cards.result: Overall response (independent review) was 68% (95% CI 48–84) in treatment-naïve patients, with median duration of response 12.6 months, and 41% (29–53) in previously treated patients, with median duration of response 9.7 months. These are single-arm response rates with no concurrent control — they cannot be read as a comparison against any alternative treatment. The most frequently reported adverse events across the study were peripheral oedema (51%) and nausea (45%), mostly grade 1 or 2 — peripheral oedema is the class-defining harm of MET inhibition.
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled, single-arm evidence: response rates in a biomarker-selected population cannot separate drug effect from patient selection, and there is no randomised survival comparison for capmatinib in this disease.
cards.source: Wolf J et al. Capmatinib in MET Exon 14-Mutated or MET-Amplified Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2020. PMID: 32877583. Registry ID: NCT02414139. cards.headline: GEOMETRY mono-1 final results (Wolf 2024) — CAPMATINIB, single-arm: response in 68% of 60 treatment-naïve and 44% of 100 previously treated MET exon 14 patients at long follow-up (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: GEOMETRY mono-1 final results (Wolf 2024) — CAPMATINIB, single-arm: response in 68% of 60 treatment-naïve and 44% of 100 previously treated MET exon 14 patients at long follow-up (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 trial final results (GEOMETRY mono-1), capmatinib — MET exon 14 cohorts; NO concurrent control. Same programme as the primary-report card above, not a second trial
cards.people: 160 patients with MET exon 14-skipping NSCLC in four cohorts (60 treatment-naïve, 100 previously treated), within 373 treated patients across all GEOMETRY mono-1 cohorts; median follow-up 46.4 months (treatment-naïve) and 66.9 months (previously treated). Capmatinib 400 mg twice daily.
cards.result: Overall responses were recorded in 41 of 60 treatment-naïve patients (68%; 95% CI 55.0–79.7) and 44 of 100 previously treated patients (44%; 34.1–54.3). Across all 373 treated patients, the commonest treatment-related adverse events were peripheral oedema (174 patients, 47%), nausea (130, 35%), increased blood creatinine (78, 21%) and vomiting (74, 20%); grade 3–4 serious adverse events occurred in 164 (44%), dyspnoea being the commonest (18, 5%), and treatment-related deaths occurred in 4 patients (1%) — one each of cardiac arrest, hepatitis, organising pneumonia and pneumonitis. No new safety signals.
cards.watchOut: The expanded treatment-naïve denominator (60, including later cohorts) supersedes the primary report's 28 for that subgroup; still single-arm — durability of response, not comparative benefit, is what long follow-up adds.
cards.source: Wolf J et al. Capmatinib in MET exon 14-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer: final results from the open-label, phase 2 GEOMETRY mono-1 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2024. PMID: 39362249. cards.headline: VISION primary report (Paik 2020) — TEPOTINIB, single-arm: response rate 46% by independent review, median duration of response 11.1 months (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: VISION primary report (Paik 2020) — TEPOTINIB, single-arm: response rate 46% by independent review, median duration of response 11.1 months (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Single-arm open-label phase 2 trial (VISION), tepotinib; NO concurrent control
cards.people: 152 patients with advanced or metastatic NSCLC with a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation received tepotinib 500 mg once daily in an open-label phase 2 study; the primary analysis covered 99 patients followed for at least 9 months, with mutation detected by liquid biopsy, tissue biopsy, or both.
cards.result: The response rate by independent review was 46% (95% CI 36–57), with median duration of response 11.1 months (7.2–not estimable); response rates were 48% in the liquid-biopsy group (66 patients) and 50% in the tissue-biopsy group (60 patients), and the investigator-assessed rate was 56%, similar regardless of previous therapy. Grade 3-or-higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 28% of patients, including peripheral oedema in 7%; adverse events led to permanent discontinuation in 11%. A molecular response in circulating free DNA was seen in 67% of patients with matched samples. Single-arm rates: no concurrent control.

cards.watchOut: Still single-arm: the very long median duration of response in treatment-naïve patients (46.4 months, CI 13.8–not estimable) is imprecise, and cross-programme comparison with capmatinib's rates is not a randomised comparison.

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — two single-arm programmes: GEOMETRY mono-1 (capmatinib; 160 MET exon 14 patients at final analysis) and VISION (tepotinib; 313 patients at long-term follow-up), plus the FDA's joint approval summary.
cards.result: Capmatinib: response 68% in treatment-naïve and 41–44% in previously treated disease, median response duration 12.6 and 9.7 months at the primary report. Tepotinib: response 46% at the primary report and 51.4% overall at long-term follow-up (57.3% treatment-naïve, 45.0% previously treated), median response duration up to 18.0 months overall. Neither programme has a concurrent control, so no relative benefit, survival effect or between-drug comparison can be claimed — the two drugs' rates come from separate uncontrolled trials and must not be ranked against each other. Peripheral oedema is the shared class harm (47–51% with capmatinib across reports; 67.1% with tepotinib at long-term follow-up, grade 3-or-worse in 11.2%). The MET-amplified cohorts of GEOMETRY mono-1 are a different biomarker question and are not carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each programme's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. Every efficacy figure on this shelf is a single-arm response rate — there are no relative (comparative) measures to report.
