shelves.title: TRIDENT-1: repotrectinib responds in 79% of TKI-naïve and 38% of previously treated ROS1-positive NSCLC — single-arm evidence, dizziness the defining harm
shelves.question: In patients with advanced ROS1 fusion-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, TKI-naïve or previously treated (including with the ROS1 G2032R resistance mutation), does repotrectinib, versus no concurrent control, produce objective and intracranial responses?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Lung Neoplasms · Protein-Tyrosine Kinases · Proto-Oncogene Proteins · Antineoplastic Agents · Treatment Outcome · Pyrazoles · Macrocyclic Compounds
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on a single-arm, single-programme base, stated plainly: TRIDENT-1 has no concurrent control. Repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb) produced responses in 56 of 71 TKI-naïve patients (79%; median duration of response 34.1 months) and 21 of 56 patients after one prior ROS1 TKI (38%; median duration 14.8 months) with ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, including 10 of 17 patients with the G2032R resistance mutation and responses in CNS metastases — enough for traditional FDA approval in November 2023, but uncontrolled response data cannot establish a survival effect or superiority over any other ROS1 inhibitor. The defining harms are neurological: dizziness (58%), dysgeusia (50%), paraesthesia, ataxia and cognitive effects, with dose interruption in 39% and reduction in 38% but discontinuation in only about 3%. Taletrectinib (separate shelf) asks the same question of a different agent with no head-to-head trial. TRIDENT-1's NTRK cohort is homed by cross-reference to the TRK question — not carded here.

cards.headline: TRIDENT-1 registrational report (Drilon 2024) — single-arm: response in 79% of 71 TKI-naïve and 38% of 56 previously treated ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC patients; 59% in the G2032R resistance subgroup (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: TRIDENT-1 registrational report (Drilon 2024) — single-arm: response in 79% of 71 TKI-naïve and 38% of 56 previously treated ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC patients; 59% in the G2032R resistance subgroup (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Registrational single-arm phase 1–2 trial (TRIDENT-1), repotrectinib in ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC; NO concurrent control
cards.people: Patients with ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC in a registrational phase 1–2 trial (efficacy analyses pooled phase 1 and phase 2): 71 who had not previously received a ROS1 TKI, 56 who had received one prior ROS1 TKI and no chemotherapy, and 17 with the ROS1 G2032R resistance mutation. The phase 2 dose was repotrectinib 160 mg daily for 14 days, then 160 mg twice daily. Product naming (clarification): repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb).
cards.result: Response occurred in 56 of 71 TKI-naïve patients (79%; 95% CI 68–88), with median duration of response 34.1 months and median progression-free survival 35.7 months; in 21 of 56 previously treated patients (38%; 25–52), with median duration of response 14.8 months and median progression-free survival 9.0 months; and in 10 of 17 patients (59%; 33–82) with the G2032R mutation. Among 426 patients who received the phase 2 dose, the commonest treatment-related adverse events were dizziness (58%), dysgeusia (50%) and paraesthesia (30%) — the CNS-penetrant profile (dizziness/ataxia) is the defining harm — and 3% discontinued repotrectinib for treatment-related adverse events. All efficacy figures are single-arm: no concurrent control.
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled, single-arm evidence in a biomarker-selected population: response rates cannot be compared with crizotinib, entrectinib or taletrectinib rates from other single-arm programmes, and there is no randomised survival evidence. The G2032R subgroup is small (17 patients).
cards.source: Drilon A et al. Repotrectinib in ROS1 Fusion-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 38197815. Registry ID: NCT03093116. cards.result: The FDA granted traditional approval to repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb Corporation) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC. Objective response by blinded independent central review was 79% (95% CI 68–88) in TKI-naïve patients, median duration of response 34.1 months, and 38% (25–52) after a prior ROS1 TKI, median duration 14.8 months; responses were also observed in CNS metastases and in patients with resistance mutations after prior TKI therapy — which the FDA noted as a distinctive feature of this approval. The commonest adverse reactions (over 20%) were dizziness, dysgeusia, peripheral neuropathy, constipation, dyspnoea, ataxia, fatigue, cognitive disorders and muscular weakness.
cards.watchOut: A regulatory restatement of the same single-arm trial; 'traditional approval' here describes the regulatory pathway, not the presence of a randomised comparator — there is none.

cards.headline: TRIDENT-1 adverse-event characterisation (Drilon 2026): dizziness in 58% and dysgeusia in 50% across 472 patients at the recommended dose; dose modification downgraded or resolved dizziness in 78% (a report OF TRIDENT-1, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: TRIDENT-1 adverse-event characterisation (Drilon 2026): dizziness in 58% and dysgeusia in 50% across 472 patients at the recommended dose; dose modification downgraded or resolved dizziness in 78% (a report OF TRIDENT-1, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Adverse-event characterisation/management analysis of TRIDENT-1 (all cohorts) — same programme as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: 472 patients across all TRIDENT-1 cohorts who started repotrectinib at the recommended dose (160 mg daily for 14 days, then 160 mg twice daily) — a safety population spanning the trial's cohorts, wider than the ROS1 NSCLC efficacy cohorts above.
cards.result: The commonest treatment-related adverse events were dizziness (58%) and dysgeusia (50%), which the authors attribute largely to TRK inhibition; median relative dose intensity was 90%, and 14% (66 of 472) never escalated from the initial daily dose to twice daily, mostly because of CNS adverse events. Dizziness (median onset 7 days) occurred at similar rates with and without baseline brain metastases; dose modifications downgraded its severity or resolved it in 78% of patients, and it downgraded or resolved in 62% (120 of 195) of patients who had neither dose modification nor pharmacological intervention. Treatment-related cognitive impairment occurred in 19% and weight gain in 12%; treatment-emergent withdrawal pain in 14% (median resolution 2.1 weeks). Dose interruption and reduction for treatment-related events occurred in 39% and 38%.
cards.watchOut: The safety population (472) pools all TRIDENT-1 cohorts, not only ROS1 NSCLC; management-outcome percentages are observational within a single arm.
cards.source: Drilon A et al. Characterization and clinical management of adverse events following treatment with repotrectinib: a TRIDENT-1 analysis. The oncologist. 2026. PMID: 41992489. cards.headline: Synthesis: one single-arm programme (TRIDENT-1) — repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb) responds in 79% of TKI-naïve and 38% of previously treated ROS1-positive NSCLC, including G2032R disease, with dizziness/ataxia as the defining harm; the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.summary: Synthesis: one single-arm programme (TRIDENT-1) — repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb) responds in 79% of TKI-naïve and 38% of previously treated ROS1-positive NSCLC, including G2032R disease, with dizziness/ataxia as the defining harm; the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single TRIDENT-1 programme (ROS1 NSCLC efficacy cohorts of 71 TKI-naïve and 56 previously treated patients; safety population 472 across cohorts).
cards.result: Repotrectinib produced durable responses without any concurrent control: 79% in TKI-naïve disease (median duration 34.1 months) and 38% after one prior ROS1 TKI (median duration 14.8 months), with responses in 10 of 17 patients carrying the G2032R resistance mutation and in CNS metastases — the basis of its traditional FDA approval in November 2023. The defining harms are neurological, reflecting CNS penetration and TRK inhibition: dizziness 58%, dysgeusia 50%, paraesthesia/peripheral neuropathy, ataxia and cognitive disorders, usually manageable with dose modification (interruption 39%, reduction 38%) and discontinuation in only about 3% in the registrational report. Taletrectinib asks the same clinical question of a different agent in its own single-arm programme (separate shelf) — there is no head-to-head trial, and response rates across the two programmes are not evidence of superiority for either. TRIDENT-1's NTRK cohort belongs to the TRK-inhibitor question and is a cross-point only here — it is not carded on this shelf.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. Every efficacy figure on this shelf is a single-arm response rate — there are no relative (comparative) measures to report.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.question: In patients with advanced ROS1-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, TKI-naïve or previously treated, does taletrectinib, versus no concurrent control, produce objective and intracranial responses?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on a single-arm base throughout, stated plainly: TRUST-I and TRUST-II are both uncontrolled phase 2 trials of one programme. Taletrectinib (Ibtrozi, Nuvation Bio) produced confirmed responses in 88.8% of 160 TKI-naïve and 55.8% of 113 TKI-pretreated patients in the pooled analysis (intracranial responses 76.5% and 65.6%; G2032R responses in 8 of 13), with median response durations of 44.2 and 16.6 months, sustained at TRUST-I long-term follow-up. Harms are mainly gastrointestinal events and transaminase rises, with unusually infrequent neurological events for this class (dizziness 21–23%, mostly grade 1) and discontinuation in 5–6.5%. Uncontrolled response data cannot establish a survival effect. This shelf and the repotrectinib shelf ask the same clinical question of two different agents with NO head-to-head trial — cross-programme response-rate comparisons are not evidence of superiority for either drug.

cards.headline: TRUST-I (Li 2024) — single-arm, China: confirmed response 91% in TKI-naïve and 52% in crizotinib-pretreated ROS1-positive NSCLC; intracranial response 88% in TKI-naïve patients (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: TRUST-I (Li 2024) — single-arm, China: confirmed response 91% in TKI-naïve and 52% in crizotinib-pretreated ROS1-positive NSCLC; intracranial response 88% in TKI-naïve patients (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 trial (TRUST-I, China), taletrectinib; NO concurrent control
cards.people: 173 patients with ROS1-positive NSCLC enrolled in China (median age 55 years; 58% female; 73% never smoked): 106 TKI-naïve and 67 crizotinib-pretreated, treated with taletrectinib. Product naming (clarification): taletrectinib (Ibtrozi, Nuvation Bio).
cards.result: Confirmed objective response by independent review was 91% in TKI-naïve patients, with intracranial confirmed response 88%, and 52% and 73% respectively in crizotinib-pretreated patients. In TKI-naïve patients, median duration of response and median PFS were not reached (follow-up 22.1 and 23.5 months); in crizotinib-pretreated patients, median duration of response was 10.6 months and median PFS 7.6 months. Eight of 12 patients (67%) with G2032R mutations responded. The commonest treatment-emergent adverse events were increased AST (76%), diarrhoea (70%) and increased ALT (68%), mostly grade 1–2; neurological events were uncommon (dizziness 23%, dysgeusia 10%, mostly grade 1). Discontinuation for adverse events was 5% and dose reduction 19%. Single-arm rates: no concurrent control.
cards.watchOut: A single-country (China), single-arm cohort: the 91% TKI-naïve response rate is not comparable with rates from other agents' single-arm programmes in different populations, and there is no randomised evidence.
cards.source: Li W et al. Efficacy and Safety of Taletrectinib in Chinese Patients With ROS1+ Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The Phase II TRUST-I Study. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2024. PMID: 38822758. Registry ID: NCT04395677. cards.headline: Integrated TRUST-I + TRUST-II pooled analysis (Pérol 2025) — single-arm: confirmed response 88.8% in 160 TKI-naïve and 55.8% in 113 TKI-pretreated patients; intracranial response 76.5% and 65.6% (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Integrated TRUST-I + TRUST-II pooled analysis (Pérol 2025) — single-arm: confirmed response 88.8% in 160 TKI-naïve and 55.8% in 113 TKI-pretreated patients; intracranial response 76.5% and 65.6% (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Integrated pooled analysis of two single-arm phase 2 trials (TRUST-I + TRUST-II), taletrectinib; NO concurrent control. TRUST-I patients are counted in both this card and the TRUST-I card above — one programme, not two independent bases
cards.people: 273 efficacy-evaluable patients pooled from the pivotal cohorts of TRUST-I (China) and TRUST-II (global), all treated with taletrectinib 600 mg once daily; the safety population was 352 patients treated at that dose across the taletrectinib programme.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response was 88.8% in TKI-naïve patients (n=160), with intracranial confirmed response 76.5%, and 55.8% in TKI-pretreated patients (n=113), with intracranial response 65.6%. Median duration of response and median PFS were 44.2 and 45.6 months in TKI-naïve patients and 16.6 and 9.7 months in TKI-pretreated patients. Confirmed response in G2032R-mutated disease was 61.5% (8 of 13). Among 352 treated patients, the commonest treatment-emergent adverse events were gastrointestinal events (88%) and increased AST (72%) and ALT (68%), mostly grade 1; neurological events were infrequent (dizziness 21%, dysgeusia 15%, mostly grade 1) and discontinuation for adverse events was 6.5%.
cards.watchOut: A pooled analysis of two single-arm trials from one development programme: pooling enlarges the denominator but adds no comparator, and the long TKI-naïve median PFS (45.6 months) is a single-arm estimate subject to selection and follow-up maturity.

cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 long-term follow-up report (TRUST-I) — same programme as the cards above, not independent evidence

shelves.title: NTRK fusion tumours: larotrectinib and entrectinib respond across histologies — pooled 75–79% and 57–61%, but only 30% in primary CNS tumours; single-arm evidence
shelves.question: In adults and children with advanced solid tumours harbouring NTRK1/2/3 gene fusions, do the TRK inhibitors larotrectinib or entrectinib, versus no concurrent control, produce objective responses across tumour types, including primary CNS tumours?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Agents · Child · Child, Preschool · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Infant · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasms · Oncogene Proteins, Fusion · Protein Kinases · Pyrazoles · Pyrimidines · Receptor Protein-Tyrosine Kinases · Young Adult
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on single-arm, tumour-agnostic evidence throughout, with the histology spread printed rather than a single headline rate. Larotrectinib responded in 75% of 55 patients (17 tumour types, ages 4 months to 76 years) at its primary analysis and 79% of 153 evaluable patients in the pooled analysis — but in only 30% of 33 patients with primary CNS tumours (24-week disease control 73%). Entrectinib responded in 57% of 54 adults (10 tumour types, 19 histologies) and 61.2% of 121 adults in the updated analysis (14 types, at least 30 histologies; intracranial response 63.6% in 11 patients). Children are inside both programmes. Responses were often durable and toxicity mostly low-grade with no treatment-related deaths, but uncontrolled pooled response rates cannot establish a survival effect, cannot be promised to any individual histology, and cannot rank the two drugs. Repotrectinib's NTRK cohort is a cross-point only — not re-carded here.

cards.headline: Larotrectinib combined phase 1/2 analysis (Drilon 2018) — single-arm, tumour-agnostic: overall response 75% by independent review across 55 patients aged 4 months to 76 years with 17 tumour types (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: Larotrectinib combined phase 1/2 analysis (Drilon 2018) — single-arm, tumour-agnostic: overall response 75% by independent review across 55 patients aged 4 months to 76 years with 17 tumour types (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Combined single-arm phase 1/2 analysis (three larotrectinib protocols), tumour-agnostic; NO concurrent control
cards.people: 55 adults and children (age range 4 months to 76 years) with prospectively identified TRK fusion-positive cancers of 17 unique tumour types, enrolled across three protocols (a phase 1 adult study, a phase 1–2 paediatric study and a phase 2 adolescent/adult study) and treated with larotrectinib.
cards.result: The overall response rate was 75% (95% CI 61–85) by independent review and 80% (67–90) by investigator assessment, pooled across all 17 tumour types — a pooled figure across histologies with very different natural histories, not a rate any single tumour type is shown to achieve. At 1 year, 71% of responses were ongoing and 55% of patients remained progression-free; median duration of response and median PFS had not been reached at median follow-up of 9.4 months, and 86% of responders (38 of 44) were continuing treatment or had undergone surgery intended to be curative. Adverse events were predominantly grade 1, no grade 3–4 event judged drug-related occurred in more than 5% of patients, and no patient discontinued for a drug-related adverse event.
cards.watchOut: The headline 75% pools 17 tumour types in 55 patients — about 3 patients per type on average — so it cannot support a response claim for any individual histology; per-histology rates are not given in the fetched record. Follow-up was short (median 9.4 months).

combined single-arm phase 1/2 analysis (three larotrectinib protocols), tumour-agnostic; no concurrent control 55 adults and children (age range 4 months to 76 years) with prospectively identified trk fusion-positive cancers of 17 unique tumour types, enrolled across three protocols (a phase 1 adult study, a phase 1–2 paediatric study and a phase 2 adolescent/adult study) and treated with larotrectinib. the overall response rate was 75% (95% ci 61–85) by independent review and 80% (67–90) by investigator assessment, pooled across all 17 tumour types — a pooled figure across histologies with very different natural histories, not a rate any single tumour type is shown to achieve. at 1 year, 71% of responses were ongoing and 55% of patients remained progression-free; median duration of response and median pfs had not been reached at median follow-up of 9.4 months, and 86% of responders (38 of 44) were continuing treatment or had undergone surgery intended to be curative. adverse events were predominantly grade 1, no grade 3–4 event judged drug-related occurred in more than 5% of patients, and no patient discontinued for a drug-related adverse event. the headline 75% pools 17 tumour types in 55 patients — about 3 patients per type on average — so it cannot support a response claim for any individual histology; per-histology rates are not given in the fetched record. follow-up was short (median 9.4 months). drilon a et al. efficacy of larotrectinib in trk fusion-positive cancers in adults and children. the new england journal of medicine. 2018. pmid: 29466156. registry id: nct02122913, nct02637687, nct02576431. mesh: adolescent · adult · aged · antineoplastic agents · child · child, preschool · disease-free survival · female · humans · infant · kaplan-meier estimate · male · middle aged · neoplasms · oncogene proteins, fusion · protein kinases · pyrazoles · pyrimidines · receptor protein-tyrosine kinases · young adult

cards.type: Pooled single-arm analysis of three phase 1/2 trials, larotrectinib; NO concurrent control. Overlaps the primary-report card above (the same 55 patients are inside both) — one programme, not two independent bases
cards.people: 159 patients with TRK fusion-positive cancer (ages from less than 1 month to 84 years) enrolled across the same three phase 1/2 trials, with locally advanced or metastatic non-CNS primary tumours who had received standard therapy previously where available; this analysis set includes the 55 patients of the primary report above. Safety was assessed in 260 patients treated regardless of TRK fusion status.
cards.result: Objective response by investigator assessment occurred in 121 of 153 evaluable patients (79%; 95% CI 72–85), with 24 complete responses (16%) — again a pooled, tumour-agnostic figure across many histologies. In the 260-patient safety population, the commonest grade 3–4 larotrectinib-related events were increased alanine aminotransferase (8 patients, 3%), anaemia (6, 2%) and decreased neutrophil count (5, 2%); the commonest related serious events were increased ALT, increased AST and nausea (2 patients each, under 1%), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Investigator-assessed (not independent-review) response in this larger pooled set, and primary CNS tumours were excluded from this analysis — the CNS question is covered by the separate card below, where the response rate was far lower.

cards.headline: Larotrectinib in TRK fusion-positive primary CNS tumours (Doz 2022) — single-arm: response only 30% in 33 patients, against a 73% 24-week disease control rate — the histology spread the pooled headline hides (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Larotrectinib in TRK fusion-positive primary CNS tumours (Doz 2022) — single-arm: response only 30% in 33 patients, against a 73% 24-week disease control rate — the histology spread the pooled headline hides (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Single-arm cohort analysis (primary CNS tumours within two larotrectinib trials); NO concurrent control
cards.people: 33 patients with TRK fusion-positive primary CNS tumours from two of the larotrectinib trials (median age 8.9 years, range 1.3–79.0); the commonest histologies were high-grade glioma (19 patients) and low-grade glioma (8 patients).
cards.result: The investigator-assessed objective response rate was 30% (95% CI 16–49) — far below the 75–79% pooled rates in non-CNS disease on the cards above — while the 24-week disease control rate was 73% (54–87) and 23 of 28 patients (82%) with measurable disease had some tumour shrinkage. Twelve-month rates were 75% for duration of response, 56% for progression-free survival and 85% for overall survival; median time to response was 1.9 months. Treatment-related adverse events were reported in 20 patients, grade 3–4 in 3, with no new safety signals.
cards.watchOut: A small (33-patient), mostly paediatric CNS cohort: its 30% response rate is the clearest demonstration on this shelf that the tumour-agnostic pooled rate does not transfer across histologies — disease control, not response, is the CNS story.
cards.source: Doz F et al. Efficacy and safety of larotrectinib in TRK fusion-positive primary central nervous system tumors. Neuro-oncology. 2022. PMID: 34850167. cards.headline: Entrectinib integrated analysis (Doebele 2020) — single-arm, tumour-agnostic: response in 31 of 54 adults (57%) across 10 tumour types and 19 histologies; median duration of response 10 months (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Entrectinib integrated analysis (Doebele 2020) — single-arm, tumour-agnostic: response in 31 of 54 adults (57%) across 10 tumour types and 19 histologies; median duration of response 10 months (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Integrated single-arm analysis of three phase 1–2 trials, entrectinib (adults); NO concurrent control
cards.people: 54 efficacy-evaluable adults with advanced or metastatic NTRK fusion-positive solid tumours (10 tumour types, 19 histologies), TRK inhibitor-naïve, treated with entrectinib at least 600 mg once daily across three phase 1–2 trials (ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, STARTRK-2); safety was assessed in 68 NTRK fusion-positive patients and 355 patients overall.
cards.result: Objective response by blinded independent central review occurred in 31 of 54 patients (57%; 95% CI 43.2–70.8) — 4 complete (7%) and 27 partial (50%) — pooled across the 10 tumour types, with median duration of response 10 months (7.1–not estimable) at median follow-up of 12.9 months. The commonest grade 3–4 treatment-related events in the NTRK fusion-positive safety population were increased weight (7 of 68, 10%) and anaemia (8 of 68, 12%); the commonest serious treatment-related events were nervous system disorders (3 of 68, 4%); there were no treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Only 54 efficacy-evaluable patients spread over 19 histologies — the pooled 57% cannot support a per-histology claim, and this adult analysis should not be compared head-to-head with larotrectinib's adult-and-paediatric pooled rates.

cards.headline: Entrectinib updated integrated analysis (Demetri 2022) — single-arm: response in 61.2% of 121 adults across 14 tumour types and at least 30 histologies; intracranial response 63.6% in 11 patients with measurable CNS disease (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Entrectinib updated integrated analysis (Demetri 2022) — single-arm: response in 61.2% of 121 adults across 14 tumour types and at least 30 histologies; intracranial response 63.6% in 11 patients with measurable CNS disease (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Updated integrated single-arm analysis of the same three entrectinib trials — same programme as the card above, not a second trial; NO concurrent control
cards.people: 121 efficacy-evaluable adults with locally advanced or metastatic NTRK fusion-positive solid tumours (14 tumour types, at least 30 histologies) with at least 12 months of follow-up, from the same three phase 1/2 trials; median follow-up 25.8 months.
cards.result: Complete or partial response occurred in 61.2% of patients (19 complete, 55 partial), with median duration of response 20.0 months (95% CI 13.0–38.2) and median progression-free survival 13.8 months (10.1–19.9). In 11 patients with measurable CNS disease by blinded review, intracranial response was 63.6% (30.8–89.1) with median intracranial duration of response 22.1 months. Most treatment-related adverse events were grade 1/2 and manageable or reversible with dose modifications; discontinuation for treatment-related events occurred in 8.3% of patients.
cards.watchOut: The intracranial figure rests on 11 patients; and the update's higher response rate than the 2020 analysis reflects a larger, differently matured analysis set, not a treatment change.

cards.headline: Synthesis: two single-arm, tumour-agnostic programmes — TRK inhibition responds across histologies, but the pooled rates (larotrectinib 75–79%, entrectinib 57–61%) conceal a wide spread, from 30% in primary CNS tumours upward; the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.summary: Synthesis: two single-arm, tumour-agnostic programmes — TRK inhibition responds across histologies, but the pooled rates (larotrectinib 75–79%, entrectinib 57–61%) conceal a wide spread, from 30% in primary CNS tumours upward; the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — two programmes: larotrectinib (55 patients in the primary analysis, 159 in the pooled analysis, plus a 33-patient primary-CNS cohort; ages from under 1 month / 4 months to 84 years, children inside both the trials and the approvals) and entrectinib (54, then 121, efficacy-evaluable adults across 10–14 tumour types and 19 to at least 30 histologies).
cards.result: Printed as a spread, not a single headline: larotrectinib response was 75% by independent review in the 55-patient primary set and 79% by investigator assessment in the pooled set, but only 30% in TRK fusion-positive primary CNS tumours (24-week disease control 73%); entrectinib response was 57% in 54 adults and 61.2% in the updated 121-patient set, with intracranial response in 7 of 11 patients with measurable CNS disease. Responses were often durable (median durations 10–20 months for entrectinib; not reached for larotrectinib at the primary report) and both drugs were largely low-grade in toxicity, with no treatment-related deaths in either programme's reports. But every figure is a single-arm response rate pooled across histologies with very different natural histories: there is no randomised evidence, no survival comparison, and no basis for ranking larotrectinib against entrectinib or for promising any individual histology the pooled rate. Repotrectinib also has an NTRK cohort in TRIDENT-1 — a cross-point here only; its home by cross-reference is the ROS1 shelf's programme, and it is not re-carded on this shelf.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each programme's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. Every efficacy figure on this shelf is a single-arm response rate — there are no relative (comparative) measures to report.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Sunvozertinib in EGFR exon 20 NSCLC: first-line PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months vs chemotherapy in a randomised trial; pretreated evidence is single-arm only (response 46–61%)
shelves.question: In patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations — after platinum chemotherapy, and as first-line therapy — does sunvozertinib, versus no concurrent control (pretreated) or versus platinum chemotherapy (first-line), produce objective responses and prolong progression-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Humans · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Mutagenesis, Insertional · Lung Neoplasms · China · Anemia · ErbB Receptors · Exons
shelves.balance: SPLIT — the base is two different kinds of evidence for two different slices, and they must not be merged. Pretreated disease: single-arm only — confirmed response 61% in WU-KONG6 (97 evaluable; China-generated, stated plainly) and 45.9% at 200 mg / 47.2% at 300 mg in the dose-randomised WU-KONG1B, which randomised dose, not treatment; that slice supports POSSIBLE at best. First-line disease: one phase 3 randomised trial showed sunvozertinib beat carboplatin–pemetrexed on progression-free survival (median 10.3 vs 7.5 months; hazard ratio 0.65, a relative measure; response 58.9% vs 31.1%), with overall survival immature and more grade 3-or-higher toxicity (75.5% vs 56.7%) — that slice is LIKELY (benefit) against chemotherapy, not against amivantamab-based therapy (homed at pack #5184). Defining harms: diarrhoea and rash, creatine-kinase rises and interstitial lung disease (5% serious in WU-KONG6). Class context only: mobocertinib was withdrawn after a failed confirmatory trial — context for caution about the uncontrolled slice, not evidence about this drug.

cards.headline: Phase 1 programme report (Wang 2022): sunvozertinib was tolerated up to 400 mg once daily, with antitumour activity at doses of 100 mg and above in EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC — a discovery/early-clinical report, not an efficacy trial (no response rate or cohort N is given in the record)
cards.summary: Phase 1 programme report (Wang 2022): sunvozertinib was tolerated up to 400 mg once daily, with antitumour activity at doses of 100 mg and above in EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC — a discovery/early-clinical report, not an efficacy trial (no response rate or cohort N is given in the record)
cards.type: Programme report: discovery and phase 1 clinical development report (two phase 1 studies) — background for the WU-KONG programme, not pivotal efficacy evidence
cards.people: Patients with previously treated NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations in two ongoing phase 1 studies of sunvozertinib (DZD9008), an oral irreversible selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor; the fetched record does not state the number of efficacy-evaluable patients (N not documented in the record), so no figure from this report is load-bearing on this shelf.
cards.result: The most common drug-related adverse events were diarrhoea and skin rash. Antitumour efficacy was observed at doses of 100 mg and above across exon 20 insertion subtypes, in patients previously treated with amivantamab, and in patients with baseline brain metastases; the median duration of response had not been reached at the report. No response rate is printed because the record gives none.
cards.watchOut: Carded only to complete the programme record: it reports no denominator and no response rate, and must not be counted toward the efficacy base, which is WU-KONG6, WU-KONG1B and the first-line phase 3 trial below.

cards.headline: WU-KONG6 (Wang 2024) — single-arm, China only: confirmed response in 61% of 97 evaluable platinum-pretreated patients at 300 mg daily (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: WU-KONG6 (Wang 2024) — single-arm, China only: confirmed response in 61% of 97 evaluable platinum-pretreated patients at 300 mg daily (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Single-arm open-label multicentre phase 2 trial (WU-KONG6, China), sunvozertinib 300 mg in platinum-pretreated disease; NO concurrent control
cards.people: 104 patients enrolled across 37 centres in China with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC carrying an EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation, all previously treated with at least one platinum-containing line; 97 were evaluable for efficacy. All received sunvozertinib 300 mg once daily.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response by independent review was 61% (59 of 97; 95% CI 50–71), all partial responses, observed irrespective of age, sex, smoking history, insertion subtype, baseline brain metastasis, prior lines and prior onco-immunotherapy. Nineteen deaths had occurred at a median follow-up of 7.6 months. The commonest grade 3-or-worse treatment-related adverse events were increased blood creatine phosphokinase (18 of 104, 17%), diarrhoea (8, 8%) and anaemia (6, 6%); the commonest serious treatment-related event was interstitial lung disease (5 of 104, 5%). This base is single-arm and China-generated — both facts belong on the face of the claim.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm and single-country: a 61% response rate in a selected, China-only pretreated population cannot be generalised to other populations or compared with other exon 20 treatments, and follow-up was short (median 7.6 months).
cards.source: Wang M et al. Sunvozertinib for patients in China with platinum-pretreated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer and EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation (WU-KONG6): single-arm, open-label, multicentre, phase 2 trial. The Lancet. Respiratory medicine. 2024. PMID: 38101437. Registry ID: NCT05712902, NCT05668988. cards.headline: WU-KONG1B (Yang 2025) — dose-randomised, multinational: confirmed response 45.9% at 200 mg and 47.2% at 300 mg in platinum-pretreated disease, with grade 3-or-worse diarrhoea in 2.2% vs 18% — the 200 mg dose looked as active and better tolerated
cards.summary: WU-KONG1B (Yang 2025) — dose-randomised, multinational: confirmed response 45.9% at 200 mg and 47.2% at 300 mg in platinum-pretreated disease, with grade 3-or-worse diarrhoea in 2.2% vs 18% — the 200 mg dose looked as active and better tolerated
cards.type: Phase 2 dose-randomised study (WU-KONG1B) — randomised between two sunvozertinib doses only; NO control-treatment arm
cards.people: Patients with advanced EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC after platinum chemotherapy, randomly assigned 1:1 to sunvozertinib 200 mg (85 efficacy-evaluable) or 300 mg (89 efficacy-evaluable) once daily, with further non-randomised patients added at 300 mg after a predefined interim analysis (107 in the 300 mg-all cohort) — a multinational phase 2 study. The randomisation is between doses of the same drug, not against a control treatment.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response by blinded independent review was 45.9% (200 mg-randomised), 47.2% (300 mg-randomised) and 45.8% (300 mg-all); the predefined null hypothesis was rejected (P<0.0001) against a historical benchmark. Duration of response was longer at 300 mg (13.8 vs 11.1 months), and responses in patients with baseline brain metastases (52.4% vs 28.6%) and prior amivantamab (41.7% vs 25%) were higher at 300 mg in subgroup comparisons. Grade 3-or-worse treatment-related events differed by dose: diarrhoea 2.2% at 200 mg versus 18% at 300 mg, increased blood creatine phosphokinase 6.6% versus 12.6%, anaemia 4.4% versus 6.3% — a more favourable safety profile at 200 mg, per the authors.
cards.watchOut: Dose randomisation answers 'which dose', not 'does it beat anything': efficacy is still judged against a historical null, and the brain-metastasis and prior-amivantamab dose differences are subgroup comparisons within small cohorts.
cards.source: Yang JC et al. cards.headline: First-line phase 3 randomised trial (Zhou 2026): sunvozertinib versus carboplatin–pemetrexed — median PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months, hazard ratio 0.65 (relative); response 58.9% vs 31.1%; overall survival immature
cards.summary: First-line phase 3 randomised trial (Zhou 2026): sunvozertinib versus carboplatin–pemetrexed — median PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months, hazard ratio 0.65 (relative); response 58.9% vs 31.1%; overall survival immature
cards.type: Phase 3 international randomised trial (WU-KONG28), sunvozertinib vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy, first-line
cards.people: 324 patients with advanced nonsquamous NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertions and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease, randomised 1:1 to sunvozertinib (n=163) or carboplatin–pemetrexed chemotherapy (n=161), internationally; crossover to sunvozertinib was allowed after confirmed progression on chemotherapy.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review was 10.3 months on sunvozertinib versus 7.5 months on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.50–0.85; P<0.001 — a relative measure), with 12-month PFS of 46.1% versus 26.7%, an absolute difference of 19.4 percentage points. Objective response was 58.9% versus 31.1%, median best tumour shrinkage −42.1% versus −24.7%, and median duration of response 11.2 versus 7.1 months. Overall survival data were immature (38.9% maturity). Grade 3-or-higher adverse events were more frequent on sunvozertinib (75.5% vs 56.7%), the commonest being increased serum creatine kinase, diarrhoea and anaemia; no deaths were attributed to sunvozertinib-related adverse events.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is chemotherapy alone — not amivantamab-based therapy, the other modern first-line exon 20 option (homed at pack #5184 for amivantamab + chemotherapy) — so this trial does not rank sunvozertinib against that regimen; crossover after progression will also dilute any later overall-survival difference, and survival was immature at the report.
cards.source: Zhou C et al. First-Line Sunvozertinib in NSCLC with EGFR Exon 20 Insertion Mutations. The New England journal of medicine. 2026. PMID: 42212913. Registry ID: NCT05668988. cards.headline: Synthesis: a split base — single-arm pretreated evidence (61% in China-only WU-KONG6; about 46–47% at either dose in multinational WU-KONG1B) plus one positive first-line randomised trial against chemotherapy (PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months); diarrhoea, rash, creatine-kinase rises and interstitial lung disease are the harms to price
cards.summary: Synthesis: a split base — single-arm pretreated evidence (61% in China-only WU-KONG6; about 46–47% at either dose in multinational WU-KONG1B) plus one positive first-line randomised trial against chemotherapy (PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months); diarrhoea, rash, creatine-kinase rises and interstitial lung disease are the harms to price
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — the WU-KONG programme: a phase 1 programme report (no efficacy denominator), WU-KONG6 (104 enrolled, China, pretreated), WU-KONG1B (dose-randomised, pretreated) and the first-line phase 3 trial (324 randomised).
cards.result: In pretreated EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC, sunvozertinib's evidence is uncontrolled: confirmed response 61% in the China-only WU-KONG6 at 300 mg and 45.9–47.2% in multinational WU-KONG1B, where 200 mg matched 300 mg on response with far less grade 3-or-worse diarrhoea (2.2% vs 18%). First-line, the phase 3 trial gives the shelf its one comparative result: median PFS 10.3 vs 7.5 months against carboplatin–pemetrexed (hazard ratio 0.65, relative; response 58.9% vs 31.1%), with overall survival immature and grade 3-or-higher events in 75.5% vs 56.7%. Harms are EGFR-class and drug-specific — diarrhoea and rash, increased creatine phosphokinase (grade 3-or-worse in 17% in WU-KONG6), anaemia, and interstitial lung disease as the commonest serious event in WU-KONG6 (5%) — not amivantamab's infusion/venous-thromboembolism profile, which belongs to a different drug and is not imported here. Class context, stated as context and not as evidence about sunvozertinib: mobocertinib, the earlier oral exon 20 TKI, was withdrawn after its confirmatory trial failed, which is why this shelf separates its uncontrolled pretreated slice from its randomised first-line slice. Amivantamab + chemotherapy in exon 20 disease is homed at pack #5184 — a different intervention, cross-point only.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. The pretreated figures are single-arm response rates; the only relative (comparative) measure on this shelf is the first-line trial's PFS hazard ratio, printed with its absolute medians.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Beamion LUNG-1: zongertinib responds in 71% of pretreated and 76% of first-line HER2-mutant NSCLC — single-arm evidence; EGFR-type harms frequent but rarely severe
shelves.question: In patients with advanced HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer — previously treated, including after HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugates, and as first-line therapy — does the HER2-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor zongertinib, versus no concurrent control, produce objective responses?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Lung Neoplasms · Mutation · Progression-Free Survival · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors · Trastuzumab · Immunoconjugates · Treatment Outcome · Camptothecin
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on a single-arm, single-programme base, stated plainly: Beamion LUNG-1 has no concurrent control at any line. Zongertinib (Hernexeos, Boehringer Ingelheim) produced confirmed responses in 71% of 75 previously treated patients with tyrosine-kinase-domain HER2 mutations at 120 mg (median duration 14.1 months), 48% of 31 patients after a HER2 antibody–drug conjugate, 30% of 20 with non-TKD mutations, and 76% of 74 first-line patients (median duration 15.2 months), with intracranial responses in 47% of 30 patients with active brain metastases. The HER2-selectivity claim is printed and tested, not just asserted: in phase Ia, diarrhoea occurred in 50% and rash in 16% — EGFR-type effects are present — but grade 3-or-worse rates were only 1% and 2%, and no drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in the pretreated cohorts. Uncontrolled response data cannot establish a survival effect or rank this drug against HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugates (homed elsewhere — cross-point only).

cards.headline: Beamion LUNG-1 phase Ia dose escalation (Heymach 2025) — single-arm: diarrhoea in 50% (grade 3-or-worse in 1%) and rash in 16% (2%) across 105 patients with HER2-altered solid tumours — the EGFR-sparing test, printed not assumed (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Beamion LUNG-1 phase Ia dose escalation (Heymach 2025) — single-arm: diarrhoea in 50% (grade 3-or-worse in 1%) and rash in 16% (2%) across 105 patients with HER2-altered solid tumours — the EGFR-sparing test, printed not assumed (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Single-arm phase Ia dose-escalation study (Beamion LUNG-1, HER2-altered solid tumours); NO concurrent control
cards.people: 105 pretreated patients with various HER2-altered solid tumours (including 54 with NSCLC), treated with zongertinib twice daily (15–150 mg) or once daily (60–360 mg) in the phase Ia part of Beamion LUNG-1; maximum tolerated dose was not reached, and the recommended expansion doses were 120 mg and 240 mg once daily.
cards.result: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 82% of patients, grade 3-or-worse in 10%. The rates that test the drug's HER2-selectivity rationale (sparing wild-type EGFR) were: diarrhoea 50% any grade but only 1% grade 3-or-worse, and rash 16% any grade and 2% grade 3-or-worse — frequent low-grade EGFR-type events, but rarely severe; other common events were anaemia (10%, 0% grade 3-or-worse), decreased appetite (10%, 1%) and increased alanine aminotransferase (10%, 4%). Two dose-limiting toxicities occurred. The confirmed investigator-assessed response rate across all doses and tumours was 30% (95% CI 23–40), median duration 12.7 months; in the 54 NSCLC patients it was 35%, and median PFS in once-daily NSCLC patients was 17.2 months.
cards.watchOut: A mixed-tumour, mixed-dose escalation population: its response figures are dose-finding background, not the NSCLC efficacy claim — but its diarrhoea/rash rates are the shelf's cleanest printed test of the EGFR-sparing rationale, and they show low-grade events remain common even when severe events are rare.

cards.headline: Beamion LUNG-1 previously treated NSCLC cohorts (Heymach 2025) — single-arm: confirmed response 71% in the tyrosine-kinase-domain cohort at 120 mg, 48% after a HER2 antibody–drug conjugate, and 30% in non-TKD mutations (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.summary: Beamion LUNG-1 previously treated NSCLC cohorts (Heymach 2025) — single-arm: confirmed response 71% in the tyrosine-kinase-domain cohort at 120 mg, 48% after a HER2 antibody–drug conjugate, and 30% in non-TKD mutations (uncontrolled base — no concurrent comparator)
cards.type: Single-arm multicohort phase 1a–1b trial report (Beamion LUNG-1, previously treated HER2-mutant NSCLC); NO concurrent control (cohort 1 contained an internal dose randomisation only)
cards.people: Previously treated patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant NSCLC in three cohorts: cohort 1, tyrosine-kinase-domain (TKD) mutations, initially dose-randomised between 120 mg and 240 mg once daily (75 patients received 120 mg; after an interim analysis all cohorts moved to 120 mg); cohort 5, TKD mutations previously treated with a HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugate (31 patients); cohort 3, non-TKD mutations (20 patients). Product naming (clarification): zongertinib (Hernexeos, Boehringer Ingelheim).
cards.result: In cohort 1 at 120 mg, 71% of patients (95% CI 60–80) had a confirmed objective response (P<0.001 against a 30% benchmark), with median duration of response 14.1 months and median progression-free survival 12.4 months; grade 3-or-higher drug-related adverse events occurred in 13 patients (17%). In cohort 5 (post-ADC), the confirmed response rate was 48% (32–65), with grade 3-or-higher drug-related events in 1 patient (3%). In cohort 3 (non-TKD), the response rate was 30% (15–52), with grade 3-or-higher drug-related events in 5 patients (25%). No cases of drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in any cohort. All figures are single-arm, judged against a benchmark, not a control arm.
cards.watchOut: Cohorts 5 and 3 are small (31 and 20 patients) and cohort 3's 30% response rate sits exactly at the benchmark the TKD cohort was tested against — mutation location matters, and the 71% headline belongs to TKD-mutated, 120 mg disease only.
cards.source: Heymach JV et al. Zongertinib in Previously Treated HER2-Mutant Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2025. PMID: 40293180. Registry ID: NCT04886804. cards.headline: Beamion LUNG-1 first-line cohort (Heymach 2026) — single-arm: confirmed response 76% in 74 previously untreated patients; intracranial response 47% in a separate 30-patient active-brain-metastases cohort (uncontrolled base)
cards.summary: Beamion LUNG-1 first-line cohort (Heymach 2026) — single-arm: confirmed response 76% in 74 previously untreated patients; intracranial response 47% in a separate 30-patient active-brain-metastases cohort (uncontrolled base)
cards.type: Single-arm phase 1a–1b multicohort report (Beamion LUNG-1 cohort 2 first-line, and exploratory cohort 4 active brain metastases); NO concurrent control
cards.people: 74 previously untreated patients with advanced or metastatic nonsquamous HER2-mutant NSCLC (cohort 2), treated with zongertinib 120 mg once daily; and, in an exploratory cohort (cohort 4), 30 patients with active brain metastases treated at the same dose.
cards.result: In cohort 2, the confirmed objective response rate was 76% (95% CI 65–84), median duration of response 15.2 months and median progression-free survival 14.4 months. Adverse events of any grade occurred in 73 of 74 patients (99%), grade 3-or-higher in 33 (45%); treatment-related events occurred in 67 (91%), grade 3-or-higher in 14 (19%). In cohort 4, 47% (30–64) had a confirmed intracranial objective response, and grade 3-or-higher treatment-related events occurred in 5 patients (17%). Treatment-related events were predominantly low-grade, consistent with the EGFR-sparing design — but this report's fetched record does not itemise diarrhoea and rash rates for these cohorts, so none are printed for them here (see the phase Ia card for the printed rates).
cards.watchOut: First-line use rests on 74 uncontrolled patients: a 76% response rate in untreated disease cannot be compared with the pretreated cohorts' rates or with any other first-line regimen, and there is no randomised or survival evidence for zongertinib at any line.
cards.source: Heymach JV et al. First-Line Zongertinib in Advanced HER2-Mutant Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2026. PMID: 41985129. Registry ID: NCT04886804. cards.headline: Synthesis: one single-arm programme (Beamion LUNG-1) — zongertinib (Hernexeos, Boehringer Ingelheim) responds in 71% of pretreated TKD-mutant and 76% of first-line HER2-mutant NSCLC, with the EGFR-sparing claim partly borne out in print (diarrhoea 50% but grade 3-or-worse in only 1%; rash 16%/2% in phase Ia); the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.summary: Synthesis: one single-arm programme (Beamion LUNG-1) — zongertinib (Hernexeos, Boehringer Ingelheim) responds in 71% of pretreated TKD-mutant and 76% of first-line HER2-mutant NSCLC, with the EGFR-sparing claim partly borne out in print (diarrhoea 50% but grade 3-or-worse in only 1%; rash 16%/2% in phase Ia); the uncontrolled base caps this shelf at POSSIBLE
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single Beamion LUNG-1 programme (105 phase Ia patients with HER2-altered tumours; NSCLC cohorts of 75 + 31 + 20 previously treated and 74 first-line patients, plus 30 with active brain metastases).
cards.result: Zongertinib produced high response rates without any concurrent control: 71% in previously treated tyrosine-kinase-domain-mutant NSCLC at the selected 120 mg dose (median duration 14.1 months, median PFS 12.4 months), 48% after a HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugate, 30% in non-TKD mutations, and 76% first-line (median duration 15.2 months), with intracranial responses in 47% of a small active-brain-metastases cohort and no drug-related interstitial lung disease in the pretreated cohorts. The HER2-selectivity rationale — sparing wild-type EGFR — is tested by the printed harm rates, not merely asserted: in phase Ia, diarrhoea occurred in 50% and rash in 16% of patients, so EGFR-type effects are not absent, but they were rarely severe (grade 3-or-worse: diarrhoea 1%, rash 2%), and grade 3-or-higher drug-related events were 17–19% in the main NSCLC cohorts. Single-arm response data cannot establish a survival benefit or rank zongertinib against HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugates or chemotherapy. Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-mutant lung disease is homed in the breast/gastric families — cross-point only, not carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. Every efficacy figure on this shelf is a single-arm response rate — there are no relative (comparative) measures to report.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: MARIPOSA: amivantamab + lazertinib beats osimertinib first-line — PFS 23.7 vs 16.6 months and 3-year survival 60% vs 51%, with grade 3+ toxicity in 80% vs 52%
shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) advanced NSCLC, does amivantamab plus lazertinib, versus osimertinib, prolong progression-free and overall survival, and at what added toxicity?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Acrylamides · Aniline Compounds · Antibodies, Bispecific · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · ErbB Receptors · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lung Neoplasms · Morpholines · Mutation · Progression-Free Survival · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Quinolines · Pyrimidines · Pyrazoles · Treatment Outcome · Indoles
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, MARIPOSA (1,074 randomised 2:2:1), for the first-line exon 19 deletion / L858R question only (PARTIAL scope: EGFR exon 20 insertion disease is homed at pack #5184 and is not asked here). Amivantamab + lazertinib beat osimertinib on progression-free survival (median 23.7 vs 16.6 months; hazard ratio 0.70, a relative measure) and, at the protocol-specified final analysis, on overall survival (hazard ratio 0.75, relative; 3-year survival 60% vs 51% — the final report, fetched at build, supersedes the interim and Asian-subgroup survival reads). The lazertinib-alone arm showed lazertinib performs like osimertinib alone (hazard ratio 0.98), so the gain belongs to the combination. The price: grade 3-or-higher adverse events in 80% vs 52% — particularly skin-related events, venous thromboembolism (with its prophylactic-anticoagulation burden) and infusion-related events — and discontinuation of all agents for toxicity in 10% vs 3%. FLAURA2 (osimertinib + chemotherapy, pack #5183) is the competing intensification question — cross-point only; there is no head-to-head trial between the two intensifications.

cards.headline: MARIPOSA primary report (Cho 2024): amivantamab + lazertinib versus osimertinib — median PFS 23.7 vs 16.6 months, hazard ratio 0.70 (relative); response duration 25.8 vs 16.8 months; discontinuation of all agents for treatment-related events 10% vs 3%
cards.summary: MARIPOSA primary report (Cho 2024): amivantamab + lazertinib versus osimertinib — median PFS 23.7 vs 16.6 months, hazard ratio 0.70 (relative); response duration 25.8 vs 16.8 months; discontinuation of all agents for treatment-related events 10% vs 3%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (MARIPOSA) primary report, amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib (with a lazertinib-alone component arm)
cards.people: 1,074 patients with previously untreated EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, randomised 2:2:1 to amivantamab + lazertinib (n=429, open-label), osimertinib (n=429, blinded) or lazertinib alone (n=216, blinded — included to assess the contribution of the components) in a phase 3 international trial. This shelf covers only this first-line common-mutation question; amivantamab in EGFR exon 20 insertion disease is a different population and regimen, homed at pack #5184.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review was 23.7 months on amivantamab + lazertinib versus 16.6 months on osimertinib (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.58–0.85; P<0.001 — a relative measure; absolute median gain 7.1 months). Objective response was almost identical (86% vs 85%), but among confirmed responders the median response duration was 25.8 versus 16.8 months. At a planned interim overall-survival analysis the hazard ratio for death was 0.80 (0.61–1.05) — not yet significant (the final analysis is carded below). Predominant adverse events were EGFR-related toxic effects, and discontinuation of all agents because of treatment-related adverse events occurred in 10% on the combination versus 3% on osimertinib.
cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence: all cards are reports of the one MARIPOSA trial. The combination arm was open-label while the monotherapy arms were blinded, and the PFS gain came with roughly triple the rate of discontinuation of all treatment for toxicity (10% vs 3%) even at this early report.
cards.source: Cho BC et al. Amivantamab plus Lazertinib in Previously Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced NSCLC. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 38924756. Registry ID: NCT04487080. cards.headline: MARIPOSA final overall survival (Yang 2025): amivantamab + lazertinib significantly prolonged survival versus osimertinib — hazard ratio 0.75 (relative); 3-year survival 60% vs 51%; grade 3-or-higher adverse events 80% vs 52% (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: MARIPOSA final overall survival (Yang 2025): amivantamab + lazertinib significantly prolonged survival versus osimertinib — hazard ratio 0.75 (relative); 3-year survival 60% vs 51%; grade 3-or-higher adverse events 80% vs 52% (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Phase 3 trial protocol-specified final overall-survival report (MARIPOSA) — same trial as the primary-report card above
cards.people: The same randomised population, analysed for the protocol-specified final overall-survival comparison between the amivantamab + lazertinib arm (n=429) and the osimertinib arm (n=429), at median follow-up of 37.8 months. This final report supersedes both the primary report's interim survival analysis and the Asian-subgroup survival analysis carded below.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer on amivantamab + lazertinib: hazard ratio for death 0.75 (95% CI 0.61–0.92; P=0.005) — a relative measure — with 3-year overall survival of 60% versus 51%, an absolute difference of 9 percentage points; median overall survival values are not stated in the fetched record. At the cutoff, 38% of the combination group and 28% of the osimertinib group were still receiving their assigned treatment. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were substantially more common on the combination (80% vs 52%), particularly skin-related events, venous thromboembolism and infusion-related events; no new safety signals emerged with longer follow-up. Venous thromboembolism — with its prophylactic-anticoagulation burden — infusion reactions and rash/paronychia-type EGFR toxicity are the added harms that price the survival gain; the fetched records name these event classes without printing their individual rates, so no rates are printed here.
cards.watchOut: This is the shelf's definitive survival read and it replaces the interim and subgroup survival figures; the trade is explicit — a 9-percentage-point absolute gain in 3-year survival against grade 3-or-higher toxicity in 80% versus 52% of patients.
cards.source: Yang JC et al. Overall Survival with Amivantamab-Lazertinib in EGFR-Mutated Advanced NSCLC. The New England journal of medicine. 2025. PMID: 40923797. Registry ID: NCT04487080. cards.headline: MARIPOSA high-risk biomarker secondary analysis (Felip 2024): the PFS advantage persisted across TP53 co-mutation, detectable ctDNA, non-clearance of ctDNA and liver metastases (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: MARIPOSA high-risk biomarker secondary analysis (Felip 2024): the PFS advantage persisted across TP53 co-mutation, detectable ctDNA, non-clearance of ctDNA and liver metastases (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Secondary biomarker analysis of MARIPOSA — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence
cards.people: Patients randomised to amivantamab + lazertinib (n=429) or osimertinib (n=429) in MARIPOSA; baseline blood ctDNA next-generation sequencing was available for 636 patients (320 combination, 316 osimertinib), with droplet-digital PCR ctDNA analyses at baseline and cycle 3 day 1.
cards.result: Median PFS favoured the combination in every high-risk subgroup examined (hazard ratios are relative measures): TP53 co-mutations, 18.2 vs 12.9 months (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48–0.87); wild-type TP53, 22.1 vs 19.9 months (HR 0.75, 0.52–1.07); detectable baseline ctDNA, 20.3 vs 14.8 months (HR 0.68, 0.53–0.86); no ctDNA clearance at cycle 3 day 1, 16.5 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.49, 0.27–0.87); ctDNA clearance, 24.0 vs 16.5 months (HR 0.64, 0.48–0.87); baseline liver metastases, 18.2 vs 11.0 months (HR 0.58, 0.37–0.91); and no liver metastases, 24.0 vs 18.3 months (HR 0.74, 0.60–0.91). The combination also improved PFS in patients with a history of brain metastases (HR 0.69, per the primary analysis).
cards.watchOut: Subgroup analyses of one trial, with ctDNA data in only 636 of 858 patients in the two compared arms: they show consistency of the PFS effect, not separate proof in each subgroup, and the wild-type TP53 interval crosses 1.

cards.headline: MARIPOSA lazertinib-alone exploratory analysis (Lee 2025): lazertinib alone was comparable to osimertinib (median PFS 18.5 vs 16.6 months, hazard ratio 0.98) — so the combination's gain is not explained by lazertinib alone (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: MARIPOSA lazertinib-alone exploratory analysis (Lee 2025): lazertinib alone was comparable to osimertinib (median PFS 18.5 vs 16.6 months, hazard ratio 0.98) — so the combination's gain is not explained by lazertinib alone (a report OF MARIPOSA, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Exploratory randomised component-contribution analysis within MARIPOSA (lazertinib arm vs osimertinib arm) — same trial as the cards above
cards.people: The lazertinib monotherapy arm of MARIPOSA (n=216) compared exploratorily with the osimertinib arm (n=429) — the first randomised, double-blind comparison of two third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, at median follow-up of 22.0 months.
cards.result: Median PFS was 18.5 months on lazertinib versus 16.6 months on osimertinib (hazard ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.79–1.22; P=0.86 — the treatment made no difference between the two monotherapies), with comparable results across predefined subgroups. Objective response in measurable disease was 83% versus 85%, median response duration 16.6 versus 16.8 months, and median overall survival was not reached in either arm (hazard ratio 1.00, 0.73–1.38) at this interim analysis. Adverse events were mostly grade 1–2 and frequently EGFR-related for both; lazertinib had lower rates of QT-interval prolongation. The component-contribution read: lazertinib alone performs like osimertinib alone, so the combination's superiority over osimertinib (PFS hazard ratio 0.70; final overall-survival hazard ratio 0.75) depends on the amivantamab combination, not on swapping one third-generation TKI for another.
cards.watchOut: Exploratory and not powered as a standalone non-inferiority comparison: 'comparable' here means no difference was shown (hazard ratio 0.98 with an interval spanning 0.79–1.22), not that equivalence was formally proven.

cards.headline: MARIPOSA Asian-subgroup overall survival (Hayashi 2026): in 629 Asian participants, median overall survival not reached versus 38.4 months, hazard ratio 0.74 (relative); 36-month survival 61% vs 53% (a subgroup report OF MARIPOSA — superseded as the survival source by the final overall analysis above)
cards.summary: MARIPOSA Asian-subgroup overall survival (Hayashi 2026): in 629 Asian participants, median overall survival not reached versus 38.4 months, hazard ratio 0.74 (relative); 36-month survival 61% vs 53% (a subgroup report OF MARIPOSA — superseded as the survival source by the final overall analysis above)
cards.type: Prespecified-race subgroup overall-survival analysis of MARIPOSA — same trial as the cards above, not independent evidence; the overall-population final OS card above is this shelf's survival source
cards.people: 629 self-identified Asian participants of MARIPOSA (250 amivantamab + lazertinib, 251 osimertinib, 128 lazertinib), Asian race being a stratification factor at randomisation; median follow-up 38.7 months.
cards.result: Overall survival favoured amivantamab + lazertinib in Asian participants: median not reached (95% CI not reached–not reached) versus 38.4 months (35.1–not reached) on osimertinib (hazard ratio 0.74, 0.56–0.97; nominal P=0.026 — a relative measure), with 61% versus 53% alive at 36 months, an absolute difference of 8 percentage points, consistent with the overall-population final analysis (hazard ratio 0.75). The authors' projection of a greater-than-12-month median survival prolongation assumes an exponential survival distribution and is a projection, not an observed median. The safety profile was consistent with the overall population.
cards.watchOut: A subgroup of one trial with a nominal P value: it supports consistency of the survival effect in Asian participants and adds no independent evidence beyond the final overall analysis.
cards.source: Hayashi H et al. cards.headline: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (MARIPOSA) — amivantamab + lazertinib beats osimertinib first-line on both PFS (23.7 vs 16.6 months) and final overall survival (3-year survival 60% vs 51%), with lazertinib alone shown comparable to osimertinib, at the price of grade 3-or-higher toxicity in 80% vs 52%
cards.summary: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (MARIPOSA) — amivantamab + lazertinib beats osimertinib first-line on both PFS (23.7 vs 16.6 months) and final overall survival (3-year survival 60% vs 51%), with lazertinib alone shown comparable to osimertinib, at the price of grade 3-or-higher toxicity in 80% vs 52%
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single MARIPOSA trial (1,074 randomised 2:2:1; 429 combination, 429 osimertinib, 216 lazertinib alone). PARTIAL scope: this shelf asks only the first-line exon 19 deletion / L858R question.
cards.result: The combination's benefit is two-layered and now survival-confirmed: median PFS 23.7 vs 16.6 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative) with far longer response duration (25.8 vs 16.8 months) despite near-identical response rates (86% vs 85%), and, at the protocol-specified final analysis, significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio 0.75, relative; 3-year survival 60% vs 51%), consistent in Asian participants (hazard ratio 0.74) and across high-risk biomarker subgroups for PFS. The lazertinib-alone arm does its designed job: lazertinib alone was comparable to osimertinib alone (PFS hazard ratio 0.98 — the treatment made no difference between the monotherapies), so the gain belongs to the combination. The price is substantial: grade 3-or-higher adverse events in 80% vs 52%, particularly skin-related events, venous thromboembolism (with its prophylactic-anticoagulation burden) and infusion-related events, and discontinuation of all agents for toxicity in 10% vs 3% at the primary report. Cross-points, in prose only: amivantamab + chemotherapy in EGFR exon 20 insertion disease is homed at pack #5184 — a different population and regimen, none of whose studies are carded here; and osimertinib + chemotherapy (FLAURA2, pack #5183) is the competing first-line intensification question, with no head-to-head trial against this combination.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. All hazard ratios are relative measures and are printed with absolute medians or rates on the cards above.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Adjuvant alectinib after resection of ALK-positive NSCLC (ALINA): 2-year disease-free survival 93.8% vs 63.0% on chemotherapy; overall survival immature
shelves.question: In patients with completely resected stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, does 24 months of adjuvant alectinib, versus platinum-based chemotherapy, improve disease-free and CNS disease-free survival, and at what cost in harms and quality of life? (PARTIAL scope: alectinib in metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC is homed at live #1833.)
shelves.mesh: Humans · Carbazoles · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Lung Neoplasms · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Piperidines · Receptor Protein-Tyrosine Kinases · Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors · Treatment Outcome · Administration, Oral · Administration, Intravenous · Platinum Compounds · Antineoplastic Agents · Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, ALINA (257 randomised), for the adjuvant question only (PARTIAL scope: alectinib in metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC is homed at live #1833 and is not asked here). Adjuvant alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 24 months markedly improved disease-free survival versus four cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy: in stage II–IIIA disease, 93.8% versus 63.0% were alive and disease-free at 2 years (hazard ratio 0.24 — a relative measure; the absolute rates are printed beside it), with the same hazard ratio in the full intention-to-treat population and a CNS disease-free-survival hazard ratio of 0.22 (relative). Overall survival was immature at the primary report and remained unreported in the 2026 companion reports carded here, so the claim is a recurrence claim, not yet a survival claim. Companion reports show quality of life improved and was maintained over the 2 years of treatment, with fewer discontinuations for adverse events than chemotherapy (5% vs 13%) but a long treatment exposure and characteristic laboratory harms (grade 3–4 creatine phosphokinase increase 6%).

cards.headline: ALINA phase 3 RCT (Wu 2024): adjuvant alectinib for 24 months — 2-year disease-free survival 93.8% vs 63.0% on chemotherapy in stage II–IIIA disease (hazard ratio 0.24, relative)
cards.summary: ALINA phase 3 RCT (Wu 2024): adjuvant alectinib for 24 months — 2-year disease-free survival 93.8% vs 63.0% on chemotherapy in stage II–IIIA disease (hazard ratio 0.24, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 global open-label randomised trial (ALINA), adjuvant alectinib vs platinum-based chemotherapy
cards.people: 257 patients with completely resected ALK-positive NSCLC of stage IB (tumours ≥4 cm), II or IIIA (AJCC/UICC 7th edition) were randomised 1:1 — 130 to oral alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 24 months and 127 to intravenous platinum-based chemotherapy for four 21-day cycles — in a global open-label trial.
cards.result: Among patients with stage II or IIIA disease, 93.8% (alectinib) versus 63.0% (chemotherapy) were alive and disease-free at 2 years; the hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death was 0.24 (95% CI 0.13 to 0.45; P<0.001) — a relative measure, printed with the absolute rates. In the intention-to-treat population the 2-year rates were 93.6% versus 63.7% (hazard ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.43; relative). CNS disease-free survival also favoured alectinib (hazard ratio 0.22, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.58; relative). Overall-survival data were immature. No unexpected safety findings were observed.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the comparator is chemotherapy alone — there is no randomised comparison against observation or against another ALK inhibitor in the adjuvant setting. Overall survival was immature: the benefit shown is in disease-free and CNS disease-free survival.
cards.source: Wu YL et al. Alectinib in Resected ALK-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 38598794. Registry ID: NCT03456076. cards.headline: ALINA companion report — quality of life and safety (Dziadziuszko 2026): HRQoL improved and was maintained over 2 years of alectinib; grade 3–4 creatine phosphokinase increase was the commonest severe event (6%)
cards.summary: ALINA companion report — quality of life and safety (Dziadziuszko 2026): HRQoL improved and was maintained over 2 years of alectinib; grade 3–4 creatine phosphokinase increase was the commonest severe event (6%)
cards.type: Companion report of the ALINA phase 3 trial (same programme and patients as the primary card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same ALINA trial population as the card above (257 randomised; safety-evaluable 128 on alectinib and 120 on chemotherapy) — a companion report of the ALINA programme, not an independent trial. Median safety follow-up was 24.8 months on alectinib versus 3.7 months on chemotherapy, reflecting the very different treatment durations.
cards.result: The most common grade 3–4 adverse events on alectinib were blood creatine phosphokinase increased (8 of 128, 6%), alanine aminotransferase increased (2, 2%) and blood bilirubin increased (2, 2%); on chemotherapy they were neutrophil count decreased (12 of 120, 10%), neutropenia (10, 8%) and nausea (5, 4%). Serious treatment-related adverse events occurred in 2% on alectinib versus 7% on chemotherapy, no adverse-event deaths occurred in either group, and discontinuations for adverse events were fewer with alectinib (5% vs 13%). Health-related quality of life (SF-36v2) improved by week 12 in bodily pain, role physical, mental health, social functioning and vitality domains and was maintained to week 96, reaching general-population norm levels (Mental Component Summary 49.9, Physical Component Summary 48.8 at week 96; population norm 50).
cards.watchOut: Safety follow-up is grossly asymmetric (24.8 vs 3.7 months median) because alectinib is given for 2 years and chemotherapy for about 3 months — crude event counts across arms are not exposure-adjusted, and the quality-of-life analysis is exploratory.
cards.source: Dziadziuszko R et al. Adjuvant alectinib versus chemotherapy in resected ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (ALINA): health-related quality-of-life and safety outcomes from a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2026. PMID: 42636834. Registry ID: NCT03456076. cards.headline: ALINA companion report — disease characteristics (Barlesi 2026): the disease-free-survival benefit was consistent across stage (7th and 8th edition), nodal status and tumour size subgroups
cards.summary: ALINA companion report — disease characteristics (Barlesi 2026): the disease-free-survival benefit was consistent across stage (7th and 8th edition), nodal status and tumour size subgroups
cards.type: Companion exploratory subgroup report of the ALINA phase 3 trial (same programme and patients as the primary card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same ALINA primary-analysis population as the cards above (257 randomised; most had tumours ≤3 cm in this report's description, 57.4%; stage IIIA 52.1%; N2 nodal disease 50.6%) — an exploratory subgroup report of the ALINA programme, not an independent trial.
cards.result: Consistent with the primary results, patients receiving alectinib had longer disease-free survival than those receiving chemotherapy irrespective of disease stage re-classified by the AJCC/UICC 8th edition, nodal status, tumour size, or other surgical characteristics. The authors describe alectinib as the first ALK inhibitor to show a consistent adjuvant disease-free-survival benefit over chemotherapy across these subgroups.
cards.watchOut: Exploratory subgroup analysis without new endpoints: it adds consistency, not independent confirmation, and it does not supply the still-missing overall-survival readout.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial (ALINA, n=257) is the whole randomised base — adjuvant alectinib for 24 months roughly quadrupled the relative chance of remaining disease-free at 2 years versus chemotherapy, with overall survival still immature
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial (ALINA, n=257) is the whole randomised base — adjuvant alectinib for 24 months roughly quadrupled the relative chance of remaining disease-free at 2 years versus chemotherapy, with overall survival still immature
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (one phase 3 trial and two of its companion reports).
cards.result: In resected stage IB (≥4 cm)–IIIA ALK-positive NSCLC, adjuvant alectinib gave 2-year disease-free survival of 93.8% versus 63.0% with platinum chemotherapy in stage II–IIIA disease (hazard ratio 0.24, relative) and a similar CNS disease-free-survival advantage (hazard ratio 0.22, relative), with improved and maintained quality of life and fewer treatment discontinuations for adverse events (5% vs 13%). Overall survival was immature at the primary report and is not reported in the companion reports carded here — the shelf's claim is prevention/delay of recurrence, and it must be revisited at the overall-survival readout. The metastatic alectinib question is homed separately at live #1833 and is not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
