shelves.title: Osimertinib after chemoradiotherapy in stage III EGFR-mutated NSCLC (LAURA): progression-free survival 39.1 vs 5.6 months; CNS progression 9% vs 36% at 12 months
shelves.question: In patients with unresectable stage III EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer without progression after definitive chemoradiotherapy, does osimertinib, versus placebo, prolong progression-free survival and prevent CNS progression, and at what cost in pneumonitis and other harms? (PARTIAL scope: adjuvant osimertinib is homed at live #763, first-line metastatic osimertinib at live #1832, and osimertinib plus chemotherapy at pack #5183.)
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Acrylamides · Aniline Compounds · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Chemoradiotherapy · Double-Blind Method · ErbB Receptors · Indoles · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lung Neoplasms · Mutation · Neoplasm Staging · Progression-Free Survival · Pyrimidines · Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single-programme base — one phase 3 trial, LAURA (216 randomised), for the post-chemoradiotherapy consolidation question only (PARTIAL scope: adjuvant osimertinib after resection is homed at live #763, first-line metastatic osimertinib at live #1832, and osimertinib plus chemotherapy at pack #5183 — none is re-carded here). Osimertinib until progression gave median progression-free survival of 39.1 versus 5.6 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.16 — a relative measure; 74% vs 22% were progression-free at 12 months), with CNS progression markedly reduced (cumulative incidence at 12 months 9% vs 36%). Overall survival was interim and immature (20% maturity; hazard ratio 0.81, not significant; 36-month survival 84% vs 74%), so the proven claim is progression delay, not yet longer life. The comparator was placebo, not durvalumab consolidation (the PACIFIC standard, which many LAURA patients had not received) — the trial does not answer osimertinib versus durvalumab. Harms: grade 3-or-worse adverse events 35% vs 12%, radiation pneumonitis 48% vs 38% (mostly grade 1–2), and treatment discontinuation 13% vs 5% over a median exposure of 24.0 versus 8.3 months; patient-reported quality of life was maintained, with no substantial difference in time to deterioration.

cards.headline: LAURA phase 3 RCT (Lu 2024): osimertinib after chemoradiotherapy — median progression-free survival 39.1 vs 5.6 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.16, relative)
cards.summary: LAURA phase 3 RCT (Lu 2024): osimertinib after chemoradiotherapy — median progression-free survival 39.1 vs 5.6 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.16, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (LAURA), osimertinib vs placebo after definitive chemoradiotherapy
cards.people: 216 patients with unresectable stage III EGFR-mutated NSCLC without progression during or after definitive chemoradiotherapy were randomised 2:1, double-blind — 143 to osimertinib and 73 to placebo — with treatment until disease progression (blinded independent central review) or discontinuation.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 39.1 months with osimertinib versus 5.6 months with placebo (hazard ratio for disease progression or death 0.16, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.24; P<0.001 — a relative measure, printed with the absolute medians); 74% (95% CI 65 to 80) versus 22% (95% CI 13 to 32) were alive and progression-free at 12 months. Interim overall survival (20% maturity) showed 36-month survival of 84% versus 74% (hazard ratio for death 0.81, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.56; P=0.53 — not significant). Grade 3-or-higher adverse events occurred in 35% versus 12%; radiation pneumonitis (mostly grade 1–2) was reported in 48% versus 38%. No new safety concerns emerged.
cards.watchOut: The comparator was placebo, not durvalumab consolidation — LAURA does not compare osimertinib with the PACIFIC regimen, and many participants had not received durvalumab. Overall survival was only 20% mature and not significantly different; the established benefit is progression-free survival.
cards.source: Lu S et al. Osimertinib after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III EGFR-Mutated NSCLC. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 38828946. Registry ID: NCT03521154. cards.headline: LAURA companion analysis — CNS efficacy (Lu 2024): CNS progression at 12 months in 9% on osimertinib vs 36% on placebo; median CNS progression-free survival not reached vs 14.9 months
cards.summary: LAURA companion analysis — CNS efficacy (Lu 2024): CNS progression at 12 months in 9% on osimertinib vs 36% on placebo; median CNS progression-free survival not reached vs 14.9 months
cards.type: Companion secondary-endpoint analysis of the LAURA phase 3 trial (same programme and patients as the primary card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same LAURA trial population as the card above (216 randomised: 143 osimertinib, 73 placebo) — a secondary-endpoint analysis of the LAURA programme, not an independent trial.
cards.result: Median CNS progression-free survival (neuroradiologist blinded central review) was not reached with osimertinib versus 14.9 months with placebo (hazard ratio 0.17, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.32 — relative). The cumulative incidence of CNS progression at 12 months was 9% (95% CI 5 to 14) versus 36% (95% CI 24 to 47). Time to death or distant metastases also favoured osimertinib (hazard ratio 0.21, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.38 — relative), with cumulative distant-metastasis incidence at 12 months of 11% versus 37%.
cards.watchOut: Secondary endpoints of the same trial: they show where progression was prevented (CNS and distant sites), not a second confirmation of the primary result.

cards.headline: LAURA companion report — patient-reported outcomes (Arriola 2026): quality of life, functioning and symptoms were maintained on osimertinib, with no substantial difference in time to confirmed deterioration versus placebo
cards.summary: LAURA companion report — patient-reported outcomes (Arriola 2026): quality of life, functioning and symptoms were maintained on osimertinib, with no substantial difference in time to confirmed deterioration versus placebo
cards.type: Companion patient-reported-outcomes report of the LAURA phase 3 trial (same programme and patients as the primary card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same LAURA trial population as the cards above (216 randomised) — a patient-reported-outcomes report of the LAURA programme, not an independent trial. Outcomes were EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13 score changes and time to confirmed deterioration, plus PRO-CTCAE tolerability items.
cards.result: Baseline EORTC scores were comparable between arms. The risk of confirmed deterioration was generally not substantially different between osimertinib and placebo (hazard ratios: global health status/quality of life 1.14, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.78; physical function 1.06, 0.65 to 1.71; fatigue 1.23, 0.85 to 1.80; appetite loss 1.00, 0.63 to 1.58; dyspnoea 1.30, 0.91 to 1.86; coughing 1.17, 0.81 to 1.71; chest pain 1.46, 0.95 to 2.23 — all relative measures whose intervals cross 1). Over 40 weeks, changes from baseline in key functioning and symptom scales were minimal in both arms. PRO-CTCAE responses indicated similar tolerability except for loose/watery stools and dry skin, which were somewhat worse on osimertinib.
cards.watchOut: Patient-reported outcomes were maintained, not improved: this report supports tolerability of a long consolidation course, and adds no efficacy evidence beyond the primary trial.

cards.headline: LAURA companion report — safety in depth (Kato 2026): radiation pneumonitis 48% vs 38% (mostly low grade, 87% of affected patients continued osimertinib); discontinuation 13% vs 5%
cards.summary: LAURA companion report — safety in depth (Kato 2026): radiation pneumonitis 48% vs 38% (mostly low grade, 87% of affected patients continued osimertinib); discontinuation 13% vs 5%
cards.type: Companion in-depth safety report of the LAURA phase 3 trial (same programme and patients as the primary card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same LAURA trial population as the cards above (216 randomised and treated: 143 osimertinib, 73 placebo) — an in-depth safety report of the LAURA programme, not an independent trial. Median treatment exposure was 24.0 months on osimertinib versus 8.3 months on placebo.
cards.result: Exposure-adjusted rates of grade 3-or-worse adverse events were 18 versus 13 per 100 patient-years and of serious adverse events 20 versus 15 per 100 patient-years (osimertinib versus placebo). Diarrhoea and paronychia showed the greatest exposure-adjusted excess on osimertinib. Adverse events led to interruption in 56% versus 25% and to discontinuation in 13% versus 5%. Radiation pneumonitis (grouped term) occurred in 48% versus 38%, was mostly low grade, and almost all events were reported by 18 weeks after randomisation; 60 of 69 affected osimertinib patients (87%) continued treatment, with or without interruption, and 64 of 69 (93%) had no recurrence. Interstitial lung disease (grouped term) was mainly grade 1–2 and manageable, with most events within 20 weeks.
cards.watchOut: Exposure was three times longer on osimertinib than placebo (24.0 vs 8.3 months median), so crude percentages overstate the per-time harm; the exposure-adjusted rates on this card are the fairer comparison. Pneumonitis after thoracic chemoradiation remains the monitoring burden of this strategy.

cards.result: In unresectable stage III EGFR-mutated NSCLC without progression after definitive chemoradiotherapy, osimertinib until progression gave median progression-free survival of 39.1 versus 5.6 months versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.16, relative; 12-month progression-free rates 74% vs 22%), CNS progression at 12 months of 9% versus 36%, maintained patient-reported quality of life, and a manageable but real harm load (grade ≥3 adverse events 35% vs 12%; radiation pneumonitis 48% vs 38%, mostly low grade; discontinuation 13% vs 5%). Interim overall survival (20% maturity) did not differ significantly (hazard ratio 0.81). The other osimertinib settings are homed separately — adjuvant after resection at live #763 (ADAURA), first-line metastatic at live #1832 (FLAURA), and osimertinib plus chemotherapy at pack #5183 (FLAURA2) — and are not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Ponsegromab for cancer cachexia (single programme, floor-risk): phase 2 weight gain vs placebo 1.22–2.81 kg by dose at 12 weeks; phase Ib N=10 for tolerability
shelves.question: In adults with cancer cachexia and elevated serum GDF-15, does the anti-GDF-15 antibody ponsegromab improve body weight, appetite, physical activity and quality of life versus placebo, and is it safe? (FLOOR-RISK: a single programme — one randomised trial plus one open-label first-in-patient study with N=10.)
shelves.mesh: Aged · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Appetite · Body Weight · Cachexia · Double-Blind Method · Exercise · Growth Differentiation Factor 15 · Neoplasms · Injections, Subcutaneous
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit), on a FLOOR-RISK single-programme base, labelled as such: the ponsegromab programme has exactly two RESULT reports — one phase 2 randomised trial (n=187) and one open-label phase Ib first-in-patient study at the reference floor (N=10, printed on its card) — plus a study-design paper carded as provenance only, not as evidence. In the phase 2 trial, patients with cancer cachexia and serum GDF-15 ≥1500 pg/mL gained more weight on ponsegromab than placebo over 12 weeks, with a dose gradient (median between-group differences of 1.22 kg at 100 mg, 1.92 kg at 200 mg and 2.81 kg at 400 mg), and the 400 mg group also improved on appetite/cachexia-symptom measures and digital physical-activity measures. Adverse events of any cause were reported in 70% on ponsegromab versus 80% on placebo. The phase Ib study (n=10) showed no treatment-related adverse events, complete suppression of unbound GDF-15, and a least-squares mean weight increase of 4.63 kg at week 12 — exploratory and uncontrolled, so efficacy rests on the phase 2 trial alone. Twelve weeks is short for a cachexia claim, and no survival or phase 3 result exists. A 2026 anti-GDF-15 combination paper (PMID 42126170) was NOT carded or counted: its fetched record describes mouse and cell-line experiments despite human-trial publication-type tags.

cards.headline: Phase 2 RCT (Groarke 2024): ponsegromab in cancer cachexia with elevated GDF-15 — dose-ordered weight gain versus placebo at 12 weeks (median differences 1.22, 1.92 and 2.81 kg at 100, 200 and 400 mg)
cards.summary: Phase 2 RCT (Groarke 2024): ponsegromab in cancer cachexia with elevated GDF-15 — dose-ordered weight gain versus placebo at 12 weeks (median differences 1.22, 1.92 and 2.81 kg at 100, 200 and 400 mg)
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial (PROACC-1), ponsegromab vs placebo in cancer cachexia — the programme's single randomised report
cards.people: 187 patients with cancer cachexia and an elevated serum GDF-15 level (≥1500 pg/mL) were randomised 1:1:1:1 to subcutaneous ponsegromab 100 mg, 200 mg or 400 mg or placebo every 4 weeks for three doses (12 weeks). Cancer types: 40% non-small-cell lung cancer, 32% pancreatic cancer, 29% colorectal cancer. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in body weight at 12 weeks.
cards.result: At 12 weeks, patients in the ponsegromab groups had significantly greater weight gain than placebo, with median between-group differences of 1.22 kg (95% credible interval 0.37 to 2.25) at 100 mg, 1.92 kg (0.92 to 2.97) at 200 mg and 2.81 kg (1.55 to 4.08) at 400 mg. Improvements across measures of appetite and cachexia symptoms, along with physical activity, were observed in the 400 mg group relative to placebo. Adverse events of any cause were reported in 70% of patients in the ponsegromab groups and 80% in the placebo group.
cards.watchOut: Twelve weeks, a weight primary endpoint, and a biomarker-selected population (GDF-15 ≥1500 pg/mL in three cancer types): the result does not extend to cachexia with lower GDF-15, to other cancers, or to survival. Between-group differences are medians with credible intervals from the trial's Bayesian analysis, as reported.
cards.source: Groarke JD et al. Ponsegromab for the Treatment of Cancer Cachexia. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 39282907. Registry ID: NCT05546476. cards.headline: Phase Ib first-in-patient study (Crawford 2024) — N=10, AT THE REFERENCE FLOOR, printed on the face: open-label ponsegromab 200 mg every 3 weeks; no treatment-related adverse events, GDF-15 suppressed below quantification, least-squares mean weight +4.63 kg at week 12 (exploratory, uncontrolled)
cards.summary: Phase Ib first-in-patient study (Crawford 2024) — N=10, AT THE REFERENCE FLOOR, printed on the face: open-label ponsegromab 200 mg every 3 weeks; no treatment-related adverse events, GDF-15 suppressed below quantification, least-squares mean weight +4.63 kg at week 12 (exploratory, uncontrolled)
cards.type: Phase Ib open-label first-in-patient study (single programme as the phase 2 card above — a programme report, not independent randomised evidence). SMALL N=10
cards.people: 10 adults with advanced cancer, cachexia and elevated serum GDF-15 concentration received open-label subcutaneous ponsegromab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 12 weeks (24-week study), in addition to standard-of-care anticancer treatment. Median baseline unbound GDF-15 was 2.269 ng/mL. SMALL N=10 — this study is at the floor and is not load-bearing for efficacy.
cards.result: No treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events, injection-site reactions, or adverse trends in laboratory tests, vital signs or ECG parameters attributable to ponsegromab were identified. Median unbound GDF-15 fell below the lower limit of quantification (0.0424 ng/mL) from 3 hours after the first dose through week 15. Body weight increased at all time points; the least-squares mean (SE) increase at week 12 was 4.63 (1.98) kg, approximately 6.6% relative to baseline. Improvements were also observed in actigraphy-based physical activity and in quality of life including appetite (Functional Assessment of Anorexia-Cachexia Therapy scores).
cards.watchOut: Ten patients, open-label, no comparator, concurrent anticancer treatment: the weight and activity changes are hypothesis-generating only. This card's firm content is tolerability and complete GDF-15 suppression at the tested dose.
cards.source: Crawford J et al. A Phase Ib First-In-Patient Study Assessing the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of Ponsegromab in Participants with Cancer and Cachexia. cards.headline: Programme provenance card — PROACC-1 study-design paper (Groarke 2024): the published design of the phase 2 trial carded above (randomised n≈168 planned, 100/200/400 mg vs placebo, weight at week 12 primary) — a design report, NOT a results report and not evidence
cards.summary: Programme provenance card — PROACC-1 study-design paper (Groarke 2024): the published design of the phase 2 trial carded above (randomised n≈168 planned, 100/200/400 mg vs placebo, weight at week 12 primary) — a design report, NOT a results report and not evidence
cards.type: Programme report: published study-design paper for the PROACC-1 phase 2 trial (provenance only — not a results report, not counted as evidence)
cards.people: The PROACC-1 programme: approximately 168 adults with non-small-cell lung, pancreatic or colorectal cancer, cachexia and elevated GDF-15 concentrations, planned for randomisation 1:1:1:1 to ponsegromab 100, 200 or 400 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for a 12-week double-blind period, followed by optional open-label ponsegromab 400 mg for up to 1 year. The completed trial (187 randomised) is the first card on this shelf.
cards.result: The design paper prespecifies the primary endpoint (mean change in body weight at week 12, analysed by a mixed model and a Bayesian Emax model) and the secondary endpoints the results paper reports: physical activity and function including actigraphy by remote digital sensors, appetite-related symptoms (Functional Assessment of Anorexia-Cachexia Therapy subscales), cachexia-symptom diary items, safety, and exploratory pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, immunogenicity and lumbar skeletal muscle index. It contains no results.
cards.watchOut: Carded only so the shelf's provenance is complete and the programme's report count is honest: two result reports (one randomised, one n=10 open-label) plus this design paper. It must never be cited as a third result.

cards.result: In 187 randomised patients with cancer cachexia and GDF-15 ≥1500 pg/mL, ponsegromab every 4 weeks for 12 weeks gave median weight differences versus placebo of 1.22 kg (100 mg), 1.92 kg (200 mg) and 2.81 kg (400 mg), with appetite, cachexia-symptom and activity improvements concentrated at 400 mg and no adverse-event excess (70% vs 80% any-cause). The phase Ib study (N=10, open-label) supports tolerability and target engagement (unbound GDF-15 suppressed below quantification) but not efficacy. Excluded from this shelf: PMID 42126170 (2026), whose record carries phase 3 publication-type tags but whose fetched abstract and MeSH describe mouse and cell-line experiments — it is not a human report and was neither carded nor counted. The other cachexia agents are homed separately (megestrol live #1790, mirtazapine pack #2807, anamorelin pack #6112) and are not re-carded here.

shelves.title: Divarasib in KRAS G12C NSCLC: phase 3 beat sotorasib/adagrasib — PFS 9.8 vs 5.7 months and OS 17.7 vs 12.0 months, response 58.4% vs 32.3%
shelves.question: In patients with advanced KRAS G12C-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer, does the next-generation covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib, versus no concurrent control (phase 1) or versus sotorasib/adagrasib (phase 3, previously treated disease), produce responses and prolong progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Colorectal Neoplasms · Lung Neoplasms · Mutation · Proto-Oncogene Proteins p21(ras) · Administration, Oral · Enzyme Inhibitors
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — on a phase 3 head-to-head trial plus a consistent single-arm phase 1 base. In previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC, divarasib beat the first-generation control (sotorasib or adagrasib) on progression-free survival (median 9.8 vs 5.7 months; hazard ratio 0.58, a relative measure) and overall survival (median 17.7 vs 12.0 months; hazard ratio 0.56, relative), with confirmed response in 58.4% versus 32.3% (absolute rates) and fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related events (24.6% vs 34.5%). The control arm was investigator's choice with a very uneven split (156 sotorasib, 15 adagrasib), so the shelf answers 'divarasib versus the first-generation class as randomised' — the adagrasib comparison is not separately powered. The phase 1 slices are single-arm dose/activity evidence, labelled as such.

cards.headline: Phase 3 head-to-head RCT, Krascendo 1 (Skoulidis 2026): divarasib beat sotorasib/adagrasib control on PFS (9.8 vs 5.7 months; HR 0.58, relative) and OS (17.7 vs 12.0 months; HR 0.56, relative); response 58.4% vs 32.3%
cards.summary: Phase 3 head-to-head RCT, Krascendo 1 (Skoulidis 2026): divarasib beat sotorasib/adagrasib control on PFS (9.8 vs 5.7 months; HR 0.58, relative) and OS (17.7 vs 12.0 months; HR 0.56, relative); response 58.4% vs 32.3%
cards.type: Phase 3 international open-label randomised trial (Krascendo 1), divarasib vs sotorasib or adagrasib
cards.people: 338 patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC randomised to divarasib 400 mg once daily (n=167) or control (n=171: sotorasib 960 mg once daily in 156, adagrasib 600 mg twice daily in 15); median follow-up 14.3 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 9.8 months on divarasib versus 5.7 months on control (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.58, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.76 — a relative measure; P<0.001). Median overall survival was 17.7 versus 12.0 months (hazard ratio for death 0.56, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.78 — relative; P<0.001). Among 328 evaluable patients, confirmed response occurred in 58.4% on divarasib versus 32.3% on control (absolute rates), and median duration of response was 11.9 versus 6.9 months. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were fewer on divarasib (24.6% vs 34.5%).
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the control is a class as randomised — 156 patients received sotorasib but only 15 adagrasib, so no separately powered divarasib-versus-adagrasib claim can be made.
cards.source: Skoulidis F et al. Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C-Mutated NSCLC. The New England journal of medicine. 2026. PMID: 42929675. Registry ID: NCT06497556. MeSH: none in the record

cards.headline: Phase 1 primary report (Sacher 2023): single-agent divarasib — NSCLC confirmed response 53.4% and median PFS 13.1 months in 60 patients; mostly low-grade adverse events (single-arm)
cards.summary: Phase 1 primary report (Sacher 2023): single-agent divarasib — NSCLC confirmed response 53.4% and median PFS 13.1 months in 60 patients; mostly low-grade adverse events (single-arm)
cards.type: Phase 1 single-arm dose-escalation/expansion study of single-agent divarasib
cards.people: 137 patients with advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated solid tumours (60 NSCLC, 55 colorectal cancer, 22 other) received divarasib 50–400 mg once daily in a phase 1 dose study.
cards.result: Among patients with NSCLC, confirmed response was 53.4% (95% CI 39.9 to 66.7) and median progression-free survival 13.1 months; in colorectal cancer, response was 29.1% and median PFS 5.6 months (a different disease, shown for programme context only). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 93%; grade 3 events in 11% and a grade 4 event in 1%; dose reduction in 14% and discontinuation in 3%; no dose-limiting toxic effects or treatment-related deaths.

cards.type: Long-term follow-up report of the phase 1 study (same programme as the Sacher 2023 card — not an independent trial)
cards.people: 65 patients with advanced KRAS G12C-positive NSCLC treated with single-agent divarasib 50–400 mg once daily in the same phase 1 programme; 31 patients (48%) were treated beyond 1 year; 63 had measurable disease at baseline.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response rate was 55.6% (95% CI 42.5 to 68.1), median duration of response 18.0 months (95% CI 11.1 to 24.9), and median progression-free survival 13.8 months (95% CI 9.8 to 25.4) overall and 15.3 months in the 400-mg dose group (n=44). cards.headline: ctDNA companion report (Choi 2024): KRAS G12C circulating tumour DNA was detectable in 72.9% of NSCLC patients and early ctDNA decline tracked with response — exploratory biomarker report of the phase 1 programme, not an efficacy trial
cards.summary: ctDNA companion report (Choi 2024): KRAS G12C circulating tumour DNA was detectable in 72.9% of NSCLC patients and early ctDNA decline tracked with response — exploratory biomarker report of the phase 1 programme, not an efficacy trial
cards.type: Exploratory ctDNA biomarker analysis of the phase 1 divarasib programme (companion report — not independent efficacy evidence)
cards.people: 134 patients with KRAS G12C-mutated solid tumours treated with single-agent divarasib in the phase 1 study, with serial plasma ctDNA profiling at baseline, cycle 1 day 15 and cycle 3 day 1.
cards.result: KRAS G12C ctDNA was detectable in 72.9% (43 of 59) of patients with NSCLC and 92.6% (50 of 54) with colorectal cancer. A decline in ctDNA level was seen as early as cycle 1 day 15, and decline in ctDNA tumour fraction was associated with response and progression-free survival; except for a few cases of sub-clonality, KRAS G12C variant allele frequency changes mirrored overall ctDNA tumour fraction, supporting KRAS G12C as a truncal mutation in most patients.
cards.watchOut: Exploratory and associational: ctDNA dynamics are a response correlate within a single-arm programme, not a validated surrogate and not comparative evidence.

cards.headline: Synthesis: a phase 3 win over the first-generation class (PFS and OS), built on a phase 1 base with durable single-arm responses — the comparative claim is against sotorasib/adagrasib as randomised, mostly sotorasib
cards.summary: Synthesis: a phase 3 win over the first-generation class (PFS and OS), built on a phase 1 base with durable single-arm responses — the comparative claim is against sotorasib/adagrasib as randomised, mostly sotorasib
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Krascendo 1 (n=338) showed divarasib superior to sotorasib-or-adagrasib control in previously treated KRAS G12C NSCLC: median PFS 9.8 versus 5.7 months (HR 0.58, relative), median OS 17.7 versus 12.0 months (HR 0.56, relative), response 58.4% versus 32.3%, with fewer grade 3–4 treatment-related events (24.6% vs 34.5%). The phase 1 programme (response 53.4–55.6%, median duration of response 18.0 months at long-term follow-up) is consistent single-arm background, and the ctDNA report is an exploratory companion. Because only 15 control patients received adagrasib, the head-to-head verdict is a class verdict dominated by sotorasib.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-mutant NSCLC: response ~50% at the licensed 5.4 mg/kg dose, with ILD in 14.9% — versus 56% response and 32.0% ILD at 6.4 mg/kg
shelves.question: In patients with previously treated metastatic HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer, does trastuzumab deruxtecan (5.4 or 6.4 mg/kg), versus no concurrent control, produce objective responses, and what is the interstitial lung disease cost at each dose?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Camptothecin · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Immunoconjugates · Lung Diseases, Interstitial · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Pneumonia · Progression-Free Survival · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Trastuzumab
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-arm evidence throughout (DESTINY-Lung02 randomised dose, not treatment), so response rates have no concurrent comparator. The dose story is the shelf: at 5.4 mg/kg, confirmed response was 50.0% in DESTINY-Lung02's final analysis with adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease (ILD) in 14.9%; at 6.4 mg/kg, response was 56.0% with ILD in 32.0% — and in the earlier DESTINY-Lung01 at 6.4 mg/kg, response was 55% with ILD in 26% including 2 deaths. The licensed 5.4 mg/kg dose follows from that balance. ILD is the class-defining harm for every deruxtecan shelf and is not softened here. The DESTINY-Lung01 HER2-overexpressing cohort is a different biomarker question and is cross-pointed in prose only, not carded. The Lung02 final analysis carded here supersedes the primary report to which two errata (against that earlier report) were issued.

cards.headline: DESTINY-Lung01 HER2-mutant cohort (Li 2022): response 55% at 6.4 mg/kg in 91 patients — and adjudicated drug-related ILD in 26%, with 2 deaths (single-arm)
cards.summary: DESTINY-Lung01 HER2-mutant cohort (Li 2022): response 55% at 6.4 mg/kg in 91 patients — and adjudicated drug-related ILD in 26%, with 2 deaths (single-arm)
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm study (DESTINY-Lung01, HER2-mutant cohort), trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg
cards.people: 91 patients with metastatic HER2-mutant NSCLC refractory to standard treatment, given trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg; median follow-up 13.1 months.
cards.result: Centrally confirmed objective response occurred in 55% (95% CI 44 to 65); median duration of response was 9.3 months, median progression-free survival 8.2 months and median overall survival 17.8 months. Grade 3 or higher drug-related adverse events occurred in 46%, most commonly neutropenia (19%). Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 26% of patients and resulted in death in 2 patients. Responses occurred across HER2 mutation subtypes and in patients with no detectable HER2 expression or amplification.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm at the higher, unlicensed dose: the 55% response rate has no comparator, and the 26% ILD rate with 2 deaths is the reason the dose question had to be randomised in Lung02.
cards.source: Li BT et al. Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in HER2-Mutant Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2022. PMID: 34534430. Registry ID: NCT03505710. cards.headline: DESTINY-Lung02 final analysis (Jänne 2025): response 50.0% at 5.4 mg/kg vs 56.0% at 6.4 mg/kg — but ILD 14.9% vs 32.0% and grade ≥3 drug-related events 39.6% vs 60.0% (randomised dose, not randomised treatment)
cards.summary: DESTINY-Lung02 final analysis (Jänne 2025): response 50.0% at 5.4 mg/kg vs 56.0% at 6.4 mg/kg — but ILD 14.9% vs 32.0% and grade ≥3 drug-related events 39.6% vs 60.0% (randomised dose, not randomised treatment)
cards.type: Randomised dose-blinded phase 2 trial (DESTINY-Lung02) — dose comparison only, final analysis
cards.people: 152 patients with previously treated HER2-mutant metastatic NSCLC randomised 2:1, dose-blinded, to trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg (102 received) or 6.4 mg/kg (50 received) every 3 weeks; median follow-up about 16 months in both arms.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response rate was 50.0% (51 of 102; 95% CI 39.9 to 60.1) at 5.4 mg/kg and 56.0% (28 of 50; 95% CI 41.3 to 70.0) at 6.4 mg/kg. Drug-related grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 39.6% (40 of 101) versus 60.0% (30 of 50); nausea was the commonest event (67.3% and 82.0%). Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 14.9% (15 of 101) versus 32.0% (16 of 50), mostly grade 1–2, with one grade 5 event in each arm. Health-related quality of life was preserved while sample size sufficed for analysis. The authors concluded the approved 5.4 mg/kg dose has the more favourable benefit–risk profile.
cards.watchOut: Randomisation was between doses, not against any control treatment, so efficacy remains single-arm in kind; this final analysis supersedes the primary report (against which errata were issued). ILD rates here are from longer follow-up and are higher than in the FDA approval dataset carded next — the datasets and cutoffs differ.

cards.headline: FDA approval summary (Mehta 2024): accelerated approval at 5.4 mg/kg rested on a Lung02 interim response rate of 58% with ILD of 6% at 5.4 mg/kg vs 14% at 6.4 mg/kg in the approval dataset
cards.summary: FDA approval summary (Mehta 2024): accelerated approval at 5.4 mg/kg rested on a Lung02 interim response rate of 58% with ILD of 6% at 5.4 mg/kg vs 14% at 6.4 mg/kg in the approval dataset
cards.type: FDA approval summary (regulatory review of DESTINY-Lung02 interim analysis) — companion card, not a trial report
cards.people: The FDA review of the accelerated approval (11 August 2022) for unresectable or metastatic NSCLC with activating HER2 mutations after prior systemic therapy, based on a prespecified interim analysis of DESTINY-Lung02.
cards.result: At the approved dose of 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks, overall response rate was 58% (95% CI 43 to 71) and median duration of response 8.7 months, consistent with the 6.4 mg/kg dose. In the approval dataset, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 6% at 5.4 mg/kg and 14% at 6.4 mg/kg. The commonest adverse reactions (20% or more) were nausea, constipation, decreased appetite, vomiting, fatigue and alopecia. In the setting of similar efficacy and reduced toxicity, approval was granted for 5.4 mg/kg — the first approval of a targeted therapy for HER2-mutated NSCLC.
cards.watchOut: An approval summary of an interim dataset: its ILD rates (6% and 14%) are lower than the Lung02 final-analysis rates (14.9% and 32.0%) because of the earlier cutoff and different analysis set — do not mix the two datasets' numbers.

cards.headline: DESTINY-Lung05, China (Liu 2026): response 56.9% at 5.4 mg/kg in 72 Chinese patients; grade ≥3 drug-related events 55.6%; ILD in 12.5% with no grade 5 event reported (single-arm)
cards.summary: DESTINY-Lung05, China (Liu 2026): response 56.9% at 5.4 mg/kg in 72 Chinese patients; grade ≥3 drug-related events 55.6%; ILD in 12.5% with no grade 5 event reported (single-arm)
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm study (DESTINY-Lung05, China), trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg, final analysis
cards.people: 72 patients from China with HER2-mutant metastatic NSCLC progressed on or after at least 1 prior anticancer therapy, given trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks in the open-label single-arm phase 2 DESTINY-Lung05 study; median follow-up 20.2 months.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response rate by independent central review was 56.9% (95% CI 44.7 to 68.6); median progression-free survival was 9.9 months and median overall survival 21.0 months. Grade 3 or higher drug-related adverse events occurred in 40 patients (55.6%). Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis occurred in 9 patients (12.5%): 8 grade 1–2 and 1 grade 3. No new safety signals were reported.

cards.type: Post hoc pooled secondary analysis of DESTINY-Lung01 and DESTINY-Lung02 by brain-metastases status — not an independent trial

cards.result: At 5.4 mg/kg, systemic confirmed response was 47% (15 of 32) in patients with brain metastases and 50% (35 of 70) without; at 6.4 mg/kg, 50% (27 of 54) and 59% (51 of 87). Among patients with measurable baseline brain metastases, intracranial confirmed response was 50% (7 of 14) at 5.4 mg/kg and 30% (9 of 30) at 6.4 mg/kg. Safety was generally manageable regardless of brain metastases, favouring 5.4 mg/kg.

cards.result: Across DESTINY-Lung01 (6.4 mg/kg, response 55%, ILD 26% with 2 deaths), DESTINY-Lung02 (response 50.0% at 5.4 mg/kg versus 56.0% at 6.4 mg/kg; ILD 14.9% versus 32.0%; grade ≥3 drug-related events 39.6% versus 60.0%), the FDA approval summary, the Chinese DESTINY-Lung05 cohort (response 56.9% at 5.4 mg/kg; ILD 12.5%) and the pooled brain-metastases analysis, trastuzumab deruxtecan is consistently active in previously treated HER2-mutant NSCLC. All evidence is single-arm in kind — Lung02 randomised dose only — so there is no comparative survival evidence. The HER2-overexpressing (non-mutant) DESTINY-Lung01 cohort asks a different biomarker question and is not carded here; the HER2-mutant TKI question (zongertinib) is a different intervention, cross-pointed in prose only.

shelves.title: Datopotamab deruxtecan in NSCLC: SPLIT — PFS gain vs docetaxel (HR 0.75) with null OS and a squamous reversal; single-arm response 35.8% in genomically selected disease
shelves.question: In patients with previously treated advanced or metastatic NSCLC — unselected by histology, and with actionable genomic alterations after targeted therapy and platinum chemotherapy — does the TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugate datopotamab deruxtecan, versus docetaxel (or no concurrent control), prolong progression-free survival and produce responses?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Docetaxel · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Female · Middle Aged · Aged · Adult · Progression-Free Survival · Aged, 80 and over
shelves.balance: SPLIT — by histology and by slice. In the randomised TROPION-Lung01 (n=604), datopotamab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival versus docetaxel (median 4.4 vs 3.7 months; hazard ratio 0.75, a relative measure) but overall survival was not significantly different (12.9 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.94, relative). The PFS effect was driven by nonsquamous histology (HR 0.63, relative), while the squamous subgroup numerically favoured docetaxel (PFS HR 1.41, OS HR 1.32 — relative, neither significant). The single-arm TROPION-Lung05 in genomically selected disease found a 35.8% response rate (43.6% in EGFR-mutated disease). The two slices are labelled and never pooled as one verdict. Stomatitis (any grade 56.2% in Lung05) and interstitial lung disease (8.8% adjudicated drug-related in Lung01 versus 4.1% on docetaxel) are the harms on the face. The breast-cancer datopotamab question is homed separately (pack #6405) and is not folded in.

cards.headline: TROPION-Lung01 phase 3 RCT (Ahn 2025): PFS improved vs docetaxel (4.4 vs 3.7 months; HR 0.75, relative) but OS did not (12.9 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.94, not significant) — and the squamous subgroup numerically favoured docetaxel
cards.summary: TROPION-Lung01 phase 3 RCT (Ahn 2025): PFS improved vs docetaxel (4.4 vs 3.7 months; HR 0.75, relative) but OS did not (12.9 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.94, not significant) — and the squamous subgroup numerically favoured docetaxel
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (TROPION-Lung01), datopotamab deruxtecan vs docetaxel
cards.people: 604 patients with pretreated advanced/metastatic NSCLC randomised to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg (n=299) or docetaxel 75 mg/m² (n=305) every 3 weeks.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 4.4 months (95% CI 4.2 to 5.6) on datopotamab deruxtecan versus 3.7 months (2.9 to 4.2) on docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.91 — a relative measure; P=0.004). Median overall survival was 12.9 versus 11.8 months (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.14 — relative; P=0.530, not significant). In the prespecified nonsquamous subgroup, median PFS was 5.5 versus 3.6 months (HR 0.63, relative) and OS 14.6 versus 12.3 months (HR 0.84, relative, not significant); in the squamous subgroup, median PFS was 2.8 versus 3.9 months (HR 1.41, relative) and OS 7.6 versus 9.4 months (HR 1.32, relative), neither significant. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 25.6% versus 42.1%, and any-grade adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis in 8.8% versus 4.1%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, with a dual primary endpoint split: the statistically significant PFS gain is modest in absolute terms (0.7 months of median PFS) and the overall-survival endpoint was null; the histology split is prespecified but the squamous reversal is a subgroup finding.
cards.source: Ahn MJ et al. cards.headline: TROPION-Lung05 phase 2 (Sands 2025): single-arm response 35.8% overall in actionable-alteration NSCLC after targeted therapy and platinum — 43.6% in EGFR-mutated, 23.5% in ALK-rearranged disease; stomatitis in 56.2%
cards.summary: TROPION-Lung05 phase 2 (Sands 2025): single-arm response 35.8% overall in actionable-alteration NSCLC after targeted therapy and platinum — 43.6% in EGFR-mutated, 23.5% in ALK-rearranged disease; stomatitis in 56.2%
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm study (TROPION-Lung05) in genomically selected NSCLC
cards.people: 137 patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC with actionable genomic alterations, progressing on or after targeted therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy (56.9% EGFR mutations, 24.8% ALK rearrangements; 71.5% had received at least 3 prior lines), given datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response rate was 35.8% (95% CI 27.8 to 44.4) overall, 43.6% (32.4 to 55.3) in EGFR-mutated and 23.5% (10.7 to 41.2) in ALK-rearranged disease; median duration of response was 7.0 months and disease control rate 78.8%. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 28.5%; the commonest was stomatitis (any grade 56.2%; grade 3 or higher 9.5%). Five patients (3.6%) had adjudicated treatment-related interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, including 1 grade 5 event (0.7%).
cards.watchOut: Single-arm in a heavily pretreated, genomically selected population: response rates cannot be compared with the randomised Lung01 population, and the EGFR/ALK split is descriptive.

cards.result: TROPION-Lung01 gives the only comparative verdict: median PFS 4.4 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.75, relative) with no significant overall-survival difference (HR 0.94), driven by nonsquamous histology (PFS HR 0.63) while squamous disease numerically favoured docetaxel (PFS HR 1.41). TROPION-Lung05 and its EGFR-mutated pool with Lung01 show single-arm activity after targeted therapy and platinum (response 35.8% overall; 43% in the EGFR pool), at the cost of stomatitis in over half of patients and interstitial lung disease in 3.6–8.8% across reports. This is not a general win in unselected NSCLC, and the slices must not be pooled into one.

shelves.question: In patients with advanced NSCLC — first-line PD-L1-positive disease, first-line squamous disease, or EGFR-mutated nonsquamous disease after EGFR-TKI progression — does ivonescimab, alone versus pembrolizumab or added to chemotherapy versus chemotherapy (or versus tislelizumab plus chemotherapy), prolong progression-free and overall survival?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — across three distinct randomised questions, labelled as separate slices and never pooled: (1) first-line PD-L1-positive disease (HARMONi-2, China, n=398): ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab on PFS (11.1 vs 5.8 months; HR 0.51, a relative measure) with overall survival immature; (2) first-line squamous disease (HARMONi-6, China, n=532 randomised): ivonescimab plus chemotherapy beat tislelizumab plus chemotherapy on PFS (11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.60, relative); (3) EGFR-mutated disease after EGFR-TKI progression: HARMONi-A (China, n=322) showed an overall-survival benefit for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy (16.8 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.74, relative; 30-month survival 29.1% vs 18.4%, absolute rates), while the global HARMONi trial (n=438) showed a PFS benefit (6.8 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.52, relative) with an overall-survival estimate that was not significant (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.01). Every trial except the global HARMONi was run in China. VEGF-class and immune harms price the gain: grade 3 or higher treatment-related events were 29% versus 16% against pembrolizumab in HARMONi-2 and 64% versus 54% against tislelizumab-chemotherapy in HARMONi-6. Product naming: ivonescimab (Akeso/Summit), a PD-1×VEGF bispecific antibody.

cards.headline: HARMONi-2 phase 3 (Xiong 2025): ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab first-line in PD-L1-positive NSCLC — PFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.51, relative); survival immature; grade ≥3 treatment-related events 29% vs 16%
cards.summary: HARMONi-2 phase 3 (Xiong 2025): ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab first-line in PD-L1-positive NSCLC — PFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.51, relative); survival immature; grade ≥3 treatment-related events 29% vs 16%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (HARMONi-2, China), ivonescimab vs pembrolizumab, first-line PD-L1-positive NSCLC
cards.people: 398 patients with locally advanced or metastatic PD-L1-positive NSCLC without sensitising EGFR mutations or ALK translocations, randomised at 55 hospitals in China to ivonescimab 20 mg/kg (n=198) or pembrolizumab 200 mg (n=200) every 3 weeks.
cards.result: At the preplanned interim analysis, median progression-free survival was 11.1 months on ivonescimab versus 5.8 months on pembrolizumab (stratified hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.69 — a relative measure; P<0.0001), consistent in the PD-L1 TPS 1–49% subgroup (HR 0.54, relative) and TPS 50% or higher (HR 0.48, relative). Overall survival was immature at this report. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 29% (58 patients) on ivonescimab versus 16% (31) on pembrolizumab; grade 3 or higher immune-related events were 7% versus 8%.
cards.watchOut: A single-country (China) interim PFS result with immature survival: a hazard ratio of 0.51 is a relative measure, and whether the PFS win becomes a survival win — or replicates outside China — is not answered by this report.
cards.source: Xiong A et al. Ivonescimab versus pembrolizumab for PD-L1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (HARMONi-2): a randomised, double-blind, phase 3 study in China. Lancet (London, England). 2025. PMID: 40057343. Registry ID: NCT05499390. cards.headline: HARMONi-A final OS analysis (Fang 2026): ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival after EGFR-TKI progression — 16.8 vs 14.1 months (HR 0.74, relative); 30-month survival 29.1% vs 18.4%
cards.summary: HARMONi-A final OS analysis (Fang 2026): ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival after EGFR-TKI progression — 16.8 vs 14.1 months (HR 0.74, relative); 30-month survival 29.1% vs 18.4%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (HARMONi-A, China), final overall-survival report, ivonescimab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy after EGFR-TKI progression
cards.people: 322 adults with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-variant nonsquamous NSCLC after prior EGFR-TKI therapy, randomised at 55 sites in China to ivonescimab 20 mg/kg (n=161) or placebo (n=161) plus pemetrexed–carboplatin for 4 cycles, then maintenance; median follow-up 32.5 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 16.8 months with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy versus 14.1 months with placebo plus chemotherapy (stratified hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.95 — a relative measure; P=0.02), an absolute median difference of 2.7 months; estimated 30-month survival was 29.1% versus 18.4% (absolute rates). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 67.1% versus 54.7%. Progression-free survival was the trial's primary endpoint and overall survival the key secondary endpoint, tested hierarchically.
cards.watchOut: China-only, and the survival gain is modest in absolute median terms (2.7 months) with substantially more grade 3 or higher toxicity; the global HARMONi trial carded below did not reach significance on overall survival.
cards.source: Fang W et al. Bispecific Antibody Ivonescimab Added to Chemotherapy in EGFR-Variant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The HARMONi-A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2026. PMID: 42307937. Registry ID: NCT05184712. cards.headline: HARMONi-6 phase 3 (Chen 2025): first-line squamous NSCLC — ivonescimab plus chemotherapy beat tislelizumab plus chemotherapy on PFS (11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.60, relative); grade ≥3 treatment-related events 64% vs 54%
cards.summary: HARMONi-6 phase 3 (Chen 2025): first-line squamous NSCLC — ivonescimab plus chemotherapy beat tislelizumab plus chemotherapy on PFS (11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.60, relative); grade ≥3 treatment-related events 64% vs 54%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (HARMONi-6, China), ivonescimab + chemotherapy vs tislelizumab + chemotherapy, first-line squamous NSCLC
cards.people: 532 patients with previously untreated unresectable stage IIIB/IIIC or IV squamous NSCLC randomised at 50 sites in China (761 screened) to ivonescimab 20 mg/kg or tislelizumab 200 mg, each plus paclitaxel–carboplatin for 4 cycles, then antibody maintenance for up to 24 months; median follow-up 10.3 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 11.1 months (95% CI 9.9 to not evaluable) with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy versus 6.9 months (5.8 to 8.6) with tislelizumab plus chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.78 — a relative measure; P<0.0001), consistent regardless of PD-L1 status. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 64% (170 patients) versus 54% (144); grade 3 or higher immune-related events in 9% versus 10%; grade 3 or higher treatment-related haemorrhage in 2% (5 patients) versus 1% (2). Overall survival is not reported in this record.
cards.watchOut: Short follow-up (median 10.3 months), no survival result yet, and the comparator (tislelizumab) is a China-standard PD-1 inhibitor — the trial answers the squamous first-line question against that comparator, in China.
cards.source: Chen Z et al. cards.headline: Global HARMONi phase 3 (Le 2026): after third-generation EGFR-TKI progression, PFS improved (6.8 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.52, relative) but overall survival was not significant (16.8 vs 14.0 months; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.01)
cards.summary: Global HARMONi phase 3 (Le 2026): after third-generation EGFR-TKI progression, PFS improved (6.8 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.52, relative) but overall survival was not significant (16.8 vs 14.0 months; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.01)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (global HARMONi), ivonescimab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy after third-generation EGFR-TKI progression
cards.people: 438 patients with stage IIIB/IIIC or IV nonsquamous EGFR-mutated NSCLC progressed after a third-generation EGFR-TKI, randomised at 114 centres across Asia, Europe and North America to ivonescimab 20 mg/kg (n=219) or placebo (n=219) plus pemetrexed–carboplatin every 3 weeks.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 6.8 months (95% CI 5.7 to 7.1) with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy versus 4.4 months (4.1 to 5.5) with placebo plus chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.52, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.66 — a relative measure; P<0.0001), on an analysis set of 345 patients with 275 events. Median overall survival was 16.8 versus 14.0 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.01 — relative; not significant). The commonest grade 3–4 treatment-related events were cytopenias (decreased neutrophil count 19% vs 17%); serious treatment-related adverse events occurred in 28% versus 15%, and treatment-related deaths in 4 versus 5 patients.
cards.watchOut: The one global trial: its PFS result confirms HARMONi-A's direction, but its overall-survival confidence interval crosses 1 — the shelf must not present a global survival benefit as established.
cards.source: Le X et al. Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with advanced EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer after disease progression on EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HARMONi): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2026. PMID: 42636833. Registry ID: NCT06396065. cards.result: Ivonescimab improved progression-free survival in every randomised slice: versus pembrolizumab first-line in PD-L1-positive disease (11.1 vs 5.8 months; HR 0.51, relative; survival immature), with chemotherapy in first-line squamous disease versus tislelizumab-chemotherapy (11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.60, relative; survival unreported), and with chemotherapy after EGFR-TKI progression in both HARMONi-A (PFS primary; OS 16.8 vs 14.1 months, HR 0.74, relative, significant) and the global HARMONi (PFS 6.8 vs 4.4 months, HR 0.52, relative; OS HR 0.79, not significant). Added grade 3 or higher toxicity is consistent (for example 29% vs 16% against pembrolizumab alone). All but the global trial were conducted in China.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Amivantamab + chemotherapy after osimertinib (MARIPOSA-2, PARTIAL): PFS 6.3 months (8.3 with lazertinib) vs 4.2 on chemotherapy alone; response 64% vs 36%
shelves.question: In patients with EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC progressed on osimertinib, does amivantamab plus carboplatin–pemetrexed, with or without lazertinib, versus chemotherapy alone, prolong progression-free survival, and at what added toxicity?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Acrylamides · Aniline Compounds · Antibodies, Bispecific · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carboplatin · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Disease Progression · ErbB Receptors · Indoles · Lung Neoplasms · Morpholines · Mutation · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Pyrazoles · Pyrimidines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme evidence: one phase 3 trial (MARIPOSA-2, n=657) reported across a primary report, a patient-relevant-outcomes report and an Asian-subgroup analysis, which are reports of one trial, not three trials. After osimertinib progression, amivantamab–chemotherapy prolonged median PFS to 6.3 months and amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy to 8.3 months versus 4.2 months on chemotherapy alone (hazard ratios 0.48 and 0.44 — relative measures), with objective response in 64% and 63% versus 36% (absolute rates). The lazertinib-containing arm required a mid-trial regimen change — lazertinib started only after carboplatin finished — because of haematologic toxicity, so that arm as finally delivered differs from the arm as started. Predominant harms were haematologic, EGFR- and MET-related toxicities, lower for haematologic events without lazertinib. This shelf is PARTIAL by design: it asks only the post-osimertinib question. The first-line amivantamab plus lazertinib question (MARIPOSA) is homed at pack #7239 and the EGFR exon 20 insertion question (PAPILLON) at pack #5184 — both cross-pointed in prose only, with no reports re-carded here.

cards.headline: MARIPOSA-2 primary report (Passaro 2024): after osimertinib, amivantamab–chemotherapy PFS 6.3 months and amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy 8.3 months vs 4.2 on chemotherapy (HR 0.48 and 0.44, relative); response 64%/63% vs 36%
cards.summary: MARIPOSA-2 primary report (Passaro 2024): after osimertinib, amivantamab–chemotherapy PFS 6.3 months and amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy 8.3 months vs 4.2 on chemotherapy (HR 0.48 and 0.44, relative); response 64%/63% vs 36%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (MARIPOSA-2), amivantamab ± lazertinib + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy after osimertinib progression
cards.people: 657 patients with EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after progression on osimertinib, randomised 2:2:1 to amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy, chemotherapy alone, or amivantamab–chemotherapy (carboplatin–pemetrexed backbone).
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer for both amivantamab arms versus chemotherapy: median 6.3 months for amivantamab–chemotherapy (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.48 — a relative measure; P<0.001) and 8.3 months for amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy (HR 0.44, relative; P<0.001), versus 4.2 months on chemotherapy. Objective response was 64% and 63% versus 36% (absolute rates; P<0.001 for both). Median intracranial PFS was 12.5 and 12.8 versus 8.3 months (HR 0.55 and 0.58, relative). During the study, haematologic toxicities in the lazertinib arm necessitated a regimen change to start lazertinib after carboplatin completion. Predominant adverse events in the amivantamab regimens were haematologic, EGFR- and MET-related toxicities, with lower haematologic rates for amivantamab–chemotherapy than for the lazertinib combination.
cards.watchOut: One trial, and the lazertinib arm changed mid-trial (lazertinib deferred until after carboplatin) — its 8.3-month PFS mixes two versions of the regimen, and longer follow-up of the modified regimen was still needed at this report. No overall-survival result is reported in this record.

cards.headline: Patient-relevant outcomes report (Tomasini 2026): quality of life was not compromised by adding amivantamab to chemotherapy, and time to symptomatic progression was prolonged (HR 0.73, relative) — a report of the same MARIPOSA-2 trial
cards.summary: Patient-relevant outcomes report (Tomasini 2026): quality of life was not compromised by adding amivantamab to chemotherapy, and time to symptomatic progression was prolonged (HR 0.73, relative) — a report of the same MARIPOSA-2 trial
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcomes report of the MARIPOSA-2 trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: Patients in the amivantamab–chemotherapy (n=131) and chemotherapy-alone (n=263) arms of MARIPOSA-2, assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30, PROMIS Physical Function Short Form 8c and the NSCLC Symptom Assessment Questionnaire.
cards.result: Patient-reported outcome scores were stable over time with little or no between-group difference in least-squares mean change from baseline. At 6 months, 55.1% of patients on amivantamab–chemotherapy reported improved or stable global health status/quality-of-life scores versus 29.1% on chemotherapy alone. Time to symptomatic progression was prolonged with amivantamab–chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.96 — a relative measure; nominal P=0.0259). The authors concluded the clinical benefit was achieved without compromising health-related quality of life.
cards.watchOut: Covers only two of the three trial arms, the symptomatic-progression P value is nominal, and 'stable quality of life' in a trial where the control arm progresses sooner partly reflects the efficacy difference itself.
cards.source: Tomasini P et al. Patient-Relevant Outcomes From the Phase III MARIPOSA-2 Trial: Amivantamab-Chemotherapy Versus Chemotherapy in EGFR-Mutant Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Following Disease Progression on Osimertinib. cards.headline: Asian-subgroup analysis (Shih 2026): amivantamab–chemotherapy PFS 6.8 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.54, relative) and response 66% vs 32% in 190 Asian participants — a subgroup report of the same MARIPOSA-2 trial
cards.summary: Asian-subgroup analysis (Shih 2026): amivantamab–chemotherapy PFS 6.8 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.54, relative) and response 66% vs 32% in 190 Asian participants — a subgroup report of the same MARIPOSA-2 trial
cards.type: Post hoc Asian-subgroup analysis of the MARIPOSA-2 trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 190 Asian participants in MARIPOSA-2: 63 in the amivantamab–chemotherapy group and 127 in the chemotherapy group (the lazertinib arm is not reported here because its dosing-schedule follow-up is ongoing); median follow-up 9.5 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 6.8 months on amivantamab–chemotherapy versus 4.2 months on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.81 — a relative measure; nominal P=0.002). Objective response was 66% versus 32% (absolute rates) and median intracranial PFS 12.5 versus 8.5 months (HR 0.58, relative; nominal P=0.049). The safety profile was in line with the overall MARIPOSA-2 population.
cards.watchOut: A post hoc regional subgroup with nominal P values and short follow-up: it shows consistency with the primary result, nothing more, and it omits the lazertinib arm entirely.
cards.source: Shih JY et al. Amivantamab plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on osimertinib: a MARIPOSA-2 analysis of the Asian subgroup. Translational lung cancer research. 2026. PMID: 42870814. Registry ID: NCT04988295. MeSH: none in the record

cards.headline: Synthesis: PARTIAL shelf — one trial (MARIPOSA-2, n=657) answers the post-osimertinib question with a clear PFS and response gain for amivantamab plus chemotherapy, at haematologic and EGFR/MET toxicity cost; the first-line question lives at pack #7239

cards.result: MARIPOSA-2 randomised 657 patients after osimertinib progression: amivantamab–chemotherapy gave median PFS 6.3 months and amivantamab–lazertinib–chemotherapy 8.3 months versus 4.2 months on chemotherapy (HR 0.48 and 0.44, relative), response 64%/63% versus 36%, with quality of life maintained and symptomatic progression delayed (HR 0.73, relative) in the outcomes report, and consistent results in the Asian subgroup. All three cards are reports of this single trial. The lazertinib arm's mid-trial regimen change and the absence of a survival result in these records bound the claim. This shelf deliberately covers only the post-osimertinib slice: first-line amivantamab plus lazertinib (MARIPOSA) is pack #7239 and amivantamab in EGFR exon 20 insertion disease (PAPILLON) is pack #5184 — cross-pointed in prose, not re-carded.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Furmonertinib vs gefitinib first-line in EGFR NSCLC (FURLONG, one China trial): PFS 20.8 vs 11.1 months; CNS PFS 20.8 vs 9.8 months — no osimertinib comparison exists
shelves.question: In Chinese patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) NSCLC, does the third-generation EGFR inhibitor furmonertinib (80 mg/day), versus gefitinib, prolong progression-free survival, including in the central nervous system?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Gefitinib · Lung Neoplasms · ErbB Receptors · Quinazolines · Disease-Free Survival · China · Mutation · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Tyrosine · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Double-Blind Method · Indoles · Pyridines · Pyrimidines
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme evidence: one phase 3 trial (FURLONG, n=358, China) reported across a primary report, a CNS efficacy report and a patient-reported-outcomes report — reports of one trial, not three trials. Furmonertinib beat gefitinib on progression-free survival (median 20.8 vs 11.1 months; hazard ratio 0.44, a relative measure), with a strong CNS slice (CNS PFS 20.8 vs 9.8 months; HR 0.40, relative) and fewer grade 3 or higher treatment-related events (11% vs 18%). The comparator is gefitinib, a first-generation agent: the shelf answers 'furmonertinib versus gefitinib in China', not 'furmonertinib versus osimertinib' — no such head-to-head exists. Furmonertinib is approved in China and is not FDA/EMA-approved; that status is stated plainly. There is likewise no head-to-head against aumolertinib (the parallel third-generation agent on shelf #7302) — cross-trial PFS comparisons are not evidence of superiority, and the two shelves cross-point each other in prose only.

cards.headline: FURLONG phase 3 primary report (Shi 2022): furmonertinib beat gefitinib first-line — median PFS 20.8 vs 11.1 months (HR 0.44, relative); grade ≥3 treatment-related events 11% vs 18%
cards.summary: FURLONG phase 3 primary report (Shi 2022): furmonertinib beat gefitinib first-line — median PFS 20.8 vs 11.1 months (HR 0.44, relative); grade ≥3 treatment-related events 11% vs 18%
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre double-blind randomised trial (FURLONG, China), furmonertinib vs gefitinib, first-line
cards.people: 358 Chinese patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR mutation-positive (exon 19 deletion or L858R) NSCLC at 55 hospitals in mainland China, randomised to furmonertinib 80 mg/day (n=178) or gefitinib 250 mg/day (n=180); 357 were treated and analysed; median follow-up 21.0 months in both groups.
cards.result: Median independent-review progression-free survival was 20.8 months (95% CI 17.8 to 23.5) on furmonertinib versus 11.1 months (9.7 to 12.5) on gefitinib (hazard ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.58 — a relative measure; P<0.0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or more occurred in 11% (20 of 178) on furmonertinib versus 18% (32 of 179) on gefitinib; treatment-related serious events in 6% in both groups. Ten patients (6%) on furmonertinib and 3 (2%) on gefitinib died due to adverse events, all judged possibly unrelated to study treatment by the investigators.
cards.watchOut: Single trial, single country, first-generation comparator: overall survival was still in follow-up at this report, and the result cannot be read as a comparison against osimertinib, the third-generation standard elsewhere.
cards.source: Shi Y et al. Furmonertinib (AST2818) versus gefitinib as first-line therapy for Chinese patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR mutation-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (FURLONG): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised phase 3 study. The Lancet. Respiratory medicine. 2022. PMID: 35662408. Registry ID: NCT03787992. cards.headline: FURLONG CNS efficacy report (Shi 2022): in 133 patients with CNS lesions, CNS PFS 20.8 vs 9.8 months (HR 0.40, relative); in 60 with measurable CNS lesions, CNS response 91% vs 65% — a preplanned subgroup report of the same trial
cards.summary: FURLONG CNS efficacy report (Shi 2022): in 133 patients with CNS lesions, CNS PFS 20.8 vs 9.8 months (HR 0.40, relative); in 60 with measurable CNS lesions, CNS response 91% vs 65% — a preplanned subgroup report of the same trial
cards.type: Preplanned CNS subgroup analysis of the FURLONG trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The preplanned CNS subgroup of FURLONG (all patients had brain imaging at screening): 133 patients (37%) with measurable or non-measurable CNS lesions, of whom 60 (17%) had measurable CNS lesions; all had asymptomatic, stable CNS metastases at baseline.
cards.result: CNS progression-free survival was 20.8 months (95% CI 15.2 to 25.3) on furmonertinib versus 9.8 months (7.2 to 18.0) on gefitinib (hazard ratio 0.40, 95% CI 0.23 to 0.71 — a relative measure; P=0.0011). In patients with measurable CNS lesions, CNS objective response was 91% (95% CI 72 to 99) versus 65% (48 to 80) (absolute rates), and least-squares mean CNS depth of response was 62% versus 39% (mean difference 23 percentage points; P=0.0011).
cards.watchOut: A subgroup of the same trial with small measurable-lesion denominators: the 91% CNS response rate rests on roughly 30 patients per arm and should be read as supportive, not standalone, evidence.
cards.source: Shi Y et al. Central Nervous System Efficacy of Furmonertinib (AST2818) Versus Gefitinib as First-Line Treatment for EGFR-Mutated NSCLC: Results From the FURLONG Study. Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer. 2022. PMID: 35932953. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: FURLONG patient-reported outcomes (Shi 2024): score differences favoured furmonertinib on several scales but none reached the 10-point clinical-relevance threshold; time to deterioration was longer on furmonertinib — a report of the same trial
cards.summary: FURLONG patient-reported outcomes (Shi 2024): score differences favoured furmonertinib on several scales but none reached the 10-point clinical-relevance threshold; time to deterioration was longer on furmonertinib — a report of the same trial
cards.type: Prespecified patient-reported-outcomes report of the FURLONG trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 357 treated FURLONG patients (furmonertinib n=178, gefitinib n=179), all completing at least one assessment with the EORTC QLQ-C30 and lung-cancer module QLQ-LC13; a between-group difference of 10 points or more was predefined as clinically relevant.
cards.result: Overall score changes from baseline statistically favoured furmonertinib for physical functioning (difference 2.14 points), nausea/vomiting (−1.56), appetite loss (−2.24), diarrhoea (−3.36), alopecia (−2.62) and pain in other parts (−4.55), but none reached clinical relevance. Time to deterioration was longer with furmonertinib for physical functioning (hazard ratio 0.63 — a relative measure), diarrhoea (HR 0.63, relative), dyspnoea (HR 0.72, relative), cough (HR 0.67, relative) and dysphagia (HR 0.54, relative), among other scales.
cards.watchOut: Statistically significant but clinically small score differences: by the study's own 10-point threshold, patients would not feel most of these differences; the time-to-deterioration pattern is the more meaningful signal.
cards.source: Shi Y et al. Patient-reported outcomes for the phase 3 FURLONG study of furmonertinib versus gefitinib as first-line therapy for Chinese patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer. The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific. 2024. PMID: 38993541. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: none in the record

shelves.title: Aumolertinib vs gefitinib first-line in EGFR NSCLC (AENEAS, one China trial): PFS 19.3 vs 9.9 months, CNS PFS 29.0 vs 8.3 months — the gain is durability, not response rate
shelves.question: In Chinese patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) NSCLC, does the third-generation EGFR inhibitor aumolertinib (110 mg/day), versus gefitinib, prolong progression-free survival, including in the central nervous system?
shelves.mesh: Acrylamides · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Disease-Free Survival · ErbB Receptors · Exons · Gefitinib · Humans · Indoles · Lung Neoplasms · Mutation · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Pyrimidines · Quinazolines · Small Cell Lung Carcinoma
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single-programme comparative evidence: one phase 3 trial (AENEAS, n=429, China) reported across a primary report and a CNS efficacy report — reports of one trial, not two trials. Aumolertinib beat gefitinib on progression-free survival (median 19.3 vs 9.9 months; hazard ratio 0.46, a relative measure) through durability rather than response (objective response 73.8% vs 72.1%, absolute rates; median duration of response 18.1 vs 8.3 months), with a strong CNS slice (CNS PFS 29.0 vs 8.3 months; HR 0.31, relative) and less rash (23.4% vs 41.4%) and diarrhoea (16.4% vs 35.8%) at similar grade 3 or higher event rates (36.4% vs 35.8%). A third carded report is a small single-arm real-world study (n=33) — it is NOT an AENEAS report (the commissioning row described it as one; the fetched record shows a real-world cohort), and it carries no comparative weight. The comparator is gefitinib, a first-generation agent: the shelf answers 'aumolertinib versus gefitinib in China', not 'aumolertinib versus osimertinib'. Aumolertinib (formerly almonertinib, HS-10296) is approved in China only and is not FDA/EMA-approved. There is no head-to-head against furmonertinib (shelf #7301) — cross-trial PFS comparisons are not evidence of superiority. The separate stage III programme (ADVANCE) is a different setting, cross-pointed in prose only and not carded.

cards.headline: AENEAS phase 3 primary report (Lu 2022): aumolertinib beat gefitinib first-line — median PFS 19.3 vs 9.9 months (HR 0.46, relative) with near-identical response rates (73.8% vs 72.1%): the gain is durability (response duration 18.1 vs 8.3 months)
cards.summary: AENEAS phase 3 primary report (Lu 2022): aumolertinib beat gefitinib first-line — median PFS 19.3 vs 9.9 months (HR 0.46, relative) with near-identical response rates (73.8% vs 72.1%): the gain is durability (response duration 18.1 vs 8.3 months)
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind randomised trial (AENEAS, China), aumolertinib vs gefitinib, first-line
cards.people: 429 treatment-naive patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) NSCLC at 53 sites in China, randomised 1:1 to aumolertinib 110 mg or gefitinib 250 mg once daily in a double-blind trial.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer on aumolertinib (hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.60 — a relative measure; P<0.0001): median 19.3 months (95% CI 17.8 to 20.8) versus 9.9 months (8.3 to 12.6). Objective response rate was 73.8% versus 72.1% and disease control rate 93.0% versus 96.7% (absolute rates), but median duration of response was 18.1 versus 8.3 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events (any cause) occurred in 36.4% versus 35.8%; rash occurred in 23.4% versus 41.4% and diarrhoea in 16.4% versus 35.8%.
cards.watchOut: Single trial, single country, first-generation comparator, investigator-assessed primary endpoint: no overall-survival verdict is reported in this record, and nothing here compares aumolertinib with osimertinib.
cards.source: Lu S et al. cards.headline: AENEAS CNS efficacy report (Lu 2024): in 106 patients with baseline CNS metastases, CNS PFS 29.0 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.31, relative); CNS response 85.7% vs 75.0% in 60 patients with target lesions — a subgroup report of the same trial
cards.summary: AENEAS CNS efficacy report (Lu 2024): in 106 patients with baseline CNS metastases, CNS PFS 29.0 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.31, relative); CNS response 85.7% vs 75.0% in 60 patients with target lesions — a subgroup report of the same trial
cards.type: CNS subgroup analysis of the AENEAS trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The CNS analysis set of AENEAS: 106 of the 429 randomised patients had CNS metastases at baseline by blinded neuroradiological review, and 60 of them had CNS target lesions; all had asymptomatic, stable CNS disease.
cards.result: Median CNS progression-free survival was 29.0 months on aumolertinib versus 8.3 months on gefitinib in the full CNS set (hazard ratio 0.31, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.56 — a relative measure; P<0.001) and likewise 29.0 versus 8.3 months in the target-lesion set (HR 0.26, relative; P<0.001). Confirmed CNS objective response in the target-lesion set was 85.7% versus 75.0% (absolute rates). Competing-risk analysis showed a consistently lower probability of CNS progression on aumolertinib in patients with and without baseline CNS metastases. No new safety findings were observed.
cards.watchOut: A subgroup analysis (106 and 60 patients) of the same trial: the very large CNS hazard-ratio advantage rests on few events and wide uncertainty in absolute terms, and supports rather than extends the primary verdict.
cards.source: Lu S et al. Central nervous system efficacy of aumolertinib versus gefitinib in patients with untreated, EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small cell lung cancer: data from a randomized phase III trial (AENEAS). Cancer communications (London, England). 2024. PMID: 39016053. Registry ID: NCT03849768. cards.headline: Real-world study (Li 2024): in 33 patients given first-line aumolertinib outside a trial, response was 65.2% among 23 with efficacy data and symptom scores improved — a small single-arm cohort, NOT an AENEAS report, and not load-bearing
cards.summary: Real-world study (Li 2024): in 33 patients given first-line aumolertinib outside a trial, response was 65.2% among 23 with efficacy data and symptom scores improved — a small single-arm cohort, NOT an AENEAS report, and not load-bearing
cards.type: Single-arm real-world cohort study of first-line aumolertinib (not a trial report and not part of AENEAS)
cards.people: 33 patients with advanced EGFR-sensitising-mutation NSCLC receiving aumolertinib as initial therapy in routine practice, 23 of whom had efficacy information by January 2024; median follow-up 264 days. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13.
cards.result: Objective response rate was 65.2% and disease control rate 91.3% among the 23 patients with efficacy data (absolute rates, single-arm). Functional scales on the QLQ-C30 rose and symptom scales fell during treatment; on the lung-cancer module, improvements in cough, sore mouth or tongue, tingling in hands or feet, chest pain, arm or shoulder pain and pain at other sites were clinically and statistically significant after 6 months (P<0.05).
cards.watchOut: Only 33 patients, 23 with efficacy data, no comparator, and PRO improvement without a control arm cannot be separated from natural history and expectation effects — this card is context only; the shelf stands on AENEAS alone.
cards.source: Li H et al. Efficacy and patient-reported outcomes in advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients receiving aumolertinib as first-line therapy: a real-world study. Frontiers in pharmacology. 2024. PMID: 39323634. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: none in the record
