cards.headline: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports of one trial — a significant radiographic-PFS benefit (33.2 vs 25.7 months; relative hazard ratio 0.81), survival not significant at the confirmatory primary read and only nominally favourable in a later descriptive update, at a high common-toxicity price
cards.summary: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports of one trial — a significant radiographic-PFS benefit (33.2 vs 25.7 months; relative hazard ratio 0.81), survival not significant at the confirmatory primary read and only nominally favourable in a later descriptive update, at a high common-toxicity price
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: CAPItello-281 only — 1,012 randomised patients with PTEN-deficient tumours, from 6,003 screened with valid tests (25.3% PTEN-deficient).
cards.result: There is no second trial and no third report. The primary report establishes a radiographic progression-free-survival benefit for adding capivasertib to abiraterone (with prednisone/prednisolone and ADT) in PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. It does not establish a survival benefit: interim overall survival hazard ratio 0.90 was not significant, and the later ad hoc descriptive update (hazard ratio 0.82, nominal P=0.044, medians 57.4 vs 46.5 months) is not prespecified or alpha-controlled. Harms are frequent: diarrhoea 51.9%, hyperglycaemia 38.0%, rash 35.4%, and adverse-event-associated deaths 7.2% versus 5.2%. Cross-point only, in prose: pack #6403 asks capivasertib plus fulvestrant in breast cancer (CAPItello-291) — a different disease and question, not carded here.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK: if either of the 2 reports had failed to verify, this shelf would not have been built. A prespecified final overall-survival analysis would be a third report and could change the stamp.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Durvalumab ± olaparib maintenance in endometrial cancer (DUO-E, PARTIAL): PFS hazard ratios 0.71 and 0.55 — olaparib's increment is mainly in pMMR disease
shelves.question: In patients with newly diagnosed advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, does carboplatin–paclitaxel plus durvalumab followed by maintenance durvalumab — with or without olaparib — versus carboplatin–paclitaxel alone, prolong progression-free survival, overall and within mismatch-repair-deficient and -proficient disease?
shelves.mesh: Female · Humans · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Antineoplastic Agents · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Carboplatin · Endometrial Neoplasms · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Paclitaxel · Phthalazines · Piperazines · Poly(ADP-ribose) Polymerase Inhibitors · Double-Blind Method
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival) — PARTIAL shelf, one trial (DUO-E, 718 randomised) in three reports. Carboplatin/paclitaxel plus durvalumab followed by durvalumab maintenance gave a progression-free-survival hazard ratio of 0.71 versus chemotherapy alone, and adding olaparib to the maintenance gave 0.55 (both relative). The two comparisons are kept separate throughout: in dMMR disease the reads were 0.42 and 0.41 (olaparib adds little), in pMMR disease 0.77 and 0.57 (the olaparib increment is principally a pMMR story). Overall survival was interim at about 28% maturity — not significant for durvalumab alone (0.77, relative) — and is not claimed as established. The RUBY/GY018 question is homed at live #853 and is cross-pointed only.

cards.headline: DUO-E primary report (Westin 2024): durvalumab maintenance improved PFS (relative hazard ratio 0.71), and durvalumab + olaparib maintenance improved it more (0.55) — the olaparib increment is principally a pMMR story (pMMR 0.57 vs dMMR reads 0.42 and 0.41)
cards.summary: DUO-E primary report (Westin 2024): durvalumab maintenance improved PFS (relative hazard ratio 0.71), and durvalumab + olaparib maintenance improved it more (0.55) — the olaparib increment is principally a pMMR story (pMMR 0.57 vs dMMR reads 0.42 and 0.41)
cards.type: Phase 3 global double-blind placebo-controlled trial (DUO-E), three arms — primary report
cards.people: 718 patients with newly diagnosed advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, randomised 1:1:1 to carboplatin/paclitaxel plus durvalumab placebo then placebo maintenance (control); carboplatin/paclitaxel plus durvalumab then maintenance durvalumab plus olaparib placebo (durvalumab arm); or carboplatin/paclitaxel plus durvalumab then maintenance durvalumab plus olaparib (durvalumab + olaparib arm).
cards.result: Progression-free survival hazard ratios versus control were 0.71 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.89; P=.003) for the durvalumab arm and 0.55 (0.43 to 0.69; P<.0001) for the durvalumab + olaparib arm — both relative measures; the primary report's abstract gives no absolute median PFS rates, so none are printed here. Prespecified exploratory subgroups: mismatch-repair-deficient (dMMR) hazard ratios 0.42 (durvalumab) and 0.41 (durvalumab + olaparib); mismatch-repair-proficient (pMMR) hazard ratios 0.77 and 0.57 — all relative. Interim overall survival at about 28% maturity: hazard ratio 0.77 (durvalumab; P=.120, NOT significant) and 0.59 (durvalumab + olaparib; P=.003) — both relative and immature. Safety profiles were generally consistent with the individual agents.
cards.watchOut: An erratum exists against this primary report (PMID 39121439); its PubMed record carries no abstract text, so no corrected figure could be taken from it this session — every number on this card is from the primary report's fetched record and should be re-checked against the erratum at full-text review. Overall survival was interim at ~28% maturity: do not read it as established. PARTIAL shelf: live #853 homes RUBY and NRG GY018 (dostarlimab / pembrolizumab) — cross-pointed in prose only, never re-carded here.

cards.headline: DUO-E Japan subset (Nishio 2025): 88 Japanese patients — PFS hazard ratios 0.61 (durvalumab) and 0.44 (durvalumab + olaparib), relative, consistent with the overall population; median PFS 9.9 and 15.1 vs 9.5 months
cards.summary: DUO-E Japan subset (Nishio 2025): 88 Japanese patients — PFS hazard ratios 0.61 (durvalumab) and 0.44 (durvalumab + olaparib), relative, consistent with the overall population; median PFS 9.9 and 15.1 vs 9.5 months
cards.type: Prespecified exploratory Japan-subset report of the DUO-E trial (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 88 patients in the Japan subset of DUO-E, randomised 1:1:1 to the same three arms (durvalumab 1,120 mg every 3 weeks with chemotherapy, then 1,500 mg every 4 weeks maintenance, with olaparib 300 mg twice daily in the combination arm). This was a prespecified exploratory subset analysis.
cards.result: Progression-free survival favoured durvalumab (hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.32 to 1.12) and durvalumab + olaparib (0.44, 0.22 to 0.85) versus control — relative measures; median PFS was 9.9 and 15.1 versus 9.5 months, and 18-month PFS rates were 37.0% and 42.1% versus 22.2%. The safety profile in the Japan subset was generally consistent with the full safety set.
cards.watchOut: A subset of 88 patients: its confidence intervals are wide (the durvalumab-only interval crosses 1) and it adds consistency, not independent confirmation.

cards.headline: DUO-E pMMR biomarker/histology analysis (Westin 2026, exploratory): in mismatch-repair-proficient disease, PFS favoured the durvalumab + olaparib arm across most biomarker and histology subgroups
cards.summary: DUO-E pMMR biomarker/histology analysis (Westin 2026, exploratory): in mismatch-repair-proficient disease, PFS favoured the durvalumab + olaparib arm across most biomarker and histology subgroups
cards.type: Exploratory biomarker and histology analysis of the pMMR subpopulation of DUO-E (same trial — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The mismatch-repair-proficient (pMMR) subpopulation of DUO-E: biomarkers were evaluable in 486 of 575 pMMR patients; 84% (407) were positive for at least one biomarker, most prevalently PD-L1 positive (67%) and TP53-mutated (59%); histology in the biomarker-known subpopulation was 52% endometrioid and 27% serous.
cards.result: In exploratory analyses, progression-free-survival hazard ratios were improved versus control for both treatment arms across multiple biomarker and histology subgroups, and favoured the durvalumab + olaparib arm in the majority of assessed subgroups. The pMMR subpopulation was highly heterogeneous, with frequent overlap of biomarkers and histology. The report's abstract gives no subgroup hazard-ratio values, so none are printed here.
cards.watchOut: Exploratory and hypothesis-generating only: it supports, but cannot prove, the reading that the olaparib increment belongs principally to pMMR disease. It must not be generalised to dMMR disease, where the durvalumab-only and combination hazard ratios in the primary report were nearly identical (0.42 and 0.41).
cards.source: Westin SN et al. Biomarker heterogeneity and efficacy of durvalumab plus carboplatin/paclitaxel followed by durvalumab with or without olaparib in patients with mismatch repair proficient endometrial cancer: exploratory analyses of the DUO-E/GOG-3041/ENGOT-EN10 trial. shelves.title: Encorafenib + binimetinib in BRAF V600 melanoma (COLUMBUS): PFS 14.9 vs 7.3 months vs vemurafenib, durable to 7 years — no head-to-head vs dabrafenib + trametinib
shelves.question: In patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma, treatment-naïve or progressed after first-line immunotherapy, does encorafenib 450 mg daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily, versus vemurafenib (or encorafenib alone), prolong progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Benzimidazoles · Biomarkers, Tumor · Carbamates · Female · Humans · Male · Melanoma · Middle Aged · Molecular Targeted Therapy · Mutation · Progression-Free Survival · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Proto-Oncogene Proteins B-raf · Skin Neoplasms · Sulfonamides · Time Factors · Vemurafenib · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — single programme (COLUMBUS, one trial in three reports, 577 randomised). Encorafenib 450 mg daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily beat vemurafenib on progression-free survival (median 14.9 vs 7.3 months; hazard ratio 0.54, relative) and the advantage persisted: 5-year PFS/OS 23%/35% vs 10%/21% and 7-year 21.2%/27.4% vs 6.4%/18.2% (absolute rates). The comparator frame is dated — vemurafenib monotherapy is no longer a standard, and there is no head-to-head against dabrafenib + trametinib; cross-trial comparison is not evidence and is not made here.

cards.headline: COLUMBUS part 1 primary report (Dummer 2018): encorafenib + binimetinib doubled median PFS versus vemurafenib — 14.9 vs 7.3 months, hazard ratio 0.54 (relative)
cards.summary: COLUMBUS part 1 primary report (Dummer 2018): encorafenib + binimetinib doubled median PFS versus vemurafenib — 14.9 vs 7.3 months, hazard ratio 0.54 (relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised trial (COLUMBUS part 1) — primary report
cards.people: 577 patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma (stage IIIB, IIIC or IV, ECOG 0–1), treatment-naïve or progressed after first-line immunotherapy, randomised 1:1:1 at 162 hospitals in 28 countries: encorafenib 450 mg daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily (192), encorafenib 300 mg daily alone (194), or vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily (191).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by blinded central review was 14.9 months (95% CI 11.0 to 18.5) with the combination versus 7.3 months (5.6 to 8.2) with vemurafenib — hazard ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.41 to 0.71; P<0.0001), a relative measure beside the absolute medians. The commonest grade 3–4 events with the combination were increased gamma-glutamyltransferase (9%), increased creatine phosphokinase (7%) and hypertension (6%). One death in the combination group was considered possibly treatment-related; there were no other treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is vemurafenib monotherapy, a first-generation benchmark that is no longer a standard: this trial does not compare encorafenib + binimetinib with dabrafenib + trametinib, and no such head-to-head exists. Open-label, though the primary endpoint was centrally reviewed blinded.
cards.source: Dummer R et al. Encorafenib plus binimetinib versus vemurafenib or encorafenib in patients with BRAF-mutant melanoma (COLUMBUS): a multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2018. PMID: 29573941. Registry ID: NCT01909453. phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised trial (columbus part 1) — primary report 577 patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic braf v600e/k-mutant melanoma (stage iiib, iiic or iv, ecog 0–1), treatment-naïve or progressed after first-line immunotherapy, randomised 1:1:1 at 162 hospitals in 28 countries: encorafenib 450 mg daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily (192), encorafenib 300 mg daily alone (194), or vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily (191). median progression-free survival by blinded central review was 14.9 months (95% ci 11.0 to 18.5) with the combination versus 7.3 months (5.6 to 8.2) with vemurafenib — hazard ratio 0.54 (95% ci 0.41 to 0.71; p<0.0001), a relative measure beside the absolute medians. the commonest grade 3–4 events with the combination were increased gamma-glutamyltransferase (9%), increased creatine phosphokinase (7%) and hypertension (6%). one death in the combination group was considered possibly treatment-related; there were no other treatment-related deaths. the comparator is vemurafenib monotherapy, a first-generation benchmark that is no longer a standard: this trial does not compare encorafenib + binimetinib with dabrafenib + trametinib, and no such head-to-head exists. open-label, though the primary endpoint was centrally reviewed blinded. dummer r et al. encorafenib plus binimetinib versus vemurafenib or encorafenib in patients with braf-mutant melanoma (columbus): a multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. the lancet. oncology. 2018. pmid: 29573941. registry id: nct01909453. mesh: adult · aged · aged, 80 and over · antineoplastic combined chemotherapy protocols · benzimidazoles · biomarkers, tumor · carbamates · female · humans · male · melanoma · middle aged · molecular targeted therapy · mutation · progression-free survival · protein kinase inhibitors · proto-oncogene proteins b-raf · skin neoplasms · sulfonamides · time factors · vemurafenib · young adult

cards.headline: COLUMBUS 5-year update (Dummer 2022): 5-year PFS 23% and overall survival 35% with encorafenib + binimetinib versus 10% and 21% with vemurafenib (absolute rates); median duration of response 18.6 vs 12.3 months
cards.summary: COLUMBUS 5-year update (Dummer 2022): 5-year PFS 23% and overall survival 35% with encorafenib + binimetinib versus 10% and 21% with vemurafenib (absolute rates); median duration of response 18.6 vs 12.3 months
cards.type: 5-year update of the COLUMBUS trial (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 577 randomised patients (192 combination, 191 vemurafenib, 194 encorafenib alone), in an updated analysis 65 months after the last patient was randomised.
cards.result: Five-year progression-free survival and overall survival with encorafenib plus binimetinib were 23% and 35% overall (31% and 45% in patients with normal lactate dehydrogenase), versus 10% and 21% with vemurafenib (12% and 28% with normal lactate dehydrogenase) — absolute rates, printed in pairs. Median duration of response was 18.6 months with the combination versus 12.3 months with vemurafenib, and disease control was achieved in 92.2% versus 81.2%. No new safety concerns emerged.
cards.watchOut: Long-term rates are descriptive follow-up of the same randomised comparison against the same dated vemurafenib benchmark; they do not create a comparison with any modern combination.
cards.source: Dummer R et al. cards.headline: COLUMBUS 7-year update (Schadendorf 2024): 7-year PFS 21.2% and overall survival 27.4% with the combination versus 6.4% and 18.2% with vemurafenib; median melanoma-specific survival 36.8 vs 19.3 months
cards.summary: COLUMBUS 7-year update (Schadendorf 2024): 7-year PFS 21.2% and overall survival 27.4% with the combination versus 6.4% and 18.2% with vemurafenib; median melanoma-specific survival 36.8 vs 19.3 months
cards.type: 7-year update of the COLUMBUS trial (same trial as the cards above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 577 randomised patients, at 99.7 months median duration between randomisation and data cut-off — the longest follow-up from a phase 3 BRAF/MEK combination trial in this disease, per the report.
cards.result: Seven-year progression-free survival and overall survival were 21.2% and 27.4% in the encorafenib plus binimetinib arm versus 6.4% and 18.2% in the vemurafenib arm (absolute rates). Median melanoma-specific survival was 36.8 months (95% CI 27.7 to 51.5) versus 19.3 months (14.8 to 25.9). Thirty-four long-term responders (complete or partial response ongoing at 7 years) were identified across arms. Safety remained consistent with the known tolerability profile, with no new concerns.
cards.watchOut: By 7 years the surviving fractions are small and the comparison remains against vemurafenib alone. The 2026 COLUMBUS-AD adjuvant report is a different, adjuvant question and is deliberately NOT carded on this shelf (cross-point only).
cards.source: Schadendorf D et al. cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: COLUMBUS part 1 only — 577 randomised (192 combination, 194 encorafenib alone, 191 vemurafenib).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 14.9 versus 7.3 months (relative hazard ratio 0.54); 5-year progression-free survival and overall survival were 23% and 35% versus 10% and 21%, and at 7 years 21.2% and 27.4% versus 6.4% and 18.2% (absolute rates). cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence (one trial, three reports): the stamp rests on that one programme, against a dated comparator, stated plainly.

shelves.title: Pexidartinib in TGCT (ENLIVEN): response 39% vs 0% at 25 weeks, durable in open follow-up — mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity is the price
shelves.question: In adults with symptomatic, advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour for whom surgery is not recommended, does the CSF1-receptor inhibitor pexidartinib, versus placebo (blinded phase) and in long-term open treatment, produce tumour responses and durable benefit, and with what hepatotoxicity cost?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Agents · Double-Blind Method · Female · Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath · Humans · Intention to Treat Analysis · Male · Middle Aged · Protein Kinase Inhibitors · Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors · Survival Analysis · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, tumour response) — the randomised evidence is one 25-week blinded comparison in 120 patients with a rare tumour (N printed on the face): response 39% with pexidartinib versus 0% with placebo (absolute difference 39 percentage points). Long-term open-label follow-up (labelled as such, never as randomised evidence) shows responses of about 60% by RECIST with median duration not reached. The price is hepatotoxicity: mixed/cholestatic injury stopped ENLIVEN enrolment early, occurred in about 3% of pooled treated patients (reversible over 1–7 months), and AST/ALT reached ≥3× the upper limit of normal in 31% in the final report. Pain relief was modest and its primary definition was not met. Product: pexidartinib (Turalio, Daiichi Sankyo).

cards.headline: ENLIVEN primary report (Tap 2019): pexidartinib produced a week-25 tumour response in 39% versus 0% on placebo (absolute difference 39 percentage points) — and enrolment was stopped early for mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity
cards.summary: ENLIVEN primary report (Tap 2019): pexidartinib produced a week-25 tumour response in 39% versus 0% on placebo (absolute difference 39 percentage points) — and enrolment was stopped early for mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind randomised trial (ENLIVEN part 1), pexidartinib vs placebo — primary report
cards.people: 120 patients with symptomatic, advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour for whom surgery was not recommended, randomised 1:1 (61 pexidartinib, 59 placebo) in the double-blind part of ENLIVEN. Pexidartinib dosing was 1,000 mg/day for 2 weeks, then 800 mg/day for 22 weeks. The randomised N of 120 is printed on the face, as the row directs for this rare tumour.
cards.result: Overall response at week 25 by RECIST 1.1 (centrally reviewed) was 39% (24 of 61) with pexidartinib versus 0% (0 of 59) with placebo — an absolute difference of 39 percentage points (95% CI 27 to 53; P<0.0001). Serious adverse events occurred in 13% (8 of 61) versus 2% (1 of 59). Common pexidartinib events included hair colour changes (67%), fatigue (54%), aspartate aminotransferase increase (39%), nausea (38%), alanine aminotransferase increase (28%) and dysgeusia (25%). Three pexidartinib patients had aminotransferases ≥3× the upper limit of normal with bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase ≥2× the upper limit of normal — mixed or cholestatic hepatotoxicity — one lasting 7 months and biopsy-confirmed; emergence of this toxicity caused the data monitoring committee to stop enrolment six patients short of target.
cards.watchOut: Product naming (clarification exception, as the row directs): pexidartinib (Turalio, Daiichi Sankyo). The randomised comparison lasts 25 weeks only; everything after that is open-label and is labelled as such on the cards below. Hepatotoxicity is the defining harm and the reason for restricted distribution in the US.
cards.source: Tap WD et al. Pexidartinib versus placebo for advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour (ENLIVEN): a randomised phase 3 trial. Lancet (London, England). 2019. PMID: 31229240. Registry ID: NCT02371369. cards.headline: Pooled long-term analysis (Gelderblom 2021, open-label, NOT randomised evidence): 130 pexidartinib-treated patients — RECIST response 60%, tumour-volume-score response 65%; mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity in 4 patients (3%), all reversible over 1–7 months
cards.summary: Pooled long-term analysis (Gelderblom 2021, open-label, NOT randomised evidence): 130 pexidartinib-treated patients — RECIST response 60%, tumour-volume-score response 65%; mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity in 4 patients (3%), all reversible over 1–7 months
cards.type: Pooled long-term analysis of three pexidartinib-treated cohorts (phase 1 extension + ENLIVEN) — single-arm follow-up, no concurrent control
cards.people: 130 patients pooled from three pexidartinib-treated cohorts: a phase 1 extension study (39), ENLIVEN patients randomised to pexidartinib (61) and ENLIVEN crossover patients (30). Median treatment duration was 19 months; 54 patients (42%) remained on treatment at the analysis cut-off.
cards.result: Best overall response was 60% by RECIST and 65% by tumour volume score; median times to response were 3.4 and 2.8 months. Hair colour changes were the commonest treatment-emergent event (75%). Most liver abnormalities (92%) were aminotransferase elevations; 4 patients (3%) had mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity, all within the first 2 months of treatment and all reversible (recovery 1–7 months).
cards.watchOut: The pooled 60% response must never be presented as randomised evidence: there is no placebo group in this analysis, and responders who stay on treatment are over-represented in long-term pools.
cards.source: Gelderblom H et al. Long-term outcomes of pexidartinib in tenosynovial giant cell tumors. Cancer. 2021. PMID: 33197285. Registry ID: NCT01004861 and NCT02371369 (both named in the report). cards.headline: ENLIVEN final long-term report (Wagner 2025, open-label part 2): 91 patients ever treated with pexidartinib in ENLIVEN — response 60.4% by RECIST and 68.1% by tumour volume score at median follow-up 31.2 months; grade 3/4 AST increase 9% and ALT increase 10%
cards.summary: ENLIVEN final long-term report (Wagner 2025, open-label part 2): 91 patients ever treated with pexidartinib in ENLIVEN — response 60.4% by RECIST and 68.1% by tumour volume score at median follow-up 31.2 months; grade 3/4 AST increase 9% and ALT increase 10%
cards.type: Final long-term report of ENLIVEN parts 1 and 2 — open-label follow-up of the trial above, not a new randomised comparison
cards.people: 91 patients who received pexidartinib at any time during ENLIVEN (blinded part 1 plus open-label part 2, in which patients received 800 mg/day until progression, toxicity or study completion), followed for a median of 31.2 months (range 2–66).
cards.result: Overall response was 60.4% by RECIST and 68.1% by tumour volume score; median duration of response by RECIST was not reached. Patient-reported outcomes improved or were maintained. The commonest grade 3/4 treatment-emergent events were aspartate aminotransferase increase (9%), alanine aminotransferase increase (10%) and hypertension (8%); 28 patients (31%) had AST or ALT ≥3× the upper limit of normal and 17 (19%) had AST or ALT ≥5×. No new safety signals were observed with long-term treatment.
cards.watchOut: Long-term figures come from patients who tolerated and stayed on pexidartinib; they describe durability in that selected group, not the effect of starting the drug in an unselected patient.
cards.source: Wagner AJ et al. Long-term efficacy and safety of pexidartinib in patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumor: final results of the ENLIVEN study. The oncologist. 2025. PMID: 40613752. cards.type: Patient-reported pain analysis of the ENLIVEN randomised trial (same trial — a secondary-outcome report, not independent evidence)
cards.people: The 120 treated ENLIVEN patients (61 pexidartinib, 59 placebo; mean age 45 years, 59% female, tumours mostly in the knee [61%] and ankle [18%]). Pain was assessed as worst pain at the tumour site on an 11-point scale; pain data were complete for only 54% of the pexidartinib group and 59% of the placebo group.
cards.result: The primary pain-response definition (≥30% fall in weekly mean worst pain without a ≥30% rise in narcotic use) was not detected as different: 31% (19 of 61) versus 15% (9 of 59), one-sided P=0.03, which did not meet the prespecified one-sided threshold of P<0.025. Exploratory thresholds (≥50% fall; ≥2-point fall) favoured pexidartinib (26% vs 10% and 31% vs 14%). The least-squares mean change in worst pain was −2.5 with pexidartinib versus −0.3 with placebo (difference −2.2, 95% CI −3.0 to −1.4), just over the minimum clinically important difference, and pain improvement correlated with tumour shrinkage. The authors conclude the findings are insufficient to justify routine use of pexidartinib for pain relief alone.
cards.watchOut: Incomplete pain data (about half the patients) and a missed primary pain definition: the honest headline is a robust tumour response with, at most, modest pain relief — not a pain indication.
cards.source: Healey JH et al. Pexidartinib Provides Modest Pain Relief in Patients With Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor: Results From ENLIVEN. Clinical orthopaedics and related research. 2023. cards.headline: Synthesis: one randomised 25-week comparison (response 39% vs 0%) plus open-label long-term follow-up (response about 60% in treated cohorts) — tumour response is real and durable, pain relief is modest and unproven on its primary definition, and mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity is the pricing harm
cards.summary: Synthesis: one randomised 25-week comparison (response 39% vs 0%) plus open-label long-term follow-up (response about 60% in treated cohorts) — tumour response is real and durable, pain relief is modest and unproven on its primary definition, and mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity is the pricing harm
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: ENLIVEN (120 randomised) and its pooled/final long-term follow-up (130 pooled treated; 91 ever-treated in ENLIVEN).
cards.result: Pexidartinib is the first systemic therapy to show a robust tumour response in symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumour not amenable to surgery: 39% versus 0% at week 25 in the only randomised comparison, rising to about 60% by RECIST with longer open-label treatment, with median duration of response not reached in the final ENLIVEN report. Against that: mixed or cholestatic hepatotoxicity stopped ENLIVEN's enrolment early, occurred in about 3% in the pooled cohorts (all reversible over 1–7 months, all within the first 2 months), aminotransferases reached ≥3× the upper limit of normal in 31% in the final report, and the pain report's primary definition was not met.
cards.watchOut: The randomised evidence is one 25-week blinded comparison in 120 patients with a rare tumour; long-term percentages are open-label and selected, and are labelled as such throughout this shelf.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Zanidatamab ± tislelizumab in HER2+ gastroesophageal cancer (HERIZON-GEA-01, exactly 2 reports): PFS win for both arms, survival win only with tislelizumab so far
shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated, centrally confirmed HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, does the HER2×HER2 bispecific antibody zanidatamab plus chemotherapy — with or without the PD-1 inhibitor tislelizumab — versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy, prolong progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Young Adult · Adenocarcinoma · Antibodies, Bispecific · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents, Immunological · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Diarrhea · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Esophageal Neoplasms · Esophagogastric Junction · Follow-Up Studies · Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors · Incidence · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Progression-Free Survival · Stomach Neoplasms · Time Factors · Trastuzumab · Combined Antibody Therapeutics
shelves.balance: SPLIT — by arm, on a FLOOR-RISK base of exactly 2 reports (one phase 3 trial, HERIZON-GEA-01, 914 randomised, plus its 33-patient single-arm phase Ib/II predecessor). Both zanidatamab arms prolonged progression-free survival versus trastuzumab + chemotherapy (median 12.4 vs 8.1 months; hazard ratios 0.63 with tislelizumab and 0.65 without, both relative). Overall survival splits the arms: significant only for zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy (26.4 vs 19.2 months; hazard ratio 0.72, relative, P=0.004); zanidatamab + chemotherapy did NOT differ significantly at this interim analysis (hazard ratio 0.80, relative, P=0.06) — its claim is PFS only. Diarrhoea is the pricing harm (grade ≥3 in 24.8% / 20.0% / 12.9%).

cards.headline: HERIZON-GEA-01 primary report (Shitara 2026): BOTH zanidatamab arms improved PFS (median 12.4 vs 8.1 months; relative hazard ratios 0.63 and 0.65), but at this interim analysis ONLY the tislelizumab-containing arm improved overall survival (26.4 vs 19.2 months; relative hazard ratio 0.72, P=0.004) — the zanidatamab-without-tislelizumab arm did NOT (hazard ratio 0.80, P=0.06)
cards.summary: HERIZON-GEA-01 primary report (Shitara 2026): BOTH zanidatamab arms improved PFS (median 12.4 vs 8.1 months; relative hazard ratios 0.63 and 0.65), but at this interim analysis ONLY the tislelizumab-containing arm improved overall survival (26.4 vs 19.2 months; relative hazard ratio 0.72, P=0.004) — the zanidatamab-without-tislelizumab arm did NOT (hazard ratio 0.80, P=0.06)
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (HERIZON-GEA-01), three arms — primary report (report 1 of exactly 2 on this shelf)
cards.people: 914 patients with previously untreated, centrally confirmed HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, randomised 1:1:1 in an open-label phase 3 trial: zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy (302), zanidatamab + chemotherapy (304), or trastuzumab + chemotherapy (308). Median follow-up was 25.9 months.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was median 12.4 months in both zanidatamab arms versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab + chemotherapy — hazard ratios 0.63 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.78) for the tislelizumab-containing arm and 0.65 (0.52 to 0.81) for zanidatamab + chemotherapy, both relative measures, P<0.001 for both. Overall survival was longer only for the tislelizumab-containing arm: median 26.4 versus 19.2 months, hazard ratio 0.72 (0.57 to 0.90), relative, P=0.004. For zanidatamab + chemotherapy, overall survival did NOT differ significantly at this interim analysis (median 24.4 months; hazard ratio 0.80, 0.64 to 1.01; P=0.06), relative. The two arms' claims are kept separate on this shelf, exactly as the row directs.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: exactly 2 reports (this phase 3 report and its phase Ib/II predecessor below), stated on the face. Overall survival for the zanidatamab-only arm is an interim, non-significant read — further analyses are planned, and a later report could change that arm's claim.
cards.source: Shitara K et al. Zanidatamab with and without Tislelizumab in HER2-Positive Gastroesophageal Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2026. PMID: 42202319. Registry ID: NCT05152147. cards.headline: HERIZON-GEA-01 primary report — harm slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): grade ≥3 adverse events 83.3% / 73.8% / 74.5% across the three arms, with grade ≥3 diarrhoea in 24.8% / 20.0% / 12.9% — diarrhoea is the pricing harm
cards.summary: HERIZON-GEA-01 primary report — harm slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): grade ≥3 adverse events 83.3% / 73.8% / 74.5% across the three arms, with grade ≥3 diarrhoea in 24.8% / 20.0% / 12.9% — diarrhoea is the pricing harm
cards.type: Harm slice of the HERIZON-GEA-01 primary report above (same report, carded separately so the harm figures are not buried — it adds no independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 914 randomised patients as the card above (302 zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy; 304 zanidatamab + chemotherapy; 308 trastuzumab + chemotherapy).
cards.result: Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 83.3% of the zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy arm, 73.8% of the zanidatamab + chemotherapy arm and 74.5% of the trastuzumab + chemotherapy arm. Diarrhoea was the most common grade ≥3 event, in 24.8%, 20.0% and 12.9% of patients respectively — so the tislelizumab-containing arm, the only arm with a significant survival read, also carries the highest grade ≥3 event and diarrhoea rates.
cards.watchOut: Chemotherapy backbones contribute much of the grade ≥3 burden in all three arms; the comparison that matters is the increment — about 9 percentage points more grade ≥3 events and about 12 points more grade ≥3 diarrhoea with the tislelizumab-containing combination than with trastuzumab + chemotherapy.
cards.source: Shitara K et al. Zanidatamab with and without Tislelizumab in HER2-Positive Gastroesophageal Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2026. PMID: 42202319. Registry ID: NCT05152147. cards.headline: Phase Ib/II predecessor (Lee 2026, single-arm): zanidatamab + tislelizumab + CAPOX in 33 first-line patients — confirmed response 75.8%, median duration of response 23.3 months, PFS 16.7 months, overall survival 32.4 months; diarrhoea in 100% (grade ≥3 in 27.3%)
cards.summary: Phase Ib/II predecessor (Lee 2026, single-arm): zanidatamab + tislelizumab + CAPOX in 33 first-line patients — confirmed response 75.8%, median duration of response 23.3 months, PFS 16.7 months, overall survival 32.4 months; diarrhoea in 100% (grade ≥3 in 27.3%)
cards.type: Phase Ib/II single-arm combination study (the HERIZON programme's predecessor report — report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf; different design and size from the phase 3 trial)
cards.people: 33 adults with previously untreated, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, treated in two dose cohorts (19 and 14) with zanidatamab every 3 weeks plus tislelizumab 200 mg and CAPOX chemotherapy. No control group.
cards.result: Confirmed objective response was 75.8%; median duration of response, progression-free survival and overall survival were 23.3, 16.7 and 32.4 months — all uncontrolled, single-arm figures. Treatment-related adverse events included diarrhoea in 100% of patients (grade ≥3 in 27.3%), nausea in 63.6% and decreased appetite in 48.5%; grade ≥3 treatment-related events occurred in 66.7%.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm evidence in 33 patients: its response and survival figures have no comparator and must not be read alongside the phase 3 medians as if they were the same kind of number. Its role here is the programme's second report, as the row specifies.

cards.headline: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports — in the phase 3 trial both zanidatamab arms prolong progression-free survival, only the tislelizumab-containing arm has a significant survival read at this interim analysis, and diarrhoea is the common harm
cards.summary: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports — in the phase 3 trial both zanidatamab arms prolong progression-free survival, only the tislelizumab-containing arm has a significant survival read at this interim analysis, and diarrhoea is the common harm
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: HERIZON-GEA-01 (914 randomised) and its phase Ib/II predecessor (33 patients, single-arm).
cards.result: Progression-free survival: median 12.4 months in both zanidatamab arms versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab + chemotherapy (relative hazard ratios 0.63 and 0.65). Overall survival: significant only for zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemotherapy (median 26.4 vs 19.2 months; relative hazard ratio 0.72); zanidatamab + chemotherapy did not differ significantly (hazard ratio 0.80, P=0.06) at this interim analysis. Grade ≥3 diarrhoea ran 24.8% / 20.0% / 12.9% across the arms. Cross-point only, in prose: pack #6706 asks zanidatamab in previously treated HER2-positive biliary tract cancer, and pack #6707 asks zolbetuximab in HER2-negative CLDN18.2 disease — the complementary biomarker slice — neither re-carded here.

shelves.question: In patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC progressed after osimertinib and platinum-based chemotherapy, does subcutaneous amivantamab, versus intravenous amivantamab (both with lazertinib), achieve noninferior pharmacokinetics and response, and what does it change in infusion reactions, venous thromboembolism, administration time and patient experience?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, route and tolerability) — PARTIAL + FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one trial (PALOMA-3, 418 randomised). Subcutaneous amivantamab (with lazertinib) met pharmacokinetic noninferiority versus the intravenous route (trough ratio 1.15, cycle-2 AUC ratio 1.03 — relative ratios) with similar response (30% vs 33%) and median PFS 6.1 vs 4.3 months. Its advantages are practical: infusion-related reactions 13% vs 66%, venous thromboembolism 9% vs 14%, first administration 4.8 minutes vs 5 hours, cycle-1 time in chair 0.4 vs 6.5 hours, and better patient experience. The overall-survival difference (hazard ratio 0.62, relative, nominal P=0.02) was a predefined exploratory endpoint, not powered or alpha-controlled — a route change is not a plausible sole cause of such a gap, and no survival claim is made. Amivantamab's efficacy itself is homed at pack #7239 / the MARIPOSA-2 row, cross-pointed only.

cards.headline: PALOMA-3 primary report (Leighl 2024): subcutaneous amivantamab met pharmacokinetic noninferiority versus intravenous (trough geometric mean ratio 1.15; cycle-2 AUC ratio 1.03), with response 30% vs 33% and median PFS 6.1 vs 4.3 months
cards.summary: PALOMA-3 primary report (Leighl 2024): subcutaneous amivantamab met pharmacokinetic noninferiority versus intravenous (trough geometric mean ratio 1.15; cycle-2 AUC ratio 1.03), with response 30% vs 33% and median PFS 6.1 vs 4.3 months
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (PALOMA-3), subcutaneous vs intravenous amivantamab, both with lazertinib — primary report (report 1 of exactly 2 on this shelf)
cards.people: 418 patients with EGFR-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer progressed after osimertinib and platinum-based chemotherapy, randomised 1:1 to subcutaneous (206) or intravenous (212) amivantamab, both with lazertinib. The coprimary endpoints were pharmacokinetic noninferiority endpoints (trough concentration and cycle-2 area under the curve).
cards.result: Pharmacokinetic noninferiority was met: geometric mean ratios for subcutaneous versus intravenous trough concentration were 1.15 (90% CI 1.04 to 1.26) at cycle-2-day-1 and 1.42 (1.27 to 1.61) at cycle-4-day-1, and the cycle-2 AUC ratio was 1.03 (0.98 to 1.09) — all relative ratios. Objective response was 30% subcutaneous versus 33% intravenous (absolute rates), and median progression-free survival was 6.1 versus 4.3 months. This is a formulation/route question, not a new efficacy question: amivantamab's efficacy itself is homed elsewhere (see the synthesis card) and is not re-litigated here.
cards.watchOut: PARTIAL + FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 reports of one trial, stated on the face. Noninferiority was defined on pharmacokinetics, with response as a key secondary endpoint — the trial was not designed to prove the subcutaneous route more efficacious.

cards.headline: PALOMA-3 primary report — route-harm and convenience slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): infusion-related reactions 13% vs 66%, venous thromboembolism 9% vs 14%, first administration 4.8 minutes vs 5 hours; the overall-survival difference (hazard ratio 0.62, relative, nominal P=0.02) was a predefined EXPLORATORY endpoint and is labelled as such
cards.summary: PALOMA-3 primary report — route-harm and convenience slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): infusion-related reactions 13% vs 66%, venous thromboembolism 9% vs 14%, first administration 4.8 minutes vs 5 hours; the overall-survival difference (hazard ratio 0.62, relative, nominal P=0.02) was a predefined EXPLORATORY endpoint and is labelled as such
cards.type: Route-harm, administration-time and exploratory-survival slice of the PALOMA-3 primary report above (same report — it adds no independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 418 randomised patients as the card above (206 subcutaneous, 212 intravenous).
cards.result: Fewer subcutaneous patients had infusion-related reactions (13% versus 66%) and venous thromboembolism (9% versus 14%) — absolute rates. Median administration time for the first dose was 4.8 minutes (range 0–18) subcutaneous versus 5 hours (range 0.2–9.9) intravenous. At cycle-1-day-1, 85% of subcutaneous versus 52% of intravenous patients considered treatment convenient (85% versus 35% at end of treatment). Overall survival was longer in the subcutaneous group (hazard ratio for death 0.62, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.92; nominal P=0.02) — a relative measure from a predefined exploratory endpoint that was not powered or alpha-controlled for survival.
cards.watchOut: A change of injection route is not a plausible sole cause of a survival gap of this size: the face of this shelf states plainly that the survival difference is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, exactly as the commissioning row directs. Do not cite PALOMA-3 as evidence that subcutaneous amivantamab prolongs survival.

cards.headline: PALOMA-3 satisfaction / resource report (Alexander 2025): time in chair at cycle 1 day 1 was a median 0.4 hours subcutaneous versus 6.5 hours intravenous; more subcutaneous patients felt unrestricted (66% vs 29%) and unbothered (69% vs 30%) by administration; moderate-to-very-severe injection-site pain in 14–16%
cards.summary: PALOMA-3 satisfaction / resource report (Alexander 2025): time in chair at cycle 1 day 1 was a median 0.4 hours subcutaneous versus 6.5 hours intravenous; more subcutaneous patients felt unrestricted (66% vs 29%) and unbothered (69% vs 30%) by administration; moderate-to-very-severe injection-site pain in 14–16%
cards.type: Patient-satisfaction and resource-utilisation report of PALOMA-3 (report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf — same trial as the cards above)
cards.people: The same PALOMA-3 population (206 subcutaneous, 212 intravenous, both with lazertinib), with resource use and participant-reported treatment satisfaction assessed at cycle 1 day 1 and cycle 3 day 1.
cards.result: Median time in chair was 0.4 hours (range 0–12.0) subcutaneous versus 6.5 hours (0–24.0) intravenous at cycle 1 day 1, and 0.6 versus 3.4 hours at cycle 3 day 1; healthcare-professional time and participant time in room were also lower. More subcutaneous recipients reported feeling unrestricted (66% versus 29% at cycle 1 day 1) or unbothered (69% versus 30%) by administration, and more reported gaining time for other activities (36% versus 7%). Moderate-to-very-severe injection-site pain was reported by 14% (cycle 1 day 1) to 16% (cycle 3 day 1) of subcutaneous recipients, with swelling and redness each in 5–6%. Most subcutaneous recipients preferred the subcutaneous route over their historical intravenous experience and would recommend it.
cards.watchOut: Satisfaction comparisons against patients' remembered historical intravenous therapy are not randomised comparisons; the randomised, same-trial figures are the time-in-chair and feeling-unrestricted/unbothered contrasts printed here.

shelves.title: Telisotuzumab vedotin in c-Met NSCLC (LUMINOSITY, exactly 2 reports, single-arm): response 29% — about 35% c-Met-high, 23–24% intermediate; neuropathy in a third
shelves.question: In patients with previously treated (≤2 prior lines, ≤1 chemotherapy) locally advanced or metastatic c-Met protein-overexpressing, EGFR-wildtype nonsquamous NSCLC, does the c-Met-directed antibody–drug conjugate telisotuzumab vedotin 1.9 mg/kg every 2 weeks, versus no concurrent control, produce objective responses, and with what neuropathy cost?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Proto-Oncogene Proteins c-met · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Female · Male · Lung Neoplasms · Aged · Middle Aged · ErbB Receptors · Immunoconjugates · Adult · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Oligopeptides
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one single-arm phase 2 trial (LUMINOSITY; 172 treated, 168 efficacy-evaluable), and single-arm throughout, so the stamp is capped at POSSIBLE. Telisotuzumab vedotin 1.9 mg/kg every 2 weeks produced responses in 28.6% (primary report) and 29.2% (updated analysis) of patients with previously treated c-Met-overexpressing (≥25% of tumour cells 3+, SP44 assay), EGFR-wildtype nonsquamous NSCLC — 34.6%/34.5% in c-Met-high and 22.9%/23.8% in c-Met-intermediate disease — with median duration of response 8.3 then 7.2 months. There is no comparator: no survival or comparative claim can be made. Peripheral sensory neuropathy is the price (30–31% any grade, 7% grade ≥3). Product: telisotuzumab vedotin (Emrelis, AbbVie), US-approved on the accelerated pathway on this evidence.

cards.headline: LUMINOSITY primary report (Camidge 2024, single-arm, NO comparator): telisotuzumab vedotin response 28.6% overall — 34.6% in c-Met-high and 22.9% in c-Met-intermediate disease; median duration of response 8.3 months, median overall survival 14.5 months, median PFS 5.7 months
cards.summary: LUMINOSITY primary report (Camidge 2024, single-arm, NO comparator): telisotuzumab vedotin response 28.6% overall — 34.6% in c-Met-high and 22.9% in c-Met-intermediate disease; median duration of response 8.3 months, median overall survival 14.5 months, median PFS 5.7 months
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial (LUMINOSITY) — primary report (report 1 of exactly 2 on this shelf); no concurrent control
cards.people: 172 patients with locally advanced or metastatic c-Met protein-overexpressing, EGFR-wildtype nonsquamous NSCLC received telisotuzumab vedotin 1.9 mg/kg every 2 weeks in stages I and II of LUMINOSITY. Eligible patients had ≤2 previous lines of therapy, including ≤1 line of systemic chemotherapy. c-Met overexpression was defined as ≥25% of tumour cells with 3+ staining — high ≥50% 3+, intermediate ≥25% to <50% 3+. The biomarker definition is part of the tested intervention and is printed here, in the header population, as the row directs.
cards.result: Overall response rate by independent central review, the primary endpoint, was 28.6% (95% CI 21.7 to 36.2) — 34.6% (24.2 to 46.2) in c-Met-high and 22.9% (14.4 to 33.4) in c-Met-intermediate disease. Median duration of response was 8.3 months, median overall survival 14.5 months and median progression-free survival 5.7 months — all single-arm figures with no concurrent control, framed as such on this shelf. Product naming (clarification exception, as the row directs): telisotuzumab vedotin (Emrelis, AbbVie), approved in the US on the accelerated pathway on this evidence — stated plainly.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: exactly 2 reports of one single-arm phase 2 trial, stated on the face. A response rate without a comparator cannot show that patients live longer or feel better than they would on another treatment.

cards.headline: LUMINOSITY updated analysis (Girard 2026, single-arm): 168 efficacy-evaluable patients — response 29.2% (34.5% c-Met-high, 23.8% c-Met-intermediate), median duration of response 7.2 months; prior platinum and/or immunotherapy did not change efficacy; neuropathy 31% any grade, 7% grade ≥3
cards.summary: LUMINOSITY updated analysis (Girard 2026, single-arm): 168 efficacy-evaluable patients — response 29.2% (34.5% c-Met-high, 23.8% c-Met-intermediate), median duration of response 7.2 months; prior platinum and/or immunotherapy did not change efficacy; neuropathy 31% any grade, 7% grade ≥3
cards.type: Updated analysis of the LUMINOSITY trial (report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf — same single-arm trial as the cards above, longer follow-up)
cards.people: 172 patients received at least one dose of telisotuzumab vedotin 1.9 mg/kg every 2 weeks; 168 were evaluable for efficacy (84 c-Met-high, 84 c-Met-intermediate, by the SP44 assay definition: ≥25% of tumour cells at 3+, split at 50%). This analysis adds about 6 months' further follow-up (cut-off 21 February 2024) and explores the effect of previous therapy type.
cards.result: Overall response rate was 29.2% (95% CI 22.4 to 36.7) — 34.5% (24.5 to 45.7) in c-Met-high and 23.8% (15.2 to 34.3) in c-Met-intermediate disease. Median duration of response was 7.2 months (5.5 to 11.0), the same in both c-Met groups. Previous therapy (platinum, immune checkpoint inhibitors, or both) did not impact efficacy outcomes. The most common treatment-related adverse event remained peripheral sensory neuropathy (31% any grade, 7% grade ≥3). All figures are single-arm and uncontrolled.
cards.watchOut: An updated analysis of the same patients is not a second trial: the evidence base for this shelf remains one single-arm phase 2 study. The phase 3 TeliMET NSCLC-01 results, when published, would be the report that could change this stamp.

cards.result: Response was 28.6% in the primary report and 29.2% in the updated analysis, consistently higher in c-Met-high (34.6% / 34.5%) than c-Met-intermediate (22.9% / 23.8%) disease; median duration of response was 8.3 then 7.2 months, median overall survival 14.5 months and median progression-free survival 5.7 months in the primary report — every one of these is an uncontrolled figure. cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK, single-arm throughout: if either of the 2 reports had failed to verify, this shelf would not have been built. The stamp is capped at POSSIBLE because a single-arm base can do no more, per the standing rule.

shelves.title: Tislelizumab vs sorafenib in HCC (RATIONALE-301, exactly 2 reports): noninferiority met, superiority NOT met — better responses and QoL, worse median PFS
shelves.question: In systemic-therapy-naïve adults with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage B or C, Child-Pugh A), does tislelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks, versus sorafenib, prolong overall survival (noninferiority, then superiority), and with what response durability and quality-of-life effect?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Male · Humans · Middle Aged · Sorafenib · Carcinoma, Hepatocellular · Liver Neoplasms · Antineoplastic Agents · Treatment Outcome · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized
shelves.balance: SPLIT — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports of one trial (RATIONALE-301, 674 randomised), and the headline is printed exactly as the row directs: overall-survival NONINFERIORITY was met (median 15.9 vs 14.1 months; hazard ratio 0.85, relative, interval crossing 1) and SUPERIORITY was NOT met. Tislelizumab gave a higher response rate (14.3% vs 5.4%, absolute) with far more durable responses (median 36.1 vs 11.0 months), fewer grade ≥3 treatment-related events (22.2% vs 53.4%) and better quality of life (no difference for pain) — but median progression-free survival was numerically worse (2.1 vs 3.4 months; hazard ratio 1.11, relative, favouring sorafenib). All three reads stay on the face together; this is not stamped as a superiority win.

cards.headline: RATIONALE-301 primary report (Qin 2023): overall-survival NONINFERIORITY was met (median 15.9 vs 14.1 months; relative hazard ratio 0.85, 95.003% CI 0.71 to 1.02) and SUPERIORITY was NOT met — printed as such on this shelf; response 14.3% vs 5.4%, median duration of response 36.1 vs 11.0 months, but median PFS was numerically WORSE with tislelizumab (2.1 vs 3.4 months; relative hazard ratio 1.11)
cards.summary: RATIONALE-301 primary report (Qin 2023): overall-survival NONINFERIORITY was met (median 15.9 vs 14.1 months; relative hazard ratio 0.85, 95.003% CI 0.71 to 1.02) and SUPERIORITY was NOT met — printed as such on this shelf; response 14.3% vs 5.4%, median duration of response 36.1 vs 11.0 months, but median PFS was numerically WORSE with tislelizumab (2.1 vs 3.4 months; relative hazard ratio 1.11)
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (RATIONALE-301), tislelizumab vs sorafenib — primary report (report 1 of exactly 2 on this shelf)
cards.people: 674 systemic-therapy-naïve adults with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage B or C, Child-Pugh A, ECOG performance status ≤1), randomised 1:1 to tislelizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks or sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily, in an open-label global phase 3 trial; 84.6% were men and median age was 61 years. Minimum follow-up was 33 months.
cards.result: The primary endpoint, overall-survival noninferiority of tislelizumab versus sorafenib, was met: median overall survival 15.9 months (95% CI 13.2 to 19.7) versus 14.1 months (12.6 to 17.4), hazard ratio 0.85 (95.003% CI 0.71 to 1.02) — a relative measure whose interval crosses 1, so superiority was NOT met, and this shelf prints that plainly. Objective response was 14.3% (49 patients) versus 5.4% (18) — absolute rates — and median duration of response was 36.1 versus 11.0 months. Median progression-free survival, however, was 2.1 months with tislelizumab versus 3.4 months with sorafenib (hazard ratio 1.11, 0.92 to 1.33), a relative measure numerically favouring sorafenib. All three reads — noninferior survival, better and more durable response, worse median PFS — belong on the face together, as the row directs.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: exactly 2 reports of one trial, stated on the face. Noninferiority is not superiority: any summary that calls this trial a survival win over sorafenib is wrong, and this shelf is stamped accordingly.
cards.source: Qin S et al. Tislelizumab vs Sorafenib as First-Line Treatment for Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA oncology. 2023. PMID: 37796513. Registry ID: NCT03412773. cards.headline: RATIONALE-301 primary report — safety slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events 22.2% with tislelizumab versus 53.4% with sorafenib; treatment-related discontinuation 6.2% vs 10.2% and dose modification 20.1% vs 57.7%
cards.summary: RATIONALE-301 primary report — safety slice (same report as the card above, NOT a second report): grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events 22.2% with tislelizumab versus 53.4% with sorafenib; treatment-related discontinuation 6.2% vs 10.2% and dose modification 20.1% vs 57.7%
cards.type: Safety slice of the RATIONALE-301 primary report above (same report, carded separately so the tolerability figures are not buried — it adds no independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 674 randomised patients as the card above (338 received tislelizumab and 324 received sorafenib in the safety population, per the report).
cards.result: Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 96.2% of tislelizumab patients and 100% of sorafenib patients. Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events were reported in 75 patients (22.2%) receiving tislelizumab and 173 (53.4%) receiving sorafenib. Treatment-related events leading to discontinuation were less frequent with tislelizumab (6.2% versus 10.2%), as were events leading to drug modification (20.1% versus 57.7%). The authors describe tislelizumab's safety profile as favourable versus sorafenib.
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial: adverse-event reporting and dose modification are more susceptible to knowledge of the assigned drug than in a blinded trial, and sorafenib's dose-modification pattern is a long-known feature of that drug.

cards.headline: RATIONALE-301 quality-of-life report (Finn 2024): at cycles 4 and 6 tislelizumab patients had better global health status, physical functioning and fatigue scores than sorafenib patients, with lower risk of deterioration (time-to-deterioration hazard ratios, relative, 0.45 to 0.68 across the prespecified scales) — and NO difference for pain (hazard ratio 0.78, interval crossing 1)
cards.summary: RATIONALE-301 quality-of-life report (Finn 2024): at cycles 4 and 6 tislelizumab patients had better global health status, physical functioning and fatigue scores than sorafenib patients, with lower risk of deterioration (time-to-deterioration hazard ratios, relative, 0.45 to 0.68 across the prespecified scales) — and NO difference for pain (hazard ratio 0.78, interval crossing 1)
cards.type: Health-related quality-of-life report of RATIONALE-301 (report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf — same trial as the cards above)
cards.people: The same RATIONALE-301 population (342 randomised to tislelizumab, 332 to sorafenib), assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-HCC18 and EQ-5D-5L instruments; the prespecified patient-reported endpoints were compared at cycles 4 and 6 by mixed models, with time to deterioration by Kaplan–Meier methods.
cards.result: Patients on tislelizumab had better mean-change differences in global health status/quality of life, QLQ-C30 physical functioning and fatigue, and the QLQ-HCC18 symptom index. Risk of deterioration was lower with tislelizumab for global health status (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.94), physical functioning (0.45, 0.32 to 0.63), fatigue (0.47, 0.36 to 0.61), the HCC18 symptom index (0.52, 0.34 to 0.81) and HCC-specific fatigue (0.59, 0.45 to 0.79) — all relative measures. For pain there was no difference (hazard ratio 0.78, 0.56 to 1.09). On the EQ-5D-5L visual analogue scale, tislelizumab patients maintained their scores at cycles 4 and 6 while sorafenib patients' scores decreased.
cards.watchOut: Quality-of-life comparisons in an open-label trial are vulnerable to patients knowing which drug they are on; the pain null is printed alongside the positive scales so the shelf does not cherry-pick.

health-related quality-of-life report of rationale-301 (report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf — same trial as the cards above) the same rationale-301 population (342 randomised to tislelizumab, 332 to sorafenib), assessed with the eortc qlq-c30, qlq-hcc18 and eq-5d-5l instruments; the prespecified patient-reported endpoints were compared at cycles 4 and 6 by mixed models, with time to deterioration by kaplan–meier methods. patients on tislelizumab had better mean-change differences in global health status/quality of life, qlq-c30 physical functioning and fatigue, and the qlq-hcc18 symptom index. risk of deterioration was lower with tislelizumab for global health status (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% ci 0.49 to 0.94), physical functioning (0.45, 0.32 to 0.63), fatigue (0.47, 0.36 to 0.61), the hcc18 symptom index (0.52, 0.34 to 0.81) and hcc-specific fatigue (0.59, 0.45 to 0.79) — all relative measures. for pain there was no difference (hazard ratio 0.78, 0.56 to 1.09). on the eq-5d-5l visual analogue scale, tislelizumab patients maintained their scores at cycles 4 and 6 while sorafenib patients' scores decreased. quality-of-life comparisons in an open-label trial are vulnerable to patients knowing which drug they are on; the pain null is printed alongside the positive scales so the shelf does not cherry-pick. finn rs et al. tislelizumab versus sorafenib in first-line treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: impact on health-related quality of life in rationale-301 study. liver cancer. 2024. pmid: 39435268. registry id: nct03412773 (named in the report). mesh: none in the record

cards.headline: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports of one trial — the honest headline is noninferior survival (superiority NOT met), better and far more durable responses, better quality of life and tolerability, but a numerically worse median progression-free survival
cards.summary: Synthesis: exactly 2 reports of one trial — the honest headline is noninferior survival (superiority NOT met), better and far more durable responses, better quality of life and tolerability, but a numerically worse median progression-free survival
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: RATIONALE-301 only — 674 randomised (tislelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks versus sorafenib), minimum follow-up 33 months, plus its quality-of-life report.
cards.result: Overall survival: median 15.9 versus 14.1 months, relative hazard ratio 0.85 with its interval crossing 1 — noninferiority met, superiority not met, printed as such. Response: 14.3% versus 5.4%, with median duration of response 36.1 versus 11.0 months. Progression-free survival: median 2.1 versus 3.4 months, numerically favouring sorafenib. Grade ≥3 treatment-related events: 22.2% versus 53.4%. Quality of life favoured tislelizumab on global health, functioning and fatigue, with no difference for pain. Cross-point only, in prose: live #850 covers the first-line HCC immunotherapy family anchored on HIMALAYA/STRIDE, pack #6532 asks nivolumab + ipilimumab first-line (CheckMate 9DW) and pack #6855 asks camrelizumab + rivoceranib (CARES-310) — none re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK: if either of the 2 reports had failed to verify, this shelf would not have been built. A long-term survival update would be a third report.

shelves.title: Oral glutamine for oral mucositis: SPLIT — small chemo/BMT trials favoured it (morphine days 5.0 vs 10.3 in autologous BMT); radiotherapy trial and pooled incidence (relative risk 0.91) are null
shelves.question: In patients receiving chemotherapy, radiotherapy or chemoradiation (including bone-marrow transplantation), does oral glutamine (swish-and-swallow or dissolved oral dosing, as tested) reduce the incidence, duration and severity of oral mucositis / stomatitis versus placebo or standard oral care?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects · Bone Marrow Transplantation/adverse effects · Cross-Over Studies · Double-Blind Method · Glutamine/administration & dosage · Head and Neck Neoplasms/radiotherapy · Humans · Radiotherapy/adverse effects · Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic · Stomatitis · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: SPLIT — by treatment setting, and the split is the shelf. In chemotherapy and autologous bone-marrow transplantation, three small early randomised reports favoured oral glutamine: a 14-patient pilot (mucositis days 2.7 vs 9.9 across successive courses), a 24-patient randomised crossover trial (mouth pain 4.5 days shorter than placebo) and a 193-patient BMT trial in which autologous recipients used morphine for 5.0 versus 10.3 days — while allogeneic recipients showed no benefit and longer opiate use. In head-and-neck radiotherapy, the one modern phase 3 trial (71 randomised) found no significant effect on mucositis severity, and the 2020 synthesis of randomised trials found the same risk of oral mucositis with glutamine as control (relative risk 0.91, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.05; n=314; low-confidence evidence). The early trials are small and their Ns are printed on their faces. PROPOSED STAMP: SPLIT.

cards.headline: Pilot trial (Skubitz 1996, N=14 printed on the face): oral glutamine 4 g swish-and-swallow twice daily — mucositis grade fell in 12 of 14 patients and mucositis days fell in 13 of 14 across successive chemotherapy courses
cards.summary: Pilot trial (Skubitz 1996, N=14 printed on the face): oral glutamine 4 g swish-and-swallow twice daily — mucositis grade fell in 12 of 14 patients and mucositis days fell in 13 of 14 across successive chemotherapy courses
cards.type: Pilot trial, oral glutamine vs the same patients' previous chemotherapy course (within-patient comparison)
cards.people: 14 patients who had experienced stomatitis after a course of chemotherapy (12 receiving doxorubicin, 1 etoposide, 1 ifosfamide/etoposide/carboplatin), who received the same chemotherapy regimen in the next course plus a suspension of L-glutamine 4 g swish and swallow twice a day from day 1 for 28 days or until 4 days past resolution of mucositis.
cards.result: The maximum grade of mucositis (CALGB criteria) decreased in 12 of 14 patients with glutamine (median score 2A vs 0.5; P<0.001), and the total number of days of mucositis decreased in 13 of 14 patients (2.7 +/- 0.8 vs 9.9 +/- 1.1 days, mean +/- SEM). Thirteen of the 14 patients felt the mucositis was less severe with glutamine. No change in nadir neutrophil count was noted and no toxicity of glutamine was observed.
cards.watchOut: N=14, printed here and on the headline: a small pilot comparing each patient's glutamine course with their own previous course — not a parallel-group randomised comparison — so it is supportive only and never load-bearing on this shelf.
cards.source: Skubitz KM et al. Oral glutamine to prevent chemotherapy induced stomatitis: a pilot study. The Journal of laboratory and clinical medicine. 1996. PMID: 8636652. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Randomised crossover RCT (Anderson 1998, N=24): oral glutamine shortened chemotherapy stomatitis — duration of mouth pain 4.5 days less and severe-pain days 4 days less than glycine placebo
cards.summary: Randomised crossover RCT (Anderson 1998, N=24): oral glutamine shortened chemotherapy stomatitis — duration of mouth pain 4.5 days less and severe-pain days 4 days less than glycine placebo
cards.type: Randomised double-blind crossover trial, oral glutamine vs glycine placebo during chemotherapy
cards.people: 24 patients (16 children and 8 adults) receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy, in a randomised double-blind crossover trial of glutamine or placebo (glycine) suspension, 2 g amino acid/m2/dose twice daily, swish and swallow on chemotherapy days and for at least 14 additional days.
cards.result: Paired data showed significant amelioration of stomatitis with glutamine: the duration of mouth pain was 4.5 days less in glutamine courses than placebo courses (Wilcoxon signed rank test, P=0.0005), and the number of days mucositis restricted oral intake to soft foods (grade 2 or worse, modified ECOG) was 4 days less with glutamine (P=0.002).
cards.watchOut: N=24 (mixed children and adults) in a crossover design: a small early trial whose effect sizes are large relative to its size; read beside the null radiotherapy trial and the null pooled incidence result below.
cards.source: Anderson PM et al. Oral glutamine reduces the duration and severity of stomatitis after cytotoxic cancer chemotherapy. Cancer. 1998. PMID: 9762946. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: BMT RCT (Anderson 1998, 193 randomised): oral glutamine halved morphine days in autologous transplantation (5.0 vs 10.3 days) but showed no benefit — and longer opiate use — in allogeneic transplantation
cards.summary: BMT RCT (Anderson 1998, 193 randomised): oral glutamine halved morphine days in autologous transplantation (5.0 vs 10.3 days) but showed no benefit — and longer opiate use — in allogeneic transplantation
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, oral glutamine vs glycine placebo during bone marrow transplantation
cards.people: 193 patients undergoing bone marrow transplantation in a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled study; glutamine or placebo (glycine) 1.0 g amino acid/m2/dose swish and swallow four times a day from admission until day +28. Autologous recipients numbered 87; the remainder were allogeneic (including matched sibling) recipients.
cards.result: In autologous BMT patients, glutamine was associated with significantly less mouth pain by self-report and by opiate use (5.0 +/- 6.2 days of morphine for glutamine vs 10.3 +/- 9.8 days for placebo; P=0.005). Matched sibling BMT patients had no effect by self-report and an increased duration of opiate use (23.2 +/- 5.7 days for glutamine vs 16.3 +/- 8.3 days for placebo; P=0.002). Day-28 survival of allogeneic patients was improved by glutamine (no figures printed in the record). No significant differences were seen in total parenteral nutrition use, relapse or progression, parenteral antibiotic use, graft-versus-host disease or days of hospitalisation, and no toxicity of glutamine was observed.
cards.watchOut: The benefit is confined to the autologous subgroup; the allogeneic result points the other way on opiate use (the authors suggest a possible interaction with methotrexate). Transplant conditioning mucositis is a different setting from conventional chemotherapy or head-and-neck radiotherapy — do not pool them.
cards.source: Anderson PM et al. Effect of low-dose oral glutamine on painful stomatitis during bone marrow transplantation. Bone marrow transplantation. 1998. PMID: 9722068. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Head-and-neck radiotherapy phase 3 RCT (Huang 2019, 71 randomised): oral glutamine had NO significant effect on radiation-induced oral mucositis severity (odds ratio 0.3, 95% CI 0.05 to 1.67; P=0.169)
cards.summary: Head-and-neck radiotherapy phase 3 RCT (Huang 2019, 71 randomised): oral glutamine had NO significant effect on radiation-induced oral mucositis severity (odds ratio 0.3, 95% CI 0.05 to 1.67; P=0.169)
cards.type: Phase 3 parallel double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial, oral glutamine vs maltodextrin placebo during head-and-neck radiotherapy
cards.people: 71 patients with stage I-IV head and neck cancer undergoing radiotherapy at a university hospital, randomised to oral glutamine (5 g glutamine and 10 g maltodextrin) or placebo (15 g maltodextrin) three times daily from 7 days before radiotherapy to 14 days after; 64 patients (33 placebo, 31 glutamine) completed radiotherapy and formed the completers' analysis.
cards.result: On multivariate analysis, glutamine had no significant effect on the severity of oral mucositis (odds ratio 0.3, 95% CI 0.05 to 1.67; P=0.169); only the change in body mass index was significantly related to mucositis severity. No difference was found in the incidence or severity of neck dermatitis between the arms.
cards.watchOut: The largest modern trial on this shelf and the only one in pure radiotherapy; its confidence interval is wide (0.05 to 1.67), so it excludes neither a moderate benefit nor harm — but it is a null result in the setting where the chemotherapy-era trials do not apply.
cards.source: Huang CJ et al. Randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating oral glutamine on radiation-induced oral mucositis and dermatitis in head and neck cancer patients. The American journal of clinical nutrition. 2019. PMID: 30753262. Registry ID: NCT03015077. cards.headline: Synthesis of randomised trials (de Meneses 2020): oral mucositis risk with glutamine was the same as control (relative risk 0.91, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.05; n=314) — low-confidence evidence
cards.summary: Synthesis of randomised trials (de Meneses 2020): oral mucositis risk with glutamine was the same as control (relative risk 0.91, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.05; n=314) — low-confidence evidence
cards.type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials of oral supplementation for oral mucositis
cards.people: Twelve randomised clinical trials of oral supplementation (elemental diet/elental, glutamine and zinc) for oral mucositis in cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy, pooled in a systematic review and meta-analysis with GRADE assessment.
cards.result: The meta-analysis found the glutamine group presented the same risk of oral mucositis as the control group (relative risk 0.91, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.05; P=0.19; n=314) — a relative measure, printed beside the trial-level results above. Most included studies reported benefits in delaying occurrence (glutamine and zinc) and reducing severity (glutamine, zinc and elental), but the evidence quality suggested low confidence for the glutamine and zinc estimates. (For completeness: zinc, a different supplement not asked on this shelf, gave relative risk 0.71, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.96.)
cards.watchOut: The pooled glutamine estimate rests on only 314 patients across small trials and is graded low-confidence; incidence (this pooled result) and severity/duration (the early trials' endpoints) are different outcomes and must not be conflated.
cards.source: de Menêses AG et al. Effects of oral supplementation in the management of oral mucositis in cancer patients: A meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials. Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology. 2020. PMID: 31172573. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: Chemoradiotherapy · Dietary Supplements · Humans · Neoplasms · Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic · Stomatitis

cards.headline: Synthesis: oral glutamine is SPLIT by setting — small chemotherapy and autologous-BMT trials favoured it, the radiotherapy phase 3 trial and the pooled incidence estimate are null
cards.summary: Synthesis: oral glutamine is SPLIT by setting — small chemotherapy and autologous-BMT trials favoured it, the radiotherapy phase 3 trial and the pooled incidence estimate are null
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Chemotherapy/transplant limb: a 14-patient pilot (mucositis days 2.7 vs 9.9 across successive courses), a 24-patient randomised crossover trial (mouth pain 4.5 days shorter than placebo) and a 193-patient BMT trial (autologous morphine days 5.0 vs 10.3; allogeneic opiate use longer on glutamine) all favoured glutamine on pain/duration endpoints. Radiotherapy limb: the 71-patient phase 3 head-and-neck trial found no significant effect on mucositis severity. Pooled: relative risk 0.91 (95% CI 0.78 to 1.05) for mucositis incidence, low-confidence. Refusal recorded as the row directs: the widely cited radiation-specific glutamine synthesis PMID 32363198 was excluded as an anchor under the row's empty-abstract ruling and is not carded or relied on here; this shelf rests on PMID 31172573 as its synthesis instead. The neuropathy limb of the original question was dropped at mining (no randomised base) and no card here makes any neuropathy claim.
