cards.search: synthesis: oral glutamine is split by setting — small chemotherapy and autologous-bmt trials favoured it, the radiotherapy phase 3 trial and the pooled incidence estimate are null synthesis: oral glutamine is split by setting — small chemotherapy and autologous-bmt trials favoured it, the radiotherapy phase 3 trial and the pooled incidence estimate are null in patients receiving chemotherapy, radiotherapy or chemoradiation (including bone-marrow transplantation), does oral glutamine (swish-and-swallow or dissolved oral dosing, as tested) reduce the incidence, duration and severity of oral mucositis / stomatitis versus placebo or standard oral care? synthesis all reports carded on this shelf. chemotherapy/transplant limb: a 14-patient pilot (mucositis days 2.7 vs 9.9 across successive courses), a 24-patient randomised crossover trial (mouth pain 4.5 days shorter than placebo) and a 193-patient bmt trial (autologous morphine days 5.0 vs 10.3; allogeneic opiate use longer on glutamine) all favoured glutamine on pain/duration endpoints. radiotherapy limb: the 71-patient phase 3 head-and-neck trial found no significant effect on mucositis severity. pooled: relative risk 0.91 (95% ci 0.78 to 1.05) for mucositis incidence, low-confidence. refusal recorded as the row directs: the widely cited radiation-specific glutamine synthesis pmid 32363198 was excluded as an anchor under the row's empty-abstract ruling and is not carded or relied on here; this shelf rests on pmid 31172573 as its synthesis instead. the neuropathy limb of the original question was dropped at mining (no randomised base) and no card here makes any neuropathy claim. see the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Carfilzomib in relapsed/refractory myeloma: ASPIRE — PFS 26.3 vs 17.6 months, OS 48.3 vs 40.4; ENDEAVOR — PFS 18.7 vs 9.4 months vs bortezomib; cardiac, hypertension and renal harm is the price
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 prior lines, does the irreversible proteasome inhibitor carfilzomib — added to lenalidomide–dexamethasone (ASPIRE), or as carfilzomib–dexamethasone against bortezomib–dexamethasone (ENDEAVOR) — prolong progression-free and overall survival, and with what cardiac, renal and hypertension cost?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Dexamethasone · Female · Humans · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lenalidomide · Male · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Oligopeptides · Recurrence · Thalidomide
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on two large phase 3 trials testing two different comparisons — labelled as separate limbs and never pooled. Add-on limb (ASPIRE, 792 patients): carfilzomib added to lenalidomide–dexamethasone (KRd, carfilzomib in the 27 mg/m²-era regimen) prolonged progression-free survival (median 26.3 vs 17.6 months; hazard ratio 0.69, relative) and overall survival at final analysis (median 48.3 vs 40.4 months; HR 0.79, relative), with overall response 87.1% vs 66.7%. Head-to-head limb (ENDEAVOR, 929 patients): carfilzomib 56 mg/m²–dexamethasone beat bortezomib–dexamethasone on progression-free survival (median 18.7 vs 9.4 months; HR 0.53, relative) and on interim overall survival (median 47.6 vs 40.0 months; HR 0.791, relative). The pricing harms are cardiac failure (grade ≥3: 4.3% vs 2.1% in ASPIRE), hypertension (6.4% vs 2.3% in ASPIRE; grade ≥3 15% vs 3% at ENDEAVOR's survival analysis) and acute renal failure (3.8% vs 3.3%), with more serious adverse events on carfilzomib in ENDEAVOR (48% vs 36% at the primary report). CANDOR (carfilzomib–dexamethasone ± daratumumab) is NOT carded here — it belongs to the daratumumab question at shelf #7431 and is cross-pointed in prose only.

cards.headline: ASPIRE phase 3 primary report (Stewart 2015): adding carfilzomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone — median PFS 26.3 vs 17.6 months (HR 0.69, relative); overall response 87.1% vs 66.7%
cards.summary: ASPIRE phase 3 primary report (Stewart 2015): adding carfilzomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone — median PFS 26.3 vs 17.6 months (HR 0.69, relative); overall response 87.1% vs 66.7%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (ASPIRE) — add-on limb: carfilzomib + lenalidomide–dexamethasone vs lenalidomide–dexamethasone
cards.people: 792 patients with relapsed multiple myeloma randomised to carfilzomib with lenalidomide and dexamethasone (KRd) or lenalidomide and dexamethasone alone (Rd); the primary endpoint was progression-free survival, assessed at a protocol interim analysis.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly improved with carfilzomib: median 26.3 versus 17.6 months (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.83; P=0.0001 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). Median overall survival was not reached in either group at this interim analysis; 24-month overall survival rates were 73.3% vs 65.0% (HR for death 0.79, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.99). Overall response was 87.1% vs 66.7% (P<0.001), with complete response or better in 31.8% vs 9.3% and stringent complete response in 14.1% vs 4.3%. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 83.7% vs 80.7%; discontinuation for adverse events in 15.3% vs 17.7%. Patients on KRd reported superior health-related quality of life.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis for the primary report (overall survival immature, medians not reached); the survival read belongs to the final-analysis card below. ASPIRE used the 27 mg/m²-era carfilzomib dosing with Rd — a different dose frame from ENDEAVOR's 56 mg/m².
cards.source: Stewart AK et al. Carfilzomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone for relapsed multiple myeloma. The New England Journal of Medicine. 2015. PMID: 25482145. Registry ID: NCT01080391. cards.headline: ASPIRE final overall-survival analysis (Siegel 2018): median OS 48.3 vs 40.4 months (HR 0.79, relative) — with grade ≥3 cardiac failure 4.3% vs 2.1% and hypertension 6.4% vs 2.3%
cards.summary: ASPIRE final overall-survival analysis (Siegel 2018): median OS 48.3 vs 40.4 months (HR 0.79, relative) — with grade ≥3 cardiac failure 4.3% vs 2.1% and hypertension 6.4% vs 2.3%
cards.type: Prespecified final overall-survival analysis of the ASPIRE trial (same trial as the card above — not a separate trial)
cards.people: The same ASPIRE population (792 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 prior lines, randomised 1:1 to KRd or Rd in 28-day cycles; after 18 cycles all patients received Rd only). This prespecified analysis reports final overall survival and updated safety.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 48.3 months (95% CI 42.4 to 52.8) on KRd versus 40.4 months (95% CI 33.6 to 44.4) on Rd (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.95 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). The OS advantage was 11.4 months in patients with one prior line and 6.5 months in those with ≥2 prior lines. Discontinuation for adverse events: 19.9% (KRd) vs 21.5% (Rd). Grade ≥3 adverse events: 87.0% vs 83.3%, including acute renal failure 3.8% vs 3.3%, cardiac failure 4.3% vs 2.1%, ischaemic heart disease 3.8% vs 2.3%, hypertension 6.4% vs 2.3%, thrombocytopenia 20.2% vs 14.9% and peripheral neuropathy 2.8% vs 3.1%.
cards.watchOut: A report of the same ASPIRE trial, not independent evidence. Cardiac failure, hypertension and renal failure are the consistent excess harms of the carfilzomib arm and are part of the benefit's price.
cards.source: Siegel DS et al. Improvement in Overall Survival With Carfilzomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma. Journal of Clinical Oncology : Official Journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2018. PMID: 29341834. Registry ID: NCT01080391. cards.headline: ENDEAVOR phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2016): carfilzomib 56 mg/m²–dexamethasone vs bortezomib–dexamethasone — median PFS 18.7 vs 9.4 months (HR 0.53, relative); serious adverse events 48% vs 36%
cards.summary: ENDEAVOR phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2016): carfilzomib 56 mg/m²–dexamethasone vs bortezomib–dexamethasone — median PFS 18.7 vs 9.4 months (HR 0.53, relative); serious adverse events 48% vs 36%
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (ENDEAVOR) — head-to-head limb: carfilzomib–dexamethasone vs bortezomib–dexamethasone
cards.people: 929 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 previous treatments, randomised 1:1 (464 carfilzomib, 465 bortezomib) in an open-label multicentre trial; carfilzomib was given at 20 mg/m² on days 1–2 of cycle 1 and 56 mg/m² thereafter as a 30-minute infusion, with dexamethasone 20 mg in both arms. Median follow-up 11.9 vs 11.1 months at this interim analysis of the primary endpoint.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 18.7 months (95% CI 15.6 to not estimable) on carfilzomib–dexamethasone versus 9.4 months (8.4 to 10.4) on bortezomib–dexamethasone (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.65; P<0.0001 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). On-study deaths due to adverse events occurred in 4% vs 3%. Serious adverse events were reported in 48% of carfilzomib patients versus 36% on bortezomib. The most frequent grade ≥3 adverse events were anaemia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (9% vs 3%), thrombocytopenia (8% vs 9%) and pneumonia (7% vs 8%).
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and a different question from ASPIRE: a head-to-head proteasome-inhibitor comparison at 56 mg/m², not an add-on to Rd. The two limbs are labelled and never pooled on this shelf.
cards.source: Dimopoulos MA et al. The Lancet. Oncology. 2016. PMID: 26671818. Registry ID: NCT01568866. cards.headline: ENDEAVOR interim overall-survival analysis (Dimopoulos 2017): median OS 47.6 vs 40.0 months (HR 0.791, relative) — grade ≥3 hypertension 15% vs 3%
cards.summary: ENDEAVOR interim overall-survival analysis (Dimopoulos 2017): median OS 47.6 vs 40.0 months (HR 0.791, relative) — grade ≥3 hypertension 15% vs 3%
cards.type: Prospectively planned interim overall-survival analysis of the ENDEAVOR trial (same trial as the card above — not a separate trial)
cards.people: The same ENDEAVOR population (929 randomised; 198 hospitals and clinics in 27 countries), in a prospectively planned second interim analysis of overall survival (cutoff January 3, 2017).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 47.6 months (95% CI 42.5 to not evaluable) on carfilzomib–dexamethasone versus 40.0 months (32.6 to 42.3) on bortezomib–dexamethasone (hazard ratio 0.791, 95% CI 0.648 to 0.964 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 81% vs 71% and serious adverse events in 59% vs 40%. The most frequent grade ≥3 events were anaemia (16% vs 10%), hypertension (15% vs 3%), pneumonia (9% vs 9%), thrombocytopenia (9% vs 9%), fatigue (7% vs 8%), dyspnoea (6% vs 2%), decreased lymphocyte count (6% vs 2%), diarrhoea (4% vs 9%) and peripheral neuropathy (1% vs 6%).
cards.watchOut: An interim (not final) survival analysis of the same ENDEAVOR trial. The hypertension excess (grade ≥3 in 15% vs 3%) is the clearest single harm separating the two proteasome inhibitors here; peripheral neuropathy, by contrast, was less frequent on carfilzomib (1% vs 6%).
cards.source: Dimopoulos MA et al. Carfilzomib or bortezomib in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (ENDEAVOR): an interim overall survival analysis of an open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2017. PMID: 28843768. Registry ID: NCT01568866. cards.headline: ASPIRE health-related quality-of-life report (Stewart 2016): KRd improved global health status/quality of life over 18 cycles versus Rd, meeting the minimal important difference at cycle 12
cards.summary: ASPIRE health-related quality-of-life report (Stewart 2016): KRd improved global health status/quality of life over 18 cycles versus Rd, meeting the minimal important difference at cycle 12
cards.type: Health-related quality-of-life report of the ASPIRE trial (same trial as the first two cards — a programme report, not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: The ASPIRE trial population (792 randomised); the EORTC QLQ-C30 and myeloma module were administered at baseline, day 1 of cycles 3, 6, 12 and 18, and after treatment, with baseline questionnaire compliance of 94.1%.
cards.result: Patients on KRd had higher Global Health Status/Quality of Life scores than patients on Rd over 18 treatment cycles (two-sided P<.001); the minimal important difference was met at cycle 12 (5.6 points) and approached at cycle 18 (4.8 points). There was no difference between groups on the other prespecified subscales (fatigue, nausea and vomiting, pain, physical and role functioning, disease symptoms, adverse effects of treatment). More KRd patients met the ≥5-point responder definition, with statistical differences at cycle 12 (25.5% vs 17.4%) and cycle 18 (24.2% vs 12.9%).
cards.watchOut: A quality-of-life companion report of ASPIRE in an open-label trial — patient-reported outcomes in an unblinded comparison should be read with that caveat; it adds no efficacy evidence beyond ASPIRE itself.
cards.source: Stewart AK et al. Health-Related Quality-of-Life Results From the Open-Label, Randomized, Phase III ASPIRE Trial Evaluating Carfilzomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone Versus Lenalidomide and Dexamethasone in Patients With Relapsed Multiple Myeloma. cards.headline: Synthesis: two trials, two comparisons, both positive on progression-free and overall survival — ASPIRE (add-on to Rd) and ENDEAVOR (head-to-head vs bortezomib), priced in cardiac, hypertension and renal harm
cards.summary: Synthesis: two trials, two comparisons, both positive on progression-free and overall survival — ASPIRE (add-on to Rd) and ENDEAVOR (head-to-head vs bortezomib), priced in cardiac, hypertension and renal harm
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: ASPIRE (792 patients) showed adding carfilzomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged median progression-free survival (26.3 vs 17.6 months; hazard ratio 0.69, relative) and median overall survival (48.3 vs 40.4 months; HR 0.79, relative), with a quality-of-life advantage. ENDEAVOR (929 patients) showed carfilzomib 56 mg/m²–dexamethasone beat bortezomib–dexamethasone on median progression-free survival (18.7 vs 9.4 months; HR 0.53, relative) and interim median overall survival (47.6 vs 40.0 months; HR 0.791, relative). The consistent costs are cardiac failure, hypertension and renal events, and more serious adverse events. The two limbs test different doses and different comparisons and are not pooled. CANDOR, which adds daratumumab to carfilzomib–dexamethasone, is carded at shelf #7431 (the daratumumab question), not here.

cards.search: synthesis: two trials, two comparisons, both positive on progression-free and overall survival — aspire (add-on to rd) and endeavor (head-to-head vs bortezomib), priced in cardiac, hypertension and renal harm synthesis: two trials, two comparisons, both positive on progression-free and overall survival — aspire (add-on to rd) and endeavor (head-to-head vs bortezomib), priced in cardiac, hypertension and renal harm in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 prior lines, does the irreversible proteasome inhibitor carfilzomib — added to lenalidomide–dexamethasone (aspire), or as carfilzomib–dexamethasone against bortezomib–dexamethasone (endeavor) — prolong progression-free and overall survival, and with what cardiac, renal and hypertension cost? synthesis all reports carded on this shelf. aspire (792 patients) showed adding carfilzomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged median progression-free survival (26.3 vs 17.6 months; hazard ratio 0.69, relative) and median overall survival (48.3 vs 40.4 months; hr 0.79, relative), with a quality-of-life advantage. endeavor (929 patients) showed carfilzomib 56 mg/m²–dexamethasone beat bortezomib–dexamethasone on median progression-free survival (18.7 vs 9.4 months; hr 0.53, relative) and interim median overall survival (47.6 vs 40.0 months; hr 0.791, relative). the consistent costs are cardiac failure, hypertension and renal events, and more serious adverse events. the two limbs test different doses and different comparisons and are not pooled. candor, which adds daratumumab to carfilzomib–dexamethasone, is carded at shelf #7431 (the daratumumab question), not here. see the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Daratumumab in relapsed/refractory myeloma (PARTIAL beside first-line #844): POLLUX, CASTOR, CANDOR and APOLLO all prolonged progression-free survival; POLLUX final OS 67.6 vs 51.8 months
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after ≥1 prior line, does adding the anti-CD38 antibody daratumumab to a standard backbone — lenalidomide–dexamethasone (POLLUX), bortezomib–dexamethasone (CASTOR), carfilzomib–dexamethasone (CANDOR) or pomalidomide–dexamethasone (APOLLO) — prolong progression-free survival, and with what infusion-reaction and cytopenia cost?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Dexamethasone · Disease-Free Survival · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lenalidomide · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Recurrence · Thalidomide
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) for progression-free survival in the relapsed/refractory slice — this shelf is PARTIAL beside live shelf #844, which asks daratumumab FIRST-LINE in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed myeloma (MAIA/ALCYONE) only; only the relapsed/refractory slice is carded here, and #844 is cross-pointed, not re-carded. Four phase 3 trials, four backbones, each slice labelled and never pooled: POLLUX (daratumumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone, 569 patients) — progression or death 18.5% vs 41.0% at interim (hazard ratio 0.37, relative), and at final analysis median overall survival 67.6 vs 51.8 months (HR 0.73, relative); CASTOR (daratumumab + bortezomib–dexamethasone, 498 patients) — median PFS not reached vs 7.2 months (HR 0.39, relative); CANDOR (daratumumab + carfilzomib–dexamethasone, 466 patients) — median PFS not reached vs 15.8 months (HR 0.63, relative); APOLLO (daratumumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone, 304 patients) — median PFS 12.4 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.63, relative). The class costs are infusion-related reactions (47.7% in POLLUX and 45.3% in CASTOR, mostly grade 1/2 and mostly at the first infusion; APOLLO used subcutaneous daratumumab 1800 mg as an alternative to intravenous dosing) and neutropenia (grade 3/4: 51.9% vs 37.0% in POLLUX; 68% vs 51% in APOLLO). One-home assignments: CANDOR is carded HERE (its question is adding daratumumab) and only cross-pointed at the carfilzomib shelf #7430; APOLLO is carded HERE and only cross-pointed at the pomalidomide shelf #7432.

cards.headline: POLLUX phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2016): daratumumab + Rd — progression or death 18.5% vs 41.0% (HR 0.37, relative); MRD negativity 22.4% vs 4.6%; infusion reactions 47.7%
cards.summary: POLLUX phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2016): daratumumab + Rd — progression or death 18.5% vs 41.0% (HR 0.37, relative); MRD negativity 22.4% vs 4.6%; infusion reactions 47.7%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (POLLUX) — daratumumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone vs lenalidomide–dexamethasone (lenalidomide backbone slice)
cards.people: 569 patients with multiple myeloma who had received one or more previous lines of therapy, randomised to lenalidomide and dexamethasone alone (283) or with daratumumab (286); primary endpoint progression-free survival, at a protocol-specified interim analysis with median follow-up 13.5 months.
cards.result: Disease progression or death occurred in 53 of 286 patients (18.5%) on daratumumab versus 116 of 283 (41.0%) on control (hazard ratio 0.37, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.52; P<0.001 — a relative measure, absolute rates beside it). The 12-month progression-free survival rate was 83.2% vs 60.1%. Overall response was 92.9% vs 76.4% and complete response or better 43.1% vs 19.2%. Minimal residual disease negativity at a threshold of 1 tumour cell per 10⁵ white cells was 22.4% vs 4.6%. The most common grade 3/4 adverse events were neutropenia (51.9% vs 37.0%), thrombocytopenia (12.7% vs 13.5%) and anaemia (12.4% vs 19.6%). Daratumumab infusion-related reactions occurred in 47.7% and were mostly grade 1 or 2.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis at 13.5 months' median follow-up; the survival read is the final-analysis card below. Open-label trial.
cards.source: Dimopoulos MA et al. Daratumumab, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma. The New England Journal of Medicine. 2016. PMID: 27705267. Registry ID: NCT02076009. cards.headline: POLLUX final overall-survival analysis (Dimopoulos 2023): median OS 67.6 vs 51.8 months (HR 0.73, relative) at 79.7 months' median follow-up
cards.summary: POLLUX final overall-survival analysis (Dimopoulos 2023): median OS 67.6 vs 51.8 months (HR 0.73, relative) at 79.7 months' median follow-up
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the POLLUX trial (same trial as the card above — not a separate trial)
cards.people: The same POLLUX population (569 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after ≥1 prior line, randomised 1:1 to daratumumab-Rd or Rd until progression or unacceptable toxicity); after the positive primary analysis and a protocol amendment, control patients were offered daratumumab monotherapy after disease progression.
cards.result: A significant overall-survival benefit was observed with daratumumab-Rd (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.91; P=.0044 — a relative measure) at a median follow-up of 79.7 months: median overall survival 67.6 months versus 51.8 months on Rd. Prespecified analyses favoured daratumumab-Rd in most subgroups, including age ≥65, one to three prior lines, stage III disease, high-risk cytogenetics, and refractoriness to the last prior line or a proteasome inhibitor. The most common grade 3/4 treatment-emergent adverse events on daratumumab-Rd versus Rd were neutropenia (57.6% vs 41.6%), anaemia (19.8% vs 22.4%), pneumonia (17.3% vs 11.0%), thrombocytopenia (15.5% vs 15.7%) and diarrhoea (10.2% vs 3.9%).
cards.watchOut: A report of the same POLLUX trial. Control-arm patients could receive daratumumab monotherapy after progression under the protocol amendment, which would tend to dilute, not inflate, the survival contrast.
cards.source: Dimopoulos MA et al. Overall Survival With Daratumumab, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone in Previously Treated Multiple Myeloma (POLLUX): A Randomized, Open-Label, Phase III Trial. Journal of Clinical Oncology : Official Journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2023. PMID: 36599114. Registry ID: NCT02076009. cards.headline: CASTOR phase 3 primary report (Palumbo 2016): daratumumab + Vd — median PFS not reached vs 7.2 months (HR 0.39, relative); overall response 82.9% vs 63.2%; infusion reactions 45.3%
cards.summary: CASTOR phase 3 primary report (Palumbo 2016): daratumumab + Vd — median PFS not reached vs 7.2 months (HR 0.39, relative); overall response 82.9% vs 63.2%; infusion reactions 45.3%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (CASTOR) — daratumumab + bortezomib–dexamethasone vs bortezomib–dexamethasone (bortezomib backbone slice)
cards.people: 498 patients with relapsed or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma randomised to bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² and dexamethasone 20 mg alone or with daratumumab 16 mg/kg; primary endpoint progression-free survival, at a prespecified interim analysis with median follow-up 7.4 months.
cards.result: The 12-month progression-free survival rate was 60.7% on daratumumab versus 26.9% on control; median progression-free survival was not reached versus 7.2 months (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.39, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.53; P<0.001 — a relative measure, absolute rates beside it). Overall response was 82.9% vs 63.2%, very good partial response or better 59.2% vs 29.1%, and complete response or better 19.2% vs 9.0%. Common grade 3/4 adverse events were thrombocytopenia (45.3% vs 32.9%), anaemia (14.4% vs 16.0%) and neutropenia (12.8% vs 4.2%). Infusion-related reactions occurred in 45.3% of daratumumab patients, mostly grade 1 or 2 (grade 3 in 8.6%), and in 98.2% of cases during the first infusion.
cards.watchOut: A short-follow-up interim analysis (median 7.4 months; median PFS not yet reached on daratumumab) in an open-label trial — the size of the PFS advantage at this read is an early estimate.
cards.source: Palumbo A et al. Daratumumab, Bortezomib, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma. The New England Journal of Medicine. 2016. PMID: 27557302. Registry ID: NCT02136134. cards.headline: CANDOR phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2020): daratumumab + Kd — median PFS not reached vs 15.8 months (HR 0.63, relative); grade ≥3 events 82% vs 74%
cards.summary: CANDOR phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2020): daratumumab + Kd — median PFS not reached vs 15.8 months (HR 0.63, relative); grade ≥3 events 82% vs 74%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (CANDOR) — daratumumab + carfilzomib–dexamethasone vs carfilzomib–dexamethasone (carfilzomib backbone slice)
cards.people: 466 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at 102 sites, randomised 2:1 to carfilzomib, dexamethasone and daratumumab (KdD) or carfilzomib and dexamethasone (Kd); all patients received twice-weekly carfilzomib at 56 mg/m² (20 mg/m² on days 1–2 of cycle 1), with intravenous daratumumab and weekly dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg if ≥75 years). Median follow-up approximately 17 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was not reached in the KdD group versus 15.8 months in the Kd group (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.85; P=0.0027 — a relative measure). Median treatment duration was 70.1 versus 40.3 weeks. Grade ≥3 adverse events were reported in 82% of KdD patients versus 74% on Kd; adverse events leading to discontinuation were similar (22% vs 25%). The authors concluded KdD significantly prolonged progression-free survival with a favourable benefit-risk profile.
cards.watchOut: Carded HERE under the one-home rule because its question is adding daratumumab; the carfilzomib shelf (#7430) cross-points it in prose and does not re-card it. The abstract does not report infusion-reaction rates for this trial, so none are printed here.
cards.source: Dimopoulos M et al. cards.headline: APOLLO phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2021): daratumumab (subcutaneous or intravenous) + Pd — median PFS 12.4 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.63, relative); grade 3/4 neutropenia 68% vs 51%
cards.summary: APOLLO phase 3 primary report (Dimopoulos 2021): daratumumab (subcutaneous or intravenous) + Pd — median PFS 12.4 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.63, relative); grade 3/4 neutropenia 68% vs 51%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (APOLLO) — daratumumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone vs pomalidomide–dexamethasone (pomalidomide backbone slice)
cards.people: 304 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (median age 67 years; 53% men) at 48 centres in 12 European countries, all with at least one previous line including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, randomised 1:1 to pomalidomide and dexamethasone alone (153) or with daratumumab (151) given as 1800 mg subcutaneously or 16 mg/kg intravenously. Median follow-up 16.9 months.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was improved with daratumumab plus pomalidomide–dexamethasone: median 12.4 months (95% CI 8.3 to 19.3) versus 6.9 months (5.5 to 9.3) (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.85; P=0.0018 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). The most common grade 3/4 adverse events were neutropenia (68% vs 51%), anaemia (17% vs 21%) and thrombocytopenia (17% vs 18%). Serious adverse events occurred in 50% vs 39%, most commonly pneumonia (15% vs 8%) and lower respiratory tract infection (12% vs 9%). Treatment-emergent deaths were 7% in each group.
cards.watchOut: Carded HERE under the one-home rule because its question is adding daratumumab; the pomalidomide shelf (#7432) cross-points it in prose and does not re-card it. APOLLO belongs to the subcutaneous-daratumumab era (1800 mg SC as an alternative to IV), unlike the intravenous-only earlier trials on this shelf.

cards.headline: Synthesis: four backbones, four phase 3 progression-free-survival wins, one final overall-survival win (POLLUX) — the relapsed/refractory slice only, beside first-line shelf #844
cards.summary: Synthesis: four backbones, four phase 3 progression-free-survival wins, one final overall-survival win (POLLUX) — the relapsed/refractory slice only, beside first-line shelf #844
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Adding daratumumab to four different standard backbones in relapsed or refractory myeloma prolonged progression-free survival in every trial: hazard ratios (relative measures) of 0.37 (POLLUX, lenalidomide backbone), 0.39 (CASTOR, bortezomib backbone), 0.63 (CANDOR, carfilzomib backbone) and 0.63 (APOLLO, pomalidomide backbone), each printed with its absolute rates or medians on its card. POLLUX's final analysis adds a survival benefit (median 67.6 vs 51.8 months; HR 0.73, relative). The consistent costs are first-infusion infusion-related reactions (about 45–48% where reported, mostly low-grade) and more neutropenia. This shelf deliberately excludes the first-line question, which is homed at live shelf #844 (MAIA/ALCYONE in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed disease), and the amyloidosis, transplant-eligible and smouldering-myeloma daratumumab questions, which have their own homes.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Pomalidomide in relapsed/refractory myeloma: PFS improved in MM-003 and OPTIMISMM, but OPTIMISMM final overall survival was null unadjusted (35.6 vs 31.6 months; HR 0.94, P=.571) — a split result
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma previously treated with lenalidomide (and, in MM-003, bortezomib) — does pomalidomide plus dexamethasone, alone against high-dose dexamethasone (MM-003) or added to bortezomib–dexamethasone (OPTIMISMM), prolong progression-free survival, and does the progression benefit convert to survival?

shelves.balance: SPLIT — a large relative progression-free-survival benefit in both trials, but the mature survival read is null unadjusted, and that null is flagged on the face. MM-003 (455 patients refractory to both bortezomib and lenalidomide): pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone versus high-dose dexamethasone alone gave median progression-free survival of 4.0 vs 1.9 months (hazard ratio 0.48, relative), with grade 3/4 neutropenia in 48% vs 16% and pneumonia in 13% vs 8%. OPTIMISMM (559 lenalidomide-pretreated patients): adding pomalidomide to bortezomib–dexamethasone gave median PFS of 11.20 vs 7.10 months (HR 0.61, relative), but the final survival analysis at 70% maturity found median overall survival of 35.6 vs 31.6 months (HR 0.94, relative, NOT significant, P=.571). The subsequent-therapy-adjusted analysis (HR 0.76) is a sensitivity analysis and is labelled as such wherever it appears — it is never the headline. MM-003's comparator (high-dose dexamethasone alone) is a last-resort control in a doubly refractory population; that population is printed exactly. APOLLO (daratumumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone) belongs to shelf #7431 and OCEAN (melflufen vs pomalidomide–dexamethasone) to the melflufen row — both are cross-pointed in prose only and are not re-carded here.

cards.headline: MM-003 phase 3 primary report (San Miguel 2013): pomalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone vs high-dose dexamethasone alone — median PFS 4.0 vs 1.9 months (HR 0.48, relative) in doubly refractory disease
cards.summary: MM-003 phase 3 primary report (San Miguel 2013): pomalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone vs high-dose dexamethasone alone — median PFS 4.0 vs 1.9 months (HR 0.48, relative) in doubly refractory disease
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (MM-003) — pomalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone vs high-dose dexamethasone alone
cards.people: 455 patients with refractory or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma who had failed at least two previous treatments including bortezomib and lenalidomide, randomised 2:1 to pomalidomide 4 mg/day on days 1–21 plus low-dose dexamethasone (302) or high-dose dexamethasone alone (153), in 28-day cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Median follow-up 10.0 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 4.0 months (95% CI 3.6 to 4.7) on pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone versus 1.9 months (1.9 to 2.2) on high-dose dexamethasone (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.60; P<0.0001 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). The most common grade 3–4 haematological adverse events were neutropenia (48% vs 16%), anaemia (33% vs 37%) and thrombocytopenia (22% vs 26%); grade 3–4 non-haematological events included pneumonia (13% vs 8%), bone pain (7% vs 5%) and fatigue (5% vs 6%). Treatment-related adverse events leading to death occurred in 4% vs 5%. The authors concluded pomalidomide plus low-dose dexamethasone could be considered a new treatment option in this refractory population.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is high-dose dexamethasone alone — a last-resort control in patients refractory to both bortezomib and lenalidomide — so the absolute progression-free-survival gain (4.0 vs 1.9 months) is small even though the relative effect is large; both are printed.

cards.headline: OPTIMISMM phase 3 primary report (Richardson 2019): adding pomalidomide to bortezomib–dexamethasone — median PFS 11.20 vs 7.10 months (HR 0.61, relative); grade 3/4 neutropenia 42% vs 9%
cards.summary: OPTIMISMM phase 3 primary report (Richardson 2019): adding pomalidomide to bortezomib–dexamethasone — median PFS 11.20 vs 7.10 months (HR 0.61, relative); grade 3/4 neutropenia 42% vs 9%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (OPTIMISMM) — pomalidomide + bortezomib–dexamethasone vs bortezomib–dexamethasone
cards.people: 559 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who had received 1–3 previous regimens including a lenalidomide-containing regimen, randomised 1:1 at 133 centres in 21 countries to pomalidomide, bortezomib and dexamethasone (PVd, 281) or bortezomib and dexamethasone (Vd, 278), in 21-day cycles. Median follow-up 15.9 months.
cards.result: Pomalidomide, bortezomib and dexamethasone significantly improved progression-free survival versus bortezomib and dexamethasone (median 11.20 months, 95% CI 9.66 to 13.73, vs 7.10 months, 5.88 to 8.48; hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.77; P<0.0001 — a relative measure, absolute medians beside it). The most common grade 3/4 treatment-emergent adverse events were neutropenia (42% vs 9%; febrile neutropenia 3% vs 0%), infections (31% vs 18%) and thrombocytopenia (27% vs 29%). Serious adverse events occurred in 57% vs 42%. Eight deaths were related to treatment (6 on PVd, 2 on Vd).
cards.watchOut: Overall survival was immature at this primary report; the mature survival read is the next card, and it is null unadjusted — do not read this PFS card as a survival claim.

cards.headline: OPTIMISMM final survival analysis (Richardson 2025) — FLAGGED: median OS 35.6 vs 31.6 months, HR 0.94, NOT significant (P=.571) unadjusted; the adjusted HR 0.76 is a sensitivity analysis only
cards.summary: OPTIMISMM final survival analysis (Richardson 2025) — FLAGGED: median OS 35.6 vs 31.6 months, HR 0.94, NOT significant (P=.571) unadjusted; the adjusted HR 0.76 is a sensitivity analysis only
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the OPTIMISMM trial (same trial as the card above — not a separate trial)
cards.people: The same OPTIMISMM population (559 patients with relapsed or refractory myeloma after 1–3 prior regimens including lenalidomide), with overall survival data mature at a 70.0% event rate and median follow-up of 64.5 months (data cutoff May 13, 2022).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 35.6 months on PVd versus 31.6 months on Vd (hazard ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.15; P=0.571 — a relative measure, NOT significant). Adjusting for subsequent therapies, overall survival favoured PVd (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.619 to 0.931; P=0.008) — a prespecified sensitivity/adjusted analysis, labelled as such and never the headline. Median PFS2 (progression-free survival on next-line therapy) was 22.1 versus 16.9 months (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.94). Treatment-emergent adverse events led to discontinuation in 33.1% on PVd versus 19.6% on Vd. The authors describe the unadjusted result as a non-significant trend towards improved overall survival.
cards.watchOut: The unadjusted final survival result is null (HR 0.94, P=.571) at mature follow-up — the progression-free-survival benefit did not convert into a demonstrated overall-survival benefit. The adjusted HR 0.76 depends on modelling subsequent therapy and must stay labelled a sensitivity analysis.

shelves.title: Ixazomib + lenalidomide–dexamethasone in relapsed myeloma (TOURMALINE-MM1): PFS win (20.6 vs 14.7 months), no significant overall-survival benefit at 85 months
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed, refractory, or relapsed-and-refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 prior therapies, does adding the oral proteasome inhibitor ixazomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone, versus placebo plus lenalidomide–dexamethasone, prolong progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Boron Compounds · Dexamethasone · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Exanthema · Glycine · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Lenalidomide · Male · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Proportional Hazards Models · Quality of Life · Thalidomide · Thrombocytopenia
shelves.balance: SPLIT — progression-free survival benefit without a significant overall-survival benefit, on a single-trial base (TOURMALINE-MM1, three reports of one trial). Adding oral ixazomib to lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged median progression-free survival (20.6 vs 14.7 months; hazard ratio 0.74, a relative measure) and raised overall response (78% vs 72%). At the final analysis, with median follow-up of 85 months, median overall survival was 53.6 vs 51.6 months (hazard ratio 0.939, relative, not significant, P=.495) — the PFS win did not convert to a significant survival win on intention-to-treat analysis, and a subsequent-therapy-adjusted modelling analysis is carded only as a labelled sensitivity analysis, never as the survival headline. Serious adverse events were similar (47% vs 49%); grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia and rash were more frequent with ixazomib. Cross-point: ixazomib maintenance in newly diagnosed myeloma is a different setting and question (shelf #7434).

cards.headline: TOURMALINE-MM1 phase 3 primary (Moreau 2016): ixazomib + lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 20.6 vs 14.7 months (hazard ratio 0.74, relative)
cards.summary: TOURMALINE-MM1 phase 3 primary (Moreau 2016): ixazomib + lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 20.6 vs 14.7 months (hazard ratio 0.74, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (TOURMALINE-MM1), ixazomib + lenalidomide–dexamethasone vs placebo + lenalidomide–dexamethasone
cards.people: 722 patients with relapsed, refractory, or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma, randomised double-blind to ixazomib plus lenalidomide–dexamethasone or placebo plus lenalidomide–dexamethasone.
cards.result: At median follow-up 14.7 months, median progression-free survival was 20.6 vs 14.7 months (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.74; P=0.01 — a relative measure), with benefit in all prespecified subgroups including high-risk cytogenetics. Overall response was 78% vs 72% and complete response plus very good partial response 48% vs 39% (absolute rates). Serious adverse events occurred in 47% vs 49%; grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia was more frequent with ixazomib (grade 3: 12% vs 5%; grade 4: 7% vs 4%), as was rash (36% vs 23%); peripheral neuropathy occurred in 27% vs 22% (grade 3 in 2% in each group).
cards.watchOut: One trial is the whole comparative base for this question; overall survival was immature at this primary report — the final survival read is carded separately below and is null.

cards.headline: TOURMALINE-MM1 final overall survival (Richardson 2021): at 85 months, median overall survival 53.6 vs 51.6 months — hazard ratio 0.939, NOT significant (P=.495)
cards.summary: TOURMALINE-MM1 final overall survival (Richardson 2021): at 85 months, median overall survival 53.6 vs 51.6 months — hazard ratio 0.939, NOT significant (P=.495)
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the TOURMALINE-MM1 phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 722 randomised patients as the primary report (360 ixazomib-Rd, 362 placebo-Rd), followed to a median of 85 months; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint, analysed intention-to-treat.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 53.6 months with ixazomib-Rd vs 51.6 months with placebo-Rd (hazard ratio 0.939, a relative measure; P=.495 — not significant). Lower hazard ratios favouring ixazomib-Rd were seen in prespecified subgroups including refractory disease, stage III disease and high-risk cytogenetics — subgroup reads, not the headline. After study treatment, 71.7% vs 69.9% received at least one further anticancer therapy, with imbalances in subsequent daratumumab (24.7% vs 33.9%) and proteasome-inhibitor use that the authors note confound survival interpretation. New primary malignancies occurred in 10.3% vs 11.9%, with no new safety concerns.

cards.headline: Subsequent-therapy-adjusted survival analysis (Ramasamy 2024): modelling adjustments moved the survival hazard ratio from 0.94 to 0.89 — a labelled sensitivity analysis, never the headline
cards.summary: Subsequent-therapy-adjusted survival analysis (Ramasamy 2024): modelling adjustments moved the survival hazard ratio from 0.94 to 0.89 — a labelled sensitivity analysis, never the headline
cards.type: Sensitivity analysis: subsequent-therapy-adjusted modelling of TOURMALINE-MM1 overall survival (same trial — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The TOURMALINE-MM1 intention-to-treat population (the same 722 randomised patients), re-analysed with statistical models adjusting for subsequent therapies received after study treatment.
cards.result: The unadjusted hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.94 (95% CI 0.78–1.13). After adjustment by the rank-preserving structural failure time model, the estimated hazard ratio was 0.89 (95% CI 0.74–1.07); inverse-probability-of-censoring and marginal-structural-model adjustments also moved the estimate in ixazomib's favour, most markedly in the subgroup with at least 2 prior lines (hazard ratios 0.52 by those methods, 0.68 by the structural failure time model). All are relative measures from modelling assumptions, and the intention-to-treat confidence intervals include no effect.
cards.watchOut: A modelling adjustment, carded only as a labelled sensitivity analysis exactly as the commissioning row directs: it does not overturn the null intention-to-treat survival result and must never be quoted as the trial's survival finding.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — ixazomib-Rd prolonged progression-free survival (20.6 vs 14.7 months) but did not significantly prolong overall survival at 85 months (53.6 vs 51.6 months, P=.495)

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf — all are reports of the single TOURMALINE-MM1 trial.
cards.result: TOURMALINE-MM1 is the entire evidence base: a statistically significant relative progression-free survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.74) with higher response rates, no statistically significant overall-survival benefit at the final 85-month analysis (hazard ratio 0.939), and a subsequent-therapy-adjusted analysis that remains a sensitivity analysis. Harms were modestly increased thrombocytopenia and rash, with serious adverse events similar between arms (47% vs 49%). The all-oral triplet is the regimen's practical distinction.
cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence — one trial, three reports; there is no second randomised trial of this question to card. See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Ixazomib maintenance in newly diagnosed myeloma (TOURMALINE-MM3/MM4): PFS benefit in both trials, no overall-survival benefit in either
shelves.question: In patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who responded to induction — after autologous stem-cell transplantation (TOURMALINE-MM3) or without transplantation (TOURMALINE-MM4) — does fixed-duration single-agent ixazomib maintenance, versus placebo, prolong progression-free survival, and does it prolong overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Antineoplastic Agents · Boron Compounds · Disease Progression · Double-Blind Method · Female · Glycine · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Stem Cell Transplantation · Time Factors · Transplantation, Autologous · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: SPLIT — consistent relative progression-free survival benefit in both trials, no overall-survival benefit in either at final analysis. Post-transplant (TOURMALINE-MM3): median PFS 26.5 vs 21.3 months (hazard ratio 0.72, relative). Without transplant (TOURMALINE-MM4): median PFS from randomisation 17.4 vs 9.4 months (hazard ratio 0.659, relative). At final survival analysis (~8 years in MM3, ~5 years in MM4), median overall survival was not reached in either MM3 arm (hazard ratio 1.025, relative, not significant) and was 64.8 vs 69.5 months in MM4 (hazard ratio 1.090, relative, not significant) — both halves belong on the face. The two populations are labelled separately and never pooled. Maintenance was fixed-duration (up to 26 cycles / 24 months). Cross-points in prose only: lenalidomide maintenance after transplant (live #675) is the established comparator strategy, and ixazomib in relapsed disease is shelf #7433.

cards.headline: TOURMALINE-MM3 phase 3 (Dimopoulos 2019): post-transplant ixazomib maintenance prolonged progression-free survival — median 26.5 vs 21.3 months (hazard ratio 0.72, relative)
cards.summary: TOURMALINE-MM3 phase 3 (Dimopoulos 2019): post-transplant ixazomib maintenance prolonged progression-free survival — median 26.5 vs 21.3 months (hazard ratio 0.72, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (TOURMALINE-MM3), ixazomib maintenance vs placebo after autologous transplantation
cards.people: 656 adults with newly diagnosed symptomatic multiple myeloma who had at least a partial response after induction, high-dose melphalan and single autologous stem-cell transplantation, randomised 3:2 to oral ixazomib (395) or placebo (261) on days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles for 2 years (167 sites, 30 countries).
cards.result: At median follow-up 31 months, ixazomib reduced the risk of progression or death by 28% relative (median progression-free survival 26.5 vs 21.3 months; hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.58–0.89; P=.0023). Serious adverse events occurred in 108 (27%) of 394 ixazomib patients vs 51 (20%) of 259 placebo patients; one patient died on ixazomib during treatment and none on placebo. Second malignancies were not increased (3% vs 3%).
cards.watchOut: Post-transplant population only — do not apply this read to transplant-ineligible patients (that is TOURMALINE-MM4, carded separately). Overall survival was immature here; the final survival read is carded below and is null.

Lancet (London, England). 2019. PMID: 30545780. Registry ID: NCT02181413. cards.headline: TOURMALINE-MM4 phase 3 (Dimopoulos 2020): ixazomib maintenance without transplant prolonged progression-free survival — median 17.4 vs 9.4 months from randomisation (hazard ratio 0.659, relative)
cards.summary: TOURMALINE-MM4 phase 3 (Dimopoulos 2020): ixazomib maintenance without transplant prolonged progression-free survival — median 17.4 vs 9.4 months from randomisation (hazard ratio 0.659, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (TOURMALINE-MM4), ixazomib maintenance vs placebo in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed myeloma
cards.people: 706 patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma not undergoing autologous transplantation who had at least a partial response after 6–12 months of standard induction, randomised 3:2 to ixazomib (425) or placebo (281) on days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles for 24 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival from randomisation was 17.4 vs 9.4 months (hazard ratio 0.659, 95% CI 0.542–0.801; P<.001 — a 34.1% relative reduction in the risk of progression or death), with larger benefit in patients in complete or very good partial response after induction (25.6 vs 12.9 months; hazard ratio 0.586). Grade 3-or-worse treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 36.6% vs 23.2%; discontinuation for adverse events in 12.9% vs 8.0%; nausea (26.8% vs 8.0%), vomiting (24.2% vs 4.3%) and diarrhoea (23.2% vs 12.3%) were more common with ixazomib. New primary malignancies were not increased (5.2% vs 6.2%); on-study deaths were 2.6% vs 2.2%.
cards.watchOut: Transplant-ineligible population after induction — a different slice from MM3's post-transplant population; the two trials are never pooled on this shelf. Overall survival was immature here; the final read is carded below and is null.

cards.headline: Joint final overall survival, MM3 + MM4 (Dimopoulos 2025): NO survival benefit in either trial — MM3 hazard ratio 1.025; MM4 median 64.8 vs 69.5 months, hazard ratio 1.090 (both not significant)
cards.summary: Joint final overall survival, MM3 + MM4 (Dimopoulos 2025): NO survival benefit in either trial — MM3 hazard ratio 1.025; MM4 median 64.8 vs 69.5 months, hazard ratio 1.090 (both not significant)
cards.type: Joint final overall-survival analysis of the TOURMALINE-MM3 and TOURMALINE-MM4 phase 3 trials (same two trials as the cards above — not independent trials)
cards.people: The TOURMALINE-MM3 (656 randomised, post-transplant) and TOURMALINE-MM4 (706 randomised, transplant-ineligible) populations, each analysed separately at final overall-survival analysis, at median follow-up of approximately 8 years (MM3) and 5 years (MM4).
cards.result: In MM3, median overall survival was not reached in either arm (hazard ratio 1.025, 95% CI 0.789–1.332; P=.850 — a relative measure, not significant). In MM4, median overall survival was 64.8 months with ixazomib vs 69.5 months with placebo (hazard ratio 1.090, 95% CI 0.861–1.381; P=.473 — relative, not significant; the point estimate numerically favours placebo). No new safety signals were identified in either study and new primary malignancies were uncommon. The authors note that effective salvage therapies make demonstrating a survival advantage in front-line myeloma increasingly challenging.
cards.watchOut: The survival headline of this shelf: despite both trials meeting their progression-free survival endpoints, NEITHER showed a statistically significant overall-survival difference at final analysis.

shelves.title: Elotuzumab + IMiD in relapsed myeloma (ELOQUENT-2/3): PFS and overall-survival benefit with both backbones; frontline ELOQUENT-1 was negative (cross-pointed)
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, does adding the SLAMF7 antibody elotuzumab to lenalidomide–dexamethasone (ELOQUENT-2) or to pomalidomide–dexamethasone in lenalidomide- and proteasome-inhibitor-exposed disease (ELOQUENT-3) prolong progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Dexamethasone · Disease-Free Survival · Humans · Lenalidomide · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Receptors, Immunologic · Recurrence · Signaling Lymphocytic Activation Molecule Family · Thalidomide
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit, on two randomised trials with two different immunomodulatory backbones, labelled separately and never pooled. With lenalidomide–dexamethasone (ELOQUENT-2, phase 3, n=646): median progression-free survival 19.4 vs 14.9 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative) and, at final analysis, median overall survival 48.3 vs 39.6 months (hazard ratio 0.82, relative; P=.0408). With pomalidomide–dexamethasone in lenalidomide- and proteasome-inhibitor-exposed disease (ELOQUENT-3, randomised phase 2, n=117): median progression-free survival 10.3 vs 4.7 months (hazard ratio 0.54, relative) and median overall survival 29.8 vs 17.4 months (hazard ratio 0.59, relative; P=.0217). Infusion reactions were uncommon and mostly low-grade (10% in ELOQUENT-2; 5% in ELOQUENT-3). Cross-point, never silent: the programme's frontline trial ELOQUENT-1 (elotuzumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone in newly diagnosed, transplant-ineligible myeloma, PMID 35550060) was NEGATIVE for progression-free survival (31.4 vs 29.5 months; hazard ratio 0.93; P=.44) — a different setting, not carded into this relapsed shelf's balance, and not evidence for the relapsed question either way.

cards.headline: ELOQUENT-2 phase 3 primary (Lonial 2015): elotuzumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 19.4 vs 14.9 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative); response 79% vs 66%
cards.summary: ELOQUENT-2 phase 3 primary (Lonial 2015): elotuzumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 19.4 vs 14.9 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative); response 79% vs 66%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (ELOQUENT-2), elotuzumab + lenalidomide–dexamethasone vs lenalidomide–dexamethasone
cards.people: 646 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, randomised to elotuzumab plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone (321) or lenalidomide and dexamethasone alone (325).
cards.result: At median follow-up 24.5 months, median progression-free survival was 19.4 vs 14.9 months (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.70, 95% CI 0.57–0.85; P<.001 — described by the authors as a significant 30% relative reduction in the risk of progression or death). Overall response was 79% vs 66% (absolute rates; P<.001). Common grade 3–4 adverse events were lymphocytopenia, neutropenia, fatigue and pneumonia. Infusion reactions occurred in 33 patients (10%) in the elotuzumab group and were grade 1 or 2 in 29 of them.

cards.headline: ELOQUENT-2 final overall survival (Dimopoulos 2020): median overall survival 48.3 vs 39.6 months — hazard ratio 0.82, relative (P=.0408)
cards.summary: ELOQUENT-2 final overall survival (Dimopoulos 2020): median overall survival 48.3 vs 39.6 months — hazard ratio 0.82, relative (P=.0408)
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the ELOQUENT-2 phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 646 ELOQUENT-2 patients (1–3 prior lines of therapy), at the pre-planned final overall-survival analysis after a minimum follow-up of 70.6 months and 427 deaths.
cards.result: Elotuzumab plus lenalidomide/dexamethasone improved median overall survival by 8.7 months over lenalidomide/dexamethasone alone (48.3 vs 39.6 months; hazard ratio 0.82, 95.4% CI 0.68–1.00; P=.0408 — a relative measure, statistically significant against the allotted alpha), with benefit consistently observed across predefined subgroups and greatest in patients with adverse prognostic factors. No additional safety signals emerged at extended follow-up.
cards.watchOut: The upper confidence limit touches 1.00 (95.4% CI 0.68–1.00) — a significant but borderline survival read; quote it with its interval, not as a large survival effect.

cards.headline: ELOQUENT-3 randomised phase 2 primary (Dimopoulos 2018): elotuzumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 10.3 vs 4.7 months (hazard ratio 0.54, relative); response 53% vs 26%
cards.summary: ELOQUENT-3 randomised phase 2 primary (Dimopoulos 2018): elotuzumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 10.3 vs 4.7 months (hazard ratio 0.54, relative); response 53% vs 26%
cards.type: Randomised phase 2 trial (ELOQUENT-3), elotuzumab + pomalidomide–dexamethasone vs pomalidomide–dexamethasone
cards.people: 117 patients with multiple myeloma refractory or relapsed and refractory to lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, randomised to elotuzumab plus pomalidomide and dexamethasone (60) or pomalidomide and dexamethasone alone (57).
cards.result: After a minimum follow-up of 9.1 months, median progression-free survival was 10.3 vs 4.7 months (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.54, 95% CI 0.34–0.86; P=.008 — a relative measure). Overall response was 53% vs 26% (absolute rates). The most common grade 3–4 adverse events were neutropenia (13% with elotuzumab vs 27% control), anaemia (10% vs 20%) and hyperglycaemia (8% vs 7%); infections occurred in 65% of each group. Infusion reactions occurred in 3 patients (5%) in the elotuzumab group.
cards.watchOut: A small randomised phase 2 (n=117 — the N belongs on the face) in a more refractory, lenalidomide- and proteasome-inhibitor-exposed population than ELOQUENT-2; never pool its read with ELOQUENT-2's.
cards.source: Dimopoulos MA et al. Elotuzumab plus Pomalidomide and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma. The New England journal of medicine. 2018. PMID: 30403938. Registry ID: NCT02654132. cards.headline: ELOQUENT-3 final overall survival (Dimopoulos 2023): median overall survival 29.8 vs 17.4 months — hazard ratio 0.59, relative (P=.0217)
cards.summary: ELOQUENT-3 final overall survival (Dimopoulos 2023): median overall survival 29.8 vs 17.4 months — hazard ratio 0.59, relative (P=.0217)
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the randomised phase 2 ELOQUENT-3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 117 ELOQUENT-3 patients (60 elotuzumab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone, 57 pomalidomide–dexamethasone), all previously treated with lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor with disease refractory to last therapy; 37 (61.7%) deaths in the elotuzumab group and 41 (74.5%) among treated control patients.
cards.result: Median overall survival was significantly improved with elotuzumab plus pomalidomide/dexamethasone (29.8 months, 95% CI 22.9–45.7) versus pomalidomide/dexamethasone alone (17.4 months, 95% CI 13.8–27.7; hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.37–0.93; P=.0217 — a relative measure), with benefit in most subgroups. The safety profile was consistent with prior reports, with no new signals.
cards.watchOut: A survival win from a 117-patient phase 2 trial: the effect estimate is large but the confidence interval is wide (0.37–0.93); it supports, and does not replace, the phase 3 ELOQUENT-2 read.

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (ELOQUENT-2, n=646; ELOQUENT-3, n=117).
cards.result: Both randomised comparisons favoured elotuzumab on progression-free survival and, at final analysis, on overall survival, with infusion reactions uncommon and mostly low-grade. The pomalidomide trial was small (n=117) and in a more refractory population; the lenalidomide trial's survival confidence interval touches 1.00. Neither read is pooled with the other.

See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone in relapsed myeloma (PANORAMA-1/2): PFS win, no survival win, heavy diarrhoea and thrombocytopenia
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or relapsed-and-refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 prior regimens, does adding the pan-deacetylase inhibitor panobinostat to bortezomib–dexamethasone, versus placebo plus bortezomib–dexamethasone, prolong progression-free and overall survival — and in bortezomib-refractory disease, what response does the combination produce (PANORAMA-2) — at what gastrointestinal and haematologic cost?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Boronic Acids · Bortezomib · Dexamethasone · Disease-Free Survival · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Double-Blind Method · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Humans · Hydroxamic Acids · Indoles · Infusions, Intravenous · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Maximum Tolerated Dose · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Panobinostat · Prognosis · Pyrazines · Remission Induction · Survival Analysis · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: SPLIT — a progression-free survival win with no overall-survival win, at a heavy gastrointestinal and haematologic cost. PANORAMA-1 (phase 3, n=768): median progression-free survival 11.99 vs 8.08 months (hazard ratio 0.63, relative), but final median overall survival was 40.3 vs 35.8 months (hazard ratio 0.94, relative, not significant, P=.54). Grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia occurred in 67% vs 31%, diarrhoea in 26% vs 8% and fatigue/asthenia in 24% vs 12%; serious adverse events in 60% vs 42%. PANORAMA-2 (phase 2, n=55) is single-arm support in bortezomib-refractory disease (response 34.5%, uncontrolled) and is never presented as comparative. Product naming (clarification exception): panobinostat (Farydak, Novartis/Secura Bio lineage as published) — a product whose boxed-warning history and restricted uptake followed its diarrhoea and fatigue burden.

cards.headline: PANORAMA-1 phase 3 primary (San-Miguel 2014): panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 11.99 vs 8.08 months (hazard ratio 0.63, relative) — with far more thrombocytopenia and diarrhoea
cards.summary: PANORAMA-1 phase 3 primary (San-Miguel 2014): panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival — median 11.99 vs 8.08 months (hazard ratio 0.63, relative) — with far more thrombocytopenia and diarrhoea
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (PANORAMA-1), panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone vs placebo + bortezomib–dexamethasone
cards.people: 768 patients with relapsed or relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 previous regimens, randomised double-blind to panobinostat (387) or placebo (381), each with bortezomib and dexamethasone.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 11.99 vs 8.08 months (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.52–0.76; P<.0001 — a relative measure). Overall response did not differ (60.7% vs 54.6%; P=.09), though complete or near-complete response was higher with panobinostat (27.6% vs 15.7%). Overall survival was immature (hazard ratio 0.87, not significant). Serious adverse events were reported in 60% vs 42%. Grade 3–4 events included thrombocytopenia (67% vs 31%), lymphopenia (53% vs 40%), diarrhoea (26% vs 8%), asthenia or fatigue (24% vs 12%) and peripheral neuropathy (18% vs 15%).
cards.watchOut: The progression benefit came with substantially more grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea and fatigue — the pricing harms of this class. Overall survival was immature at this report; the final read is carded below and is null.

cards.headline: PANORAMA-1 final overall survival (San-Miguel 2016): median overall survival 40.3 vs 35.8 months — hazard ratio 0.94, NOT significant (P=.54)
cards.summary: PANORAMA-1 final overall survival (San-Miguel 2016): median overall survival 40.3 vs 35.8 months — hazard ratio 0.94, NOT significant (P=.54)
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the PANORAMA-1 phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 768 PANORAMA-1 patients, at the final overall-survival analysis (data cutoff June 29, 2015; 415 deaths).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 40.3 months (95% CI 35.0–44.8) with panobinostat plus bortezomib and dexamethasone vs 35.8 months (95% CI 29.0–40.6) with placebo plus bortezomib and dexamethasone (hazard ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.78–1.14; P=.54 — a relative measure, not significant). In the subgroup with at least two previous regimens including bortezomib and an immunomodulatory drug, median overall survival was 25.5 vs 19.5 months (hazard ratio 1.01 — no difference). The authors describe the survival benefit as modest and suggest regimen optimisation would need further trials.
cards.watchOut: The survival headline of this shelf: the progression-free survival benefit did NOT convert to a significant overall-survival benefit.

cards.headline: PANORAMA-2 phase 2 (Richardson 2013): in bortezomib-refractory disease, panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone produced a 34.5% response rate — SINGLE-ARM, uncontrolled
cards.summary: PANORAMA-2 phase 2 (Richardson 2013): in bortezomib-refractory disease, panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone produced a 34.5% response rate — SINGLE-ARM, uncontrolled
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial (PANORAMA-2), panobinostat + bortezomib–dexamethasone in bortezomib-refractory myeloma — uncontrolled
cards.people: 55 heavily pretreated patients with relapsed and bortezomib-refractory multiple myeloma (median 4 prior regimens, including a median of 2 prior bortezomib-containing regimens; all had progressed on or within 60 days of their last bortezomib-based therapy), treated with panobinostat plus bortezomib and dexamethasone, with no comparator arm.
cards.result: The overall response rate was 34.5% (1 near-complete response and 18 partial responses); a further 10 patients achieved minimal response, for a clinical benefit rate of 52.7%. Median progression-free survival was 5.4 months and median duration of response 6.0 months. Common grade 3/4 adverse events included thrombocytopenia (63.6%), fatigue (20.0%) and diarrhoea (20.0%); only 1 patient had grade 3 peripheral neuropathy.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm with 55 patients: the 34.5% response rate is uncontrolled and must never be presented as comparative evidence; it is support for activity in a refractory slice only.

cards.headline: Synthesis: panobinostat added to bortezomib–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival (11.99 vs 8.08 months) but not overall survival (40.3 vs 35.8 months, P=.54), with substantially more thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea and fatigue; PANORAMA-2 adds only single-arm refractory-disease support
cards.summary: Synthesis: panobinostat added to bortezomib–dexamethasone prolonged progression-free survival (11.99 vs 8.08 months) but not overall survival (40.3 vs 35.8 months, P=.54), with substantially more thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea and fatigue; PANORAMA-2 adds only single-arm refractory-disease support
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (PANORAMA-1, n=768 randomised; PANORAMA-2, n=55 single-arm).
cards.result: The randomised evidence is one phase 3 trial: a clear relative progression-free survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.63), no significant overall-survival benefit at final analysis (hazard ratio 0.94), and a heavy toxicity price (grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia 67% vs 31%; diarrhoea 26% vs 8%; serious adverse events 60% vs 42%). PANORAMA-2 shows the combination can recapture responses in bortezomib-refractory disease, without a comparator.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Melflufen + dexamethasone in relapsed myeloma (HORIZON/OCEAN): WITHDRAWN product — PFS win over pomalidomide, survival favoured pomalidomide
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma — heavily pretreated, including triple-class-refractory disease (HORIZON) — does the peptide–drug conjugate melphalan flufenamide plus dexamethasone produce responses, and against pomalidomide–dexamethasone in lenalidomide-refractory disease (OCEAN) does it prolong progression-free survival without an overall-survival cost?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Dexamethasone · Disease Progression · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm · Europe · Female · Humans · Male · Melphalan · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma · Phenylalanine · Progression-Free Survival · Recurrence · Time Factors · United States
shelves.balance: WITHDRAWN PRODUCT — this history leads the shelf: melphalan flufenamide (melflufen; Pepaxto/Pepaxti, Oncopeptides) was withdrawn from the US market in 2021 after the OCEAN survival signal, and the EU authorisation was later revoked. The evidence is SPLIT: in OCEAN (phase 3, n=495), melflufen plus dexamethasone beat pomalidomide plus dexamethasone on progression-free survival (median 6.8 vs 4.9 months; hazard ratio 0.79, relative) but overall survival numerically favoured the comparator (median 19.8 vs 25.0 months; hazard ratio 1.10, relative, not significant), with grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia in 63% vs 11%. HORIZON (phase 2, n=157) is single-arm support in heavily pretreated, largely triple-class-refractory disease (response 29%, uncontrolled). A longer-follow-up benefit–risk analysis exploring post-transplant-timing subgroups is carded as a labelled subgroup analysis, not a rescue of the survival read. OCEAN belongs to this shelf; the pomalidomide shelf cross-points it in prose only.

cards.headline: HORIZON phase 2 (Richardson 2021): melflufen + dexamethasone in heavily pretreated myeloma — response 29% (26% in triple-class-refractory disease), median PFS 4.2 months — SINGLE-ARM, uncontrolled
cards.summary: HORIZON phase 2 (Richardson 2021): melflufen + dexamethasone in heavily pretreated myeloma — response 29% (26% in triple-class-refractory disease), median PFS 4.2 months — SINGLE-ARM, uncontrolled
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial (HORIZON), melflufen + dexamethasone in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory myeloma — uncontrolled
cards.people: 157 treated patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma refractory to pomalidomide and/or an anti-CD38 antibody (median age 65 years; median 5 prior lines; 119 patients, 76%, had triple-class-refractory disease; 35% had extramedullary disease), treated with melflufen 40 mg intravenously on day 1 of each 28-day cycle plus weekly dexamethasone, with no comparator arm.
cards.result: The overall response rate was 29% in all treated patients and 26% in the triple-class-refractory population. Median duration of response was 5.5 months, median progression-free survival 4.2 months and median overall survival 11.6 months at median follow-up 14 months — all uncontrolled. Grade 3-or-worse treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 96% of patients, most commonly neutropenia (79%), thrombocytopenia (76%) and anaemia (43%); pneumonia (10%) was the most common grade 3/4 non-haematologic event.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: every number on this card is uncontrolled and describes activity in a heavily pretreated population only; the comparative evidence is OCEAN, carded below.

cards.headline: OCEAN phase 3 (Schjesvold 2022): melflufen + dexamethasone beat pomalidomide + dexamethasone on PFS (6.8 vs 4.9 months; hazard ratio 0.79, relative) but overall survival favoured pomalidomide (19.8 vs 25.0 months; hazard ratio 1.10, not significant)
cards.summary: OCEAN phase 3 (Schjesvold 2022): melflufen + dexamethasone beat pomalidomide + dexamethasone on PFS (6.8 vs 4.9 months; hazard ratio 0.79, relative) but overall survival favoured pomalidomide (19.8 vs 25.0 months; hazard ratio 1.10, not significant)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised head-to-head open-label trial (OCEAN), melflufen + dexamethasone vs pomalidomide + dexamethasone
cards.people: 495 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma refractory to lenalidomide and to their last line of therapy, after 2–4 previous lines including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, randomised to melflufen plus dexamethasone (246) or pomalidomide plus dexamethasone (249) at 108 centres in 21 countries.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 6.8 vs 4.9 months (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.64–0.98; P=.032 — a relative measure). Median overall survival was 19.8 vs 25.0 months (hazard ratio 1.10, 95% CI 0.85–1.44; P=.47 — relative, not significant; the direction favours the pomalidomide comparator). The most common grade 3–4 treatment-emergent adverse events were thrombocytopenia (63% of 228 in the melflufen safety population vs 11% of 246), neutropenia (54% vs 41%) and anaemia (43% vs 18%). Serious treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 42% vs 46%; fatal treatment-emergent adverse events in 12% vs 13%.
cards.watchOut: The survival direction favours the comparator — the signal behind the product's US withdrawal in 2021. Open-label trial conducted partly during the COVID-19 period (COVID-19 pneumonia appears among serious events in both arms).
cards.source: Schjesvold FH et al. Melflufen or pomalidomide plus dexamethasone for patients with multiple myeloma refractory to lenalidomide (OCEAN): a randomised, head-to-head, open-label, phase 3 study. The Lancet. Haematology. 2022. PMID: 35032434. Registry ID: NCT03151811. cards.headline: Benefit–risk analysis with longer follow-up (Sonneveld 2023): OCEAN survival differences tracked post-transplant timing subgroups — a labelled subgroup analysis, not a reversal of the survival read
cards.summary: Benefit–risk analysis with longer follow-up (Sonneveld 2023): OCEAN survival differences tracked post-transplant timing subgroups — a labelled subgroup analysis, not a reversal of the survival read
cards.type: Benefit–risk subgroup analysis of the OCEAN and HORIZON studies with longer follow-up (same trials as the cards above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: Updated data from OCEAN (495 randomised) and HORIZON (157 treated), re-analysed by prognostic subgroups including previous autologous stem-cell transplantation and time to progression after transplantation.
cards.result: In OCEAN, age (P=.011; patients under 65 favoured pomalidomide) and transplant history (P=.001; no previous transplant or progression more than 36 months after transplant favoured melflufen) were prognostic for overall survival. Excluding patients who progressed within 36 months of transplantation (145 melflufen, 148 pomalidomide), median overall survival was 23.6 vs 19.8 months (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.62–1.12; P=.22 — relative, not significant). In HORIZON's triple-class-refractory population, patients progressing within 36 months of transplant had lower response and shorter progression-free survival. Safety was consistent with previous reports.
cards.watchOut: Post-hoc subgroup exploration: the transplant-timing slices are hypothesis-generating, the subgroup survival comparison is not significant, and none of it changes the headline — a PFS win with a numerically worse overall survival that preceded market withdrawal.
cards.source: Sonneveld P et al. Benefit Versus Risk Assessment of Melflufen and Dexamethasone in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Analyses From Longer Follow-up of the OCEAN and HORIZON Studies. Clinical lymphoma, myeloma & leukemia. 2023. PMID: 37355418. Registry ID: NCT03151811. cards.headline: Synthesis: a withdrawn product with a split record — OCEAN showed a PFS win over pomalidomide (6.8 vs 4.9 months) with overall survival numerically favouring pomalidomide (19.8 vs 25.0 months) and far more thrombocytopenia; HORIZON adds only single-arm activity in triple-class-refractory disease
cards.summary: Synthesis: a withdrawn product with a split record — OCEAN showed a PFS win over pomalidomide (6.8 vs 4.9 months) with overall survival numerically favouring pomalidomide (19.8 vs 25.0 months) and far more thrombocytopenia; HORIZON adds only single-arm activity in triple-class-refractory disease
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (HORIZON, n=157 single-arm; OCEAN, n=495 randomised).
cards.result: Melphalan flufenamide plus dexamethasone produced responses in heavily pretreated disease (29% in HORIZON, uncontrolled) and superior progression-free survival against an active comparator in OCEAN, but overall survival pointed the other way and grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia was six times as frequent (63% vs 11%). The product was withdrawn from the US market in 2021 after the OCEAN survival signal and its EU authorisation was later revoked; the longer-follow-up subgroup analyses do not reverse that record.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
