cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial (ALTER0303, three reports) — anlotinib beat placebo on survival and progression-free survival in third-line-or-later NSCLC, with better quality of life and hypertension as the signature harm
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial (ALTER0303, three reports) — anlotinib beat placebo on survival and progression-free survival in third-line-or-later NSCLC, with better quality of life and hypertension as the signature harm
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (the single ALTER0303 trial and its reports).
cards.result: In patients progressing after at least two lines of therapy, anlotinib prolonged median overall survival from 6.3 to 9.6 months (hazard ratio 0.68, relative) and median progression-free survival from 1.4 to 5.4 months (hazard ratio 0.25, relative) versus placebo, with quality of life favouring anlotinib on most scales and grade ≥3 hypertension and hyponatraemia as the commonest high-grade harms. The histology subgroup read was significant for survival in adenocarcinoma and not in squamous disease. This is a single-trial, single-region (China) shelf from the pre-chemo-immunotherapy era.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: CLEOPATRA: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab–docetaxel prolonged survival in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (median 56.5 vs 40.8 months) — one trial, three reports
shelves.question: In patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, does adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel prolong progression-free and overall survival versus trastuzumab plus docetaxel alone?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Breast Neoplasms · Disease-Free Survival · Docetaxel · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Taxoids · Trastuzumab · Ventricular Dysfunction, Left · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — on one trial reported three times (CLEOPATRA, 808 randomised), labelled a single-programme shelf. Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel prolonged median progression-free survival from 12.4 to 18.5 months (hazard ratio 0.62, a relative measure) and median overall survival from 40.8 to 56.5 months at the final analysis (hazard ratio 0.68; 15.7-month absolute median difference), maintained at end of study (57.1 vs 40.8 months; 8-year survival 37% vs 23%). The survival analyses are unadjusted for crossover and therefore conservative. Added toxicity was grade 3 or above febrile neutropenia and diarrhoea, with no increase in left ventricular systolic dysfunction. The PUFFIN bridging trial is a separate regional programme — cross-point only, never pooled.

cards.headline: CLEOPATRA primary report (Baselga 2012): median progression-free survival 18.5 vs 12.4 months with pertuzumab added (hazard ratio 0.62 — a relative measure, absolutes beside it)
cards.summary: CLEOPATRA primary report (Baselga 2012): median progression-free survival 18.5 vs 12.4 months with pertuzumab added (hazard ratio 0.62 — a relative measure, absolutes beside it)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised placebo-controlled trial (CLEOPATRA) — primary report, one trial of which the following cards are later reports
cards.people: 808 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer randomised to placebo plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel or pertuzumab plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel as first-line treatment, until progression or unmanageable toxicity; the primary endpoint was independently assessed progression-free survival.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 18.5 months in the pertuzumab group versus 12.4 months in the control group (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.62, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.75; P<0.001 — a relative measure, with the absolute medians printed here). The interim overall-survival analysis showed a strong trend favouring pertuzumab. Safety was generally similar, with no increase in left ventricular systolic dysfunction; grade 3 or above febrile neutropenia and diarrhoea were more frequent in the pertuzumab group.
cards.watchOut: One trial, three reports: this shelf is a single-programme shelf and the three cards must not be counted as three trials. Overall survival at this report was an interim trend, not the final result.
cards.source: Baselga J et al. Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel for metastatic breast cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2012. PMID: 22149875. Registry ID: NCT00567190. cards.headline: CLEOPATRA final overall-survival analysis (Swain 2015): median overall survival 56.5 vs 40.8 months (hazard ratio 0.68 — a relative measure; a 15.7-month absolute median difference)
cards.summary: CLEOPATRA final overall-survival analysis (Swain 2015): median overall survival 56.5 vs 40.8 months (hazard ratio 0.68 — a relative measure; a 15.7-month absolute median difference)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (CLEOPATRA) — final prespecified overall-survival report of the same trial
cards.people: The CLEOPATRA population (808 randomised) with median follow-up of 50 months; the prespecified final overall-survival analysis, with sensitivity analyses adjusted for patients who crossed over from placebo to pertuzumab after the interim analysis.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 56.5 months (95% CI 49.3 to not reached) with pertuzumab versus 40.8 months (95% CI 35.8 to 48.3) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.84; P<0.001 — a relative measure; absolute median difference 15.7 months). The analysis was not adjusted for crossover and is therefore conservative; crossover-adjusted sensitivity analyses were consistent. Investigator-assessed median progression-free survival improved by 6.3 months (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.80), and median duration of response was extended by 7.7 months. Most adverse events occurred during docetaxel administration, and long-term cardiac safety was maintained.
cards.watchOut: Crossover from placebo to pertuzumab after the interim analysis dilutes the control arm's disadvantage, so the unadjusted 15.7-month median difference is, if anything, an underestimate — the opposite of the usual crossover concern, and stated by the authors.
cards.source: Swain SM et al. Pertuzumab, trastuzumab, and docetaxel in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2015. PMID: 25693012. Registry ID: NCT00567190. cards.headline: CLEOPATRA end-of-study report (Swain 2020): at over 8 years, median overall survival 57.1 vs 40.8 months and 8-year survival 37% vs 23%
cards.summary: CLEOPATRA end-of-study report (Swain 2020): at over 8 years, median overall survival 57.1 vs 40.8 months and 8-year survival 37% vs 23%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (CLEOPATRA) — end-of-study report of the same trial (descriptive analyses)
cards.people: 808 patients enrolled and randomised at 204 centres in 25 countries (402 pertuzumab, 406 placebo), with median follow-up 99.9 months in the pertuzumab group and 98.7 months in the placebo group; 50 patients crossed from placebo to pertuzumab between July 2012 and the November 2018 clinical cutoff. Analyses are descriptive, the confirmatory survival analysis having already occurred.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 57.1 months (95% CI 50 to 72) with pertuzumab versus 40.8 months (36 to 48) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.82 — a relative measure, absolutes beside it); 8-year landmark overall survival was 37% (95% CI 31 to 42) versus 23% (19 to 28). The most common grade 3–4 adverse event was neutropenia (200 of 408 [49%] pertuzumab, 183 of 396 [46%] placebo). Treatment-related deaths occurred in 5 (1%) pertuzumab and 6 (2%) placebo patients. One new serious adverse event suggestive of congestive heart failure (pertuzumab group) and one new symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction (post-crossover) occurred since the previous analysis.
cards.watchOut: Descriptive end-of-study analyses (the confirmatory analysis had already occurred) and unadjusted for crossover, hence conservative; still the same single trial — not independent confirmation.

Pertuzumab, trastuzumab, and docetaxel for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (CLEOPATRA): end-of-study results from a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study. The Lancet. Oncology. 2020. PMID: 32171426. Registry ID: NCT00567190. shelves.title: APHINITY: adjuvant pertuzumab improved disease-free survival in node-positive HER2-positive early breast cancer — overall survival still not significant at 8.4 years (92.7% vs 92.0%)
shelves.question: In patients with node-positive or high-risk node-negative HER2-positive early breast cancer, does one year of adjuvant pertuzumab added to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy improve invasive disease-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Breast Neoplasms · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Diarrhea · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Heart Failure · Humans · Middle Aged · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases · Survival Rate · Trastuzumab
shelves.balance: SPLIT — the split is nodal status, and the survival null leads beside it. One trial reported three times (APHINITY, 4,805 randomised): invasive disease-free survival improved overall (3-year 94.1% vs 93.2%; hazard ratio 0.81, a relative measure), concentrated in node-positive disease (hazard ratio 0.77 primary; 8-year rates 86.1% vs 81.2%, hazard ratio 0.72), with no benefit seen in node-negative disease (primary hazard ratio 1.13). Overall survival has NOT reached significance at any analysis: hazard ratio 0.85 (P=.17) at 6 years and 0.83 (P=.078, above the 0.006 threshold) at 8.4 years, 8-year rates 92.7% vs 92.0%. Added harm was grade 3 or higher diarrhoea during chemotherapy (9.8% vs 3.7%); cardiac events were infrequent. Do not let the stamp outrun the survival null.

cards.headline: APHINITY primary report (von Minckwitz 2017): 3-year invasive disease-free survival 94.1% vs 93.2% (hazard ratio 0.81 — a relative measure); node-positive 92.0% vs 90.2% (HR 0.77), node-negative HR 1.13
cards.summary: APHINITY primary report (von Minckwitz 2017): 3-year invasive disease-free survival 94.1% vs 93.2% (hazard ratio 0.81 — a relative measure); node-positive 92.0% vs 90.2% (HR 0.77), node-negative HR 1.13
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised placebo-controlled adjuvant trial (APHINITY) — primary report, one trial of which the following cards are later reports
cards.people: 4,805 patients with node-positive or high-risk node-negative HER2-positive operable breast cancer randomised to pertuzumab (2,400) or placebo (2,405) added to standard adjuvant chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab; 63% had node-positive disease and 36% hormone-receptor-negative disease.
cards.result: Disease recurrence occurred in 171 patients (7.1%) on pertuzumab versus 210 (8.7%) on placebo (hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.00; P=0.045 — a relative measure, absolute rates beside it). Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 94.1% versus 93.2% overall; in node-positive disease 92.0% versus 90.2% (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.96; P=0.02); in node-negative disease 97.5% versus 98.4% (hazard ratio 1.13, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.86; P=0.64). Heart failure, cardiac death and cardiac dysfunction were infrequent in both groups. Grade 3 or higher diarrhoea occurred almost exclusively during chemotherapy and was more frequent with pertuzumab (9.8% vs 3.7%).
cards.watchOut: The overall absolute 3-year gain was 0.9 percentage points, and the node-negative subgroup's point estimate favoured placebo — the subgroup split is part of the primary result, not a later refinement.
cards.source: von Minckwitz G et al. Adjuvant Pertuzumab and Trastuzumab in Early HER2-Positive Breast Cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2017. PMID: 28581356. Registry ID: NCT01358877. cards.headline: APHINITY 6-year follow-up (Piccart 2021): invasive disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.76 (91% vs 88%); overall survival hazard ratio 0.85, P=.17 — NOT significant
cards.summary: APHINITY 6-year follow-up (Piccart 2021): invasive disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.76 (91% vs 88%); overall survival hazard ratio 0.85, P=.17 — NOT significant
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised adjuvant trial (APHINITY) — 6-year follow-up report of the same trial
cards.people: The APHINITY population (4,805 randomised) at 74 months median follow-up; the preplanned second interim overall-survival analysis and a descriptive updated invasive disease-free survival analysis based on 508 events.
cards.result: The interim overall-survival comparison did not reach the P=.0012 level required for significance (P=.17; hazard ratio 0.85 — a relative measure): 6-year overall survival was 95% versus 94%, with 125 deaths (5.2%) versus 147 (6.1%). Invasive disease-free survival: hazard ratio 0.76 (95% CI 0.64 to 0.91), 6-year rates 91% versus 88%. The node-positive cohort continued to derive clear benefit (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.87; 6-year rates 88% vs 83%); benefit was not seen in the node-negative cohort. Primary cardiac events remained under 1% in both groups and no new safety signals were seen.
cards.watchOut: Overall survival had not reached significance at 6 years against a stringent interim threshold (P=.0012 required); the authors state longer follow-up is needed to assess the survival benefit fully — do not upgrade the interim trend.
cards.source: Piccart M et al. Adjuvant Pertuzumab and Trastuzumab in Early HER2-Positive Breast Cancer in the APHINITY Trial: 6 Years' Follow-Up. Journal of clinical oncology. 2021. PMID: 33539215. cards.headline: APHINITY third interim survival analysis, median follow-up 8.4 years (Loibl 2024): overall survival 92.7% vs 92.0% (hazard ratio 0.83; P=.078) — STILL NOT significant; node-positive 8-year invasive disease-free survival 86.1% vs 81.2%
cards.summary: APHINITY third interim survival analysis, median follow-up 8.4 years (Loibl 2024): overall survival 92.7% vs 92.0% (hazard ratio 0.83; P=.078) — STILL NOT significant; node-positive 8-year invasive disease-free survival 86.1% vs 81.2%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised adjuvant trial (APHINITY) — third interim overall-survival report of the same trial, median follow-up 8.4 years
cards.people: 4,804 patients in the intention-to-treat population of APHINITY, at 8.4 years median follow-up; the preplanned third interim overall-survival analysis with a descriptive updated invasive disease-free survival analysis.
cards.result: Eight-year overall survival was 92.7% on pertuzumab versus 92.0% on placebo (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.02; P=.078 — a relative measure, absolute rates beside it — above the 0.006 significance threshold, so NOT significant). Overall survival hazard ratios were 0.80 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.00) in the node-positive cohort and 0.99 (95% CI 0.64 to 1.55) in the node-negative cohort. In node-positive disease, 8-year invasive disease-free survival was 86.1% versus 81.2% (an absolute improvement of 4.9 percentage points; hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.87). The node-negative cohort did well without pertuzumab (8-year invasive disease-free survival 93.3% and overall survival 96.4% on placebo). The authors state that despite improvement in overall invasive disease-free survival, adding pertuzumab did not improve overall survival at this analysis.
cards.watchOut: ON THE FACE: overall survival has NOT reached significance at 8.4 years (P=.078 against a 0.006 threshold). The invasive disease-free survival benefit is concentrated in node-positive disease; node-negative patients did well without pertuzumab.
cards.source: Loibl S et al. cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf are reports of the single APHINITY trial (4,805 randomised; 4,804 in the intention-to-treat population at the third interim analysis) — a single-programme shelf, labelled as such.
cards.result: Primary: 3-year invasive disease-free survival 94.1% versus 93.2% (hazard ratio 0.81, a relative measure), driven by node-positive disease (hazard ratio 0.77) with no benefit in node-negative disease (hazard ratio 1.13). Six years: invasive disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.76 (91% vs 88%); overall survival hazard ratio 0.85, P=.17, not significant. At 8.4 years: overall survival 92.7% versus 92.0% (hazard ratio 0.83; P=.078, above the 0.006 threshold — not significant), while node-positive 8-year invasive disease-free survival was 86.1% versus 81.2% (hazard ratio 0.72). Added harm was mainly grade 3 or higher diarrhoea during chemotherapy (9.8% vs 3.7% at the primary report); cardiac events stayed infrequent (primary cardiac events under 1% at 6 years).
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: T-DM1 in pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer: EMILIA — survival 29.9 vs 25.9 months with less toxicity than lapatinib-capecitabine; TH3RESA — 22.7 vs 15.8 months vs physician's choice
shelves.question: In patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, does trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) prolong progression-free and overall survival versus lapatinib plus capecitabine (EMILIA) or versus treatment of physician's choice (TH3RESA), and with what toxicity trade?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — two independent phase 3 trials in pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, each showing both a progression-free and an overall-survival advantage for T-DM1, with absolutes printed beside every relative measure. EMILIA (991 randomised, vs lapatinib plus capecitabine): PFS 9.6 vs 6.4 months (HR 0.65, relative); final median OS 29.9 vs 25.9 months (HR 0.75, relative); grade 3/4 adverse events 41% vs 57% at the primary analysis — the control was more toxic. TH3RESA (602 randomised, later line, vs physician's choice): PFS 6.2 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.528, relative); final median OS 22.7 vs 15.8 months (HR 0.68, relative). PARTIAL beside #1856 (KATHERINE, adjuvant residual disease) and #856 (DESTINY-Breast03, T-DXd vs T-DM1): only the pretreated-metastatic slice is carded here.

cards.headline: EMILIA primary (Verma 2012): T-DM1 prolonged progression-free survival (9.6 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.65, relative) and interim overall survival (30.9 vs 25.1 months, HR 0.68, relative) versus lapatinib plus capecitabine, with fewer grade 3/4 adverse events (41% vs 57%)
cards.summary: EMILIA primary (Verma 2012): T-DM1 prolonged progression-free survival (9.6 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.65, relative) and interim overall survival (30.9 vs 25.1 months, HR 0.68, relative) versus lapatinib plus capecitabine, with fewer grade 3/4 adverse events (41% vs 57%)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (EMILIA), T-DM1 vs lapatinib plus capecitabine
cards.people: 991 patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, randomised to T-DM1 or lapatinib plus capecitabine.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by independent review was 9.6 months with T-DM1 versus 6.4 months with lapatinib plus capecitabine (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.65; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.77; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. At the second interim analysis median overall survival was 30.9 versus 25.1 months (hazard ratio for death 0.68; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.85; P<0.001), crossing the stopping boundary. Objective response was 43.6% versus 30.8%. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events were higher with lapatinib plus capecitabine than with T-DM1 (57% vs 41%); thrombocytopenia and increased aminotransferases were higher with T-DM1, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia higher with the control.
cards.watchOut: Open-label; the overall-survival figure on this card is the second interim analysis — the final analysis is carded separately below and must not be counted as a second trial.

cards.headline: EMILIA final overall survival (Diéras 2017): median survival 29.9 vs 25.9 months (HR 0.75, relative), despite 27% crossover from control to T-DM1
cards.summary: EMILIA final overall survival (Diéras 2017): median survival 29.9 vs 25.9 months (HR 0.75, relative), despite 27% crossover from control to T-DM1
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of the EMILIA phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same EMILIA population: 991 randomised (495 T-DM1, 496 control); safety population 490 treated with T-DM1 and 488 with capecitabine plus lapatinib; median follow-up 24.1 months.
cards.result: In this descriptive final analysis, median overall survival was 29.9 months (95% CI 26.3–34.1) with T-DM1 versus 25.9 months (22.7–28.3) with control (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.64–0.88) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. 136 of 496 control patients (27%) crossed over to T-DM1 after the interim boundary was crossed. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 233 of 490 (48%) on T-DM1 versus 291 of 488 (60%) on control; on T-DM1 the commonest were thrombocytopenia (70 [14%]), increased aspartate aminotransferase (22 [5%]) and anaemia (19 [4%]); on control, diarrhoea (103 [21%]) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (87 [18%]). Nine patients died from adverse events, five judged treatment-related (three on T-DM1, two on control).
cards.watchOut: Descriptive final analysis (the trial had already crossed its survival boundary at interim) and 27% crossover would, if anything, dilute the survival difference; 51% of the T-DM1 group later received capecitabine and 49% lapatinib after discontinuation.
cards.source: Diéras V et al. Trastuzumab emtansine versus capecitabine plus lapatinib in patients with previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer (EMILIA): a descriptive analysis of final overall survival results from a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2017. PMID: 28526536. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00829166. cards.summary: EMILIA patient-reported outcomes (Welslau 2014): time to symptom worsening was delayed on T-DM1 (7.1 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.796, relative) — a report OF the EMILIA trial, not a separate trial
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcomes report of the EMILIA trial (same programme — not independent comparative evidence)

cards.headline: TH3RESA primary (Krop 2014): in patients progressed on two or more HER2-directed regimens, T-DM1 prolonged progression-free survival versus physician's choice (6.2 vs 3.3 months, HR 0.528, relative)
cards.summary: TH3RESA primary (Krop 2014): in patients progressed on two or more HER2-directed regimens, T-DM1 prolonged progression-free survival versus physician's choice (6.2 vs 3.3 months, HR 0.528, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (TH3RESA), T-DM1 vs treatment of physician's choice, later-line setting
cards.people: 602 patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer who had received two or more HER2-directed regimens in the advanced setting, including trastuzumab and lapatinib, plus a taxane, randomised 2:1 to T-DM1 (404) or treatment of physician's choice (198) in 22 countries.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 6.2 months (95% CI 5.59–6.87) with T-DM1 versus 3.3 months (2.89–4.14) with physician's choice (stratified hazard ratio 0.528; 95% CI 0.422–0.661; P<0.0001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. The first interim overall-survival analysis trended to T-DM1 (hazard ratio 0.552) but did not cross its stopping boundary. Grade 3 or worse adverse events were reported in 130 events (32%) of 403 patients on T-DM1 versus 80 events (43%) of 184 on physician's choice; thrombocytopenia was more common on T-DM1 (19 [5%] vs 3 [2%]), neutropenia and febrile neutropenia more common on physician's choice. 44 control patients had crossed over to T-DM1 by this cutoff.
cards.watchOut: A different, later-line slice than EMILIA and a heterogeneous physician's-choice comparator — the two trials are labelled slices, never pooled. The survival result on this card is interim only; the final analysis is carded below.
cards.source: Krop IE et al. Trastuzumab emtansine versus treatment of physician's choice for pretreated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer (TH3RESA): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2014. PMID: 24793816. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01419197. cards.headline: TH3RESA final overall survival (Krop 2017): median survival 22.7 vs 15.8 months (HR 0.68, relative), with 47% of the control group crossing over to T-DM1
cards.summary: TH3RESA final overall survival (Krop 2017): median survival 22.7 vs 15.8 months (HR 0.68, relative), with 47% of the control group crossing over to T-DM1
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of the TH3RESA phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same TH3RESA population: 602 randomised (404 T-DM1, 198 physician's choice) from 146 centres in 22 countries; data cutoff Feb 13, 2015, at about 67% of expected deaths.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer with T-DM1: median 22.7 months (95% CI 19.4–27.5) versus 15.8 months (13.5–18.7) (hazard ratio 0.68; 95% CI 0.54–0.85; P=0.0007) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians; the stopping boundary was crossed, making this the final confirmatory survival analysis. 93 of 198 control patients (47%) had crossed over to T-DM1. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 161 of 403 (40%) on T-DM1 versus 87 of 184 (47%) on physician's choice; thrombocytopenia (24 [6%] vs 5 [3%]) and haemorrhage of any type (17 [4%] vs 1 [<1%]) were more frequent on T-DM1, neutropenia and febrile neutropenia more frequent on control. Deaths from adverse events: nine (2%) on T-DM1 (three treatment-related) and three (2%) on control (one treatment-related).
cards.watchOut: Nearly half the control group crossed over to T-DM1, which would dilute the observed survival difference; the trial was terminated per protocol once the boundary was crossed.
cards.source: Krop IE et al. Trastuzumab emtansine versus treatment of physician's choice in patients with previously treated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (TH3RESA): final overall survival results from a randomised open-label phase 3 trial. cards.headline: Synthesis: two trials, two comparators, the same direction — T-DM1 prolonged progression-free and overall survival in pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, and the EMILIA control arm was the more toxic treatment
cards.summary: Synthesis: two trials, two comparators, the same direction — T-DM1 prolonged progression-free and overall survival in pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, and the EMILIA control arm was the more toxic treatment
cards.people: EMILIA (991 randomised, vs lapatinib plus capecitabine) and TH3RESA (602 randomised, vs physician's choice, later line), with EMILIA's patient-reported-outcomes report carded as a programme report.
cards.result: EMILIA: progression-free survival 9.6 vs 6.4 months (HR 0.65, relative) and final median overall survival 29.9 vs 25.9 months (HR 0.75, relative), with grade 3 or worse adverse events in 48% vs 60% at final analysis. TH3RESA: progression-free survival 6.2 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.528, relative) and final median overall survival 22.7 vs 15.8 months (HR 0.68, relative). Symptom worsening was also delayed on T-DM1 in EMILIA (7.1 vs 4.6 months). This shelf is PARTIAL by design: it cards only the pretreated-metastatic question. T-DM1 for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy is homed at shelf #1856 (KATHERINE), and trastuzumab deruxtecan versus T-DM1 is homed at shelf #856 (DESTINY-Breast03) — cross-pointed here, not re-carded.
cards.watchOut: Both trials were open-label and both allowed crossover to T-DM1 (27% in EMILIA, 47% in TH3RESA); the comparators differ, so the slices are reported separately and never pooled.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Lapatinib in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer: progression delayed with capecitabine (8.4 vs 4.4 months) but survival not significant; dual blockade with trastuzumab improved survival vs lapatinib alone
shelves.question: In patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer progressing after trastuzumab, does lapatinib — added to capecitabine, or combined with trastuzumab chemotherapy-free — prolong time to progression and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antimetabolites, Antineoplastic/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Breast Neoplasms/chemistry,drug therapy,mortality · Capecitabine · Deoxycytidine/adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Disease Progression · Female · Fluorouracil/adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Heart Diseases/chemically induced · Humans · Lapatinib · Middle Aged · Proportional Hazards Models · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Quinazolines/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases/analysis,antagonists & inhibitors · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: SPLIT — progression and survival point in different strengths. Adding lapatinib to capecitabine after trastuzumab doubled time to progression (8.4 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.49 interim / 0.57 updated, relative) but overall survival was only a non-significant trend (HR 0.78; P=.177). Adding trastuzumab to lapatinib (EGF104900, chemotherapy-free) improved progression-free survival (HR 0.73, relative) and, at final analysis, overall survival (HR 0.74, relative; +4.5 months median) — but against lapatinib alone. A first-line paclitaxel trial was negative overall with a positive HER2-positive subset (n=86) — carded labelled, never load-bearing. CNS first progression 4 vs 13 is a small-count signal.

cards.headline: Geyer 2006: adding lapatinib to capecitabine doubled time to progression after trastuzumab (8.4 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.49, relative)
cards.summary: Geyer 2006: adding lapatinib to capecitabine doubled time to progression after trastuzumab (8.4 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.49, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial, lapatinib plus capecitabine vs capecitabine alone (interim primary report)
cards.people: Women with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that had progressed after regimens including an anthracycline, a taxane and trastuzumab, randomised to lapatinib 1250 mg daily plus capecitabine or capecitabine alone; the primary report is an interim analysis (49 progression events on combination, 72 on monotherapy).
cards.result: The hazard ratio for independently assessed time to progression was 0.49 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.71; P<0.001) — a relative measure — with median time to progression 8.4 months on lapatinib plus capecitabine versus 4.4 months on capecitabine alone. The interim analysis met the prespecified criteria for early reporting on superiority. The improvement was achieved without an increase in serious toxic effects or symptomatic cardiac events in this report.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis reported early for superiority, in a trial whose final randomised total (399) is given in the updated report below; early-reported effects tend to be optimistic, and this card carries no survival result.
cards.source: Geyer CE et al. Lapatinib plus capecitabine for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2006. PMID: 17192538. cards.headline: Cameron 2008 (updated analysis of the same trial): time-to-progression HR 0.57 (relative); overall survival HR 0.78, P=.177 — not significant; CNS as first progression site in 4 vs 13 patients
cards.summary: Cameron 2008 (updated analysis of the same trial): time-to-progression HR 0.57 (relative); overall survival HR 0.78, P=.177 — not significant; CNS as first progression site in 4 vs 13 patients
cards.type: Updated efficacy and biomarker analysis of the Geyer trial (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 399 women randomised in the same trial (HER2-positive advanced breast cancer progressing after anthracycline-, taxane- and trastuzumab-containing regimens), to lapatinib plus capecitabine or capecitabine alone.
cards.result: Adding lapatinib prolonged time to progression (hazard ratio 0.57; 95% CI 0.43–0.77; P<0.001) — a relative measure. Overall survival showed only a trend (hazard ratio 0.78; 95% CI 0.55–1.12; P=0.177) — not significant, and printed as such. Fewer patients had CNS involvement at first progression on the combination (4 vs 13 patients; P=0.045) — small counts, printed with their counts. Baseline serum HER2 extracellular domain did not predict benefit from lapatinib.
cards.watchOut: The survival trend did not reach significance and the CNS comparison rests on 4 versus 13 patients; neither should be upgraded beyond what is printed here.
cards.source: Cameron D et al. A phase III randomized comparison of lapatinib plus capecitabine versus capecitabine alone in women with advanced breast cancer that has progressed on trastuzumab: updated efficacy and biomarker analyses. cards.headline: EGF104900 primary (Blackwell 2010): chemotherapy-free dual blockade — lapatinib plus trastuzumab beat lapatinib alone on progression-free survival (HR 0.73, relative) and clinical benefit (24.7% vs 12.4%)
cards.summary: EGF104900 primary (Blackwell 2010): chemotherapy-free dual blockade — lapatinib plus trastuzumab beat lapatinib alone on progression-free survival (HR 0.73, relative) and clinical benefit (24.7% vs 12.4%)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (EGF104900), lapatinib plus trastuzumab vs lapatinib alone
cards.people: 296 patients with HER2 (ErbB2)-positive, trastuzumab-refractory metastatic breast cancer who had received a median of three prior trastuzumab-containing regimens, randomised to lapatinib alone or lapatinib plus trastuzumab.
cards.result: Progression-free survival favoured the combination (hazard ratio 0.73; 95% CI 0.57 to 0.93; P=.008) — a relative measure. Clinical benefit rate was 24.7% on the combination versus 12.4% on lapatinib alone (P=.01); objective response was 10.3% versus 6.9% (P=.46, not significant). Overall survival trended to the combination (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.07; P=.106) — not significant at this analysis. Diarrhoea was more frequent on the combination (P=.03); symptomatic cardiac events were 2% on combination versus 0.7% on monotherapy, asymptomatic 3.4% versus 1.4%.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is lapatinib alone, not chemotherapy or another standard — this card shows dual blockade beats single-agent lapatinib, in a heavily pretreated population.
cards.source: Blackwell KL et al. Randomized study of Lapatinib alone or in combination with trastuzumab in women with ErbB2-positive, trastuzumab-refractory metastatic breast cancer. cards.headline: EGF104900 final overall survival (Blackwell 2012): the combination gave a significant survival advantage (HR 0.74, relative; +4.5 months median) over lapatinib alone
cards.summary: EGF104900 final overall survival (Blackwell 2012): the combination gave a significant survival advantage (HR 0.74, relative; +4.5 months median) over lapatinib alone
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of EGF104900 (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: All randomised patients in EGF104900 analysed with strata (n=291 of the 296 randomised), HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer progressing on prior trastuzumab-based therapy.
cards.result: At the final planned analysis, lapatinib plus trastuzumab remained superior on progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.74; 95% CI 0.58 to 0.94; P=.011) and showed a significant overall-survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.74; 95% CI 0.57 to 0.97; P=.026) — relative measures — with a 4.5-month median overall-survival advantage and absolute survival-rate improvements of 10% at 6 months and 15% at 12 months for the combination. Adverse-event incidence was consistent with the earlier report.
cards.watchOut: A crossover study design is recorded in this report's MeSH; crossover after progression can dilute a survival comparison, and the control remains lapatinib monotherapy.

cards.headline: Labelled subset slice only (Di Leo 2008): first-line lapatinib plus paclitaxel was negative in the whole population (n=579) and positive only in the retrospectively identified HER2-positive subset (n=86) — never load-bearing
cards.summary: Labelled subset slice only (Di Leo 2008): first-line lapatinib plus paclitaxel was negative in the whole population (n=579) and positive only in the retrospectively identified HER2-positive subset (n=86) — never load-bearing
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind randomised trial, first-line — LABELLED SUBSET SLICE: ITT-negative, HER2-positive subset (n=86) positive; not load-bearing for this shelf
cards.people: 579 women with metastatic breast cancer (HER2-negative or HER2-uncharacterised at entry) randomised first-line to paclitaxel plus lapatinib 1500 mg/day or paclitaxel plus placebo, with preplanned retrospective HER2 testing; the HER2-positive subset numbered 86 patients (15%).
cards.result: In the intention-to-treat population there were no significant differences in time to progression, event-free survival or overall survival between the arms. Only in the 86-patient HER2-positive subset did paclitaxel plus lapatinib significantly improve time to progression, event-free survival, response and clinical benefit; no endpoint differed in HER2-negative patients. Diarrhoea and rash were significantly more frequent with lapatinib; cardiac event rates were low and did not differ.
cards.watchOut: A retrospective subset of a negative trial: it is carded, labelled, only to keep the record honest — the shelf's conclusions rest on the two post-trastuzumab trials above, not on this subset.

cards.headline: Synthesis: lapatinib delayed progression in both post-trastuzumab settings, but the survival record splits — a non-significant trend against capecitabine alone (HR 0.78, P=.177) and a significant gain only against lapatinib alone in EGF104900 (HR 0.74)
cards.summary: Synthesis: lapatinib delayed progression in both post-trastuzumab settings, but the survival record splits — a non-significant trend against capecitabine alone (HR 0.78, P=.177) and a significant gain only against lapatinib alone in EGF104900 (HR 0.74)
cards.people: Two post-trastuzumab trials (lapatinib plus capecitabine, 399 randomised; EGF104900, 296 randomised) plus one labelled first-line subset slice (86 HER2-positive patients within a negative 579-patient trial).
cards.result: Time to progression / progression-free survival consistently favoured lapatinib combinations (HR 0.49 at interim and 0.57 updated, relative, vs capecitabine alone; HR 0.73–0.74, relative, for adding trastuzumab to lapatinib). Overall survival did not reach significance in the capecitabine trial (HR 0.78; P=.177) and did reach significance in EGF104900's final analysis (HR 0.74; +4.5 months median) — against a lapatinib-alone control. CNS as first progression site was 4 vs 13 patients in the capecitabine trial — a small-count signal, printed with its counts. Diarrhoea and rash are the recurring harms; cardiac events were uncommon in these reports.
cards.watchOut: Lapatinib is a superseded agent in this setting; these trials are carded as the randomised record of dual HER2 blockade before the antibody–drug-conjugate era, not as a current treatment recommendation.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Everolimus plus exemestane in HR-positive advanced breast cancer (BOLERO-2): progression-free survival more than doubled, overall survival not significant (31.0 vs 26.6 months, P=.14)
shelves.question: In postmenopausal patients with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer recurring after a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, does everolimus plus exemestane prolong progression-free survival versus exemestane alone, and does it prolong overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Androstadienes/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Aromatase Inhibitors/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Bone Neoplasms/secondary · Breast Neoplasms/chemistry,drug therapy · Disease-Free Survival · ErbB Receptors/analysis · Everolimus · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Middle Aged · Postmenopause · Recurrence · Sirolimus/adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Stomatitis/chemically induced · TOR Serine-Threonine Kinases/antagonists & inhibitors
shelves.balance: SPLIT, on a single trial (BOLERO-2, 724 randomised). Progression-free survival: a large relative gain — final local assessment 7.8 vs 3.2 months (HR 0.45, relative), central 11.0 vs 4.1 months (HR 0.38, relative). Overall survival: NO significant benefit — median 31.0 vs 26.6 months (HR 0.89; P=.14), printed on the face as the row directs. Quality-of-life deterioration was delayed at a 5% threshold (HR 0.74) but not at a 10-point threshold (HR 0.80; P=.1017). Pricing harms: grade 3/4 stomatitis 8% vs 1%, pneumonitis 3% vs 0%, anaemia 6% vs <1%.

cards.headline: BOLERO-2 primary (Baselga 2012): everolimus plus exemestane more than doubled progression-free survival (local 6.9 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.43, relative; central 10.6 vs 4.1 months, HR 0.36, relative)
cards.summary: BOLERO-2 primary (Baselga 2012): everolimus plus exemestane more than doubled progression-free survival (local 6.9 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.43, relative; central 10.6 vs 4.1 months, HR 0.36, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (BOLERO-2), everolimus plus exemestane vs placebo plus exemestane (interim primary report)
cards.people: 724 postmenopausal patients with hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer recurring or progressing on a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, randomised 2:1 to everolimus plus exemestane or placebo plus exemestane; median age 62 years, 56% visceral disease.
cards.result: At the preplanned interim analysis, median progression-free survival was 6.9 months with everolimus plus exemestane versus 2.8 months with placebo plus exemestane by local assessment (hazard ratio 0.43; 95% CI 0.35 to 0.54; P<0.001) and 10.6 versus 4.1 months by central assessment (hazard ratio 0.36; 95% CI 0.27 to 0.47; P<0.001) — relative measures beside the absolute medians. The commonest grade 3 or 4 adverse events on the combination were stomatitis (8% vs 1%), anaemia (6% vs <1%), dyspnoea (4% vs 1%), hyperglycaemia (4% vs <1%), fatigue (4% vs 1%) and pneumonitis (3% vs 0%).
cards.watchOut: An interim progression-free-survival report; the final progression-free and overall-survival analyses are carded separately below and are reports of this same trial, not new trials.

cards.headline: BOLERO-2 final progression-free survival (Yardley 2013): the gain held at final analysis (local 7.8 vs 3.2 months, HR 0.45, relative; central 11.0 vs 4.1 months, HR 0.38, relative)
cards.summary: BOLERO-2 final progression-free survival (Yardley 2013): the gain held at final analysis (local 7.8 vs 3.2 months, HR 0.45, relative; central 11.0 vs 4.1 months, HR 0.38, relative)
cards.type: Final progression-free-survival report of BOLERO-2 (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same BOLERO-2 population (724 randomised), at a median follow-up of 18 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival remained significantly longer with everolimus plus exemestane: 7.8 versus 3.2 months by investigator review (hazard ratio 0.45; 95% CI 0.38–0.54; P<0.0001) and 11.0 versus 4.1 months by central review (hazard ratio 0.38; 95% CI 0.31–0.48; P<0.0001) — relative measures beside the absolute medians — in the overall population and in all prospectively defined subgroups, including visceral metastases and irrespective of age. The adverse-event incidence and severity were consistent with the interim report.
cards.watchOut: Local and central progression-free-survival medians differ substantially (7.8 vs 11.0 months on the combination); both are printed, neither is cherry-picked.

cards.headline: BOLERO-2 final overall survival (Piccart 2014): NO significant survival benefit — median 31.0 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.89, P=.14
cards.summary: BOLERO-2 final overall survival (Piccart 2014): NO significant survival benefit — median 31.0 vs 26.6 months, HR 0.89, P=.14
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of BOLERO-2 (same trial as the cards above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same BOLERO-2 population; at the Oct 3, 2013 cutoff, 410 deaths had occurred and 13 patients remained on treatment.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 31.0 months (95% CI 28.0–34.6) with everolimus plus exemestane versus 26.6 months (22.6–33.1) with placebo plus exemestane (hazard ratio 0.89; 95% CI 0.73–1.10; log-rank P=0.14) — not significant, and printed on the face as the row directs. Post-study treatment was received by 84% of the combination arm and 90% of the control arm (chemotherapy 53% vs 63%). No new safety concerns were identified. The authors state plainly that adding everolimus did not confer a statistically significant improvement in overall survival despite the significant progression-free-survival gain.
cards.watchOut: Overall survival was a secondary endpoint and the result is null; quoting the progression-free-survival gain without this card misstates the trial.
cards.source: Piccart M et al. Everolimus plus exemestane for hormone-receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2-negative advanced breast cancer: overall survival results from BOLERO-2†. Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology. 2014. PMID: 25231953. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00863655. cards.headline: BOLERO-2 quality of life (Burris 2013): time to definitive deterioration of global health status was longer on the combination (8.3 vs 5.8 months, HR 0.74, relative) at the 5% threshold, but not significant at the 10-point threshold (HR 0.80, P=.1017)
cards.summary: BOLERO-2 quality of life (Burris 2013): time to definitive deterioration of global health status was longer on the combination (8.3 vs 5.8 months, HR 0.74, relative) at the 5% threshold, but not significant at the 10-point threshold (HR 0.80, P=.1017)
cards.type: Health-related quality-of-life report of BOLERO-2 (same trial — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: BOLERO-2 participants assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30 at baseline and every 6 weeks until progression or discontinuation; baseline global health status was similar (64.7 vs 65.3).
cards.result: Median time to definitive deterioration in global health status (a 5% decrease with no subsequent increase above the threshold) was 8.3 months with everolimus plus exemestane versus 5.8 months with placebo plus exemestane (hazard ratio 0.74; P=.0084) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. At the stricter 10-point minimal-important-difference threshold the medians were 11.7 versus 8.4 months (hazard ratio 0.80; P=.1017) — not significant, and printed as such.
cards.watchOut: The quality-of-life conclusion depends on the deterioration threshold chosen: significant at 5%, not at 10 points. Both are printed.
cards.source: Burris HA et al. Health-related quality of life of patients with advanced breast cancer treated with everolimus plus exemestane versus placebo plus exemestane in the phase 3, randomized, controlled, BOLERO-2 trial. Cancer. 2013. PMID: 23504821. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial, two answers that must travel together — a large relative progression-free-survival gain (final local HR 0.45) and no demonstrated overall-survival benefit (HR 0.89, P=.14), priced in stomatitis and pneumonitis
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial, two answers that must travel together — a large relative progression-free-survival gain (final local HR 0.45) and no demonstrated overall-survival benefit (HR 0.89, P=.14), priced in stomatitis and pneumonitis
cards.people: BOLERO-2 alone: 724 randomised postmenopausal patients with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor; all four cards are reports of this single trial.
cards.result: Progression-free survival: interim local 6.9 vs 2.8 months (HR 0.43, relative), final local 7.8 vs 3.2 months (HR 0.45, relative) and final central 11.0 vs 4.1 months (HR 0.38, relative). Overall survival: 31.0 vs 26.6 months (HR 0.89; P=.14) — not significant. Quality-of-life deterioration was delayed at the 5% threshold (8.3 vs 5.8 months) but not significantly at the 10-point threshold. Grade 3/4 stomatitis 8% vs 1% and pneumonitis 3% vs 0% price the progression gain.
cards.watchOut: A single-trial shelf by design: BOLERO-2 is the whole base, and its reports are counted once.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Afatinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC: progression-free survival 11.1 vs 6.9 and 11.0 vs 5.6 months vs platinum doublets; vs gefitinib HR 0.73 with medians 11.0 vs 10.9 months
shelves.question: In patients with EGFR-mutation-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, does first-line afatinib prolong progression-free survival versus platinum doublet chemotherapy (LUX-Lung 3, LUX-Lung 6), and versus gefitinib (LUX-Lung 7)?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma/drug therapy,enzymology,genetics,pathology · Adenocarcinoma of Lung · Adult · Afatinib · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,pharmacokinetics,therapeutic use · Cisplatin/administration & dosage,adverse effects,pharmacokinetics · ErbB Receptors/genetics · Female · Glutamates/administration & dosage,adverse effects,pharmacokinetics · Guanine/administration & dosage,adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,pharmacokinetics · Humans · Lung Neoplasms/drug therapy,enzymology,genetics,pathology · Male · Middle Aged · Mutation · Neoplasm Metastasis · Pemetrexed · Quinazolines/adverse effects,pharmacokinetics,therapeutic use
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit, on progression-free survival only) — three randomised trials, two comparator classes, labelled separately. Chemotherapy-controlled: LUX-Lung 3 (345 randomised) PFS 11.1 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.58, relative); LUX-Lung 6 (364 randomised, Asian population) PFS 11.0 vs 5.6 months (HR 0.28, relative). Gefitinib-controlled: LUX-Lung 7 (319 randomised) PFS HR 0.73 (relative) with medians 11.0 vs 10.9 months — printed together so the hazard ratio is not mistaken for a median gain. No overall-survival claim is carded or made. Pricing harms: diarrhoea and rash/acne (grade 3/4 diarrhoea 13% vs 1% vs gefitinib).

cards.headline: LUX-Lung 3 (Sequist 2013): first-line afatinib prolonged progression-free survival versus cisplatin plus pemetrexed (11.1 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.58, relative; in common mutations 13.6 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.47, relative)
cards.summary: LUX-Lung 3 (Sequist 2013): first-line afatinib prolonged progression-free survival versus cisplatin plus pemetrexed (11.1 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.58, relative; in common mutations 13.6 vs 6.9 months, HR 0.47, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (LUX-Lung 3), afatinib vs cisplatin plus pemetrexed — chemotherapy-controlled slice
cards.people: 345 patients with stage IIIB/IV EGFR-mutation-positive lung adenocarcinoma (1,269 screened), randomised 2:1 to afatinib 40 mg daily or up to six cycles of cisplatin plus pemetrexed, stratified by mutation type and race.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by independent review was 11.1 months on afatinib versus 6.9 months on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.58; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.78; P=.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Among patients with the common mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R, n=308), median progression-free survival was 13.6 versus 6.9 months (hazard ratio 0.47; 95% CI 0.34 to 0.65; P=.001). The commonest treatment-related adverse events on afatinib were diarrhoea, rash/acne and stomatitis; patient-reported outcomes favoured afatinib for cough, dyspnoea and pain control.
cards.watchOut: A chemotherapy-controlled slice; the gefitinib-controlled comparison (LUX-Lung 7) is a separate card and the two comparator classes are never pooled. No overall-survival result is carded from this report.
cards.source: Sequist LV et al. Phase III study of afatinib or cisplatin plus pemetrexed in patients with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutations. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2013. PMID: 23816960. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00949650. cards.headline: LUX-Lung 6 (Wu 2014): in Asian patients, afatinib prolonged progression-free survival versus cisplatin plus gemcitabine (11.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.28, relative)
cards.summary: LUX-Lung 6 (Wu 2014): in Asian patients, afatinib prolonged progression-free survival versus cisplatin plus gemcitabine (11.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.28, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (LUX-Lung 6), afatinib vs cisplatin plus gemcitabine, Asian population — chemotherapy-controlled slice
cards.people: 364 Asian patients with EGFR-mutation-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (910 screened) at 36 centres in China, Thailand and South Korea, randomised 2:1 to afatinib 40 mg daily (242) or gemcitabine plus cisplatin (122).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by independent central review was 11.0 months (95% CI 9.7–13.7) on afatinib versus 5.6 months (5.1–6.7) on gemcitabine plus cisplatin (hazard ratio 0.28; 95% CI 0.20–0.39; P<0.0001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events on afatinib were rash or acne in 35 of 239 (14.6%), diarrhoea in 13 (5.4%) and stomatitis or mucositis in 13 (5.4%), versus neutropenia (26.5%), vomiting (19.5%) and leucopenia (15.0%) on chemotherapy. Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 6.3% versus 8.0%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label (central imaging review was blinded) and conducted in an Asian population with a different chemotherapy backbone than LUX-Lung 3 — a labelled slice, not a replicate to pool.
cards.source: Wu YL et al. Afatinib versus cisplatin plus gemcitabine for first-line treatment of Asian patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring EGFR mutations (LUX-Lung 6): an open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2014. PMID: 24439929. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01121393. cards.headline: LUX-Lung 7 (Park 2016): afatinib versus gefitinib — progression-free survival HR 0.73 (relative) but medians almost identical (11.0 vs 10.9 months); overall survival not mature
cards.summary: LUX-Lung 7 (Park 2016): afatinib versus gefitinib — progression-free survival HR 0.73 (relative) but medians almost identical (11.0 vs 10.9 months); overall survival not mature
cards.type: Phase 2B randomised open-label trial (LUX-Lung 7), afatinib vs gefitinib — gefitinib-controlled slice
cards.people: 319 treatment-naive patients with stage IIIB/IV non-small-cell lung cancer and a common EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion or Leu858Arg), randomised to afatinib 40 mg daily (160) or gefitinib 250 mg daily (159) at 64 centres in 13 countries; median follow-up 27.3 months.
cards.result: Progression-free survival by independent central review was significantly longer on afatinib (hazard ratio 0.73; 95% CI 0.57–0.95; P=0.017) — a relative measure — although the medians were 11.0 months (95% CI 10.6–12.9) versus 10.9 months (9.1–11.5), and both figures are printed so the hazard ratio is not read as a median gain. Time to treatment failure also favoured afatinib (13.7 vs 11.5 months; hazard ratio 0.73). Overall survival data were not mature. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related diarrhoea occurred in 20 of 160 (13%) on afatinib versus 2 of 159 (1%) on gefitinib, and rash or acne in 15 (9%) versus 5 (3%); liver-enzyme elevations occurred in 0 versus 14 (9%). Serious treatment-related adverse events: 11% versus 4%.
cards.watchOut: A phase 2B exploratory trial, and its headline is the caution: a significant hazard ratio with essentially identical medians. The exon-19-deletion overall-survival signal sometimes quoted for afatinib lives in a pooled analysis that is not carded here.
cards.source: Park K et al. Afatinib versus gefitinib as first-line treatment of patients with EGFR mutation-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (LUX-Lung 7): a phase 2B, open-label, randomised controlled trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2016. PMID: 27083334. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01466660. median follow-up 27.3 months. progression-free survival by independent central review was significantly longer on afatinib (hazard ratio 0.73; 95% ci 0.57–0.95; p=0.017) — a relative measure — although the medians were 11.0 months (95% ci 10.6–12.9) versus 10.9 months (9.1–11.5), and both figures are printed so the hazard ratio is not read as a median gain. time to treatment failure also favoured afatinib (13.7 vs 11.5 months; hazard ratio 0.73). overall survival data were not mature. grade 3 or 4 treatment-related diarrhoea occurred in 20 of 160 (13%) on afatinib versus 2 of 159 (1%) on gefitinib, and rash or acne in 15 (9%) versus 5 (3%); liver-enzyme elevations occurred in 0 versus 14 (9%). serious treatment-related adverse events: 11% versus 4%. a phase 2b exploratory trial, and its headline is the caution: a significant hazard ratio with essentially identical medians. the exon-19-deletion overall-survival signal sometimes quoted for afatinib lives in a pooled analysis that is not carded here. park k et al. afatinib versus gefitinib as first-line treatment of patients with egfr mutation-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (lux-lung 7): a phase 2b, open-label, randomised controlled trial. the lancet. oncology. 2016. pmid: 27083334. registry id: clinicaltrials.gov: nct01466660. mesh: adult · afatinib · aged · aged, 80 and over · carcinoma, non-small-cell lung/drug therapy,genetics,pathology · disease-free survival · drug-related side effects and adverse reactions/classification,genetics,physiopathology · erbb receptors/genetics · female · gefitinib · humans · kaplan-meier estimate · male · middle aged · mutation · protein kinase inhibitors/administration & dosage,adverse effects · quinazolines/administration & dosage,adverse effects

cards.headline: Synthesis: afatinib prolonged progression-free survival against platinum doublets in two phase 3 trials (HR 0.58 and 0.28, relative) and edged gefitinib on the hazard ratio (0.73) with near-identical medians — a progression-free-survival shelf, with no overall-survival claim carded

cards.people: LUX-Lung 3 (345 randomised, vs cisplatin-pemetrexed), LUX-Lung 6 (364 randomised, Asian population, vs cisplatin-gemcitabine) and LUX-Lung 7 (319 randomised, vs gefitinib) — three trials, two comparator classes, labelled separately.
cards.result: Against chemotherapy, median progression-free survival was 11.1 vs 6.9 months (HR 0.58, relative) and 11.0 vs 5.6 months (HR 0.28, relative). Against gefitinib, the hazard ratio was 0.73 (relative) with medians of 11.0 vs 10.9 months. Diarrhoea and rash/acne are the pricing harms throughout (grade 3/4 diarrhoea 13% vs 1% against gefitinib; grade 3/4 rash/acne 14.6% in LUX-Lung 6). No card on this shelf establishes an overall-survival benefit, and none is claimed.
cards.watchOut: Two comparator classes (platinum doublet; a first-generation EGFR inhibitor) answer different questions and are kept as labelled slices.

shelves.title: Ceritinib in ALK-positive NSCLC: progression-free survival 16.6 vs 8.1 months first-line and 5.4 vs 1.6 months after crizotinib — at the superseded 750 mg fasted dose
shelves.question: In patients with ALK-rearranged advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, does ceritinib prolong progression-free survival versus chemotherapy — first-line (ASCEND-4) and after crizotinib plus chemotherapy (ASCEND-5)?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit, on progression-free survival) — two phase 3 randomised trials versus chemotherapy: ASCEND-4 first-line (376 randomised) PFS 16.6 vs 8.1 months (HR 0.55, relative); ASCEND-5 after crizotinib and chemotherapy (231 randomised) PFS 5.4 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.49, relative). The ASCEND-1 phase 1 report is carded as a LABELLED SINGLE-ARM companion (responses 72% naive, 56% pretreated) and is never load-bearing. DOSE-ERA WARNING on the face: all three used ceritinib 750 mg fasted; the labelled dose has since changed to 450 mg with food. Pricing harms at the trial dose: diarrhoea 85%, grade 3–4 ALT elevation 21%. No overall-survival claim is carded.

cards.headline: ASCEND-4 (Soria 2017): first-line ceritinib 750 mg fasted prolonged progression-free survival versus platinum chemotherapy (16.6 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.55, relative), with diarrhoea in 85%
cards.summary: ASCEND-4 (Soria 2017): first-line ceritinib 750 mg fasted prolonged progression-free survival versus platinum chemotherapy (16.6 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.55, relative), with diarrhoea in 85%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (ASCEND-4), first-line ceritinib vs platinum chemotherapy
cards.people: 376 untreated patients with stage IIIB/IV ALK-rearranged non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer at 134 centres in 28 countries, randomised to oral ceritinib 750 mg/day (189) or platinum-based chemotherapy (187).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent review was 16.6 months (95% CI 12.6–27.2) on ceritinib versus 8.1 months (5.8–11.1) on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.55; 95% CI 0.42–0.73; P<0.00001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. The commonest adverse events on ceritinib were diarrhoea (160 of 189, 85%), nausea (130, 69%), vomiting (125, 66%) and increased alanine aminotransferase (114, 60%).
cards.watchOut: DOSE-ERA WARNING: this trial used ceritinib 750 mg taken fasted — the labelled dose has since changed to 450 mg with food, so the gastrointestinal toxicity on this card belongs to the superseded dose and schedule.
cards.source: Soria JC et al. First-line ceritinib versus platinum-based chemotherapy in advanced ALK-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer (ASCEND-4): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 study. Lancet (London, England). 2017. PMID: 28126333. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01828099. cards.headline: ASCEND-5 (Shaw 2017): after crizotinib and chemotherapy, ceritinib prolonged progression-free survival versus single-agent chemotherapy (5.4 vs 1.6 months, HR 0.49, relative), with grade 3–4 ALT elevation in 21%
cards.summary: ASCEND-5 (Shaw 2017): after crizotinib and chemotherapy, ceritinib prolonged progression-free survival versus single-agent chemotherapy (5.4 vs 1.6 months, HR 0.49, relative), with grade 3–4 ALT elevation in 21%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (ASCEND-5), ceritinib vs single-agent chemotherapy after crizotinib
cards.people: 231 patients with ALK-rearranged stage IIIB/IV non-small-cell lung cancer who had progressed after crizotinib and platinum-based doublet chemotherapy, at 99 centres in 20 countries, randomised to ceritinib 750 mg/day fasted (115) or chemotherapy (116; pemetrexed or docetaxel); median follow-up 16.5 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival by masked independent review was 5.4 months (95% CI 4.1–6.9) on ceritinib versus 1.6 months (1.4–2.8) on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.36–0.67; P<0.0001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Serious adverse events were reported in 49 of 115 (43%) on ceritinib versus 36 of 113 (32%) on chemotherapy. Grade 3–4 adverse events on ceritinib were increased alanine aminotransferase (24 [21%] vs 2 [2%]), increased gamma-glutamyltransferase (24 [21%] vs 1 [1%]) and increased aspartate aminotransferase (16 [14%] vs 1 [1%]). Deaths during the treatment period: 15 of 115 (13%) on ceritinib (13 from disease progression, 2 from adverse events, neither judged treatment-related) versus 5 of 113 (4%) on chemotherapy, all from progression. Patients progressing on chemotherapy could cross over to ceritinib.
cards.watchOut: DOSE-ERA WARNING as on the ASCEND-4 card: 750 mg fasted. Crossover from chemotherapy to ceritinib was allowed, and the chemotherapy control's median progression-free survival (1.6 months) reflects a heavily pretreated population.
cards.source: Shaw AT et al. cards.headline: ASCEND-1 updated report (Kim 2016) — LABELLED SINGLE-ARM companion, never load-bearing: ceritinib 750 mg/day gave responses in 72% of ALK-inhibitor-naive and 56% of ALK-inhibitor-pretreated patients, with no comparator
cards.summary: ASCEND-1 updated report (Kim 2016) — LABELLED SINGLE-ARM companion, never load-bearing: ceritinib 750 mg/day gave responses in 72% of ALK-inhibitor-naive and 56% of ALK-inhibitor-pretreated patients, with no comparator
cards.type: Phase 1 single-arm open-label trial update (ASCEND-1) — LABELLED SINGLE-ARM COMPANION, not comparative evidence
cards.people: 255 patients enrolled in this open-label phase 1 trial, of whom 246 with ALK-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer received at least one dose of ceritinib 750 mg/day (83 ALK-inhibitor-naive, 163 ALK-inhibitor-pretreated); median follow-up 11.1 months.
cards.result: Overall response was reported in 60 of 83 ALK-inhibitor-naive patients (72%; 95% CI 61–82) and 92 of 163 ALK-inhibitor-pretreated patients (56%; 49–64); median duration of response was 17.0 and 8.3 months, and median progression-free survival 18.4 and 6.9 months, respectively — all single-arm figures with no control group. Among 94 patients with brain metastases and a post-baseline scan, intracranial disease control was reported in 15 of 19 naive (79%) and 49 of 75 pretreated (65%) patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 117 of 246 (48%); grade 3–4 increased alanine aminotransferase in 73 (30%) and aspartate aminotransferase in 25 (10%); two on-treatment deaths were deemed related to study drug (interstitial lung disease; multiorgan failure in the context of infection and ischaemic hepatitis).
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: response rates without a comparator cannot show that ceritinib is better than anything. This card is a labelled companion only; the shelf rests on ASCEND-4 and ASCEND-5. Same 750 mg fasted dose-era warning.
cards.source: Kim DW et al. Activity and safety of ceritinib in patients with ALK-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer (ASCEND-1): updated results from the multicentre, open-label, phase 1 trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2016. PMID: 26973324. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01283516. cards.headline: Synthesis: two randomised trials show ceritinib prolongs progression-free survival versus chemotherapy — first-line (16.6 vs 8.1 months) and after crizotinib (5.4 vs 1.6 months) — at the superseded 750 mg fasted dose, with heavy gastrointestinal and liver toxicity; the single-arm ASCEND-1 report adds response context only
cards.summary: Synthesis: two randomised trials show ceritinib prolongs progression-free survival versus chemotherapy — first-line (16.6 vs 8.1 months) and after crizotinib (5.4 vs 1.6 months) — at the superseded 750 mg fasted dose, with heavy gastrointestinal and liver toxicity; the single-arm ASCEND-1 report adds response context only
cards.people: ASCEND-4 (376 randomised, first-line), ASCEND-5 (231 randomised, post-crizotinib) and the single-arm ASCEND-1 update (246 patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC treated at 750 mg/day), labelled as such.
cards.result: Progression-free-survival hazard ratios were 0.55 (ASCEND-4) and 0.49 (ASCEND-5), both relative measures with absolute medians printed on their cards. No overall-survival claim is carded. Toxicity at the trial dose: diarrhoea in 85% (ASCEND-4), grade 3–4 alanine aminotransferase elevation in 21% (ASCEND-5) and 30% grade 3–4 laboratory ALT increase in ASCEND-1, where two on-treatment deaths were deemed drug-related. Ceritinib is a superseded agent in a neighbourhood now homed at other ALK inhibitors; this shelf records its randomised evidence, with the dose-era warning on the face.
cards.watchOut: The labelled dose has since changed to 450 mg with food; neither randomised trial tested that dose, so their toxicity figures must not be transferred to current dosing.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Panitumumab plus FOLFOX in metastatic colorectal cancer (PRIME): benefit in RAS wild-type (survival 26.0 vs 20.2 months), harm in RAS-mutant tumours (PFS HR 1.29)
shelves.question: In patients with metastatic colorectal cancer, does adding panitumumab to FOLFOX4 improve progression-free and overall survival in RAS wild-type tumours — and does it harm patients whose tumours carry RAS mutations?

shelves.balance: SPLIT by biomarker — one trial (PRIME, 1,183 randomised), opposite answers by RAS status, and the harm half is on the face. RAS wild-type: progression-free survival 10.1 vs 7.9 months (HR 0.72, relative) and overall survival 26.0 vs 20.2 months (HR 0.78, relative) in the fully RAS wild-type group (n=512). KRAS wild-type final overall survival was HR 0.88 (P=.17, not significant) at the prespecified analysis and HR 0.83 (P=.03) in an exploratory update — both printed. RAS-mutant: progression-free survival significantly worse with panitumumab (HR 1.29, relative) in mutant KRAS, and other RAS mutations likewise predicted harm. Full RAS testing is therefore part of the intervention.

cards.headline: PRIME primary (Douillard 2010): in KRAS wild-type tumours, panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 improved progression-free survival (9.6 vs 8.0 months, HR 0.80, relative) with a non-significant survival trend (23.9 vs 19.7 months, HR 0.83); in mutant KRAS it HARMED (PFS HR 1.29, relative)
cards.summary: PRIME primary (Douillard 2010): in KRAS wild-type tumours, panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 improved progression-free survival (9.6 vs 8.0 months, HR 0.80, relative) with a non-significant survival trend (23.9 vs 19.7 months, HR 0.83); in mutant KRAS it HARMED (PFS HR 1.29, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (PRIME), panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4, analysed prospectively by KRAS status
cards.people: 1,183 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer and no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, randomised 1:1 to panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 or FOLFOX4 alone; KRAS results were available for 93%.
cards.result: In the wild-type KRAS stratum, panitumumab-FOLFOX4 significantly improved progression-free survival (median 9.6 vs 8.0 months; hazard ratio 0.80; 95% CI 0.66 to 0.97; P=.02) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Overall survival was 23.9 vs 19.7 months (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% CI 0.67 to 1.02; P=.072) — not significant at this analysis. In the mutant KRAS stratum, progression-free survival was significantly REDUCED with panitumumab (hazard ratio 1.29; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.62; P=.02) and median overall survival was 15.5 vs 19.3 months (hazard ratio 1.24; 95% CI 0.98 to 1.57; P=.068) — the harm signal is on the face, as the row directs. Adverse events were generally comparable except for toxicities known to be associated with anti-EGFR therapy.
cards.watchOut: The KRAS analysis was prospective, but the survival result in wild-type disease had not reached significance in this primary report; the extended RAS analysis and the final analysis follow below.

cards.headline: PRIME RAS analysis (Douillard 2013): in fully RAS wild-type tumours (n=512), progression-free survival 10.1 vs 7.9 months (HR 0.72, relative) and overall survival 26.0 vs 20.2 months (HR 0.78, relative); other RAS mutations predicted harm
cards.summary: PRIME RAS analysis (Douillard 2013): in fully RAS wild-type tumours (n=512), progression-free survival 10.1 vs 7.9 months (HR 0.72, relative) and overall survival 26.0 vs 20.2 months (HR 0.78, relative); other RAS mutations predicted harm
cards.type: Prospective-retrospective RAS biomarker analysis of the PRIME trial (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: Patients from PRIME without KRAS exon 2 mutations who had results for additional RAS loci: 639 patients tested, with RAS status ascertained in 90%; 512 had no RAS mutations, and 108 (17%) of those without KRAS exon 2 mutations had other RAS mutations.
cards.result: Among the 512 patients without RAS mutations, progression-free survival was 10.1 months with panitumumab-FOLFOX4 versus 7.9 months with FOLFOX4 alone (hazard ratio 0.72; 95% CI 0.58 to 0.90; P=0.004) and overall survival was 26.0 versus 20.2 months (hazard ratio 0.78; 95% CI 0.62 to 0.99; P=0.04) — relative measures beside the absolute medians. The 108 patients with other RAS mutations had inferior progression-free and overall survival with panitumumab-FOLFOX4, consistent with the KRAS exon 2 mutant findings. BRAF mutations were a negative prognostic factor. No new safety signals were identified.
cards.watchOut: A prospective-retrospective biomarker analysis: the fully RAS wild-type group (n=512) is a subset of the 1,183 randomised, defined by extended testing that was 90% ascertained — the cleaner benefit estimate and the selection caveat travel together.
cards.source: Douillard JY et al. Panitumumab-FOLFOX4 treatment and RAS mutations in colorectal cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 24024839. cards.headline: PRIME final analysis (Douillard 2014): KRAS wild-type overall survival HR 0.88 (P=.17, not significant) at the prespecified final analysis, and HR 0.83 (P=.03) in the exploratory updated analysis at over 80% of events — both printed, neither cherry-picked
cards.summary: PRIME final analysis (Douillard 2014): KRAS wild-type overall survival HR 0.88 (P=.17, not significant) at the prespecified final analysis, and HR 0.83 (P=.03) in the exploratory updated analysis at over 80% of events — both printed, neither cherry-picked
cards.type: Prespecified final analysis of PRIME, with an exploratory updated survival analysis (same trial — not independent evidence)
cards.people: All 1,183 patients randomised in PRIME; the prespecified final descriptive analysis was planned for 30 months after the last patient was enrolled (68% overall-survival events), with an exploratory updated survival analysis at over 80% of events.
cards.result: In wild-type KRAS disease, median progression-free survival was 10.0 months (95% CI 9.3–11.4) on panitumumab-FOLFOX4 versus 8.6 months (7.5–9.5) on FOLFOX4 (hazard ratio 0.80; 95% CI 0.67–0.95; P=0.01). Median overall survival was 23.9 months (20.3–27.7) versus 19.7 months (17.6–22.7) (hazard ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.73–1.06; P=0.17) — not significant at the prespecified final analysis. The exploratory updated analysis showed a significant survival difference (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% CI 0.70–0.98; P=0.03). Both analyses are printed, as the row directs. The adverse-event profile was consistent with the primary analysis.
cards.watchOut: The prespecified final survival analysis is the non-significant one; the significant figure comes from a later exploratory update. Quoting only the second misstates the record.

cards.headline: Synthesis: PRIME is a biomarker-selection shelf — panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 helps RAS wild-type tumours (fully wild-type: PFS 10.1 vs 7.9 months, OS 26.0 vs 20.2 months) and harms RAS-mutant tumours (mutant KRAS PFS HR 1.29, relative), so RAS testing is half the answer
cards.summary: Synthesis: PRIME is a biomarker-selection shelf — panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 helps RAS wild-type tumours (fully wild-type: PFS 10.1 vs 7.9 months, OS 26.0 vs 20.2 months) and harms RAS-mutant tumours (mutant KRAS PFS HR 1.29, relative), so RAS testing is half the answer
cards.people: PRIME alone: 1,183 randomised first-line patients; 512 fully RAS wild-type in the extended analysis; all three cards are reports of this single trial.
cards.result: Benefit in wild-type disease: KRAS wild-type progression-free survival 9.6 vs 8.0 months (HR 0.80, relative) at the primary analysis; fully RAS wild-type progression-free survival 10.1 vs 7.9 months (HR 0.72, relative) and overall survival 26.0 vs 20.2 months (HR 0.78, relative). The KRAS wild-type final overall-survival analysis was not significant (HR 0.88; P=.17), with an exploratory update at HR 0.83 (P=.03) — both printed. Harm in mutant disease: progression-free-survival HR 1.29 (relative) in mutant KRAS, with other RAS mutations likewise predicting inferior outcomes on panitumumab.
cards.watchOut: A single-trial shelf: PRIME is the whole base. The result applies only with full RAS testing — KRAS exon 2 testing alone leaves the other-RAS-mutant patients, who were harmed, inside the treated group.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Sunitinib in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours: progression-free survival doubled (11.4 vs 5.5 months) in an early-stopped trial; final overall survival not significant (P=.094)
shelves.question: In patients with advanced, well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, does continuous sunitinib 37.5 mg daily prolong progression-free survival versus placebo, and does the final analysis show an overall-survival benefit?
