shelves.balance: SPLIT, on a single small trial (171 randomised) that was STOPPED EARLY. Progression-free survival doubled: 11.4 vs 5.5 months (HR 0.42, relative), confirmed by blinded central review at 12.6 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.32, relative); objective response 9.3% vs 0%. Overall survival: the interim HR 0.41 at early stopping did NOT hold — final median 38.6 vs 29.1 months (HR 0.73; P=.094, not significant), with 69% crossover from placebo to sunitinib; the crossover-adjusted RPSFT analysis is carded as a labelled sensitivity analysis only. Quality of life was maintained except for worse diarrhoea.

cards.headline: Primary report (Raymond 2011): sunitinib 37.5 mg daily doubled progression-free survival versus placebo (11.4 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.42, relative) in a trial stopped early; response 9.3% vs 0%
cards.summary: Primary report (Raymond 2011): sunitinib 37.5 mg daily doubled progression-free survival versus placebo (11.4 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.42, relative) in a trial stopped early; response 9.3% vs 0%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, sunitinib vs placebo (primary report; trial stopped early)
cards.people: 171 patients with advanced, well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours and documented progression within the previous 12 months, randomised 1:1 to best supportive care with sunitinib 37.5 mg daily or placebo.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 11.4 months on sunitinib versus 5.5 months on placebo (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.42; 95% CI 0.26 to 0.66; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. The objective response rate was 9.3% versus 0%. At this early cutoff, 9 deaths (10%) were reported on sunitinib versus 21 (25%) on placebo (hazard ratio for death 0.41; 95% CI 0.19 to 0.89; P=0.02) — an immature figure from a stopped-early trial, superseded by the final analysis carded below. The most frequent adverse events on sunitinib were diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, asthenia and fatigue.
cards.watchOut: EARLY STOPPING, on the face as the row directs: the study was discontinued early after the monitoring committee saw more serious adverse events and deaths on placebo and a progression-free-survival difference favouring sunitinib — early stopping tends to inflate effect estimates, and the interim survival hazard ratio of 0.41 did not survive to the final analysis.
cards.source: Raymond E et al. Sunitinib malate for the treatment of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. The New England journal of medicine. 2011. PMID: 21306237. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00428597. cards.headline: Final analysis (Faivre 2017): central-review progression-free survival 12.6 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.32, relative), but final overall survival was NOT significant — 38.6 vs 29.1 months, HR 0.73, P=.094 — with 69% crossover; the crossover-adjusted analysis is a labelled sensitivity analysis only
cards.summary: Final analysis (Faivre 2017): central-review progression-free survival 12.6 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.32, relative), but final overall survival was NOT significant — 38.6 vs 29.1 months, HR 0.73, P=.094 — with 69% crossover; the crossover-adjusted analysis is a labelled sensitivity analysis only
cards.type: Updated central-review progression-free survival and final overall-survival report of the same trial (not independent evidence); RPSFT crossover adjustment labelled as a sensitivity analysis
cards.people: The same 171 randomised patients (86 sunitinib, 85 placebo); 160 (94%) had complete scan sets for the retrospective blinded independent central review; overall survival was assessed five years after study closure.
cards.result: By blinded central review, median progression-free survival was 12.6 months (95% CI 11.1–20.6) on sunitinib versus 5.8 months (3.8–7.2) on placebo (hazard ratio 0.32; 95% CI 0.18–0.55; P=0.000015) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Final median overall survival was 38.6 months (25.6–56.4) versus 29.1 months (16.4–36.8) (hazard ratio 0.73; 95% CI 0.50–1.06; P=0.094) — not significant, and printed on the face as the row directs. 69% of placebo patients had crossed over to sunitinib. A rank-preserving structural failure time (RPSFT) crossover-adjusted analysis is reported as confirming a survival benefit — carded here as a LABELLED SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS only, not as the trial's survival result.
cards.watchOut: The unadjusted final survival result is the null one (P=.094); the crossover-adjusted RPSFT figure rests on modelling assumptions and must never be quoted as the trial's overall-survival result.

cards.people: The same trial's patients (86 sunitinib, 85 placebo) completing the EORTC QLQ-C30 at baseline, on day 1 of every 4-week cycle, and at end of treatment or withdrawal; changes of 10 points or more were deemed clinically meaningful.
cards.result: Baseline health-related quality-of-life scores were well balanced and generally maintained over time in both groups. Over the first 10 cycles there were no significant differences in global quality of life or in cognitive, emotional, physical, role or social functioning, or in symptom scales, except worsening diarrhoea with sunitinib (P<0.0001 versus placebo). Insomnia also worsened with sunitinib (P=0.0372) but the difference was not clinically meaningful by the 10-point threshold.
cards.watchOut: A retrospective patient-reported analysis of a trial stopped early, so follow-up is short; it supports tolerability context only.

shelves.question: In men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, does enzalutamide prolong overall survival after docetaxel (AFFIRM) and before chemotherapy (PREVAIL)?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — two large phase 3 placebo-controlled trials, one in each mCRPC setting, both showing overall-survival gains with absolutes beside every relative measure. AFFIRM, post-docetaxel (1,199 randomised): median OS 18.4 vs 13.6 months (HR 0.63, relative); seizures in 5 patients (0.6%) on enzalutamide. PREVAIL, chemotherapy-naive (1,717 randomised): radiographic PFS at 12 months 65% vs 14% (HR 0.19, relative); OS HR 0.71 (relative) at interim, attenuating to HR 0.77 (relative; median 35.3 vs 31.3 months) at the extended final analysis after crossover. The two settings are labelled slices, never pooled.

cards.headline: AFFIRM (Scher 2012): after docetaxel, enzalutamide prolonged overall survival (18.4 vs 13.6 months, HR 0.63, relative); seizures in 5 patients (0.6%) on enzalutamide
cards.summary: AFFIRM (Scher 2012): after docetaxel, enzalutamide prolonged overall survival (18.4 vs 13.6 months, HR 0.63, relative); seizures in 5 patients (0.6%) on enzalutamide
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (AFFIRM), post-docetaxel setting
cards.people: 1,199 men with castration-resistant prostate cancer after chemotherapy, randomised 2:1 to oral enzalutamide 160 mg daily (800) or placebo (399), stratified by performance status and pain intensity; the trial was stopped after a planned interim analysis at 520 deaths.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 18.4 months (95% CI 17.3 to not yet reached) on enzalutamide versus 13.6 months (11.3 to 15.8) on placebo (hazard ratio for death 0.63; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.75; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. All secondary endpoints favoured enzalutamide: PSA reduction of 50% or more in 54% vs 2%, soft-tissue response 29% vs 4%, quality-of-life response 43% vs 18%, radiographic progression-free survival 8.3 vs 2.9 months (hazard ratio 0.40) and time to first skeletal-related event 16.7 vs 13.3 months (hazard ratio 0.69). Fatigue, diarrhoea and hot flashes were more frequent on enzalutamide; seizures were reported in five patients (0.6%) receiving enzalutamide — the seizure risk is on the face, as the row directs.
cards.watchOut: Stopped at a planned interim analysis (520 deaths), so the survival estimate is from an interim look; the population is post-docetaxel disease — the chemotherapy-naive slice is PREVAIL, carded next, and the two settings are labelled, not pooled.
cards.source: Scher HI et al. Increased survival with enzalutamide in prostate cancer after chemotherapy. The New England journal of medicine. 2012. PMID: 22894553. cards.headline: PREVAIL primary (Beer 2014): before chemotherapy, enzalutamide gave radiographic progression-free survival of 65% vs 14% at 12 months (HR 0.19, relative) and an interim overall-survival advantage (HR 0.71, relative)
cards.summary: PREVAIL primary (Beer 2014): before chemotherapy, enzalutamide gave radiographic progression-free survival of 65% vs 14% at 12 months (HR 0.19, relative) and an interim overall-survival advantage (HR 0.71, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (PREVAIL), chemotherapy-naive setting (interim primary report)
cards.people: 1,717 chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic prostate cancer progressing despite androgen-deprivation therapy, randomised to enzalutamide 160 mg daily or placebo; the trial was stopped after a planned interim analysis at 540 deaths.
cards.result: The rate of radiographic progression-free survival at 12 months was 65% on enzalutamide versus 14% on placebo (hazard ratio 0.19; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.23; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute rates. At the data cutoff, 626 patients (72%) in the enzalutamide group and 532 (63%) in the placebo group were alive (hazard ratio for death 0.71; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.84; P<0.001). All secondary endpoints favoured enzalutamide, including time to chemotherapy initiation (hazard ratio 0.35) and PSA decline of at least 50% (78% vs 3%). Fatigue and hypertension were the most common clinically relevant adverse events associated with enzalutamide.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis at 540 deaths in a trial stopped for benefit; the extended final analysis is carded below, where the survival hazard ratio attenuates with longer follow-up and subsequent therapy — both figures are printed.
cards.source: Beer TM et al. Enzalutamide in metastatic prostate cancer before chemotherapy. The New England journal of medicine. 2014. PMID: 24881730. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01212991. cards.headline: PREVAIL extended final analysis (Beer 2017): with longer follow-up the survival advantage persisted but attenuated — median 35.3 vs 31.3 months, HR 0.77 (relative); radiographic progression-free survival 20.0 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.32 (relative)
cards.summary: PREVAIL extended final analysis (Beer 2017): with longer follow-up the survival advantage persisted but attenuated — median 35.3 vs 31.3 months, HR 0.77 (relative); radiographic progression-free survival 20.0 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.32 (relative)
cards.type: Extended final analysis of PREVAIL (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same PREVAIL population (1,717 randomised); this prespecified final analysis added 20 months of follow-up for investigator-assessed radiographic progression-free survival, 9 months for overall survival and 4 months for safety; 167 placebo patients had crossed over to enzalutamide by the survival analysis.
cards.result: Enzalutamide reduced the risk of radiographic progression or death by 68% in relative terms (hazard ratio 0.32; 95% CI 0.28–0.37; P<0.0001), with median investigator-assessed radiographic progression-free survival of 20.0 months (95% CI 18.9–22.1) versus 5.4 months (4.1–5.6), and reduced the risk of death by 23% in relative terms (hazard ratio 0.77; 95% CI 0.67–0.88; P=0.0002), with median overall survival 35.3 months (32.2–not yet reached) versus 31.3 months (28.8–34.2) — relative measures beside the absolute medians. The most common adverse events on enzalutamide were fatigue, back pain, constipation and arthralgia.
cards.watchOut: The attenuation from HR 0.71 (interim) to 0.77 (final) is expected as placebo patients cross over and receive subsequent effective therapy; it does not erase the benefit, and both numbers are kept on the shelf.

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — two large phase 3 placebo-controlled trials, one in each mCRPC setting, both with final overall-survival gains and absolutes beside every relative measure. COU-AA-301, post-docetaxel (1,195 randomised): final median OS 15.8 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.74, relative; interim HR 0.65). COU-AA-302, chemotherapy-naive (1,088 randomised): radiographic PFS 16.5 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.53, relative); interim OS HR 0.75 did NOT cross its prespecified boundary — printed as such — and final median OS was 34.7 vs 30.3 months (HR 0.81, relative; P=0.0033) despite 44% of controls later receiving abiraterone. Pricing harms: mineralocorticoid effects (hypertension, hypokalaemia, fluid retention) and liver-function abnormalities.

cards.summary: COU-AA-301 primary (de Bono 2011): after docetaxel, abiraterone plus prednisone prolonged overall survival (14.8 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.65, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (COU-AA-301), post-docetaxel setting (interim primary report)
cards.people: 1,195 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who had previously received docetaxel, randomised 2:1 to abiraterone acetate 1000 mg plus prednisone (797) or placebo plus prednisone (398); median follow-up 12.8 months at this interim analysis, after which the data were unblinded.
cards.result: Overall survival was longer with abiraterone-prednisone: 14.8 versus 10.9 months (hazard ratio 0.65; 95% CI 0.54 to 0.77; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. All secondary endpoints favoured abiraterone: time to PSA progression 10.2 vs 6.6 months, radiographic progression-free survival 5.6 vs 3.6 months, and PSA response rate 29% vs 6% (all P<0.001). Mineralocorticoid-related adverse events — fluid retention, hypertension and hypokalaemia — were more frequent on abiraterone.
cards.watchOut: An interim analysis that exceeded the stopping criteria and led to unblinding; the final analysis is carded next and must not be counted as a second trial.
cards.source: de Bono JS et al. Abiraterone and increased survival in metastatic prostate cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2011. PMID: 21612468. cards.headline: COU-AA-301 final overall survival (Fizazi 2012): median survival 15.8 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.74, relative) — confirming the interim result before crossover
cards.summary: COU-AA-301 final overall survival (Fizazi 2012): median survival 15.8 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.74, relative) — confirming the interim result before crossover
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of COU-AA-301 (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 1,195 patients (797 abiraterone, 398 placebo) at 147 sites in 13 countries; final analysis after 775 of the prespecified 797 deaths, at median follow-up 20.2 months, before crossover from placebo to abiraterone.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 15.8 months (95% CI 14.8–17.0) on abiraterone plus prednisone versus 11.2 months (10.4–13.1) on placebo plus prednisone (hazard ratio 0.74; 95% CI 0.64–0.86; P<0.0001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Time to PSA progression (8.5 vs 6.6 months; hazard ratio 0.63), radiographic progression-free survival (5.6 vs 3.6 months; hazard ratio 0.66) and PSA response (29.5% vs 5.5%) all favoured abiraterone. The commonest grade 3–4 adverse events were fatigue (9% vs 10%), anaemia (8% vs 8%), back pain (7% vs 10%) and bone pain (6% vs 8%); no new safety signals emerged with longer follow-up.
cards.watchOut: The final hazard ratio (0.74) is closer to 1 than the interim figure (0.65) — the usual pattern as data mature; both are printed. Note this report's abstract text prints a different registry number in its registration sentence; the registry ID in the source line is taken from the record's databank fields, consistent with the primary report.

cards.headline: COU-AA-302 primary (Ryan 2013): before chemotherapy, abiraterone doubled radiographic progression-free survival (16.5 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.53, relative); overall survival HR 0.75 did NOT cross the prespecified efficacy boundary at this analysis
cards.summary: COU-AA-302 primary (Ryan 2013): before chemotherapy, abiraterone doubled radiographic progression-free survival (16.5 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.53, relative); overall survival HR 0.75 did NOT cross the prespecified efficacy boundary at this analysis
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (COU-AA-302), chemotherapy-naive setting (interim primary report)
cards.people: 1,088 chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, randomised to abiraterone acetate 1000 mg plus prednisone or placebo plus prednisone; the study was unblinded after a planned interim analysis at 43% of expected deaths, with median follow-up 22.2 months.
cards.result: Median radiographic progression-free survival was 16.5 months with abiraterone-prednisone versus 8.3 months with prednisone alone (hazard ratio 0.53; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.62; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. Overall survival was improved numerically (median not reached vs 27.2 months; hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.61 to 0.93; P=0.01) but did NOT cross the prespecified efficacy boundary — printed honestly here, as the row directs, beside the final analysis below. Abiraterone also delayed chemotherapy initiation, opiate use, PSA progression and performance-status decline. Grade 3 or 4 mineralocorticoid-related adverse events and liver-function-test abnormalities were more common on abiraterone.
cards.watchOut: At this analysis the survival result was a trend that had not crossed its boundary — anyone quoting HR 0.75 from this card as a proven survival benefit is overstating it; the final analysis follows.
cards.source: Ryan CJ et al. Abiraterone in metastatic prostate cancer without previous chemotherapy. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 23228172. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00887198. cards.headline: COU-AA-302 final overall survival (Ryan 2015): median survival 34.7 vs 30.3 months (HR 0.81, relative; P=0.0033), despite 44% of the control group later receiving abiraterone
cards.summary: COU-AA-302 final overall survival (Ryan 2015): median survival 34.7 vs 30.3 months (HR 0.81, relative; P=0.0033), despite 44% of the control group later receiving abiraterone
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of COU-AA-302 (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same 1,088 patients (546 abiraterone, 542 placebo) at median follow-up 49.2 months, with 741 of the prespecified 773 deaths observed; 238 of the control group (44%) subsequently received abiraterone as crossover or subsequent therapy, and 67% vs 80% received any subsequent approved therapy.
cards.result: Median overall survival was significantly longer with abiraterone plus prednisone: 34.7 months (95% CI 32.7–36.8) versus 30.3 months (28.7–33.3) (hazard ratio 0.81; 95% CI 0.70–0.93; P=0.0033) — a relative measure beside the absolute medians. The commonest grade 3–4 adverse events of special interest on abiraterone were cardiac disorders (41 of 542 [8%] vs 20 of 540 [4%]), increased alanine aminotransferase (32 [6%] vs 4 [<1%]) and hypertension (25 [5%] vs 17 [3%]).
cards.watchOut: Substantial crossover and subsequent therapy (44% of controls later received abiraterone) would dilute the survival difference, so the final HR 0.81 is a conservative estimate of the drug's effect in this setting.

cards.headline: Synthesis: abiraterone plus prednisone prolonged overall survival in both mCRPC settings — after docetaxel (COU-AA-301 final: 15.8 vs 11.2 months, HR 0.74) and before chemotherapy (COU-AA-302 final: 34.7 vs 30.3 months, HR 0.81) — at the price of mineralocorticoid effects
cards.summary: Synthesis: abiraterone plus prednisone prolonged overall survival in both mCRPC settings — after docetaxel (COU-AA-301 final: 15.8 vs 11.2 months, HR 0.74) and before chemotherapy (COU-AA-302 final: 34.7 vs 30.3 months, HR 0.81) — at the price of mineralocorticoid effects
cards.people: COU-AA-301 (1,195 randomised, post-docetaxel) and COU-AA-302 (1,088 randomised, chemotherapy-naive), each with its interim and final reports carded — two trials, two settings, labelled slices.
cards.result: Final overall-survival hazard ratios were 0.74 (301) and 0.81 (302), both relative measures with absolute medians on their cards; the interim figures (0.65 and 0.75) are also printed, including the fact that 302's interim survival result did not cross its prespecified boundary. Radiographic progression-free survival in 302 was 16.5 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.53, relative). The pricing harms are mineralocorticoid effects — hypertension, hypokalaemia, fluid retention — plus liver-function abnormalities and, at final analysis in 302, cardiac disorders in 8% vs 4% (grade 3–4). Abiraterone in hormone-sensitive disease is a different question, homed at shelf #767 — not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: Both trials compared abiraterone plus prednisone against prednisone alone, so the shelf answers the added-drug question, not a comparison against enzalutamide or chemotherapy.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: ARPI doublets in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: ARCHES, ENZAMET and TITAN — final overall-survival HRs 0.66, 0.70 and 0.65 for adding enzalutamide or apalutamide to ADT
shelves.question: In men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, does adding enzalutamide (ARCHES, ENZAMET) or apalutamide (TITAN) to androgen deprivation therapy prolong radiographic progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Androgen Antagonists/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Benzamides · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Metastasis · Nitriles · Phenylthiohydantoin/administration & dosage,adverse effects,analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Progression-Free Survival · Prostatic Neoplasms/drug therapy,pathology
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — three phase 3 trials, two agents, concordant overall-survival gains when an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor is added to androgen deprivation, with absolutes beside every relative measure where the records provide them. ARCHES (enzalutamide vs placebo, both plus ADT; 1,150 randomised): radiographic PFS HR 0.39 (relative); final OS HR 0.66 (relative), medians not reached in either arm, 31.3% crossover. ENZAMET (enzalutamide vs standard antiandrogen, both with testosterone suppression; 1,125 randomised): OS HR 0.67 (relative) at primary, 0.70 (relative) at the 68-month update with 5-year survival 67% vs 57%; seizures 7 vs 0. TITAN (apalutamide vs placebo, both plus ADT; 1,052 randomised): radiographic PFS HR 0.48 and final OS HR 0.65 (both relative; median not reached vs 52.2 months), crossover-adjusted HR 0.52 labelled as a sensitivity analysis. PARTIAL beside #767 (abiraterone/docetaxel intensification): only the enzalutamide/apalutamide doublet slice is carded here.

cards.headline: ARCHES primary (Armstrong 2019): enzalutamide plus ADT reduced radiographic progression or death versus placebo plus ADT (HR 0.39, relative; median not reached vs 19.0 months)
cards.summary: ARCHES primary (Armstrong 2019): enzalutamide plus ADT reduced radiographic progression or death versus placebo plus ADT (HR 0.39, relative; median not reached vs 19.0 months)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (ARCHES), enzalutamide plus ADT vs placebo plus ADT — enzalutamide slice (primary report)
cards.people: 1,150 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, randomised 1:1 to enzalutamide 160 mg/day or placebo, each plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), stratified by disease volume and prior docetaxel.
cards.result: As of Oct 14, 2018, the risk of radiographic progression or death was significantly reduced with enzalutamide plus ADT (hazard ratio 0.39; 95% CI 0.30 to 0.50; P<.001) — a relative measure — with median radiographic progression-free survival not reached versus 19.0 months. Benefits were consistent in prespecified subgroups by disease volume and prior docetaxel, and enzalutamide also reduced PSA progression, new antineoplastic therapy, first symptomatic skeletal events, castration resistance and pain progression. Grade 3 or greater adverse events occurred in 24.3% on enzalutamide plus ADT versus 25.6% on placebo plus ADT, with no unexpected adverse events. Overall survival was immature at this report; its final analysis is carded next.
cards.watchOut: The primary endpoint is radiographic progression-free survival; no survival claim rests on this card.

cards.headline: ARCHES final overall survival (Armstrong 2022): enzalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 34% in relative terms (HR 0.66, relative), with 31.3% of the placebo group crossing over to enzalutamide
cards.summary: ARCHES final overall survival (Armstrong 2022): enzalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 34% in relative terms (HR 0.66, relative), with 31.3% of the placebo group crossing over to enzalutamide
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of ARCHES (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same ARCHES population (1,150 randomised: 574 enzalutamide plus ADT, 576 placebo plus ADT); final prespecified survival analysis at median follow-up 44.6 months (May 28, 2021), by which time 154 and 202 patients had died in the two groups and 180 progression-free placebo patients (31.3%) had crossed over to open-label enzalutamide after unblinding.
cards.result: Enzalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 34% in relative terms versus placebo plus ADT (hazard ratio 0.66; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.81; P<.001), with median overall survival not reached in either group — so no absolute median gain can be printed from this record, and none is invented. Radiographic progression-free survival and other secondary endpoints continued to favour enzalutamide. Adverse events were generally consistent with previous reports of long-term enzalutamide use.
cards.watchOut: Crossover of nearly a third of the placebo group to enzalutamide would dilute the survival difference; medians were not reached in either arm, so the benefit is expressed only as the relative hazard ratio printed here.

final overall-survival report of arches (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence) the same arches population (1,150 randomised: 574 enzalutamide plus adt, 576 placebo plus adt); final prespecified survival analysis at median follow-up 44.6 months (may 28, 2021), by which time 154 and 202 patients had died in the two groups and 180 progression-free placebo patients (31.3%) had crossed over to open-label enzalutamide after unblinding. enzalutamide plus adt reduced the risk of death by 34% in relative terms versus placebo plus adt (hazard ratio 0.66; 95% ci 0.53 to 0.81; p<.001), with median overall survival not reached in either group — so no absolute median gain can be printed from this record, and none is invented. radiographic progression-free survival and other secondary endpoints continued to favour enzalutamide. adverse events were generally consistent with previous reports of long-term enzalutamide use. crossover of nearly a third of the placebo group to enzalutamide would dilute the survival difference; medians were not reached in either arm, so the benefit is expressed only as the relative hazard ratio printed here. armstrong aj et al. improved survival with enzalutamide in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the american society of clinical oncology. 2022. pmid: 35420921. registry id: clinicaltrials.gov: nct02677896. mesh: androgen antagonists/adverse effects · benzamides · disease-free survival · hormones/therapeutic use · humans · male · nitriles/therapeutic use · phenylthiohydantoin/adverse effects · prostatic neoplasms/pathology · prostatic neoplasms, castration-resistant/drug therapy,pathology · treatment outcome

cards.headline: ENZAMET primary (Davis 2019): testosterone suppression plus enzalutamide improved overall survival versus testosterone suppression plus a standard non-steroidal antiandrogen (HR 0.67, relative; 3-year survival 80% vs 72%); seizures 7 vs 0
cards.summary: ENZAMET primary (Davis 2019): testosterone suppression plus enzalutamide improved overall survival versus testosterone suppression plus a standard non-steroidal antiandrogen (HR 0.67, relative; 3-year survival 80% vs 72%); seizures 7 vs 0
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (ENZAMET), enzalutamide vs standard non-steroidal antiandrogen, each with testosterone suppression — enzalutamide slice (primary report)
cards.people: 1,125 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, randomised open-label to testosterone suppression plus enzalutamide or testosterone suppression plus a standard non-steroidal antiandrogen, with or without early docetaxel; median follow-up 34 months, with 102 deaths on enzalutamide and 143 on standard care.
cards.result: Overall survival favoured enzalutamide (hazard ratio for death 0.67; 95% CI 0.52 to 0.86; P=0.002) — a relative measure beside the absolute rates: Kaplan-Meier 3-year overall survival was 80% in the enzalutamide group versus 72% in the standard-care group. PSA progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.39) and clinical progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.40) also favoured enzalutamide. Treatment discontinuation for adverse events was more frequent on enzalutamide (33 vs 14 events); fatigue was more common, and seizures occurred in 7 patients in the enzalutamide group (1%) and in none in the standard-care group — printed on the face, as the row directs.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the control is an active standard antiandrogen (not placebo plus ADT alone) — a different comparison from ARCHES and TITAN, kept as a labelled slice. Toxicity was higher among patients also receiving early docetaxel.

cards.headline: ENZAMET updated overall survival (Sweeney 2023): the benefit was sustained at 68 months — 5-year survival 67% vs 57% (HR 0.70, relative); grade 3–4 fatigue 6% vs 1% and hypertension 10% vs 6%
cards.summary: ENZAMET updated overall survival (Sweeney 2023): the benefit was sustained at 68 months — 5-year survival 67% vs 57% (HR 0.70, relative); grade 3–4 fatigue 6% vs 1% and hypertension 10% vs 6%
cards.type: Updated planned primary overall-survival analysis of ENZAMET (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The same ENZAMET population (1,125 randomised: 563 enzalutamide, 562 standard antiandrogen; median age 69 years); the planned primary overall-survival analysis was triggered at 470 deaths, with 476 deaths (42%) identified at median follow-up 68 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was not reached in either group; 5-year overall survival was 67% (95% CI 0.63–0.70) with enzalutamide versus 57% (0.53–0.61) with standard care (hazard ratio 0.70; 95% CI 0.58–0.84; P<0.0001) — a relative measure beside the absolute rates. Benefits were consistent across predefined prognostic subgroups and by planned concurrent docetaxel use. The commonest grade 3–4 adverse events included febrile neutropenia associated with docetaxel (37 of 563 [6%] vs 33 of 558 [6%]), fatigue (33 [6%] vs 4 [1%]) and hypertension (59 [10%] vs 31 [6%]); grade 1–3 memory impairment occurred in 75 (13%) versus 25 (4%). No deaths were attributed to study treatment.
cards.watchOut: Concurrent docetaxel was at clinician/patient discretion in both arms and drives part of the febrile-neutropenia burden; the enzalutamide-specific excesses here are fatigue, hypertension and memory impairment.
cards.source: Sweeney CJ et al. cards.headline: TITAN primary (Chi 2019): apalutamide plus ADT improved radiographic progression-free survival at 24 months (68.2% vs 47.5%; HR 0.48, relative) and overall survival at 24 months (82.4% vs 73.5%; HR 0.67, relative)
cards.summary: TITAN primary (Chi 2019): apalutamide plus ADT improved radiographic progression-free survival at 24 months (68.2% vs 47.5%; HR 0.48, relative) and overall survival at 24 months (82.4% vs 73.5%; HR 0.67, relative)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (TITAN), apalutamide plus ADT vs placebo plus ADT — apalutamide slice (first interim report)
cards.people: 1,052 patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, randomised to apalutamide 240 mg daily (525) or placebo (527), each added to ADT; median age 68 years; 62.7% had high-volume and 37.3% low-volume disease, and 10.7% had received previous docetaxel; first interim analysis at median follow-up 22.7 months.
cards.result: Radiographic progression-free survival at 24 months was 68.2% with apalutamide versus 47.5% with placebo (hazard ratio for radiographic progression or death 0.48; 95% CI 0.39 to 0.60; P<0.001) and overall survival at 24 months was 82.4% versus 73.5% (hazard ratio for death 0.67; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.89; P=0.005) — relative measures beside the absolute rates. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 42.2% versus 40.8%; rash was more common with apalutamide.
cards.watchOut: PMID discipline, printed deliberately: TITAN's reports are the two PMIDs in this shelf's source lines. The neighbouring number one digit away from ENZAMET's primary-report PMID is NOT TITAN — it is the POLO olaparib trial in pancreatic cancer, homed and gated at shelf #1884 — and it is not carded here (the full trap note is in the wave summary). This card is a first interim analysis; the final analysis follows.

cards.headline: TITAN final overall survival (Chi 2021): apalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 35% in relative terms (HR 0.65, relative; median not reached vs 52.2 months) despite 39.5% crossover; the crossover-adjusted HR 0.52 is a labelled sensitivity analysis
cards.summary: TITAN final overall survival (Chi 2021): apalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 35% in relative terms (HR 0.65, relative; median not reached vs 52.2 months) despite 39.5% crossover; the crossover-adjusted HR 0.52 is a labelled sensitivity analysis
cards.type: Final overall-survival report of TITAN (same trial as the card above — not independent evidence); crossover adjustment labelled as a sensitivity analysis
cards.people: The same TITAN population (1,052 randomised); final analysis at median follow-up 44.0 months with 405 deaths, after unblinding in January 2019 allowed 208 placebo patients (39.5%) to cross over to apalutamide; median treatment duration 39.3 months (apalutamide), 20.2 months (placebo) and 15.4 months (crossover).
cards.result: Apalutamide plus ADT reduced the risk of death by 35% in relative terms versus placebo plus ADT (median overall survival not reached versus 52.2 months; hazard ratio 0.65; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.79; P<.0001), and by 48% in relative terms after adjustment for crossover (hazard ratio 0.52; 95% CI 0.42 to 0.64; P<.0001) — the adjusted figure is carded as a LABELLED SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS, not as the trial's headline result. Apalutamide also delayed second progression-free survival and castration resistance (P<.0001 for both); health-related quality of life was maintained in both groups, and safety was consistent with previous reports.
cards.watchOut: The unadjusted HR 0.65 is the trial's result; the crossover-adjusted HR 0.52 depends on modelling assumptions and must not be quoted in its place.
cards.source: Chi KN et al. Apalutamide in Patients With Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer: Final Survival Analysis of the Randomized, Double-Blind, Phase III TITAN Study. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2021. PMID: 33914595. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02489318. cards.headline: Synthesis: three trials, two agents, one answer — adding an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor to ADT prolongs survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (ARCHES final OS HR 0.66; ENZAMET updated HR 0.70 with 5-year survival 67% vs 57%; TITAN final HR 0.65, all relative)
cards.summary: Synthesis: three trials, two agents, one answer — adding an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor to ADT prolongs survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (ARCHES final OS HR 0.66; ENZAMET updated HR 0.70 with 5-year survival 67% vs 57%; TITAN final HR 0.65, all relative)
cards.people: ARCHES (1,150 randomised, enzalutamide vs placebo, both plus ADT), ENZAMET (1,125 randomised, enzalutamide vs standard antiandrogen, both with testosterone suppression) and TITAN (1,052 randomised, apalutamide vs placebo, both plus ADT) — labelled by agent and by comparator, never pooled.
cards.result: Final overall-survival hazard ratios were 0.66 (ARCHES), 0.70 (ENZAMET) and 0.65 (TITAN) — all relative measures, with the absolute rates each record provides printed on their cards (ENZAMET 5-year survival 67% vs 57%; TITAN median not reached vs 52.2 months; ARCHES medians not reached in either arm). Radiographic progression-free survival hazard ratios were 0.39 (ARCHES) and 0.48 (TITAN). Harms: seizures 7 vs 0 in ENZAMET's primary report, with fatigue, hypertension and memory impairment in excess at its update; rash with apalutamide in TITAN. This shelf is PARTIAL beside shelf #767, which homes abiraterone (LATITUDE) and docetaxel (CHAARTED) intensification in the same disease — cross-pointed, not re-carded; the darolutamide doublet (ARANOTE) is homed at pack #7308, also cross-pointed only.
cards.watchOut: The three trials use different comparators (placebo plus ADT; an active standard antiandrogen; placebo plus ADT) and two different agents — concordance across them is the argument, and no pooled estimate is offered.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Docetaxel in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: TAX 327 — 3-weekly docetaxel prolonged survival (18.9 vs 16.5 months), weekly did not; SWOG 9916 — docetaxel plus estramustine 17.5 vs 15.6 months
shelves.question: In men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, does docetaxel-based chemotherapy prolong overall survival versus mitoxantrone-based treatment?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Docetaxel · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Mitoxantrone · Prednisone · Prostatic Neoplasms · Quality of Life · Survival Analysis · Taxoids
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit, for the every-3-weeks schedule. Two randomised trials against mitoxantrone plus prednisone found a survival benefit for docetaxel-based chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: TAX 327 (3-weekly docetaxel plus prednisone, median survival 18.9 vs 16.5 months; hazard ratio 0.76, a relative measure; benefit confirmed on updated follow-up, 19.2 vs 16.3 months) and SWOG 9916 (docetaxel plus estramustine, 17.5 vs 15.6 months; HR 0.80, relative). Weekly docetaxel in TAX 327 did NOT significantly prolong survival (HR 0.91) — schedule is part of the answer. Toxicity was higher on docetaxel, including estramustine-associated cardiovascular events in SWOG 9916.

cards.headline: TAX 327 primary (Tannock 2004): docetaxel every 3 weeks plus prednisone prolonged survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (median 18.9 vs 16.5 months; hazard ratio 0.76, a relative measure) — weekly docetaxel did not (HR 0.91, not significant)
cards.summary: TAX 327 primary (Tannock 2004): docetaxel every 3 weeks plus prednisone prolonged survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (median 18.9 vs 16.5 months; hazard ratio 0.76, a relative measure) — weekly docetaxel did not (HR 0.91, not significant)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (TAX 327), docetaxel (3-weekly or weekly) plus prednisone vs mitoxantrone plus prednisone
cards.people: 1,006 men with metastatic hormone-refractory (castration-resistant) prostate cancer randomised to mitoxantrone plus prednisone, docetaxel 75 mg/m² every 3 weeks plus prednisone, or docetaxel 30 mg/m² weekly for 5 of every 6 weeks plus prednisone (2000–2002).
cards.result: Median survival was 16.5 months on mitoxantrone, 18.9 months on docetaxel every 3 weeks and 17.4 months on weekly docetaxel. The hazard ratio for death was 0.76 (95% CI 0.62 to 0.94; P=0.009) for 3-weekly docetaxel — a relative measure, printed beside the 2.4-month absolute median gain — and 0.91 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.11; P=0.36, not significant) for weekly docetaxel. A ≥50% PSA decrease occurred in 32% (mitoxantrone), 45% (3-weekly) and 48% (weekly); predefined pain reductions in 22%, 35% (P=0.01) and 31% (P=0.08); quality-of-life improvements in 13%, 22% (P=0.009) and 23% (P=0.005). Adverse events were more common in the docetaxel groups.
cards.watchOut: Schedule is part of the answer: only the every-3-weeks schedule showed a survival benefit; the weekly schedule's hazard ratio was not significant, and it must not be quoted as equivalent.

cards.headline: TAX 327 updated survival (Berthold 2008): the 3-weekly docetaxel survival benefit persisted with extended follow-up (median 19.2 vs 16.3 months; survival beyond 3 years 18.6% vs 13.5%)
cards.summary: TAX 327 updated survival (Berthold 2008): the 3-weekly docetaxel survival benefit persisted with extended follow-up (median 19.2 vs 16.3 months; survival beyond 3 years 18.6% vs 13.5%)
cards.type: Updated survival analysis of the TAX 327 phase 3 randomised trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 1,006 men randomised in TAX 327; investigators supplied death or last-follow-up dates for patients alive at the original August 2003 analysis, adding 310 deaths (867 in total) by March 2007.
cards.result: Median survival was 19.2 months (95% CI 17.5 to 21.3) on 3-weekly docetaxel plus prednisone, 17.8 months (95% CI 16.2 to 19.2) on weekly docetaxel and 16.3 months (95% CI 14.3 to 17.9) on mitoxantrone plus prednisone; the 3-weekly benefit remained significant (P=.004). More patients survived ≥3 years on 3-weekly (18.6%) and weekly (16.6%) docetaxel than on mitoxantrone (13.5%). Trends were similar in men older and younger than 65, with and without baseline pain, and above and below the median baseline PSA of 115 ng/mL.
cards.watchOut: An update of the same trial, not a second trial: it confirms durability of the TAX 327 result and adds no independent evidence.

cards.headline: SWOG 9916 (Petrylak 2004): docetaxel plus estramustine prolonged survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (median 17.5 vs 15.6 months; hazard ratio 0.80, a relative measure), at a higher cost in neutropenic fever, nausea/vomiting and cardiovascular events
cards.summary: SWOG 9916 (Petrylak 2004): docetaxel plus estramustine prolonged survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (median 17.5 vs 15.6 months; hazard ratio 0.80, a relative measure), at a higher cost in neutropenic fever, nausea/vomiting and cardiovascular events
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (SWOG 9916), docetaxel plus estramustine vs mitoxantrone plus prednisone
cards.people: 770 men with metastatic, hormone-independent prostate cancer randomised to docetaxel plus estramustine (with dexamethasone premedication) or mitoxantrone plus prednisone in 21-day cycles; 674 patients were eligible (338 docetaxel–estramustine, 336 mitoxantrone–prednisone).
cards.result: Median overall survival was 17.5 versus 15.6 months (hazard ratio for death 0.80, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.97; P=0.02) — a relative measure beside a 1.9-month absolute median gain. Median time to progression was 6.3 versus 3.2 months (P<0.001); PSA declines of ≥50% occurred in 50% versus 27% (P<0.001); objective responses in 17% versus 11% of patients with measurable disease (P=0.30). Grade 3 or 4 neutropenic fevers (P=0.01), nausea and vomiting (P<0.001) and cardiovascular events (P=0.001) were more common with docetaxel–estramustine; pain relief was similar.
cards.watchOut: The docetaxel partner here is estramustine, whose thromboembolic/cardiovascular cost is this slice's pricing harm; the regimen differs from TAX 327's docetaxel–prednisone, so the two trials are labelled slices, not replicates.
cards.source: Petrylak DP et al. Docetaxel and estramustine compared with mitoxantrone and prednisone for advanced refractory prostate cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2004. cards.headline: Synthesis: two randomised trials established docetaxel as the first life-prolonging chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer — TAX 327 (3-weekly docetaxel plus prednisone, median survival 18.9 vs 16.5 months, confirmed on updated follow-up) and SWOG 9916 (docetaxel plus estramustine, 17.5 vs 15.6 months) — while weekly docetaxel in TAX 327 showed no significant survival benefit
cards.summary: Synthesis: two randomised trials established docetaxel as the first life-prolonging chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer — TAX 327 (3-weekly docetaxel plus prednisone, median survival 18.9 vs 16.5 months, confirmed on updated follow-up) and SWOG 9916 (docetaxel plus estramustine, 17.5 vs 15.6 months) — while weekly docetaxel in TAX 327 showed no significant survival benefit
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Both trials compared a docetaxel regimen against mitoxantrone plus prednisone and both found a modest absolute median survival gain of about 2 months, with hazard ratios of 0.76 (TAX 327, 3-weekly) and 0.80 (SWOG 9916) — relative measures printed beside those absolute gains. The weekly docetaxel schedule in TAX 327 was null for survival (HR 0.91, not significant). Toxicity was greater on docetaxel in both trials, including estramustine-associated cardiovascular events in SWOG 9916.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Sipuleucel-T in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: IMPACT — survival prolonged (25.8 vs 21.7 months) with no effect on progression; earlier reports' HRs above 1 are reverse-coded
shelves.question: In men with asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, does sipuleucel-T immunotherapy prolong overall survival — despite showing no effect on time to progression?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Androgen Antagonists · Antigen-Presenting Cells · Antineoplastic Agents · Cancer Vaccines · Cell Culture Techniques · Combined Modality Therapy · Disease Progression · Double-Blind Method · Humans · Immunotherapy · Infusions, Intravenous · Intercellular Adhesion Molecule-1 · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Proportional Hazards Models · Prostatic Neoplasms · Tissue Extracts
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for overall survival, with no effect on progression. IMPACT (512 randomised) found median overall survival 25.8 versus 21.7 months with sipuleucel-T versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.78, a relative measure; 36-month survival 31.7% vs 23.0%), and the earlier D9901/D9902A programme pointed the same way on survival (D9901 medians 25.9 vs 21.4 months). No trial showed an effect on time to progression — D9901's progression primary endpoint was missed (P=.052). CAUTION printed on the cards: the two earlier reports print hazard ratios above 1 (1.70 and 1.50) under reversed reference coding; the direction is worded from the survival medians, never from those HR signs.

cards.headline: IMPACT (Kantoff 2010): sipuleucel-T prolonged overall survival (median 25.8 vs 21.7 months; hazard ratio 0.78, a relative measure; 36-month survival 31.7% vs 23.0%) with NO effect on time to objective disease progression
cards.summary: IMPACT (Kantoff 2010): sipuleucel-T prolonged overall survival (median 25.8 vs 21.7 months; hazard ratio 0.78, a relative measure; 36-month survival 31.7% vs 23.0%) with NO effect on time to objective disease progression
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial (IMPACT), sipuleucel-T vs placebo
cards.people: 512 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer randomised 2:1 to sipuleucel-T (341) or placebo (171), given intravenously every 2 weeks for three infusions; the primary endpoint was overall survival.
cards.result: There was a 22% relative reduction in the risk of death with sipuleucel-T (hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.98; P=0.03), representing a 4.1-month improvement in median survival (25.8 vs 21.7 months); 36-month survival probability was 31.7% versus 23.0% (absolute rates). The effect persisted unadjusted (HR 0.77) and after adjustment for post-study docetaxel use (HR 0.78). Time to objective disease progression was similar in the two groups. Adverse events more frequent with sipuleucel-T included chills, fever and headache.
cards.watchOut: The survival-without-progression paradox is the point of this shelf: overall survival improved while time to objective progression did not, so progression-based monitoring cannot be used to judge this treatment's effect.
cards.source: Kantoff PW et al. Sipuleucel-T immunotherapy for castration-resistant prostate cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2010. PMID: 20818862. Registry ID: NCT00065442. cards.headline: D9901 primary report (Small 2006): the time-to-progression primary endpoint was MISSED (11.7 vs 10.0 weeks, P=.052), yet median survival favoured sipuleucel-T (25.9 vs 21.4 months, P=.01) — the printed hazard ratios above 1 use reversed reference coding and are worded here from the survival direction, not copied blindly
cards.summary: D9901 primary report (Small 2006): the time-to-progression primary endpoint was MISSED (11.7 vs 10.0 weeks, P=.052), yet median survival favoured sipuleucel-T (25.9 vs 21.4 months, P=.01) — the printed hazard ratios above 1 use reversed reference coding and are worded here from the survival direction, not copied blindly
cards.type: Phase 3 placebo-controlled randomised trial (D9901), sipuleucel-T (APC8015) vs placebo
cards.people: 127 patients with asymptomatic metastatic hormone-refractory prostate cancer randomly assigned 2:1 to three infusions of sipuleucel-T (82) or placebo (45) every 2 weeks; on progression, placebo patients could receive a frozen-cell product (APC8015F). All patients were followed for survival for 36 months.
cards.result: Median time to disease progression was 11.7 weeks on sipuleucel-T versus 10.0 weeks on placebo (P=.052 — the primary endpoint did not achieve statistical significance; the report prints HR 1.45, 95% CI 0.99 to 2.11). Median survival was 25.9 versus 21.4 months (P=.01), favouring sipuleucel-T; the report prints HR 1.70 (95% CI 1.13 to 2.56) and an adjusted HR of 2.12 — values above 1 that reflect reversed reference coding (placebo relative to sipuleucel-T), NOT harm from sipuleucel-T, as the survival medians show. The median ratio of T-cell stimulation at 8 weeks to pretreatment was eight-fold higher with sipuleucel-T (16.9 vs 1.99; P<.001). Treatment was well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: HR-CODING CAUTION, printed on the face as the commissioning row directs: this report's hazard ratios above 1 are coded with the opposite reference group to IMPACT's 0.78. Anyone copying 1.70 as a harm signal would reverse the finding; the direction must be read from the survival medians (25.9 vs 21.4 months favouring sipuleucel-T).
cards.source: Small EJ et al. Placebo-controlled phase III trial of immunologic therapy with sipuleucel-T (APC8015) in patients with metastatic, asymptomatic hormone refractory prostate cancer. cards.headline: Integrated analysis of D9901 and D9902A (Higano 2009): across the two earlier phase 3 trials, survival favoured sipuleucel-T (a reported 33% relative reduction in the risk of death) — again with a printed hazard ratio above 1 (1.50) under reversed reference coding
cards.summary: Integrated analysis of D9901 and D9902A (Higano 2009): across the two earlier phase 3 trials, survival favoured sipuleucel-T (a reported 33% relative reduction in the risk of death) — again with a printed hazard ratio above 1 (1.50) under reversed reference coding
cards.type: Integrated analysis of two phase 3 randomised trials (D9901 and D9902A — one programme, labelled as such; the D9901 patients overlap the card above)
cards.people: 225 patients randomised across two identically designed double-blind placebo-controlled trials (D9901 and D9902A) to sipuleucel-T (147) or placebo (78), as three intravenous infusions about 2 weeks apart, and followed for survival until death or a prespecified 36-month cutoff.
cards.result: The integrated analysis reports a 33% relative reduction in the risk of death for sipuleucel-T (printed hazard ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.05; P=.011 — the value above 1 reflects reversed reference coding, with the survival benefit in the sipuleucel-T group, as in the D9901 card above). The treatment effect remained after adjustment for baseline prognostic imbalances, post-study chemotherapy use and non-prostate-cancer deaths. A measure of product potency (CD54 up-regulation) correlated with overall survival. The most common adverse events were chills, pyrexia, headache, asthenia, dyspnea, vomiting and tremor, primarily grade 1–2 and lasting 1–2 days.
cards.watchOut: This is an integrated analysis of two trials, one of which (D9901) is carded separately above — it is a single programme's pooled report, not two additional independent trials, and its printed HR of 1.50 carries the same reversed-coding caution.
cards.source: Higano CS et al. Integrated data from 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trials of active cellular immunotherapy with sipuleucel-T in advanced prostate cancer. Cancer. 2009. PMID: 19536890. Registry ID: none in the record. integrated analysis of two phase 3 randomised trials (d9901 and d9902a — one programme, labelled as such; the d9901 patients overlap the card above) 225 patients randomised across two identically designed double-blind placebo-controlled trials (d9901 and d9902a) to sipuleucel-t (147) or placebo (78), as three intravenous infusions about 2 weeks apart, and followed for survival until death or a prespecified 36-month cutoff. the integrated analysis reports a 33% relative reduction in the risk of death for sipuleucel-t (printed hazard ratio 1.50, 95% ci 1.10 to 2.05; p=.011 — the value above 1 reflects reversed reference coding, with the survival benefit in the sipuleucel-t group, as in the d9901 card above). the treatment effect remained after adjustment for baseline prognostic imbalances, post-study chemotherapy use and non-prostate-cancer deaths. a measure of product potency (cd54 up-regulation) correlated with overall survival. the most common adverse events were chills, pyrexia, headache, asthenia, dyspnea, vomiting and tremor, primarily grade 1–2 and lasting 1–2 days. this is an integrated analysis of two trials, one of which (d9901) is carded separately above — it is a single programme's pooled report, not two additional independent trials, and its printed hr of 1.50 carries the same reversed-coding caution. higano cs et al. integrated data from 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trials of active cellular immunotherapy with sipuleucel-t in advanced prostate cancer. cancer. 2009. pmid: 19536890. registry id: none in the record. mesh: adenocarcinoma · aged · aged, 80 and over · cancer vaccines · disease progression · double-blind method · humans · immunity, active · male · middle aged · neoplasm metastasis · placebos · prostatic neoplasms · time factors · tissue extracts

cards.headline: Synthesis: sipuleucel-T prolonged overall survival in asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in the IMPACT trial (median 25.8 vs 21.7 months; HR 0.78, a relative measure) and in the earlier D9901/D9902A programme, despite no effect on time to progression in any trial — D9901's progression primary endpoint was missed (P=.052)
cards.summary: Synthesis: sipuleucel-T prolonged overall survival in asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in the IMPACT trial (median 25.8 vs 21.7 months; HR 0.78, a relative measure) and in the earlier D9901/D9902A programme, despite no effect on time to progression in any trial — D9901's progression primary endpoint was missed (P=.052)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The pattern is consistent across the programme: survival medians favour sipuleucel-T (IMPACT 25.8 vs 21.7 months; D9901 25.9 vs 21.4 months) while progression endpoints do not move. Two of the three reports print hazard ratios above 1 (1.70 in D9901; 1.50 in the integrated analysis) under reversed reference coding; read beside the medians, they describe the same survival benefit as IMPACT's conventionally coded 0.78, and this shelf words every direction from the medians. Toxicity was mainly brief grade 1–2 infusion-type symptoms (chills, fever, headache).
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits, including the reversed HR coding; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in metastatic pancreatic cancer: MPACT — survival 8.5 vs 6.7 months, priced in neutropenia (38% vs 27%) and neuropathy (17% vs 1%)
shelves.question: In patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, does gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel prolong overall survival versus gemcitabine alone, and at what haematologic and neuropathy cost?
shelves.mesh: Adenocarcinoma · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Albumins · Antimetabolites, Antineoplastic · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Deoxycytidine · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Nervous System Diseases · Neutropenia · Paclitaxel · Pancreatic Neoplasms · Gemcitabine
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit, absolutely modest. The single phase 3 trial MPACT (861 randomised) found gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel prolonged overall survival versus gemcitabine alone (median 8.5 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio 0.72, a relative measure; 1-year survival 35% vs 22%), confirmed on longer follow-up (8.7 vs 6.6 months). The price was grade ≥3 neutropenia 38% vs 27%, fatigue 17% vs 7% and peripheral neuropathy 17% vs 1% (febrile neutropenia 3% vs 1%). Two further MPACT reports (prognostic factors; CA19-9) are carded as labelled companions of the same trial, not independent evidence.

cards.headline: MPACT primary (Von Hoff 2013): gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel prolonged overall survival versus gemcitabine alone (median 8.5 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio 0.72, a relative measure), at a cost of more neutropenia (38% vs 27%) and peripheral neuropathy (17% vs 1%)
cards.summary: MPACT primary (Von Hoff 2013): gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel prolonged overall survival versus gemcitabine alone (median 8.5 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio 0.72, a relative measure), at a cost of more neutropenia (38% vs 27%) and peripheral neuropathy (17% vs 1%)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (MPACT), nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine vs gemcitabine alone
cards.people: 861 patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and Karnofsky performance status ≥70 randomised to nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine (431) or gemcitabine alone (430), treated until disease progression; the primary endpoint was overall survival.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 8.5 versus 6.7 months (hazard ratio for death 0.72, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside an absolute median gain of 1.8 months. Survival rates were 35% versus 22% at 1 year and 9% versus 4% at 2 years (absolute rates). Median progression-free survival was 5.5 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.69, relative); response rate 23% versus 7% (P<0.001). The most common grade ≥3 adverse events were neutropenia (38% vs 27%), fatigue (17% vs 7%) and neuropathy (17% vs 1%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 3% versus 1%. Grade ≥3 neuropathy improved to grade ≤1 in a median of 29 days.
cards.watchOut: The absolute gain is modest — about 2 months of median survival — and is priced in myelosuppression and neuropathy; the relative hazard ratio must not be quoted without those absolute numbers.
cards.source: Von Hoff DD et al. Increased survival in pancreatic cancer with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 24131140. Registry ID: NCT00844649. cards.headline: MPACT long-term survival update (Goldstein 2015): with longer follow-up, median survival was 8.7 versus 6.6 months (HR 0.72, relative), and survivors beyond 3 years occurred only in the combination arm (4%)
cards.summary: MPACT long-term survival update (Goldstein 2015): with longer follow-up, median survival was 8.7 versus 6.6 months (HR 0.72, relative), and survivors beyond 3 years occurred only in the combination arm (4%)
cards.type: Long-term survival update of the MPACT phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 861 patients randomised in MPACT, with overall-survival data collected through May 9, 2013 for this post hoc update; exploratory analyses of CA19-9 and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were also conducted.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 8.7 months on nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine versus 6.6 months on gemcitabine alone (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83; P<.001 — a relative measure beside a 2.1-month absolute median difference). Long-term (>3-year) survivors were identified in the combination arm only (4%). In pooled analyses, higher baseline CA19-9 and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were associated with worse survival.
cards.watchOut: A post hoc update of the same single trial: it confirms and extends the primary result but is not a second trial, and its biomarker analyses are exploratory.
cards.source: Goldstein D et al. nab-Paclitaxel plus gemcitabine for metastatic pancreatic cancer: long-term survival from a phase III trial. Journal of the National Cancer Institute. 2015. cards.headline: Labelled companion — prognostic factors in MPACT (Tabernero 2015): Karnofsky status, liver metastases, age and number of metastatic sites were independent prognostic factors; the treatment effect favoured the combination across most prespecified factors (a companion analysis, not an efficacy report)
cards.summary: Labelled companion — prognostic factors in MPACT (Tabernero 2015): Karnofsky status, liver metastases, age and number of metastatic sites were independent prognostic factors; the treatment effect favoured the combination across most prespecified factors (a companion analysis, not an efficacy report)
cards.type: Labelled companion: prognostic-factor analysis of the MPACT randomised trial (same trial — not independent efficacy evidence)
cards.people: Patients randomised in the MPACT trial (861; see the primary card above); prespecified baseline prognostic factors were examined in Cox models adjusted for stratification factors, with a stepwise multivariate analysis.
cards.result: The treatment effect was significantly associated with survival, of similar magnitude to the primary analysis, and consistently favoured nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine across the majority of prespecified factors. In addition to Karnofsky performance status and presence of liver metastases, age and number of metastatic sites were independent prognostic factors for overall and progression-free survival. Baseline CA19-9 was not an independent prognostic factor in this analysis.
cards.watchOut: A prognostic companion, carded as labelled: it identifies who fares worse, not whether the treatment works, and must not be counted as a further efficacy report.

cards.headline: Labelled companion — CA19-9 decrease at 8 weeks in MPACT (Chiorean 2016): any CA19-9 decline by week 8 marked patients with longer survival, including patients whose best response was stable disease (an exploratory marker analysis, not an efficacy report)
cards.summary: Labelled companion — CA19-9 decrease at 8 weeks in MPACT (Chiorean 2016): any CA19-9 decline by week 8 marked patients with longer survival, including patients whose best response was stable disease (an exploratory marker analysis, not an efficacy report)
cards.type: Labelled companion: exploratory CA19-9 marker analysis of the MPACT randomised trial (same trial — not independent efficacy evidence)
cards.people: MPACT patients with baseline and week-8 CA19-9 measurements were analysed (252 on nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine; 202 on gemcitabine alone) from the 861 randomised.
cards.result: Pooling the arms, patients with any CA19-9 decline (80%) had longer survival than those without (20%): median 11.1 versus 8.0 months (P=0.005). In the combination arm, patients with versus without a week-8 decline had a response rate of 40% versus 13% and median survival of 13.2 versus 8.3 months (P=0.001); in the gemcitabine arm the corresponding survival figures were 9.4 versus 7.1 months (P=0.404). The authors concluded that a week-8 CA19-9 decrease can be an early marker of chemotherapy benefit, including in stable disease.
cards.watchOut: An exploratory, within-trial marker analysis: a CA19-9 fall identifies patients already doing better and does not prove that acting on the marker changes outcomes.

shelves.title: ATRA plus arsenic trioxide in acute promyelocytic leukaemia: APL0406 — event-free survival 97.3% vs 80% without chemotherapy; AML17 — less relapse, null quality-of-life primary
shelves.question: In patients with acute promyelocytic leukaemia, does the chemotherapy-free combination of all-trans retinoic acid plus arsenic trioxide match or beat ATRA plus chemotherapy for event-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Arsenic Trioxide · Arsenicals · Consolidation Chemotherapy · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Induction Chemotherapy · Leukemia, Promyelocytic, Acute · Maintenance Chemotherapy · Male · Middle Aged · Neutropenia · Oxides · Thrombocytopenia · Tretinoin · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit. In low-to-intermediate-risk acute promyelocytic leukaemia, APL0406 found chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide noninferior and then superior to ATRA plus chemotherapy (final report: 50-month event-free survival 97.3% vs 80%, relapse 1.9% vs 13.9%, overall survival 99.2% vs 92.6% — absolute rates), with less haematologic toxicity and fewer infections but more hepatic toxicity. In all risk groups, AML17 found less relapse and less supportive-care need with survival not different — and its quality-of-life primary endpoint was NULL (p=0.39), printed on the card. The APL0406 long-term update (PMID 31611624) was refused: its fetched record has an empty abstract.

cards.headline: APL0406 primary (Lo-Coco 2013): chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide was noninferior — and on event-free survival superior — to ATRA plus chemotherapy in low-to-intermediate-risk APL (complete remission 100% vs 95%; 2-year event-free survival 97% vs 86%)
cards.summary: APL0406 primary (Lo-Coco 2013): chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide was noninferior — and on event-free survival superior — to ATRA plus chemotherapy in low-to-intermediate-risk APL (complete remission 100% vs 95%; 2-year event-free survival 97% vs 86%)
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre noninferiority randomised trial (APL0406), ATRA plus arsenic trioxide vs ATRA plus chemotherapy, low-to-intermediate-risk APL
cards.people: Patients with acute promyelocytic leukaemia classified as low-to-intermediate risk (white-cell count ≤10×10⁹ per litre); 156 evaluable for remission (77 ATRA–arsenic trioxide, 79 ATRA–chemotherapy), in a phase 3 noninferiority trial (noninferiority margin 5 percentage points for 2-year event-free survival). Median follow-up was 34.4 months.
cards.result: Complete remission was achieved in all 77 evaluable patients on ATRA–arsenic trioxide (100%) and 75 of 79 on ATRA–chemotherapy (95%) (P=0.12). Two-year event-free survival was 97% versus 86% (95% CI for the difference 2 to 22 percentage points; P<0.001 for noninferiority and P=0.02 for superiority of ATRA–arsenic trioxide; absolute rates). Overall survival was also better with ATRA–arsenic trioxide (P=0.02). ATRA–arsenic trioxide caused less haematologic toxicity and fewer infections but more hepatic toxicity.
cards.watchOut: This slice is low-to-intermediate-risk disease only; high-risk APL is addressed by AML17 (card below), not by this trial.
cards.source: Lo-Coco F et al. Retinoic acid and arsenic trioxide for acute promyelocytic leukemia. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 23841729. Registry ID: NCT00482833. cards.headline: APL0406 final report (Platzbecker 2017): on the complete enrolled series, 50-month event-free survival was 97.3% versus 80%, relapse 1.9% versus 13.9%, and overall survival 99.2% versus 92.6% — the advantage grew over time
cards.summary: APL0406 final report (Platzbecker 2017): on the complete enrolled series, 50-month event-free survival was 97.3% versus 80%, relapse 1.9% versus 13.9%, and overall survival 99.2% versus 92.6% — the advantage grew over time
cards.type: Final report of the APL0406 phase 3 randomised trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: 276 patients aged 18–71 with newly diagnosed low- or intermediate-risk APL (white-cell count ≤10×10⁹/L) randomly assigned to ATRA–arsenic trioxide or ATRA–chemotherapy between October 2007 and January 2013; 263 were evaluable for response to induction. Median follow-up was 40.6 months.
cards.result: Complete remission was achieved in 127 of 127 patients (100%) on ATRA–arsenic trioxide and 132 of 136 (97%) on ATRA–chemotherapy (P=.12). At 50 months, event-free survival was 97.3% versus 80% (P<.001), cumulative incidence of relapse 1.9% versus 13.9% (P=.0013) and overall survival 99.2% versus 92.6% (P=.0073) — all absolute rates. Post-induction events in the ATRA–arsenic arm were two relapses and one death in remission, versus two instances of molecular resistance, 15 relapses and five deaths in remission on ATRA–chemotherapy; two ATRA–chemotherapy patients developed a therapy-related myeloid neoplasm.
cards.watchOut: The final report of the same trial as the primary card, on the full enrolled series: it supersedes the primary report's numbers where they differ and is not a second trial.
cards.source: Platzbecker U et al. cards.headline: AML17 (Burnett 2015): in all risk groups including high-risk APL, ATRA plus arsenic trioxide gave less relapse and no survival difference versus ATRA plus idarubicin — and its quality-of-life primary endpoint was NULL
cards.summary: AML17 (Burnett 2015): in all risk groups including high-risk APL, ATRA plus arsenic trioxide gave less relapse and no survival difference versus ATRA plus idarubicin — and its quality-of-life primary endpoint was NULL
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised controlled trial (AML17), ATRA plus arsenic trioxide vs ATRA plus idarubicin, all risk groups
cards.people: 235 patients aged ≥16 with PML-RARA-positive acute promyelocytic leukaemia, including 57 high-risk patients, enrolled at 81 UK hospitals and randomised to ATRA plus arsenic trioxide (116) or ATRA plus idarubicin (119); high-risk patients could receive an initial dose of gemtuzumab ozogamicin. Neither maintenance nor CNS prophylaxis was given. The primary endpoint was quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status).
cards.result: Quality of life did not differ significantly between groups (effect size 2.17, 95% CI −2.79 to 7.12; p=0.39) — the primary endpoint was null, and it is printed here rather than dropped. Overall, 57 patients on ATRA–idarubicin and 40 on ATRA–arsenic trioxide reported grade 3–4 toxicities; after course 1, grade 3–4 alopecia occurred in 23% versus 5%, raised alanine transaminase in 10% versus 25%, and oral toxicity in 19% versus 1%. Patients on ATRA–arsenic trioxide required significantly less supportive care. The authors report a high cure rate with less relapse than, and survival not different to, ATRA–idarubicin, with a low incidence of liver toxicity.
cards.watchOut: A different risk frame from APL0406 (all risk groups, including 57 high-risk patients, some of whom received gemtuzumab ozogamicin) and a different comparator backbone — a labelled slice, not a replicate of APL0406. Its null quality-of-life primary endpoint is part of the answer.

cards.headline: Synthesis: chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide matched or beat ATRA plus chemotherapy in two randomised trials — APL0406 in low-to-intermediate-risk APL (50-month event-free survival 97.3% vs 80%; overall survival 99.2% vs 92.6%) and AML17 across all risk groups (less relapse, survival not different, less supportive care) — while AML17's quality-of-life primary endpoint was null
cards.summary: Synthesis: chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide matched or beat ATRA plus chemotherapy in two randomised trials — APL0406 in low-to-intermediate-risk APL (50-month event-free survival 97.3% vs 80%; overall survival 99.2% vs 92.6%) and AML17 across all risk groups (less relapse, survival not different, less supportive care) — while AML17's quality-of-life primary endpoint was null
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The benefit pattern differs by slice: APL0406 shows outright superiority on event-free survival, relapse and (at final report) overall survival in non-high-risk disease; AML17 shows feasibility and less relapse in all risk groups without a survival difference and without the quality-of-life improvement it was powered to test. Toxicity trades chemotherapy's haematologic toxicity, infections and alopecia for more hepatic enzyme elevation with arsenic trioxide. shelves.title: Obinutuzumab in indolent NHL: GALLIUM — PFS 80.0% vs 73.3% over rituximab-based therapy; GADOLIN — PFS 25.8 vs 14.1 months in rituximab-refractory disease; more high-grade toxicity
shelves.question: In patients with indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma, does obinutuzumab-based immunochemotherapy prolong progression-free survival versus rituximab-based immunochemotherapy in untreated follicular lymphoma (GALLIUM), and versus bendamustine alone in rituximab-refractory disease (GADOLIN)?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Agents · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Immunologic Factors · Induction Chemotherapy · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Leukopenia · Lymphoma, Follicular · Male · Middle Aged · Nausea · Rituximab
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for progression-free survival in both settings, priced in toxicity. GALLIUM (1,202 randomised, untreated follicular lymphoma): obinutuzumab-based versus rituximab-based immunochemotherapy gave 3-year PFS 80.0% vs 73.3% (hazard ratio 0.66, a relative measure). GADOLIN (rituximab-refractory indolent NHL): obinutuzumab plus bendamustine versus bendamustine alone gave PFS 25.8 vs 14.1 months on updated analysis (HR 0.57, relative) with an overall-survival HR of 0.67 (relative). Grade 3–5 adverse events were higher on obinutuzumab in both trials (74.6% vs 67.8%; 72.5% vs 65.5%), as were infusion-related reactions.

cards.headline: GALLIUM (Marcus 2017): obinutuzumab-based immunochemotherapy prolonged progression-free survival versus rituximab-based therapy in untreated follicular lymphoma (3-year PFS 80.0% vs 73.3%; hazard ratio 0.66, a relative measure), with more grade 3–5 adverse events (74.6% vs 67.8%)
cards.summary: GALLIUM (Marcus 2017): obinutuzumab-based immunochemotherapy prolonged progression-free survival versus rituximab-based therapy in untreated follicular lymphoma (3-year PFS 80.0% vs 73.3%; hazard ratio 0.66, a relative measure), with more grade 3–5 adverse events (74.6% vs 67.8%)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (GALLIUM), obinutuzumab-based vs rituximab-based immunochemotherapy, untreated follicular lymphoma
cards.people: 1,202 patients with previously untreated advanced-stage follicular lymphoma randomised (601 per group) to obinutuzumab-based or rituximab-based chemotherapy induction, with responders receiving maintenance with the same antibody for up to 2 years. Median follow-up was 34.5 months; the primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
cards.result: Obinutuzumab-based treatment gave a lower risk of progression, relapse or death (estimated 3-year progression-free survival 80.0% vs 73.3%; hazard ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.85; P=0.001 — a relative measure beside the 6.7-percentage-point absolute difference). Response rates were similar (88.5% vs 86.9%). Grade 3–5 adverse events were more frequent with obinutuzumab (74.6% vs 67.8%), as were serious adverse events (46.1% vs 39.9%); adverse events resulting in death were similar (4.0% vs 3.4%). Infusion-related events occurred in 59.3% of obinutuzumab patients versus 48.9% of rituximab patients (P<0.001). Deaths numbered 35 (5.8%) versus 46 (7.7%).
cards.watchOut: Untreated follicular lymphoma only — one of the two settings on this shelf. The progression-free gain is bought with a real toxicity premium over rituximab, which is part of the answer, not a footnote.
cards.source: Marcus R et al. Obinutuzumab for the First-Line Treatment of Follicular Lymphoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2017. PMID: 28976863. Registry ID: NCT01332968. cards.headline: GADOLIN primary (Sehn 2016): in rituximab-refractory indolent NHL, obinutuzumab plus bendamustine (then obinutuzumab maintenance) prolonged progression-free survival versus bendamustine alone (median not reached vs 14.9 months; hazard ratio 0.55, a relative measure)
cards.summary: GADOLIN primary (Sehn 2016): in rituximab-refractory indolent NHL, obinutuzumab plus bendamustine (then obinutuzumab maintenance) prolonged progression-free survival versus bendamustine alone (median not reached vs 14.9 months; hazard ratio 0.55, a relative measure)
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (GADOLIN), obinutuzumab plus bendamustine vs bendamustine alone, rituximab-refractory indolent NHL
cards.people: 396 patients with CD20-positive indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma refractory to rituximab randomised (194 to obinutuzumab plus bendamustine, 202 to bendamustine monotherapy) at 83 sites in 14 countries; non-progressing combination patients received obinutuzumab maintenance for up to 2 years. The trial was stopped after a preplanned interim analysis; median follow-up was about 21.9 versus 20.3 months.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer with obinutuzumab plus bendamustine (median not reached, 95% CI 22.5 months to not estimable) than with bendamustine alone (14.9 months, 95% CI 12.8 to 16.6; hazard ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.74; p=0.0001 — a relative measure). Grade 3–5 adverse events occurred in 68% versus 62%; the most frequent were neutropenia (33% vs 26%), thrombocytopenia (11% vs 16%), anaemia (8% vs 10%) and infusion-related reactions (11% vs 6%). Serious adverse events occurred in 38% versus 33%, and deaths due to adverse events in 12 patients (6%) in each group.
cards.watchOut: A different setting from GALLIUM (rituximab-refractory disease, bendamustine comparator without rituximab) — a labelled slice. The trial stopped early at a preplanned interim analysis, which can inflate the estimated benefit.
