cards.headline: GADOLIN updated analysis (Cheson 2018): with longer follow-up the PFS benefit persisted (25.8 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.57, relative) and an overall-survival benefit appeared (HR 0.67, relative)
cards.summary: GADOLIN updated analysis (Cheson 2018): with longer follow-up the PFS benefit persisted (25.8 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.57, relative) and an overall-survival benefit appeared (HR 0.67, relative)
cards.type: Updated analysis of the GADOLIN phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: 413 patients were randomised in the updated intention-to-treat population (204 obinutuzumab plus bendamustine, 209 bendamustine alone), of whom 335 had follicular lymphoma; median follow-up was 31.8 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 25.8 versus 14.1 months (hazard ratio 0.57, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.73; P<.001 — a relative measure beside an 11.7-month absolute median difference). Overall survival was also prolonged (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.96; P=.027, relative). Benefits were similar in the follicular-lymphoma subset. Grade 3–5 adverse events were reported by 72.5% versus 65.5% (neutropenia 34.8% vs 27.1%; infusion-related reactions 9.3% vs 3.4%); serious adverse events in 43.6% versus 36.9%, and fatal adverse events in 7.8% versus 6.4%.
cards.watchOut: An update of the same trial as the primary GADOLIN card (the randomised total grew from 396 to 413 as the intention-to-treat population was finalised): it adds the overall-survival result but is not a third trial.

shelves.title: Idelalisib in relapsed CLL: huge PFS gains (HR 0.15 and 0.27) — but 22 vs 6 treatment-related deaths with ofatumumab and cumulative colitis, pneumonitis and diarrhoea
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, does idelalisib — added to rituximab (Study 116) or combined with ofatumumab — prolong progression-free survival, and what serious toxicity emerged with longer exposure?

shelves.balance: SPLIT — very large efficacy, very serious toxicity. Idelalisib plus rituximab in relapsed CLL (Study 116, stopped early for efficacy) gave a progression-free-survival hazard ratio of 0.15 (a relative measure), response 81% vs 13% and 12-month survival 92% vs 80%; idelalisib plus ofatumumab gave PFS 16.3 vs 8.0 months (HR 0.27, relative). Against that: with prolonged exposure, grade ≥3 diarrhoea 16.4%, colitis 8.2% and pneumonitis 6.4%, and in the ofatumumab trial 22 treatment-related deaths on the combination versus 6 on control — the number that leads this shelf. No regulatory (boxed-warning/withdrawal) claim is printed: it was not verifiable from the records fetched at build, as the Synthesis card states.

cards.headline: Study 116 primary (Furman 2014): idelalisib plus rituximab produced a very large progression-free-survival gain in comorbid relapsed CLL (hazard ratio 0.15, a relative measure; response 81% vs 13%) and the trial was stopped early for efficacy — serious adverse events 40% vs 35%
cards.summary: Study 116 primary (Furman 2014): idelalisib plus rituximab produced a very large progression-free-survival gain in comorbid relapsed CLL (hazard ratio 0.15, a relative measure; response 81% vs 13%) and the trial was stopped early for efficacy — serious adverse events 40% vs 35%
cards.type: Phase 3 double-blind randomised trial (Study 116), idelalisib plus rituximab vs placebo plus rituximab, relapsed CLL
cards.people: 220 patients with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and decreased renal function, previous therapy-induced myelosuppression or major coexisting illnesses, randomised to rituximab plus idelalisib 150 mg twice daily or rituximab plus placebo; the primary endpoint was progression-free survival.
cards.result: At the first prespecified interim analysis the study was stopped early for overwhelming efficacy: median progression-free survival was 5.5 months on placebo–rituximab and not reached on idelalisib–rituximab (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.15; P<0.001 — a relative measure). Overall response was 81% versus 13% (odds ratio 29.92; P<0.001) and overall survival at 12 months was 92% versus 80% (hazard ratio for death 0.28; P=0.02, relative). Serious adverse events occurred in 40% of the idelalisib group and 35% of the placebo group.
cards.watchOut: Stopped early for efficacy, which inflates effect estimates — and the early report could not show the cumulative immune-mediated toxicity that longer exposure revealed (next card). The efficacy headline must never be read without the toxicity cards on this shelf.
cards.source: Furman RR et al. Idelalisib and rituximab in relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The New England journal of medicine. 2014. PMID: 24450857. Registry ID: NCT01539512. cards.headline: Study 116 final analysis (Sharman 2019): with prolonged exposure, median PFS was 20.3 months and survival 40.6 versus 34.6 months — while grade ≥3 diarrhoea reached 16.4%, colitis 8.2% and pneumonitis 6.4%
cards.summary: Study 116 final analysis (Sharman 2019): with prolonged exposure, median PFS was 20.3 months and survival 40.6 versus 34.6 months — while grade ≥3 diarrhoea reached 16.4%, colitis 8.2% and pneumonitis 6.4%
cards.type: Final analysis of the Study 116 phase 3 trial with open-label extension (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The same 220 patients randomised in Study 116 (110 idelalisib–rituximab, 110 placebo–rituximab); patients from either arm could enter an extension study of open-label idelalisib monotherapy (75 did). Long-term data cover the 110 patients who received at least one idelalisib dose in the primary study, with median follow-up of 18 months (range 0.3 to 67.6).
cards.result: The idelalisib–rituximab-to-idelalisib group had a median progression-free survival of 20.3 months (95% CI 17.3 to 26.3) and an overall response rate of 85.5% (94 of 110; one complete response). Median overall survival was 40.6 months (95% CI 28.5 to 57.3) for idelalisib–rituximab versus 34.6 months (95% CI 16.0 to not reached) for placebo–rituximab. Prolonged idelalisib exposure increased all-grade diarrhoea (46.4%), grade ≥3 diarrhoea (16.4%), all-grade colitis (10.9%) and grade ≥3 colitis (8.2%), and all-grade pneumonitis (10.0%) and grade ≥3 pneumonitis (6.4%), without increasing elevated hepatic aminotransferases. The authors report no new idelalisib-related adverse events with longer exposure.
cards.watchOut: The extension design (placebo patients could cross to idelalisib) blurs the long-term survival comparison, and the cumulative colitis/pneumonitis/diarrhoea rates — not the early interim picture — are the safety record prescribers actually faced.
cards.source: Sharman JP et al. cards.headline: Idelalisib plus ofatumumab (Jones 2017): PFS 16.3 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.27, relative) — but 22 treatment-related deaths on the combination versus 6 on ofatumumab alone; TOXICITY LEADS THIS SHELF
cards.summary: Idelalisib plus ofatumumab (Jones 2017): PFS 16.3 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.27, relative) — but 22 treatment-related deaths on the combination versus 6 on ofatumumab alone; TOXICITY LEADS THIS SHELF
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial, idelalisib plus ofatumumab vs ofatumumab alone, relapsed CLL
cards.people: 261 patients with relapsed CLL progressing less than 24 months from last therapy (median age 68; median three previous therapies), randomised 2:1 to idelalisib plus ofatumumab or ofatumumab alone; patients refractory to ofatumumab were excluded. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by independent review.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 16.3 months (95% CI 13.6 to 17.8) on idelalisib plus ofatumumab versus 8.0 months (5.7 to 8.2) on ofatumumab alone (adjusted hazard ratio 0.27, 95% CI 0.19 to 0.39; p<0.0001 — a relative measure beside an 8.3-month absolute median difference). The most frequent grade ≥3 adverse events on the combination were neutropenia (34% vs 16%), diarrhoea (20% vs 1%) and pneumonia (14% vs 8%). Serious infections were more common on the combination, including pneumonia (13% vs 10%), sepsis (6% vs 1%) and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (5% vs 1%). TWENTY-TWO treatment-related deaths occurred in the idelalisib-plus-ofatumumab group (most commonly sepsis, septic shock, viral sepsis and pneumonia) versus SIX in the ofatumumab group.
cards.watchOut: The death imbalance (22 vs 6 treatment-related deaths) is the single most important number on this shelf. A PFS hazard ratio of 0.27 does not offset it without an explicit, patient-level judgement about infection risk and monitoring.
cards.source: Jones JA et al. Efficacy and safety of idelalisib in combination with ofatumumab for previously treated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia: an open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. The Lancet. Haematology. 2017. PMID: 28257752. Registry ID: NCT01659021. shelves.title: Rituximab maintenance: PRIMA and LyMA — large durable PFS gains (10.5 vs 4.1 years; 7-year PFS 78.5% vs 47.4%) with no demonstrated overall-survival benefit in either trial
shelves.question: In patients with follicular lymphoma responding to first-line immunochemotherapy (PRIMA), or with mantle-cell lymphoma after autologous transplantation (LyMA), does rituximab maintenance prolong progression-free survival — and does it prolong overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Murine-Derived · Antineoplastic Agents · Disease Progression · Female · Humans · Immunologic Factors · Lymphoma, Follicular · Male · Middle Aged · Remission Induction · Rituximab · Tumor Burden · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for progression-free survival; NO demonstrated overall-survival benefit — printed plainly. PRIMA (follicular lymphoma responders to first-line immunochemotherapy): maintenance prolonged PFS (long-term median 10.5 vs 4.1 years; HR 0.61, a relative measure) but overall survival did not differ (HR 1.04; 10-year survival about 80% in both arms), with more infections (39% vs 24%). LyMA (mantle-cell lymphoma after autologous transplantation): maintenance prolonged PFS (7-year 78.5% vs 47.4%; HR 0.36, relative) while overall survival at 7 years was not significant (83.2% vs 72.2%; HR 0.63, P=.088) despite a significant 4-year result. Two diseases, labelled slices.

cards.headline: PRIMA primary (Salles 2011): 2 years of rituximab maintenance after response to first-line immunochemotherapy prolonged progression-free survival in follicular lymphoma (74.9% vs 57.6% progression-free; HR 0.55, a relative measure) — overall survival did NOT differ (HR 0.87, not significant); infections 39% vs 24%
cards.summary: PRIMA primary (Salles 2011): 2 years of rituximab maintenance after response to first-line immunochemotherapy prolonged progression-free survival in follicular lymphoma (74.9% vs 57.6% progression-free; HR 0.55, a relative measure) — overall survival did NOT differ (HR 0.87, not significant); infections 39% vs 24%
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (PRIMA), rituximab maintenance vs observation after response to first-line immunochemotherapy, follicular lymphoma
cards.people: 1,217 patients with previously untreated high-tumour-burden follicular lymphoma received first-line immunochemotherapy; 1,019 responders were randomised to 2 years of rituximab maintenance (505; 375 mg/m² every 8 weeks) or observation (513). Median follow-up was 36 months; the primary endpoint was progression-free survival.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was 74.9% (95% CI 70.9 to 78.9) on maintenance versus 57.6% (53.2 to 62.0) on observation (130 vs 218 progressions; hazard ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.68; p<0.0001 — a relative measure beside a 17.3-percentage-point absolute difference). At 2 years, 71.5% of the maintenance group versus 52.2% of the observation group were in complete or unconfirmed complete response (p=0.0001). Overall survival did not differ significantly (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.47). Grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 24% versus 17% (risk ratio 1.46; p=0.0026), and grade 2–4 infections in 39% versus 24% (risk ratio 1.62; p<0.0001).
cards.watchOut: Only responders to induction were randomised — the result applies to that selected population, not to all patients starting first-line treatment. The survival null is printed here at the primary report, not left to the update.
cards.source: Salles G et al. Rituximab maintenance for 2 years in patients with high tumour burden follicular lymphoma responding to rituximab plus chemotherapy (PRIMA): a phase 3, randomised controlled trial. cards.headline: PRIMA long-term follow-up (Bachy 2019): the PFS benefit endured (median 10.5 vs 4.1 years; HR 0.61, relative) — and overall survival still did NOT differ (HR 1.04; 10-year survival about 80% in both arms)
cards.summary: PRIMA long-term follow-up (Bachy 2019): the PFS benefit endured (median 10.5 vs 4.1 years; HR 0.61, relative) — and overall survival still did NOT differ (HR 1.04; 10-year survival about 80% in both arms)
cards.type: Long-term follow-up of the PRIMA phase 3 trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The 1,018 patients randomised in PRIMA (505 maintenance, 513 observation); 607 (59.6%) consented to extended follow-up, with a data cutoff of December 31, 2016, after about 9 years of follow-up.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 10.5 years on rituximab maintenance versus 4.1 years on observation (hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.73; P<.001 — a relative measure beside a 6.4-year absolute median difference). No overall-survival difference was seen (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.40; P=.7948); 10-year overall-survival estimates were approximately 80% in both arms. No new safety signals were observed.
cards.watchOut: Only 59.6% of randomised patients consented to the extended follow-up, so the long-term estimates rest on a subset; even so, the survival null at 10 years is the mature answer for this question and is printed as such.

cards.headline: LyMA primary (Le Gouill 2017): rituximab maintenance for 3 years after autologous transplantation in mantle-cell lymphoma prolonged event-free, progression-free and overall survival at 4 years (EFS 79% vs 61%; PFS 83% vs 64%; OS 89% vs 80%; HR for death 0.50, a relative measure)
cards.summary: LyMA primary (Le Gouill 2017): rituximab maintenance for 3 years after autologous transplantation in mantle-cell lymphoma prolonged event-free, progression-free and overall survival at 4 years (EFS 79% vs 61%; PFS 83% vs 64%; OS 89% vs 80%; HR for death 0.50, a relative measure)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (LyMA), rituximab maintenance vs observation after autologous stem-cell transplantation, mantle-cell lymphoma
cards.people: 299 patients younger than 66 with mantle-cell lymphoma received R-DHAP induction (overall response 89%, complete response 77%); 257 underwent autologous stem-cell transplantation, and 240 were randomised afterwards (120 per group) to rituximab maintenance (375 mg/m² every 2 months for 3 years) or observation. Median follow-up from randomisation was 50.2 months; the primary endpoint was event-free survival.
cards.result: Four-year event-free survival was 79% (95% CI 70 to 86) on maintenance versus 61% (51 to 70) on observation (P=0.001); progression-free survival 83% (73 to 88) versus 64% (55 to 73) (P<0.001); and overall survival 89% (81 to 94) versus 80% (72 to 88) (P=0.04) — absolute rates, with an unadjusted hazard ratio for death of 0.50 (95% CI 0.26 to 0.99; P=0.04, relative).
cards.watchOut: A different disease and setting from PRIMA (post-transplant mantle-cell lymphoma in patients under 66) — a labelled slice. Its 4-year overall-survival advantage was an unadjusted secondary-endpoint result and did not remain significant at 7 years (next card).

cards.headline: LyMA 7-year update (Sarkozy 2024): the PFS benefit remained large (7-year PFS 78.5% vs 47.4%; HR 0.36, relative) — overall survival was 83.2% vs 72.2% but NOT significant (HR 0.63, P=.088)
cards.summary: LyMA 7-year update (Sarkozy 2024): the PFS benefit remained large (7-year PFS 78.5% vs 47.4%; HR 0.36, relative) — overall survival was 83.2% vs 72.2% but NOT significant (HR 0.63, P=.088)
cards.type: Long-term (7-year) follow-up of the LyMA randomised trial (same trial as the card above — not an independent trial)
cards.people: The LyMA trial population followed for a median of 7.5 years from inclusion; the update reports event-free, progression-free and overall survival for the rituximab-maintenance and observation groups.
cards.result: Event-free survival remained superior on maintenance (median not reached vs 5.8 years; 7-year estimate 76.2% vs 46%; P<.0001). Progression-free survival at 7 years was 78.5% versus 47.4% (hazard ratio 0.36, 95% CI 0.23 to 0.56; P<.0001 — a relative measure beside a 31.1-percentage-point absolute difference). Overall survival at 7 years was 83.2% versus 72.2% (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.08; P=.088 — NOT significant). Cause of death did not differ significantly between groups, lymphoma being the leading cause, with a very low rate of infection-related death.
cards.watchOut: CAUTION, as the commissioning row directs: this report's printed event-free-survival confidence interval for the hazard ratio ('[0.52 to 0.6]') is internally impossible beside its point estimate and is an abstract typo — it is therefore NOT cited on this card. The mature survival result (P=.088, not significant) supersedes the primary report's 4-year survival claim for the shelf's headline.

cards.headline: Synthesis: rituximab maintenance gives a large, durable progression-free-survival gain in both diseases — PRIMA in follicular lymphoma (median PFS 10.5 vs 4.1 years) and LyMA after transplantation in mantle-cell lymphoma (7-year PFS 78.5% vs 47.4%) — with NO demonstrated overall-survival benefit in either trial at latest follow-up (PRIMA HR 1.04, 10-year survival about 80% in both arms; LyMA HR 0.63, P=.088, not significant)
cards.summary: Synthesis: rituximab maintenance gives a large, durable progression-free-survival gain in both diseases — PRIMA in follicular lymphoma (median PFS 10.5 vs 4.1 years) and LyMA after transplantation in mantle-cell lymphoma (7-year PFS 78.5% vs 47.4%) — with NO demonstrated overall-survival benefit in either trial at latest follow-up (PRIMA HR 1.04, 10-year survival about 80% in both arms; LyMA HR 0.63, P=.088, not significant)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: That is the honest headline the commissioning row directs, and it is printed here and in the balance: maintenance delays progression and retreatment for years, at the cost of more infections in PRIMA (grade 2–4 infections 39% vs 24%; grade 3–4 adverse events 24% vs 17%), without a proven survival extension in either disease. LyMA's 4-year survival advantage (HR 0.50, unadjusted) attenuated and lost significance by 7 years. The two trials are labelled slices — follicular lymphoma after first-line immunochemotherapy, and mantle-cell lymphoma after autologous transplantation — never pooled.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits, including the LyMA update's uncited abstract-typo confidence interval; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Adjuvant trastuzumab vs observation in HER2-positive early breast cancer (HERA / B-31+N9831): DFS and survival improved — the founding benefit; duration (6 vs 12 months) is shelf #760
shelves.question: In women with HER2-positive early breast cancer who have completed locoregional therapy and adjuvant chemotherapy, does adding one year of trastuzumab improve disease-free and overall survival versus observation alone?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — PARTIAL beside shelf #760: this shelf cards only trastuzumab versus OBSERVATION; duration (6 vs 12 months) lives on #760 and is cross-pointed, not re-carded. Two programmes, two designs, never pooled. HERA (sequential, after chemotherapy): DFS hazard ratio 0.54 (relative) with an absolute 2-year DFS benefit of 8.4 percentage points; death hazard ratio 0.66 at 2 years and 0.74 at 11 years (relative), 10-year DFS 69% vs 63%, despite 52% selective crossover from observation. NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831 joint analysis (concurrent with paclitaxel): a 39% relative reduction in the death rate. Pricing harm: cardiotoxicity (severe 0.5% in HERA's primary report; secondary cardiac endpoints 4.4% vs 0.9% at 11 years).

cards.headline: HERA primary (Piccart-Gebhart 2005): 1 year of trastuzumab vs observation — DFS event hazard ratio 0.54 (relative), absolute 2-year DFS benefit 8.4 percentage points; deaths 29 vs 37 (not significant); severe cardiotoxicity 0.5%
cards.summary: HERA primary (Piccart-Gebhart 2005): 1 year of trastuzumab vs observation — DFS event hazard ratio 0.54 (relative), absolute 2-year DFS benefit 8.4 percentage points; deaths 29 vs 37 (not significant); severe cardiotoxicity 0.5%
cards.type: International multicentre randomised trial (HERA) — adjuvant trastuzumab vs OBSERVATION slice (sequential, after chemotherapy)
cards.people: 5,081 women with HER2-positive node-negative or node-positive breast cancer who had completed locoregional therapy and at least four cycles of neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, randomised to 2 years of trastuzumab (1,694), 1 year of trastuzumab (1,694) or observation (1,693); this report covers the 1-year versus observation comparison at a median follow-up of 1 year. HERA gave trastuzumab SEQUENTIALLY, after chemotherapy.
cards.result: 347 disease-free-survival events occurred: 127 on 1-year trastuzumab versus 220 on observation. The unadjusted hazard ratio for an event was 0.54 (95% CI 0.43 to 0.67; P<0.0001 — a relative measure), representing an absolute benefit in 2-year disease-free survival of 8.4 percentage points. Overall survival did not yet differ significantly (29 deaths on trastuzumab vs 37 on observation). Severe cardiotoxicity developed in 0.5% of trastuzumab-treated women.
cards.watchOut: Interim analysis at a median of 1 year — the survival contrast was immature, and the 2-year trastuzumab arm of HERA is a duration question (the province of shelf #760), not carded as evidence here.

cards.type: Randomised trial follow-up report (HERA) — adjuvant trastuzumab vs OBSERVATION slice
cards.people: The HERA population as above; this analysis covers 1,703 women randomised to 1 year of trastuzumab and 1,698 to observation, at a median follow-up of 23.5 months (172 women stopped trastuzumab prematurely; 5.7% of the observation group and 3.4% of the trastuzumab group were lost to follow-up).
cards.result: Deaths: 59 on 1-year trastuzumab versus 90 on observation — unadjusted hazard ratio for death 0.66 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.91; P=0.0115, relative). Disease-free-survival events: 218 versus 321 — hazard ratio 0.64 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.76; P<0.0001, relative). The authors concluded 1 year of trastuzumab after adjuvant chemotherapy has a significant overall-survival benefit at 2 years of follow-up.
cards.watchOut: A follow-up report of the same HERA trial as the primary card — not a second trial. Selective crossover of observation patients to trastuzumab (which reached 52% by the final analysis) dilutes the later survival contrast.

cards.type: Final long-term analysis of a randomised trial (HERA) — adjuvant trastuzumab vs OBSERVATION slice
cards.people: The HERA intention-to-treat population of 5,099 women (observation 1,697; 1-year trastuzumab 1,702; 2-year trastuzumab 1,700), enrolled in 39 countries (2001–2005), at a median follow-up of 11 years. Only the 1-year versus observation contrast is carded on this shelf.
cards.result: One year of trastuzumab significantly reduced the risk of a disease-free-survival event (hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.86, relative) and of death (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.86, relative) versus observation; estimated 10-year disease-free survival was 69% with 1-year trastuzumab versus 63% on observation (absolute rates). Two years of trastuzumab added nothing over 1 year (hazard ratio 1.02) — a duration finding, cross-pointed to shelf #760 and not carded here as evidence. Secondary cardiac endpoints: 4.4% (1-year) versus 0.9% (observation); 884 (52%) observation patients selectively crossed over to trastuzumab, diluting the late survival contrast.
cards.watchOut: Same trial, third report — HERA is one programme. The 52% selective crossover means the 11-year survival hazard ratio understates the effect of trastuzumab versus never receiving it; cardiotoxicity, though low, is the pricing harm and is printed here.
cards.source: Cameron D et al. 11 years' follow-up of trastuzumab after adjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer: final analysis of the HERceptin Adjuvant (HERA) trial. Lancet (London, England). 2017. PMID: 28215665. Registry ID: NCT00045032. cards.headline: B-31 + N9831 joint analysis (Perez 2011): trastuzumab WITH chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone — a statistically significant 39% relative reduction in the death rate, with consistent DFS advantage at 3.9 years
cards.summary: B-31 + N9831 joint analysis (Perez 2011): trastuzumab WITH chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone — a statistically significant 39% relative reduction in the death rate, with consistent DFS advantage at 3.9 years
cards.type: Joint analysis of two randomised trials (NSABP B-31 + NCCTG N9831) — adjuvant trastuzumab vs no-trastuzumab slice (concurrent with paclitaxel)
cards.people: Patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer in two North American trials — NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831 — randomised to doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel, with or without trastuzumab given CONCURRENTLY with paclitaxel; the similar designs allowed a joint analysis of the control and trastuzumab-containing arms. This is the concurrent-design programme, a separate slice from HERA's sequential design.
cards.result: At a median follow-up of 3.9 years, the joint analysis continued to show a highly statistically significant reduction in disease-free-survival event rate favouring the trastuzumab-containing arm (P<.001) and a statistically significant 39% relative reduction in the death rate favouring trastuzumab (P<.001) — a relative measure, as the report prints it. The authors concluded the DFS and overall-survival advantages persist with the longest follow-up then reported and continue to outweigh the risks of adverse effects.
cards.watchOut: The abstract of this joint report prints the relative death-rate reduction without the underlying absolute rates — the 39% figure must never be quoted bare. Two trials pooled by design in one joint analysis: one report, two programmes' data, and a different (concurrent) trastuzumab timing from HERA — slices labelled, never pooled on this shelf.

cards.headline: Synthesis
cards.summary: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: PARTIAL shelf — the vs-observation slice only. Two programmes, two designs, never pooled: HERA (trastuzumab sequentially after chemotherapy; primary, 2-year and 11-year reports of ONE trial) and the B-31/N9831 joint analysis (trastuzumab concurrently with paclitaxel). HERA: DFS hazard ratio 0.54 (relative) with an absolute 2-year DFS benefit of 8.4 percentage points at the primary analysis; death hazard ratio 0.66 at 2 years and 0.74 at 11 years (both relative), with 10-year DFS 69% versus 63% — despite 52% of the observation arm crossing over to trastuzumab. B-31/N9831: a 39% relative reduction in the death rate (as printed; no absolute rates in that report's abstract). Cardiotoxicity is the pricing harm: severe cardiotoxicity 0.5% in HERA's primary report and secondary cardiac endpoints 4.4% versus 0.9% at 11 years. How LONG to give trastuzumab (6 vs 12 months, PERSEPHONE/PHARE) is shelf #760 — this shelf cards only trastuzumab versus observation and cross-points #760 for duration.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Adjuvant aromatase inhibitor vs tamoxifen (ATAC / BIG 1-98 / IES): disease-free survival improved across upfront and switch strategies; no survival advantage shown; harm trade is the teaching content
shelves.question: In postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer, does an aromatase inhibitor — anastrozole (ATAC) or letrozole (BIG 1-98) upfront, or a switch to exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen (IES) — improve disease-free survival versus tamoxifen, and with what harm trade?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Anastrozole · Anticarcinogenic Agents/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Aromatase Inhibitors · Breast Neoplasms/drug therapy,mortality,prevention & control · Chemotherapy, Adjuvant · Combined Modality Therapy · Endpoint Determination/methods · Enzyme Inhibitors/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Female · Humans · Middle Aged · Nitriles/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Postmenopause · Prognosis · Tamoxifen/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Triazoles/adverse effects,therapeutic use
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — for disease-free survival, across three trials and three labelled strategies (never pooled): upfront anastrozole (ATAC: DFS hazard ratio 0.83 at 3 years, 0.86 at 10 years in hormone-receptor-positive patients, both relative; absolute recurrence difference 4.3% at 10 years), upfront letrozole (BIG 1-98: 5-year DFS 84.0% vs 81.4%; hazard ratio 0.81, relative) and switching to exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen (IES: hazard ratio 0.68, relative; absolute benefit 4.7 points at 3 years). No overall-survival advantage was shown (ATAC mortality HR 0.95; IES deaths 93 vs 106, not significant). ATAC's combination arm was null (HR 1.02) and is on the face. Harm trade: fractures and arthralgia on aromatase inhibitors against endometrial cancer and thromboembolism on tamoxifen.

cards.headline: ATAC primary (Baum 2002): anastrozole vs tamoxifen — 3-year DFS 89.4% vs 87.4% (hazard ratio 0.83, relative); contralateral breast cancer odds ratio 0.42; the anastrozole + tamoxifen COMBINATION arm was no better than tamoxifen (HR 1.02) — the null arm is on the face
cards.summary: ATAC primary (Baum 2002): anastrozole vs tamoxifen — 3-year DFS 89.4% vs 87.4% (hazard ratio 0.83, relative); contralateral breast cancer odds ratio 0.42; the anastrozole + tamoxifen COMBINATION arm was no better than tamoxifen (HR 1.02) — the null arm is on the face
cards.type: Randomised trial (ATAC) — UPFRONT anastrozole vs tamoxifen slice (combination arm reported, null)
cards.people: 9,366 postmenopausal women with invasive operable breast cancer who had completed primary therapy, randomised to anastrozole (3,125), tamoxifen (3,116) or the combination (3,125) for 5 years; 84% were known hormone-receptor-positive; median follow-up 33.3 months.
cards.result: Disease-free survival at 3 years was 89.4% on anastrozole versus 87.4% on tamoxifen (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96; P=0.013 — relative), with the benefit confined to hormone-receptor-positive patients. The combination arm was NOT significantly different from tamoxifen alone (87.2%; hazard ratio 1.02, P=0.8). Contralateral breast cancer was lower on anastrozole (odds ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.79, relative). Anastrozole was better tolerated for endometrial cancer, vaginal bleeding/discharge, cerebrovascular and venous thromboembolic events and hot flushes; tamoxifen was better tolerated for musculoskeletal disorders and fractures (both P<0.0001).
cards.watchOut: Upfront strategy, 5 years of assigned treatment, median follow-up under 3 years in this primary report — the 5- and 10-year ATAC reports below are the same trial, not new trials. The null combination arm is part of this shelf's record: adding tamoxifen to anastrozole erased the benefit.
cards.source: Baum M et al. Anastrozole alone or in combination with tamoxifen versus tamoxifen alone for adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with early breast cancer: first results of the ATAC randomised trial. Lancet (London, England). 2002. PMID: 12090977. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: ATAC 5-year report (Howell 2005): DFS hazard ratio 0.87 and time-to-recurrence hazard ratio 0.79 (both relative); fewer gynaecological and vascular events on anastrozole, more arthralgia and fractures
cards.summary: ATAC 5-year report (Howell 2005): DFS hazard ratio 0.87 and time-to-recurrence hazard ratio 0.79 (both relative); fewer gynaecological and vascular events on anastrozole, more arthralgia and fractures
cards.type: Randomised trial follow-up report (ATAC) — UPFRONT anastrozole vs tamoxifen slice
cards.people: The ATAC population (9,366 postmenopausal women with localised breast cancer), after a median follow-up of 68 months, with almost all patients having completed their scheduled 5 years of treatment.
cards.result: Disease-free-survival events: 575 on anastrozole versus 651 on tamoxifen (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.97; P=0.01, relative); time to recurrence 402 versus 498 events (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.90, relative); distant metastases 324 versus 375 (hazard ratio 0.86, relative); contralateral breast cancers 35 versus 59 (a 42% relative reduction as printed). Fewer withdrawals and fewer gynaecological and vascular side-effects occurred on anastrozole; arthralgia and fractures were increased.
cards.watchOut: Same trial as the primary card — a follow-up report, not independent evidence. The harm trade is the teaching content: fractures and arthralgia against endometrial cancer and thromboembolism.
cards.source: Howell A et al. Results of the ATAC (Arimidex, Tamoxifen, Alone or in Combination) trial after completion of 5 years' adjuvant treatment for breast cancer. Lancet (London, England). 2005. PMID: 15639680. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: ATAC 10-year analysis (Cuzick 2010): in hormone-receptor-positive patients DFS hazard ratio 0.86 and time-to-recurrence hazard ratio 0.79 (relative); absolute recurrence difference grew to 4.3% at 10 years; overall mortality did not differ (HR 0.95)
cards.summary: ATAC 10-year analysis (Cuzick 2010): in hormone-receptor-positive patients DFS hazard ratio 0.86 and time-to-recurrence hazard ratio 0.79 (relative); absolute recurrence difference grew to 4.3% at 10 years; overall mortality did not differ (HR 0.95)
cards.type: Randomised trial long-term analysis (ATAC) — UPFRONT anastrozole vs tamoxifen slice
cards.people: The ATAC population at a median follow-up of 120 months; the hormone-receptor-positive subgroup numbered 2,618 on anastrozole and 2,598 on tamoxifen. Safety population 3,092 and 3,094.
cards.result: In hormone-receptor-positive patients, anastrozole improved disease-free survival (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.95, relative), time to recurrence (0.79, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.89, relative) and time to distant recurrence (0.85, relative); the absolute difference in time to recurrence grew over time (2.7% at 5 years, 4.3% at 10 years), and recurrence rates stayed lower after treatment completion (hazard ratio 0.81). Overall mortality in this subgroup did not differ materially (hazard ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.06). Fractures were more frequent on anastrozole during active treatment (451 vs 351; odds ratio 1.33, relative) but similar after treatment ended; treatment-related serious adverse events were fewer on anastrozole (223 vs 369).
cards.watchOut: Same trial, third report. The durable benefit is a recurrence/disease-free-survival benefit — no overall-survival advantage was shown, and the fracture excess is confined to the on-treatment years.
cards.source: Cuzick J et al. Effect of anastrozole and tamoxifen as adjuvant treatment for early-stage breast cancer: 10-year analysis of the ATAC trial. The Lancet. Oncology. 2010. PMID: 21087898. Registry ID: ISRCTN18233230. cards.headline: BIG 1-98 primary (Thürlimann 2005): letrozole vs tamoxifen — 5-year DFS estimates 84.0% vs 81.4%; event hazard ratio 0.81 and distant-recurrence hazard ratio 0.73 (relative)
cards.summary: BIG 1-98 primary (Thürlimann 2005): letrozole vs tamoxifen — 5-year DFS estimates 84.0% vs 81.4%; event hazard ratio 0.81 and distant-recurrence hazard ratio 0.73 (relative)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind phase 3 trial (BIG 1-98) — UPFRONT letrozole vs tamoxifen slice
cards.people: 8,010 postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer (4,003 letrozole, 4,007 tamoxifen in the two initially-assigned groups of a four-arm design that also included sequential regimens, counted up to treatment switch); median follow-up 25.8 months.
cards.result: Disease-free-survival events: 351 on letrozole versus 428 on tamoxifen, with 5-year DFS estimates of 84.0% versus 81.4% (absolute rates). Letrozole reduced the risk of a DFS event (hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93; P=0.003, relative) and especially of distant recurrence (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.88, relative). Thromboembolism, endometrial cancer and vaginal bleeding were more common on tamoxifen; skeletal and cardiac events and hypercholesterolaemia were more common on letrozole.
cards.watchOut: A different aromatase inhibitor and trial from ATAC — labelled as its own slice, not pooled with anastrozole. The analysis counts the sequential-treatment arms only up to their switch, as the design specifies.
cards.source: Thürlimann B et al. A comparison of letrozole and tamoxifen in postmenopausal women with early breast cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2005. PMID: 16382061. Registry ID: NCT00004205. cards.headline: IES primary (Coombes 2004): SWITCH to exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen vs continuing tamoxifen — DFS hazard ratio 0.68 (relative), absolute DFS benefit 4.7 percentage points at 3 years; overall survival not significantly different (93 vs 106 deaths)
cards.summary: IES primary (Coombes 2004): SWITCH to exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen vs continuing tamoxifen — DFS hazard ratio 0.68 (relative), absolute DFS benefit 4.7 percentage points at 3 years; overall survival not significantly different (93 vs 106 deaths)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind trial (IES) — SWITCH strategy slice (exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen vs continued tamoxifen)
cards.people: 4,742 postmenopausal women with primary breast cancer who had already received 2–3 years of tamoxifen, randomised double-blind to switch to exemestane (2,362) or continue tamoxifen (2,380) for the remainder of 5 years; median follow-up 30.6 months.
cards.result: First events (local or metastatic recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, or death): 183 on exemestane versus 266 on continued tamoxifen — unadjusted hazard ratio 0.68 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.82; P<0.001, relative), corresponding to an absolute disease-free-survival benefit of 4.7 percentage points (95% CI 2.6 to 6.8) at 3 years after randomisation. Overall survival was not significantly different (93 vs 106 deaths). Contralateral breast cancer: 9 on exemestane versus 20 on tamoxifen (P=0.04). Severe toxic effects of exemestane were rare.
cards.watchOut: A switch strategy in women who had already tolerated and survived 2–3 years of tamoxifen — not an upfront comparison, and its population is selected by that run-in. Labelled as the third, distinct strategy slice on this shelf.
cards.source: Coombes RC et al. A randomized trial of exemestane after two to three years of tamoxifen therapy in postmenopausal women with primary breast cancer. cards.headline: Synthesis
cards.summary: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Three trials, three strategies, labelled slices, never pooled. Upfront anastrozole (ATAC, one trial in three reports): DFS hazard ratios 0.83 at 3 years, 0.87 at 5 years and 0.86 at 10 years in hormone-receptor-positive patients (all relative), with the absolute recurrence difference reaching 4.3% at 10 years — and no overall-mortality difference (HR 0.95); ATAC's anastrozole-plus-tamoxifen combination arm was null versus tamoxifen (HR 1.02) and is on the face of this shelf. Upfront letrozole (BIG 1-98): 5-year DFS 84.0% versus 81.4%, event hazard ratio 0.81 (relative). Switch to exemestane after 2–3 years of tamoxifen (IES): DFS hazard ratio 0.68 (relative), absolute benefit 4.7 percentage points at 3 years, overall survival not significantly different. The harm trade is consistent across trials: aromatase inhibitors bring fractures and arthralgia; tamoxifen brings endometrial cancer, vaginal bleeding and thromboembolism.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Adjuvant FOLFOX vs FL in stage II–III colon cancer (MOSAIC — one trial, three reports): survival improved, driven by stage III; stage II null (HR 1.00); neuropathy is the price
shelves.question: In patients with resected stage II or III colon cancer, does adding oxaliplatin to fluorouracil–leucovorin (FOLFOX4) improve disease-free and overall survival versus fluorouracil–leucovorin alone, and does the benefit reach stage II disease?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — in stage III disease; ONE trial (MOSAIC, 2,246 patients) reported three times, labelled as a single programme. FOLFOX4 improved disease-free survival versus FL (3-year 78.2% vs 72.9%; recurrence hazard ratio 0.77, relative) and overall survival overall (10-year 71.7% vs 67.1%; hazard ratio 0.85, relative), driven by stage III (hazard ratio 0.80). In stage II there was NO survival benefit (10-year hazard ratio 1.00) — the null is on the face. Price: grade 3 sensory neuropathy 12.4% during treatment, 0.7% persisting at 48 months.

cards.headline: MOSAIC primary (André 2004) — ONE trial, first report: FOLFOX4 vs FL — 3-year DFS 78.2% vs 72.9%, recurrence hazard ratio 0.77 (relative); grade 3 sensory neuropathy 12.4% on treatment
cards.summary: MOSAIC primary (André 2004) — ONE trial, first report: FOLFOX4 vs FL — 3-year DFS 78.2% vs 72.9%, recurrence hazard ratio 0.77 (relative); grade 3 sensory neuropathy 12.4% on treatment
cards.type: Randomised trial primary report (MOSAIC — ONE trial, report 1 of 3) — adjuvant FOLFOX4 vs FL
cards.people: 2,246 patients who had undergone curative resection for stage II or III colon cancer, randomly assigned (1,123 per group) to fluorouracil–leucovorin (FL) alone or FL plus oxaliplatin (FOLFOX4) for six months; median follow-up 37.9 months. MOSAIC is ONE trial reported three times on this shelf — the reports are labelled as one programme.
cards.result: Cancer-related events: 237 on FOLFOX4 versus 293 on FL (21.1% vs 26.1%); hazard ratio for recurrence 0.77 (P=0.002, relative). Three-year disease-free survival was 78.2% (95% CI 75.6 to 80.7) versus 72.9% (95% CI 70.2 to 75.7) (absolute rates). On FOLFOX4, febrile neutropenia occurred in 1.8%, gastrointestinal adverse effects were low, and grade 3 sensory neuropathy occurred in 12.4% during treatment, falling to 1.1% at one year. Six patients in each group died during treatment (0.5%).
cards.watchOut: One trial, three reports: do not count this shelf as three trials. The primary report's follow-up (37.9 months) is too short for a survival verdict — that comes from the later reports of the same trial, carded below.
cards.source: André T et al. Oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin as adjuvant treatment for colon cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2004. PMID: 15175436. cards.headline: MOSAIC survival report (André 2009) — ONE trial, second report: 5-year DFS 73.3% vs 67.4% (HR 0.80, relative); 6-year OS 78.5% vs 76.0% (HR 0.84) overall, driven by stage III (72.9% vs 68.7%, HR 0.80); NO overall-survival difference in stage II
cards.summary: MOSAIC survival report (André 2009) — ONE trial, second report: 5-year DFS 73.3% vs 67.4% (HR 0.80, relative); 6-year OS 78.5% vs 76.0% (HR 0.84) overall, driven by stage III (72.9% vs 68.7%, HR 0.80); NO overall-survival difference in stage II
cards.type: Randomised trial survival report (MOSAIC — ONE trial, report 2 of 3) — adjuvant FOLFOX4 vs FL
cards.people: The MOSAIC population (2,246 patients, resected stage II or III colon cancer), randomised to LV5FU2 or FOLFOX4 for 6 months; this report gives final 6-year overall survival and updated 5-year disease-free survival for the same trial.
cards.result: Five-year DFS: 73.3% on FOLFOX4 versus 67.4% on LV5FU2 (hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.93; P=.003, relative). Six-year overall survival: 78.5% versus 76.0% (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.00; P=.046, relative) overall — in stage III disease 72.9% versus 68.7% (hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.97), with NO difference in overall survival in the stage II population. Grade 3 peripheral sensory neuropathy among oxaliplatin patients was 1.3% at 12 months after treatment and 0.7% at 48 months. Second non-colorectal cancers: 5.5% versus 6.1%.
cards.watchOut: The stage-II null is half the answer and is printed on the face of this shelf: the overall survival gain is a stage III gain. Same trial as the primary card — not a second trial.

cards.headline: MOSAIC 10-year update (André 2015) — ONE trial, third report: 10-year OS 71.7% vs 67.1% (HR 0.85, relative); stage II hazard ratio 1.00 — null; stage III hazard ratio 0.80
cards.summary: MOSAIC 10-year update (André 2015) — ONE trial, third report: 10-year OS 71.7% vs 67.1% (HR 0.85, relative); stage II hazard ratio 1.00 — null; stage III hazard ratio 0.80
cards.type: Randomised trial 10-year update (MOSAIC — ONE trial, report 3 of 3) — adjuvant FOLFOX4 vs FL
cards.people: The MOSAIC population (2,246 patients), at a median follow-up of 9.5 years; mismatch-repair (MMR) status and BRAF mutation were assessed in 1,008 tumour specimens.
cards.result: Ten-year overall survival: 71.7% on FOLFOX4 versus 67.1% on LV5FU2 (hazard ratio 0.85; P=.043, relative) in the whole population; stage II 78.4% versus 79.5% (hazard ratio 1.00; P=.980 — null) and stage III 67.1% versus 59.0% (hazard ratio 0.80; P=.016). BRAF mutation was not prognostic for overall survival; deficient MMR was an independent prognostic factor. DFS and OS hazard ratios favoured FOLFOX4 numerically in the small dMMR and BRAF-mutant subgroups, with wide intervals.
cards.watchOut: Same trial, third report — the shelf's evidence base is 2,246 patients once, not three times. The biomarker subgroups (about 95 dMMR and 94 BRAF-mutant tumours) are small with wide confidence intervals and are not a basis for withholding FOLFOX in stage III disease.

cards.result: One trial, three reports — labelled as a single programme throughout: MOSAIC randomised 2,246 patients with resected stage II–III colon cancer to FOLFOX4 or fluorouracil–leucovorin. Disease-free survival improved (3-year 78.2% vs 72.9%; recurrence hazard ratio 0.77, relative; 5-year DFS 73.3% vs 67.4%). Overall survival improved modestly overall (6-year 78.5% vs 76.0%; 10-year 71.7% vs 67.1%, hazard ratio 0.85, relative) — and the gain is a stage III gain (10-year OS hazard ratio 0.80): in stage II the 10-year hazard ratio was 1.00, a null printed on the face of this shelf. The price is oxaliplatin neuropathy: grade 3 sensory neuropathy in 12.4% during treatment, persisting at grade 3 in 0.7% at 48 months — the figure that prices the stage III gain and argues against routine oxaliplatin in stage II.

shelves.question: In patients with metastatic colorectal cancer, does adding cetuximab to first-line FOLFIRI (CRYSTAL) or FOLFOX-4 (OPUS) improve progression-free survival and response — and is the benefit confined to RAS wild-type tumours?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit, confined to RAS wild-type tumours) — a biomarker-selection shelf. CRYSTAL (1,198 patients): cetuximab + FOLFIRI gave a small relative PFS gain overall (hazard ratio 0.85) and NO significant overall-survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.93) — both on the face. In KRAS wild-type tumours the PFS hazard ratio was 0.68 (relative); the extended-RAS reanalysis found benefit across all endpoints in fully RAS wild-type tumours and none in RAS-mutant tumours (14.7% of KRAS exon-2 wild-type tumours carried another RAS mutation). OPUS (phase 2) concurs in KRAS wild-type disease (PFS hazard ratio 0.567, relative). Price: grade 3 skin reactions 19.7% vs 0.2%, more diarrhoea.

cards.headline: CRYSTAL primary (Van Cutsem 2009): cetuximab + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI — PFS hazard ratio 0.85 (relative); overall survival hazard ratio 0.93, NOT significant; in KRAS wild-type tumours PFS hazard ratio 0.68
cards.summary: CRYSTAL primary (Van Cutsem 2009): cetuximab + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI — PFS hazard ratio 0.85 (relative); overall survival hazard ratio 0.93, NOT significant; in KRAS wild-type tumours PFS hazard ratio 0.68
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (CRYSTAL) — cetuximab + FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI, first-line mCRC
cards.people: 1,198 patients with EGFR-positive metastatic colorectal cancer with unresectable metastases, randomised to FOLFIRI alone (599) or FOLFIRI plus cetuximab (599) as first-line treatment; KRAS mutation status was assessed in tumour samples as a pre-planned biomarker analysis.
cards.result: Progression-free survival favoured cetuximab plus FOLFIRI (hazard ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.72 to 0.99; P=0.048 — relative, and small). Overall survival did NOT differ significantly (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.07; P=0.31). In patients with KRAS wild-type tumours the PFS hazard ratio was 0.68 (95% CI 0.50 to 0.94, relative); the treatment-by-KRAS interaction was significant for tumour response (P=0.03). Grade 3–4 adverse events more frequent with cetuximab: skin reactions 19.7% vs 0.2% (grade 3 only), infusion-related reactions 2.5% vs 0%, diarrhoea 15.7% vs 10.5%.
cards.watchOut: The intention-to-treat PFS effect is small and the overall-survival result is null — both facts are on the face of this shelf. The trial enrolled EGFR-positive tumours by the era's testing; the biomarker story is completed by the extended-RAS report below.
cards.source: Van Cutsem E et al. Cetuximab and chemotherapy as initial treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2009. PMID: 19339720. cards.headline: CRYSTAL extended-RAS analysis (Van Cutsem 2015): 14.7% of KRAS exon-2 wild-type tumours carried another RAS mutation — in fully RAS wild-type tumours cetuximab benefited every efficacy endpoint; in RAS-mutant tumours it benefited NONE
cards.summary: CRYSTAL extended-RAS analysis (Van Cutsem 2015): 14.7% of KRAS exon-2 wild-type tumours carried another RAS mutation — in fully RAS wild-type tumours cetuximab benefited every efficacy endpoint; in RAS-mutant tumours it benefited NONE
cards.type: Extended-RAS biomarker reanalysis report (CRYSTAL — same trial as the primary card, not independent evidence)
cards.people: 430 evaluable patients from CRYSTAL with KRAS exon-2 wild-type tumours (64.6% of the 666 KRAS exon-2 wild-type patients), reanalysed for other RAS mutations (four additional KRAS codons and six NRAS codons) with a ≥5% mutant-allele cutoff. A reanalysis report of the CRYSTAL trial — not a new trial.
cards.result: Other RAS mutations were found in 63 of 430 patients (14.7%) whose tumours were KRAS exon-2 wild-type. In patients with fully RAS wild-type tumours, adding cetuximab to FOLFIRI was associated with a significant benefit across all efficacy endpoints; in patients with other RAS mutations, no difference in efficacy outcomes was seen between treatment groups. The safety profile in the RAS subgroups was as expected.
cards.watchOut: Only 430 of the KRAS exon-2 wild-type patients had evaluable samples — a reanalysis subset, labelled as such. Its practical message is a testing rule: all activating RAS mutations must be excluded before anti-EGFR therapy, not just KRAS exon 2.
cards.source: Van Cutsem E et al. Fluorouracil, leucovorin, and irinotecan plus cetuximab treatment and RAS mutations in colorectal cancer. cards.headline: OPUS biomarker report (Bokemeyer 2011): cetuximab + FOLFOX-4 vs FOLFOX-4 in KRAS wild-type disease — PFS hazard ratio 0.567 and response odds ratio 2.551 (both relative)
cards.summary: OPUS biomarker report (Bokemeyer 2011): cetuximab + FOLFOX-4 vs FOLFOX-4 in KRAS wild-type disease — PFS hazard ratio 0.567 and response odds ratio 2.551 (both relative)
cards.type: Randomised phase 2 trial biomarker report (OPUS) — cetuximab + FOLFOX-4 vs FOLFOX-4, KRAS wild-type slice
cards.people: 337 patients randomised in the phase 2 OPUS trial of first-line cetuximab plus FOLFOX-4 versus FOLFOX-4 in metastatic colorectal cancer; KRAS status was evaluable in 315 samples (93%), of which 179 (57%) were KRAS wild-type; 11 of 309 KRAS/BRAF-evaluable tumours carried BRAF mutations.
cards.result: In KRAS wild-type tumours, adding cetuximab to FOLFOX-4 significantly improved progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.567; P=0.0064, relative) and response (odds ratio 2.551; P=0.0027, relative), with a favourable effect on survival also observed. The authors concluded KRAS mutation status is an effective predictive biomarker; the 11 BRAF-mutant tumours were too few for definitive conclusions.
cards.watchOut: A phase 2 trial's biomarker analysis (179 KRAS wild-type patients) — supportive of CRYSTAL's biomarker reading, not a second phase 3 confirmation. Cross-point: the panitumumab / PRIME programme (slate-14 row S14-3-08) tells a parallel biomarker story for the other anti-EGFR antibody — parallel, not pooled with this shelf.
cards.source: Bokemeyer C et al. Efficacy according to biomarker status of cetuximab plus FOLFOX-4 as first-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer: the OPUS study. shelves.question: In patients with advanced EGFR-mutation-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, does first-line gefitinib or erlotinib prolong progression-free survival versus platinum-doublet chemotherapy — and does it prolong overall survival?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — for progression-free survival: six trials, two agents (gefitinib: IPASS, NEJ002, WJTOG3405; erlotinib: OPTIMAL, EURTAC, ENSURE), labelled by agent, never pooled, consistently showed large relative PFS gains versus platinum chemotherapy (hazard ratios 0.16–0.49 in mutation-confirmed populations; median PFS roughly doubled) with less grade 3/4 toxicity. NO overall-survival benefit was demonstrated (NEJ002 P=.31; ENSURE hazard ratio 0.91, not significant) in crossover-era trials. IPASS's mutation-negative harm signal (hazard ratio 2.85, relative) is on the face — it is why testing precedes treatment. Gefitinib interstitial-lung-disease deaths are printed on the relevant cards.

cards.headline: IPASS (Mok 2009) — GEFITINIB: PFS hazard ratio 0.74 overall (relative); in EGFR-mutation-POSITIVE patients HR 0.48, but in mutation-NEGATIVE patients HR 2.85 — HARM — which is why testing precedes treatment
cards.summary: IPASS (Mok 2009) — GEFITINIB: PFS hazard ratio 0.74 overall (relative); in EGFR-mutation-POSITIVE patients HR 0.48, but in mutation-NEGATIVE patients HR 2.85 — HARM — which is why testing precedes treatment
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (IPASS) — gefitinib vs carboplatin-paclitaxel, clinically selected population with mutation subgroup
cards.people: 1,217 previously untreated East Asian patients with advanced pulmonary adenocarcinoma who were nonsmokers or former light smokers, randomised to gefitinib 250 mg/day (609) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (608); EGFR mutation status was known in a subgroup (261 mutation-positive, 176 mutation-negative). IPASS selected patients clinically, not by mutation — the mutation analysis is a subgroup of the trial.
cards.result: Twelve-month progression-free survival was 24.9% on gefitinib versus 6.7% on carboplatin-paclitaxel; PFS hazard ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001, relative) in the intention-to-treat population, meeting non-inferiority and showing superiority. In EGFR-mutation-positive patients the hazard ratio was 0.48 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.64, relative); in mutation-negative patients it was 2.85 (95% CI 2.05 to 3.98, relative) — significantly LONGER progression-free survival on chemotherapy, i.e. gefitinib harmed the mutation-negative subgroup relative to chemotherapy. Common adverse events: rash/acne 66.2% and diarrhoea 46.6% on gefitinib; neurotoxic effects 69.9%, neutropenia 67.1% and alopecia 58.4% on chemotherapy.
cards.watchOut: The mutation-negative harm signal (HR 2.85) is on the face of this shelf by design: it is the reason EGFR testing precedes first-line TKI treatment. IPASS's overall result mixes mutation-positive and mutation-negative patients because selection was clinical.
cards.source: Mok TS et al. Gefitinib or carboplatin-paclitaxel in pulmonary adenocarcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2009. PMID: 19692680. Registry ID: NCT00322452. cards.headline: NEJ002 (Maemondo 2010) — GEFITINIB in confirmed EGFR-mutant disease: median PFS 10.8 vs 5.4 months (HR 0.30, relative); response 73.7% vs 30.7%; overall survival 30.5 vs 23.6 months, P=.31 — NOT significant; one gefitinib death from interstitial lung disease
cards.summary: NEJ002 (Maemondo 2010) — GEFITINIB in confirmed EGFR-mutant disease: median PFS 10.8 vs 5.4 months (HR 0.30, relative); response 73.7% vs 30.7%; overall survival 30.5 vs 23.6 months, P=.31 — NOT significant; one gefitinib death from interstitial lung disease
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (NEJ002) — gefitinib vs carboplatin-paclitaxel in EGFR-mutation-positive NSCLC
cards.people: 230 patients with metastatic NSCLC and confirmed EGFR mutations, chemotherapy-naive, randomised to gefitinib or carboplatin-paclitaxel; the trial was terminated early after a planned interim analysis of the first 200 patients showed a significant PFS advantage.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 10.8 months on gefitinib versus 5.4 months on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.41; P<0.001, relative); response rate 73.7% versus 30.7% (P<0.001). Median overall survival was 30.5 versus 23.6 months (P=0.31 — not significant). Common adverse events on gefitinib were rash (71.1%) and raised aminotransferases (55.3%); on chemotherapy, neutropenia (77.0%), anaemia (64.6%), appetite loss (56.6%) and sensory neuropathy (54.9%). One gefitinib patient died of interstitial lung disease.
cards.watchOut: Early termination for efficacy inflates the apparent PFS effect size; and despite the large PFS gain, overall survival did not differ significantly — the crossover-era pattern that runs through this whole shelf.
cards.source: Maemondo M et al. Gefitinib or chemotherapy for non-small-cell lung cancer with mutated EGFR. The New England journal of medicine. 2010. PMID: 20573926. cards.headline: WJTOG3405 (Mitsudomi 2010) — GEFITINIB: median PFS 9.2 vs 6.3 months vs cisplatin + docetaxel (HR 0.489, relative); interstitial lung disease in 2 gefitinib patients (2.3%), one fatal
cards.summary: WJTOG3405 (Mitsudomi 2010) — GEFITINIB: median PFS 9.2 vs 6.3 months vs cisplatin + docetaxel (HR 0.489, relative); interstitial lung disease in 2 gefitinib patients (2.3%), one fatal
cards.type: Open-label randomised phase 3 trial (WJTOG3405) — gefitinib vs cisplatin + docetaxel in EGFR-mutant NSCLC
cards.people: 177 chemotherapy-naive patients aged 75 or younger with stage IIIB/IV NSCLC or postoperative recurrence harbouring EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations, randomised to gefitinib 250 mg/day (88) or cisplatin plus docetaxel every 21 days for three to six cycles (89), at 36 Japanese centres; 172 patients (86 per group) were included in the survival analyses after five exclusions.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 9.2 months (95% CI 8.0 to 13.9) on gefitinib versus 6.3 months (95% CI 5.8 to 7.8) on cisplatin plus docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.489, 95% CI 0.336 to 0.710; P<0.0001, relative). Myelosuppression, alopecia and fatigue were more frequent on chemotherapy; skin toxicity, liver dysfunction and diarrhoea were more frequent on gefitinib. Two gefitinib patients (2.3%) developed interstitial lung disease, one of whom died.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the comparator is a cisplatin doublet — the PFS gain is consistent with NEJ002's carboplatin-based comparison, but the two trials are separate slices and are not pooled on this shelf.
cards.source: Mitsudomi T et al. cards.headline: OPTIMAL (Zhou 2011) — ERLOTINIB: median PFS 13.1 vs 4.6 months vs gemcitabine + carboplatin (HR 0.16, relative); grade 3/4 toxicity far more frequent on chemotherapy
cards.summary: OPTIMAL (Zhou 2011) — ERLOTINIB: median PFS 13.1 vs 4.6 months vs gemcitabine + carboplatin (HR 0.16, relative); grade 3/4 toxicity far more frequent on chemotherapy
cards.type: Multicentre open-label randomised phase 3 trial (OPTIMAL / CTONG-0802) — erlotinib vs gemcitabine + carboplatin in EGFR-mutant NSCLC
cards.people: 165 patients with advanced EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R) at 22 Chinese centres, randomised to erlotinib 150 mg/day (83) or up to four cycles of gemcitabine plus carboplatin (82); 82 and 72 patients respectively were analysed for the primary endpoint.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 13.1 months (95% CI 10.58 to 16.53) on erlotinib versus 4.6 months (95% CI 4.21 to 5.42) on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.26; P<0.0001, relative). Grade 3/4 toxicity was much more frequent on chemotherapy (neutropenia 42% and thrombocytopenia 40% of analysed patients, versus none on erlotinib); erlotinib's commonest grade 3/4 effects were raised alanine aminotransferase (4%) and rash (2%). Treatment-related serious adverse events: 14% on chemotherapy versus 2% on erlotinib.
cards.watchOut: The hazard ratio of 0.16 is the largest on this shelf and comes from the smallest analysed population — read it as directionally concordant with the other trials, not as a precise class estimate. Erlotinib slice; gefitinib trials are labelled separately.
cards.source: Zhou C et al. cards.headline: EURTAC (Rosell 2012) — ERLOTINIB in European patients: median PFS 9.7 vs 5.2 months (HR 0.37, relative); grade 3/4 rash 13% on erlotinib
cards.summary: EURTAC (Rosell 2012) — ERLOTINIB in European patients: median PFS 9.7 vs 5.2 months (HR 0.37, relative); grade 3/4 rash 13% on erlotinib
cards.type: Multicentre open-label randomised phase 3 trial (EURTAC) — erlotinib vs platinum chemotherapy in European EGFR-mutant NSCLC
cards.people: 174 European patients (France, Italy, Spain) with advanced NSCLC and EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations and no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, randomised to erlotinib 150 mg/day (86) or standard platinum chemotherapy (87 analysed; cisplatin with docetaxel or gemcitabine, carboplatin substituted where cisplatin was unsuitable); enrolment was halted at the preplanned interim analysis because the primary endpoint was met.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 9.7 months (95% CI 8.4 to 12.3) on erlotinib versus 5.2 months (95% CI 4.5 to 5.8) on chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.37, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.54; P<0.0001, relative). Main grade 3/4 toxicities: rash 13% on erlotinib versus none on chemotherapy; neutropenia 22% on chemotherapy versus none on erlotinib. Treatment-related severe adverse events: 6% on erlotinib versus 20% on chemotherapy; one erlotinib patient and two chemotherapy patients died of treatment-related causes.
cards.watchOut: The European-population confirmation of the Asian trials — same direction, stopped early at interim analysis, which again flatters the effect size.

cards.headline: ENSURE (Wu 2015) — ERLOTINIB: median PFS 11.0 vs 5.5 months vs gemcitabine/cisplatin (HR 0.34, relative); overall survival 26.3 vs 25.5 months (HR 0.91 — NOT significant)
cards.summary: ENSURE (Wu 2015) — ERLOTINIB: median PFS 11.0 vs 5.5 months vs gemcitabine/cisplatin (HR 0.34, relative); overall survival 26.3 vs 25.5 months (HR 0.91 — NOT significant)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (ENSURE) — erlotinib vs gemcitabine/cisplatin in EGFR-mutant NSCLC
cards.people: 217 patients from China, Malaysia and the Philippines with stage IIIB/IV EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC, randomised to erlotinib 150 mg/day (110) or gemcitabine/cisplatin for up to four cycles (107).
cards.result: Investigator-assessed median progression-free survival was 11.0 months on erlotinib versus 5.5 months on gemcitabine/cisplatin (hazard ratio 0.34, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.51; P<0.0001, relative); independent-review assessment was consistent (hazard ratio 0.42). Median overall survival was 26.3 versus 25.5 months (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.31; P=.607 — not significant). Response rate 62.7% versus 33.6%. Treatment-related serious adverse events: 2.7% versus 10.6%; commonest grade ≥3 event on erlotinib was rash (6.4%), on chemotherapy neutropenia (25.0%), leukopenia (14.4%) and anaemia (12.5%).
cards.watchOut: The shelf's second explicit survival null (with NEJ002): a doubling of median PFS with no demonstrated overall-survival benefit, in a crossover-era trial — the honest headline for the whole shelf.

cards.headline: Synthesis
cards.summary: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Six trials, two agents, labelled by agent and never pooled into a single estimate. Gefitinib: IPASS (clinically selected; PFS hazard ratio 0.74 overall, 0.48 in mutation-positive patients and 2.85 — harm — in mutation-negative patients, all relative), NEJ002 (median PFS 10.8 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.30) and WJTOG3405 (9.2 vs 6.3 months, HR 0.489). Erlotinib: OPTIMAL (13.1 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.16), EURTAC (9.7 vs 5.2 months, HR 0.37) and ENSURE (11.0 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.34). The honest headline: a large, consistent relative progression-free-survival gain and higher response rates, with less grade 3/4 toxicity than chemotherapy — and NO demonstrated overall-survival benefit (NEJ002 overall survival P=.31; ENSURE hazard ratio 0.91, not significant), in crossover-era trials. IPASS's mutation-negative harm signal (HR 2.85) is why EGFR testing precedes treatment. Interstitial lung disease deaths occurred on gefitinib in NEJ002 and WJTOG3405. Cross-point: afatinib (slate-14 row S14-3-06) is the second-generation slice of the same era — not merged here; third-generation (osimertinib) comparisons live on packs #7301–#7302, where gefitinib/erlotinib appear as comparators.

cards.search: synthesis synthesis in patients with advanced egfr-mutation-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, does first-line gefitinib or erlotinib prolong progression-free survival versus platinum-doublet chemotherapy — and does it prolong overall survival? synthesis all reports carded on this shelf. six trials, two agents, labelled by agent and never pooled into a single estimate. gefitinib: ipass (clinically selected; pfs hazard ratio 0.74 overall, 0.48 in mutation-positive patients and 2.85 — harm — in mutation-negative patients, all relative), nej002 (median pfs 10.8 vs 5.4 months, hr 0.30) and wjtog3405 (9.2 vs 6.3 months, hr 0.489). erlotinib: optimal (13.1 vs 4.6 months, hr 0.16), eurtac (9.7 vs 5.2 months, hr 0.37) and ensure (11.0 vs 5.5 months, hr 0.34). the honest headline: a large, consistent relative progression-free-survival gain and higher response rates, with less grade 3/4 toxicity than chemotherapy — and no demonstrated overall-survival benefit (nej002 overall survival p=.31; ensure hazard ratio 0.91, not significant), in crossover-era trials. ipass's mutation-negative harm signal (hr 2.85) is why egfr testing precedes treatment. interstitial lung disease deaths occurred on gefitinib in nej002 and wjtog3405. cross-point: afatinib (slate-14 row s14-3-06) is the second-generation slice of the same era — not merged here; third-generation (osimertinib) comparisons live on packs #7301–#7302, where gefitinib/erlotinib appear as comparators. see the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Pemetrexed in advanced NSCLC: non-inferior first-line with a histology reversal (squamous disease favoured gemcitabine), and maintenance prolonged survival in JMEN and PARAMOUNT
shelves.question: In advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, is cisplatin–pemetrexed non-inferior to cisplatin–gemcitabine first-line with a histology-dependent advantage (JMDB) — and does pemetrexed maintenance after platinum induction prolong survival (JMEN, PARAMOUNT)?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antineoplastic Agents · Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Fatigue · Female · Glutamates · Guanine · Humans · Lung Neoplasms · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Staging · Neutropenia · Pemetrexed · Prognosis · Proportional Hazards Models · Survival Rate · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), in two labelled limbs that are never pooled. First-line (JMDB, 1,725 randomised): cisplatin–pemetrexed was non-inferior to cisplatin–gemcitabine overall (median OS 10.3 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.94) with less haematologic toxicity — but histology reversed the direction: adenocarcinoma favoured pemetrexed (12.6 vs 10.9 months) while squamous histology favoured gemcitabine (10.8 vs 9.4 months). Maintenance (JMEN, 663 non-progressors after platinum induction; PARAMOUNT, 539 nonsquamous non-progressors after pemetrexed–cisplatin induction): pemetrexed prolonged overall survival in both trials (13.4 vs 10.6 months, HR 0.79; and 13.9 vs 11.0 months, HR 0.78 — both relative measures, absolute median gains 2.8 and 2.9 months), at the cost of more grade 3–4 fatigue, neutropenia and anaemia. The maintenance benefit applies only to patients whose disease did not progress on induction.

cards.headline: JMDB phase 3 RCT (Scagliotti 2008): cisplatin–pemetrexed was non-inferior to cisplatin–gemcitabine first-line (median OS 10.3 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.94) — but histology reversed the direction: adenocarcinoma favoured pemetrexed (12.6 vs 10.9 months), squamous histology favoured gemcitabine (10.8 vs 9.4 months)
cards.summary: JMDB phase 3 RCT (Scagliotti 2008): cisplatin–pemetrexed was non-inferior to cisplatin–gemcitabine first-line (median OS 10.3 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.94) — but histology reversed the direction: adenocarcinoma favoured pemetrexed (12.6 vs 10.9 months), squamous histology favoured gemcitabine (10.8 vs 9.4 months)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised non-inferiority trial (JMDB), cisplatin–pemetrexed vs cisplatin–gemcitabine, first-line advanced NSCLC — first-line histology-selection limb
cards.people: 1,725 chemotherapy-naive patients with stage IIIB or IV NSCLC and ECOG performance status 0–1, randomised to cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 plus gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m² days 1 and 8 (n=863) or cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² day 1 (n=862), every 3 weeks for up to six cycles.
cards.result: Overall survival with cisplatin–pemetrexed was non-inferior to cisplatin–gemcitabine (median 10.3 vs 10.3 months; HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.05, against a non-inferiority margin of HR 1.176). By histology the direction reversed: in adenocarcinoma (n=847) survival was superior with pemetrexed (12.6 vs 10.9 months) and in large-cell carcinoma (n=153) likewise (10.4 vs 6.7 months), whereas in squamous histology (n=473) survival was significantly better with gemcitabine (10.8 vs 9.4 months). Grade 3/4 neutropenia, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia and alopecia were significantly less common with pemetrexed; grade 3/4 nausea was more common.
cards.watchOut: Non-inferiority overall does not mean equivalence in every patient: the histology interaction is the result — pemetrexed should not be read as the better drug in squamous NSCLC, where gemcitabine won. No registry ID is in the PubMed record.
cards.source: Scagliotti et al. Phase III study comparing cisplatin plus gemcitabine with cisplatin plus pemetrexed in chemotherapy-naive patients with advanced-stage non-small-cell lung cancer. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2008. PMID: 18506025. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: JMEN maintenance RCT (Ciuleanu 2009): pemetrexed maintenance after platinum induction prolonged progression-free survival (4.3 vs 2.6 months, HR 0.50) and overall survival (13.4 vs 10.6 months, HR 0.79) versus placebo
cards.summary: JMEN maintenance RCT (Ciuleanu 2009): pemetrexed maintenance after platinum induction prolonged progression-free survival (4.3 vs 2.6 months, HR 0.50) and overall survival (13.4 vs 10.6 months, HR 0.79) versus placebo
cards.type: Randomised double-blind phase 3 trial (JMEN), pemetrexed maintenance + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care after platinum induction — maintenance limb
cards.people: 663 patients with stage IIIB or IV NSCLC who had not progressed on four cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy, randomised 2:1 in 83 centres in 20 countries to pemetrexed 500 mg/m² day 1 plus best supportive care (n=441) or placebo plus best supportive care (n=222) in 21-day cycles until progression; all patients received vitamin B12, folic acid and dexamethasone.
cards.result: Pemetrexed significantly improved progression-free survival (4.3 months, 95% CI 4.1 to 4.7, vs 2.6 months, 1.7 to 2.8; HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.61; P<0.0001 — a relative measure) and overall survival (13.4 months, 11.9 to 15.9, vs 10.6 months, 8.7 to 12.0; HR 0.79, 0.65 to 0.95; P=0.012 — a relative measure). Drug-related grade 3-or-higher toxicity was higher with pemetrexed (70 patients, 16%, vs 9, 4%), specifically fatigue (5% vs 1%) and neutropenia (3% vs 0); discontinuations for drug-related toxicity were 5% vs 1%. No pemetrexed-related deaths occurred. Fewer pemetrexed patients received post-discontinuation systemic therapy (51% vs 67%).
cards.watchOut: A maintenance trial in non-progressors only: the survival contrast applies to patients whose disease was already controlled by induction, not to all patients starting first-line therapy. Funded by Eli Lilly, the manufacturer, as stated in the record.
cards.source: Ciuleanu et al. Maintenance pemetrexed plus best supportive care versus placebo plus best supportive care for non-small-cell lung cancer: a randomised, double-blind, phase 3 study. Lancet (London, England). 2009. PMID: 19767093. Registry ID: NCT00102804. cards.headline: PARAMOUNT final OS report (Paz-Ares 2013): pemetrexed continuation maintenance after pemetrexed–cisplatin induction prolonged survival (median 13.9 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.78 — a 22% relative reduction in the risk of death)
cards.summary: PARAMOUNT final OS report (Paz-Ares 2013): pemetrexed continuation maintenance after pemetrexed–cisplatin induction prolonged survival (median 13.9 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.78 — a 22% relative reduction in the risk of death)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial final overall-survival report (PARAMOUNT), pemetrexed continuation maintenance vs placebo after pemetrexed–cisplatin induction, nonsquamous NSCLC — maintenance limb
cards.people: 939 patients with advanced nonsquamous NSCLC received four cycles of pemetrexed–cisplatin induction; the 539 who had not progressed and had ECOG performance status 0–1 were randomised 2:1 to maintenance pemetrexed 500 mg/m² day 1 of 21-day cycles (n=359) or placebo (n=180). Mean maintenance cycles delivered: 7.9 on pemetrexed, 5.0 on placebo.
cards.result: After 397 deaths and median follow-up of 24.3 months for patients still alive, pemetrexed continuation maintenance gave a statistically significant 22% relative reduction in the risk of death (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.96; P=0.0195), with median overall survival 13.9 months versus 11.0 months on placebo — an absolute median difference of 2.9 months. Benefit was consistent across subgroups, including induction complete/partial responders (OS HR 0.81) and patients with stable disease (HR 0.76). Post-discontinuation therapy use was similar (64% vs 72%). Drug-related grade 3–4 anaemia, fatigue and neutropenia were significantly more frequent on pemetrexed; no new safety findings emerged.
cards.watchOut: PARAMOUNT is restricted to nonsquamous histology and to induction non-progressors, and its induction regimen itself contained pemetrexed — it tests continuing the same drug, not switching to it. This is the trial's final OS report; its earlier progression report is not separately carded.
cards.source: Paz-Ares et al. PARAMOUNT: Final overall survival results of the phase III study of maintenance pemetrexed versus placebo immediately after induction treatment with pemetrexed plus cisplatin for advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer. cards.headline: Synthesis: two distinct questions, labelled and never pooled — first-line, cisplatin–pemetrexed is non-inferior overall with a histology interaction that makes pemetrexed the choice in nonsquamous disease and the wrong choice in squamous disease (JMDB); as maintenance after platinum induction in non-progressors, pemetrexed prolongs survival in two randomised trials (JMEN HR 0.79; PARAMOUNT HR 0.78, both relative measures, with absolute median gains of 2.8 and 2.9 months)
cards.summary: Synthesis: two distinct questions, labelled and never pooled — first-line, cisplatin–pemetrexed is non-inferior overall with a histology interaction that makes pemetrexed the choice in nonsquamous disease and the wrong choice in squamous disease (JMDB); as maintenance after platinum induction in non-progressors, pemetrexed prolongs survival in two randomised trials (JMEN HR 0.79; PARAMOUNT HR 0.78, both relative measures, with absolute median gains of 2.8 and 2.9 months)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: JMDB (1,725 randomised, first-line), JMEN (663 randomised, maintenance) and PARAMOUNT (539 randomised, continuation maintenance).
cards.result: The first-line and maintenance limbs answer different questions and are not combined. JMDB's overall non-inferiority (HR 0.94) conceals opposite histology effects — adenocarcinoma 12.6 vs 10.9 months favouring pemetrexed, squamous 10.8 vs 9.4 months favouring gemcitabine — which is why histology became a selection test. Both maintenance trials enrolled only patients who had not progressed on induction, and both showed an overall-survival benefit of similar relative size with more grade 3–4 fatigue, neutropenia and anaemia on pemetrexed. No trial here tests pemetrexed maintenance in squamous disease.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
