cards.headline: Z9001 long-term pathology and molecular analysis (Corless 2014): recurrence-free survival remained superior on imatinib (hazard ratio 0.6, relative), the advantage concentrated in KIT exon 11 deletion tumours — and adjuvant imatinib did not seem to alter overall survival
cards.summary: Z9001 long-term pathology and molecular analysis (Corless 2014): recurrence-free survival remained superior on imatinib (hazard ratio 0.6, relative), the advantage concentrated in KIT exon 11 deletion tumours — and adjuvant imatinib did not seem to alter overall survival
cards.type: Long-term pathology/molecular report of the Z9001 trial (same programme as the card above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 645 tumour specimens from Z9001 patients were available for mitotic-rate or mutation analysis (328 patients assigned to placebo and 317 to imatinib in this analysis population); median follow-up was 74 months. This is a long-term report OF the Z9001 trial carded above, not a separate trial.
cards.result: Recurrence-free survival remained superior in the imatinib arm (hazard ratio 0.6, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.75 — a relative measure). On the placebo arm, large tumour size, small-bowel location and high mitotic rate predicted lower recurrence-free survival, while tumour genotype was not significantly associated with outcome. Comparing the arms, imatinib was associated with higher recurrence-free survival in patients with a KIT exon 11 deletion of any type, but not in KIT exon 11 insertion or point mutation, KIT exon 9 mutation, PDGFRA mutation or wild-type tumours — although some of these groups were small. Adjuvant imatinib did not seem to alter overall survival.
cards.watchOut: The exon-11-deletion concentration of benefit is a subgroup finding in a trial not powered for genotype slices, and several genotype groups were small; the null overall-survival finding belongs beside the recurrence-free-survival headline, not underneath it.
cards.source: Corless CL et al. Pathologic and molecular features correlate with long-term outcome after adjuvant therapy of resected primary GI stromal tumor: the ACOSOG Z9001 trial. cards.headline: Recurrence-risk scores (Joensuu 2014): scores built in SSGXVIII and validated in the Z9001 imatinib arm — high mitotic count and non-gastric site mark the highest risk (5-year recurrence-free survival 8.4% in the highest stratum)
cards.summary: Recurrence-risk scores (Joensuu 2014): scores built in SSGXVIII and validated in the Z9001 imatinib arm — high mitotic count and non-gastric site mark the highest risk (5-year recurrence-free survival 8.4% in the highest stratum)
cards.type: Risk-stratification analysis: derivation in SSGXVIII, validation in the Z9001 imatinib arm (a report using the Z9001 programme's data)
cards.people: Risk scores were developed in the Scandinavian Sarcoma Group XVIII (SSGXVIII) trial database — 358 patients with high-risk GIST randomised to adjuvant imatinib 400 mg/day for 12 or 36 months — and validated in the imatinib arm of Z9001 (359 patients assigned to imatinib for 12 months). This is a risk-analysis report using Z9001 data, not a new trial of adjuvant imatinib versus none.
cards.result: Five factors — high tumour mitotic count, non-gastric location, large size, tumour rupture, and adjuvant imatinib for 12 months — were independently associated with unfavourable recurrence-free survival in SSGXVIII; the five-factor score had a concordance index of 78.9% for recurrence. A simpler two-factor score (mitotic count and tumour site) separated groups with 5-year recurrence-free survival of 76.7%, 47.5% and 8.4%. Both scores were strongly associated with recurrence-free survival in the Z9001 validation cohort (P<.001 for each comparison).
cards.watchOut: The derivation cohort is the SSGXVIII duration trial (the 3-years-versus-1-year question, homed at live #1926) — this card uses its data only for recurrence-risk stratification in imatinib-treated patients and does not re-card the duration comparison.
cards.source: Joensuu H et al. Risk factors for gastrointestinal stromal tumor recurrence in patients treated with adjuvant imatinib. Cancer. 2014. PMID: 24737415. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial (Z9001, 713 randomised), three reports — one year of adjuvant imatinib clearly delays recurrence after GIST resection (1-year recurrence-free survival 98% versus 83%), with no overall-survival benefit shown and benefit concentrated in KIT exon 11 deletion tumours
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial (Z9001, 713 randomised), three reports — one year of adjuvant imatinib clearly delays recurrence after GIST resection (1-year recurrence-free survival 98% versus 83%), with no overall-survival benefit shown and benefit concentrated in KIT exon 11 deletion tumours
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: the Z9001 trial and its long-term and risk-score reports.
cards.result: The founding question — any adjuvant imatinib versus none — rests on this single trial. Its primary report found 1-year recurrence-free survival of 98% versus 83% (hazard ratio 0.35, relative); at 74 months' median follow-up the recurrence-free-survival advantage persisted (hazard ratio 0.6, relative) but adjuvant imatinib did not seem to alter overall survival, in a trial where placebo patients crossed to imatinib at recurrence. Recurrence risk after adjuvant imatinib is dominated by mitotic count and non-gastric site (5-year recurrence-free survival 8.4% in the highest-risk stratum of the derivation cohort). The separate question of how LONG adjuvant imatinib should run (3 years versus 1 year, SSGXVIII) is homed at live #1926 and is not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; the single-trial base and the early stopping of Z9001 are the shelf's main limits, and this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: MPT in elderly myeloma: survival 51.6 versus 33.2 months (age 65–75) and 44.0 versus 29.1 months (over 75); pooled hazard ratio 0.83 — neuropathy is the price
shelves.question: In previously untreated elderly patients with multiple myeloma, does adding thalidomide to melphalan–prednisone (MPT) prolong overall survival versus melphalan–prednisone (MP) alone?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antineoplastic Agents, Alkylating/administration & dosage · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Female · Humans · Immunosuppressive Agents/administration & dosage · Male · Melphalan/administration & dosage · Multiple Myeloma/drug therapy,mortality,therapy · Prednisone/administration & dosage · Stem Cell Transplantation · Survival Rate · Thalidomide/administration & dosage
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), priced in neuropathy. Two randomised trials split by age band agree: in patients aged 65–75 (IFM 99-06, 447 randomised) MPT gave median overall survival of 51.6 versus 33.2 months on MP (hazard ratio 0.59, relative), and in patients over 75 (IFM 01/01, 229 randomised, placebo-controlled) 44.0 versus 29.1 months. The individual-patient-data meta-analysis of all six randomised MPT trials (1,685 patients, carded as a labelled companion) found a more modest pooled hazard ratio of 0.83 (relative) and a 6.6-month median gain (39.3 versus 32.7 months) — the pooled figure is the conservative summary. Grade 2–4 peripheral neuropathy (20% versus 5% in the over-75 trial) and grade 3/4 neutropenia (23% versus 9%) are the pricing harms, and the reason the regimen was later displaced.

cards.headline: IFM 99-06 (Facon 2007): melphalan–prednisone plus thalidomide prolonged median overall survival to 51.6 months versus 33.2 months on melphalan–prednisone alone in patients aged 65–75 (hazard ratio 0.59, relative)
cards.summary: IFM 99-06 (Facon 2007): melphalan–prednisone plus thalidomide prolonged median overall survival to 51.6 months versus 33.2 months on melphalan–prednisone alone in patients aged 65–75 (hazard ratio 0.59, relative)
cards.type: Randomised trial (IFM 99-06), three arms — the MPT-versus-MP comparison is the carded slice
cards.people: 447 previously untreated patients with multiple myeloma aged 65 to 75 years, randomised to melphalan–prednisone (MP, n=196), melphalan–prednisone plus thalidomide (MPT, n=125), or reduced-intensity autologous stem-cell transplantation with melphalan 100 mg/m² (MEL100, n=126); median follow-up 51.5 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 51.6 months on MPT versus 33.2 months on MP (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.81; P=0.0006 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians) and 38.3 months on MEL100. MPT also beat MEL100 (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.96), while MEL100 did not differ significantly from MP (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.15; P=0.32 — a null comparison).
cards.watchOut: The fetched abstract of this report does not print arm-specific toxicity rates, so none are claimed on this card; the pricing harm of thalidomide is quantified on the IFM 01/01 card below. The MEL100 transplant arm is a separate comparison and is not this shelf's question.
cards.source: Facon T et al. cards.headline: IFM 01/01 (Hulin 2009): in patients older than 75, MPT prolonged median overall survival to 44.0 versus 29.1 months on MP plus placebo — at the price of grade 2–4 peripheral neuropathy in 20% versus 5%
cards.summary: IFM 01/01 (Hulin 2009): in patients older than 75, MPT prolonged median overall survival to 44.0 versus 29.1 months on MP plus placebo — at the price of grade 2–4 peripheral neuropathy in 20% versus 5%
cards.type: Randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (IFM 01/01), age band over 75 — a separate trial from IFM 99-06, carded as its own slice
cards.people: 232 previously untreated patients with newly diagnosed myeloma aged 75 years or older were enrolled and 229 randomised to melphalan–prednisone plus thalidomide 100 mg/day continuously for 72 weeks (n=113) or melphalan–prednisone plus placebo (n=116), in a randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 trial; median follow-up 47.5 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 44.0 months on MPT versus 29.1 months on MP plus placebo (P=.028), and median progression-free survival 24.1 versus 18.5 months (P=.001) — absolute medians as published. Two adverse events were significantly increased on MPT: grade 2 to 4 peripheral neuropathy (20% versus 5%; P<.001) and grade 3 to 4 neutropenia (23% versus 9%; P=.003).
cards.watchOut: Thalidomide here was 100 mg/day for a fixed 72 weeks in the very elderly; neuropathy rates from this dose and duration should not be read across to other thalidomide regimens.
cards.source: Hulin C et al. Efficacy of melphalan and prednisone plus thalidomide in patients older than 75 years with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: IFM 01/01 trial. cards.headline: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of six MPT trials (Fayers 2011) — labelled meta-analytic companion: overall-survival hazard ratio 0.83 (relative), a 6.6-month median gain (39.3 versus 32.7 months)
cards.summary: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of six MPT trials (Fayers 2011) — labelled meta-analytic companion: overall-survival hazard ratio 0.83 (relative), a 6.6-month median gain (39.3 versus 32.7 months)
cards.type: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of six randomised MPT trials — labelled meta-analytic companion to the trials above
cards.people: 1,685 individual patients from six randomised trials launched in or after 2000 comparing melphalan–prednisone alone with melphalan–prednisone plus thalidomide in previously untreated elderly myeloma, including the two IFM trials carded above — this is a pooled companion to those trials, not a seventh trial.
cards.result: Adding thalidomide to MP improved overall survival (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.73 to 0.94; P=.004 — a relative measure), representing a median overall-survival gain of 6.6 months, from 32.7 months (MP) to 39.3 months (MPT). Progression-free survival also improved (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.76 — relative), and 1-year response rates (partial response or better) were 59% on MPT versus 37% on MP. The individual trials' overall-survival effects varied, and there was no evidence the effect differed by baseline prognostic factors.
cards.watchOut: The pooled hazard ratio (0.83) is smaller than IFM 99-06's (0.59): the trials differed in patients and thalidomide regimens and their survival effects varied, so the pooled figure — not the most favourable single trial — is the conservative summary.
cards.source: Fayers PM et al. Thalidomide for previously untreated elderly patients with multiple myeloma: meta-analysis of 1685 individual patient data from 6 randomized clinical trials. Blood. 2011. PMID: 21670471. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: adding thalidomide to melphalan–prednisone prolongs survival in elderly newly diagnosed myeloma in both age bands (65–75 and over 75) and in the six-trial pooled analysis — with peripheral neuropathy as the pricing harm
cards.summary: Synthesis: adding thalidomide to melphalan–prednisone prolongs survival in elderly newly diagnosed myeloma in both age bands (65–75 and over 75) and in the six-trial pooled analysis — with peripheral neuropathy as the pricing harm
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: IFM 99-06 (n=447, aged 65–75), IFM 01/01 (n=229 randomised, aged over 75), and the individual-patient-data meta-analysis of six trials (n=1,685).
cards.result: Median overall survival favoured MPT in both trials — 51.6 versus 33.2 months (IFM 99-06; hazard ratio 0.59, relative) and 44.0 versus 29.1 months (IFM 01/01) — and the pooled analysis of all six randomised trials found a more modest hazard ratio of 0.83 (relative) with a 6.6-month median gain. The harm that prices the benefit is thalidomide neuropathy (grade 2–4 in 20% versus 5% in the over-75 trial) with more grade 3/4 neutropenia (23% versus 9%). This was the pre-lenalidomide standard for transplant-ineligible elderly myeloma; later regimens are cross-points, not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Chemotherapy-era APL (European APL Group): ATRA plus chemotherapy — 4-year survival 76% versus 49% without ATRA; maintenance cut 10-year relapse to 13.4%; omitting cytarabine raised relapse
shelves.question: In patients with newly diagnosed acute promyelocytic leukaemia, does adding all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) to anthracycline-based chemotherapy improve event-free and overall survival versus chemotherapy alone (APL91) — and, once ATRA is standard, do early chemotherapy and maintenance therapy further reduce relapse (APL93), and does omitting cytarabine from ATRA–daunorubicin increase relapse in standard-risk disease (APL2000)?
shelves.mesh: Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Humans · Leukemia, Promyelocytic, Acute/drug therapy · Leukocyte Count · Prognosis · Tretinoin/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), as three labelled successive slices of the chemotherapy era, never pooled. APL91 (n=101, printed on the face) found ATRA followed by daunorubicin–cytarabine chemotherapy far superior to the same chemotherapy alone (4-year event-free survival 63% versus 17%; survival 76% versus 49%). APL93 (n=576, 10-year follow-up) showed maintenance therapy cut 10-year relapse from 43.2% to 13.4%, while deaths in complete remission rose steeply with age (5.7% under 55 to 21.7% over 65) — the historical argument for less myelosuppressive treatment. APL2000 showed that in standard-risk disease, omitting cytarabine from ATRA–daunorubicin increased 7-year relapse (28.6% versus 12.9%), a regimen-dependent finding. The ATRA plus arsenic trioxide (chemotherapy-free) question is homed at pack #7496 and is cross-pointed only, never re-carded here.

cards.headline: APL91 long-term follow-up (Fenaux 2000): ATRA followed by daunorubicin–cytarabine chemotherapy beat the same chemotherapy alone — 4-year event-free survival 63% versus 17% and survival 76% versus 49% (n=101, printed on the face)
cards.summary: APL91 long-term follow-up (Fenaux 2000): ATRA followed by daunorubicin–cytarabine chemotherapy beat the same chemotherapy alone — 4-year event-free survival 63% versus 17% and survival 76% versus 49% (n=101, printed on the face)
cards.type: Randomised trial (APL91) — long-term follow-up report; the add-ATRA slice of this shelf
cards.people: 101 patients with newly diagnosed acute promyelocytic leukaemia randomised between all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) followed by three courses of daunorubicin–AraC (cytarabine) chemotherapy and the same chemotherapy alone (European APL Group, APL91); results reanalysed 73 months after entry closed. The trial's small size — 101 patients — is printed here because it is small for a founding trial.
cards.result: Kaplan–Meier estimates at 4 years: event-free survival 63% in the ATRA group versus 17% in the chemotherapy group, relapse 31% versus 78%, and survival 76% versus 49% (absolute rates as published; the report also prints relative risks of 2.95, 3.68 and 2.7 for these contrasts). In the chemotherapy group, 23 of 25 patients who relapsed achieved a second complete remission with ATRA.
cards.watchOut: A single small founding trial (n=101) carries the ATRA-versus-no-ATRA contrast; its effect is very large, but the shelf does not present n=101 as if it were a large modern trial.
cards.source: Fenaux P et al. Long-term follow-up confirms the benefit of all-trans retinoic acid in acute promyelocytic leukemia. European APL group. Leukemia. 2000. PMID: 10942231. cards.headline: APL93 very-long-term report (Adès 2010): with ATRA plus chemotherapy standard, maintenance therapy cut 10-year relapse from 43.2% (none) to 13.4% (combined maintenance); deaths in complete remission rose steeply with age (5.7% under 55 to 21.7% over 65)
cards.summary: APL93 very-long-term report (Adès 2010): with ATRA plus chemotherapy standard, maintenance therapy cut 10-year relapse from 43.2% (none) to 13.4% (combined maintenance); deaths in complete remission rose steeply with age (5.7% under 55 to 21.7% over 65)
cards.type: Randomised trial programme report (APL93) — the maintenance and early-chemotherapy slices, a successive question to APL91, not a replicate
cards.people: 576 patients with newly diagnosed acute promyelocytic leukaemia in the European APL Group's APL93 trial, treated with ATRA and anthracycline-based chemotherapy, with randomised questions on the timing of chemotherapy addition and on maintenance therapy; median follow-up 10 years.
cards.result: Ten-year survival was 77%. Maintenance significantly reduced the 10-year cumulative incidence of relapse: 43.2% with no maintenance, 33% with intermittent ATRA alone, 23.4% with continuous 6-mercaptopurine plus methotrexate alone, and 13.4% with both (P<.001), particularly benefiting patients with a white-cell count above 5 × 10⁹/L. Early addition of chemotherapy to ATRA significantly improved 10-year event-free survival without a significant effect on overall survival. The 10-year cumulative incidence of deaths in complete remission — mainly from myelosuppression — was 5.7% in patients younger than 55, 15.4% at 55 to 65, and 21.7% over 65.
cards.watchOut: The age gradient in deaths in complete remission is the historical argument for less myelosuppressive (arsenic-era) consolidation; it is a within-era observation, not a comparison with ATRA–arsenic therapy, which is homed elsewhere (see Synthesis).
cards.source: Adès L et al. Very long-term outcome of acute promyelocytic leukemia after treatment with all-trans retinoic acid and chemotherapy: the European APL Group experience. Blood. 2010. PMID: 20018913. Registry ID: NCT00599937. cards.headline: APL2000 long-term follow-up (Adès 2013): in standard-risk APL, omitting cytarabine from ATRA–daunorubicin increased 7-year relapse (28.6% versus 12.9%) — the cytarabine question is regimen-dependent
cards.summary: APL2000 long-term follow-up (Adès 2013): in standard-risk APL, omitting cytarabine from ATRA–daunorubicin increased 7-year relapse (28.6% versus 12.9%) — the cytarabine question is regimen-dependent
cards.type: Randomised trial (APL2000) — long-term follow-up of the cytarabine slice in standard-risk APL; a successive question, not pooled with APL91/APL93
cards.people: Patients with standard-risk acute promyelocytic leukaemia (baseline white-cell count below 10,000/mm³) in the European APL Group's APL2000 trial, randomised between ATRA with daunorubicin plus cytarabine (AraC) and ATRA with daunorubicin without AraC; all patients subsequently received combined maintenance. The fetched record does not print the randomised N for this standard-risk limb, so none is claimed here. The trial was terminated prematurely because of significantly more relapses in the no-AraC group; median follow-up in this report was 103 months.
cards.result: With long-term follow-up, the 7-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 28.6% in the no-AraC group versus 12.9% in the AraC group (P=.0065) — absolute rates as published. The authors conclude that, at least when the anthracycline used is daunorubicin, avoiding cytarabine may increase relapse risk, suggesting the need for cytarabine is regimen-dependent.
cards.watchOut: This result is specific to standard-risk patients on a daunorubicin backbone and the trial stopped early for the relapse difference; it does not settle cytarabine's role with other anthracyclines or in high-risk disease.
cards.source: Adès L et al. Long-term follow-up of European APL 2000 trial, evaluating the role of cytarabine combined with ATRA and Daunorubicin in the treatment of nonelderly APL patients. American journal of hematology. 2013. PMID: 23564205. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: three European APL Group trials answering three successive chemotherapy-era questions — add ATRA (large benefit), maintain after remission (relapse cut by two-thirds), and keep cytarabine with daunorubicin in standard-risk disease (relapse 12.9% versus 28.6%)
cards.summary: Synthesis: three European APL Group trials answering three successive chemotherapy-era questions — add ATRA (large benefit), maintain after remission (relapse cut by two-thirds), and keep cytarabine with daunorubicin in standard-risk disease (relapse 12.9% versus 28.6%)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: APL91 (n=101), APL93 (n=576) and APL2000 (standard-risk limb; N not printed in the fetched record).
cards.result: These are labelled successive slices of one era, never pooled. APL91 established ATRA plus anthracycline–cytarabine chemotherapy over chemotherapy alone (4-year survival 76% versus 49%). APL93, once ATRA was standard, showed maintenance therapy reduced 10-year relapse from 43.2% to 13.4% and that deaths in complete remission rose from 5.7% under age 55 to 21.7% over 65 — the toxicity argument that later motivated the arsenic era. APL2000 showed omitting cytarabine from ATRA–daunorubicin in standard-risk disease increased 7-year relapse (28.6% versus 12.9%). The chemotherapy-free ATRA plus arsenic trioxide question (APL0406/AML17) is a different, later slice, homed at pack #7496 — cross-pointed here and never re-carded on this shelf.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Isatuximab combinations in relapsed/refractory myeloma: PFS improved in both programmes (11.5 vs 6.5 and 35.7 vs 19.2 months); survival borderline in ICARIA-MM, null in IKEMA
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, does adding the anti-CD38 antibody isatuximab to pomalidomide–dexamethasone (ICARIA-MM, after ≥2 prior lines including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor) or to carfilzomib–dexamethasone (IKEMA, after 1–3 prior lines) improve progression-free and overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal/administration & dosage · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Asia · Dexamethasone/administration & dosage · Europe · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Multiple Myeloma/drug therapy · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/drug therapy · North America · Progression-Free Survival · Thalidomide/administration & dosage/analogs & derivatives · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, for progression-free survival) — the honest headline is a PFS drug. Both phase 3 programmes improved progression-free survival clearly: ICARIA-MM (isatuximab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone, after ≥2 prior lines) 11.5 vs 6.5 months (hazard ratio 0.596, relative) and IKEMA (isatuximab–carfilzomib–dexamethasone, after 1–3 prior lines) 35.7 vs 19.2 months on updated analysis (hazard ratio 0.58, relative), with deeper responses in IKEMA (MRD negativity 33.5% vs 15.4%). Overall survival is weaker: ICARIA-MM's final analysis is borderline (24.6 vs 17.7 months; hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.59–1.02, interval crossing 1, with daratumumab crossover in the control arm) and IKEMA's is null (hazard ratio 0.855, 95% CI 0.608–1.202). Two trials, six reports — labelled slices by backbone, never pooled.

cards.headline: ICARIA-MM primary (Attal 2019): adding isatuximab to pomalidomide–dexamethasone — median progression-free survival 11.5 vs 6.5 months, hazard ratio 0.596 (relative)
cards.summary: ICARIA-MM primary (Attal 2019): adding isatuximab to pomalidomide–dexamethasone — median progression-free survival 11.5 vs 6.5 months, hazard ratio 0.596 (relative)
cards.type: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial (ICARIA-MM), isatuximab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone vs pomalidomide–dexamethasone — primary PFS report
cards.people: 307 patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma at 102 hospitals in 24 countries, who had received at least two prior lines including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor (anti-CD38-refractory patients excluded); isatuximab 10 mg/kg plus pomalidomide–dexamethasone (154) versus pomalidomide–dexamethasone (153), open-label phase 3. Median follow-up 11.6 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 11.5 months (95% CI 8.9–13.9) with isatuximab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone versus 6.5 months (95% CI 4.5–8.3) with pomalidomide–dexamethasone — hazard ratio 0.596 (95% CI 0.44–0.81), p=0.001, a relative measure beside its absolute medians. Frequent adverse events on the isatuximab arm included infusion reactions (38% vs 0%), upper respiratory tract infections (28% vs 17%) and diarrhoea (26% vs 20%); adverse events with a fatal outcome occurred in 8% versus 9%.
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial; the primary result is a progression-free-survival result, not a survival result — overall survival is carded separately below and is borderline. This is the pomalidomide backbone after at least two prior lines; the carfilzomib backbone (IKEMA) is a different clinical moment and is never pooled with it.
cards.source: Attal M et al. Isatuximab plus pomalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone versus pomalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone in patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (ICARIA-MM): a randomised, multicentre, open-label, phase 3 study. Lancet. 2019. PMID: 31735560. Registry ID: NCT02990338. cards.headline: ICARIA-MM updated overall-survival analysis (Richardson 2022): median overall survival 24.6 vs 17.7 months, hazard ratio 0.76 (0.57–1.01) — one-sided p=0.028, which did NOT cross the prespecified stopping boundary
cards.summary: ICARIA-MM updated overall-survival analysis (Richardson 2022): median overall survival 24.6 vs 17.7 months, hazard ratio 0.76 (0.57–1.01) — one-sided p=0.028, which did NOT cross the prespecified stopping boundary
cards.type: Prespecified updated overall-survival analysis of ICARIA-MM (same trial as the primary report above)
cards.people: The same 307 ICARIA-MM patients (154 isatuximab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone, 153 pomalidomide–dexamethasone), in a prespecified second interim overall-survival analysis 24 months after the primary analysis; median follow-up 35.3 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 24.6 months (95% CI 20.3–31.3) versus 17.7 months (95% CI 14.4–26.2) — hazard ratio 0.76 (95% CI 0.57–1.01), a relative measure beside its absolute medians; the one-sided log-rank p=0.028 did not cross the prespecified stopping boundary of 0.0181. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia occurred in 50% versus 35%, pneumonia in 23% versus 21%; serious treatment-emergent adverse events in 73% versus 60%.
cards.watchOut: A prespecified analysis that formally missed its own stopping boundary must be printed as such — 'p=0.028' without the boundary would overstate it. Same trial as the card above, not independent evidence.
cards.source: Richardson PG et al. cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of ICARIA-MM (same trial as the reports above)
cards.people: The same 307 ICARIA-MM patients, at the final overall-survival analysis after 220 deaths; median follow-up 52.4 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 24.6 months (95% CI 20.3–31.3) with isatuximab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone versus 17.7 months (95% CI 14.4–26.2) with pomalidomide–dexamethasone — hazard ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.59–1.02), a relative measure beside its absolute medians, with a one-sided P=0.0319; the confidence interval crosses 1. cards.headline: IKEMA primary (Moreau 2021): adding isatuximab to carfilzomib–dexamethasone — progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.53 (relative); median not reached vs 19.15 months
cards.summary: IKEMA primary (Moreau 2021): adding isatuximab to carfilzomib–dexamethasone — progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.53 (relative); median not reached vs 19.15 months
cards.type: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial (IKEMA), isatuximab–carfilzomib–dexamethasone vs carfilzomib–dexamethasone — primary PFS report
cards.people: 302 patients with relapsed multiple myeloma at 69 centres in 16 countries, after one to three prior lines (median two); isatuximab 10 mg/kg plus carfilzomib–dexamethasone (179) versus carfilzomib–dexamethasone (123), randomised 3:2, open-label phase 3.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was not reached in the isatuximab group versus 19.15 months (95% CI 15.77–not reached) in the control group — hazard ratio 0.53 (99% CI 0.32–0.89), one-sided p=0.0007, a relative measure. Grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 77% versus 67%, serious events in 59% versus 57%, discontinuation for adverse events in 8% versus 14%, and fatal treatment-emergent events in 3% in both groups.
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial, and at this primary analysis the isatuximab median was not reached — the size of the progression-free gain only became estimable in the updated analysis carded below. This is the carfilzomib backbone after 1–3 prior lines, a different clinical moment from ICARIA-MM; the two trials are never pooled.

cards.type: Updated analysis of IKEMA (same trial as the primary report above) — PFS, response depth and MRD
cards.people: The same 302 IKEMA patients (179 isatuximab–carfilzomib–dexamethasone, 123 carfilzomib–dexamethasone), in a prespecified follow-up analysis of progression-free survival, complete response, minimal residual disease and safety.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 35.7 months (95% CI 25.8–44.0) versus 19.2 months (95% CI 15.8–25.0) — hazard ratio 0.58 (95.4% CI 0.42–0.79), a relative measure beside its absolute medians. cards.watchOut: Same trial as the card above, not independent evidence. Depth-of-response measures (MRD negativity, complete response) are not survival; IKEMA's overall-survival analysis is carded below and is null.

cards.headline: IKEMA overall-survival analysis (Yong 2024): median overall survival not reached vs 50.6 months, hazard ratio 0.855 (0.608–1.202) — no survival difference detected
cards.summary: IKEMA overall-survival analysis (Yong 2024): median overall survival not reached vs 50.6 months, hazard ratio 0.855 (0.608–1.202) — no survival difference detected
cards.type: Overall-survival analysis of IKEMA (same trial as the reports above)
cards.people: The same 302 IKEMA patients (179 isatuximab–carfilzomib–dexamethasone, 123 carfilzomib–dexamethasone), in the overall-survival analysis planned 3 years after the primary progression-free analysis; median follow-up 56.61 months; 79 deaths (44%) in the isatuximab group and 59 (48%) in the control group.
cards.result: Median overall survival was not reached (95% CI 52.17–not reached) in the isatuximab group versus 50.60 months (95% CI 38.93–not reached) in the control group — hazard ratio 0.855 (95% CI 0.608–1.202), nominal one-sided p=0.18, a relative measure; survival at 48 months was 59.7% versus 52.2%. Time to next treatment (hazard ratio 0.583, 95% CI 0.429–0.792) and second progression-free survival (0.663, 95% CI 0.491–0.895) favoured isatuximab. Infusion reactions occurred in 46% versus 3% and upper respiratory tract infections in 40% versus 28%; treatment-related fatal adverse events in 7% versus 5%.
cards.watchOut: The honest headline for IKEMA is a progression-free-survival drug: at nearly 5 years of follow-up no overall-survival difference could be detected, and the reported p values are explicitly non-inferential because of hierarchical testing. Same trial as the two cards above.

cards.headline: Synthesis: isatuximab combinations are progression-free-survival drugs — both phase 3 programmes improved PFS clearly; ICARIA-MM's survival advantage is borderline (final HR 0.78, CI crossing 1) and IKEMA's overall survival is null (HR 0.855)
cards.summary: Synthesis: isatuximab combinations are progression-free-survival drugs — both phase 3 programmes improved PFS clearly; ICARIA-MM's survival advantage is borderline (final HR 0.78, CI crossing 1) and IKEMA's overall survival is null (HR 0.855)
cards.people: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
cards.result: Synthesis: two trials, six reports, labelled slices, never pooled. ICARIA-MM (pomalidomide backbone, after ≥2 prior lines, n=307): progression-free survival 11.5 vs 6.5 months (hazard ratio 0.596, relative); final overall survival 24.6 vs 17.7 months with hazard ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.59–1.02) — borderline, its interval crossing 1, with daratumumab crossover in the control arm. IKEMA (carfilzomib backbone, after 1–3 prior lines, n=302): updated progression-free survival 35.7 vs 19.2 months (hazard ratio 0.58, relative) with deeper responses (MRD negativity 33.5% vs 15.4%), but overall survival not different (hazard ratio 0.855, 95% CI 0.608–1.202). The subcutaneous-formulation question (IRAKLIA) is a delivery question and is not carded here.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Pembrolizumab in relapsed/refractory Hodgkin lymphoma: responses 69–71% (single-arm KEYNOTE-087) and PFS 13.2 vs 8.3 months vs brentuximab (KEYNOTE-204); survival not analysed
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma, does pembrolizumab produce durable responses after autologous transplant and/or brentuximab vedotin failure (KEYNOTE-087, single-arm) — and does it beat brentuximab vedotin head-to-head on progression-free survival (KEYNOTE-204)?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/adverse effects · Antineoplastic Agents/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Cohort Studies · Female · Hodgkin Disease/drug therapy · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Recurrence · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, for response and progression-free survival; no overall-survival comparison) — KEYNOTE-087 is single-arm and is stamped as such: pembrolizumab gave response rates of 69.0% (complete response 22.4%) after autologous transplant and/or brentuximab failure, and 71.4% at 5 years with a median duration of response of 16.6 months. The randomised evidence is KEYNOTE-204, where pembrolizumab beat brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival (13.2 vs 8.3 months; hazard ratio 0.65 — a relative measure beside its absolute medians), with quality of life improving on pembrolizumab and worsening on brentuximab; overall survival was not analysed at the reported interim analysis, and no survival claim is made. Cross-point: the nivolumab programme in the same setting is shelf #7608, never pooled.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-087 primary (Chen 2017, single-arm): pembrolizumab response rate 69.0%, complete response 22.4% after transplant and/or brentuximab failure — no internal comparator
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-087 primary (Chen 2017, single-arm): pembrolizumab response rate 69.0%, complete response 22.4% after transplant and/or brentuximab failure — no internal comparator
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 study (KEYNOTE-087), pembrolizumab in relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma — primary report
cards.people: 210 patients with relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma in three cohorts: progression after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) and subsequent brentuximab vedotin (BV) (69); salvage chemotherapy and BV without ASCT because of chemoresistant disease (81); and ASCT without BV after transplantation (60). Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks; median 13 treatment cycles at analysis.
cards.result: Overall response rate by central review was 69.0% (95% CI 62.3–75.2%) and the complete response rate 22.4% (95% CI 16.9–28.6%). Response rates by cohort were 73.9% (post-ASCT + BV), 64.2% (salvage chemotherapy + BV, no ASCT) and 70.0% (post-ASCT, no BV). Thirty-one patients had a response lasting at least 6 months. The safety profile was largely consistent with previous pembrolizumab studies.
cards.watchOut: SINGLE-ARM evidence, stamped as such: these response rates have no internal comparator, so no comparative claim can be drawn from this card. The randomised evidence on this shelf is KEYNOTE-204, carded below.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-087 five-year follow-up (Armand 2023, single-arm): response rate 71.4%, complete response 27.6%; median duration of response 16.6 months; a quarter of responders maintained response ≥4 years
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-087 five-year follow-up (Armand 2023, single-arm): response rate 71.4%, complete response 27.6%; median duration of response 16.6 months; a quarter of responders maintained response ≥4 years
cards.type: Five-year follow-up of KEYNOTE-087 (same single-arm programme as the primary report above)
cards.people: The same 210 KEYNOTE-087 patients, followed for a median of 63.7 months; patients received pembrolizumab for up to 2 years, and those who discontinued in complete response and later progressed were eligible for a second course (20 received one; 19 evaluable).
cards.result: Overall response rate was 71.4% (95% CI 64.8–77.4), with complete response 27.6% and partial response 43.8%. Median duration of response was 16.6 months, median progression-free survival 13.7 months, and median overall survival was not reached. A quarter of responders — including half of complete responders — maintained a response for at least 4 years. Second-course pembrolizumab gave an overall response rate of 73.7% (95% CI 48.8–90.8) in 19 evaluable patients, with median duration of response 15.2 months. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 12.9% and there were no treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Still single-arm: the 5-year overall-survival description (median not reached) is a within-cohort description, not a treatment effect. Same programme as the card above, not independent evidence. Note the record for this report carries no registry ID — printed as 'none in the record' in its source line.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-204 primary (Kuruvilla 2021, randomised): pembrolizumab beat brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival — 13.2 vs 8.3 months, hazard ratio 0.65 (relative); overall survival was not analysed at this interim analysis
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-204 primary (Kuruvilla 2021, randomised): pembrolizumab beat brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival — 13.2 vs 8.3 months, hazard ratio 0.65 (relative); overall survival was not analysed at this interim analysis
cards.type: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial (KEYNOTE-204), pembrolizumab vs brentuximab vedotin — interim PFS report
cards.people: 304 patients with relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma at 78 centres in 20 countries, ineligible for or relapsed after autologous HSCT; pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks (151) versus brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg every 3 weeks (153), open-label phase 3. Median time from randomisation to data cutoff 25.7 months.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 13.2 months (95% CI 10.9–19.4) on pembrolizumab versus 8.3 months (95% CI 5.7–8.8) on brentuximab vedotin — hazard ratio 0.65 (95% CI 0.48–0.88), p=0.0027, a relative measure beside its absolute medians. Overall survival, a dual primary endpoint, was NOT analysed at this interim analysis. Common grade 3–5 treatment-related events included pneumonitis (4% vs 1%), neutropenia (2% vs 7%) and peripheral neuropathy (1% vs 3%); serious treatment-related events occurred in 16% versus 11%, with one treatment-related death (pneumonia) on pembrolizumab.
cards.watchOut: This is the shelf's only randomised comparison, and it is a progression-free-survival result: no overall-survival comparison was analysed at the reported interim, and none may be implied. Open-label design.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-204 quality-of-life analysis (Zinzani 2022): global health status/quality of life improved on pembrolizumab and worsened on brentuximab vedotin by week 24; time to deterioration prolonged (hazard ratio 0.40, relative)
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-204 quality-of-life analysis (Zinzani 2022): global health status/quality of life improved on pembrolizumab and worsened on brentuximab vedotin by week 24; time to deterioration prolonged (hazard ratio 0.40, relative)
cards.type: Quality-of-life / patient-reported-outcome analysis of KEYNOTE-204 (same trial as the primary report above)
cards.people: Patients in KEYNOTE-204 who received at least one dose and completed at least one patient-reported-outcome assessment (pembrolizumab 146, brentuximab vedotin 150); EORTC QLQ-C30 and EQ-5D at baseline, every 6 weeks to week 24, then every 12 weeks. Compliance exceeded 90% at baseline and 80% through week 24.
cards.result: From baseline to week 24 the global health status/quality-of-life score improved on pembrolizumab and worsened on brentuximab vedotin, a least-squares-mean difference of 8.60 points (95% CI 3.89–13.31; P=0.0004). Time to true deterioration (≥10-point decline) for global health status/quality of life was prolonged on pembrolizumab — hazard ratio 0.40 (95% CI 0.22–0.74), P=0.003, a relative measure — as it was for each QLQ-C30 domain except cognitive functioning.
cards.watchOut: A patient-reported-outcome analysis of the same trial as the card above, with p values uncontrolled for multiplicity — supportive of the randomised PFS result, not an independent efficacy claim. Note the record for this report carries no registry ID — printed as 'none in the record' in its source line.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-204 post-hoc analysis by prior lines (Kuruvilla 2025): the progression-free and response advantage held with 1 prior therapy and with ≥2 prior therapies
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-204 post-hoc analysis by prior lines (Kuruvilla 2025): the progression-free and response advantage held with 1 prior therapy and with ≥2 prior therapies
cards.type: Post-hoc analysis of KEYNOTE-204 by prior lines of therapy (same trial as the reports above)
cards.people: The same 304 KEYNOTE-204 patients, analysed post hoc by number of prior therapies: 55 had received 1 prior therapy and 249 had received 2 or more.
cards.result: With 1 prior therapy, median progression-free survival (at the primary analysis, including clinical imaging data after autologous stem cell transplant) was 16.4 months on pembrolizumab versus 8.4 months on brentuximab vedotin, with response rates 66.7% versus 53.6%. With 2 or more prior therapies, median progression-free survival was 12.6 versus 8.2 months and response rates 65.3% versus 54.4%.
cards.watchOut: Post-hoc subgroup analysis of the same trial — hypothesis-level support that the KEYNOTE-204 advantage was not confined to heavily pretreated patients; it adds no new randomised evidence and no survival data.
cards.source: Kuruvilla J et al. Pembrolizumab in relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma: a post hoc analysis of KEYNOTE-204 by prior lines of therapy. Leukemia & Lymphoma. 2025. PMID: 40548833. cards.headline: Synthesis: pembrolizumab produces frequent, sometimes durable responses in relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma (single-arm KEYNOTE-087) and beat brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival in the randomised KEYNOTE-204 — with no overall-survival comparison analysed

cards.people: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
cards.result: Synthesis: two programmes, labelled slices, never pooled. KEYNOTE-087 (single-arm, n=210) gave response rates of 69.0% at the primary report and 71.4% at 5 years, with median duration of response 16.6 months and a quarter of responders maintaining response for at least 4 years — response and durability claims only, with no internal comparator. KEYNOTE-204 (randomised, n=304) showed pembrolizumab superior to brentuximab vedotin on progression-free survival (13.2 vs 8.3 months; hazard ratio 0.65, relative), with better quality-of-life trajectories; overall survival was not analysed at the reported interim analysis. The parallel nivolumab programme (CheckMate 205) is homed on shelf #7608 — cross-point only, never pooled.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Nivolumab in R/R Hodgkin lymphoma after transplant failure (single programme, single-arm — labelled): CheckMate 205 responses 66–71%, median response duration up to 18.2 months
shelves.question: In patients with relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma whose disease has failed autologous haematopoietic cell transplantation, does nivolumab produce durable responses — in brentuximab-naïve patients and in those who received brentuximab before and/or after transplant (CheckMate 205)?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Antibodies, Monoclonal/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents/therapeutic use · Brentuximab Vedotin · Cohort Studies · Combined Modality Therapy/adverse effects · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation/adverse effects · Hodgkin Disease/drug therapy/pathology/therapy · Humans · Immunoconjugates/adverse effects · Male · Middle Aged · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/drug therapy/pathology/therapy · Neoplasm Staging · Nivolumab · Prognosis · Salvage Therapy · Survival Rate · Transplantation, Autologous
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — single programme, labelled: the entire shelf rests on one single-arm phase 2 programme, CheckMate 205 (243 patients after autologous transplant failure, in brentuximab-naïve and brentuximab-exposed cohorts). Objective response rates were 66.3% in the primary cohort B report, 69% at extended follow-up and 71.2% at 5 years, with median durations of response of 16.6–18.2 months and median progression-free survival of 15.1 months at 5 years. Five-year overall survival of 71.4% is a within-cohort description, not a treatment effect. Entirely single-arm evidence — response and durability claims only; no comparative claim is available. Cross-point: pembrolizumab in the same setting is shelf #7607, never pooled.

cards.headline: CheckMate 205 cohort B primary (Younes 2016, single-arm): nivolumab response rate 66.3% after failure of both autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin — no comparator
cards.summary: CheckMate 205 cohort B primary (Younes 2016, single-arm): nivolumab response rate 66.3% after failure of both autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin — no comparator
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 trial (CheckMate 205, cohort B), nivolumab after auto-HSCT and brentuximab failure — primary report
cards.people: 80 adults with recurrent classical Hodgkin lymphoma who had failed autologous stem-cell transplantation and had relapsed after, or failed to respond to, brentuximab vedotin, at 34 centres in Europe and North America; nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Median number of previous therapies was four; median follow-up 8.9 months.
cards.result: An objective response by independent review occurred in 53 of 80 patients (66.3%, 95% CI 54.8–76.4). Common drug-related adverse events were fatigue (25%), infusion-related reaction (20%) and rash (16%); the most common grade 3 or 4 drug-related events were neutropenia (5%) and increased lipase (5%). Three patients died during the study, none judged treatment-related.
cards.watchOut: SINGLE-ARM, single-programme evidence — this entire shelf rests on CheckMate 205 alone, labelled as such. A response rate without a comparator cannot support a comparative claim. This primary report covers cohort B only; the all-cohort reports follow below.

cards.headline: CheckMate 205 extended follow-up, all cohorts (Armand 2018, single-arm): response rate 69% overall (65–73% by cohort); median duration of response 16.6 months
cards.summary: CheckMate 205 extended follow-up, all cohorts (Armand 2018, single-arm): response rate 69% overall (65–73% by cohort); median duration of response 16.6 months
cards.type: Extended follow-up of CheckMate 205, all cohorts (same single-arm programme as the primary report above)
cards.people: 243 patients with relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma after autologous transplant failure, by brentuximab vedotin (BV) history: BV-naïve (cohort A, 63), BV after auto-HCT (cohort B, 80), and BV before and/or after auto-HCT (cohort C, 100); nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Median follow-up 18 months; 40% remained on treatment.
cards.result: The objective response rate was 69% (95% CI 63–75%) overall and 65–73% in each cohort. Median duration of response was 16.6 months (95% CI 13.2–20.3) and median progression-free survival 14.7 months (95% CI 11.3–18.5). Of 70 patients treated past conventional progression, 61% of those evaluable had stable or further reduced target tumour burdens. The most common grade 3 to 4 drug-related events were lipase increases (5%), neutropenia (3%) and ALT increases (3%); 29 deaths occurred, none considered treatment-related.
cards.watchOut: Same single-arm programme as the card above, extended to all three cohorts — not independent evidence. The cohort split (BV-naïve vs BV-exposed) is the clinically useful reading; none of these figures is a treatment effect against any comparator.
cards.source: Armand P et al. Nivolumab for Relapsed/Refractory Classic Hodgkin Lymphoma After Failure of Autologous Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Extended Follow-Up of the Multicohort Single-Arm Phase II CheckMate 205 Trial. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2018. PMID: 29584546. Registry ID: NCT02181738. cards.headline: CheckMate 205 five-year report (Ansell 2023, single-arm): response rate 71.2%, complete response 21.4%; median progression-free survival 15.1 months; 5-year overall survival 71.4% — a within-cohort description, not a treatment effect
cards.summary: CheckMate 205 five-year report (Ansell 2023, single-arm): response rate 71.2%, complete response 21.4%; median progression-free survival 15.1 months; 5-year overall survival 71.4% — a within-cohort description, not a treatment effect
cards.type: Five-year survival report of CheckMate 205 (same single-arm programme as the reports above)
cards.people: The same 243 CheckMate 205 patients (cohort A 63, cohort B 80, cohort C 100), at a median follow-up of about 5 years; cohort C patients in complete remission for 1 year could discontinue nivolumab and resume on relapse.
cards.result: The objective response rate was 71.2% (95% CI 65.1–76.8) and the complete response rate 21.4% (95% CI 16.4–27.1). Median duration of response was 18.2 months (95% CI 14.7–26.1), median duration of complete response 30.3 months and of partial remission 13.5 months. Median progression-free survival was 15.1 months (95% CI 11.3–18.5); median overall survival was not reached, with 5-year overall survival of 71.4% (95% CI 64.8–77.1). All 3 cohort C patients who discontinued in complete remission and were later re-treated achieved an objective response. No new or unexpected safety signals were identified.
cards.watchOut: The 5-year overall survival of 71.4% describes this treated cohort; with no control arm it cannot be attributed to nivolumab as an effect size. Same single programme as the cards above. The registry ID printed in this report's source line is the ID in its own record, which differs from the ID in the earlier CheckMate 205 records — printed as recorded, not harmonised.

cards.result: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — a labelled single-programme shelf. CheckMate 205 (n=243 across three brentuximab-history cohorts) reported objective response rates of 66.3% in the primary cohort B report, 69% at extended follow-up and 71.2% at 5 years, with median durations of response of 16.6–18.2 months, median progression-free survival of 15.1 months at 5 years, and 5-year overall survival of 71.4% as a within-cohort description. Entirely single-arm evidence: response and durability claims only. The parallel pembrolizumab programme is homed on shelf #7607 — cross-point only, never pooled. The frontline nivolumab cohort of CheckMate 205 (newly diagnosed disease) is a different slice and is not carded here.

shelves.title: Cabazitaxel vs mitoxantrone after docetaxel in mCRPC (FLOOR-RISK — exactly 2 reports, TROPIC): survival 15.1 vs 12.7 months; pain palliation comparable, neutropenia 82% vs 58%
shelves.question: In men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during or after docetaxel, does cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² plus prednisone prolong overall survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Aged · Androgen Antagonists/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Agents, Hormonal/therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Biomarkers, Tumor/blood · Disease Progression · Disease-Free Survival · Docetaxel · Drug Administration Schedule · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm · Humans · Infusions, Intravenous · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Male · Middle Aged · Mitoxantrone/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Neutropenia/chemically induced · Pain Measurement · Prednisone/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Prostate-Specific Antigen/blood · Prostatic Neoplasms/drug therapy/immunology/metabolism/mortality/pathology · Taxoids/administration & dosage/adverse effects · Treatment Failure · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports, both of one trial. TROPIC (n=755 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during or after docetaxel) found cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² plus prednisone prolonged median overall survival versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (15.1 vs 12.7 months; hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.59–0.83 — a relative measure beside its absolute medians, a gain of about 2.4 months). The second report, the 2-year survival and pain analysis, found more patients alive at 2 years (odds ratio 2.11, relative) and pain palliation comparable — not superior — to mitoxantrone. The price was taxane toxicity: grade ≥3 neutropenia 82% vs 58%, febrile neutropenia 8% vs 1%. The CARD question at pack #6420 presupposes this founding benefit; cross-point only.

cards.headline: TROPIC primary (de Bono 2010): cabazitaxel prolonged survival after docetaxel — median overall survival 15.1 vs 12.7 months vs mitoxantrone, hazard ratio 0.70 (relative)
cards.summary: TROPIC primary (de Bono 2010): cabazitaxel prolonged survival after docetaxel — median overall survival 15.1 vs 12.7 months vs mitoxantrone, hazard ratio 0.70 (relative)
cards.type: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial (TROPIC), cabazitaxel + prednisone vs mitoxantrone + prednisone after docetaxel — primary report
cards.people: 755 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during or after docetaxel, all on prednisone 10 mg daily, randomised open-label to cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² every 3 weeks (378) or mitoxantrone 12 mg/m² every 3 weeks (377), phase 3, intention-to-treat.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 15.1 months (95% CI 14.1–16.3) on cabazitaxel versus 12.7 months (95% CI 11.6–13.7) on mitoxantrone — an absolute gain of about 2.4 months of median survival, with hazard ratio 0.70 (95% CI 0.59–0.83), p<0.0001, a relative measure beside its absolute medians. Median progression-free survival was 2.8 months (95% CI 2.4–3.0) versus 1.4 months (95% CI 1.4–1.7) (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.64–0.86, p<0.0001, relative). Grade 3 or higher neutropenia occurred in 82% versus 58%, diarrhoea in 6% versus under 1%, and febrile neutropenia in 8% versus 1%.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base — one of exactly two reports on this shelf, both of this one trial. Open-label, against an active cytotoxic comparator (mitoxantrone), not placebo: the gain is ~2.4 months of median survival bought with substantially more neutropenia and febrile neutropenia. The later CARD question (cabazitaxel vs an androgen-receptor switch) presupposes this benefit and is homed at pack #6420 — cross-point only.
cards.source: de Bono JS et al. Prednisone plus cabazitaxel or mitoxantrone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing after docetaxel treatment: a randomised open-label trial. Lancet. 2010. PMID: 20888992. Registry ID: NCT00417079. cards.headline: TROPIC 2-year survival and pain analysis (Bahl 2013): more patients alive at 2 years on cabazitaxel (odds ratio 2.11, relative); pain palliation was COMPARABLE, not superior
cards.summary: TROPIC 2-year survival and pain analysis (Bahl 2013): more patients alive at 2 years on cabazitaxel (odds ratio 2.11, relative); pain palliation was COMPARABLE, not superior
cards.type: Two-year survival and pain analysis of TROPIC (same trial as the primary report above)
cards.people: The same 755 TROPIC patients, in an updated analysis (cut-off March 2010; median follow-up 25.5 months) of 2-year survival, prognostic factors for surviving at least 2 years, tumour-related pain and performance status.
cards.result: After 2 years, more patients remained alive on cabazitaxel than on mitoxantrone (odds ratio 2.11, 95% CI 1.33–3.33 — a relative measure), and cabazitaxel treatment was prognostic for survival of at least 2 years. Pain at baseline and pain response were comparable between the groups: the average daily pain performance index was slightly lower on cabazitaxel (difference across all cycles, 95% CI −0.27 to −0.01; P=0.035) while analgesic scores were similar. Grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathy was uncommon and comparable in both arms.
cards.watchOut: Same trial as the card above — the second of exactly two reports, not independent evidence. The honest core of the pain analysis is parity, not superiority: a slightly lower pain index with similar analgesic use and comparable pain response. A trial-summary article about TROPIC exists in the literature and is explicitly NOT counted as a third report.
cards.source: Bahl A et al. Impact of cabazitaxel on 2-year survival and palliation of tumour-related pain in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer treated in the TROPIC trial. Annals of Oncology. 2013. PMID: 23723295. Registry ID: NCT00417079. cards.headline: Cross-report harms reading of the same trial (not a third report): the survival gain was bought with taxane toxicity — grade ≥3 neutropenia 82% vs 58%, febrile neutropenia 8% vs 1%, diarrhoea 6% vs <1%; peripheral neuropathy uncommon in both arms
cards.summary: Cross-report harms reading of the same trial (not a third report): the survival gain was bought with taxane toxicity — grade ≥3 neutropenia 82% vs 58%, febrile neutropenia 8% vs 1%, diarrhoea 6% vs <1%; peripheral neuropathy uncommon in both arms
cards.type: Cross-report harms summary of the two carded TROPIC reports — not an additional report
cards.people: The safety populations of the same TROPIC trial (378 cabazitaxel, 377 mitoxantrone), read across its two carded reports — the primary report for neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and diarrhoea, and the 2-year analysis for peripheral neuropathy. No other report is counted on this shelf.
cards.result: The most common clinically significant grade 3 or higher adverse events in the primary report were neutropenia (cabazitaxel 303 patients, 82%; mitoxantrone 215, 58%) and diarrhoea (23, 6%; versus 1, under 1%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 28 patients (8%) versus 5 (1%). The 2-year analysis found grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathies uncommon and comparable between the groups — the neuropathy sparing sometimes claimed for cabazitaxel is, on this trial, a low rate in both arms rather than an advantage.
cards.watchOut: This card adds no new source — it is a cross-report harms summary of the two reports above, labelled as such so the count is never inflated. FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 reports, one trial (n=755). The dose question (20 vs 25 mg/m², PROSELICA) is a separate slice and is not carded here.

cards.summary: Synthesis: FLOOR-RISK — exactly 2 reports of one trial (TROPIC, n=755): cabazitaxel extended median survival by about 2.4 months after docetaxel (15.1 vs 12.7 months; HR 0.70 relative), with pain palliation comparable to mitoxantrone and substantially more neutropenia

cards.result: Synthesis: FLOOR-RISK — exactly 2 reports, both of the single TROPIC trial (755 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during or after docetaxel). The primary report found median overall survival of 15.1 vs 12.7 months for cabazitaxel plus prednisone versus mitoxantrone plus prednisone (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.59–0.83 — a relative measure beside its absolute medians, a gain of about 2.4 months). The 2-year analysis found more patients alive at 2 years (odds ratio 2.11, relative) and pain palliation comparable — not superior — to mitoxantrone. Toxicity was the price: grade ≥3 neutropenia 82% vs 58% and febrile neutropenia 8% vs 1%. This founding benefit is presupposed by the CARD question at pack #6420. If either TROPIC report had failed to verify, this shelf would not have been built.

shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated metastatic (predominantly clear-cell) renal-cell carcinoma, does sunitinib 50 mg daily (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) improve progression-free and overall survival versus interferon alfa?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) on progression-free survival and response — one trial, three reports, labelled a single-programme shelf. In 750 randomised patients with previously untreated metastatic renal-cell carcinoma, sunitinib gave median progression-free survival of 11 versus 5 months (hazard ratio 0.42, relative) and an objective response rate of 31% versus 6% in the primary report (47% versus 12% with updated follow-up), with significantly better reported quality of life on sunitinib. The overall-survival analysis is borderline and crossover-contaminated, and both facts are on the face: median overall survival 26.4 versus 21.8 months, hazard ratio 0.821 with p=0.051 by the primary unstratified log-rank analysis and hazard ratio 0.818 with p=0.049 by the stratified test — and within the interferon group, 33% of patients later received sunitinib and 32% other VEGF-signalling inhibitors. The honest headline is a progression-free-survival and response drug with a borderline survival analysis, not a clean survival win. The third report is a programme report of the same trial: baseline quality of life predicted progression-free survival. Sunitinib's other library homes (comparator in later RCC trials, GIST, adjuvant RCC, pancreatic NET) are different questions and are not re-carded.

cards.headline: Primary report (Motzer 2007, 750 randomised): sunitinib doubled median progression-free survival (11 vs 5 months; hazard ratio 0.42, relative) and response (31% vs 6%) versus interferon alfa

cards.type: Multicentre randomised phase 3 trial (primary report), sunitinib vs interferon alfa, first-line metastatic RCC
cards.people: 750 patients with previously untreated metastatic renal-cell carcinoma in a multicentre randomised phase 3 trial, assigned to repeated 6-week cycles of sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks off, or interferon alfa 9 MU subcutaneously three times weekly. Primary endpoint was progression-free survival; secondary endpoints included objective response, overall survival, patient-reported outcomes and safety.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was significantly longer on sunitinib (11 months) than on interferon alfa (5 months), corresponding to a hazard ratio of 0.42 (95% CI 0.32 to 0.54; p<0.001 — a relative measure, with the absolute medians beside it). The objective response rate was higher on sunitinib (31% versus 6%, p<0.001). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related fatigue was significantly more frequent on interferon alfa, whereas diarrhoea was more frequent on sunitinib. Patients on sunitinib reported significantly better quality of life than patients on interferon alfa (p<0.001).
cards.watchOut: Progression-free survival was the primary endpoint — this report does not by itself establish a survival benefit; the final survival analysis is the next card, with its borderline statistics and crossover printed on its face.
cards.source: Motzer RJ et al. Sunitinib versus interferon alfa in metastatic renal-cell carcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2007. PMID: 17215529. Registry ID: NCT00083889, NCT00098657. cards.headline: Final overall-survival analysis (Motzer 2009): median overall survival 26.4 vs 21.8 months — hazard ratio 0.821, p=0.051 by the primary unstratified log-rank test and 0.818, p=0.049 by the stratified test, with 33% of the interferon arm later receiving sunitinib
cards.summary: Final overall-survival analysis (Motzer 2009): median overall survival 26.4 vs 21.8 months — hazard ratio 0.821, p=0.051 by the primary unstratified log-rank test and 0.818, p=0.049 by the stratified test, with 33% of the interferon arm later receiving sunitinib
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the same phase 3 trial (programme report of the primary report above — one trial, not two)
cards.people: The same 750 treatment-naive patients with metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (sunitinib 50 mg on the 4-weeks-on / 2-weeks-off schedule versus interferon alfa 9 MU three times weekly), in the trial's final survival analysis with updated progression-free survival, response and safety follow-up.
cards.result: Median overall survival was greater on sunitinib than on interferon alfa (26.4 versus 21.8 months; hazard ratio 0.821, 95% CI 0.673 to 1.001; p=0.051 by the primary analysis of the unstratified log-rank test — a relative measure whose confidence interval includes 1 — and hazard ratio 0.818, 95% CI 0.669 to 0.999; p=0.049 by the stratified log-rank test). Both analyses are printed, as the row directs: the survival result sits exactly on the significance boundary and which side it falls on depends on the test. Within the interferon group, 33% of patients received sunitinib and 32% received other VEGF-signalling inhibitors after discontinuing the trial — post-progression treatment that dilutes any survival contrast. Median progression-free survival was 11 versus 5 months (p<0.001) and the objective response rate 47% versus 12% (p<0.001) with updated follow-up. The most common sunitinib-related grade 3 adverse events were hypertension (12%), fatigue (11%), diarrhoea (9%) and hand-foot syndrome (9%).
cards.watchOut: The stratified / unstratified discrepancy (p=0.049 versus p=0.051) and the 33% / 32% post-progression treatment rates in the interferon arm belong on the face, not in a footnote — both are printed in this card's headline and result.

shelves.question: In patients with advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma resistant to standard (cytokine-era) therapy, does sorafenib 400 mg twice daily improve progression-free and overall survival versus placebo?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit, progression-free survival only) — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports, stated on the face, both reports of the single TARGET trial (903 randomised). Sorafenib doubled median progression-free survival (5.5 versus 2.8 months; hazard ratio 0.44, relative) with partial responses in 10% versus 2%. Overall survival was NOT significantly different on the intention-to-treat final analysis (17.8 versus 15.2 months; hazard ratio 0.88, p=0.146); the first interim survival hazard ratio of 0.72 did not cross the prespecified O'Brien-Fleming threshold. A secondary analysis censoring placebo patients after they crossed over to sorafenib gave 17.8 versus 14.3 months (hazard ratio 0.78, p=0.029) — a sensitivity analysis shaped by the crossover the PFS result itself triggered, not the headline. Baseline VEGF was prognostic, and both high- and low-VEGF groups benefited on progression-free survival. Diarrhoea, rash, fatigue and hand-foot skin reactions were the commonest sorafenib adverse events. Cross-point: sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma (SHARP / Asia-Pacific) is a different question in a different disease, homed at pack #7567 — the two shelves cross-point and neither re-cards the other.

cards.headline: TARGET primary report (Escudier 2007, 903 randomised): sorafenib doubled median progression-free survival (5.5 vs 2.8 months; hazard ratio 0.44, relative); first interim overall-survival hazard ratio 0.72 did NOT cross the prespecified significance threshold
cards.summary: TARGET primary report (Escudier 2007, 903 randomised): sorafenib doubled median progression-free survival (5.5 vs 2.8 months; hazard ratio 0.44, relative); first interim overall-survival hazard ratio 0.72 did NOT cross the prespecified significance threshold
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (TARGET, primary report), sorafenib vs placebo, pretreated advanced clear-cell RCC
cards.people: 903 patients with advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma resistant to standard (cytokine-era) therapy, randomly assigned in a phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled trial to continuous oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily (451) or placebo (452), November 2003 to March 2005. Primary endpoint was overall survival; a single planned progression-free-survival analysis was performed in January 2005.
cards.result: At the January 2005 cutoff, median progression-free survival was 5.5 months on sorafenib versus 2.8 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.55; p<0.01 — a relative measure, with the absolute medians beside it). Consequently crossover from placebo to sorafenib was permitted from May 2005. The first interim overall-survival analysis (May 2005) gave a hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.94; p=0.02), which was not statistically significant according to the prespecified O'Brien-Fleming threshold. Partial responses were reported in 10% on sorafenib versus 2% on placebo (p<0.001). Diarrhoea, rash, fatigue and hand-foot skin reactions were the most common sorafenib adverse events; hypertension and cardiac ischaemia were rare serious events, more common on sorafenib.
cards.watchOut: The progression-free-survival benefit triggered the crossover that then diluted the survival comparison — that sequence is the trial's central interpretive fact and is printed on the face. One of exactly 2 reports on this shelf.
cards.source: Escudier B et al. Sorafenib in advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2007. PMID: 17215530. Registry ID: NCT00073307. cards.headline: TARGET final report (Escudier 2009): final overall survival 17.8 vs 15.2 months was NOT significant on intention-to-treat (hazard ratio 0.88, p=0.146); censoring post-crossover placebo data gave 17.8 vs 14.3 months (hazard ratio 0.78, p=0.029)
cards.summary: TARGET final report (Escudier 2009): final overall survival 17.8 vs 15.2 months was NOT significant on intention-to-treat (hazard ratio 0.88, p=0.146); censoring post-crossover placebo data gave 17.8 vs 14.3 months (hazard ratio 0.78, p=0.029)
cards.type: Final efficacy and safety report of the TARGET phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary report above — one trial, two reports)
cards.people: The same 903 previously treated patients with renal-cell carcinoma randomised to sorafenib versus placebo in TARGET; after the progression-free-survival benefit was demonstrated, patients assigned to placebo were offered sorafenib. Overall survival was determined at two planned interim analyses and one final analysis, with a secondary analysis censoring placebo patients who crossed over.
cards.result: Final overall survival on sorafenib was comparable with placebo on the intention-to-treat analysis: 17.8 versus 15.2 months (hazard ratio 0.88; p=0.146 — not significant). When post-crossover placebo survival data were censored, the difference became significant: 17.8 versus 14.3 months (hazard ratio 0.78; p=0.029) — a secondary, crossover-corrected sensitivity analysis, printed as such and never as the headline. Adverse events at 16 months after crossover were similar to those previously reported. Baseline VEGF levels correlated with performance status and prognostic score and with progression-free and overall survival in placebo patients (prognostic), and both high-VEGF (p<0.01) and low-VEGF (p<0.01) groups benefited from sorafenib on progression-free survival.
cards.watchOut: An overall-survival-null trial on intention-to-treat whose PFS benefit triggered the crossover that diluted overall survival — print that sequence plainly. The censored analysis is a sensitivity analysis, not the headline result.

cards.headline: Synthesis: FLOOR-RISK — exactly 2 reports of one trial (TARGET, 903 randomised): a clear progression-free-survival benefit (5.5 vs 2.8 months) and no significant overall-survival benefit on intention-to-treat (17.8 vs 15.2 months, p=0.146)

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: the TARGET trial's primary and final reports (903 randomised), plus one facet card drawn only from those two reports.
cards.result: Sorafenib was the founding targeted therapy in pretreated advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma: it doubled median progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.44, relative) and raised partial responses from 2% to 10%, at the cost of diarrhoea, rash, fatigue and hand-foot skin reactions. Its final intention-to-treat overall-survival analysis was null (hazard ratio 0.88, p=0.146), after a crossover its own PFS result had triggered; the crossover-censored analysis (hazard ratio 0.78, p=0.029) is a sensitivity reading. There is no third report to card.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK stated exactly: 2 reports, one trial. If either report had failed to verify this session, this pack would not have been built. Cross-point pack #7567 (sorafenib in HCC) — a different question in a different disease. See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Pazopanib versus sunitinib, first-line metastatic RCC (COMPARZ): one trial, three reports — noninferior PFS (HR 1.05), similar survival, better early tolerability and quality of life on pazopanib
shelves.question: In patients with treatment-naive clear-cell metastatic renal-cell carcinoma, is pazopanib 800 mg daily noninferior to sunitinib for progression-free survival, and how do overall survival, toxicity and quality of life compare?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Angiogenesis Inhibitors · Carcinoma, Renal Cell · Disease-Free Survival · Double-Blind Method · Female · Humans · Indazoles · Indoles · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Kidney Neoplasms · Male · Pyrimidines · Pyrroles · Quality of Life · Sulfonamides · Sunitinib
shelves.balance: LIKELY (noninferior) — one trial, three reports, labelled a single-programme shelf. COMPARZ (1,110 randomised, treatment-naive clear-cell metastatic RCC) met its prespecified noninferiority margin for progression-free survival: hazard ratio 1.05 (95% CI 0.90-1.22), with the upper confidence bound below 1.25. Overall survival was similar (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.76-1.08 — an interval spanning 1, so no survival claim is made). The clinical payload is tolerability: sunitinib caused more fatigue (63% versus 55%), hand-foot syndrome (50% versus 29%) and thrombocytopenia (78% versus 41%), pazopanib more alanine aminotransferase elevation (60% versus 43%), and 11 of 14 quality-of-life domains favoured pazopanib in the first 6 months. The Q-TWiST programme report qualifies its own finding: mean time with grade 3/4 toxicity was 31 days longer on sunitinib, but the quality-adjusted advantage for pazopanib was significant in fewer than half of the utility combinations examined — that qualifier is printed on the face. The Asian versus non-Asian programme report (363 Asian and 703 non-Asian patients in the safety population) found haematologic toxicity, transaminase elevation and hand-foot syndrome more prevalent in Asian patients on both drugs. 'Noninferior PFS plus better early quality of life' is never converted into a survival claim on this shelf.

cards.headline: COMPARZ primary report (Motzer 2013, 1,110 randomised): pazopanib was NONINFERIOR to sunitinib for progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.90-1.22; margin <1.25); overall survival similar (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.76-1.08)
cards.summary: COMPARZ primary report (Motzer 2013, 1,110 randomised): pazopanib was NONINFERIOR to sunitinib for progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.90-1.22; margin <1.25); overall survival similar (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.76-1.08)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised noninferiority trial (COMPARZ, primary report), pazopanib vs sunitinib, first-line metastatic clear-cell RCC
cards.people: 1,110 patients with clear-cell metastatic renal-cell carcinoma and no prior therapy, randomised (1:1) in a phase 3 trial to continuous pazopanib 800 mg once daily (557) or sunitinib in 6-week cycles, 50 mg once daily for 4 weeks then 2 weeks off (553). Primary endpoint was progression-free survival by independent review, powered to show noninferiority of pazopanib; secondary endpoints included overall survival, safety and quality of life.
cards.result: Pazopanib was noninferior to sunitinib for progression-free survival (hazard ratio for progression or death 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22 — a relative measure — meeting the predefined noninferiority margin, upper bound of the 95% confidence interval <1.25). Overall survival was similar (hazard ratio for death with pazopanib 0.91, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.08 — an interval spanning 1). Patients on sunitinib had a higher incidence of fatigue (63% versus 55%), hand-foot syndrome (50% versus 29%) and thrombocytopenia (78% versus 41%); patients on pazopanib had a higher incidence of increased alanine aminotransferase (60% versus 43%). The mean change from baseline in 11 of 14 health-related quality-of-life domains during the first 6 months favoured pazopanib (p<0.05 for all 11 comparisons).
cards.watchOut: A noninferiority trial: its demonstrated claim is 'not worse than sunitinib on PFS, within the prespecified margin, with a better early tolerability and quality-of-life profile' — not superiority, and not a survival benefit (the overall-survival interval spans 1).
cards.source: Motzer RJ et al. Pazopanib versus sunitinib in metastatic renal-cell carcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 23964934. Registry ID: NCT00720941.
