cards.headline: Programme report — Q-TWiST (Beaumont 2016): mean time with grade 3/4 toxicity was 31 days longer on sunitinib, but the quality-adjusted advantage for pazopanib was significant in FEWER THAN HALF of the utility combinations examined
cards.summary: Programme report — Q-TWiST (Beaumont 2016): mean time with grade 3/4 toxicity was 31 days longer on sunitinib, but the quality-adjusted advantage for pazopanib was significant in FEWER THAN HALF of the utility combinations examined
cards.type: Programme report: post hoc Q-TWiST analysis of the COMPARZ trial (same trial as the primary report above — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: The same 1,110 COMPARZ patients (557 pazopanib, 553 sunitinib), in a post hoc quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity (Q-TWiST) analysis partitioning overall survival into time with grade 3 or 4 toxicity, time without symptoms or grade 3/4 toxicity, and time after progression or relapse, weighted by health-state utilities from 0 to 1.
cards.result: Mean time with grade 3 or 4 toxicity was 31 days (95% CI 13-48 days) longer for sunitinib than for pazopanib. In the threshold utility analysis, the difference in Q-TWiST ranged from -11 days to 43 days in favour of pazopanib across most utility combinations; differences were significant in less than half of the utility combinations examined, typically when the utility for time with toxicity was lower than the utility for time after relapse. The authors conclude patients on pazopanib had a slightly longer Q-TWiST, primarily due to the reduced length of time with toxicity.
cards.watchOut: A post hoc analysis whose headline qualifier — significant in fewer than half of the utility combinations — is printed on this card's face, per the row. It refines the tolerability reading; it is not a second efficacy trial.
cards.source: Beaumont JL et al. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis of pazopanib versus sunitinib in patients with renal cell carcinoma. Cancer. 2016. PMID: 27000445. cards.headline: Programme report — Asian versus non-Asian safety (Guo 2018): haematologic toxicity, transaminase elevation and hand-foot syndrome were more prevalent in Asian patients on BOTH drugs
cards.summary: Programme report — Asian versus non-Asian safety (Guo 2018): haematologic toxicity, transaminase elevation and hand-foot syndrome were more prevalent in Asian patients on BOTH drugs
cards.type: Programme report: Asian versus non-Asian safety subgroup analysis of the COMPARZ trial (same trial as the cards above — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: The COMPARZ safety population: 363 Asian patients and 703 non-Asian patients randomised (1:1) to pazopanib 800 mg once daily continuously or sunitinib 50 mg once daily in 6-week cycles (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off), analysed by Asian versus non-Asian subpopulation.
cards.result: Asian patients had a similar duration of exposure to either drug compared with non-Asian patients, although Asian patients had a higher frequency of dose modifications. Overall, haematologic toxicities, cytopenias, increased AST/ALT and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia were more prevalent in Asian patients, whereas gastrointestinal toxicities were more prevalent in non-Asian patients. Among Asian patients, most adverse events were more common on sunitinib than on pazopanib; the most common grade 3/4 events on pazopanib were hypertension (grade 3, 22%) and increased alanine aminotransferase (grade 3, 12%; grade 4, 1%), and on sunitinib thrombocytopenia / decreased platelet count (grade 3, 36%; grade 4, 10%), neutropenia (grade 3, 24%; grade 4, 3%), hypertension (grade 3, 20%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (grade 3, 15%). The authors conclude both drugs were well tolerated in both subpopulations, with a distinct pattern and severity of adverse events in Asian patients.
cards.watchOut: A safety subgroup analysis of the same trial: it describes who gets which toxicity, on both drugs — it adds no efficacy evidence and must not be counted as a second trial.
cards.source: Guo J et al. Safety of pazopanib and sunitinib in treatment-naive patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma: Asian versus non-Asian subgroup analysis of the COMPARZ trial. shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival only) — PARTIAL beside live #1877, carding only the everolimus-versus-placebo slice named in the row. Live #1877 (second-line RCC after antiangiogenic therapy: nivolumab in CheckMate 025 and cabozantinib in METEOR, both versus everolimus) presupposes everolimus as its comparator background but cards no RECORD-1 report; this shelf cards that founding placebo-controlled question only, and does not re-card CheckMate 025 or METEOR. RECORD-1 is a PFS-only win, with all three caveats on the face: the trial was halted early at its second interim analysis; median progression-free survival was 4.0 versus 1.9 months at the primary analysis (hazard ratio 0.30, relative) and 4.9 versus 1.9 months in the final results (hazard ratio 0.33, relative); and overall survival was NULL on intention-to-treat — 14.8 versus 14.4 months (hazard ratio 0.87, p=0.162) — after 80% of the placebo arm crossed over to everolimus. The crossover-corrected rank-preserving structural failure-time estimate (1.9-fold longer survival, 95% CI 0.5-8.5) has an interval spanning no effect and is printed as such. Pricing harms are stomatitis (40% versus 8%), rash (25% versus 4%) and pneumonitis (8% any grade in the primary report; 27% in the small Japanese subgroup, all grade 1-2 and reversible, versus 14% overall in the final subgroup report). The Japanese subgroup (24 patients) is a programme report of the same trial, not independent evidence.

cards.headline: RECORD-1 primary report (Motzer 2008): everolimus prolonged median progression-free survival to 4.0 vs 1.9 months (hazard ratio 0.30, relative) — in a trial HALTED EARLY at its second interim analysis
cards.summary: RECORD-1 primary report (Motzer 2008): everolimus prolonged median progression-free survival to 4.0 vs 1.9 months (hazard ratio 0.30, relative) — in a trial HALTED EARLY at its second interim analysis
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (RECORD-1, primary report), everolimus vs placebo after VEGF-targeted therapy
cards.people: 410 patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma whose disease had progressed on sunitinib, sorafenib, or both, randomly assigned (2:1) in a phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled trial to everolimus 10 mg once daily (272) or placebo (138), each with best supportive care. Primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review; the study was designed to be terminated after 290 progression events.
cards.result: The results of the second interim analysis indicated a significant difference in efficacy and the trial was halted early after 191 progression events had been observed (101 [37%] events on everolimus, 90 [65%] on placebo; hazard ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.22-0.40; p<0.0001 — a relative measure, with the absolute medians beside it: median progression-free survival 4.0 months [95% CI 3.7-5.5] versus 1.9 months [1.8-1.9]). Stomatitis (107 [40%] on everolimus versus 11 [8%] on placebo), rash (66 [25%] versus 6 [4%]) and fatigue (53 [20%] versus 22 [16%]) were the most commonly reported adverse events, mostly mild or moderate. Pneumonitis (any grade) was detected in 22 (8%) everolimus patients, eight of them grade 3.
cards.watchOut: PARTIAL slice: this shelf cards only the everolimus-versus-placebo question beside live #1877, which cards nivolumab and cabozantinib against everolimus as comparator — RECORD-1 itself is carded nowhere else. Early stopping at an interim analysis tends to flatter the effect estimate; the final results are the next card.

cards.headline: RECORD-1 final results (Motzer 2010): PFS 4.9 vs 1.9 months (hazard ratio 0.33, relative), but overall survival was NULL on ITT — 14.8 vs 14.4 months (hazard ratio 0.87, p=0.162) — with 80% of the placebo arm crossing over; the crossover-corrected estimate's interval spans no effect (1.9-fold, 95% CI 0.5-8.5)
cards.summary: RECORD-1 final results (Motzer 2010): PFS 4.9 vs 1.9 months (hazard ratio 0.33, relative), but overall survival was NULL on ITT — 14.8 vs 14.4 months (hazard ratio 0.87, p=0.162) — with 80% of the placebo arm crossing over; the crossover-corrected estimate's interval spans no effect (1.9-fold, 95% CI 0.5-8.5)
cards.type: Final results of the RECORD-1 phase 3 trial (same trial as the primary report above — one trial, not two)
cards.people: 416 patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma progressing on VEGF-receptor tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, randomised (2:1) to everolimus 10 mg daily (277) or placebo (139) plus best supportive care — the final-analysis population of the same RECORD-1 trial (the primary report above analysed 410 randomised at its early halt). Progression-free survival and safety were assessed to the end of double-blind treatment, with mature overall-survival data and a rank-preserving structural failure-time model correcting for crossover.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 4.9 months on everolimus versus 1.9 months on placebo by independent central review (hazard ratio 0.33; p<0.001 — a relative measure) and 5.5 versus 1.9 months by investigators (hazard ratio 0.32; p<0.001). Median overall survival was 14.8 months on everolimus versus 14.4 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.87; p=0.162 — NOT significant), with 80% of patients in the placebo arm crossing over to everolimus. By the rank-preserving structural failure-time model, survival corrected for crossover was estimated 1.9-fold longer (95% CI 0.5-8.5) with everolimus compared with placebo only — an interval spanning no effect, printed as such. Serious adverse events on everolimus in at least 5% of patients included infections (10%), dyspnoea (7%) and fatigue (5%). Independent prognostic factors for shorter overall survival included low performance status, high corrected calcium, low haemoglobin and prior sunitinib.
cards.watchOut: The null intention-to-treat overall-survival result and the crossover caveat are on this card's face, as the row requires: after 80% crossover, the ITT survival comparison is largely everolimus versus everolimus-after-progression, and the model-corrected estimate is too imprecise (95% CI 0.5-8.5) to rescue a survival claim.

cards.headline: Programme report — Japanese subgroup (Tsukamoto 2011, 24 patients): median PFS 5.75 vs 3.61 months (hazard ratio 0.19, relative); pneumonitis in 27% of Japanese everolimus patients (all grade 1-2, reversible) versus 14% overall
cards.summary: Programme report — Japanese subgroup (Tsukamoto 2011, 24 patients): median PFS 5.75 vs 3.61 months (hazard ratio 0.19, relative); pneumonitis in 27% of Japanese everolimus patients (all grade 1-2, reversible) versus 14% overall
cards.type: Programme report: Japanese subgroup analysis of the RECORD-1 trial (same trial as the cards above — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: 24 Japanese patients in RECORD-1 (everolimus 15, placebo 9) with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma progressing after sorafenib, sunitinib or both, in a subgroup analysis of the pivotal phase 3 trial, with outcomes compared against the overall study population.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival in the Japanese subpopulation was 5.75 months (95% CI 4.90 to not reached) on everolimus versus 3.61 months (95% CI 1.91-9.03) on placebo (hazard ratio 0.19, 95% CI 0.05-0.83 — a relative measure from 24 patients, with very wide intervals). Median overall survival was not reached on everolimus and was 14.9 months on placebo (hazard ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.07-1.27). The most common adverse events on everolimus were stomatitis, infections and rash. Four Japanese everolimus patients (27%) developed grade 1 or 2 pneumonitis (all reversible, allowing continuation after interruption, steroids and dose reduction for the grade 2 cases), versus a pneumonitis incidence of 14% in the overall population (with a grade 3 incidence of 4%). The authors conclude the demonstrated benefits in the overall population were similar in Japanese patients.
cards.watchOut: A 24-patient subgroup: its hazard ratios carry very wide intervals and it is carded for its pneumonitis signal (27% versus 14% overall), not as efficacy evidence. It must not be counted as a second trial.
cards.source: Tsukamoto T et al. Phase III trial of everolimus in metastatic renal cell carcinoma: subgroup analysis of Japanese patients from RECORD-1. Japanese journal of clinical oncology. 2011. PMID: 20965941. Registry ID: none in the record. shelves.title: Temsirolimus in advanced RCC: SPLIT by line — ARCC first-line survival win in poor-prognosis disease (10.9 vs 7.3 months); INTORSECT second-line loss to sorafenib (OS 12.3 vs 16.6 months)
shelves.question: In patients with advanced renal-cell carcinoma, does the mTOR inhibitor temsirolimus improve survival — as first-line therapy versus interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic disease (ARCC), and as second-line therapy after sunitinib versus sorafenib (INTORSECT)?

shelves.balance: SPLIT (by line of therapy) — two trials, three reports, with the two slices labelled and never pooled, pointing in opposite directions. First-line, poor-prognosis disease (ARCC, 626 randomised, previously untreated): temsirolimus alone improved overall survival versus interferon alfa (median 10.9 versus 7.3 months; hazard ratio 0.73, relative), with fewer serious adverse events on temsirolimus — but the temsirolimus-plus-interferon combination did NOT beat interferon (hazard ratio 0.96; median 8.4 months), and that null combination arm is on the face. The ARCC biomarker programme report is a negative predictive-biomarker result: baseline tumour PTEN and HIF-1alpha levels did not correlate with temsirolimus efficacy. Second-line after sunitinib (INTORSECT, 512 randomised): progression-free survival did NOT differ between temsirolimus and sorafenib (median 4.3 versus 3.9 months; hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.71-1.07), and overall survival favoured SORAFENIB (median 16.6 versus 12.3 months; hazard ratio 1.31 for temsirolimus versus sorafenib, relative). The shelf's value is exactly that contrast: an mTOR inhibitor won first-line in poor-prognosis disease and lost second-line to continued VEGF blockade.

cards.headline: ARCC primary report (Hudes 2007, 626 randomised, poor-prognosis, first-line): temsirolimus alone improved overall survival versus interferon alfa (median 10.9 vs 7.3 months; hazard ratio 0.73, relative) — the temsirolimus-plus-interferon combination did NOT (hazard ratio 0.96)
cards.summary: ARCC primary report (Hudes 2007, 626 randomised, poor-prognosis, first-line): temsirolimus alone improved overall survival versus interferon alfa (median 10.9 vs 7.3 months; hazard ratio 0.73, relative) — the temsirolimus-plus-interferon combination did NOT (hazard ratio 0.96)
cards.type: Multicentre randomised phase 3 trial (Global ARCC, primary report), temsirolimus vs interferon alfa vs the combination, first-line poor-prognosis metastatic RCC
cards.people: 626 patients with previously untreated, poor-prognosis metastatic renal-cell carcinoma in a multicentre phase 3 trial, randomly assigned to intravenous temsirolimus 25 mg weekly, interferon alfa 3 million U subcutaneously three times weekly escalating to 18 million U, or combination therapy with temsirolimus 15 mg weekly plus interferon alfa 6 million U three times weekly. Primary endpoint was overall survival, comparing the temsirolimus and combination groups each with the interferon group.
cards.result: Patients receiving temsirolimus alone had longer overall survival than patients receiving interferon alone (hazard ratio for death 0.73, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.92; p=0.008 — a relative measure, with the absolute medians beside it: median overall survival 10.9 months on temsirolimus, 7.3 months on interferon and 8.4 months on the combination) and longer progression-free survival (p<0.001). Overall survival in the combination group did not differ significantly from the interferon group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.20; p=0.70). Rash, peripheral oedema, hyperglycaemia and hyperlipidaemia were more common on temsirolimus, asthenia more common on interferon, and there were fewer patients with serious adverse events in the temsirolimus group than in the interferon group (p=0.02).
cards.watchOut: A poor-prognosis, previously untreated population only — the survival win does not transfer to better-prognosis or pretreated disease (see INTORSECT, carded below, for the opposite second-line result). The combination arm's null result is part of this trial's finding, not an aside.

cards.headline: Programme report — ARCC biomarkers (Figlin 2009): baseline tumour PTEN and HIF-1alpha levels did NOT correlate with temsirolimus efficacy — a negative predictive-biomarker result (a report OF the ARCC trial, not a separate trial)
cards.summary: Programme report — ARCC biomarkers (Figlin 2009): baseline tumour PTEN and HIF-1alpha levels did NOT correlate with temsirolimus efficacy — a negative predictive-biomarker result (a report OF the ARCC trial, not a separate trial)
cards.type: Programme report: exploratory biomarker analysis of the ARCC trial (same trial as the primary report above — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: Patients in the phase 3 Global ARCC trial carded above (temsirolimus 25 mg intravenously weekly versus interferon alfa), in an exploratory analysis measuring baseline PTEN and HIF-1alpha levels in archived tumour specimens by immunohistochemistry.
cards.result: There was no correlation between baseline PTEN and HIF-1alpha levels and treatment effect with respect to overall survival, progression-free survival or objective response rate in patients with advanced renal-cell carcinoma with poor-risk prognostic factors: patients demonstrated overall-survival and progression-free-survival benefit on temsirolimus regardless of PTEN and HIF-1alpha status. The authors note baseline PTEN and HIF-1 levels may not predict response to temsirolimus, and that the lack of correlation may alternatively be due to variability in tumour specimens from the trial's global nature.
cards.watchOut: A negative biomarker result, labelled as such: it removes a proposed selection strategy rather than adding efficacy evidence, and must not be counted as a second trial.

cards.headline: INTORSECT (Hutson 2014, 512 randomised, second-line after sunitinib): progression-free survival did NOT differ (4.3 vs 3.9 months; hazard ratio 0.87) and overall survival favoured SORAFENIB (median 16.6 vs 12.3 months; hazard ratio 1.31 for temsirolimus, relative)
cards.summary: INTORSECT (Hutson 2014, 512 randomised, second-line after sunitinib): progression-free survival did NOT differ (4.3 vs 3.9 months; hazard ratio 0.87) and overall survival favoured SORAFENIB (median 16.6 vs 12.3 months; hazard ratio 1.31 for temsirolimus, relative)
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial (INTORSECT), temsirolimus vs sorafenib, second-line after sunitinib in metastatic RCC
cards.people: 512 patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma who had progressed on sunitinib, randomly assigned (1:1) in an international phase 3 trial to intravenous temsirolimus 25 mg once weekly (259) or oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily (253). Primary endpoint was progression-free survival by independent review; safety, objective response and overall survival were secondary endpoints.
cards.result: Primary analysis revealed no significant difference between the arms for progression-free survival (stratified hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.07; two-sided p=0.19 — a relative measure) or objective response rate; median progression-free survival was 4.3 months on temsirolimus and 3.9 months on sorafenib. There was a significant overall-survival difference in favour of sorafenib (stratified hazard ratio 1.31, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.63; two-sided p=0.01, for temsirolimus versus sorafenib): median overall survival was 12.3 months on temsirolimus and 16.6 months on sorafenib. Safety profiles of both agents were consistent with previous studies. The authors conclude second-line temsirolimus did not demonstrate a progression-free-survival advantage over sorafenib, and that the longer survival with sorafenib suggests sequenced VEGF-receptor inhibition may benefit patients.
cards.watchOut: The opposite slice from ARCC: a different line of therapy, a different comparator and a different result — the two trials are labelled slices and are never pooled into one temsirolimus verdict. Cross-point: sorafenib versus placebo in pretreated RCC is its own question, carded at pack #7639.

cards.headline: Synthesis: two trials, three reports, opposite directions — temsirolimus won on survival first-line in poor-prognosis disease (10.9 vs 7.3 months) and lost on survival second-line after sunitinib (12.3 vs 16.6 months against sorafenib)
cards.summary: Synthesis: two trials, three reports, opposite directions — temsirolimus won on survival first-line in poor-prognosis disease (10.9 vs 7.3 months) and lost on survival second-line after sunitinib (12.3 vs 16.6 months against sorafenib)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: ARCC (626 randomised, first-line poor-prognosis) with its biomarker programme report, and INTORSECT (512 randomised, second-line after sunitinib) — 1,138 randomised patients across two different clinical moments, never pooled.
cards.result: First-line: temsirolimus alone improved overall survival versus interferon alfa (hazard ratio 0.73, relative; median 10.9 versus 7.3 months), the temsirolimus-plus-interferon combination did not (hazard ratio 0.96), and baseline PTEN / HIF-1alpha did not predict who benefited. Second-line: temsirolimus showed no progression-free-survival advantage over sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.87, interval spanning 1) and significantly worse overall survival (hazard ratio 1.31 for temsirolimus versus sorafenib, relative; median 12.3 versus 16.6 months). The contrast — mTOR blockade winning where the comparator was interferon in poor-prognosis untreated disease, and losing where the alternative was continued VEGF blockade after sunitinib — is the shelf's answer.
cards.watchOut: Two labelled slices, never pooled. See the individual cards; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Ibrutinib + obinutuzumab vs chlorambucil + obinutuzumab in first-line CLL (iLLUMINATE): PFS not reached vs 19.0 months (HR 0.23), sustained at final analysis — exactly 2 reports (FLOOR-RISK)
shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma who are aged 65 years or older or have coexisting conditions, does ibrutinib plus obinutuzumab improve progression-free survival versus chlorambucil plus obinutuzumab (iLLUMINATE)?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) for progression-free survival, on an exactly-two-report FLOOR-RISK base. Only two reports of the iLLUMINATE trial exist and both are carded: the primary report (229 randomised) found median progression-free survival not reached versus 19.0 months (hazard ratio 0.23, a relative measure; 30-month PFS 79% vs 31%), and the final analysis at 45 months found the same pattern (hazard ratio 0.25; median not reached vs 22 months; undetectable MRD 38% vs 25%). The price in the primary report was serious adverse events in 58% versus 35%. Neither report demonstrates an overall-survival benefit, and the shelf claims none. PARTIAL context: neighbouring first-line CLL shelves presuppose this comparison without carding it; this shelf cards only the iLLUMINATE question.

cards.headline: iLLUMINATE primary report (Moreno 2019): ibrutinib + obinutuzumab kept patients progression-free far longer than chlorambucil + obinutuzumab — median PFS not reached vs 19.0 months, hazard ratio 0.23 (a relative measure); serious adverse events 58% vs 35%
cards.summary: iLLUMINATE primary report (Moreno 2019): ibrutinib + obinutuzumab kept patients progression-free far longer than chlorambucil + obinutuzumab — median PFS not reached vs 19.0 months, hazard ratio 0.23 (a relative measure); serious adverse events 58% vs 35%
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised trial (iLLUMINATE), primary report — report 1 of exactly 2 on this shelf (FLOOR-RISK base)
cards.people: 229 patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma, aged 65 years or older, or younger than 65 with coexisting conditions, randomised at 74 hospitals to ibrutinib 420 mg daily continuously plus six cycles of obinutuzumab (113) or chlorambucil plus the same obinutuzumab regimen (116). Primary endpoint: progression-free survival by masked independent review.
cards.result: At median follow-up 31.3 months, median progression-free survival was not reached on ibrutinib + obinutuzumab versus 19.0 months on chlorambucil + obinutuzumab (hazard ratio 0.23, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.37; P<0.0001 — a relative measure). Estimated 30-month progression-free survival was 79% versus 31% — an absolute difference of 48 percentage points. The most common grade 3 or 4 adverse events in both groups were neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Serious adverse events occurred in 65 of 113 patients (58%) on ibrutinib + obinutuzumab versus 40 of 115 (35%) on chlorambucil + obinutuzumab. One treatment-related death was reported in each group.
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial, and its demonstrated payload is progression-free survival, not overall survival: the hazard ratio 0.23 is a relative measure and must not be read as a survival result. The 23-percentage-point higher serious-adverse-event rate on the ibrutinib arm belongs beside the benefit.
cards.source: Moreno C et al. cards.headline: iLLUMINATE final analysis (Moreno 2022): the progression-free-survival advantage persisted at 45 months — median not reached vs 22 months, hazard ratio 0.25 (relative); undetectable MRD 38% vs 25%; no new safety signals
cards.summary: iLLUMINATE final analysis (Moreno 2022): the progression-free-survival advantage persisted at 45 months — median not reached vs 22 months, hazard ratio 0.25 (relative); undetectable MRD 38% vs 25%; no new safety signals
cards.type: Final analysis of the same phase 3 randomised trial (iLLUMINATE) — report 2 of exactly 2 on this shelf (FLOOR-RISK base)
cards.people: The same iLLUMINATE population as the primary report above (113 ibrutinib + obinutuzumab, 116 chlorambucil + obinutuzumab) — a later analysis of the same trial, not a second trial. Median follow-up 45 months (range 0.2 to 52).
cards.result: Median progression-free survival remained not reached on ibrutinib + obinutuzumab versus 22 months on chlorambucil + obinutuzumab (hazard ratio 0.25, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.39; P<0.0001 — a relative measure). The best overall rate of undetectable minimal residual disease (<0.01% by flow cytometry) was 38% versus 25%. With a median ibrutinib treatment duration of 42 months — 13 months longer than at the primary analysis — no new safety signals were identified; common grade 3-or-worse adverse events were most prevalent in the first 6 months and generally decreased over time, except hypertension.
cards.watchOut: A final analysis of the one trial, not independent confirmation of it: this shelf's entire base is two reports of a single trial, and that count is printed on its face. Overall survival was still not the demonstrated payload.

Live #764 (first-line nivolumab–ipilimumab and nivolumab–relatlimab) presupposes ipilimumab's founding benefit but cards neither founding trial; this shelf cards only that slice. MDX010-20 (676 randomised, previously treated): median survival 10.1 months on ipilimumab alone and 10.0 months with gp100 versus 6.4 months on gp100 alone (hazard ratios 0.66 and 0.68, relative measures), with grade 3–4 immune-related adverse events in 10–15% and 14 drug-related deaths (2.1%). Ipilimumab 10 mg/kg + dacarbazine first-line (502 randomised): median 11.2 versus 9.1 months (hazard ratio 0.72, relative), grade 3–4 adverse events 56.3% versus 27.5%. The pooled analysis of 1,861 treated patients (median survival 11.4 months; plateau from year 3) is a within-treatment description, not a randomised contrast, and is labelled as such. The two randomised slices differ in dose and setting and are never pooled.

cards.headline: MDX010-20 (Hodi 2010): ipilimumab — alone or with gp100 vaccine — improved survival versus gp100 alone in previously treated metastatic melanoma (median 10.1 / 10.0 vs 6.4 months; HR 0.66 / 0.68, relative); 14 drug-related deaths (2.1%)
cards.summary: MDX010-20 (Hodi 2010): ipilimumab — alone or with gp100 vaccine — improved survival versus gp100 alone in previously treated metastatic melanoma (median 10.1 / 10.0 vs 6.4 months; HR 0.66 / 0.68, relative); 14 drug-related deaths (2.1%)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (MDX010-20), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg ± gp100 vs gp100 alone, previously treated melanoma — slice 1 of this shelf
cards.people: 676 HLA-A*0201-positive patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma whose disease had progressed on therapy for metastatic disease, randomised 3:1:1 to ipilimumab 3 mg/kg plus gp100 (403), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg alone (137) or gp100 alone (136); ipilimumab given every 3 weeks for up to four induction doses. Primary endpoint: overall survival.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 10.0 months with ipilimumab plus gp100 versus 6.4 months with gp100 alone (hazard ratio for death 0.68; P<0.001) and 10.1 months with ipilimumab alone (hazard ratio 0.66; P=0.003) — both relative measures; the two ipilimumab groups did not differ from each other (hazard ratio 1.04). Grade 3 or 4 immune-related adverse events occurred in 10 to 15% of ipilimumab-treated patients versus 3% on gp100 alone. There were 14 deaths related to the study drugs (2.1%), 7 of them associated with immune-related adverse events.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is a peptide vaccine, not an active standard therapy, and the population was restricted to HLA-A*0201-positive patients. The 2.1% drug-related death rate is part of the founding fact of CTLA-4 blockade and is printed on the face of this shelf.
cards.source: Hodi FS et al. Improved survival with ipilimumab in patients with metastatic melanoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2010. PMID: 20525992. Registry ID: NCT00094653. cards.headline: Ipilimumab + dacarbazine (Robert 2011): at the higher 10 mg/kg dose, adding ipilimumab to dacarbazine improved survival first-line (median 11.2 vs 9.1 months; HR 0.72, relative; 3-year survival 20.8% vs 12.2%); grade 3–4 adverse events 56.3% vs 27.5%
cards.summary: Ipilimumab + dacarbazine (Robert 2011): at the higher 10 mg/kg dose, adding ipilimumab to dacarbazine improved survival first-line (median 11.2 vs 9.1 months; HR 0.72, relative; 3-year survival 20.8% vs 12.2%); grade 3–4 adverse events 56.3% vs 27.5%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial, ipilimumab 10 mg/kg + dacarbazine vs dacarbazine alone, previously untreated melanoma — slice 2 of this shelf (different dose and setting from MDX010-20; never pooled with it)
cards.people: 502 patients with previously untreated metastatic melanoma, randomised 1:1 to ipilimumab 10 mg/kg plus dacarbazine 850 mg/m² or dacarbazine plus placebo, with maintenance ipilimumab or placebo every 12 weeks in responders/stable patients. Primary endpoint: overall survival.
cards.result: Overall survival was longer with ipilimumab plus dacarbazine: median 11.2 versus 9.1 months (hazard ratio for death 0.72; P<0.001 — a relative measure), with survival rates at 1 year 47.3% vs 36.3%, at 2 years 28.5% vs 17.9% and at 3 years 20.8% vs 12.2%. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 56.3% versus 27.5% (P<0.001). No drug-related deaths or gastrointestinal perforations occurred in the ipilimumab–dacarbazine group; rates of elevated liver-function values were higher than in earlier ipilimumab studies.
cards.watchOut: A different dose (10 mg/kg) and a different setting (first-line, combined with dacarbazine) from MDX010-20's 3 mg/kg — the two randomised slices are labelled separately and must never be pooled into a single ipilimumab effect.
cards.source: Robert C et al. Ipilimumab plus dacarbazine for previously untreated metastatic melanoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2011. PMID: 21639810. Registry ID: NCT00324155. cards.headline: Pooled long-term survival analysis (Schadendorf 2015): across 1,861 ipilimumab-treated patients, median survival was 11.4 months and the survival curve plateaued from about year 3 (3-year survival 22%), with follow-up to 10 years — a within-treatment description, not a randomised contrast
cards.summary: Pooled long-term survival analysis (Schadendorf 2015): across 1,861 ipilimumab-treated patients, median survival was 11.4 months and the survival curve plateaued from about year 3 (3-year survival 22%), with follow-up to 10 years — a within-treatment description, not a randomised contrast
cards.type: Pooled analysis of long-term survival data from phase 2 and phase 3 ipilimumab studies — a within-treatment description, NOT a randomised comparison
cards.people: 1,861 patients from 10 prospective and 2 retrospective ipilimumab studies (including the two phase 3 trials carded above); 1,257 previously treated and 604 treatment-naïve; most received ipilimumab 3 mg/kg (965) or 10 mg/kg (706). A secondary analysis added 2,985 expanded-access patients (total 4,846).
cards.result: In the primary pooled analysis, median overall survival was 11.4 months (95% CI 10.7 to 12.1). The survival curve began to plateau around year 3, with follow-up of up to 10 years; 3-year survival rates were 22% overall, 26% in treatment-naïve patients and 20% in previously treated patients. Including the expanded-access programme, median overall survival was 9.5 months with a plateau at 21% beginning around year 3.
cards.watchOut: There is no comparator arm: the year-3 plateau describes what happened to ipilimumab-treated patients and must never be presented as a treatment effect. The randomised evidence on this shelf is the two trial cards above.

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — a PARTIAL shelf beside live #764, carding only the pembrolizumab monotherapy founding slice that #764 presupposes. KEYNOTE-006 (834 randomised, ipilimumab-naïve; three reports carded): pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg beat ipilimumab on progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.58, relative) and overall survival — hazard ratio 0.68 for both schedules at the final analysis (24-month survival 55% / 55% vs 43%), and at 5 years median survival 32.7 versus 15.9 months (hazard ratio 0.73, relative) — with less grade 3–5 toxicity than ipilimumab. KEYNOTE-002 (540 randomised, ipilimumab-refractory; separate slice): pembrolizumab improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (hazard ratios 0.57 and 0.50, relative) — a PFS claim, not a survival claim. KEYNOTE-006's dose (10 mg/kg) was above the later standard, and its comparator is the ipilimumab of shelf #7644.

cards.headline: KEYNOTE-006 primary report (Robert 2015): pembrolizumab beat ipilimumab on progression-free and overall survival — 6-month PFS 47.3% / 46.4% vs 26.5% (HR 0.58, relative); 12-month survival 74.1% / 68.4% vs 58.2%; less grade 3–5 toxicity than ipilimumab
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-006 primary report (Robert 2015): pembrolizumab beat ipilimumab on progression-free and overall survival — 6-month PFS 47.3% / 46.4% vs 26.5% (HR 0.58, relative); 12-month survival 74.1% / 68.4% vs 58.2%; less grade 3–5 toxicity than ipilimumab
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (KEYNOTE-006), primary report — report 1 of 3 KEYNOTE-006 reports on this shelf
cards.people: 834 patients with advanced (ipilimumab-naïve) melanoma randomised 1:1:1 to pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks, pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks, or four doses of ipilimumab 3 mg/kg. Primary endpoints: progression-free and overall survival. Median follow-up 7.9 months at this report.
cards.result: Estimated 6-month progression-free survival was 47.3% (pembrolizumab every 2 weeks) and 46.4% (every 3 weeks) versus 26.5% on ipilimumab (hazard ratio for progression 0.58 for both schedules — a relative measure). Estimated 12-month survival was 74.1% and 68.4% versus 58.2% (hazard ratio for death 0.63 and 0.69, relative). Response rates were 33.7% and 32.9% versus 11.9%. Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events were less frequent on pembrolizumab (13.3% and 10.1%) than on ipilimumab (19.9%).
cards.watchOut: KEYNOTE-006 used pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg — a higher dose than the later standard dose — and this shelf says so on its face. The comparator is the ipilimumab of shelf #7644: the two shelves are the same comparison seen from two sides and are not independent confirmations of each other.
cards.source: Robert C et al. Pembrolizumab versus Ipilimumab in Advanced Melanoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2015. PMID: 25891173. Registry ID: NCT01866319. cards.headline: KEYNOTE-006 five-year results (Robert 2019): median survival 32.7 vs 15.9 months (HR 0.73, relative) and median PFS 8.4 vs 3.4 months (HR 0.57, relative) for combined pembrolizumab groups vs ipilimumab
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-006 five-year results (Robert 2019): median survival 32.7 vs 15.9 months (HR 0.73, relative) and median PFS 8.4 vs 3.4 months (HR 0.57, relative) for combined pembrolizumab groups vs ipilimumab
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (KEYNOTE-006), post-hoc 5-year follow-up — report 3 of 3 KEYNOTE-006 reports on this shelf (same trial; the combined-schedule analysis was exploratory)
cards.people: The same KEYNOTE-006 population (834 randomised; the two pembrolizumab groups combined in an exploratory, not protocol-specified, analysis), at median follow-up 57.7 months in surviving patients.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 32.7 months (95% CI 24.5 to 41.6) in the combined pembrolizumab groups versus 15.9 months (13.3 to 22.0) on ipilimumab (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.88 — a relative measure). Median progression-free survival was 8.4 versus 3.4 months (hazard ratio 0.57, relative). Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 17% of the combined pembrolizumab groups versus 20% on ipilimumab; one patient assigned to pembrolizumab died from treatment-related sepsis.
cards.watchOut: Post-hoc and exploratory: combining the two pembrolizumab schedules was not protocol-specified, and the hazard ratio attenuated from 0.68 (final analysis) to 0.73 at 5 years — the direction is unchanged, the size is a little smaller with maturity.
cards.source: Robert C et al. Pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma (KEYNOTE-006): post-hoc 5-year results from an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, phase 3 study. cards.headline: KEYNOTE-002 (Ribas 2015): in ipilimumab-refractory melanoma, pembrolizumab improved progression-free survival versus investigator-choice chemotherapy — HR 0.57 (2 mg/kg) and 0.50 (10 mg/kg), relative; 6-month PFS 34% / 38% vs 16%; grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events 11% / 14% vs 26%
cards.summary: KEYNOTE-002 (Ribas 2015): in ipilimumab-refractory melanoma, pembrolizumab improved progression-free survival versus investigator-choice chemotherapy — HR 0.57 (2 mg/kg) and 0.50 (10 mg/kg), relative; 6-month PFS 34% / 38% vs 16%; grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events 11% / 14% vs 26%
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised trial (KEYNOTE-002), pembrolizumab vs investigator-choice chemotherapy in ipilimumab-refractory melanoma — a different population and clinical moment from KEYNOTE-006; labelled as its own slice, never pooled with it
cards.people: 540 patients with melanoma that had progressed on ipilimumab (and, if BRAF V600-mutant, on a BRAF or MEK inhibitor), randomised 1:1:1 to pembrolizumab 2 mg/kg, pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg every 3 weeks, or investigator-choice chemotherapy. Primary endpoint at this analysis: progression-free survival.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was improved on pembrolizumab 2 mg/kg (hazard ratio 0.57, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.73) and 10 mg/kg (hazard ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.64) versus chemotherapy — both relative measures. Six-month progression-free survival was 34% and 38% versus 16% on chemotherapy — absolute differences of 18 and 22 percentage points. Treatment-related grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 11% and 14% versus 26% on chemotherapy.
cards.watchOut: KEYNOTE-002's demonstrated payload at its primary analysis is progression-free survival, not overall survival, and its population (progression after ipilimumab) is not KEYNOTE-006's ipilimumab-naïve population — the two slices answer different questions.
cards.source: Ribas A et al. Pembrolizumab versus investigator-choice chemotherapy for ipilimumab-refractory melanoma (KEYNOTE-002): a randomised, controlled, phase 2 trial. The Lancet. shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — a PARTIAL, single-programme shelf beside live #764: one trial (CheckMate 066, 418 randomised), three reports, all carded. Nivolumab improved overall survival versus dacarbazine in previously untreated BRAF wild-type metastatic melanoma at every time-point: 1-year survival 72.9% vs 42.1% (hazard ratio 0.42, relative), 3-year 51.2% vs 21.6% (median 37.5 vs 11.2 months; hazard ratio 0.46, relative), 5-year 39% vs 17%, with 5-year progression-free survival 28% vs 3% and no excess of grade 3–4 drug-related adverse events (11.7% vs 17.6% at the primary report). Live #764 cards nivolumab only in combination; the monotherapy founding question is asked nowhere else. The comparator was a weak standard, and the responder-durability figures are within-arm descriptions — both printed on the face.

cards.headline: CheckMate 066 primary report (Robert 2015): nivolumab improved survival versus dacarbazine in untreated BRAF wild-type melanoma — 1-year survival 72.9% vs 42.1% (HR for death 0.42, relative); median PFS 5.1 vs 2.2 months; response 40.0% vs 13.9%
cards.summary: CheckMate 066 primary report (Robert 2015): nivolumab improved survival versus dacarbazine in untreated BRAF wild-type melanoma — 1-year survival 72.9% vs 42.1% (HR for death 0.42, relative); median PFS 5.1 vs 2.2 months; response 40.0% vs 13.9%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (CheckMate 066), primary report — report 1 of 3 reports of this one trial on this shelf (single-programme shelf)
cards.people: 418 previously untreated patients with metastatic melanoma without a BRAF mutation, randomised to nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (with dacarbazine-matched placebo) or dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every 3 weeks (with nivolumab-matched placebo), double-blind. Primary endpoint: overall survival.
cards.result: At 1 year, overall survival was 72.9% (95% CI 65.5 to 78.9) on nivolumab versus 42.1% (33.0 to 50.9) on dacarbazine — an absolute difference of 30.8 percentage points (hazard ratio for death 0.42, 99.79% CI 0.25 to 0.73; P<0.001 — a relative measure). Median progression-free survival was 5.1 versus 2.2 months (hazard ratio 0.43, relative). The objective response rate was 40.0% versus 13.9%. Grade 3 or 4 drug-related adverse events occurred in 11.7% on nivolumab versus 17.6% on dacarbazine.
cards.watchOut: The dacarbazine comparator was already a weak standard when the trial ran; the size of the relative benefit is read against that base, and the absolute 1-year rates are printed beside the hazard ratio.
cards.source: Robert C et al. Nivolumab in previously untreated melanoma without BRAF mutation. The New England journal of medicine. 2015. PMID: 25399552. Registry ID: NCT01721772. phase 3 randomised double-blind trial (checkmate 066), primary report — report 1 of 3 reports of this one trial on this shelf (single-programme shelf) 418 previously untreated patients with metastatic melanoma without a braf mutation, randomised to nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (with dacarbazine-matched placebo) or dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every 3 weeks (with nivolumab-matched placebo), double-blind. primary endpoint: overall survival. at 1 year, overall survival was 72.9% (95% ci 65.5 to 78.9) on nivolumab versus 42.1% (33.0 to 50.9) on dacarbazine — an absolute difference of 30.8 percentage points (hazard ratio for death 0.42, 99.79% ci 0.25 to 0.73; p<0.001 — a relative measure). median progression-free survival was 5.1 versus 2.2 months (hazard ratio 0.43, relative). the objective response rate was 40.0% versus 13.9%. grade 3 or 4 drug-related adverse events occurred in 11.7% on nivolumab versus 17.6% on dacarbazine. the dacarbazine comparator was already a weak standard when the trial ran; the size of the relative benefit is read against that base, and the absolute 1-year rates are printed beside the hazard ratio. robert c et al. nivolumab in previously untreated melanoma without braf mutation. the new england journal of medicine. 2015. pmid: 25399552. registry id: nct01721772. mesh: adolescent · adult · aged · aged, 80 and over · antibodies, monoclonal/administration & dosage/adverse effects · antineoplastic agents/administration & dosage/adverse effects · dacarbazine/administration & dosage/adverse effects · disease-free survival · double-blind method · female · humans · male · melanoma/drug therapy/genetics/mortality/secondary · middle aged · nivolumab · programmed cell death 1 receptor/antagonists & inhibitors · proto-oncogene proteins b-raf/genetics · survival rate · young adult

cards.headline: CheckMate 066 three-year follow-up (Ascierto 2019): 3-year survival 51.2% vs 21.6%; median survival 37.5 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.46, relative); complete responses 19.0% vs 1.4%
cards.summary: CheckMate 066 three-year follow-up (Ascierto 2019): 3-year survival 51.2% vs 21.6%; median survival 37.5 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.46, relative); complete responses 19.0% vs 1.4%
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial (CheckMate 066), 3-year follow-up analysis — report 2 of 3 reports of this one trial
cards.people: The same CheckMate 066 population as the primary report above (210 nivolumab, 208 dacarbazine) at minimum follow-up of about 38 months — a later analysis of the same trial, not a second trial.
cards.result: Three-year overall survival was 51.2% (95% CI 44.1% to 57.9%) on nivolumab versus 21.6% (16.1% to 27.6%) on dacarbazine. Median overall survival was 37.5 months versus 11.2 months (hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.59 — a relative measure). Complete responses were reported in 19.0% (40 of 210) on nivolumab versus 1.4% (3 of 208) on dacarbazine, and partial responses in 23.8% versus 13.0%. Treatment-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 15.0% versus 17.6%; there were no deaths due to study-drug toxicity.
cards.watchOut: A follow-up analysis of the one trial: it extends the primary result in time and adds no independent randomised evidence.
cards.source: Ascierto PA et al. Survival Outcomes in Patients With Previously Untreated BRAF Wild-Type Advanced Melanoma Treated With Nivolumab Therapy: Three-Year Follow-up of a Randomized Phase 3 Trial. JAMA oncology. 2019. cards.headline: CheckMate 066 five-year outcomes (Robert 2020): 5-year survival 39% vs 17% and 5-year PFS 28% vs 3%; of 42 nivolumab complete responders, 88% were alive at 5 years, and 83% of evaluable nivolumab patients alive at 5 years had received no subsequent therapy
cards.summary: CheckMate 066 five-year outcomes (Robert 2020): 5-year survival 39% vs 17% and 5-year PFS 28% vs 3%; of 42 nivolumab complete responders, 88% were alive at 5 years, and 83% of evaluable nivolumab patients alive at 5 years had received no subsequent therapy
cards.type: Randomised phase 3 trial (CheckMate 066), 5-year outcomes — report 3 of 3 reports of this one trial
cards.people: The same CheckMate 066 population (418 randomised), followed for a minimum of 60 months from the last patient randomised (median follow-up 32.0 months on nivolumab and 10.9 months on dacarbazine, as published).
cards.result: Five-year overall survival was 39% on nivolumab versus 17% on dacarbazine, and 5-year progression-free survival 28% versus 3%. The objective response rate was 42% versus 14%. Of the 42 nivolumab patients (20%) who had a complete response, 88% (37 of 42) were alive at the 5-year analysis. Among 75 nivolumab-treated patients alive and evaluable at 5 years, 83% had received no subsequent therapy; 23% were still on study treatment and 60% were treatment-free. Five-year survival in the dacarbazine group was 38% among the 37 patients who had subsequent therapy including nivolumab — a within-arm description of a selected subgroup.
cards.watchOut: The treatment-free and complete-responder figures are within-arm descriptions of responders and survivors, not randomised contrasts — they describe durability among those who did well, and the dacarbazine arm's later survival was itself shaped by subsequent therapy including nivolumab.
cards.source: Robert C et al. Five-Year Outcomes With Nivolumab in Patients With Wild-Type BRAF Advanced Melanoma. shelves.question: In patients with metastatic melanoma harbouring a BRAF V600 mutation, does vemurafenib improve overall and progression-free survival versus dacarbazine in previously untreated disease (BRIM-3) — and what responses does it produce after prior therapy (BRIM-2, single-arm)?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — a PARTIAL shelf beside live #1902. Live #1902 (combined BRAF + MEK inhibition versus BRAF inhibition alone, COMBI-d/v) presupposes the founding vemurafenib benefit but cards neither BRIM-3 nor BRIM-2; this shelf cards only that slice. BRIM-3 (675 randomised, untreated BRAF V600E disease; two reports): 6-month survival 84% vs 64% on dacarbazine, with a 63% relative reduction in the risk of death and a 74% relative reduction in the risk of death or progression at the interim analysis — both relative figures, labelled as such — and at extended follow-up median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative) with median PFS 6.9 vs 1.6 months. BRIM-2 (132 patients, single-arm, previously treated): response 53%, median PFS 6.8 months — response evidence only. The distinctive harm is drug-induced cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma (19% grade 3–4 in BRIM-3; 26% in BRIM-2), and resistance is rapid.

cards.headline: BRIM-3 primary report (Chapman 2011): vemurafenib improved survival versus dacarbazine in untreated BRAF V600E melanoma — 6-month survival 84% vs 64%; a 63% relative reduction in the risk of death and a 74% relative reduction in the risk of death or progression; response 48% vs 5%
cards.summary: BRIM-3 primary report (Chapman 2011): vemurafenib improved survival versus dacarbazine in untreated BRAF V600E melanoma — 6-month survival 84% vs 64%; a 63% relative reduction in the risk of death and a 74% relative reduction in the risk of death or progression; response 48% vs 5%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (BRIM-3), primary report — report 1 of 2 BRIM-3 reports on this shelf
cards.people: 675 patients with previously untreated metastatic melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation, randomised to vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily or dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every 3 weeks. Co-primary endpoints: overall and progression-free survival rates; the printed analysis is the interim overall-survival analysis (after 98 deaths) with the final progression-free-survival analysis.
cards.result: At 6 months, overall survival was 84% (95% CI 78 to 89) on vemurafenib versus 64% (56 to 73) on dacarbazine — an absolute difference of 20 percentage points. Vemurafenib was associated with a 63% relative reduction in the risk of death and a 74% relative reduction in the risk of either death or disease progression (both P<0.001), as printed in the record — both figures are relative reductions, not absolute ones. Response rates were 48% versus 5%. After the interim analysis, crossover from dacarbazine to vemurafenib was recommended. Common vemurafenib adverse events included arthralgia, rash, fatigue, alopecia, keratoacanthoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, photosensitivity, nausea and diarrhoea; 38% of patients required dose modification for toxicity.
cards.watchOut: The headline 63% and 74% figures are relative reductions from an interim analysis, printed as such under the standing relative-risk wording standard; the absolute 6-month survival rates (84% vs 64%) stand beside them. Crossover after the interim analysis dilutes later overall-survival contrasts.
cards.source: Chapman PB et al. Improved survival with vemurafenib in melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation. The New England journal of medicine. 2011. PMID: 21639808. Registry ID: NCT01006980. cards.headline: BRIM-3 extended follow-up (McArthur 2014): median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months overall (HR 0.70, relative) and 13.3 vs 10.0 months in BRAF V600E disease (HR 0.75, relative); median PFS 6.9 vs 1.6 months; grade 3–4 cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in 19% and keratoacanthoma in 10% on vemurafenib
cards.summary: BRIM-3 extended follow-up (McArthur 2014): median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months overall (HR 0.70, relative) and 13.3 vs 10.0 months in BRAF V600E disease (HR 0.75, relative); median PFS 6.9 vs 1.6 months; grade 3–4 cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in 19% and keratoacanthoma in 10% on vemurafenib
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial (BRIM-3), extended follow-up — report 2 of 2 BRIM-3 reports on this shelf (same trial as the primary report)
cards.people: The same BRIM-3 population as the primary report above (337 vemurafenib, 338 dacarbazine), at median follow-up 12.5 months on vemurafenib and 9.5 months on dacarbazine, with data censored at crossover; 83 of 338 dacarbazine patients (25%) had crossed over to vemurafenib. Subgroups: 598 patients with BRAF V600E disease and 57 with BRAF V600K disease.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 13.6 months on vemurafenib versus 9.7 months on dacarbazine (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.87 — a relative measure), and median progression-free survival 6.9 versus 1.6 months (hazard ratio 0.38, relative). In BRAF V600E disease, median overall survival was 13.3 versus 10.0 months (hazard ratio 0.75, relative) and median progression-free survival 6.9 versus 1.6 months (hazard ratio 0.39, relative). In the small BRAF V600K subgroup (57 patients), median overall survival was 14.5 versus 7.6 months (hazard ratio 0.43, relative). The most frequent grade 3–4 events on vemurafenib were cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma (65 of 337, 19%), abnormal liver function tests (11%), keratoacanthomas (34, 10%) and rash (9%); grade 5 events occurred in 2% in each group.
cards.watchOut: The V600K subgroup is only 57 patients — its hazard ratio 0.43 is imprecise and is labelled with its size. A quarter of the dacarbazine arm crossed over, so the censored-at-crossover analysis is the cleaner contrast and later survival is attenuated.
cards.source: McArthur GA et al. Safety and efficacy of vemurafenib in BRAF(V600E) and BRAF(V600K) mutation-positive melanoma (BRIM-3): extended follow-up of a phase 3, randomised, open-label study. The Lancet. Oncology. 2014. PMID: 24508103. Registry ID: NCT01006980. cards.summary: BRIM-2 (Sosman 2012): single-arm vemurafenib after prior therapy — confirmed response 53%, median duration of response 6.7 months, median PFS 6.8 months, median survival 15.9 months; cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in 26%
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial (BRIM-2), vemurafenib in previously treated BRAF V600-mutant melanoma — response evidence only; no randomised contrast
cards.people: 132 patients with previously treated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma treated with vemurafenib in a multicentre phase 2 trial with no comparator arm; median follow-up 12.9 months. Primary endpoint: overall response rate by independent review.
cards.result: The confirmed overall response rate was 53% (95% CI 44 to 62; 6% complete and 47% partial responses), the median duration of response was 6.7 months, median progression-free survival was 6.8 months, and median overall survival was 15.9 months. Primary progression was observed in only 14% of patients. The most common adverse events were grade 1 or 2 arthralgia, rash, photosensitivity, fatigue and alopecia; cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas (the majority keratoacanthoma type) were diagnosed in 26% of patients.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: the response rate is a within-treatment figure and the 15.9-month median survival has no comparator — neither may be read as a survival benefit. The randomised survival evidence on this shelf is BRIM-3 alone.
cards.source: Sosman JA et al. Survival in BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma treated with vemurafenib. The New England journal of medicine. 2012. PMID: 22356324. Registry ID: NCT00949702. cards.headline: Synthesis: vemurafenib founded BRAF inhibition — a large relative survival benefit over dacarbazine in BRIM-3 (interim 63% relative reduction in the risk of death; extended median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months) with responses in about half of patients (BRIM-3 48%; BRIM-2 53%) — but median progression-free survival under 7 months and drug-induced cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in about a fifth to a quarter of patients
cards.summary: Synthesis: vemurafenib founded BRAF inhibition — a large relative survival benefit over dacarbazine in BRIM-3 (interim 63% relative reduction in the risk of death; extended median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months) with responses in about half of patients (BRIM-3 48%; BRIM-2 53%) — but median progression-free survival under 7 months and drug-induced cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in about a fifth to a quarter of patients
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: BRIM-3 (675 randomised, two reports) and BRIM-2 (132 patients, single-arm).
cards.result: BRIM-3: 6-month survival 84% vs 64% at the interim analysis, with a 63% relative reduction in the risk of death and a 74% relative reduction in the risk of death or progression (relative figures, labelled as such); at extended follow-up, median survival 13.6 vs 9.7 months (hazard ratio 0.70, relative) and median PFS 6.9 vs 1.6 months. BRIM-2 (single-arm, previously treated): response 53%, median PFS 6.8 months. Harm: cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma in 19% (grade 3–4, BRIM-3) to 26% (any grade, BRIM-2), keratoacanthoma in 10%, and dose modification for toxicity in 38% at the primary report. PARTIAL beside live shelf #1902 (combined BRAF + MEK inhibition versus BRAF inhibition alone — COMBI-d/v and coBRIM), which presupposes this founding vemurafenib benefit without carding BRIM-3 or BRIM-2.
cards.watchOut: Resistance is rapid (median PFS under 7 months in both trials) — the founding benefit is real but short-lived for most patients, which is the context in which the combination shelf #1902 and modern immunotherapy-first sequencing sit.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Ramucirumab + docetaxel vs docetaxel, second-line stage IV NSCLC (REVEL): survival 10.5 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.86) — a 1.4-month median gain
shelves.question: In patients with stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer progressing during or after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, does adding ramucirumab 10 mg/kg to docetaxel improve overall survival (REVEL)?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — small in absolute terms, on a single-programme base: one trial (REVEL, 1,253 randomised), three reports, all carded. Adding ramucirumab 10 mg/kg to docetaxel improved overall survival second-line in stage IV NSCLC (median 10.5 vs 9.1 months; hazard ratio 0.86, a relative measure — the absolute difference in medians is 1.4 months, printed as prominently as the hazard ratio) and progression-free survival (median 4.5 vs 3.0 months; hazard ratio 0.76, relative), at the cost of more grade 3-or-worse neutropenia (49% vs 40%), febrile neutropenia (16% vs 10%) and hypertension (6% vs 2%). The prespecified age analysis found the benefit clear under 65 (hazard ratio 0.74) and not evident at 65 or older after adjustment (0.96, CI spanning 1) while establishing no true age interaction; the exposure–response report is exploratory pharmacology and implies no dosing recommendation.

cards.headline: REVEL primary report (Garon 2014): ramucirumab + docetaxel improved survival second-line in stage IV NSCLC — median 10.5 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.86, relative), an absolute median gain of 1.4 months; median PFS 4.5 vs 3.0 months; more neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and hypertension
cards.summary: REVEL primary report (Garon 2014): ramucirumab + docetaxel improved survival second-line in stage IV NSCLC — median 10.5 vs 9.1 months (HR 0.86, relative), an absolute median gain of 1.4 months; median PFS 4.5 vs 3.0 months; more neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and hypertension
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre double-blind randomised trial (REVEL), primary report — report 1 of 3 reports of this one trial on this shelf (single-programme shelf)
cards.people: 1,253 patients with squamous or non-squamous stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer progressing during or after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, randomised 1:1 to docetaxel 75 mg/m² plus ramucirumab 10 mg/kg (628) or placebo (625) every 21 days. Primary endpoint: overall survival.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 10.5 months on ramucirumab plus docetaxel versus 9.1 months on placebo plus docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.98; P=0.023 — a relative measure; the absolute difference in medians is 1.4 months). Median progression-free survival was 4.5 versus 3.0 months (hazard ratio 0.76, relative; P<0.0001). The most common grade 3-or-worse adverse events were neutropenia (49% vs 40%), febrile neutropenia (16% vs 10%), fatigue (14% vs 10%), leucopenia (14% vs 12%) and hypertension (6% vs 2%). Deaths from adverse events (5% vs 6%) and grade 3-or-worse pulmonary haemorrhage (1% vs 1%) did not differ between groups.
cards.watchOut: A statistically significant but small absolute benefit: the 1.4-month difference in median survival is printed as prominently as the hazard ratio 0.86, per this row's commissioning note.
cards.source: Garon EB et al. Ramucirumab plus docetaxel versus placebo plus docetaxel for second-line treatment of stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer after disease progression on platinum-based therapy (REVEL): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised phase 3 trial. Lancet (London, England). 2014. PMID: 24933332. Registry ID: NCT01168973. cards.headline: REVEL age-subgroup analysis (Ramalingam 2018): the benefit was clear under 65 (OS HR 0.74, PFS HR 0.68, relative) and not evident at 65 or older after adjustment (OS HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.21; PFS HR 0.87, relative) — the authors state a true age difference in treatment effect was not established
cards.summary: REVEL age-subgroup analysis (Ramalingam 2018): the benefit was clear under 65 (OS HR 0.74, PFS HR 0.68, relative) and not evident at 65 or older after adjustment (OS HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.21; PFS HR 0.87, relative) — the authors state a true age difference in treatment effect was not established
cards.type: Prespecified age-subgroup analysis of the REVEL randomised trial (65-year cutoff) — report 2 of 3 reports of this one trial
cards.people: The same REVEL population (1,253 randomised), split at the prespecified 65-year cutoff: 798 patients under 65 (391 ramucirumab, 407 control) and 455 aged 65 or older (237 ramucirumab, 218 control), with a further quintiles-of-age analysis. A subgroup analysis of the one trial, not a second trial.
cards.result: In patients under 65, ramucirumab treatment gave favourable overall survival (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.87) and progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.79) — both relative measures. In patients 65 or older, benefits were not as evident: after model adjustment for prognostic factors, the overall-survival hazard ratio was 0.96 (95% CI 0.77 to 1.21) and the progression-free-survival hazard ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.05) — both intervals span no effect, as published. The quintiles analysis showed hazard ratios favouring ramucirumab in all age groupings. Lung Cancer Symptom Scale scores and adverse events did not considerably differ between age groups, and the authors concluded that true treatment-effect differences on the basis of age have not been established and treatment should not be deterred solely because of age.
cards.watchOut: Subgroup evidence: the older-patient estimates are model-adjusted, their confidence intervals span 1, and the report itself declines to claim an age interaction — no card on this shelf may present ramucirumab as ineffective at 65 or older.
cards.source: Ramalingam SS et al. Efficacy and Safety of Ramucirumab With Docetaxel Versus Placebo With Docetaxel as Second-Line Treatment of Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Subgroup Analysis According to Patient Age in the REVEL Trial. Clinical lung cancer. 2018. PMID: 29373274. Registry ID: NCT01168973. cards.headline: REVEL exposure–response analysis (Smit 2018): higher predicted first-dose ramucirumab concentration was associated with greater survival improvement after prognostic adjustment (OS association P=0.0110) — exploratory pharmacology, not a dosing recommendation
cards.summary: REVEL exposure–response analysis (Smit 2018): higher predicted first-dose ramucirumab concentration was associated with greater survival improvement after prognostic adjustment (OS association P=0.0110) — exploratory pharmacology, not a dosing recommendation
cards.type: Exploratory exposure–response (pharmacokinetic) analysis of the REVEL trial — report 3 of 3 reports of this one trial; hypothesis-generating, never load-bearing for the efficacy claim
cards.people: 376 ramucirumab-treated and 366 placebo-treated REVEL patients in the pharmacokinetic analysis set (364 placebo patients in the safety population) — an exploratory analysis of the one trial's data, using population-pharmacokinetic predictions of minimum concentration after the first dose (Cmin,1) and average steady-state concentration.
cards.result: After adjusting for prognostic factors, the association between overall survival and predicted Cmin,1 was statistically significant (P=0.0110), while the progression-free-survival association was marginal (P=0.0515); at higher Cmin,1 exposures, greater improvements (smaller hazard ratios) were seen for both outcomes across exposure quartiles. A statistically significant correlation was also observed between average steady-state concentration and grade 3-or-worse febrile neutropenia and hypertension. The authors note two prospective randomised exposure–response trials were being conducted to address causation.
cards.watchOut: An association between achieved exposure and outcome inside one arm's data cannot separate drug effect from patient differences that drive both exposure and prognosis — it must not be used to imply a dosing recommendation.
cards.source: Smit EF et al. Exposure-response relationship for ramucirumab from the randomized, double-blind, phase 3 REVEL trial (docetaxel versus docetaxel plus ramucirumab) in second-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Cancer chemotherapy and pharmacology. 2018. PMID: 29721850. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — REVEL showed a real but small survival gain from adding ramucirumab to docetaxel second-line (median 10.5 vs 9.1 months; HR 0.86), clearest under 65 in a subgroup analysis that establishes no age interaction, with an exploratory exposure–response association that is pharmacology, not dosing guidance
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — REVEL showed a real but small survival gain from adding ramucirumab to docetaxel second-line (median 10.5 vs 9.1 months; HR 0.86), clearest under 65 in a subgroup analysis that establishes no age interaction, with an exploratory exposure–response association that is pharmacology, not dosing guidance
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: one trial (REVEL, 1,253 randomised), three reports — a single-programme shelf, labelled as such.
cards.result: Overall survival: median 10.5 vs 9.1 months (hazard ratio 0.86, relative; absolute median difference 1.4 months); progression-free survival: median 4.5 vs 3.0 months (hazard ratio 0.76, relative). Added harm: grade 3-or-worse neutropenia 49% vs 40%, febrile neutropenia 16% vs 10%, hypertension 6% vs 2%, with no difference in deaths from adverse events. Age subgroup (prespecified 65-year cutoff): hazard ratios 0.74 (under 65) and 0.96 adjusted (65 or older, CI spanning 1) — no established age interaction. Exposure–response: higher first-dose concentration associated with better survival (P=0.0110), exploratory only. Ramucirumab's gastric/GEJ and hepatocellular questions are homed elsewhere; this shelf asks only the NSCLC question.
cards.watchOut: A single trial carries the claim; its two companion reports are a subgroup analysis and an exploratory pharmacologic analysis of the same data, and neither adds independent randomised evidence.

shelves.question: In transplant-ineligible patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma after one or more prior lines, does glofitamab plus gemcitabine–oxaliplatin (Glofit-GemOx) improve overall survival versus rituximab plus GemOx?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Deoxycytidine · Male · Female · Rituximab · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Lymphoma, Large B-Cell, Diffuse · Gemcitabine · Aged · Middle Aged · Oxaliplatin · Adult · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local · Organoplatinum Compounds
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) — PARTIAL beside pack #6413, which cards CD20×CD3 bispecifics including glofitamab MONOTHERAPY in DLBCL after at least two lines; this shelf cards only the distinct randomised question #6413 does not ask: glofitamab plus GemOx versus rituximab-GemOx in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL after one or more lines. The base is ONE trial (STARGLO, 274 randomised) in three reports, labelled a single-programme shelf. The survival payload is consistent across three cut-offs, every hazard ratio a relative measure printed beside its absolute medians: primary analysis HR 0.59 (median OS not estimable vs 9.0 months); updated analysis HR 0.62 (25.5 vs 12.9 months); 3-year follow-up HR 0.60 (25.5 vs 12.5 months), with median PFS 14.4 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.41, relative) and complete response 58.5% vs 25.3%. The pricing harm is cytokine release syndrome in 44% of glofitamab-exposed patients, predominantly low grade, with treatment-related deaths 3% vs 1%. The patient-reported-outcomes report is supportive only — never load-bearing for the survival claim. Open-label trial (response endpoints were assessed by a masked independent review committee).

cards.type: Global phase 3 randomised open-label trial (STARGLO, primary and updated analyses), Glofit-GemOx vs R-GemOx
cards.people: 274 transplant-ineligible patients (183 Glofit-GemOx, 91 R-GemOx; median age 68 years; 58% men) with relapsed or refractory DLBCL after one or more previous therapies, randomised 2:1 at 62 centres in 13 countries. Glofit-GemOx: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² plus glofitamab step-up dosing to 30 mg for eight cycles, then four further glofitamab cycles; R-GemOx: the same chemotherapy plus rituximab 375 mg/m² for eight cycles. Primary endpoint overall survival; response endpoints assessed by a masked independent review committee.
cards.result: At the primary analysis (median follow-up 11.3 months), overall survival was significantly improved with Glofit-GemOx (median not estimable [95% CI 13.8 months–not estimable] vs 9.0 months [7.3–14.4]; hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.89; P=0.011 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). At the updated analysis (median follow-up 20.7 months) median OS was 25.5 months (18.3–not estimable) vs 12.9 months (7.9–18.5) (HR 0.62, 0.43 to 0.88). At least one adverse event occurred in 180 of 180 (100%) Glofit-GemOx patients and 84 of 88 (96%) R-GemOx patients; cytokine release syndrome occurred in 76 of 172 glofitamab-exposed patients (44%), predominantly low grade; deaths related to glofitamab or rituximab occurred in 5 patients (3%) vs 1 (1%).
cards.watchOut: Open-label (patients and investigators unmasked; response endpoints were committee-masked). One trial — the two further cards are reports of this same trial, not independent confirmation.

cards.headline: STARGLO 3-year follow-up (Abramson 2026): the survival benefit held — median OS 25.5 vs 12.5 months (HR 0.60, relative), median PFS 14.4 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.41, relative), complete response 58.5% vs 25.3%; no new safety signals
cards.summary: STARGLO 3-year follow-up (Abramson 2026): the survival benefit held — median OS 25.5 vs 12.5 months (HR 0.60, relative), median PFS 14.4 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.41, relative), complete response 58.5% vs 25.3%; no new safety signals
cards.type: Three-year follow-up report of the STARGLO randomised trial (same trial as the primary card — not a second trial)
cards.people: The same STARGLO trial as the card above (274 randomised; transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL), reported at a median overall-survival follow-up of 35.1 months (data cutoff 1 May 2025), including clinically relevant subgroups.
cards.result: Median OS remained 25.5 vs 12.5 months (hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.4 to 0.8 — a relative measure); median progression-free survival was 14.4 vs 3.3 months (HR 0.41, 0.3 to 0.6); complete response rate was 58.5% vs 25.3%. Benefit was more pronounced in the second-line than the third-line-or-later setting (3-year OS 54.6% vs 33.2% within the glofitamab arm's settings as reported) and was consistent across age categories including patients aged 75 or older. No new safety signals were identified.
cards.watchOut: A follow-up report of the one STARGLO trial: it extends the same evidence, it does not replicate it. Subgroup readings (line of therapy, age) are descriptive.

cards.headline: STARGLO patient-reported outcomes (Gregory 2026): nominal delays in time to deterioration for physical functioning, fatigue and lymphoma symptoms on Glofit-GemOx, with earlier clinically meaningful pain and lymphoma-symptom improvement — a supportive report, never load-bearing for the survival claim
cards.summary: STARGLO patient-reported outcomes (Gregory 2026): nominal delays in time to deterioration for physical functioning, fatigue and lymphoma symptoms on Glofit-GemOx, with earlier clinically meaningful pain and lymphoma-symptom improvement — a supportive report, never load-bearing for the survival claim
cards.type: Patient-reported-outcomes report of the STARGLO randomised trial (same trial as the cards above — supportive only)
cards.people: The same STARGLO population (274 patients; 183 Glofit-GemOx, 91 R-GemOx), assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30 and the FACT-Lymphoma subscale throughout treatment and follow-up; questionnaire response rates were 100% at baseline and over 90% on treatment.
cards.result: Baseline scores indicated moderate-to-high functioning and low-to-moderate symptom severity. Glofit-GemOx showed nominal delays in median time to deterioration versus R-GemOx for physical functioning (9.1 vs 8.2 months), fatigue (1.7 vs 1.4 months) and lymphoma symptoms (6.2 vs 4.5 months), and patients achieved clinically meaningful improvements in pain and lymphoma symptoms earlier (by cycle 3); at end of treatment, pain improvements were maintained on Glofit-GemOx while R-GemOx scores returned to baseline.
cards.watchOut: The time-to-deterioration differences are described by the authors as nominal and are small in absolute months; this report supports tolerability and symptom readings only and carries no survival information.
cards.source: Gregory GP et al. Patient-reported Outcomes in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma Treated With Glofitamab Plus Gemcitabine and Oxaliplatin in STARGLO. shelves.question: In patients with advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer, does crizotinib improve progression-free survival versus standard chemotherapy — as first-line treatment (PROFILE 1014) and after one prior platinum regimen (PROFILE 1007)?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival only) — PARTIAL beside live #1833 (first-line alectinib versus crizotinib), where crizotinib is the presupposed comparator; this shelf cards only the founding crizotinib-versus-chemotherapy question #1833 does not ask. Two trials, three reports, labelled by line of therapy and never pooled. FIRST-LINE (PROFILE 1014, 343 randomised): median PFS 10.9 vs 7.0 months (HR 0.45, relative) and response 74% vs 45%, but the final overall-survival analysis was NOT significant on intention-to-treat (HR 0.760, 95% CI 0.548 to 1.053; P=.098; 4-year survival 56.6% vs 49.1%) after 84.2% of the chemotherapy arm crossed over to crizotinib; the crossover-adjusted RPSFT estimate (HR 0.346) is a model and is never the headline. SECOND-LINE (PROFILE 1007, 347 patients after one prior platinum regimen): median PFS 7.7 vs 3.0 months (HR 0.49, relative), response 65% vs 20%, interim overall-survival HR 1.02 — no survival benefit shown. This is a PFS/response founding story whose survival analyses were diluted by near-universal crossover; both the ITT null and the modelled adjustment are printed. Crizotinib's common harms were vision disorders, gastrointestinal effects and raised liver aminotransferases.

cards.headline: PROFILE 1014 primary (Solomon 2014), first-line: crizotinib beat chemotherapy on PFS (median 10.9 vs 7.0 months; HR 0.45, relative) and response (74% vs 45%); overall survival not significant at primary analysis (HR 0.82; 1-year survival 84% vs 79%)
cards.summary: PROFILE 1014 primary (Solomon 2014), first-line: crizotinib beat chemotherapy on PFS (median 10.9 vs 7.0 months; HR 0.45, relative) and response (74% vs 45%); overall survival not significant at primary analysis (HR 0.82; 1-year survival 84% vs 79%)
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (PROFILE 1014, primary report), first-line crizotinib vs pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy
cards.people: 343 patients with previously untreated advanced ALK-positive nonsquamous NSCLC, randomised open-label to oral crizotinib 250 mg twice daily or intravenous pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin every 3 weeks for up to six cycles; crossover to crizotinib after progression was permitted for the chemotherapy group. Primary endpoint progression-free survival by independent radiological review.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly longer with crizotinib (median 10.9 vs 7.0 months; hazard ratio for progression or death 0.45, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.60; P<0.001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). Objective response rates were 74% versus 45% (P<0.001). Median overall survival was not reached in either group (HR for death 0.82, 0.54 to 1.26; P=0.36); 1-year survival probability was 84% versus 79%. The most common adverse events with crizotinib were vision disorders, diarrhoea, nausea and oedema; with chemotherapy, nausea, fatigue, vomiting and decreased appetite. Crizotinib gave greater symptom reduction and quality-of-life improvement.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and crossover after progression was built into the design — every overall-survival reading of this trial, including the final analysis carded next, is read against 84.2% crossover.
cards.source: Solomon BJ et al. First-line crizotinib versus chemotherapy in ALK-positive lung cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2014. PMID: 25470694. Registry ID: NCT01154140.
