cards.headline: PROFILE 1014 final overall survival (Solomon 2018): OS hazard ratio 0.760 was NOT significant on intention-to-treat (P=.098; 4-year survival 56.6% vs 49.1%) after 84.2% of the chemotherapy arm received crizotinib; the crossover-adjusted HR 0.346 is a model, labelled as such
cards.summary: PROFILE 1014 final overall survival (Solomon 2018): OS hazard ratio 0.760 was NOT significant on intention-to-treat (P=.098; 4-year survival 56.6% vs 49.1%) after 84.2% of the chemotherapy arm received crizotinib; the crossover-adjusted HR 0.346 is a model, labelled as such
cards.type: Final overall-survival analysis of the PROFILE 1014 randomised trial (same trial as the primary card — not a second trial)
cards.people: The same PROFILE 1014 trial as the card above (172 crizotinib, 171 chemotherapy), reported at a median overall-survival follow-up of approximately 46 months in both arms; 144 chemotherapy-arm patients (84.2%) received crizotinib in subsequent lines. A prespecified rank-preserving structural failure time (RPSFT) model was used to adjust for crossover.
cards.result: The hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.760 (95% CI 0.548 to 1.053; two-sided P=.0978) — not significant. Median OS was not reached with crizotinib (95% CI 45.8 months to not reached) and was 47.5 months with chemotherapy (32.2 to not reached); 4-year survival probability was 56.6% (48.3 to 64.1) versus 49.1% (40.5 to 57.1). After crossover adjustment by the RPSFT model, the estimate favoured crizotinib (HR 0.346; 95% bootstrap CI 0.081 to 0.718) — a modelled estimate, printed as such and never as the headline. The longest survival was seen in crizotinib patients who later received another ALK inhibitor. No new safety signals were identified.
cards.watchOut: The ITT null and the modelled adjustment must both be read: near-universal crossover (84.2%) makes the ITT comparison a comparison of treatment sequences, and the RPSFT figure depends on modelling assumptions — neither alone is 'the' survival answer.

cards.headline: PROFILE 1007 primary (Shaw 2013), second-line after one platinum regimen: crizotinib beat chemotherapy on PFS (median 7.7 vs 3.0 months; HR 0.49, relative) and response (65% vs 20%); interim overall survival HR 1.02 — no survival benefit shown
cards.summary: PROFILE 1007 primary (Shaw 2013), second-line after one platinum regimen: crizotinib beat chemotherapy on PFS (median 7.7 vs 3.0 months; HR 0.49, relative) and response (65% vs 20%); interim overall survival HR 1.02 — no survival benefit shown
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised trial (PROFILE 1007, primary report), second-line crizotinib vs pemetrexed or docetaxel
cards.people: 347 patients with locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive lung cancer who had received one prior platinum-based regimen, randomised open-label to oral crizotinib 250 mg twice daily or intravenous pemetrexed 500 mg/m² or docetaxel 75 mg/m² every 3 weeks; chemotherapy patients could cross over to crizotinib on progression as part of a separate study. Primary endpoint progression-free survival.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 7.7 months on crizotinib versus 3.0 months on chemotherapy (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.49, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.64; P<0.001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). Response rates were 65% (58 to 72) versus 20% (14 to 26) (P<0.001). An interim overall-survival analysis showed no significant improvement (HR for death 1.02, 0.68 to 1.54; P=0.54). Common crizotinib adverse events were visual disorder, gastrointestinal effects and elevated liver aminotransferases; chemotherapy's were fatigue, alopecia and dyspnoea. Patients reported greater symptom reduction and quality-of-life improvement with crizotinib.
cards.watchOut: A different line of therapy from PROFILE 1014 — the two trials are labelled slices and are never pooled. Its survival reading is an interim analysis with crossover permitted; the PFS/response benefit is the finding.
cards.source: Shaw AT et al. Crizotinib versus chemotherapy in advanced ALK-positive lung cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2013. PMID: 23724913. Registry ID: NCT00932893. shelves.question: In treatment-naïve or cytokine-pretreated patients with locally advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma, does pazopanib 800 mg daily improve progression-free survival versus placebo?

shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival only) — one trial (VEG105192, 435 randomised 2:1), three reports, labelled a single-programme shelf. Pazopanib 800 mg daily clearly prolonged progression-free survival versus placebo: median 9.2 vs 4.2 months overall (HR 0.46, relative), 11.1 vs 2.8 months in treatment-naïve patients (HR 0.40, relative) and 7.4 vs 4.2 months after cytokines (HR 0.54, relative), with objective response 30% vs 3% and no clinically important quality-of-life difference. The final overall-survival analysis was NOT significant (22.9 vs 20.5 months; HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.16), confounded by early, frequent crossover of placebo patients to pazopanib; the crossover-adjusted IPCW estimate (HR 0.504) is a post-hoc model and is never the headline — the OS null is printed as prominently as the PFS hazard ratio. The open-label extension (80 ex-placebo patients crossing to pazopanib; response 37.5%, median PFS 9.2 months) is a single-arm rollover report, labelled, never load-bearing. Common pazopanib adverse events were diarrhoea, hypertension, hair colour changes, nausea, anorexia and vomiting.

cards.headline: VEG105192 primary (Sternberg 2010): pazopanib prolonged PFS versus placebo — median 9.2 vs 4.2 months overall (HR 0.46, relative), 11.1 vs 2.8 months treatment-naïve (HR 0.40) and 7.4 vs 4.2 months after cytokines (HR 0.54); response 30% vs 3%
cards.summary: VEG105192 primary (Sternberg 2010): pazopanib prolonged PFS versus placebo — median 9.2 vs 4.2 months overall (HR 0.46, relative), 11.1 vs 2.8 months treatment-naïve (HR 0.40) and 7.4 vs 4.2 months after cytokines (HR 0.54); response 30% vs 3%
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (VEG105192, primary report), pazopanib vs placebo
cards.people: 435 adults with measurable locally advanced and/or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma (233 treatment-naïve, 54%; 202 cytokine-pretreated, 46%), randomised 2:1 double-blind to oral pazopanib 800 mg daily or placebo; primary endpoint progression-free survival, with radiographic assessments independently reviewed.
cards.result: Progression-free survival was significantly prolonged with pazopanib in the overall population (median 9.2 vs 4.2 months; hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.62; P<.0001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians), in treatment-naïve patients (11.1 vs 2.8 months; HR 0.40, 0.27 to 0.60) and in cytokine-pretreated patients (7.4 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.54, 0.35 to 0.84). The objective response rate was 30% versus 3% (P<.001) and median duration of response exceeded 1 year. The most common adverse events were diarrhoea, hypertension, hair colour changes, nausea, anorexia and vomiting. There was no evidence of clinically important quality-of-life differences.
cards.watchOut: A PFS trial: at this report overall survival was immature, and the final analysis (carded next) was not significant. The naïve and cytokine-pretreated limbs are subgroups of the one randomised population, labelled as such.

cards.headline: VEG105192 final overall survival (Sternberg 2013): OS 22.9 vs 20.5 months was NOT significant (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.16) under early, frequent crossover; the crossover-adjusted IPCW estimate (HR 0.504) is a post-hoc model, labelled as such
cards.summary: VEG105192 final overall survival (Sternberg 2013): OS 22.9 vs 20.5 months was NOT significant (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.16) under early, frequent crossover; the crossover-adjusted IPCW estimate (HR 0.504) is a post-hoc model, labelled as such
cards.type: Final overall-survival and safety report of the VEG105192 randomised trial (same trial as the primary card — not a second trial)
cards.people: The same VEG105192 trial as the card above (435 randomised 2:1, pazopanib 800 mg daily or placebo, treated until progression, death or unacceptable toxicity); on progression, placebo patients could receive pazopanib through an open-label study. Final OS was analysed intention-to-treat; rank-preserving structural failure time (RPSFT) and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) analyses were performed post hoc to adjust for crossover.
cards.result: Final overall survival did not differ significantly (22.9 vs 20.5 months; hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.16; one-sided P=.224). Early and frequent crossover from placebo to pazopanib, with prolonged crossover treatment, confounded the analysis. In the post-hoc IPCW analysis pazopanib was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.504, 0.315 to 0.762; two-sided P=.002) — a modelled estimate, printed as such; the RPSFT analysis was similar in direction but not significant (HR 0.43, 0.215 to 1.388; P=.172). Cumulative pazopanib exposure had risen 30% since the previous cutoff, with no new safety signals.
cards.watchOut: The ITT null and the post-hoc models must both be read: crossover makes the ITT comparison a comparison of sequences, and the IPCW/RPSFT figures rest on modelling assumptions made after the data were seen.

cards.headline: Open-label extension VEG107769 (Sternberg 2014): 80 patients (79 ex-placebo) crossed to pazopanib after progression — response 37.5%, median PFS 9.2 months, median OS 23.5 months (a single-arm rollover report, labelled, never load-bearing)
cards.summary: Open-label extension VEG107769 (Sternberg 2014): 80 patients (79 ex-placebo) crossed to pazopanib after progression — response 37.5%, median PFS 9.2 months, median OS 23.5 months (a single-arm rollover report, labelled, never load-bearing)
cards.type: Single-arm open-label extension study (VEG107769) of the VEG105192 programme — a rollover report, not a randomised comparison
cards.people: 80 patients from VEG105192 who had experienced disease progression — 79 previously on placebo and 1 previously on pazopanib (an exemption) — enrolled in the single-arm open-label extension (41 treatment-naïve, 39 cytokine-pretreated) and treated with pazopanib 800 mg/day; primary endpoint safety and tolerability; median exposure 9.7 months; all patients had discontinued by the analysis, 61% for disease progression.
cards.result: The most common adverse events were hypertension (45%), diarrhoea (45%), hair colour changes (44%), anorexia (30%) and nausea (25%). The response rate was 37.5% (95% CI 26.9 to 48.1), median progression-free survival 9.2 months (7.3 to 12.0) and median overall survival 23.5 months (16.3 to 28.0) — readings consistent with the pazopanib arm of the parent trial, in a population selected by surviving to cross over.
cards.watchOut: No comparator and a survivor-selected population: this report can describe what happened after crossover, never what pazopanib adds. It is carded only to complete the one-trial programme record.

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: VEG105192 is the VEGF-era placebo-controlled founding trial for pazopanib in advanced renal-cell carcinoma, completing the library's RCC founding set. Its honest summary is a PFS-only win on the ITT survival analysis: the adjusted survival estimates (IPCW HR 0.504; RPSFT HR 0.43, not significant) are post-hoc models, and the extension study is a single-arm rollover. Pazopanib's other questions — the COMPARZ head-to-head, soft-tissue sarcoma, and the adjuvant neighbourhood — keep their own homes and are not folded in.

shelves.title: BREAK-3: dabrafenib beat dacarbazine on PFS in BRAF V600E melanoma (5.1 vs 2.7 months; HR 0.30, relative) — 5-year survival converged (24% vs 22%) after crossover; PARTIAL beside live #1902
shelves.question: In patients with previously untreated unresectable or metastatic BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma, does dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily improve progression-free survival versus dacarbazine?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Agents, Alkylating · Dacarbazine · Disease-Free Survival · Female · Humans · Imidazoles · Male · Melanoma · Middle Aged · Mutation · Oximes · Proto-Oncogene Proteins B-raf · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit, progression-free survival only) — PARTIAL beside live #1902 (combined BRAF+MEK inhibition versus BRAF inhibition alone), which presupposes the founding dabrafenib benefit; this shelf cards only that founding monotherapy question. One randomised trial (BREAK-3, 250 randomised 3:1) plus its long-term pooled follow-up and quality-of-life report, labelled a single-programme shelf. The founding payload is PFS and symptom control, not survival: median PFS 5.1 vs 2.7 months on dacarbazine (HR 0.30, a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians), while at 5 years PFS was 12% on dabrafenib and overall survival had CONVERGED — 24% vs 22% — after 59% of the dacarbazine arm crossed over to dabrafenib and both arms received subsequent immunotherapy. Quality of life was maintained or improved on dabrafenib while deteriorating on dacarbazine. Grade 2-or-worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 53% vs 44%, with skin toxicities and fever predominating on dabrafenib; grade 3–4 events were uncommon in both groups. The long-term report pools BREAK-3 with the single-arm BREAK-2 study — BREAK-2 contributes follow-up data only, never a contrast.

cards.headline: BREAK-3 primary (Hauschild 2012): dabrafenib improved PFS versus dacarbazine — median 5.1 vs 2.7 months (HR 0.30, relative); grade ≥2 treatment-related adverse events 53% vs 44%, skin toxicities and fever predominating on dabrafenib
cards.summary: BREAK-3 primary (Hauschild 2012): dabrafenib improved PFS versus dacarbazine — median 5.1 vs 2.7 months (HR 0.30, relative); grade ≥2 treatment-related adverse events 53% vs 44%, skin toxicities and fever predominating on dabrafenib
cards.type: Multicentre open-label phase 3 randomised trial (BREAK-3, primary report), dabrafenib vs dacarbazine
cards.people: 250 patients with previously untreated, unresectable stage III or stage IV BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma (733 screened), randomised 3:1 open-label to oral dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily (187 patients) or intravenous dacarbazine 1000 mg/m² every 3 weeks (63 patients), stratified by AJCC stage; primary endpoint investigator-assessed progression-free survival, analysed intention-to-treat; data cutoff 19 December 2011.
cards.result: Median progression-free survival was 5.1 months on dabrafenib versus 2.7 months on dacarbazine (hazard ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.51; P<0.0001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). At cutoff, 107 of 187 dabrafenib patients (57%) and 14 of 63 dacarbazine patients (22%) remained on randomised treatment. Treatment-related adverse events of grade 2 or higher occurred in 100 of 187 dabrafenib patients (53%) and 26 of 59 treated dacarbazine patients (44%); the most common on dabrafenib were skin-related toxic effects, fever, fatigue, arthralgia and headache, and on dacarbazine nausea, vomiting, neutropenia, fatigue and asthenia. Grade 3–4 adverse events were uncommon in both groups.
cards.watchOut: Open-label with investigator-assessed PFS, an early data cutoff, and a 3:1 allocation leaving only 63 control patients — and no survival claim: the long-term card below shows 5-year survival converging after crossover.
cards.source: Hauschild A et al. Dabrafenib in BRAF-mutated metastatic melanoma: a multicentre, open-label, phase 3 randomised controlled trial. Lancet (London, England). 2012. PMID: 22735384. Registry ID: NCT01227889. cards.headline: Long-term pooled BREAK-2/BREAK-3 analysis (Hauschild 2020): in BREAK-3, 5-year PFS was 12% on dabrafenib (all dacarbazine patients had progressed or been censored; 59% had crossed over) and 5-year overall survival CONVERGED at 24% vs 22%
cards.summary: Long-term pooled BREAK-2/BREAK-3 analysis (Hauschild 2020): in BREAK-3, 5-year PFS was 12% on dabrafenib (all dacarbazine patients had progressed or been censored; 59% had crossed over) and 5-year overall survival CONVERGED at 24% vs 22%
cards.type: Long-term (5-year) outcomes analysis pooling BREAK-3 (randomised) with BREAK-2 (single-arm) — follow-up report of the card above, not a second randomised trial
cards.people: Pooled long-term follow-up of BREAK-3 (the randomised trial carded above: 187 dabrafenib, 63 dacarbazine; median follow-up 17.0 and 12.0 months in the two arms at this analysis) and BREAK-2 (a single-arm phase 2 study of dabrafenib in 92 patients with BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma, contributing follow-up data only, never a contrast). Thirty-seven dacarbazine patients (59%) crossed over to dabrafenib after progression, per protocol.
cards.result: In BREAK-3, 5-year progression-free survival was 12% in the dabrafenib arm; all dacarbazine-arm patients had progressed or been censored by 5 years. Five-year overall survival was 24% on dabrafenib versus 22% on dacarbazine — converged, after 59% crossover and subsequent therapy in both arms including anti-CTLA-4 (24% in each arm) and/or anti-PD-1 treatment (8% and 2%). Dabrafenib improved PFS regardless of baseline lactate dehydrogenase. In single-arm BREAK-2 (V600E, n=76), 5-year PFS was 11% and OS 20%, with subsequent immunotherapy in 22%. No new safety signals were observed.
cards.watchOut: The survival convergence (24% vs 22%) is the load-bearing long-term reading and belongs beside the HR 0.30 headline. BREAK-2 is single-arm: its numbers describe dabrafenib-treated patients only and support no comparison.
cards.source: Hauschild A et al. Long-term outcomes in patients with BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma receiving dabrafenib monotherapy: Analysis from phase 2 and 3 clinical trials. European journal of cancer (Oxford, England : 1990). 2020. PMID: 31864178. Registry ID: NCT01227889. cards.headline: BREAK-3 quality-of-life analysis (Grob 2014): functioning was maintained or improved on dabrafenib while deteriorating on dacarbazine, with mixed-model differences favouring dabrafenib across several symptom scales — a supportive report, labelled as such
cards.summary: BREAK-3 quality-of-life analysis (Grob 2014): functioning was maintained or improved on dabrafenib while deteriorating on dacarbazine, with mixed-model differences favouring dabrafenib across several symptom scales — a supportive report, labelled as such
cards.type: Quality-of-life analysis of the BREAK-3 randomised trial (same trial as the primary card — supportive only)
cards.people: The BREAK-3 population carded above (250 randomised), assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30 at baseline and follow-up visits, including 35 patients assessed again after crossing over from dacarbazine to dabrafenib on progression.
cards.result: On dacarbazine, all functional dimensions except role functioning worsened from baseline at follow-up; on dabrafenib, all functionality dimensions remained stable or improved at week 6, and mean change in seven symptom dimensions improved, most for appetite loss, insomnia, nausea and vomiting, and pain. Mixed-model repeated-measures analyses showed significant (P<0.05) and/or clinically meaningful improvements favouring dabrafenib for emotional and social functioning, nausea and vomiting, appetite loss, diarrhoea, fatigue, dyspnoea and insomnia at weeks 6 and/or 12. After crossover to dabrafenib (n=35), improvements in all quality-of-life dimensions were evident after 6–12 weeks on dabrafenib.
cards.watchOut: An open-label trial's patient-reported outcomes are exposed to expectation effects, and the crossover subset (n=35, shrinking to 25) is self-selected by progression and survival — supportive context for the PFS finding, never independent evidence.
cards.source: Grob JJ et al. Patient perception of the benefit of a BRAF inhibitor in metastatic melanoma: quality-of-life analyses of the BREAK-3 study comparing dabrafenib with dacarbazine. Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology. 2014. PMID: 24769640. Registry ID: NCT01227889. cards.result: BREAK-3 established dabrafenib monotherapy as superior to dacarbazine on progression-free survival and quality of life in untreated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic melanoma, with durable benefit to 5 years in a subset (5-year PFS 12%). It did not establish a survival advantage: 5-year OS was 24% vs 22% after most control patients crossed over and both arms received later immunotherapy. This shelf is PARTIAL beside live #1902 (combined BRAF+MEK versus BRAF inhibition alone) and distinct from adjuvant dabrafenib–trametinib, a different setting with its own home.

shelves.title: Founding Hodgkin chemotherapy: ABVD displaced MOPP on toxicity at equal efficacy; BEACOPP's first-progression edge over ABVD (85% vs 73%) faded after planned salvage (OS 89% vs 84%, NS) — eras never pooled
shelves.question: In patients with advanced Hodgkin lymphoma, how do the founding regimens compare — ABVD versus MOPP and MOPP/ABV-hybrid therapy (CALGB; Intergroup), and intensified BEACOPP versus COPP-ABVD and versus ABVD with planned high-dose salvage (HD9; Viviani)?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Bleomycin · Dacarbazine · Doxorubicin · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Hodgkin Disease · Humans · Male · Mechlorethamine · Middle Aged · Prednisone · Procarbazine · Remission Induction · Vinblastine · Vincristine
shelves.balance: SPLIT (by comparison and era) — four founding trials, four reports, labelled slices that are NEVER pooled, because the two eras teach opposite lessons. MOPP-ERA slice: ABVD displaced MOPP on toxicity at equal-or-better efficacy. CALGB (361 patients): complete responses 67% on MOPP vs 82% on ABVD vs 83% on MOPP alternating with ABVD (P=0.006), 5-year failure-free survival 50% vs 61% vs 65%, 5-year overall survival 66% vs 73% vs 75% (P=0.28 — not significant), with more severe marrow toxicity on MOPP. Intergroup (856 patients): ABVD versus the MOPP/ABV hybrid showed NO efficacy difference (complete remission 76% vs 80%; 5-year failure-free survival 63% vs 66%; 5-year OS 82% vs 81%) but more acute toxicity and significantly more MDS/leukaemia with the MOPP-containing hybrid (13 vs 2 in the attributable sequence; P=.011) — on which the report concludes ABVD should be the standard. BEACOPP-ERA slice: intensification bought first-progression control at higher toxicity, and its survival meaning depends on the comparator and on salvage. HD9 (1,195 evaluable): escalated BEACOPP beat COPP-ABVD on 5-year freedom from treatment failure (87% vs 69%) and 5-year OS (91% vs 83%; P=0.002). Viviani (331 patients, both arms with planned high-dose salvage): 7-year freedom from FIRST progression favoured BEACOPP (85% vs 73%; P=0.004), but after the full planned strategy including salvage, freedom from second progression (88% vs 82%; P=0.12) and overall survival (89% vs 84%; P=0.39) were NOT significantly different, with more severe adverse events on BEACOPP.

cards.headline: CALGB trial (Canellos 1992), MOPP-era: ABVD and MOPP alternating with ABVD beat MOPP alone on complete response (82% and 83% vs 67%; P=0.006) and 5-year failure-free survival (61% and 65% vs 50%); 5-year overall survival did not differ significantly (73% and 75% vs 66%; P=0.28), and MOPP was more myelotoxic
cards.summary: CALGB trial (Canellos 1992), MOPP-era: ABVD and MOPP alternating with ABVD beat MOPP alone on complete response (82% and 83% vs 67%; P=0.006) and 5-year failure-free survival (61% and 65% vs 50%); 5-year overall survival did not differ significantly (73% and 75% vs 66%; P=0.28), and MOPP was more myelotoxic
cards.type: Multicentre randomised trial (CALGB), MOPP vs ABVD vs MOPP alternating with ABVD, advanced Hodgkin's disease
cards.people: 361 eligible patients with newly diagnosed advanced Hodgkin's disease (stages IIIA2, IIIB, IVA or IVB; patients in first relapse after radiotherapy were eligible), randomised to MOPP alone for 6–8 cycles (123 patients), ABVD alone for 6–8 cycles (115), or MOPP alternating with ABVD for 12 cycles (123); no additional radiotherapy; non-responders and relapses on MOPP or ABVD alone were switched to the opposite regimen.
cards.result: The overall response rate was 93%, with complete responses in 77%: 67% on MOPP, 82% on ABVD and 83% on MOPP-ABVD (P=0.006 for MOPP versus the two doxorubicin-containing regimens). Five-year failure-free survival was 50% (MOPP), 61% (ABVD) and 65% (MOPP-ABVD); age, stage and regimen significantly influenced failure-free survival. Five-year overall survival was 66%, 73% and 75% respectively (P=0.28 — not significant). MOPP had more severe toxic effects on bone marrow than ABVD, with greater reductions in the prescribed dose. The authors concluded ABVD for 6–8 months was as effective as 12 months of alternating therapy, and both were superior to MOPP alone.
cards.watchOut: A 1992 trial from the MOPP era — its survival comparison is diluted by design, since patients failing MOPP or ABVD alone were switched to the opposite regimen. Its lesson is response/failure-free survival plus myelotoxicity, not a survival difference.
cards.source: Canellos GP et al. Chemotherapy of advanced Hodgkin's disease with MOPP, ABVD, or MOPP alternating with ABVD. The New England journal of medicine. 1992. PMID: 1383821. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Intergroup trial (Duggan 2003), MOPP-era: ABVD and MOPP/ABV hybrid were EQUALLY effective (complete remission 76% vs 80%; 5-year failure-free survival 63% vs 66%; 5-year OS 82% vs 81%) — ABVD became standard on toxicity: more acute toxicity and significantly more MDS/leukaemia with the hybrid (P=.011)
cards.summary: Intergroup trial (Duggan 2003), MOPP-era: ABVD and MOPP/ABV hybrid were EQUALLY effective (complete remission 76% vs 80%; 5-year failure-free survival 63% vs 66%; 5-year OS 82% vs 81%) — ABVD became standard on toxicity: more acute toxicity and significantly more MDS/leukaemia with the hybrid (P=.011)
cards.type: Intergroup randomised trial, ABVD vs MOPP/ABV hybrid, advanced Hodgkin's disease
cards.people: 856 adults with advanced Hodgkin's disease randomised to ABVD or to the MOPP/ABV hybrid (mechlorethamine, vincristine, procarbazine, prednisone, doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine) as initial chemotherapy; major endpoints failure-free and overall survival, life-threatening acute toxicities, and serious long-term toxicities including cardiomyopathy, pulmonary toxicity, myelodysplastic syndromes and secondary malignancies.
cards.result: Complete remission (76% vs 80%; P=.16), 5-year failure-free survival (63% vs 66%; P=.42) and 5-year overall survival (82% vs 81%; P=.82) were similar for ABVD and MOPP/ABV. Clinically significant acute pulmonary and haematological toxicity were more common with MOPP/ABV (P=.060 and .001); cardiac toxicity did not differ. Treatment-attributed deaths numbered 9 on ABVD and 15 on MOPP/ABV (P=.057), and second malignancies 18 versus 28 (P=.13). Thirteen patients developed MDS or acute leukaemia — 11 initially treated with MOPP/ABV and 2 initially treated with ABVD who later received MOPP-containing regimens and radiotherapy (P=.011). The authors concluded ABVD should be considered the standard regimen.
cards.watchOut: The decisive comparison of the MOPP era precisely because efficacy was equal: the standard changed on late harm (MDS/leukaemia), which needs the long follow-up this report provides. Never read it as an ABVD efficacy win.

cards.headline: HD9 (Diehl 2003), BEACOPP-era: escalated BEACOPP beat COPP-ABVD on 5-year freedom from treatment failure (87% vs 69%) AND 5-year overall survival (91% vs 83%; P=0.002); baseline BEACOPP was intermediate (76% and 88%)
cards.summary: HD9 (Diehl 2003), BEACOPP-era: escalated BEACOPP beat COPP-ABVD on 5-year freedom from treatment failure (87% vs 69%) AND 5-year overall survival (91% vs 83%; P=0.002); baseline BEACOPP was intermediate (76% and 88%)
cards.type: Randomised trial (HD9, German Hodgkin Study Group), COPP-ABVD vs baseline BEACOPP vs escalated BEACOPP, advanced Hodgkin's disease
cards.people: 1,195 evaluable patients (of 1,201 eligible, aged 15–65) with newly diagnosed Hodgkin's disease in unfavourable stage IIB or IIIA, or stage IIIB or IV, randomised 1993–1998 to eight cycles of COPP-ABVD (260 patients), baseline BEACOPP (469) or increased-dose (escalated) BEACOPP (466), each followed by local radiotherapy when indicated; median follow-up 72, 54 and 51 months respectively. Enrolment in the COPP-ABVD group was stopped in 1996 owing to inferior results.
cards.result: Five-year freedom from treatment failure was 69% on COPP-ABVD, 76% on baseline BEACOPP and 87% on escalated BEACOPP (P=0.04 for COPP-ABVD vs baseline BEACOPP; P<0.001 for escalated BEACOPP vs each other group). Five-year overall survival was 83%, 88% and 91% respectively (P=0.16 for COPP-ABVD vs baseline BEACOPP; P=0.06 for baseline vs escalated BEACOPP; P=0.002 for COPP-ABVD vs escalated BEACOPP). Rates of early progression were significantly lower with escalated BEACOPP. The authors concluded increased-dose BEACOPP gave better tumour control and overall survival than COPP-ABVD.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is COPP-ABVD — a COPP-containing ABVD-family regimen, not modern ABVD alone — and the COPP-ABVD arm was stopped early for inferiority. HD9 does not by itself answer BEACOPP versus ABVD; that is the Viviani card, whose answer differs once salvage is counted.
cards.source: Diehl V et al. Standard and increased-dose BEACOPP chemotherapy compared with COPP-ABVD for advanced Hodgkin's disease. The New England journal of medicine. 2003. PMID: 12802024. cards.headline: Viviani trial (Viviani 2011), BEACOPP-era: BEACOPP beat ABVD on freedom from FIRST progression at 7 years (85% vs 73%; P=0.004), but after the full planned strategy including high-dose salvage, freedom from second progression (88% vs 82%; P=0.12) and overall survival (89% vs 84%; P=0.39) were NOT significantly different — with more severe adverse events on BEACOPP
cards.summary: Viviani trial (Viviani 2011), BEACOPP-era: BEACOPP beat ABVD on freedom from FIRST progression at 7 years (85% vs 73%; P=0.004), but after the full planned strategy including high-dose salvage, freedom from second progression (88% vs 82%; P=0.12) and overall survival (89% vs 84%; P=0.39) were NOT significantly different — with more severe adverse events on BEACOPP
cards.type: Randomised trial (Viviani / Fondazione Michelangelo), BEACOPP vs ABVD with planned high-dose salvage, unfavourable Hodgkin's lymphoma
cards.people: 331 patients with previously untreated unfavourable Hodgkin's lymphoma (stage IIB, III or IV, or an international prognostic score of 3 or more), randomised to BEACOPP or ABVD, each followed by local radiotherapy when indicated; patients with residual or progressive disease were to receive a state-of-the-art high-dose salvage programme (65 patients did: 20 BEACOPP, 45 ABVD). Median follow-up 61 months.
cards.result: Seven-year freedom from first progression was 85% on BEACOPP versus 73% on ABVD (P=0.004), and event-free survival 78% versus 71% (P=0.15). Of the patients who received the intended salvage, 3 of 20 (BEACOPP) and 15 of 45 (ABVD) were alive and free of disease at cutoff. After completion of the overall planned treatment including salvage, 7-year freedom from second progression was 88% versus 82% (P=0.12) and overall survival 89% versus 84% (P=0.39) — neither significant. Severe adverse events occurred more frequently on BEACOPP. The authors concluded BEACOPP gave better initial tumour control but the long-term clinical outcome did not differ significantly.
cards.watchOut: The trial compares two STRATEGIES (regimen plus planned salvage), not two regimens in isolation — 45 ABVD patients versus 20 BEACOPP patients needed salvage, which is itself part of BEACOPP's first-progression advantage. Read the first-progression and post-salvage readings together, never the first alone.
cards.source: Viviani S et al. ABVD versus BEACOPP for Hodgkin's lymphoma when high-dose salvage is planned. The New England journal of medicine. 2011. PMID: 21774708. Registry ID: NCT01251107. cards.headline: Synthesis: the founding Hodgkin record in two labelled eras — ABVD displaced MOPP on toxicity at equal efficacy (CALGB; Intergroup), while BEACOPP's first-progression advantage over ABVD-family therapy (HD9; Viviani) came at higher toxicity and, once planned salvage was counted in Viviani, without a significant survival difference
cards.summary: Synthesis: the founding Hodgkin record in two labelled eras — ABVD displaced MOPP on toxicity at equal efficacy (CALGB; Intergroup), while BEACOPP's first-progression advantage over ABVD-family therapy (HD9; Viviani) came at higher toxicity and, once planned salvage was counted in Viviani, without a significant survival difference
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: MOPP-era (361 + 856 patients): ABVD matched or beat MOPP-containing therapy on response and failure-free survival, with no significant overall-survival difference in either trial, and won its standard status on marrow toxicity (CALGB) and on MDS/leukaemia and acute toxicity (Intergroup). BEACOPP-era (1,195 + 331 patients): escalated BEACOPP improved tumour control and, against COPP-ABVD in HD9, overall survival (91% vs 83%); against ABVD itself with planned salvage (Viviani), the advantage narrowed to first progression only (85% vs 73%), with second progression and survival not significantly different and more severe adverse events. The eras and regimens are labelled throughout and never pooled. Later Hodgkin questions — brentuximab-AVD (whose backbone is ABVD minus bleomycin), relapsed-disease PD-1 therapy, frontline nivolumab combinations — presuppose these comparisons and keep their own homes.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Tisagenlecleucel in relapsed/refractory B-cell malignancies: single-arm remission 81% in B-ALL (ELIANA), response 52% in DLBCL (JULIET), complete response 69.1% in follicular lymphoma (ELARA) — but the randomised second-line trial (BELINDA) was null
shelves.question: In children and young adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, and in adults with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell or follicular lymphoma after standard therapy, what remission and response rates does a single infusion of tisagenlecleucel achieve, at what toxicity — and what happened when it was tested head-to-head against standard care in second-line aggressive B-cell lymphoma?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Antigens, CD19 · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Child · Child, Preschool · Female · Humans · Infusions, Intravenous · Male · Precursor Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia-Lymphoma · Receptors, Antigen, T-Cell · Remission Induction · Survival Analysis · Young Adult
shelves.balance: SPLIT. The single-arm pivotal cohorts report high remission/response rates in heavily pretreated patients (ELIANA 81% remission in B-ALL; JULIET 52% response in DLBCL; ELARA 69.1% complete response in follicular lymphoma), priced with substantial cytokine-release and neurologic toxicity — but none has a concurrent control. The programme's one randomised trial, BELINDA (second-line, n=322), found tisagenlecleucel NOT superior to standard care (median event-free survival 3.0 months in both groups; hazard ratio 1.07, P=0.61). Indication limbs are labelled and never pooled. Sibling CAR-T products are packed at #7025–#7027 (and axicabtagene at #4479) — cross-points only, never re-carded here.

cards.headline: ELIANA phase 2 (Maude 2018): 75 infused children/young adults with relapsed/refractory B-ALL — overall remission 81% within 3 months, all responders MRD-negative; event-free survival 50% and overall survival 76% at 12 months; cytokine release syndrome in 77% and grade 3/4 suspected-related events in 73% (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.summary: ELIANA phase 2 (Maude 2018): 75 infused children/young adults with relapsed/refractory B-ALL — overall remission 81% within 3 months, all responders MRD-negative; event-free survival 50% and overall survival 76% at 12 months; cytokine release syndrome in 77% and grade 3/4 suspected-related events in 73% (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.type: Phase 2 single-cohort (single-arm) pivotal study (ELIANA), tisagenlecleucel in relapsed/refractory B-ALL
cards.people: 75 paediatric and young adult patients with CD19-positive relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia who received a single tisagenlecleucel infusion and could be evaluated for efficacy, in a 25-centre global single-cohort phase 2 study. Limb: B-ALL, third-line or later.
cards.result: The overall remission rate (complete remission or complete remission with incomplete haematologic recovery) within 3 months was 81%, and all responders were negative for minimal residual disease by flow cytometry. Event-free survival was 73% at 6 months and 50% at 12 months; overall survival was 90% at 6 months and 76% at 12 months; median duration of remission was not reached, and tisagenlecleucel persisted in blood for as long as 20 months. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events suspected to be related to tisagenlecleucel occurred in 73%; cytokine release syndrome in 77% (48% of those patients received tocilizumab); neurologic events in 40%, with no cerebral oedema reported.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: the 81% remission rate has no concurrent comparator and cannot be read as comparative efficacy. The toxicity is the pricing harm — CRS in over three quarters of patients and grade 3/4 related events in 73%.
cards.source: Maude SL et al. Tisagenlecleucel in Children and Young Adults with B-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia. The New England journal of medicine. 2018. PMID: 29385370. Registry ID: NCT02435849. cards.headline: JULIET phase 2 (Schuster 2019): 93 infused adults with relapsed/refractory DLBCL — best overall response 52% (complete response 40%); grade 3/4 cytokine release syndrome 22%, neurologic events 12%, cytopenias lasting >28 days 32% (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.summary: JULIET phase 2 (Schuster 2019): 93 infused adults with relapsed/refractory DLBCL — best overall response 52% (complete response 40%); grade 3/4 cytokine release syndrome 22%, neurologic events 12%, cytopenias lasting >28 days 32% (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm pivotal study (JULIET), tisagenlecleucel in relapsed/refractory DLBCL
cards.people: 93 adults with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, ineligible for or progressing after autologous stem-cell transplantation, who received centrally manufactured tisagenlecleucel and were evaluated for efficacy in an international phase 2 pivotal study; median follow-up from infusion 14 months. Limb: DLBCL, third-line or later.
cards.result: The best overall response rate was 52% (95% CI 41 to 62): complete response 40%, partial response 12%, consistent across prognostic subgroups. Estimated relapse-free survival at 12 months after response was 65% (79% among complete responders). The most common grade 3 or 4 adverse events of special interest were cytokine release syndrome (22%), neurologic events (12%), cytopenias lasting more than 28 days (32%), infections (20%) and febrile neutropenia (14%). Three patients died of disease progression within 30 days; no death was attributed to tisagenlecleucel, CRS or cerebral oedema.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm, in a population with a poor prognosis but no randomised comparator in this study: response rates describe what happened after infusion, not how much better tisagenlecleucel is than the alternatives — the randomised test of that question is BELINDA, carded below.
cards.source: Schuster SJ et al. Tisagenlecleucel in Adult Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2019. PMID: 30501490. Registry ID: NCT02445248. cards.headline: ELARA phase 2 (Fowler 2022): 94 patients in the efficacy set with relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma — complete response rate 69.1% and overall response rate 86.2%; cytokine release syndrome 48.5% with NO grade ≥3 cases, and no treatment-related deaths (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.summary: ELARA phase 2 (Fowler 2022): 94 patients in the efficacy set with relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma — complete response rate 69.1% and overall response rate 86.2%; cytokine release syndrome 48.5% with NO grade ≥3 cases, and no treatment-related deaths (single-arm — no concurrent control)
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial (ELARA), tisagenlecleucel in relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma — primary interim analysis
cards.people: 98 adults with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more treatment lines (or relapse after autologous transplant) were enrolled and 97 received tisagenlecleucel; the efficacy set was 94 patients, at median follow-up 16.59 months. Limb: follicular lymphoma, third-line or later. This is the prespecified primary interim analysis.
cards.result: The primary endpoint was met: complete response rate 69.1% (95% CI 58.8 to 78.3) and overall response rate 86.2% (95% CI 77.5 to 92.4). In the safety set (n=97), cytokine release syndrome occurred in 48.5% within 8 weeks of infusion, with no grade ≥3 cases; neurological events 37.1% (grade ≥3, 3%); immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome 4.1% (grade ≥3, 1%); no treatment-related deaths.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm interim analysis in an indolent lymphoma where disease tempo varies: high response rates without a comparator cannot separate drug effect from selection. Toxicity was milder here than in ELIANA/JULIET — the indication limbs differ and are never pooled.
cards.source: Fowler NH et al. Tisagenlecleucel in adult relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: the phase 2 ELARA trial. Nature medicine. 2022. PMID: 34921238. Registry ID: NCT03568461. cards.headline: BELINDA phase 3 RCT (Bishop 2022): the programme's one randomised trial — tisagenlecleucel was NOT superior to standard care in second-line aggressive B-cell lymphoma: median event-free survival 3.0 months in BOTH groups (hazard ratio 1.07, P=0.61, a relative measure); response 46.3% vs 42.5%
cards.summary: BELINDA phase 3 RCT (Bishop 2022): the programme's one randomised trial — tisagenlecleucel was NOT superior to standard care in second-line aggressive B-cell lymphoma: median event-free survival 3.0 months in BOTH groups (hazard ratio 1.07, P=0.61, a relative measure); response 46.3% vs 42.5%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (BELINDA), tisagenlecleucel vs standard care (salvage chemotherapy + autologous HSCT) in second-line aggressive B-cell lymphoma
cards.people: 322 patients with aggressive B-cell lymphoma refractory to, or progressing within 12 months after, first-line therapy, randomised to tisagenlecleucel (with optional bridging therapy; 95.7% received it; median leukapheresis-to-infusion time 52 days) or standard care (salvage chemotherapy and autologous HSCT; 32.5% received HSCT). Crossover to tisagenlecleucel was allowed after a defined event at or after week 12. Limb: second-line — a different, earlier setting than the three single-arm studies above.
cards.result: Median event-free survival was 3.0 months in both groups (hazard ratio for event or death 1.07, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.40, P=0.61 — a relative measure centred on no difference). A response occurred in 46.3% on tisagenlecleucel vs 42.5% on standard care. Lymphoma progression at week 6 occurred in 25.9% of the tisagenlecleucel group vs 13.8% of the standard-care group. Ten patients in the tisagenlecleucel group and 13 in the standard-care group died from adverse events. The authors concluded tisagenlecleucel was not superior to standard salvage therapy in this trial.
cards.watchOut: The discipline anchor for this shelf: when the programme was randomised, in second line, the single-arm impression did not reproduce. Baseline imbalances (more high-grade lymphoma and higher prognostic-index scores in the tisagenlecleucel group) and the 52-day vein-to-vein time are part of the record — but the primary result is null and is printed beside, never beneath, the single-arm rates.
cards.source: Bishop MR et al. Second-Line Tisagenlecleucel or Standard Care in Aggressive B-Cell Lymphoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2022. PMID: 34904798. Registry ID: NCT03570892. cards.headline: Synthesis: three single-arm pivotal cohorts across three indications (ELIANA B-ALL remission 81%; JULIET DLBCL response 52%; ELARA follicular-lymphoma complete response 69.1%) plus one randomised trial (BELINDA) that found tisagenlecleucel not superior to standard care in second line (event-free survival 3.0 months in both groups) — labelled slices, never pooled; sibling CAR-T products are homed at packs #7025–#7027 and are cross-points only, not re-carded here
cards.summary: Synthesis: three single-arm pivotal cohorts across three indications (ELIANA B-ALL remission 81%; JULIET DLBCL response 52%; ELARA follicular-lymphoma complete response 69.1%) plus one randomised trial (BELINDA) that found tisagenlecleucel not superior to standard care in second line (event-free survival 3.0 months in both groups) — labelled slices, never pooled; sibling CAR-T products are homed at packs #7025–#7027 and are cross-points only, not re-carded here
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf: ELIANA (75 infused), JULIET (93 infused), ELARA (94 in the efficacy set) and BELINDA (322 randomised).
cards.result: Response and remission rates from single-arm cohorts are not comparative efficacy. Cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity are the pricing harms and differ by indication (CRS 77% in ELIANA, grade 3/4 CRS 22% in JULIET, CRS 48.5% with no grade ≥3 in ELARA). BELINDA's null is the randomised contrast the single-arm record must be read against.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Enfortumab vedotin vs chemotherapy in previously treated advanced urothelial carcinoma (EV-301, one trial, N = 608): overall survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months (relative HR 0.70), maintained at 2 years — priced in skin reactions (47.3%) and neuropathy (48.0%)
shelves.question: In adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, does enfortumab vedotin monotherapy improve overall survival versus investigator-chosen chemotherapy — and does the benefit hold at 2 years, in the Japanese subgroup, and in patient-reported outcomes? (EV-301; four reports, ONE trial.)

shelves.balance: One phase 3 trial, four reports — labelled as such throughout, never pooled with the first-line combination question homed at live #859. EV-301 randomised 608 previously treated patients: enfortumab vedotin prolonged overall survival (median 12.88 vs 8.97 months; HR for death 0.70, a relative measure) and progression-free survival (5.55 vs 3.71 months; HR 0.62), and the benefit held at a median 23.75 months (HR 0.70, 0.58–0.85; 444 deaths). Quality of life was maintained, pain improved more and appetite loss worsened more than on chemotherapy, and the Japanese subgroup (N = 86, supportive only) was consistent. The trial was open-label and the comparator was single-agent docetaxel, paclitaxel or vinflunine — both facts print on the face. The pricing harms are skin reactions (treatment-related skin reactions in 47.3% vs 15.8%) and peripheral neuropathy (48.0% vs 31.6%), against cytopenias commoner on chemotherapy.

cards.headline: EV-301 primary (Powles 2021, phase 3, N = 608): enfortumab vedotin prolonged overall survival versus investigator-chosen chemotherapy — median 12.88 vs 8.97 months, hazard ratio for death 0.70 (95% CI 0.56–0.89, P = 0.001, a relative measure) — and progression-free survival 5.55 vs 3.71 months (HR 0.62, 0.51–0.75)
cards.summary: EV-301 primary (Powles 2021, phase 3, N = 608): enfortumab vedotin prolonged overall survival versus investigator-chosen chemotherapy — median 12.88 vs 8.97 months, hazard ratio for death 0.70 (95% CI 0.56–0.89, P = 0.001, a relative measure) — and progression-free survival 5.55 vs 3.71 months (HR 0.62, 0.51–0.75)
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised open-label trial — EV-301 primary report (ONE trial, four reports on this shelf)
cards.people: 608 adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor, randomised 1:1 to enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle (n = 301) or investigator-chosen docetaxel, paclitaxel or vinflunine on day 1 of a 21-day cycle (n = 307); global, open-label trial; median follow-up 11.1 months at the prespecified interim analysis, with 301 deaths (134 vs 167).
cards.result: Overall survival was longer on enfortumab vedotin (median 12.88 vs 8.97 months; HR for death 0.70, 95% CI 0.56–0.89, P = 0.001 — a relative measure, printed beside the absolute medians). Progression-free survival was also longer (5.55 vs 3.71 months; HR 0.62, 0.51–0.75). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 93.9% vs 91.8% and grade ≥3 events in 51.4% vs 49.8% — similar overall rates, with the event profile differing by drug (see the long-term card).
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial against single-agent taxane/vinflunine chemotherapy — not against a combination or a checkpoint inhibitor. This is the previously treated monotherapy question; it must not borrow the first-line enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (EV-302) effect size, which is homed at live shelf #859 and is cross-pointed in prose only on this shelf, never carded.
cards.source: Powles T et al. Enfortumab Vedotin in Previously Treated Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2021. PMID: 33577729. Registry ID: NCT03474107. cards.headline: EV-301 long-term outcomes (Rosenberg 2023, same trial, median follow-up 23.75 months): the survival benefit held — risk of death 30% relatively lower (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.58–0.85) and PFS HR 0.63 (0.53–0.76) — with treatment-related skin reactions in 47.3% vs 15.8% and peripheral neuropathy in 48.0% vs 31.6%
cards.summary: EV-301 long-term outcomes (Rosenberg 2023, same trial, median follow-up 23.75 months): the survival benefit held — risk of death 30% relatively lower (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.58–0.85) and PFS HR 0.63 (0.53–0.76) — with treatment-related skin reactions in 47.3% vs 15.8% and peripheral neuropathy in 48.0% vs 31.6%
cards.type: Phase 3 trial long-term / exploratory follow-up report — EV-301 (same trial as the primary card)
cards.people: The same 608 EV-301 patients (enfortumab vedotin n = 301, chemotherapy n = 307), now with 444 deaths (207 vs 237) at a median follow-up of 23.75 months; an exploratory long-term analysis of the one trial, not a second trial.
cards.result: Risk of death remained 30% relatively lower with enfortumab vedotin (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.58–0.85; one-sided log-rank P = 0.00015) and PFS improved (HR 0.63, 0.53–0.76). Grade ≥3 treatment-related events were 52.4% vs 50.5%: decreased neutrophil count (14.1% vs 6.1%), decreased white-cell count (7.2% vs 1.4%) and anaemia (7.9% vs 2.7%) were commoner on chemotherapy, while maculopapular rash (7.4% vs 0%), fatigue (6.8% vs 4.5%) and peripheral sensory neuropathy (5.1% vs 2.1%) were commoner on enfortumab vedotin. Treatment-related skin reactions occurred in 47.3% vs 15.8%, peripheral neuropathy in 48.0% vs 31.6% and hyperglycaemia in 6.8% vs 0.3%. No new safety signals were observed.
cards.watchOut: A follow-up report of the primary card's trial — never counted as independent confirmation. Skin toxicity (47.3% any treatment-related skin reaction) and neuropathy (48.0%) are the pricing harms of the survival benefit and belong beside it wherever the benefit is quoted.

cards.headline: EV-301 health-related quality of life (Rosenberg 2024, same trial): pain improved more on enfortumab vedotin (difference in change to week 12 −5.7, 95% CI −10.8 to −0.7, P = 0.027) while appetite loss worsened (+7.3, 0.90–13.69, P = 0.026); odds of confirmed improvement across ten QLQ-C30 scales were 1.67–2.76 times higher on enfortumab vedotin
cards.summary: EV-301 health-related quality of life (Rosenberg 2024, same trial): pain improved more on enfortumab vedotin (difference in change to week 12 −5.7, 95% CI −10.8 to −0.7, P = 0.027) while appetite loss worsened (+7.3, 0.90–13.69, P = 0.026); odds of confirmed improvement across ten QLQ-C30 scales were 1.67–2.76 times higher on enfortumab vedotin
cards.type: Phase 3 trial patient-reported-outcome / HRQoL report — EV-301 (same trial as the primary card)
cards.people: EV-301 patients randomised to enfortumab vedotin (n = 301) or chemotherapy (n = 307) completing the EORTC QLQ-C30 at baseline, weekly for 12 weeks, then every 12 weeks; baseline compliance 91% and 89%, averaging 70% and 67% from baseline to week 12.
cards.result: Change from baseline to week 12 favoured enfortumab vedotin on pain (−5.7, 95% CI −10.8 to −0.7, P = 0.027) and disfavoured it on appetite loss (+7.3, 0.90–13.69, P = 0.026). Larger proportions on enfortumab vedotin reported confirmed improvement, with odds of confirmed improvement across ten function/symptom scales 1.67 to 2.76 times higher than on chemotherapy (relative odds, printed as reported). Time to first confirmed deterioration in global health status/QoL was delayed on enfortumab vedotin (P = 0.027), but worsening appetite loss occurred earlier (P = 0.009). The trial is also registered on EudraCT as 2017-003344-21, as its abstract states.
cards.watchOut: Patient-reported outcomes from an open-label trial, with compliance falling to about 70% by week 12 — the pain gain and the appetite-loss harm print together, and neither is a survival result.

cards.type: Phase 3 trial prespecified-population subgroup report (Japanese subgroup) — EV-301 (same trial as the primary card)
cards.people: 86 Japanese EV-301 patients (enfortumab vedotin n = 36; standard chemotherapy — docetaxel or paclitaxel for patients in Japan — n = 50), analysed at the July 15, 2020 interim cut-off; a subgroup of the one trial, never an independent confirmation.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 15.18 months on enfortumab vedotin vs 10.55 months on chemotherapy (HR 0.437, 95% CI 0.209–0.914, a relative measure with a wide interval on 86 patients); median PFS 6.47 vs 5.39 months (HR 0.464, 0.258–0.835); confirmed response 34.4% vs 21.3%. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 91.7% vs 97.9%, including grade ≥3 events in 63.9% vs 75.0%.
cards.watchOut: N = 86 with wide confidence intervals: this card supports consistency with the overall trial result and nothing more. The chemotherapy comparator in Japan was docetaxel or paclitaxel only (no vinflunine).

cards.headline: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (EV-301, N = 608, four reports) establishes enfortumab vedotin monotherapy in previously treated advanced urothelial carcinoma — median overall survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months at the primary analysis, the benefit maintained at ~2 years (HR 0.70), quality of life maintained with less pain but worse appetite loss, and a consistent Japanese subgroup — priced in skin reactions (47.3%) and peripheral neuropathy (48.0%)
cards.summary: Synthesis: one phase 3 trial (EV-301, N = 608, four reports) establishes enfortumab vedotin monotherapy in previously treated advanced urothelial carcinoma — median overall survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months at the primary analysis, the benefit maintained at ~2 years (HR 0.70), quality of life maintained with less pain but worse appetite loss, and a consistent Japanese subgroup — priced in skin reactions (47.3%) and peripheral neuropathy (48.0%)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf are reports of the single EV-301 trial (primary, long-term follow-up, HRQoL and Japanese subgroup; N = 608 randomised). Cross-point in prose only: the first-line enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab question (EV-302) is homed at live shelf #859 — a different question, never carded here and never pooled with this monotherapy result.
cards.result: The four reports agree because they are one trial read four ways: survival benefit (relative HR 0.70 beside absolute medians 12.88 vs 8.97 months), durable at 2 years, with HRQoL maintained and the harm profile dominated by skin reactions and neuropathy rather than the cytopenias commoner on chemotherapy.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data. Four reports, ONE trial — the count is printed as such wherever this shelf is summarised.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Anti-GD2 immunotherapy in high-risk neuroblastoma: ANBL0032 — dinutuximab + cytokines vs isotretinoin alone improved 5-year survival (73.2% vs 56.6%); HR-NBL1/SIOPEN — adding interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta gave no benefit (P = 0.76) and more toxicity (two programmes, never pooled)
shelves.question: In children with high-risk neuroblastoma who have responded to induction and myeloablative consolidation, does adding anti-GD2 immunotherapy to isotretinoin improve event-free and overall survival (ANBL0032) — and, within the European programme, does adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta improve outcomes or only toxicity (HR-NBL1/SIOPEN)? (Three reports, TWO trials — limbs never pooled.)

shelves.balance: Two randomised programmes answering different questions, never pooled. ANBL0032 (N = 226, stopped early for efficacy at 61% of expected events): isotretinoin plus ch14.18 (dinutuximab, SP2/0) with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2 beat isotretinoin alone — 2-year event-free survival 66±5% vs 46±5% and, at the load-bearing 5-year follow-up, event-free survival 56.6% vs 46.1% and overall survival 73.2% vs 56.6% — at a severe price: grade 3–5 pain in 52%, capillary leak syndrome in 23% and hypersensitivity reactions in 25%. HR-NBL1/SIOPEN (N = 406): adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta (ch14.18/CHO) gave no evidence of benefit (3-year event-free survival 60% vs 56%, P = 0.76) and plainly more toxicity, with only 62% vs 87% completing allocated treatment. The products are named exactly as the publications give them — US dinutuximab (SP2/0) versus European dinutuximab beta (CHO) — related but not identical, and never silently merged.

cards.headline: ANBL0032 primary (Yu 2010, phase 3, N = 226, stopped early for efficacy at 61% of expected events): adding ch14.18 (dinutuximab, produced in SP2/0 cells) with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2 to isotretinoin improved 2-year event-free survival to 66±5% vs 46±5% (P = 0.01) and 2-year overall survival to 86±4% vs 75±5% (P = 0.02, unadjusted for interim analyses) — with grade 3–5 pain in 52%, capillary leak syndrome in 23% and hypersensitivity reactions in 25% of the immunotherapy group
cards.summary: ANBL0032 primary (Yu 2010, phase 3, N = 226, stopped early for efficacy at 61% of expected events): adding ch14.18 (dinutuximab, produced in SP2/0 cells) with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2 to isotretinoin improved 2-year event-free survival to 66±5% vs 46±5% (P = 0.01) and 2-year overall survival to 86±4% vs 75±5% (P = 0.02, unadjusted for interim analyses) — with grade 3–5 pain in 52%, capillary leak syndrome in 23% and hypersensitivity reactions in 25% of the immunotherapy group
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial — ANBL0032 primary report (programme 1 of 2 on this shelf; limbs never pooled)
cards.people: 226 eligible children with high-risk neuroblastoma who had responded to induction therapy and stem-cell transplantation, randomised to six cycles of isotretinoin alone or isotretinoin plus five concomitant cycles of ch14.18 (dinutuximab) with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2; median follow-up 2.1 years at the primary report.
cards.result: Immunotherapy was superior on event-free survival (66±5% vs 46±5% at 2 years, P = 0.01) and overall survival (86±4% vs 75±5%, P = 0.02 without adjustment for interim analyses) — absolute differences of about 20 and 11 percentage points at 2 years. The harm bill is severe and prints whole: grade 3, 4 or 5 pain in 52% of the immunotherapy group, capillary leak syndrome in 23% and hypersensitivity reactions in 25%. The study met criteria for early stopping owing to efficacy with 61% of the expected number of events observed.
cards.watchOut: Early stopping at 61% of expected events makes the 2-year point estimates optimistic — the 5-year follow-up card is the load-bearing maturity. The tested product is US dinutuximab (ch14.18 produced in SP2/0 cells, with GM-CSF/IL-2), named as the publication gives it; it is not the European dinutuximab beta of the SIOPEN card.
cards.source: Yu AL et al. Anti-GD2 antibody with GM-CSF, interleukin-2, and isotretinoin for neuroblastoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2010. PMID: 20879881. Registry ID: NCT00026312. cards.headline: ANBL0032 long-term follow-up (Yu 2021, same trial, N = 226): the benefit persisted at 5 years — event-free survival 56.6±4.7% vs 46.1±5.1% (P = 0.042) and overall survival 73.2±4.2% vs 56.6±5.1% (P = 0.045) — and dinutuximab levels, soluble IL-2 receptor, HACA (13 of 122 treated patients) and Fcγ-receptor genotypes did not correlate with outcome or clinically significant toxicity
cards.summary: ANBL0032 long-term follow-up (Yu 2021, same trial, N = 226): the benefit persisted at 5 years — event-free survival 56.6±4.7% vs 46.1±5.1% (P = 0.042) and overall survival 73.2±4.2% vs 56.6±5.1% (P = 0.045) — and dinutuximab levels, soluble IL-2 receptor, HACA (13 of 122 treated patients) and Fcγ-receptor genotypes did not correlate with outcome or clinically significant toxicity
cards.type: Phase 3 trial long-term follow-up report — ANBL0032 (same trial as the primary card)
cards.people: The same 226 randomised ANBL0032 patients (immunotherapy n = 114, isotretinoin only n = 112), with biomarker analyses in treated patients (HACA assessed in 122 patients receiving dinutuximab); a follow-up report of the primary card's trial, not a second trial.
cards.result: Five-year event-free survival was 56.6 ± 4.7% on immunotherapy vs 46.1 ± 5.1% on isotretinoin only (P = 0.042) and 5-year overall survival 73.2 ± 4.2% vs 56.6 ± 5.1% (P = 0.045) — absolute differences of about 10.5 and 16.6 percentage points. Thirteen of 122 patients receiving dinutuximab developed human anti-chimeric antibody; plasma dinutuximab levels, soluble IL-2 receptor, HACA and Fcγ receptor 2A/3A genotypes did not correlate with event-free or overall survival, or with clinically significant toxicity.
cards.watchOut: Accrual was discontinued early for efficacy, so the sample is smaller than originally planned — the authors state this on the record, and the 5-year figures, not the stopped-early 2-year figures, carry this shelf's balance.

cards.headline: HR-NBL1/SIOPEN interleukin-2 randomisation (Ladenstein 2018, phase 3, N = 406, 104 institutions in 12 countries): adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta (ch14.18/CHO) did NOT improve outcomes — 3-year event-free survival 56% (95% CI 49–63) without IL-2 vs 60% (53–66) with IL-2 (P = 0.76) — while toxicity was plainly worse: only 62% vs 87% received their allocated treatment (P < 0.0001), grade 3–4 hypersensitivity 20% vs 10%, fever 40% vs 14%, impaired general condition 41% vs 16% and capillary leak 15% vs 4%; four toxic deaths, two in each group
cards.summary: HR-NBL1/SIOPEN interleukin-2 randomisation (Ladenstein 2018, phase 3, N = 406, 104 institutions in 12 countries): adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta (ch14.18/CHO) did NOT improve outcomes — 3-year event-free survival 56% (95% CI 49–63) without IL-2 vs 60% (53–66) with IL-2 (P = 0.76) — while toxicity was plainly worse: only 62% vs 87% received their allocated treatment (P < 0.0001), grade 3–4 hypersensitivity 20% vs 10%, fever 40% vs 14%, impaired general condition 41% vs 16% and capillary leak 15% vs 4%; four toxic deaths, two in each group
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial — HR-NBL1/SIOPEN interleukin-2 randomisation (programme 2 of 2 on this shelf; limbs never pooled)
cards.people: 406 children and young people (aged 1–20 years) with high-risk neuroblastoma who had responded to induction and high-dose therapy within HR-NBL1/SIOPEN, randomised to dinutuximab beta alone (n = 200; 20 mg/m²/day as an 8-hour infusion for 5 days) or dinutuximab beta plus subcutaneous IL-2 (n = 206; 6 × 10⁶ IU/m²/day), all with isotretinoin; median follow-up 4.7 years. Of 422 eligible patients, 406 were randomised; toxicity denominators in the abstract are the treated sets as published.
cards.result: There was no evidence that adding subcutaneous IL-2 improved outcomes: 3-year event-free survival 56% (95% CI 49–63) without IL-2 vs 60% (53–66) with IL-2 (P = 0.76). Toxicity was greater with IL-2 across hypersensitivity reactions (grade 3–4: 20% vs 10% of treated patients as published), fever (40% vs 14%), impaired general condition (41% vs 16%) and capillary leak (15% vs 4%), and fewer patients completed their allocated treatment (62% vs 87%, P < 0.0001). Four patients died of toxicity, two in each group. The authors conclude dinutuximab beta and isotretinoin without subcutaneous IL-2 should be considered the standard of care on this schedule.
cards.watchOut: A negative answer is part of this shelf's balance, not a contradiction of ANBL0032: SIOPEN asks 'IL-2 versus no IL-2 on an immunotherapy backbone', ANBL0032 asks 'immunotherapy versus none'. The tested product is European dinutuximab beta (ch14.18/CHO), named as the publication gives it — related to, but not identical with, the SP2/0 dinutuximab of ANBL0032, and the two products and schedules are never silently merged.

cards.headline: Synthesis: two randomised programmes, never pooled — ANBL0032 shows anti-GD2 immunotherapy added to isotretinoin improves survival in high-risk neuroblastoma (5-year overall survival 73.2% vs 56.6%), while HR-NBL1/SIOPEN shows adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta adds toxicity and no benefit (3-year event-free survival 60% vs 56%, P = 0.76)
cards.summary: Synthesis: two randomised programmes, never pooled — ANBL0032 shows anti-GD2 immunotherapy added to isotretinoin improves survival in high-risk neuroblastoma (5-year overall survival 73.2% vs 56.6%), while HR-NBL1/SIOPEN shows adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta adds toxicity and no benefit (3-year event-free survival 60% vs 56%, P = 0.76)
cards.people: Three reports, TWO trials carded on this shelf: ANBL0032 (primary + long-term follow-up, N = 226) and the HR-NBL1/SIOPEN interleukin-2 randomisation (N = 406). Cross-point: naxitamab is a different anti-GD2 antibody in a different (relapsed/refractory, bone/bone-marrow-confined) setting and is not a limb of this shelf.
cards.result: The founding question — immunotherapy versus none after consolidation — is answered positively, at a severe toxicity price (grade 3–5 pain 52%, capillary leak 23%, hypersensitivity 25% in ANBL0032). The refinement question — more cytokine versus the antibody alone — is answered negatively in the European programme. Both answers stand; neither is averaged into a class claim.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each programme's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Naxitamab plus GM-CSF in high-risk neuroblastoma — two disease limbs, never pooled: responses in relapsed/refractory bone/bone-marrow disease (Limb A) and consolidation of complete remission (Limb B, post-protocol-therapy-confounded)
shelves.question: In children with high-risk neuroblastoma, does naxitamab (humanised anti-GD2 3F8) plus granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) (A) produce objective responses in relapsed or primary-refractory disease confined to bone/bone marrow, and (B) consolidate first or later complete remission — and at what infusion-toxicity cost? (Four reports, three registered trials, ONE programme — labelled as such; the two limbs answer different questions and are never pooled.)

shelves.balance: Every report is single-arm; there is no randomised naxitamab trial and this shelf says so on its face. The two disease limbs are never pooled. LIMB A — active disease: the pivotal phase 2 trial (74 treated, efficacy population 52, relapsed/refractory disease in bone/bone marrow) found overall response 50% (95% CI 36–64), complete response 38%, with bone-compartment response 58% and bone-marrow response 74%, against naxitamab-related grade 3 hypotension in 58% and grade 3 pain in 54% — the harm bill belongs whole on the face. The MSK primary-refractory cohort (32 patients, stepped-up GM-CSF dosing — a different schedule from the pivotal trial's; schedules are printed as published and never merged) found complete response in 24 of 32 (75%). LIMB B — consolidation of complete remission (single-arm, confounded, labelled): in first complete remission (59 patients, naxitamab + stepped-up GM-CSF plus isotretinoin), 3-year event-free survival was 73% and overall survival 93% — BUT 50 of 59 patients received post-protocol treatment (vaccine and/or difluoromethylornithine), so those survival figures cannot be attributed to naxitamab alone; the load-bearing content of this limb is that the regimen was tolerable and outpatient-deliverable. The second-or-later-CR report (60 patients) carries the same attribution warning in its own conclusion, with post-protocol anti-neuroblastoma vaccine routine. Naxitamab is a humanised 3F8 antibody, FDA-approved for the Limb A setting (relapsed/refractory disease in bone/bone marrow, patients ≥1 year). Cross-point only to pack #7778 (dinutuximab programmes) — a different antibody, schedule and evidence shape; the two anti-GD2 shelves are never presented as a class comparison.

cards.headline: LIMB A — pivotal phase 2 (Trial 201): overall response 50% (95% CI 36–64) and complete response 38% in relapsed/refractory bone/bone-marrow disease, with grade 3 hypotension in 58% and grade 3 pain in 54%
cards.summary: LIMB A — pivotal phase 2 (Trial 201): overall response 50% (95% CI 36–64) and complete response 38% in relapsed/refractory bone/bone-marrow disease, with grade 3 hypotension in 58% and grade 3 pain in 54%
cards.type: Single-arm phase 2 trial — Limb A (active relapsed/refractory disease), pivotal report
cards.people: 74 patients with relapsed/refractory high-risk neuroblastoma and residual disease in bone/bone marrow received naxitamab 3 mg/kg/day on days 1, 3 and 5 with GM-CSF (days −4 to 5) every 4 weeks; the prespecified interim efficacy population was 52 patients (58% refractory, 42% relapsed disease among the 26 responders). Single-arm, non-randomised — there is no randomised naxitamab trial.
cards.result: Overall response rate was 50% (95% CI 36–64%), with complete response 38% and partial response 12%; the primary endpoint was met (lower 95% CI limit above 20%). Bone-compartment response was 58% (29 of 50; CR 40%, PR 18%) and bone-marrow compartment response 74% (17 of 23; CR 74%). One-year overall survival was 93% (95% CI 80–98) and progression-free survival 35% (16–54) — secondary, descriptive figures from a single-arm trial. Naxitamab-related grade 3 adverse events included hypotension (58%) and pain (54%).
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: response rates have no comparator and survival figures are descriptive only. The GM-CSF schedule here differs from the stepped-up schedule of the two MSK reports on this shelf — schedules are printed as published and never merged.
cards.source: Mora J et al. The anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody naxitamab plus GM-CSF for relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma: a phase 2 clinical trial. Nature communications. 2025. PMID: 39952926. Registry ID: NCT03363373. cards.headline: LIMB A — MSK primary-refractory cohort (stepped-up GM-CSF): complete response in 24 of 32 patients (75%), bone-marrow complete response in 22 of 23 with marrow metastases
cards.summary: LIMB A — MSK primary-refractory cohort (stepped-up GM-CSF): complete response in 24 of 32 patients (75%), bone-marrow complete response in 22 of 23 with marrow metastases
cards.type: Phase I/II single-arm trial — Limb A (primary refractory disease), MSK stepped-up-GM-CSF programme
cards.people: 32 patients with primary refractory osteomedullary high-risk neuroblastoma on a phase I/II trial of naxitamab (9 mg/kg/cycle at the recommended phase II dosage) plus stepped-up GM-CSF dosing; cycles monthly ×5 after a major response. Nine patients had previously received other anti-GD2 antibodies.
cards.result: Complete response occurred in 24 of 32 (75%) — 12 by international criteria and 12 based on MIBG-avid sites with negative PET scans. Bone-marrow CR was achieved in 22 of 23 patients with marrow metastases. Of 29 patients with abnormal MIBG scans, major responses occurred in 14 of 20 with Curie scores 10–25 and 7 of 9 with scores 1–9. Five of the 9 patients previously treated with other anti-GD2 antibodies became event-free survivors. Five-year progression-free survival was 38% and overall survival 64% (descriptive, single-arm). Post-protocol, 18 patients received anti-neuroblastoma vaccine — a further reason the survival figures are not naxitamab-only effects.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm, single-programme cohort. Post-protocol vaccine in 18 of 32 patients confounds the survival figures, which print as descriptive only. Stepped-up GM-CSF schedule — do not merge with the pivotal trial's schedule.

cards.headline: LIMB B — consolidation of FIRST complete remission: 3-year event-free survival 73% and overall survival 93%, BUT 50 of 59 patients received post-protocol vaccine and/or difluoromethylornithine — the survival figures cannot be attributed to naxitamab alone
cards.summary: LIMB B — consolidation of FIRST complete remission: 3-year event-free survival 73% and overall survival 93%, BUT 50 of 59 patients received post-protocol vaccine and/or difluoromethylornithine — the survival figures cannot be attributed to naxitamab alone
cards.type: Phase II single-arm trial — Limb B (consolidation of first complete remission), confounded by post-protocol therapy
cards.people: 59 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma in first complete remission (53 stage 4, 6 stage 3) received up to five monthly cycles of naxitamab plus stepped-up GM-CSF, plus isotretinoin (21 of 59 took no isotretinoin). Phase II, single-arm.
cards.result: At 36 months, event-free survival was 73% and overall survival 93% — printed ONLY with the confounding warning attached: 50 of 59 patients received after-protocol treatment (vaccine and/or difluoromethylornithine), so these percentages are not effects of naxitamab. Six of 18 relapses were isolated in the central nervous system. Longer time from diagnosis to enrolment was an adverse prognostic factor (P = 0.04). The report's load-bearing content is that treatment was tolerable and allowed outpatient administration.
cards.watchOut: BINDING: this limb's survival percentages may be printed only with the post-protocol vaccine/DFMO confounding warning attached, never as effects. Never pool this limb with Limb A.

cards.headline: LIMB B — consolidation of SECOND or later complete remission: progression-free survival 55% at 2 years and 50% at 5 years, with the report's own conclusion stating the outcome cannot be attributed solely to naxitamab + GM-CSF
cards.summary: LIMB B — consolidation of SECOND or later complete remission: progression-free survival 55% at 2 years and 50% at 5 years, with the report's own conclusion stating the outcome cannot be attributed solely to naxitamab + GM-CSF
cards.type: Phase II single-arm trial — Limb B (consolidation of second/later complete remission), confounded by post-protocol therapy
cards.people: 60 patients consolidating post-relapse complete remission (42 after one prior relapse, 18 after ≥2; 45% MYCN-amplified) received five monthly cycles of naxitamab plus stepped-up GM-CSF. Phase II, single-arm, same registered MSK programme as the primary-refractory report (NCT01757626).
cards.result: Progression-free survival was 55% at 2 years and 50% at 5 years (descriptive, single-arm). Prior treatment with naxitamab and prior widespread relapse significantly worsened PFS. Post-protocol, patients in CR routinely received an investigational anti-neuroblastoma vaccine and two patients took difluoromethylornithine; the authors conclude the encouraging long-term outcome cannot be attributed solely to naxitamab + GM-CSF given post-protocol therapies.
cards.watchOut: Same attribution warning as the first-CR limb: routine post-protocol vaccine. Never pool with Limb A, and never present this shelf beside pack #7778 (dinutuximab) as a class comparison — different antibody (humanised 3F8), different schedule, different evidence shape.
cards.source: Kushner BH et al. A phase II trial of naxitamab plus stepped-up dosing of GM-CSF for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma in second or later complete remission. cards.headline: Synthesis: one programme, four single-arm reports, two limbs never pooled — Limb A shows real response activity at a high infusion-toxicity price; Limb B's survival figures are confounded and descriptive only
cards.summary: Synthesis: one programme, four single-arm reports, two limbs never pooled — Limb A shows real response activity at a high infusion-toxicity price; Limb B's survival figures are confounded and descriptive only
cards.people: Four reports, three registered trials, one programme: Limb A — 74 treated / 52 in the efficacy population (pivotal) and 32 (primary-refractory cohort); Limb B — 59 (first CR) and 60 (second/later CR). No randomised trial exists anywhere in this base.
cards.result: Limb A: overall response 50% and complete response 38% (pivotal), complete response 75% (primary-refractory cohort) — single-arm response evidence, priced with grade 3 hypotension 58% and pain 54%. Limb B: 3-year EFS 73% / OS 93% in first CR and 5-year PFS 50% in later CR are printed only with the post-protocol vaccine/DFMO confounding attached; the defensible Limb B claim is tolerability and outpatient deliverability. Cross-point only to pack #7778 (dinutuximab programmes), in prose, never as a class comparison.
cards.watchOut: Do not pool the limbs, do not pool the GM-CSF schedules, and do not quote any Limb B survival percentage without its confounding warning.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
